short_description.id: Mitra adalah nama ilahi Indo-Iran yang terkait dengan Mitra Rigveda dan Mithra Avesta.
short_description.en: Mitra is an Indo-Iranian divine name connected with Rigvedic Mitra and Avestan Mithra.

long_description.id:
Mitra adalah nama ilahi Indo-Iran yang terkait dengan Mitra Rigveda dan Mithra Avesta. Bahasa Avesta mempertahankan makna perjanjian untuk miθra.

Dalam bahasa Sanskerta dan Indo-Arya modern, mitra berarti sahabat. Dalam tradisi Persia, Mithra dihubungkan dengan matahari terbit, perjanjian, dan persahabatan. Sumber membedakan Mithra Persia dari Mithras kultus misteri Romawi. Mitra Weda dihubungkan dengan perjanjian, fajar, kesuburan panen, dan kebenaran. Pasangan Mitra-Varuna menghubungkan Mitra dengan dewa langit Varuna. Mithra Persia digambarkan menaiki kereta bercahaya yang ditarik kuda putih. Persenjatannya mencakup tombak perak, busur dan anak panah emas, pisau, kapak, serta gada. Mithra memberikan farr atau karunia ilahi kepada raja yang layak. Nama Mithra dipanggil dalam prasasti Kekaisaran Akhemeniyah. Mihr Yasht menyebut Mithra membela pihak seiman maupun yang berbeda iman dalam perjanjian. Mihr Yasht menyebut Mithra memberikan kecepatan kepada kuda. Himne menggambarkan Mithra memiliki seribu telinga dan sepuluh ribu mata. Mithra dipuji sebagai kuat, tidak tidur, dan selalu terjaga.
long_description.en:
Mitra is an Indo-Iranian divine name connected with Rigvedic Mitra and Avestan Mithra. Avestan miθra preserves the meaning covenant.

In Sanskrit and modern Indo-Aryan languages, mitra means friend. Persian tradition associates Mithra with the rising sun, contracts, covenants, and friendship. The source distinguishes Persian Mithra from the Mithras of the Roman mystery cult. Vedic Mitra is associated with contracts, sunrise, harvest fertility, and truth. The Mitra-Varuna pairing connects Mitra with the sky god Varuna. Persian Mithra rides a bright chariot drawn by white horses. His weapons include a silver spear, a bow and golden arrows, daggers, axes, and a mace. Mithra bestows farr, divine grace, on a worthy monarch. Mithra’s name is invoked in Achaemenid inscriptions. The Mihr Yasht says Mithra stands for both the faithful and the unfaithful in contracts. The Mihr Yasht attributes swiftness for horses to Mithra. The hymn depicts Mithra with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes. Mithra is praised as strong, sleepless, and always awake.

short_description.id: Nike adalah dewi kemenangan yang sering digambarkan bersayap dan membawa karangan kemenangan.
short_description.en: Nike is a Greek goddess of victory often shown with wings and a victory wreath.

long_description.id:
Nike mempersonifikasikan kemenangan. Styx dan Titan Pallas adalah orang tuanya; Zelus, Cratos, dan Bia adalah saudara perempuannya. Mereka berada di dekat Zeus di Olympus.

Nike digambarkan bersayap dan membawa karangan kemenangan. Patung kuno dari Delos dan vas kuno memperlihatkan ragam gambaran dirinya, termasuk menaiki kereta. Dalam seni museum ia juga berlari ke arah altar dan kemungkinan membawa karangan.

Nama Nike melekat pada gelar Athena Nike; sebuah kuil Athena sebagai kemenangan berdiri di Acropolis Athena. Patung Nike juga didirikan untuk memperingati kemenangan perang, dan patung dewa besar digambarkan memegang Nike kecil. Salah satu patung tersohor ialah karya Paionios.
long_description.en:
Nike personifies victory. Styx and the Titan Pallas are her parents; Zelus, Cratos and Bia are her sisters. They remain near Zeus on Olympus.

Nike appears winged with a victory wreath. An ancient Delos sculpture and Attic pottery show varied depictions, including a chariot. In a museum vase scene she runs toward an altar and probably carried a wreath.

Nike's name appears in the epithet Athena Nike; a temple of Athena as Victory stood on the Acropolis of Athens. Nike statues commemorated military victories, and large divine statues held a statue of Nike. A famous Nike was sculpted by Paionios.

short_description.id: Nyx ialah dewi purba dan personifikasi malam dalam mitologi Yunani.
short_description.en: Nyx is a primordial goddess and personification of night in Greek mythology.

long_description.id:
Dalam Theogony karya Hesiod, Malam lahir dari Chaos dan bersama Erebus melahirkan Aether serta Day. Nyx juga disebut melahirkan sejumlah roh, di antaranya Sleep, Death, Strife, dan Pain.

Gambaran kuno menampilkan Nyx bersayap atau mengendarai kereta. Hemera, personifikasi Day, bergantian dengannya; keduanya tidak tinggal di rumah Tartarus pada waktu yang sama. Ia juga digambarkan berselubung hitam atau berbintang saat menaiki kereta.

Dalam kisah Iliad, Hypnos mengatakan bahwa Nyx melindunginya dari Zeus. Bukti pemujaannya di kuil sangat sedikit, meskipun Pausanias menyebut orakel Malam di Megara.
long_description.en:
In Hesiod's Theogony, Night comes from Chaos and with Erebus bears Aether and Day. Nyx also bears spirits including Sleep, Death, Strife, and Pain.

Ancient depictions show Nyx with wings or a chariot. Hemera, the personification of Day, alternates with her; they are never at home in Tartarus at the same time. She is also depicted with a black or starry veil while driving the chariot.

In the Iliad, Hypnos says Nyx protected him from Zeus. Evidence of temple worship is sparse, though Pausanias mentions an Oracle of Night in Megara.

short_description.id: Ptah adalah dewa pencipta Mesir dan pelindung perajin serta arsitek.
short_description.en: Ptah is an Egyptian creator god and patron of craftsmen and architects.

long_description.id:
Ptah adalah dewa pencipta Mesir dan pelindung perajin serta arsitek. Dalam triad Memphis, ia menjadi suami Sekhmet. Nefertem dianggap sebagai putranya.

Ptah menciptakan dunia melalui gagasan dan ucapan. Batu Shabaka menghubungkan pemberian kehidupan dengan hati dan lidahnya. Bentuknya kadang digambarkan sebagai sosok kerdil. Pemujaannya menyebar ke kawasan Mediterania timur. Penggambaran umum memperlihatkan laki-laki berkulit hijau dalam kain pembungkus.

Simbol tongkatnya menggabungkan kuasa, kehidupan, dan kestabilan. Sinkretisme menghasilkan Ptah-Sokar-Osiris. World History Encyclopedia menghubungkan Ptah dengan pohon moringa. Dalam peran pencipta, ia juga disebut Ptah-Nun atau Ptah-Naunet. Gambarnya memakai penutup kepala rapat dan memegang tongkat was. Sumber itu menyebut Ptah telah muncul pada Dinasti Pertama. Budge mengaitkan Ptah dengan pembukaan mulut para dewa dalam Kitab Orang Mati.
long_description.en:
Ptah is an Egyptian creator god and patron of craftsmen and architects. In the Memphis triad he is Sekhmet’s husband. Nefertem is regarded as his son.

Ptah creates the world through conception and speech. The Shabaka Stone connects his giving life with his heart and tongue. He is sometimes represented as a dwarf. His worship spread to the eastern Mediterranean. A common depiction shows a green-skinned man in a shroud.

His staff symbols combine power, life and stability. Syncretism produces Ptah-Sokar-Osiris. World History Encyclopedia connects Ptah with the moringa tree. In his creative role he is also called Ptah-Nun or Ptah-Naunet. His image wears a skullcap and holds a was-sceptre. That source states that Ptah appears in the First Dynasty. Budge associates Ptah with opening the gods’ mouths in the Book of the Dead.

short_description.id: Shu adalah dewa udara primordial dalam mitologi Mesir.
short_description.en: Shu is a primordial air god in Egyptian mythology.

long_description.id:
Shu adalah dewa udara primordial dalam mitologi Mesir. Tefnut adalah saudari sekaligus istrinya. Atum menciptakan Shu dan Tefnut dalam kisah Heliopolis.

Shu adalah ayah Nut dan Geb. Udara yang diwakilinya dianggap menyejukkan dan menenangkan. Ia digambarkan memakai bulu burung unta sebagai lambang ringan dan kosong. Kabut dan awan juga dikaitkan dengan Shu. Sebuah mitos mengisahkan Tefnut meninggalkan Mesir setelah bertengkar dengan Shu.

Orang Yunani menghubungkannya dengan Atlas yang menopang langit. Ia umumnya berupa manusia, kadang berkepala singa saat membela dewa matahari. Nama Shu diterjemahkan sebagai Kekosongan. Satu kisah mengisahkan Mata Ra mencari Shu dan Tefnut yang lama pergi. Kepulangan mereka membuat Atum menangis bahagia dan air matanya menjadi manusia. Kabut disebut Danau Shu dalam uraian sumber ini. Budge menjelaskan empat pilar di arah mata angin sebagai penopang langit Shu.
long_description.en:
Shu is a primordial air god in Egyptian mythology. Tefnut is his sister and wife. Atum creates Shu and Tefnut in the Heliopolitan account.

Shu is the father of Nut and Geb. The air he represents is considered cooling and calming. He is shown wearing an ostrich feather signifying lightness and emptiness. Mist and clouds are also associated with Shu. One myth tells of Tefnut leaving Egypt after a quarrel with Shu.

The Greeks associate him with Atlas who supports the heavens. He is usually human, sometimes lion-headed when defending the sun god. Shu’s name is translated as Emptiness. One tale has the Eye of Ra search for Shu and Tefnut after a long absence. Their return makes Atum weep for joy and his tears become humans. Mist is called Lakes of Shu in this source. Budge describes four pillars at the cardinal points as Shu’s sky supports.

claims_provenance.quote: As the air, Shu was considered to be a cooling, and thus a calming influence and pacifier. Due to the association with dry air, calm, and thus Ma'at (truth, justice, order, and balance), Shu was depicted as the dry air/atmosphere between the Earth and sky, separating the two realms after the event of the First Occasion. Shu was also portrayed in art as wearing an ostrich feather.

Nama Shu diterjemahkan sebagai Kekosongan. Satu kisah mengisahkan Mata Ra mencari Shu dan Tefnut yang lama pergi. Kepulangan mereka membuat Atum menangis bahagia dan air matanya menjadi manusia. Kabut disebut Danau Shu dalam uraian sumber ini. Budge menjelaskan empat pilar di arah mata angin sebagai penopang langit Shu.
long_description.en: The Greeks associate him with Atlas who supports the heavens. He is usually human, sometimes lion-headed when defending the sun god. Shu’s name is translated as Emptiness. One tale has the Eye of Ra search for Shu and Tefnut after a long absence. Their return makes Atum weep for joy and his tears become humans. Mist is called Lakes of Shu in this source. Budge describes four pillars at the cardinal points as Shu’s sky supports.

short_description.id: Sin atau Nanna adalah dewa bulan dan kebijaksanaan Mesopotamia.
short_description.en: Sin, also known as Nanna, is the Mesopotamian deity of the moon and wisdom.

long_description.id:
Sin atau Nanna adalah dewa bulan dan kebijaksanaan Mesopotamia. Nanna merupakan nama Sumerianya, sedangkan Sin dan Nanna-Suen adalah nama lainnya.

Kuil dan ziggurat di Ur menjadi pusat pemujaannya. Sin disebut sebagai putra Enlil dan Ninlil. Ningal atau Nikkal, dewi kesuburan, disebut sebagai istrinya. Utu-Shamash disebut sebagai putra pasangan itu. Sin juga memiliki kuil penting di Harran. Salah satu penggambaran menunjukkan pria duduk berjanggut lapis lazuli dengan bulan sabit di atasnya. Angka 30 melambangkannya dengan merujuk jumlah hari bulan lunar. Pada bulan baru, Sin dikatakan berada di dunia bawah untuk mengadili orang mati. Dalam Perjalanan Nanna ke Nippur, ia membawa muatan persembahan dari Ur kepada Enlil. Enheduanna disebut sebagai pendeta tingginya yang paling terkenal. Sin dihubungkan dengan kesuburan perempuan dan ternak. Sumber pendamping menggambarkannya sebagai pria berdiri dengan bulan sabit. Dalam teks Turunnya Inanna, Nanna menjadi tujuan permohonan Ninshubur di Urim.
long_description.en:
Sin, also known as Nanna, is the Mesopotamian deity of the moon and wisdom. Nanna is his Sumerian name; Sin and Nanna-Suen are alternative names.

His major cult center is the temple and ziggurat at Ur. Sin is identified as the son of Enlil and Ninlil. Ningal, also called Nikkal, is his wife and a fertility goddess. Utu-Shamash is named as the couple’s son. Sin also has an important temple at Harran. One depiction shows a seated man with a lapis-lazuli beard and a crescent above him. The number 30 represents him through the days of a lunar month. At the new moon, Sin is said to judge the dead in the netherworld. In The Journey of Nanna to Nippur, he loads offerings at Ur to bring to Enlil. Enheduanna is identified as his best-known high priestess. Sin is associated with the fertility of women and cattle. The accompanying source depicts him as a standing man with a crescent moon. In the Descent of Inanna, Nanna is a recipient of Ninshubur’s appeal at Urim.

short_description.id: Surya adalah dewa matahari dalam tradisi Hindu yang diceritakan melintasi langit dengan kereta tujuh kuda.
short_description.en: Surya is the Hindu sun god who travels across the sky in a chariot drawn by seven horses.

long_description.id:
Surya, juga disebut Aditya, adalah dewa matahari dalam tradisi Hindu. Ia dipandang sebagai sumber kehidupan; kisahnya menempatkan Aruna sebagai pengemudi kereta emas yang ditarik tujuh kuda. Namanya telah muncul dalam Rigveda dan ia dikaitkan dengan sembilan benda langit kuno.

Silsilah Surya berbeda antar kisah: ia disebut putra Kasyapa dan Aditi, atau Dyaus, atau Brahma. Bersama Samjna ia memiliki Vaivasvata, Yama, dan Yami. Kisah lain mengatakan Surya menyamar sebagai kuda jantan untuk bertemu kembali dengan Samjna.

Pemujaannya terkait dengan perayaan Pongal dan mantra Gayatri. Tradisi Smarta menghitungnya di antara lima dewa utama. Kuil di Konarak menjadi penggambaran raksasa kereta matahari dengan dua belas pasang roda dan tujuh kuda.
long_description.en:
Surya, also called Aditya, is the Hindu sun god. He is regarded as a source of life; Aruna drives his golden chariot pulled by seven horses. He appears in the Rigveda and is regarded as chief of the nine ancient planets.

Surya has varying genealogies: he is named a son of Kasyapa and Aditi, or of Dyaus, or of Brahma. With Samjna he fathers Vaivasvata, Yama and Yami. Another account says he took the form of a stallion to reunite with Samjna.

His worship is linked to Pongal and the Gayatri mantra. The Smarta tradition counts him among five major deities. The temple at Konarak depicts a monumental sun chariot with twelve pairs of wheels and seven horses.

note.en: Yama is named a child of Surya and Samjna.

short_description.id: Surya adalah dewa matahari dalam tradisi Hindu yang diceritakan melintasi langit dengan kereta tujuh kuda.
short_description.en: Surya is the Hindu sun god who travels across the sky in a chariot drawn by seven horses.

long_description.id: Surya, juga disebut Aditya, adalah dewa matahari dalam tradisi Hindu. Ia dipandang sebagai sumber kehidupan; kisahnya menempatkan Aruna sebagai pengemudi kereta emas yang ditarik tujuh kuda. Namanya telah muncul dalam Rigveda dan ia dikaitkan dengan sembilan benda langit kuno.
long_description.en: Surya, also called Aditya, is the Hindu sun god. He is regarded as a source of life; Aruna drives his golden chariot pulled by seven horses. He appears in the Rigveda and is regarded as chief of the nine ancient planets.

long_description.id: Silsilah Surya berbeda antar kisah: ia disebut putra Kasyapa dan Aditi, atau Dyaus, atau Brahma. Bersama Samjna ia memiliki Vaivasvata, Yama, dan Yami. Kisah lain mengatakan Surya menyamar sebagai kuda jantan untuk bertemu kembali dengan Samjna.
long_description.en: Surya has varying genealogies: he is named a son of Kasyapa and Aditi, or of Dyaus, or of Brahma. With Samjna he fathers Vaivasvata, Yama and Yami. Another account says he took the form of a stallion to reunite with Samjna.

long_description.id: Pemujaannya terkait dengan perayaan Pongal dan mantra Gayatri. Tradisi Smarta menghitungnya di antara lima dewa utama. Kuil di Konarak menjadi penggambaran raksasa kereta matahari dengan dua belas pasang roda dan tujuh kuda.
long_description.en: His worship is linked to Pongal and the Gayatri mantra. The Smarta tradition counts him among five major deities. The temple at Konarak depicts a monumental sun chariot with twelve pairs of wheels and seven horses.

short_description.id: Tartarus adalah dewa purba Yunani yang mewujudkan jurang terdalam di bawah bumi; nama yang sama juga menunjuk tempat kurungan mitis.
short_description.en: Tartarus is a Greek primordial deity embodying the deep pit beneath the earth; the same name also denotes a mythic prison.

long_description.id:
Tartarus ialah dewa elemental yang dipahami sebagai tubuh jurang itu sendiri, bukan sosok manusia. Ia ditempatkan di bawah bumi dan termasuk wujud paling awal dalam kosmogoni Yunani.

Sebagai tempat, Tartarus berbeda dari Hades dalam gambaran awal. Jurang ini disebut penjara gelap berpintu besi; Zeus mengurung Cronus dan para Titan di sana, dan kisah lain menyebut dinding perunggu dengan penjaga Hekatonkheires. Kosmologi menempatkannya sebagai titik terendah yang terpisah dari alam bawah.

Tartarus dan Gaia disebut orang tua Typhon. Silsilahnya sendiri berbeda: Hesiod menempatkannya sebagai wujud awal tanpa orang tua, sedangkan tradisi lain menyebutnya anak Æther dan Ge. Penulis yang lebih akhir juga menjadikannya tempat hukuman orang jahat setelah mati.
long_description.en:
Tartarus is an elemental deity understood as the pit itself rather than a human form. He lies below the earth and belongs among the earliest beings in Greek cosmogony.

As a place, Tartarus differs from Hades in early accounts. It is a dark prison with iron gates where Zeus cast Cronus and the Titans; another description gives it bronze walls guarded by the Hekatonkheires. Cosmology places it at the universe’s lowest point, separate from the underworld.

Tartarus and Gaia are named as Typhon's parents. His own genealogy varies: Hesiod has him emerge without parents, while another tradition names Æther and Ge. Later writers also made the pit a place of punishment after death.

short_description.id: Varuna adalah dewa Hindu yang digambarkan sebagai penguasa langit pada zaman Weda awal.
short_description.en: Varuna is a Hindu god depicted as sovereign of the sky in early Vedic times.

long_description.id:
Varuna adalah dewa Hindu yang digambarkan sebagai penguasa langit pada zaman Weda awal. Ia menjaga kebenaran dan rta, tatanan kosmis serta moral.

Varuna sering dipasangkan dengan Mitra. Dalam tradisi Itihasa dan Purana ia menjadi penguasa lautan, sungai, aliran air, dan danau. Ia juga berperan sebagai dikpala penjaga arah barat. Penggambarannya mencakup sosok muda yang menunggang makhluk Makara. Ia membawa jerat pasha dan kendi. Tolkappiyam menyebutnya Kadalon, dewa laut dan hujan. Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia dikenal sebagai Suiten dan termasuk Dua Belas Dewa. Penjelasan Hindu mengaitkan namanya dengan akar vr yang berarti meliputi atau mengikat. Rigveda memuat sejumlah himne Varuna dan menggambarkannya sebagai raja langit, penjaga rta, penguasa air, serta pemilik maya. Rigveda 1.25 memujinya karena memahami lintasan burung, kapal, dan angin. Himne menggambarkannya menghukum pelanggaran tetapi mengasihi orang yang bertobat. Britannica 1911 mencatat gelar Jalapati dan Amburaja yang merujuk penguasa air. Patung Varuna di NGV berupa sosok batu pasir merah dalam lengkung berpilar, diapit penjaga dan makhluk leogryph.
long_description.en:
Varuna is a Hindu god depicted as sovereign of the sky in early Vedic times. He maintains truth and rta, cosmic and moral order.

Varuna is frequently paired with Mitra. In Itihasa and Purana traditions he becomes lord of oceans, rivers, streams, and lakes. He also serves as the dikpala guarding the west. His depictions include a youthful figure riding the creature Makara. He carries a pasha noose and pitcher. The Tolkappiyam calls him Kadalon, god of sea and rain. In Japanese Buddhism he is known as Suiten and belongs to the Twelve Devas. A Hindu explanation connects his name with the root vr, meaning to encompass or bind. The Rigveda contains several Varuna hymns and depicts him as sky sovereign, guardian of rta, water deity, and wielder of maya. Rigveda 1.25 praises him for understanding the paths of birds, ships, and winds. Hymns depict him as punishing wrongdoing while showing mercy to the penitent. The 1911 Britannica records the epithets Jalapati and Amburaja referring to lordship over water. The NGV Varuna sculpture is a red sandstone figure in a columned arch, flanked by guardians and leogryphs.

short_description.id: Vayu adalah dewa angin Hindu dan utusan ilahi para dewa.
short_description.en: Vayu is the Hindu wind god and divine messenger of the gods.

long_description.id:
Vayu adalah dewa angin Hindu dan utusan ilahi para dewa. Nama lainnya termasuk Vata dan Pavana.

Ia berhubungan erat dengan Indra dalam kitab Weda. Ia disebut lahir dari napas Vishvapurusha. Ia menjadi dewa pertama yang minum Soma dalam uraian Weda. Upanishad memujinya sebagai Prana, napas hidup dunia. Kitab kemudian menyebutnya penjaga arah barat laut. Wiracarita menyebutnya ayah Hanuman dan Bhima. Vayu dijelaskan sebagai peniup dan Prana sebagai napas kehidupan. Rigveda menghubungkannya dengan kereta bercahaya yang ditarik kuda. Sebagai anggota delapan Vasu ia juga disebut Anila. Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia termasuk Dua Belas Dewa penjaga arah. Nama Jepangnya adalah Futen. Mackenzie mengutip himne yang menghubungkan Vayu dengan dua kuda merah pada kereta serta kawanan rusa. Rigveda 1.2 memanggil Vayu untuk minum Soma yang dipersiapkan dan mendengar doa.
long_description.en:
Vayu is the Hindu wind god and divine messenger of the gods. His other names include Vata and Pavana.

He is closely associated with Indra in Vedic scriptures. He is described as born from Vishvapurusha's breath. He is the first god to drink Soma in Vedic accounts. The Upanishads praise him as Prana, the world's life breath. Later scriptures describe him as guardian of the northwest. The epics describe him as Hanuman and Bhima's father. Vayu is explained as blower and Prana as the breath of life. The Rigveda connects him with a shining chariot drawn by horses. As a member of the eight Vasus he is also called Anila. In Japanese Buddhism he belongs to the Twelve Devas guarding directions. His Japanese name is Futen. Mackenzie quotes a hymn connecting Vayu with two red horses on a chariot and a team of deer. Rigveda 1.2 calls Vayu to drink the prepared Soma and hear the prayer.

long_description.en: Vayu is the Hindu wind god and divine messenger of the gods. His other names include Vata and Pavana.

long_description.id: Ia berhubungan erat dengan Indra dalam kitab Weda. Ia disebut lahir dari napas Vishvapurusha. Ia menjadi dewa pertama yang minum Soma dalam uraian Weda. Upanishad memujinya sebagai Prana, napas hidup dunia. Kitab kemudian menyebutnya penjaga arah barat laut. Wiracarita menyebutnya ayah Hanuman dan Bhima. Vayu dijelaskan sebagai peniup dan Prana sebagai napas kehidupan. Rigveda menghubungkannya dengan kereta bercahaya yang ditarik kuda. Sebagai anggota delapan Vasu ia juga disebut Anila. Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia termasuk Dua Belas Dewa penjaga arah. Nama Jepangnya adalah Futen. Mackenzie mengutip himne yang menghubungkan Vayu dengan dua kuda merah pada kereta serta kawanan rusa. Rigveda 1.2 memanggil Vayu untuk minum Soma yang dipersiapkan dan mendengar doa.
long_description.en: He is closely associated with Indra in Vedic scriptures. He is described as born from Vishvapurusha's breath. He is the first god to drink Soma in Vedic accounts. The Upanishads praise him as Prana, the world's life breath. Later scriptures describe him as guardian of the northwest. The epics describe him as Hanuman and Bhima's father. Vayu is explained as blower and Prana as the breath of life. The Rigveda connects him with a shining chariot drawn by horses. As a member of the eight Vasus he is also called Anila. In Japanese Buddhism he belongs to the Twelve Devas guarding directions. His Japanese name is Futen. Mackenzie quotes a hymn connecting Vayu with two red horses on a chariot and a team of deer. Rigveda 1.2 calls Vayu to drink the prepared Soma and hear the prayer.

claims.quote: The word for air (vāyu) or wind (pavana) is one of the classical elements in Hinduism. The Sanskrit word Vāta literally means 'blown'; Vāyu, 'blower' and Prāna, 'breathing' (viz. the breath of life, cf. the *an- in animate).

short_description.id: Aditi adalah dewi Weda penting dalam Hindu, dengan nama yang berarti tak terbatas atau tak terikat.
short_description.en: Aditi is an important Vedic goddess in Hinduism, with a name meaning boundless or unbound.

long_description.id:
Aditi adalah dewi Weda penting dalam Hindu, dengan nama yang berarti tak terbatas atau tak terikat. Ia mempersonifikasikan keluasan kosmos.

Ia dikaitkan dengan keibuan dan kesuburan. Aditi disebut ibu kelompok dewa Aditya. Artikel mencatat namanya disebut lebih dari 250 kali dalam Rigveda. Versi Purana menyebut Aditi putri Daksha dan Asikni serta pasangan Kashyapa. Dalam kisah itu Indra lahir setelah Aditi meminta seorang putra ideal. Versi Purana tersebut kemudian memberi dua belas Aditya sebagai putranya. Shatapatha Brahmana juga memanggil Aditi sebagai bumi dalam pengorbanan. Ia disebut ibu Vamana, penjelmaan Vishnu. Pemohon memanggil Aditi untuk perlindungan, keselamatan, dan kelimpahan. Rigveda 1.89.10 menyebut Aditi sebagai semua dewa. Himne itu juga menyamakan Aditi dengan segala yang telah lahir dan yang akan lahir. Versi yang dibahas Mackenzie memberi Aditi delapan putra dan menyebut putra kedelapan yang dibuang lalu dibentuk menjadi Vivasvat. Rigveda 1.89.10 mengidentifikasi Aditi dengan langit, ruang antara, ibu, ayah, dan putra.
long_description.en:
Aditi is an important Vedic goddess in Hinduism, with a name meaning boundless or unbound. She personifies the vastness of the cosmos.

She is associated with motherhood and fertility. Aditi is called the mother of the Aditya gods. The article records her name appearing more than 250 times in the Rigveda. A Puranic version describes Aditi as Daksha and Asikni's daughter and Kashyapa's consort. In that account Indra is born after Aditi asks for an ideal son. That Puranic version subsequently gives twelve Adityas as her sons. The Shatapatha Brahmana also invokes Aditi as earth in sacrifice. She is called Vamana's mother, an incarnation of Vishnu. Petitioners invoke Aditi for protection, safety, and abundance. Rigveda 1.89.10 calls Aditi all Gods. The hymn also identifies Aditi with all that has been born and shall be born. The version discussed by Mackenzie gives Aditi eight sons and describes the discarded eighth son later fashioned into Vivasvat. Rigveda 1.89.10 identifies Aditi with heaven, mid air, mother, father, and son.

short_description.id: Avalokiteśvara adalah bodhisattva welas asih dalam Buddhism, dikenal sebagai Guanyin dalam bahasa Chinese dan Kannon dalam bahasa Japanese.
short_description.en: Avalokiteśvara is the bodhisattva of compassion in Buddhism, known as Guanyin in Chinese and Kannon in Japanese.

long_description.id:
Avalokiteśvara dipahami sebagai bodhisattva welas asih. Dalam penuturan Lotus Sutra, ia mendengar mereka yang memanggil namanya saat menderita dan menolong mereka dari bahaya seperti api dan banjir. Bab itu juga mengaitkannya dengan bantuan mengatasi keserakahan, amarah, dan ketidaktahuan.

Sumber tersebut menggambarkan kemampuannya menampakkan diri dalam banyak wujud sesuai kebutuhan makhluk; salah satu uraian menyebut tiga puluh tiga bentuk. Sebuah museum mencatat gambaran Lokeshvara berlengan sepuluh, sedangkan nama Guanyin dan Kannon dipakai dalam bahasa Chinese dan Japanese.

Sebuah museum menjelaskan bahwa gambar di Tibet dan Nepal lama menampilkan Avalokiteśvara sebagai laki-laki; di China, Guanyin mulai ditampilkan sebagai perempuan sekitar abad kedua belas. Dalam tradisi China ia juga dikenal sebagai pelindung ibu dan pelaut. Perbedaan ini merupakan variasi penggambaran lintas daerah, bukan sosok yang harus disamakan dalam semua rinciannya.
long_description.en:
Avalokiteśvara is understood as the bodhisattva of compassion. In an account of the Lotus Sutra, the bodhisattva hears those who call during suffering and delivers them from dangers such as fire and floods. The chapter also links this compassion with overcoming greed, anger, and ignorance.

The source describes the bodhisattva appearing in many forms suited to different beings; one account names thirty-three forms. An art museum account records a ten-armed Lokeshvara image, while Guanyin and Kannon are names used in Chinese and Japanese.

A museum describes Avalokiteśvara as male in art from Tibet and Nepal, while Guanyin began to be shown as female in China around the 12th century. In China Guanyin also became a patron of mothers and sailors. These are regional forms whose details vary across traditions.

description.id: Ia dikisahkan mendengar dan menolong mereka yang memanggil namanya dalam penderitaan.
description.en: He is said to hear and help those who call his name while suffering.

description.id: Ia dapat menampakkan diri dalam berbagai bentuk sesuai kebutuhan makhluk.
description.en: He can appear in many forms suited to the needs of beings.

short_description.id: Baal adalah dewa cuaca dan kesuburan, terutama hujan dan badai, yang kisahnya terekam di Ugarit.
short_description.en: Baal is a Canaanite storm, rain and fertility god whose stories were recorded at Ugarit.

long_description.id:
Baal, juga disebut Baal Hadad, dikaitkan dengan hujan, badai, dan kesuburan. Sebutan Baal juga bermakna penguasa dan dipakai bagi lebih dari satu dewa. Lempeng bertulis dari Ugarit menjadi sumber utama kisahnya; dalam sumber itu ia disebut putra El dan bertakhta di Gunung Zaphon.

Pada sebuah prasasti, Baal membawa gada dan petir serta mengenakan helm bertanduk. Siklus kisahnya menampilkan pertarungan dengan Yamm, dewa laut, dan perselisihan dengan Mot, dewa kematian. Anat ikut berperan menghadapi Mot. Karena ada tafsir berbeda tentang apakah Baal sungguh mati dan hidup kembali, kisah itu perlu dibaca sebagai tradisi dengan perdebatan penafsiran.

Sebagai dewa yang membawa hujan, Baal digambarkan menjaga kesuburan tanah dan dapat dipanggil penunggang awan. Dalam kisah tentang Mot, ketiadaan Baal dikaitkan dengan tanah yang menjadi tandus. Sebutan dan perannya berubah menurut tradisi setempat, sehingga setiap nama Baal tidak otomatis menunjuk figur yang sama.
long_description.en:
Baal, also called Baal Hadad, is linked to rain, storms and fertility. His name also means lord and was used for more than one god. Tablets from Ugarit preserve his stories; he is called El’s son and placed on Mount Zaphon.

A stele shows Baal with a mace, thunderbolt and horned helmet. His cycle includes conflict with Yamm, god of the sea, and Mot, god of death; Anat also confronts Mot. Interpretations differ over whether Baal actually dies and returns to life.

As a rain god, Baal brings fertility and can be called rider of the clouds. In the story of Mot, Baal’s absence leaves the land barren. His title was applied across local traditions and does not always identify the same figure.

long_description.id: Baal, juga disebut Baal Hadad, dikaitkan dengan hujan, badai, dan kesuburan. Sebutan Baal juga bermakna penguasa dan dipakai bagi lebih dari satu dewa. Lempeng bertulis dari Ugarit menjadi sumber utama kisahnya; dalam sumber itu ia disebut putra El dan bertakhta di Gunung Zaphon.
long_description.en: Baal, also called Baal Hadad, is linked to rain, storms and fertility. His name also means lord and was used for more than one god. Tablets from Ugarit preserve his stories; he is called El’s son and placed on Mount Zaphon.

long_description.id: Pada sebuah prasasti, Baal membawa gada dan petir serta mengenakan helm bertanduk. Siklus kisahnya menampilkan pertarungan dengan Yamm, dewa laut, dan perselisihan dengan Mot, dewa kematian. Anat ikut berperan menghadapi Mot. Karena ada tafsir berbeda tentang apakah Baal sungguh mati dan hidup kembali, kisah itu perlu dibaca sebagai tradisi dengan perdebatan penafsiran.
long_description.en: A stele shows Baal with a mace, thunderbolt and horned helmet. His cycle includes conflict with Yamm, god of the sea, and Mot, god of death; Anat also confronts Mot. Interpretations differ over whether Baal actually dies and returns to life.

long_description.id: Sebagai dewa yang membawa hujan, Baal digambarkan menjaga kesuburan tanah dan dapat dipanggil penunggang awan. Dalam kisah tentang Mot, ketiadaan Baal dikaitkan dengan tanah yang menjadi tandus. Sebutan dan perannya berubah menurut tradisi setempat, sehingga setiap nama Baal tidak otomatis menunjuk figur yang sama.
long_description.en: As a rain god, Baal brings fertility and can be called rider of the clouds. In the story of Mot, Baal’s absence leaves the land barren. His title was applied across local traditions and does not always identify the same figure.

note.id: Baal mengalahkan Yamm dalam kisah pertarungan laut.

note.id: Mot menjadi lawan Baal dalam siklus kisahnya.
note.en: Mot opposes Baal in the myth cycle.

short_description.id: Bes adalah dewa Mesir pelindung rumah tangga, ibu, anak, dan kelahiran.
short_description.en: Bes is an Egyptian deity protecting households, mothers, children and childbirth.

long_description.id:
Bes adalah dewa Mesir pelindung rumah tangga, ibu, anak, dan kelahiran. Beset adalah pasangan femininnya. Pemujaannya menyebar ke Siria dan Kepulauan Balearik.

Ia menjaga anak dan menghadapi roh jahat saat perempuan melahirkan. Berbeda dari kebanyakan dewa Mesir, gambarnya menghadap depan. Patungnya dipasang di rumah sebagai perlindungan terhadap setan. Bes juga mewakili musik, tari, dan kenikmatan seksual. Gambarnya terdapat pada masker, jimat, botol bayi, dan pisau magis.

Ruangan Saqqara bergambar Bes dan Beset dikaitkan dengan ritual penyembuhan. Gambar Bes ditemukan di Susa dan Asia Tengah. Bes digambarkan berjanggut, bertelinga besar, berkaki bengkok, dan menggoyang alat bunyi. Sumber ini menyebut Taweret sebagai pasangannya. Perabot, cermin, dan gagang pisau rumah tangga memuat gambarnya. Mackenzie menyebut orakel Bes di Abydos masih dikenal pada masa Romawi. Dalam uraian Mackenzie, Bes mengoyak ular yang menyerang dewa anak.
long_description.en:
Bes is an Egyptian deity protecting households, mothers, children and childbirth. Beset is his feminine counterpart. His worship spreads to Syria and the Balearic Islands.

He watches over children and fights evil spirits during childbirth. Unlike most Egyptian gods, his image faces forward. His statue is placed in homes for protection against demons. Bes also symbolizes music, dance and sexual pleasure. His image occurs on masks, amulets, infant bottles and magical knives.

Rooms at Saqqara showing Bes and Beset are associated with healing rituals. Images of Bes are found at Susa and in Central Asia. Bes is shown bearded, large-eared, bow-legged and shaking a rattle. This source names Taweret as his consort. Household furniture, mirrors and knife handles bear his image. Mackenzie states that Bes’s oracle at Abydos is still known in Roman times. In Mackenzie’s account, Bes tears apart serpents attacking the child god.

short_description.id: Circe adalah dewi dan penyihir yang mengubah manusia menjadi hewan dalam kisah perjalanan Odysseus.
short_description.en: Circe is a goddess and sorceress who transforms people into animals in the story of Odysseus.

long_description.id:
Circe adalah putri Helios dan Perseis yang tinggal di pulau Aeaea. Ia mengenal ramuan dan tanaman serta dapat mengubah manusia menjadi hewan. Penggambaran dirinya mencakup dewi bersuara manusia dan penyihir dengan kekuatan sihir; dalam kisah Odysseus ia mengubah beberapa awak kapal menjadi babi.

Hermes memberi Odysseus tanaman moly sehingga ia dapat melawan sihir Circe. Setelah awak kapal dipulihkan, mereka tinggal bersama Circe selama setahun. Ia kemudian memberi petunjuk menuju Tiresias di dunia bawah dan memperingatkan tentang Sirens. Kisah lain menghubungkannya dengan perubahan Scylla menjadi monster laut.

Sumber kuno tidak satu suara tentang keturunannya: beberapa menyebut Telegonus, Agrius, dan Latinus, sementara yang lain hanya Telegonus. Theoi juga mencatat versi silsilah yang menjadikannya putri Hyperion dan Aerope. Ragam ini memperlihatkan bahwa rincian keluarganya bergantung pada tradisi yang dikutip.
long_description.en:
Circe is the daughter of Helios and Perseis, living on Aeaea. She knows potions and herbs and can turn people into animals. Accounts call her a goddess with a human voice and a sorceress; in Odysseus’ tale she changes crew members into pigs.

Hermes gives Odysseus the herb moly to resist Circe. After the crew is restored, they stay with her for a year. She then directs him toward Tiresias in the underworld and warns him about the Sirens. Another story links her to Scylla’s transformation into a sea monster.

Ancient accounts differ on her children: some name Telegonus, Agrius and Latinus, while others name only Telegonus. Theoi also records a genealogy making her the daughter of Hyperion and Aerope. The details depend on the cited tradition.

short_description.id: Circe adalah dewi dan penyihir yang mengubah manusia menjadi hewan dalam kisah perjalanan Odysseus.
short_description.en: Circe is a goddess and sorceress who transforms people into animals in the story of Odysseus.

long_description.id: Circe adalah putri Helios dan Perseis yang tinggal di pulau Aeaea. Ia mengenal ramuan dan tanaman serta dapat mengubah manusia menjadi hewan. Penggambaran dirinya mencakup dewi bersuara manusia dan penyihir dengan kekuatan sihir; dalam kisah Odysseus ia mengubah beberapa awak kapal menjadi babi.
long_description.en: Circe is the daughter of Helios and Perseis, living on Aeaea. She knows potions and herbs and can turn people into animals. Accounts call her a goddess with a human voice and a sorceress; in Odysseus’ tale she changes crew members into pigs.

long_description.id: Hermes memberi Odysseus tanaman moly sehingga ia dapat melawan sihir Circe. Setelah awak kapal dipulihkan, mereka tinggal bersama Circe selama setahun. Ia kemudian memberi petunjuk menuju Tiresias di dunia bawah dan memperingatkan tentang Sirens. Kisah lain menghubungkannya dengan perubahan Scylla menjadi monster laut.
long_description.en: Hermes gives Odysseus the herb moly to resist Circe. After the crew is restored, they stay with her for a year. She then directs him toward Tiresias in the underworld and warns him about the Sirens. Another story links her to Scylla’s transformation into a sea monster.

long_description.id: Sumber kuno tidak satu suara tentang keturunannya: beberapa menyebut Telegonus, Agrius, dan Latinus, sementara yang lain hanya Telegonus. Theoi juga mencatat versi silsilah yang menjadikannya putri Hyperion dan Aerope. Ragam ini memperlihatkan bahwa rincian keluarganya bergantung pada tradisi yang dikutip.
long_description.en: Ancient accounts differ on her children: some name Telegonus, Agrius and Latinus, while others name only Telegonus. Theoi also records a genealogy making her the daughter of Hyperion and Aerope. The details depend on the cited tradition.

short_description.id: Devi adalah istilah Sanskerta untuk dewi dalam agama India.
short_description.en: Devi is the Sanskrit term for a goddess in Indian religions.

long_description.id:
Devi adalah istilah Sanskerta untuk dewi dalam agama India. Pasangan istilah maskulinnya adalah Deva.

Tradisi Shaktisme berpusat pada Devi. Literatur Purana abad pertengahan memperluas kisah Devi, termasuk Devi Mahatmya. Devi Mahatmya memujanya sebagai kebenaran tertinggi dan daya utama. Devi dan Deva dijelaskan mengacu pada yang ilahi, luhur, dan bersinar. Bhagavati menjadi sebutan kehormatan dewi seperti Lakshmi dan Durga. Artikel menghubungkan Devisukta dengan Rigveda 10.125. Weda menyebut Prithvi, Aditi, Vac, Ratri, dan Aranyani sebagai sejumlah dewi kosmis. Dalam tradisi Shakta Devi adalah sosok tertinggi; tradisi Smarta memasukkannya dalam lima bentuk utama Brahman. Tradisi lain menekankan daya aktif dewi yang melengkapi dewa pasangan. Devi Upanishad mengajarkan Shakti sebagai Brahman serta asal materi dan kesadaran. Dalam Devi Upanishad, Devi menyatakan dirinya pencipta bumi dan langit serta kesadaran tak terbatas. WHE menjelaskan sisi Uma yang ramah dan sisi Durga yang menakutkan sebagai penggambaran Devi berbeda. Pembicara perempuan dalam Rigveda 10.125 menyebut dirinya Ratu dan penghimpun harta yang layak dipuja.
long_description.en:
Devi is the Sanskrit term for a goddess in Indian religions. Its masculine counterpart is Deva.

Shaktism centres on Devi. Medieval Puranic literature expands Devi narratives, including the Devi Mahatmya. The Devi Mahatmya reveres her as ultimate truth and supreme power. Devi and Deva are explained as referring to the divine, exalted, and shining. Bhagavati is an honorific for goddesses such as Lakshmi and Durga. The article connects the Devisukta with Rigveda 10.125. The Vedas name Prithvi, Aditi, Vac, Ratri, and Aranyani among cosmic goddesses. In Shakta tradition Devi is supreme; Smarta tradition includes her among five primary forms of Brahman. Other traditions emphasise the goddess's active power complementing her divine partner. The Devi Upanishad teaches Shakti as Brahman and the origin of matter and consciousness. In the Devi Upanishad, Devi declares herself creator of earth and heaven and infinite consciousness. WHE explains benevolent Uma and fearsome Durga as different depictions of Devi. The female speaker in Rigveda 10.125 calls herself Queen and gatherer of treasures worthy of worship.

claims_provenance.quote:
Devi and deva are Sanskrit terms found in Vedic literature around the 3rd millennium BCE. Deva is masculine, and the related feminine equivalent is devi. Monier-Williams translates it as 'heavenly, divine, terrestrial things of high excellence, exalted, shining ones'.
Etymologically, a cognate of devi is Latin dea. When capitalised, Devi maata refers to the mother goddess in Hinduism.

claim.en: Bhagavati is an honorific for goddesses such as Lakshmi and Durga.

claims_provenance.quote: A synonym for the word Devi in the Vedas is Bhagavati. Bhagavatī (Devanagari: भगवती, IAST: Bhagavatī), is an Indian epithet of Sanskrit origin, used as an honorific title for goddesses in Hinduism and Buddhism. In Hinduism, it is primarily used to address the goddesses Lakshmi and Durga. In Buddhism, it is used to refer to several Mahayana Buddhist female deities, like Cundā.

claim.en: The Vedas name Prithvi, Aditi, Vac, Ratri, and Aranyani among cosmic goddesses.

claims_provenance.quote: The Vedas name numerous cosmic goddesses such as Prithvi (earth), Aditi (cosmic moral order), Vāc (sound), Nirṛti (destruction), Ratri (night) and Aranyani (forest); bounty goddesses such as Dinsana, Raka, Puramdhi, Parendi, Bharati and Mahi are among others are mentioned in the Rigveda. However, the goddesses are not discussed as frequently as gods (devas).

claim.id: Dalam tradisi Shakta Devi adalah sosok tertinggi; tradisi Smarta memasukkannya dalam lima bentuk utama Brahman.
claim.en: In Shakta tradition Devi is supreme; Smarta tradition includes her among five primary forms of Brahman.

claims_provenance.quote: Devi is the supreme being in the Shakta tradition of Hinduism; in the Smarta tradition, she is one of the five primary forms of Brahman that is revered. In other Hindu traditions, Devi embodies the active energy and power of Deva, and they always appear together complementing each other.

claim.id: Tradisi lain menekankan daya aktif dewi yang melengkapi dewa pasangan.

claim.id: Devi Upanishad mengajarkan Shakti sebagai Brahman serta asal materi dan kesadaran.
claim.en: The Devi Upanishad teaches Shakti as Brahman and the origin of matter and consciousness.

claims_provenance.quote: Devi-inspired philosophy is propounded in many Hindu texts such as the Devi Upanishad, which teaches that Shakti is essentially Brahman (ultimate metaphysical Reality) and that from her arises prakṛti (matter) and purusha (consciousness) and that she is bliss and non-bliss, the Vedas and what is different from it, the born and the unborn and all of the universe.

claim.id: Dalam Devi Upanishad, Devi menyatakan dirinya pencipta bumi dan langit serta kesadaran tak terbatas.
claim.en: In the Devi Upanishad, Devi declares herself creator of earth and heaven and infinite consciousness.

claims_provenance.quote: Devi asserts that she is the creator of earth and heaven and resides there. ... She is, states Devi, the eternal and infinite consciousness engulfing earth and heaven, and 'all forms of bliss and non-bliss, knowledge and ignorance, Brahman and Non-Brahman'.

claim.id: WHE menjelaskan sisi Uma yang ramah dan sisi Durga yang menakutkan sebagai penggambaran Devi berbeda.
claim.en: WHE explains benevolent Uma and fearsome Durga as different depictions of Devi.

claims_provenance.quote: Devi's character has two opposing sides represented by various separate female deities: as Uma, the benevolent, and as Durga, the terrible.

short_description.id: Naga (dragon) adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya, berbentuk kurang lebih seperti ular dengan ciri hewan lain; di Asia Timur ia dianggap baik dan pembawa hujan, dalam tradisi Barat ia penyembur api.
short_description.en: The dragon is a mythical creature of the folklore of many cultures, roughly serpentine with features of other animals; in East Asia it is seen as benevolent and a rain-bringer, in Western tradition as a fire-breather.

long_description.id:
Naga adalah makhluk mitos yang ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya di seluruh dunia. Bentuknya kurang lebih seperti ular, sering dengan ciri dari hewan lain seperti sayap dan cakar, dan dalam hampir semua budaya ia dipandang sebagai makhluk yang kuat dan menggetarkan.

Makhluk mirip naga sudah muncul dalam seni Mesopotamia kuno, kadang bermusuhan kadang baik hati. Di Asia Timur naga umumnya dianggap makhluk baik: naga Tiongkok dipercaya menguasai hujan, laut, dan air, dan sejak dinasti Han menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar. Drakon Yunani kuno adalah ular besar bersifat gaib yang dalam mitos dikalahkan pahlawan atau dewa, sedangkan dalam pemujaan ia sosok lembut yang dikaitkan dengan penyembuhan dan kekayaan. Dalam tradisi Barat, naga digambarkan menyemburkan api dan melambangkan kejahatan serta kematian.

Menurut World History Encyclopedia, naga Tiongkok paling sering digambarkan sebagai makhluk raksasa yang lentur, berdiam di sumber air atau awan, dan bila terbang disertai kilat dan guntur. Deskripsi tradisional memberinya tanduk rusa jantan, dahi unta, leher ular, sisik ikan mas, dan cakar elang, dan ia dapat mengubah bentuk serta ukurannya sesuka hati. Petani kuno menganggapnya pembawa hujan, sehingga di desa-desa diadakan tarian naga untuk memohon hujan, dan menurut keyakinan tradisional tiap Empat Laut dipimpin seorang raja naga.

Berbeda dari budaya lain tempat naga biasanya dibunuh pahlawan, naga di Tiongkok umumnya dipandang adil dan baik hati. Bagi banyak orang kaisar adalah penjelmaan naga pembawa hujan, naga menjadi shio kelima dalam zodiak, dan sebuah mitos menyebut naga membantu Yu Agung mengendalikan banjir. Penggambaran naga tertua yang diketahui adalah figur giok berbentuk C dari budaya Hongshan, berusia antara 4500 dan 3000 SM.

Dalam puisi Beowulf, terjemahan J. Lesslie Hall, naga api digambarkan terbang berapi-api ke gundukan makam pada malam hari, dan penghancur bangsa-bangsa itu menguasai balai hartanya selama tiga ratus musim dingin. Naga itu menyemburkan api untuk membakar balai megah, dan dalam puisi yang sama Sigmund memperoleh kemuliaan karena menghancurkan seekor naga penjaga harta. Perairan yang digambarkan puisi itu juga dipenuhi ular dan naga-danau.

Kata dragon masuk ke bahasa Inggris pada awal abad ke-13 dari bahasa Prancis Kuno, dari bahasa Latin draco, yang berasal dari bahasa Yunani drákōn, ular. Kata Yunani itu kemungkinan berasal dari kata kerja dérkomai, melihat, yang mungkin merujuk pada tatapan maut atau mata tajam. Naga juga muncul dalam karya fiksi modern, antara lain karya J. R. R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin, dan George R. R. Martin.
long_description.en:
The dragon is a mythical creature found in the folklore of cultures worldwide. It is roughly serpentine, often with features drawn from other animals such as wings and claws, and in nearly all cultures it is seen as a powerful, awe-inspiring creature.

Creatures resembling dragons already appear in the art of ancient Mesopotamia, sometimes as foes and sometimes as friends. In East Asia dragons were mostly seen as benevolent: Chinese dragons were believed to rule over rain, seas and other waters, and from Han times they stood for the emperor's authority. Ancient Greek drakontes were huge snakes with uncanny powers, slain by gods or heroes in myth yet gentle bringers of healing and riches in worship. Western tradition, by contrast, pictures dragons breathing fire and standing for evil and death.

According to the World History Encyclopedia, the Chinese dragon is most often pictured as a giant, lithe creature living in water sources or clouds, flying amid lightning and thunder. The traditional description lends it a stag's horns, a camel's forehead, a snake's neck, a carp's scales and an eagle's claws, and it can alter its shape and size at will. Ancient farmers saw it as a bringer of rain, so villages held dragon dances to ask for rain, and by traditional belief each of the Four Seas has a dragon king.

Unlike other cultures where the dragon is typically slain by a hero, the dragon in China was usually regarded as just and benevolent. For many the emperor was an incarnation of the rain-bringing dragon, the dragon is the fifth sign of the zodiac, and one myth has a dragon helping Yu the Great control the floods. The earliest known depiction of a dragon is a C-shaped jade figure of the Hongshan culture, dated between 4500 and 3000 BCE.

In the poem Beowulf, in J. Lesslie Hall's translation, the fire-dragon is described as flying flaming to the barrows by night, and the waster of peoples held its hoard-hall for three hundred winters. The dragon spits fire to burn the great manor, and in the same poem Sigmund wins glory by destroying a hoard-guarding dragon. The waters it describes are also filled with serpents and mere-dragons.

The word dragon reached English in the early 13th century by way of Old French and Latin draco from Greek drákōn, serpent. The Greek term probably grew from the verb dérkomai, to see, perhaps alluding to a lethal stare or piercing eyes. Dragons also loom large in modern fantasy, not least in the books of J. R. R. Tolkien, of Ursula K. Le Guin and of George R. R. Martin.

claims_provenance.quote: The earliest known depiction of a dragon is a stylised C-shaped representation carved in jade. Found in eastern Inner Mongolia, it belonged to the Hongshan culture, which thrived between 4500 and 3000 BCE.

claim.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia (in its article on the dragon in ancient China), folk-tales tell of a race of dragons led by their Dragon-king Lung-Wang; they have scaly bodies, four legs and horns, could take human form and whisk away young girls, and are similar to the Nagas, the snake-like creatures of Hindu folklore that protect water sources.

claims_provenance.quote: In folk-tales, there was a race of dragons led by their Dragon-king Lung-Wang. short_description.id: Naga (dragon) adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya, berbentuk kurang lebih seperti ular dengan ciri hewan lain; di Asia Timur ia dianggap baik dan pembawa hujan, dalam tradisi Barat ia penyembur api.
short_description.en: The dragon is a mythical creature of the folklore of many cultures, roughly serpentine with features of other animals; in East Asia it is seen as benevolent and a rain-bringer, in Western tradition as a fire-breather.

long_description.id: Naga adalah makhluk mitos yang ditemukan dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya di seluruh dunia. Bentuknya kurang lebih seperti ular, sering dengan ciri dari hewan lain seperti sayap dan cakar, dan dalam hampir semua budaya ia dipandang sebagai makhluk yang kuat dan menggetarkan.
long_description.en: The dragon is a mythical creature found in the folklore of cultures worldwide. It is roughly serpentine, often with features drawn from other animals such as wings and claws, and in nearly all cultures it is seen as a powerful, awe-inspiring creature.

long_description.id: Makhluk mirip naga sudah muncul dalam seni Mesopotamia kuno, kadang bermusuhan kadang baik hati. Di Asia Timur naga umumnya dianggap makhluk baik: naga Tiongkok dipercaya menguasai hujan, laut, dan air, dan sejak dinasti Han menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar. Drakon Yunani kuno adalah ular besar bersifat gaib yang dalam mitos dikalahkan pahlawan atau dewa, sedangkan dalam pemujaan ia sosok lembut yang dikaitkan dengan penyembuhan dan kekayaan. Dalam tradisi Barat, naga digambarkan menyemburkan api dan melambangkan kejahatan serta kematian.
long_description.en: Creatures resembling dragons already appear in the art of ancient Mesopotamia, sometimes as foes and sometimes as friends. In East Asia dragons were mostly seen as benevolent: Chinese dragons were believed to rule over rain, seas and other waters, and from Han times they stood for the emperor's authority. Ancient Greek drakontes were huge snakes with uncanny powers, slain by gods or heroes in myth yet gentle bringers of healing and riches in worship. Western tradition, by contrast, pictures dragons breathing fire and standing for evil and death.

long_description.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, naga Tiongkok paling sering digambarkan sebagai makhluk raksasa yang lentur, berdiam di sumber air atau awan, dan bila terbang disertai kilat dan guntur. Deskripsi tradisional memberinya tanduk rusa jantan, dahi unta, leher ular, sisik ikan mas, dan cakar elang, dan ia dapat mengubah bentuk serta ukurannya sesuka hati. Petani kuno menganggapnya pembawa hujan, sehingga di desa-desa diadakan tarian naga untuk memohon hujan, dan menurut keyakinan tradisional tiap Empat Laut dipimpin seorang raja naga.
long_description.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the Chinese dragon is most often pictured as a giant, lithe creature living in water sources or clouds, flying amid lightning and thunder. The traditional description lends it a stag's horns, a camel's forehead, a snake's neck, a carp's scales and an eagle's claws, and it can alter its shape and size at will. Ancient farmers saw it as a bringer of rain, so villages held dragon dances to ask for rain, and by traditional belief each of the Four Seas has a dragon king.

long_description.id: Berbeda dari budaya lain tempat naga biasanya dibunuh pahlawan, naga di Tiongkok umumnya dipandang adil dan baik hati. Bagi banyak orang kaisar adalah penjelmaan naga pembawa hujan, naga menjadi shio kelima dalam zodiak, dan sebuah mitos menyebut naga membantu Yu Agung mengendalikan banjir. Penggambaran naga tertua yang diketahui adalah figur giok berbentuk C dari budaya Hongshan, berusia antara 4500 dan 3000 SM.
long_description.en: Unlike other cultures where the dragon is typically slain by a hero, the dragon in China was usually regarded as just and benevolent. For many the emperor was an incarnation of the rain-bringing dragon, the dragon is the fifth sign of the zodiac, and one myth has a dragon helping Yu the Great control the floods. The earliest known depiction of a dragon is a C-shaped jade figure of the Hongshan culture, dated between 4500 and 3000 BCE.

long_description.id: Dalam puisi Beowulf, terjemahan J. Lesslie Hall, naga api digambarkan terbang berapi-api ke gundukan makam pada malam hari, dan penghancur bangsa-bangsa itu menguasai balai hartanya selama tiga ratus musim dingin. Naga itu menyemburkan api untuk membakar balai megah, dan dalam puisi yang sama Sigmund memperoleh kemuliaan karena menghancurkan seekor naga penjaga harta. Perairan yang digambarkan puisi itu juga dipenuhi ular dan naga-danau.
long_description.en: In the poem Beowulf, in J. Lesslie Hall's translation, the fire-dragon is described as flying flaming to the barrows by night, and the waster of peoples held its hoard-hall for three hundred winters. The dragon spits fire to burn the great manor, and in the same poem Sigmund wins glory by destroying a hoard-guarding dragon. The waters it describes are also filled with serpents and mere-dragons.

long_description.id: Kata dragon masuk ke bahasa Inggris pada awal abad ke-13 dari bahasa Prancis Kuno, dari bahasa Latin draco, yang berasal dari bahasa Yunani drákōn, ular. Kata Yunani itu kemungkinan berasal dari kata kerja dérkomai, melihat, yang mungkin merujuk pada tatapan maut atau mata tajam. Naga juga muncul dalam karya fiksi modern, antara lain karya J. R. R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin, dan George R. R. Martin.
long_description.en: The word dragon reached English in the early 13th century by way of Old French and Latin draco from Greek drákōn, serpent. The Greek term probably grew from the verb dérkomai, to see, perhaps alluding to a lethal stare or piercing eyes. Dragons also loom large in modern fantasy, not least in the books of J. R. R. Tolkien, of Ursula K. Le Guin and of George R. R. Martin.

claims.quote: A dragon is a mythical creature found in the folklore of cultures throughout the world. It is roughly serpentine in form, and often possesses features drawn from different animals, such as wings and claws. In nearly all cultures, it is conceived of as a powerful and awe-inspiring creature.

statement.id: Naga adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat berbagai budaya di dunia, berbentuk kurang lebih seperti ular dengan ciri hewan lain seperti sayap dan cakar, dan dipandang kuat serta menggetarkan.
statement.en: The dragon is a mythical creature of folklore worldwide, roughly serpentine with features like wings and claws, seen as powerful and awe-inspiring.

claims.quote: Dragon-like creatures appear in ancient Mesopotamian art, where they could be hostile or benevolent. In East Asia, dragons were usually regarded as positive beings; Chinese dragons were thought to govern the rain, the sea, and other forms of water, and from the Han dynasty onwards they were emblems of imperial power.

statement.id: Makhluk mirip naga muncul dalam seni Mesopotamia kuno; di Asia Timur naga umumnya makhluk baik, naga Tiongkok menguasai hujan, laut, dan air, dan sejak dinasti Han menjadi lambang kekuasaan kaisar.
statement.en: Dragon-like creatures appear in ancient Mesopotamian art; in East Asia dragons were usually positive, Chinese dragons governed rain, sea and water, and from the Han dynasty were imperial emblems.

claims.quote: Ancient Greek drakontes were large serpents endowed with supernatural qualities; in myth they were defeated by heroes or gods, whereas in cult they were gentle figures associated with healing and wealth. In the Western tradition, dragons have been depicted as fire-breathing embodiments of evil, associated with death.

statement.id: Drakon Yunani kuno adalah ular besar bersifat gaib yang dikalahkan pahlawan atau dewa dalam mitos tetapi dalam pemujaan dikaitkan dengan penyembuhan dan kekayaan; dalam tradisi Barat naga menyemburkan api dan melambangkan kejahatan serta kematian.
statement.en: Ancient Greek drakontes were supernatural serpents defeated by heroes or gods in myth but linked to healing and wealth in cult; in the Western tradition dragons are fire-breathing embodiments of evil and death.

claims.quote: The word dragon entered the English language in the early 13th century from Old French dragon, which, in turn, comes from Latin draco (genitive draconis), meaning "huge serpent, dragon", from Ancient Greek: δράκων, drákōn (genitive δράκοντος, drákontos) "serpent".

statement.id: Kata dragon masuk ke bahasa Inggris pada awal abad ke-13 dari bahasa Prancis Kuno, dari Latin draco ('ular besar'), dari Yunani Kuno δράκων (drákōn), 'ular'.
statement.en: The word dragon entered English in the early 13th century from Old French, from Latin draco ('huge serpent'), from Ancient Greek δράκων (drákōn), 'serpent'.

claims.quote: The Greek word δράκων is most likely derived from the Greek verb δέρκομαι (dérkomai) meaning "I see"

statement.id: Kata Yunani δράκων kemungkinan berasal dari kata kerja δέρκομαι (dérkomai), 'aku melihat', yang mungkin merujuk pada tatapan maut atau mata tajam.
statement.en: The Greek δράκων most likely derives from the verb δέρκομαι (dérkomai), 'I see', perhaps referring to a deadly glance or sharp eyes.

claims.quote: Dragons have featured in works of modern fiction by writers such as J. R. R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin, and George R. R. Martin.

statement.id: Naga muncul dalam karya fiksi modern penulis seperti J. R. R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin, dan George R. R. Martin.
statement.en: Dragons feature in modern fiction by writers such as J. R. R. Tolkien, Ursula K. Le Guin and George R. R. Martin.

claims.quote: One of the earliest creatures to appear in the tales and legends of ancient China, the dragon is most often depicted as a giant and lithe beast which dwells in either water sources or clouds. The Chinese dragon is extraordinarily powerful, and when it flies, it is usually accompanied by lightning and thunder.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, naga Tiongkok paling sering digambarkan sebagai makhluk raksasa yang lentur dan berdiam di sumber air atau awan; ia amat kuat, dan bila terbang biasanya disertai kilat dan guntur.
statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the Chinese dragon is most often depicted as a giant, lithe beast dwelling in water sources or clouds; it is extraordinarily powerful and, when it flies, is usually accompanied by lightning and thunder.

claims.quote: The traditional description gives it the horns of a stag, the forehead of a camel, the eyes of a demon, the neck of a snake, the belly of a sea-monster, the scales of a carp, the claws of an eagle, the pads of a tiger, and the ears of an ox.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, deskripsi tradisional naga Tiongkok memberinya tanduk rusa jantan, dahi unta, mata iblis, leher ular, perut makhluk laut, sisik ikan mas, cakar elang, telapak harimau, dan telinga sapi.
statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the traditional description of the Chinese dragon gives it the horns of a stag, forehead of a camel, eyes of a demon, neck of a snake, belly of a sea-monster, scales of a carp, claws of an eagle, pads of a tiger and ears of an ox.

claims.quote: Other qualities of the dragon were that it could change its shape and size at will and disappear or reappear wherever it wished.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, naga Tiongkok dipercaya dapat mengubah bentuk dan ukurannya sesuka hati serta menghilang atau muncul di mana pun ia mau.
statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the Chinese dragon was believed able to change its shape and size at will and to disappear or reappear wherever it wished.

claims.quote: Despite the dragon's fearsome aspect, it was not usually seen as the bad-intentioned monster that inhabits the myths of other cultures around the world where it is typically slain by a brave hero figure. Indeed, in China, the dragon was and is regarded as being a just and benevolent creature.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, meski tampak menakutkan, naga di Tiongkok umumnya tidak dipandang sebagai monster jahat seperti dalam mitos budaya lain yang biasanya menampilkannya dibunuh pahlawan, melainkan makhluk yang adil dan baik hati.
statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, despite its fearsome aspect the dragon in China was not usually seen as the bad-intentioned monster of other cultures' myths, where it is typically slain by a hero, but as a just and benevolent creature.

claims.quote: Further, ancient farmers thought dragons brought much-needed rains and water to aid their crops. Dragons were also thought responsible for strong winds, hailstorms, thunder, lightning, and tornadoes

statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, ancient farmers thought dragons brought the rain and water their crops needed, and dragons were also held responsible for strong winds, hailstorms, thunder, lightning and tornadoes.

claims.quote: In rural communities, there was a dragon dance to induce the creature's generosity in dispensing rain and a procession where a large figure of a dragon made from paper or cloth spread over a wooden frame was carried.

statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, rural communities in China held a dragon dance to induce the creature's generosity in dispensing rain, and a procession carrying a large dragon figure of paper or cloth over a wooden frame.

claims.quote: Another traditional belief was that the Four Seas of the world (to the ancient Chinese there were four and not seven) were each presided over by a dragon king.

statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, for many people the emperor was actually an incarnation of the supreme rain-bringing dragon.

claims.quote: The earliest known depiction of a dragon is a stylised C-shaped representation carved in jade. Found in eastern Inner Mongolia, it belonged to the Hongshan culture, which thrived between 4500 and 3000 BCE.

statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia, the earliest known depiction of a dragon is a stylised C-shaped figure carved in jade, found in eastern Inner Mongolia and belonging to the Hongshan culture, which thrived between 4500 and 3000 BCE.

claims.quote: In folk-tales, there was a race of dragons led by their Dragon-king Lung-Wang. With scaly bodies, four legs, and horns they could take on human form and whisk away young girls. They are similar to Nagas, the snake-like creatures of Hindu folklore which protect water sources.

statement.en: According to the World History Encyclopedia (in its article on the dragon in ancient China), folk-tales tell of a race of dragons led by their Dragon-king Lung-Wang; they have scaly bodies, four legs and horns, could take human form and whisk away young girls, and are similar to the Nagas, the snake-like creatures of Hindu folklore that protect water sources.

short_description.id: Athena adalah dewi Yunani kuno yang dikaitkan dengan kebijaksanaan, peperangan, dan kerajinan, pelindung kota Athena; menurut Hesiod ia lahir dari kepala Zeus.
short_description.en: Athena is an ancient Greek goddess associated with wisdom, warfare and handicraft, patron of the city of Athens; according to Hesiod she was born from the head of Zeus.

long_description.id:
Athena atau Athene, yang sering bergelar Pallas, adalah dewi Yunani kuno yang dikaitkan dengan kebijaksanaan, peperangan, dan kerajinan, dan kemudian disamakan dengan dewi Romawi Minerva dan Menrva dari Etruria. Ia dianggap pelindung berbagai kota di Yunani, terutama kota Athena, yang kemungkinan menjadi asal namanya; para ahli kini umumnya sepakat bahwa sang dewi mengambil nama dari kota itu. Lambang utamanya adalah burung hantu, pohon zaitun, ular, dan gorgoneion, dan dalam seni ia biasanya digambarkan berhelm dan memegang tombak. Menurut World History Encyclopedia, burung hantu adalah lambang kebijaksanaan.

Parthenon di Akropolis Athena dipersembahkan kepadanya, dan festival utamanya di kota itu adalah Panathenaia, festival terpenting dalam kalender Athena. Sebagai Polias dan Poliouchos ia pelindung kota, sebagai Ergane pelindung kerajinan dan tenun, dan sebagai Promachos ia dipercaya memimpin prajurit ke medan perang. Dalam perannya sebagai Parthenos, "perawan", ia dipercaya tetap perawan selamanya.

Dalam mitologi Yunani, Athena lahir dari dahi ayahnya, Zeus; menurut Hesiod, hal itu terjadi setelah Zeus menelan Metis yang sedang mengandungnya. Sumber lain berbeda: Homer menyebutnya putri Zeus tanpa menyinggung ibunya, satu kelompok tradisi menyebutnya putri raksasa Pallas, dan tradisi yang membawa ke Libya menyebutnya putri Poseidon dan Tritonis. Dalam mitos pendirian Athena, ia mengalahkan Poseidon dalam perebutan perlindungan kota dengan menciptakan pohon zaitun pertama, sedangkan Poseidon menghasilkan kuda pertama.

Menurut theoi.com, Athena adalah dewi Olimpus kebijaksanaan dan nasihat yang baik, perang, pertahanan kota, usaha kepahlawanan, menenun, tembikar, dan berbagai kerajinan lain, digambarkan beraigis berhias wajah Gorgon Medousa. Ia membantu Perseus membunuh Gorgon, para Argonaut, dan Herakles dalam kedua belas pekerjaannya; menurut World History Encyclopedia ia juga melindungi Odysseus dan mendukung bangsa Achaea dalam Perang Troya. Dewi ini juga dikaitkan dengan hukuman, misalnya atas Arachne dan Teiresias, dan dipercaya mendirikan pengadilan kuno Areiopagus.

Menurut World History Encyclopedia, arca Athena yang paling terkenal di dunia kuno adalah arca emas dan gading karya Pheidias di Parthenon yang tingginya lebih dari 12 m. Menurut sumber lain, replika Parthenon di Nashville, Tennessee, mendapat replika Athena Parthenos setinggi empat puluh dua kaki pada 1990.
long_description.en:
Athena, also spelled Athene and often bearing the epithet Pallas, is an ancient Greek goddess tied to wisdom, warfare and crafts, later equated with the Roman Minerva and the Etruscan Menrva. Greeks looked to her as protector of many cities, Athens above all, and she most likely took her name from it; scholars now generally agree that the goddess is named after the city. Owls, olive trees, snakes and the gorgoneion are her chief emblems, and artists usually show her helmeted and holding a spear. The World History Encyclopedia calls the owl a symbol of wisdom.

The Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens is dedicated to her, and her principal festival there was the Panathenaia, the most significant event in the Athenian calendar. As Polias and Poliouchos she guards the city, as Ergane she patronises craft and weaving, and as Promachos she was believed to lead soldiers into battle. In her aspect as Parthenos, "virgin", she was believed to stay a virgin for ever.

In Greek myth Athena sprang from the brow of her father Zeus; Hesiod says this followed Zeus swallowing Metis while she carried Athena. Other sources disagree: Homer calls her Zeus's daughter without naming a mother, one set of traditions makes her the daughter of the giant Pallas, and the tradition that leads to Libya makes her the daughter of Poseidon and Tritonis. In the founding myth of Athens she defeated Poseidon in the contest over the city's patronage by creating the first olive tree, while he produced the first horse.

Theoi.com describes Athena as the Olympian goddess of wisdom and sound counsel, war, defence of towns, heroic endeavour, weaving, pottery and assorted other crafts, depicted in an aigis decorated with the face of the Gorgon Medousa. She aided Perseus against the Gorgon, the Argonauts, and Heracles in his twelve labours; the World History Encyclopedia adds that she protected Odysseus and backed the Achaeans in the Trojan War. She is also linked with punishment, as in the cases of Arachne and Teiresias, and was believed to have instituted the ancient court of the Areiopagus.

The World History Encyclopedia names Pheidias's gold and ivory statue in the Parthenon, over 12 m high, as the most celebrated image of Athena in the ancient world. Another source reports that the Parthenon replica in Nashville, Tennessee, gained a forty-two-foot replica of the Athena Parthenos in 1990.

era: A goddess of ancient Greek religion; the Panathenaia was the most important festival of the Athenian calendar.

literal_meaning.en: The plural name of the city of Athens; scholars now generally agree the goddess takes her name from the city.

who.id: Dewi kebijaksanaan, peperangan, dan kerajinan dalam agama Yunani kuno.
who.en: Goddess of wisdom, warfare and handicraft in ancient Greek religion.

origin.id: Agama Yunani kuno, terutama kota Athena, yang namanya diambil sang dewi menurut para ahli.
origin.en: Ancient Greek religion, especially the city of Athens, from which scholars say the goddess takes her name.

role.id: Pelindung kota Athena dan berbagai kota Yunani lain.
role.en: Patron and protectress of Athens and various other Greek cities.

famous_for.id: Lahir dari kepala Zeus dan menciptakan pohon zaitun pertama dalam perebutan Athena dengan Poseidon.
famous_for.en: Being born from the head of Zeus and creating the first olive tree in her contest with Poseidon for Athens.

did_you_know.id: Menurut theoi.com, dalam perebutan Athena, Athena menghasilkan pohon zaitun pertama dan Poseidon kuda pertama.
did_you_know.en: According to theoi.com, in the contest for Athens Athena produced the first olive tree and Poseidon the first horse.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology di theoi.com, kekuatan dan kebijaksanaan Athena tampak pada perannya sebagai pelindung dan penjaga negara serta lembaga-lembaga sosial. Dalam sumber yang sama ia disebut dewi yang di dalam dirinya kekuatan dan kebijaksanaan berpadu selaras. Panathenaia adalah festival terpenting dalam kalender Athena.
cultural_context.en: According to the Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology on theoi.com, Athena's power and wisdom appear in her role as protectress and preserver of the state and of social institutions, and she is described as a goddess in whom power and wisdom blend harmoniously. The Panathenaia was the most important festival of the Athenian calendar.

description.id: Menurut theoi.com, Athena adalah dewi kebijaksanaan dan nasihat yang baik; World History Encyclopedia menyebutnya mungkin yang paling bijak, paling berani, dan paling cerdik di antara dewa Olimpus.
description.en: According to theoi.com, Athena was goddess of wisdom and good counsel; the World History Encyclopedia calls her perhaps the wisest, most courageous and most resourceful of the Olympian gods.

description.id: Athena melindungi berbagai kota Yunani dan membantu pahlawan seperti Perseus, Herakles, dan Odysseus.
description.en: Athena protected various Greek cities and helped heroes such as Perseus, Heracles and Odysseus.

description.id: Athena adalah dewi perang yang dipercaya memimpin prajurit sebagai Athena Promachos dan mendukung pihak Yunani dalam Perang Troya.
description.en: Athena is a goddess of war believed to lead soldiers as Athena Promachos, and she supported the Greek side in the Trojan War.

description.id: Athena adalah pelindung kerajinan dan tenun (Ergane) dan dianggap penemu bajak dan garu.
description.en: Athena is patron of craft and weaving (Ergane) and is represented as the inventor of the plough and rake.

description.id: Menurut theoi.com, Athena mengubah Arachne menjadi laba-laba, dan menurut Ovidius ia mengubah Medusa menjadi Gorgon.
description.en: According to theoi.com Athena turned Arachne into a spider, and according to Ovid she transformed Medusa into the Gorgon.

description.id: Athena membutakan Teiresias yang melihatnya telanjang saat mandi dan menyerang kapal-kapal Yunani dengan badai karena pelanggaran terhadap kuilnya di Troya.
description.en: Athena blinded Teiresias for seeing her naked while bathing and attacked the Greek ships with a storm over the violation of her Trojan shrine.

description.id: Menurut tradisi ketiga yang dicatat Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology di theoi.com, yang membawa kita ke Libya, Athena adalah putri Poseidon dan Tritonis.
description.en: In a third tradition recorded in the Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology on theoi.com, which takes us to Libya, Athena is a daughter of Poseidon and Tritonis.

title.en: Birth from the head of Zeus

summary.id: Menurut Hesiod, Zeus menelan Metis yang sedang mengandung Athena, lalu sendiri melahirkan Athena yang melompat keluar dari kepalanya. Homer hanya menyebut Athena putri Zeus tanpa menyebut ibunya.
summary.en: According to Hesiod, Zeus swallowed Metis while she was pregnant with Athena and then gave birth to Athena himself, who sprang from his head. Homer only calls Athena a daughter of Zeus without mentioning her mother.

summary.id: Athena dan Poseidon memperebutkan perlindungan atas Athena; Athena menang dengan menciptakan pohon zaitun pertama, sedangkan Poseidon menghasilkan kuda pertama.
summary.en: Athena and Poseidon contested for patronage of Athens; Athena won by creating the first olive tree, while Poseidon produced the first horse.

summary.id: Menurut theoi.com, dalam Perang Para Raksasa Athena mengubur Enceladus di bawah Gunung Etna dan membuat aigisnya dari kulit Pallas.
summary.en: Theoi.com reports that during the War of the Giants Athena covered Enceladus with Mount Etna and fashioned her aigis from the hide of Pallas.

summary.id: Athena meminjamkan Perseus perisai perunggunya agar ia dapat melihat bayangan Medusa tanpa menjadi batu, dan Perseus memberinya kepala Gorgon yang menghiasi aigisnya.
summary.en: Athena lent Perseus her bronze shield so he could see Medusa's reflection without being petrified, and Perseus gave her the Gorgon's head that adorns her aegis.

summary.id: Athena bertanding menenun dengan Arachne yang fana; menurut Ovidius ia mengubah Arachne menjadi laba-laba pertama.
summary.en: Athena held a weaving contest with the mortal Arachne; according to Ovid she turned Arachne into the first spider.

summary.id: Athena bersaing dengan Hera dan Aphrodite memperebutkan hadiah apel emas.

summary.en: In the Iliad Athena supports the Achaeans; according to theoi.com she attacked the Greek ships with a storm when Oilean Aias was not punished for violating her Trojan shrine.
