short_description.id: Bedawang Nala adalah penyu raksasa dalam mitologi Bali yang memikul seluruh dunia di punggungnya; bila ia bergerak, terjadilah gempa dan letusan gunung berapi.
short_description.en: Bedawang Nala is a giant turtle of Balinese mythology that carries the whole world on its back; when it moves, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur.

long_description.id: Bedawang Nala adalah penyu raksasa dari mitologi Bali yang memikul seluruh dunia di punggungnya. Dalam mitos penciptaan, ia disebut perubahan wujud Anantaboga dan, bersama dua ular naga, menopang dunia manusia. Bila ia bergerak, bumi diguncang gempa dan gunung berapi meletus.
long_description.en: Bedawang Nala is a giant turtle of Balinese mythology that carries the whole world on its back. In the creation myth it is a transformation of Anantaboga, and together with two dragon-serpents it supports the human world. When it moves, earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur.

long_description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Prancis, Bedawang termasuk dalam mitos penciptaan Hindu Bali dan tercipta dari semadi ular kosmis Antaboga. Dua naga, Naga Basuki dan Naga Antaboga, yang melambangkan kebutuhan manusia, bertindak sebagai penstabil. Sebuah kajian jurnal menamai kedua naga yang membelit kura-kura itu Naga Basuki dan Naga Anantabhoga, yang melambangkan air dan tanah, dan menyebut bahwa mereka ditugaskan mengawasi dan mencegah setiap gerakan sang kura-kura.
long_description.en: According to the French Wikipedia, Bedawang is part of the Balinese Hindu creation myth and was created from the meditation of the cosmic serpent Antaboga. Two nagas, Naga Basuki and Naga Antaboga, representing human needs, act as stabilizers. A journal study names the two nagas coiling the turtle Naga Basuki and Naga Anantabhoga, symbolizing water and earth, and says they are charged with watching and preventing every movement of the turtle.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi rakyat Bali dan Jawa, kura-kura raksasa digambarkan menyangga sebuah pulau di punggungnya, dan bila ia bergerak terjadilah gempa bumi. Ornamen bedawang nala lazimnya berwujud kura-kura raksasa berambut api dengan mulut berapi yang dibelit seekor atau dua ekor naga, dan menjadi dasar penyangga bangunan meru. Contohnya terdapat di Pura Taman Sari, Klungkung, dengan seekor naga, dan di Pura Kehen, Bangli, dengan dua naga. Secara umum, penggambaran Bedawang dalam seni dan ornamen terwujud dalam dua bentuk, yaitu teriomorfik dan terio-antropomorfik.
long_description.en: In Balinese and Javanese mythology a giant turtle is depicted supporting an island on its back, and when it moves an earthquake occurs. The bedawang nala ornament usually shows a giant turtle with fiery hair and a fiery mouth coiled by one or two nagas, forming the base that supports a meru building. Examples are at Pura Taman Sari, Klungkung, with one naga, and at Pura Kehen, Bangli, with two nagas. In general, Bedawang is represented in art and ornamentation in two forms, theriomorphic and therio-anthropomorphic.

long_description.id: Istilah bedawang nala berasal dari bahasa Sanskerta vadava, yang berarti kuda betina, dan berhubungan erat dengan Vadavamukha atau Vadavanala, kepala kuda betina berapi di dasar laut dalam mitologi Hindu di India; kata anala sendiri berarti api. Seorang peneliti menyebut konsep itu diadaptasi di Bali menjadi kura-kura berapi raksasa di dasar laut, karena menurut Hooykaas penyu sudah dikenal dan hidup di perairan Pulau Bali. Di alam nyata, kura-kura berapi itu dinyatakan sebagai simbol magma di perut bumi, dan sebagai simbol konsep neraka bila berada di dasar bangunan meru.
long_description.en: The term bedawang nala comes from the Sanskrit vadava, meaning a mare, and is closely related to Vadavamukha or Vadavanala, the head of a fiery mare on the seabed in Hindu mythology in India; the word anala itself means fire. One researcher says the concept was adapted in Bali into a giant fiery turtle on the seabed because, according to Hooykaas, turtles were well known and live in the waters of Bali. In the real world the fiery turtle is said to symbolize magma in the belly of the earth, and the concept of hell when placed at the base of a meru building.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita wayang, Bedawang Nala adalah seorang pendeta berasal dari pertapaan Gisik Samodra atau Eka Pratala, tinggal di sungai Wailu, dan memiliki Cupu Manik Astagina serta Cupu Tirta Manik berisi air kehidupan. Ia disebut berkekuatan gaib luar biasa dan mampu menghancurkan sebuah pulau dengan satu pukulan. Teks Korawasrama memuat kalimat "Nusa yawa kasangga de badawang nala". Penyu laut dahulu diburu dan dipersembahkan dalam upacara dengan kepalanya melambangkan Bedawang; kini para pemuka agama Bali menetapkan bahwa gambar atau kue beras berbentuk penyu boleh dipakai sebagai gantinya.
long_description.en: According to the puppet story, Bedawang Nala is a priest of the Gisik Samodra (or Eka Pratala) hermitage, living in the Wailu river and owning the Cupu Manik Astagina and Cupu Tirta Manik, vessels of the water of life. He is said to have extraordinary supernatural powers and to be able to make an island fall apart with one blow. The Korawasrama contains the sentence "Nusa yawa kasangga de badawang nala". Sea turtles were once hunted and offered in ceremonies with their heads symbolizing Bedawang; Balinese religious leaders now decree that a turtle-shaped image or rice cake may be used instead.

Dalam mitologi penciptaan dunia, ia merupakan perubahan dari Anantaboga. Ia bersama dua ular naga mendukung dunia manusia. Jikalau ia bergerak maka akan terjadilah gempa dan letusan gunung berapi di atas bumi.

statement.id: Bedawang Nala (ᬩᭂᬤᬯᬂᬦᬮ) adalah penyu raksasa dalam mitologi Bali yang memikul dunia di punggungnya; dalam mitos penciptaan ia perubahan dari Anantaboga, bersama dua naga menopang dunia manusia, dan bila bergerak terjadi gempa dan letusan gunung berapi.
statement.en: Bedawang Nala (ᬩᭂᬤᬯᬂᬦᬮ) is a giant turtle of Balinese mythology carrying the world on its back; in the creation myth it is a transformation of Anantaboga, supports the human world with two nāgas, and its movement causes earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.

statement.en: The words ananta bhoga literally mean inexhaustible food; Naga Anantabhoga symbolizes the earth as the eternal source of food for all living beings.

short_description.id: Pyinsarupa adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar yang tersusun dari ciri lima hewan, tampil pada gendang hsaing waing dan kepala tongkang kerajaan, serta kini menjadi logo sebuah maskapai.
short_description.en: The pyinsarupa is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology made of features of five animals, shown on hsaing waing drums and royal barge figureheads and now the logo of an airline.

long_description.id:
Pyinsarupa, dari kata Pali pañcarūpa, adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar; dalam bahasa Thai ia disebut phaya luang. Satu sumber menyusunnya dari gajah, sapi jantan, kuda, ikan karper putih, dan tonaya (singa-naga bertanduk dalam mitos), sedangkan versi lain mengganti bahan-bahan itu dengan singa, gajah, kerbau, karper putih, dan hamsa.

Sumber lain memberi rincian yang berbeda. Katalog koleksi alat musik menyebut belalai gajah, badan sapi atau kerbau, kaki dan telinga kuda, ekor dan sisik ikan karper, serta sayap hamsa, dan menyebut gabungan itu melambangkan makhluk darat, air, dan bersayap. Dalam zodiak Myanmar, lambang Ketu adalah Hewan Lima Keindahan bernama pyinsarupa, dengan tanduk rusa, gading dan belalai gajah, surai singa, tubuh ular naga, dan ekor ikan.

Pyinsarupa tampil dalam benda dan upacara kerajaan serta musik. Pada masa dinasti Konbaung ada beberapa jenis tongkang kerajaan yang dibedakan oleh kepala mitosnya, dan satu di antaranya, berlapis emas, dipakai para permaisuri utama dengan kepala pyinsarupa. Gendang besar pat ma gyi dalam ansambel hsaing waing digantung pada rangka tiang yang menggambarkan pyinsarupa, dan sebuah harpa Myanmar dalam sebuah koleksi berbentuk pyinsarupa serta dihias mika, kaca, dan sepuhan emas.

Pada masa kini pyinsarupa menjadi logo Myanmar Airways International, dan ia sering tampil dalam orkestra tradisional hsaing waing.
long_description.en:
The pyinsarupa, from the Pali pañcarūpa, is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology; in Thai it is called phaya luang. One source composes it from an elephant, bullock, horse, white carp and tonaya (a mythical horned leodragon), while another telling swaps in a lion, elephant, water buffalo, white carp and hamsa.

Other sources give different details. A musical instrument collection's catalog lists an elephant's trunk, a bullock's or buffalo's body, a horse's legs and ears, a carp's tail and scales and a hamsa's wings, and says the combination symbolizes land, water and winged creatures. In the Burmese zodiac, Ketu's sign is an Animal of Five Beauties named pyinsarupa, with a deer's antlers, an elephant's tusks and trunk, a lion's mane, a naga serpent's body and a fish's tail.

The pyinsarupa appears in royal objects and in music. By the Konbaung dynasty there were several types of royal barges distinguished by their mythical figureheads, and one of them, a gilt barge, was used by the chief queens with a pyinsarupa figurehead. The big pat ma gyi drum of the hsaing waing ensemble is suspended from a pole frame depicting a pyinsarupa, and a Burmese harp in one collection is shaped like a pyinsarupa and decorated with mica, glass and gilt.

Today the pyinsarupa is the logo of Myanmar Airways International, and it is commonly featured in traditional hsaing waing orchestras.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, juga pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'lima wujud'), juga dikenal sebagai phaya luang (bahasa Thai), adalah hewan campuran dalam mitologi Myanmar.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ, also pyinsa rupa; Pali pañcarūpa, 'five forms'), also known in Thai as phaya luang, is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology.

claims.quote: The Pyinsarupa is made of parts of an elephant, a bullock, a horse, a white carp (ငါးကြင်း) and a tonaya (တိုးနရား, a mythical horned leodragon), or alternately a lion, an elephant, a water buffalo, a white carp, and a hamsa.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa tersusun dari bagian gajah, sapi jantan, kuda, ikan karper putih, dan tonaya (singa-naga bertanduk), atau dalam versi lain singa, gajah, kerbau, karper putih, dan hamsa.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa combines an elephant, bullock, horse, white carp and tonaya (a horned leodragon), or alternately a lion, elephant, water buffalo, white carp and hamsa.

claims.quote: The creature is commonly featured in traditional Burmese hsaing waing orchestras, and serves as the logo of Myanmar's flagship air carrier, Myanmar Airways International.

statement.id: Makhluk ini sering tampil dalam orkestra tradisional Myanmar hsaing waing dan menjadi logo maskapai unggulan Myanmar, Myanmar Airways International.
statement.en: It features in traditional Burmese hsaing waing orchestras and is the logo of Myanmar's flagship airline, Myanmar Airways International.

claims.quote: The ‘Pyinsarupa’ is a chimeric animal from Burmese mythology, meaning an amalgamation of the physical characteristics of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water, and winged creatures.

statement.id: Pyinsarupa adalah hewan campuran dari mitologi Myanmar yang menggabungkan ciri fisik lima hewan berbeda, melambangkan gabungan makhluk darat, air, dan bersayap.
statement.en: The pyinsarupa is a chimeric animal of Burmese mythology that combines physical features of five different animals, symbolizing a combination of land, water and winged creatures.

claims.quote: The components of this ‘Pyinsarupa’ consist of the Elephant (trunk); Bullock/Water Buffalo (body); Horse (legs and ears); White Carp/Nga Gyin Fish (tail and scales); and Hamsa (wings).

statement.id: Menurut katalog koleksi ini, komponen pyinsarupa adalah gajah (belalai), sapi jantan atau kerbau (badan), kuda (kaki dan telinga), ikan karper putih atau nga gyin (ekor dan sisik), dan hamsa (sayap).
statement.en: According to this collection catalog, the pyinsarupa's components are the elephant (trunk), bullock or water buffalo (body), horse (legs and ears), white carp or nga gyin fish (tail and scales) and hamsa (wings).

claims.quote: This Burmese harp ... is in the shape of the Burmese creature called a ‘Pyinsarupa’ and is an important cultural symbol in Myanmar (Burma).

statement.id: Sebuah harpa Myanmar dalam koleksi ini berbentuk pyinsarupa, yang disebut sebagai simbol budaya penting di Myanmar.
statement.en: A Burmese harp in this collection is shaped like the pyinsarupa, which the catalog calls an important cultural symbol in Myanmar.

claims.quote: The ‘Pyinsarupa’ is fully decorated with pieces of mica (Mandalay pearls’), glass, and gilt.

statement.id: Katalog menyebut pyinsarupa pada harpa itu dihias penuh dengan keping mika, kaca, dan sepuhan emas.
statement.en: The catalog says the pyinsarupa on that harp is fully decorated with pieces of mica, glass and gilt.

claims.quote: Ketu's sign is a mythical Animal of Five Beauties called pyinsarupa ... with the antlers of a deer, the tusks and the trunk of an elephant, the mane of a lion, the body of a naga serpent, and the tail of a fish.

statement.id: Dalam zodiak Myanmar, lambang Ketu adalah Hewan Lima Keindahan mitos bernama pyinsarupa, dengan tanduk rusa, gading dan belalai gajah, surai singa, tubuh ular naga, dan ekor ikan.
statement.en: In the Burmese zodiac, Ketu's sign is a mythical Animal of Five Beauties called pyinsarupa, with a deer's antlers, an elephant's tusks and trunk, a lion's mane, a naga serpent's body and a fish's tail.

claims.quote: Pyinsarupa – (lit five features); a creature made from the amalgamation of parts of five different animals, mascot of Myanmar Airways International.

statement.id: Daftar makhluk mitos Myanmar menerjemahkan nama pyinsarupa secara harfiah sebagai 'lima ciri' dan menyebutnya makhluk gabungan bagian lima hewan berbeda.
statement.en: A list of Burmese mythical creatures glosses the name pyinsarupa literally as 'five features' and calls it a creature made from parts of five different animals.

claims.quote: Pyinsarupa (ပဉ္စရူပ) - used by the chief queens, a gilt barge with the figurehead of a pyinsarupa (a chimeric animal with the mane of karaweik bird, the tusk and trunk of an elephant, the hump of bull, the tail of a ngagyin fish, and the horns of a toe naya)

statement.id: Tongkang kerajaan bernama Pyinsarupa dipakai para permaisuri utama: tongkang berlapis emas berhias kepala pyinsarupa, hewan campuran dengan surai burung karaweik, gading dan belalai gajah, punuk sapi, ekor ikan ngagyin, dan tanduk toe naya.
statement.en: A royal barge named Pyinsarupa was used by the chief queens: a gilt barge with a pyinsarupa figurehead, a chimeric animal with the mane of a karaweik bird, an elephant's tusk and trunk, a bull's hump, a ngagyin fish's tail and the horns of a toe naya.

claims.quote: By the Konbaung dynasty, several types of royal state barges existed, each distinguished by a specific mythical figurehead at the front of the barge, and each allocated to different members of the royal court

statement.id: Pada masa dinasti Konbaung ada beberapa jenis tongkang kerajaan, masing-masing dibedakan oleh kepala mitos tertentu di haluan dan diperuntukkan bagi anggota istana yang berbeda.
statement.en: By the Konbaung dynasty there were several types of royal state barges, each distinguished by a specific mythical figurehead at the bow and allocated to different members of the royal court.

claims.quote: Pat ma gyi (ပတ်မကြီး) - a big drum suspended from a pole frame depicting a mythical pyinsarupa

statement.id: Dalam ansambel hsaing waing, pat ma gyi adalah gendang besar yang digantung pada rangka tiang dan menggambarkan pyinsarupa mitos.
statement.en: In the hsaing waing ensemble, the pat ma gyi is a big drum suspended from a pole frame depicting a mythical pyinsarupa.

claims.quote: borrowed from Pali pañca (“five”) + Pali rūpa (“beauties”).

statement.id: Kata ini dipinjam dari kata Pali pañca ('lima') dan rūpa ('keindahan'; artikel Wikipedia memberi arti 'wujud').
statement.en: The word is borrowed from Pali pañca ('five') and rūpa ('beauties'); the Wikipedia article glosses it as 'forms'.

claims.quote: MAI's logo shows pyinsarupa (Burmese: ပဉ္စရူပ), a traditional Burmese chimeric animal.

statement.id: Logo maskapai Myanmar Airways International menampilkan pyinsarupa, hewan campuran tradisional Myanmar.
statement.en: The logo of Myanmar Airways International shows pyinsarupa, a traditional Burmese chimeric animal.

claims.quote: Nawarupa – (lit nine features); a creature made from the amalgamation of parts of nine different animals.

statement.id: Nawarupa ('sembilan ciri') adalah makhluk yang terbentuk dari gabungan bagian sembilan hewan berbeda.
statement.en: The nawarupa ('nine features') is a creature made from the amalgamation of parts of nine different animals.

short_description.id: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) adalah siluman muda dalam novel Journey to the West, putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan. Ia menguasai api sanmei zhenhuo sebelum ditundukkan Guanyin dan dijadikan Shancai Tongzi.
short_description.en: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) is a young demon in the novel Journey to the West, the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan. He wields the sanmei zhenhuo fire before Guanyin subdues him and names him Shancai Tongzi.

long_description.id:
Red Boy adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat). Ia putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan, yang menurut Wikipedia seorang Rakshasa. Dalam novel ia dikenal dengan gelar Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) dan tinggal di Huoyun Dong, sebuah gua di Gunung Hao.

Menurut novel, ia berlatih di Flaming Mountain hingga menguasai sanmei zhenhuo, api yang tak bisa dipadamkan hujan Dragon King, dan diutus ayahnya menjaga Gunung Hao. Ia mendengar bahwa memakan daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang, lalu menyamar sebagai anak yang tergantung di pohon pinus untuk memancing rombongan itu. Ia juga menyamar sebagai Guanyin untuk menjebak Zhu Bajie.

Sun Wukong mengundang Guanyin, yang kemudian menaklukkannya. Sang Bodhisattva mencukur kepalanya, menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi, dan memasangkan gelang emas padanya karena ia bersikap kurang ajar. Wikipedia mencatat pula bahwa beberapa agama rakyat daerah menghormatinya sebagai dewa, dengan patung di sebuah gua di Meishan.
long_description.en:
Red Boy is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West. He is the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan, who according to Wikipedia is a Rakshasa. In the novel he is known by the title Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) and lives at Huoyun Dong, a cave on Mount Hao.

According to the novel, he trained on the Flaming Mountain until he mastered sanmei zhenhuo, a fire that the Dragon King's rain cannot put out, and was sent by his father to guard Mount Hao. He heard that eating the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life and disguised himself as a child hung in a pine tree to lure the party. He also disguised himself as Guanyin to trap Zhu Bajie.

Sun Wukong invites Guanyin, who then subdues him. The Bodhisattva shaves his head, names him Shancai Tongzi, and fastens a golden band on him because he is disrespectful. Wikipedia also notes that some regional folk religions venerate him as a deity, with a statue in a cavern at Meishan.

summary.id: Red Boy muncul sebagai awan merah, menyamar sebagai anak yang tergantung di pohon pinus, dan mengincar Tang Sanzang karena ingin hidup panjang. Ia bertarung dengan tombak api di depan Huoyun Dong, dan api sanmei zhenhuo-nya tidak padam oleh hujan Dragon King.
summary.en: Red Boy appears as a red cloud, poses as a child hung in a pine tree, and targets Tang Sanzang because he wants long life. He fights with a fire-tipped spear before Huoyun Dong, and his sanmei zhenhuo fire is not put out by the Dragon King's rain.

claims_provenance.quote: Red Boy was also known as the Boy Sage Great King (聖嬰大王; Shèngyīng Dàwáng) and "Bull Boy Sage" (牛聖嬰; Niú Shèngyīng).

claim.id: Red Boy (紅孩兒) adalah putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan (seorang Rakshasa) yang digambarkan garang.
claim.en: Red Boy (紅孩兒) is the ferocious son of the Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan (a Rakshasa).

claims_provenance.quote: Red Boy (紅孩兒) is the ferocious son of the Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan (a Rakshasa).
claims_provenance.locator: Bagian "Life as Red Boy in Journey to the West"

claim.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menyampaikan keterangan dewa setempat bahwa siluman itu putra Bull Demon King (牛魔王) yang dilahirkan Luocha Nü (羅剎女), bernama Red Boy (紅孩兒) dan bergelar Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王).
claim.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong relays what the local deities told him: the demon is the son of Bull Demon King (牛魔王), born of Luocha Nü (羅剎女), named Red Boy (紅孩兒) and styled Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王).

claims_provenance.quote: 我問他妖怪的原因，他道是牛魔王的兒子，羅剎女養的，名字喚做紅孩兒，號聖嬰大王。

claim.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa Red Boy berlatih tiga ratus tahun di Flaming Mountain (火燄山), menguasai sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), berkesaktian besar, dan diutus Bull Demon King (牛魔王) menjaga Gunung Hao (號山).
claim.en: In the novel it is said that Red Boy trained for three hundred years on the Flaming Mountain (火燄山), mastered sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), has great powers, and was sent by Bull Demon King (牛魔王) to guard Mount Hao (號山).

claims_provenance.quote: 他曾在火燄山修行了三百年，煉成三昧真火，卻也神通廣大，牛魔王使他來鎮守號山。

claim.id: Dalam novel, saat para peziarah melewati gunung itu, awan merah naik dari lembah hingga ke langit dan menggumpal menjadi hawa api.
claim.en: In the novel, as the travelers cross the mountain, a red cloud rises from the hollow into the sky and gathers into a mass of fire.

claims_provenance.quote: 師徒們正當悚懼，又只見那山凹裡有一朵紅雲，直冒到九霄空內，結聚了一團火氣。

claim.id: Dalam novel, makhluk di dalam cahaya merah itu adalah seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman). Ia mendengar bahwa Tang Sanzang (唐僧), yang bepergian ke Barat untuk mengambil kitab, adalah reinkarnasi Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), dan bahwa orang yang memakan sepotong dagingnya akan hidup panjang.
claim.en: In the novel, the being in the red light is a yaojing (妖精, demon). He has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐僧), traveling west to fetch scriptures, is the reincarnation of Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live long.

claims_provenance.quote: 卻說紅光裡，真是個妖精。他數年前聞得人講：東土唐僧往西天取經，乃是金蟬長老轉生，十世修行的好人，有人吃他一塊肉，延生長壽，與天地同休。

claim.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy berubah wujud (搖身一變) menjadi anak berusia tujuh tahun yang telanjang, tangan dan kakinya diikat tali rami dan digantung di pucuk pohon pinus sambil berteriak minta tolong.
claim.en: In the novel, Red Boy transforms (搖身一變) into a seven-year-old child, naked, hands and feet bound with hemp rope and hung from the top of a pine tree, shouting for help.

claims_provenance.quote: 好妖怪，即散紅光，按雲頭落下。去那山坡裡，搖身一變，變作七歲頑童，赤條條的身上無衣，將麻繩綑了手足，高吊在那松樹梢頭，口口聲聲只叫：「救人，救人！」

claim.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy keluar bertarung membawa tombak ujung api (火尖槍) sepanjang satu zhang delapan chi, tanpa baju zirah, hanya mengenakan rok perang bersulam dan bertelanjang kaki.
claim.en: In the novel, Red Boy comes out to fight with a fire-tipped spear (火尖槍) eighteen chi long, wearing no armor, only an embroidered war skirt, and barefoot.

claims_provenance.quote: 有那一夥管兵器的小妖，著兩個擡出一桿丈八長的火尖槍，遞與妖王。妖王掄槍拽步，也無甚麼盔甲，只是腰間束一條錦繡戰裙，赤著腳，走出門前。

claim.id: Dalam novel, gua tempat tinggal Red Boy berada di Gunung Hao (號山), di Lembah Pinus Kering (枯松澗), dan bernama Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
claim.en: In the novel, Red Boy's cave lies on Mount Hao (號山), at the Withered Pine Ravine (枯松澗), and is named Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).

claims_provenance.quote: 將近行到門前，見有一座石碣，上鐫八個大字，乃是「號山枯松澗火雲洞」。

claim.id: Dalam novel, hujan yang dikirim Dragon King (龍王) hanya bisa memadamkan api biasa, bukan sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火) milik siluman itu; hujan justru membuat api makin membara.
claim.en: In the novel, the rain sent by the Dragon King (龍王) can only put out ordinary fire, not the demon's sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火); it only makes the fire burn the fiercer.

claims_provenance.quote: 原來龍王私雨，只好潑得凡火，妖精的三昧真火如何潑得？好一似火上澆油，越潑越灼。

claim.id: Dalam novel, Red Boy sendiri mengatakan bahwa ia menyamar sebagai Guanyin (觀音) untuk memancing Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), yang kini tergantung di dalam kantong.
claim.en: In the novel, Red Boy himself says that he disguised himself as Guanyin (觀音) to lure Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), who now hangs in a bag.

claims_provenance.quote: 是我假變觀音，把豬八戒賺來，見吊在如意袋中，也要蒸他與眾小的們吃哩。

claim.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong dengan gembira mengundang Guanyin (觀音) keluar dari gua Chaoyin (潮音仙洞); para dewa berjajar di batu karang Putuo (普陀巖), dan sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) berkata kepadanya, "Wukong, seberangi laut."
claim.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong gladly invites Guanyin (觀音) out of the Chaoyin cave (潮音仙洞); the gods line up on the Putuo rock (普陀巖), and the Bodhisattva (菩薩) says to him, "Wukong, cross the sea."

claims_provenance.quote: 孫大聖十分歡喜，請觀音出了潮音仙洞。諸天大神都列在普陀巖上。菩薩道：「悟空，過海。」

claim.id: Dalam novel, setelah Red Boy memohon ampun, sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) mencukur kepalanya dengan pisau emas hingga berbentuk "太山壓頂" dan menyisakan tiga jambul.
claim.en: In the novel, after Red Boy begs for mercy, the Bodhisattva (菩薩) shaves his head with a golden razor into a "Mount Tai pressing down" (太山壓頂) style, leaving three tufts.

claims_provenance.quote: 菩薩道：「既如此，我與你摩頂受戒。」就袖中取出一把金剃頭刀兒，近前去，把那怪分頂剃了幾刀，剃作一個太山壓頂，與他留下三個頂搭，挽起三個窩角揪兒。

claim.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) setelah ia menerima ajaran; Red Boy mengangguk menerimanya dengan harapan diampuni.
claim.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva names him Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) after he accepts the precepts; Red Boy nods and accepts, hoping to be spared.

claims_provenance.quote: 菩薩道：「你今既受我戒，我卻也不慢你，稱你做善財童子，如何？」那妖點頭受持，只望饒命。

short_description.id: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) adalah siluman muda dalam novel Journey to the West, putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan. Ia menguasai api sanmei zhenhuo sebelum ditundukkan Guanyin dan dijadikan Shancai Tongzi.
short_description.en: Red Boy (Hong Hai-er) is a young demon in the novel Journey to the West, the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan. He wields the sanmei zhenhuo fire before Guanyin subdues him and names him Shancai Tongzi.

long_description.id: Red Boy adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat). Ia putra Bull Demon King dan Princess Iron Fan, yang menurut Wikipedia seorang Rakshasa. Dalam novel ia dikenal dengan gelar Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) dan tinggal di Huoyun Dong, sebuah gua di Gunung Hao.
long_description.en: Red Boy is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West. He is the son of Bull Demon King and Princess Iron Fan, who according to Wikipedia is a Rakshasa. In the novel he is known by the title Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王, Boy Sage Great King) and lives at Huoyun Dong, a cave on Mount Hao.

long_description.id: Menurut novel, ia berlatih di Flaming Mountain hingga menguasai sanmei zhenhuo, api yang tak bisa dipadamkan hujan Dragon King, dan diutus ayahnya menjaga Gunung Hao. Ia mendengar bahwa memakan daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang, lalu menyamar sebagai anak yang tergantung di pohon pinus untuk memancing rombongan itu. Ia juga menyamar sebagai Guanyin untuk menjebak Zhu Bajie.
long_description.en: According to the novel, he trained on the Flaming Mountain until he mastered sanmei zhenhuo, a fire that the Dragon King's rain cannot put out, and was sent by his father to guard Mount Hao. He heard that eating the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life and disguised himself as a child hung in a pine tree to lure the party. He also disguised himself as Guanyin to trap Zhu Bajie.

long_description.id: Sun Wukong mengundang Guanyin, yang kemudian menaklukkannya. Sang Bodhisattva mencukur kepalanya, menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi, dan memasangkan gelang emas padanya karena ia bersikap kurang ajar. Wikipedia mencatat pula bahwa beberapa agama rakyat daerah menghormatinya sebagai dewa, dengan patung di sebuah gua di Meishan.
long_description.en: Sun Wukong invites Guanyin, who then subdues him. The Bodhisattva shaves his head, names him Shancai Tongzi, and fastens a golden band on him because he is disrespectful. Wikipedia also notes that some regional folk religions venerate him as a deity, with a statue in a cavern at Meishan.

cultural_context.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa beberapa agama rakyat daerah menghormati Red Boy sebagai dewa; di sebuah gua di Meishan, Provinsi Sichuan, patungnya menjadi objek pemujaan setempat.
cultural_context.en: Wikipedia notes that some regional folk religions venerate Red Boy as a deity; in a cavern at Meishan, Sichuan Province, a statue of him is an object of local worship.

summary.id: Red Boy muncul sebagai awan merah, menyamar sebagai anak yang tergantung di pohon pinus, dan mengincar Tang Sanzang karena ingin hidup panjang. Ia bertarung dengan tombak api di depan Huoyun Dong, dan api sanmei zhenhuo-nya tidak padam oleh hujan Dragon King.
summary.en: Red Boy appears as a red cloud, poses as a child hung in a pine tree, and targets Tang Sanzang because he wants long life. He fights with a fire-tipped spear before Huoyun Dong, and his sanmei zhenhuo fire is not put out by the Dragon King's rain.

statement.id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menyampaikan keterangan dewa setempat bahwa siluman itu putra Bull Demon King (牛魔王) yang dilahirkan Luocha Nü (羅剎女), bernama Red Boy (紅孩兒) dan bergelar Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王).
statement.en: In the novel, Sun Wukong relays what the local deities told him: the demon is the son of Bull Demon King (牛魔王), born of Luocha Nü (羅剎女), named Red Boy (紅孩兒) and styled Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王).

statement.id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa Red Boy berlatih tiga ratus tahun di Flaming Mountain (火燄山), menguasai sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), berkesaktian besar, dan diutus Bull Demon King (牛魔王) menjaga Gunung Hao (號山).
statement.en: In the novel it is said that Red Boy trained for three hundred years on the Flaming Mountain (火燄山), mastered sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火), has great powers, and was sent by Bull Demon King (牛魔王) to guard Mount Hao (號山).

statement.id: Dalam novel, saat para peziarah melewati gunung itu, awan merah naik dari lembah hingga ke langit dan menggumpal menjadi hawa api.
statement.en: In the novel, as the travelers cross the mountain, a red cloud rises from the hollow into the sky and gathers into a mass of fire.

statement.id: Dalam novel, makhluk di dalam cahaya merah itu adalah seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman). Ia mendengar bahwa Tang Sanzang (唐僧), yang bepergian ke Barat untuk mengambil kitab, adalah reinkarnasi Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), dan bahwa orang yang memakan sepotong dagingnya akan hidup panjang.
statement.en: In the novel, the being in the red light is a yaojing (妖精, demon). He has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐僧), traveling west to fetch scriptures, is the reincarnation of Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live long.

statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy transforms (搖身一變) into a seven-year-old child, naked, hands and feet bound with hemp rope and hung from the top of a pine tree, shouting for help.

claims.quote: 將近行到門前，見有一座石碣，上鐫八個大字，乃是「號山枯松澗火雲洞」。

statement.id: Dalam novel, gua tempat tinggal Red Boy berada di Gunung Hao (號山), di Lembah Pinus Kering (枯松澗), dan bernama Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
statement.en: In the novel, Red Boy's cave lies on Mount Hao (號山), at the Withered Pine Ravine (枯松澗), and is named Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).

short_description.id: Six-Eared Macaque (Liu'er Mihou) adalah kera spiritual dalam novel Journey to the West yang menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dengan sangat mirip. Ia dikenali Buddha lalu dibunuh Sun Wukong.
short_description.en: The Six-Eared Macaque (Liu'er Mihou) is a spiritual monkey in the novel Journey to the West who impersonates Sun Wukong so closely that none can tell them apart. The Buddha identifies him and Sun Wukong then kills him.

long_description.id:
Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴) adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat) karya Wu Cheng'en, yang oleh Wikipedia disebut antagonis utama dan paling diingat karena menirukan Sun Wukong. Dalam novel, Rulai (Buddha) menyebutnya satu dari empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk, dan ia pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, serta memahami segala hal.

Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, ia berharap menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha. Ia muncul menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong, membuat Tang Sanzang pingsan, mencuri barangnya, dan membawanya ke Flower-Fruit Mountain untuk membentuk rombongan sendiri. Dalam novel, sosok itu memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas dua bungkusan, lalu berkata bahwa ia sendiri akan mengambil kitab suci ke Barat.

Di alam baka, Diting menyatakan bahwa kesaktian siluman itu sama dengan Sun Wukong sehingga ia tak bisa ditangkap di sana. Di hadapan Rulai, kera itu dikenali sebagai Liu'er Mihou yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong; ia berubah menjadi lebah, dikurung mangkuk emas, lalu dipukul mati oleh Sun Wukong. Sang Bodhisattva kemudian memberi tahu Tang Sanzang bahwa pemukulnya adalah Sun Wukong palsu.
long_description.en:
The Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴) is a literary character from the novel Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en, called by Wikipedia a major antagonist and best remembered for impersonating Sun Wukong. In the novel, Rulai (the Buddha) names him one of four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings, skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

According to Wikipedia's summary, he hoped to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha. He appears disguised as Sun Wukong, knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage, and takes it to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up a band of his own. In the novel, the figure strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes two bundles, then says he himself will go west to fetch the scriptures.

In the underworld, Diting states that the demon's powers are the same as Sun Wukong's so he cannot be captured there. Before Rulai, the monkey is identified as Liu'er Mihou, matching Sun Wukong in form and voice; he turns into a bee, is trapped under a golden bowl, and is struck dead by Sun Wukong. The Bodhisattva then tells Tang Sanzang that the one who struck him was the false Sun Wukong.

cultural_context.id: Wikipedia mencatat tafsir bahwa nama tokoh ini mungkin merujuk pada pepatah "rahasia tidak aman di antara enam telinga", dan bahwa dua kera itu mungkin metafora pikiran sejati dan pikiran palsu dalam Buddhisme Tiongkok.

claim.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Buddha juga berkata bahwa Six-Eared Macaque "hampir mahatahu" (near-omniscient) karena enam telinganya menyadap banyak informasi di sekelilingnya, "mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan", dan "memahami segala hal".
claim.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Buddha also says the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" because his six ears eavesdrop on information around him, "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

claims_provenance.quote: Buddha also says that the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" (thanks to his six ears eavesdropping upon many tidbits of information around him far and wide), "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

claim.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, dengan harapan menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha, Six-Eared Macaque pertama kali muncul di Xiliang (西粱) menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage and paperwork, and takes them to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

claims_provenance.quote: Hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha in Sun Wukong's place, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) in disguise as Sun Wukong. claim.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Six-Eared Macaque tries to flee when he hears the Buddha speak of his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl; the macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

claims_provenance.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque attempts to flee when he hears the Buddha speak about his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl. The macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

claim.en: In the novel, the figure who appears as Sun Wukong (行者) in chapter 57 scolds Tang Sanzang, strikes him on the back with an iron staff until he faints, and then flies off on a somersault cloud with two bundles.

claim.en: In the novel, the "Sun Wukong" at the Water Curtain Cave says that he beat Tang Sanzang and took his baggage, and that he himself will go west to worship the Buddha and fetch the scriptures, so that the world will honor him as a founder and his name will be passed down for generations.

claim.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來, the Buddha) names four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings: the Lingming stone monkey (靈明石猴), the red-buttocked horse monkey (赤尻馬猴), the long-armed ape (通臂猿猴), and the fourth, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

claim.en: In the novel, the monkey transforms into a bee (蜜蜂兒) and flies upward, but Rulai (如來) throws his golden bowl (金缽盂), which falls and covers the bee.

claim.id: Dalam novel, ketika mangkuk diangkat, tampaklah wujud aslinya, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) tak tahan dan memukul kepalanya dengan tongkat besi sampai mati, sehingga jenis ini punah.
claim.en: In the novel, when the bowl is lifted his true form appears, a Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) cannot hold back and strikes his head dead with the iron staff, so that this kind is extinct.

claim.en: According to Hongmei Sun as cited by Wikipedia, Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme".

claims_provenance.quote: Hongmei Sun argues that Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme"

claim.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, tak seorang pun dapat membedakan Sun Wukong asli dan palsu; mantra penyamaran Six-Eared Macaque begitu baik sehingga ia juga bereaksi terhadap "Headache Sutra", sampai keduanya menghadap Buddha, yang menjelaskan tentang empat primata spiritual.
claim.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, no one can tell the real Sun Wukong from the fake; the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.

claims_provenance.quote: No one is able to differentiate between the real and the fake Sun Wukong—the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", preventing the pilgrims from differentiating between him and Sun Wukong—until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.

origin.en: The novel Journey to the West by Wu Cheng'en.

role.id: Penyamar yang menggantikan Sun Wukong di hadapan Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya.
role.en: An impersonator who takes Sun Wukong's place before Tang Sanzang and seizes his baggage.

famous_for.id: Kemiripannya dengan Sun Wukong yang begitu sempurna sampai tak seorang pun dapat membedakan keduanya hingga mereka menghadap Buddha.
famous_for.en: His likeness to Sun Wukong, so perfect that no one could tell them apart until they appeared before the Buddha.

name.id: Menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dan berubah menjadi lebah
name.en: Impersonating Sun Wukong and turning into a bee

description.id: Ia menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong dan, saat terdesak di hadapan Rulai, berubah menjadi lebah.
description.en: He impersonates Sun Wukong and, when cornered before Rulai, turns into a bee.

description.id: Menurut Rulai, ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan ucapan manusia, serta mengetahui sebelum dan sesudah.
description.en: According to Rulai, he can know events a thousand li away and what people say, and knows before and after.

title.en: The real and the false Sun Wukong

role.id: Sun Wukong palsu yang menyaingi Sun Wukong asli sampai dikenali Buddha.
role.en: The false Sun Wukong who rivals the real one until the Buddha identifies him.

summary.id: Sosok yang menyerupai Sun Wukong memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas bungkusannya, lalu mengaku akan mengambil kitab sendiri. Tak seorang pun dapat membedakan keduanya hingga keduanya menghadap Rulai, yang mengungkapkan jati dirinya. Sun Wukong membunuhnya setelah Rulai mengurungnya di bawah mangkuk emas.
summary.en: A figure resembling Sun Wukong strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes his bundles, then claims he will fetch the scriptures himself. No one can tell the two apart until they appear before Rulai, who reveals his identity. Sun Wukong kills him after Rulai traps him under a golden bowl.

description.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Six-Eared Macaque dilahirkan kembali dalam salah satu sekuel tidak resmi paling awal dari Xiyouji, yaitu Xu Xiyouji.
description.en: Wikipedia notes that the Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, Xu Xiyouji.

note.id: Kembaran, rekan, dan saingan Sun Wukong menurut Hongmei Sun; Sun Wukong akhirnya membunuhnya.
note.en: Sun Wukong's doppelganger, peer, and rival according to Hongmei Sun; Sun Wukong finally kills him.

note.id: Ia memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya.
note.en: He strikes Tang Sanzang and seizes his baggage.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tokoh yang menirukan Sun Wukong begitu sulit dibedakan dari aslinya dalam kisah ini?
learning_questions.en: Why is the character who imitates Sun Wukong so hard to tell apart from the original in this story?

learning_questions.id: Apa makna kisah dua kera jika dibaca sebagai metafora pikiran sejati dan pikiran palsu?
learning_questions.en: What does the story of the two monkeys mean when read as a metaphor of the true mind and the false mind?

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana penafsiran akademis berbeda dari apa yang dikatakan teks novel itu sendiri?
learning_questions.en: How do scholarly interpretations differ from what the text of the novel itself says?

claims.quote: is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).

statement.id: Six-Eared Macaque adalah antagonis utama dan salah satu tokoh paling kuat dalam novel fantasi Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat) karya Wu Cheng'en, yang paling diingat karena menirukan Sun Wukong (Monkey King) dengan sangat mirip.
statement.en: Six-Eared Macaque is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).

claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque (Chinese: 六耳獼猴; pinyin: Liù'ěr míhóu)

statement.id: Nama Tionghoa Six-Eared Macaque adalah 六耳獼猴, dalam pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.
statement.en: The Chinese name of the Six-Eared Macaque is 六耳獼猴, in pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.

claims.quote: according to the Buddha, one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories that all beings in the universe are classified under.

statement.id: Menurut Buddha dalam novel, Six-Eared Macaque adalah satu dari empat primata spiritual yang tidak termasuk dalam sepuluh golongan yang menjadi pengelompokan semua makhluk di alam semesta.
statement.en: According to the Buddha in the novel, the Six-Eared Macaque is one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories into which all beings in the universe are classified.

claims.quote: Buddha also says that the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" (thanks to his six ears eavesdropping upon many tidbits of information around him far and wide), "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Buddha juga berkata bahwa Six-Eared Macaque "hampir mahatahu" (near-omniscient) karena enam telinganya menyadap banyak informasi di sekelilingnya, "mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan", dan "memahami segala hal".
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Buddha also says the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" because his six ears eavesdrop on information around him, "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

claims.quote: Hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha in Sun Wukong's place, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) in disguise as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious and steals the baggage and paperwork which he takes to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, dengan harapan menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha, Six-Eared Macaque pertama kali muncul di Xiliang (西粱) menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong. Ia membuat Tang Sanzang pingsan, mencuri barang dan dokumennya, lalu membawanya ke Flower-Fruit Mountain untuk membentuk rombongan peziarahnya sendiri.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) disguised as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage and paperwork, and takes them to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque attempts to flee when he hears the Buddha speak about his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl. The macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Six-Eared Macaque mencoba kabur saat mendengar Buddha membicarakan jati dirinya, tetapi Buddha mengurungnya di bawah mangkuk sedekah emas raksasa; setelah itu ia dibunuh Sun Wukong.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Six-Eared Macaque tries to flee when he hears the Buddha speak of his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl; the macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

claims.quote: 那行者變了臉，發怒生嗔，喝罵長老道：「你這個狠心的潑禿！十分賤我。」掄鐵棒，丟了磁杯，望長老脊背上砑了一下。那長老昏暈在地，不能言語，被他把兩個青氈包袱提在手中，駕觔斗雲，不知去向。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sosok yang tampil sebagai Sun Wukong (行者) di Bab 57 memarahi Tang Sanzang, memukulnya dengan tongkat besi hingga pingsan, lalu membawa kabur dua bungkusan kain dengan awan salto.
statement.en: In the novel, the figure who appears as Sun Wukong (行者) in chapter 57 scolds Tang Sanzang, strikes him on the back with an iron staff until he faints, and then flies off on a somersault cloud with two bundles.

claims.quote: 我打唐僧，搶行李，不因我不上西方，亦不因我愛居此地。我今熟讀了牒文，我自己上西方拜佛求經，送上東土，我獨成功，教那南贍部洲人立我為祖，萬代傳名也。
claims.locator: Bab 57, ucapan "Sun Wukong" di Gua Tirai Air

statement.id: Dalam novel, "Sun Wukong" di Gua Tirai Air berkata bahwa ia memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya, dan bahwa ia sendiri akan pergi ke Barat untuk menghadap Buddha dan mengambil kitab, agar dunia mengangkatnya sebagai perintis dan namanya dikenang turun-temurun.
statement.en: In the novel, the "Sun Wukong" at the Water Curtain Cave says that he beat Tang Sanzang and took his baggage, and that he himself will go west to worship the Buddha and fetch the scriptures, so that the world will honor him as a founder and his name will be passed down for generations.

claims.quote: 妖精神通，與孫大聖無二。幽冥之神，能有多少法力？故此不能擒拿。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Diting (諦聽) berkata di alam baka bahwa kesaktian siluman itu sama dengan Sun Wukong, sehingga para dewa alam baka tidak mampu menangkapnya.
statement.en: In the novel, Diting (諦聽) says in the underworld that the demon's powers are the same as Sun Wukong's, so the gods of the underworld cannot capture him.

claims.quote: 又有四猴混世，不入十類之種。」菩薩道：「敢問是那四猴？」如來道：「第一是靈明石猴，通變化，識天時，知地利，移星換斗；第二是赤尻馬猴，曉陰陽，會人事，善出入，避死延生；第三是通臂猿猴，拿日月，縮千山，辨休咎，乾坤摩弄；第四是六耳獼猴，善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來, Buddha) menyebut empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk: kera batu Lingming (靈明石猴), kera pantat merah (赤尻馬猴), kera lengan panjang (通臂猿猴), dan yang keempat Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, dan memahami segala hal.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來, the Buddha) names four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings: the Lingming stone monkey (靈明石猴), the red-buttocked horse monkey (赤尻馬猴), the long-armed ape (通臂猿猴), and the fourth, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.

claims.quote: 此猴若立一處，能知千里外之事；凡人說話，亦能知之。故此善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。與真悟空同像同音者，六耳獼猴也。

statement.id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來) berkata bahwa bila kera ini berdiri di satu tempat ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan juga ucapan manusia, dan bahwa Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) adalah yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong (真悟空) yang asli.
statement.en: In the novel, Rulai (如來) says that when this monkey stands in one place he can know events a thousand li away and also what people say, and that Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) is the one who matches the real Sun Wukong (真悟空) in form and voice.

claims.quote: 那獼猴毛骨悚然，料著難脫，即忙搖身一變，變作個蜜蜂兒，往上便飛。如來將金缽盂撇起去，正蓋著那蜂兒，落下來。

statement.id: Dalam novel, kera itu berubah menjadi seekor lebah (蜜蜂兒) dan terbang ke atas, tetapi Rulai (如來) melemparkan mangkuk emas (金缽盂) yang jatuh menutupi lebah itu.
statement.en: In the novel, the monkey transforms into a bee (蜜蜂兒) and flies upward, but Rulai (如來) throws his golden bowl (金缽盂), which falls and covers the bee.

claims.quote: 大眾一發上前，把缽盂揭起，果然見了本像，是一個六耳獼猴。孫大聖忍不住，掄起鐵棒，劈頭一下打死，至今絕此一種。

statement.id: Dalam novel, ketika mangkuk diangkat, tampaklah wujud aslinya, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) tak tahan dan memukul kepalanya dengan tongkat besi sampai mati, sehingga jenis ini punah.
statement.en: In the novel, when the bowl is lifted his true form appears, a Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) cannot hold back and strikes his head dead with the iron staff, so that this kind is extinct.

claims.quote: 菩薩道：「唐僧，前日打你的，乃假行者六耳獼猴也。幸如來知識，已被悟空打死。

statement.id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva memberi tahu Tang Sanzang bahwa yang memukulnya tempo hari adalah Sun Wukong palsu (假行者), yaitu Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang telah dibunuh Sun Wukong berkat pengenalan Rulai.
statement.en: In the novel, the Bodhisattva tells Tang Sanzang that the one who struck him the other day was the false Sun Wukong (假行者), Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), who has been killed by Sun Wukong thanks to Rulai's recognition.

claims.quote: The Six-eared Macaque's name is a likely nod to the old saying that "a secret is not safe between six ears"

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, nama Six-eared Macaque kemungkinan merujuk pada pepatah lama bahwa "rahasia tidak aman di antara enam telinga".
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, the name of the Six-eared Macaque is a likely nod to the old saying that "a secret is not safe between six ears".

claims.quote: Monkey symbolizes the mind in Chinese Buddhism, and the two monkeys are likely metaphors for zhenxin (真心; "true mind") and wangxin (妄心; "false mind")

statement.id: Menurut tafsir yang dicatat Wikipedia, kera melambangkan pikiran dalam Buddhisme Tiongkok, dan kedua kera itu kemungkinan metafora zhenxin (真心, "pikiran sejati") dan wangxin (妄心, "pikiran palsu").
statement.en: According to an interpretation recorded by Wikipedia, the monkey symbolizes the mind in Chinese Buddhism, and the two monkeys are likely metaphors for zhenxin (真心, "true mind") and wangxin (妄心, "false mind").

claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, the Ming dynasty Xu Xiyouji

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia, Six-Eared Macaque dilahirkan kembali dalam salah satu sekuel tidak resmi paling awal dari Xiyouji, yaitu Xu Xiyouji dari dinasti Ming.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia, the Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, the Ming dynasty Xu Xiyouji.

claims.quote: Hongmei Sun argues that Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme"

statement.id: Menurut Hongmei Sun yang dikutip Wikipedia, pembunuhan Sun Wukong atas rekan, saingan, dan kembaran dirinya adalah "pertentangan diri yang ekstrem" (self-contradiction to an extreme).
statement.en: According to Hongmei Sun as cited by Wikipedia, Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme".

claims.quote: No one is able to differentiate between the real and the fake Sun Wukong—the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", preventing the pilgrims from differentiating between him and Sun Wukong—until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, tak seorang pun dapat membedakan Sun Wukong asli dan palsu; mantra penyamaran Six-Eared Macaque begitu baik sehingga ia juga bereaksi terhadap "Headache Sutra", sampai keduanya menghadap Buddha, yang menjelaskan tentang empat primata spiritual.
statement.en: According to Wikipedia's summary, no one can tell the real Sun Wukong from the fake; the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.

short_description.id: Abumi-guchi adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien dalam kumpulan ilustrasi makhluk gaibnya.
short_description.en: Abumi-guchi is a Japanese yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien in his collection of supernatural beings.

long_description.id:
Abumi-guchi digambarkan sebagai yōkai berbulu yang namanya secara harfiah berarti “mulut sanggurdi”. Toriyama Sekien memasukkannya ke Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. Halaman berkas Commons mencatat ilustrasi tersebut bertanggal 1784.

Dalam bahasa Jepang namanya ditulis 鐙口 dan dibaca あぶみくち. Ia digambarkan sebagai yōkai berwujud sanggurdi (abumi, salah satu perlengkapan berkuda) yang ditumbuhi mulut dan mata. Keterangan Sekien hampir tidak menjelaskan jenis yōkai ini, sehingga muncul dugaan bahwa ia adalah sanggurdi seorang panglima yang gugur dan dibiarkan terbuang di padang.

Sekien menggambar Abumi-guchi pada halaman bentang yang sama dengan Kurayarō (鞍野郎). Keduanya juga diduga diciptakan dengan motif Tsurezuregusa, yang pada bagian ke-186 memuat peringatan tentang perlengkapan berkuda seperti pelana. Mizuki Shigeru menjelaskan bahwa Abumi-guchi menanti tuan yang tak akan kembali seperti anjing menanti pemiliknya, tetapi Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro sendiri tidak memuat tradisi demikian.
long_description.en:
Abumi-guchi is depicted as a furry yōkai whose name literally means “stirrup mouth.” Toriyama Sekien included it in Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. The Commons file page dates the illustration to 1784.

In Japanese the name is written 鐙口 and read あぶみくち. It is depicted as a yōkai in the form of a stirrup (abumi, a piece of horse tack) with a mouth and eyes. Sekien's caption hardly explains what kind of yōkai it is, so it has been suggested that it is the stirrup of a military commander killed in battle and left abandoned in the field.

Sekien drew Abumi-guchi on the same double-page spread as Kurayarō (鞍野郎). The two are also thought to have been created on the motif of Tsurezuregusa, which in section 186 contains a caution about horse tack such as saddles. Mizuki Shigeru explains that Abumi-guchi waits for a master who will not return, like a dog waiting for its owner, but Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro itself does not state such a tradition.

short_description.id: Abumi-guchi adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien dalam kumpulan ilustrasi makhluk gaibnya.
short_description.en: Abumi-guchi is a Japanese yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien in his collection of supernatural beings.

long_description.id: Abumi-guchi digambarkan sebagai yōkai berbulu yang namanya secara harfiah berarti “mulut sanggurdi”. Toriyama Sekien memasukkannya ke Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. Halaman berkas Commons mencatat ilustrasi tersebut bertanggal 1784.
long_description.en: Abumi-guchi is depicted as a furry yōkai whose name literally means “stirrup mouth.” Toriyama Sekien included it in Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro. The Commons file page dates the illustration to 1784.

long_description.id: Dalam bahasa Jepang namanya ditulis 鐙口 dan dibaca あぶみくち. Ia digambarkan sebagai yōkai berwujud sanggurdi (abumi, salah satu perlengkapan berkuda) yang ditumbuhi mulut dan mata. Keterangan Sekien hampir tidak menjelaskan jenis yōkai ini, sehingga muncul dugaan bahwa ia adalah sanggurdi seorang panglima yang gugur dan dibiarkan terbuang di padang.
long_description.en: In Japanese the name is written 鐙口 and read あぶみくち. It is depicted as a yōkai in the form of a stirrup (abumi, a piece of horse tack) with a mouth and eyes. Sekien's caption hardly explains what kind of yōkai it is, so it has been suggested that it is the stirrup of a military commander killed in battle and left abandoned in the field.

long_description.id: Sekien menggambar Abumi-guchi pada halaman bentang yang sama dengan Kurayarō (鞍野郎). Keduanya juga diduga diciptakan dengan motif Tsurezuregusa, yang pada bagian ke-186 memuat peringatan tentang perlengkapan berkuda seperti pelana. Mizuki Shigeru menjelaskan bahwa Abumi-guchi menanti tuan yang tak akan kembali seperti anjing menanti pemiliknya, tetapi Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro sendiri tidak memuat tradisi demikian.
long_description.en: Sekien drew Abumi-guchi on the same double-page spread as Kurayarō (鞍野郎). The two are also thought to have been created on the motif of Tsurezuregusa, which in section 186 contains a caution about horse tack such as saddles. Mizuki Shigeru explains that Abumi-guchi waits for a master who will not return, like a dog waiting for its owner, but Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro itself does not state such a tradition.

short_description.id: Baigujing (Siluman Tulang Putih) adalah iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dalam novel Journey to the West. Wujud aslinya kerangka; ia menyamar tiga kali untuk memakan daging Tang Sanzang tetapi dikenali Sun Wukong.
short_description.en: Baigujing (White Bone Spirit) is a shapeshifting demoness in the novel Journey to the West. Her true form is a skeleton; she disguises herself three times to eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang but is recognized by Sun Wukong.

long_description.id:
Baigujing adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat), yang oleh Wikipedia disebut iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dengan wujud asli berupa kerangka. Terjemahan William John Francis Jenner menamainya White Bone Spirit. Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menyebutnya jiangshi yang menjelma pengacau, dan di punggungnya tertulis nama Baigu Furen.

Dalam novel, ia mengetahui bahwa memakan sepotong daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang. Ia lalu menyamar sebagai gadis cantik dengan kendi dan botol, kemudian sebagai perempuan tua dan seorang kakek. Isi kendi ternyata belatung, katak, dan kodok. Sun Wukong, dengan mata api bermata emasnya, mengenali penyamaran itu; ia memakai jieshi fa untuk meninggalkan mayat palsu ketika dipukul.

Pada akhirnya Sun Wukong memukul mati sosok itu dan tubuhnya menjadi setumpuk tengkorak. Zhu Bajie menghasut Tang Sanzang agar tidak percaya bahwa itu siluman, dan Tang Sanzang kembali merapal mantra; akhirnya Sun Wukong berpamitan dan kembali ke Gua Tirai Air.
long_description.en:
Baigujing is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West, called by Wikipedia a shapeshifting demoness whose true form is a skeleton. The William John Francis Jenner translation names her White Bone Spirit. In the novel, Sun Wukong calls her a jiangshi that has turned into a troublemaker, and her back bears the name Baigu Furen.

In the novel, she learns that eating a piece of the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life. She disguises herself as a beautiful girl with a jar and bottle, then as an old woman and an old man. The contents of the jar turn out to be maggots, frogs, and toads. Sun Wukong, with his fiery golden eyes, recognizes the disguise; she uses the jieshi fa technique to leave a false corpse when struck.

In the end Sun Wukong strikes the figure dead and its body becomes a pile of skeleton. Zhu Bajie goads Tang Sanzang into doubting that it was a demon, and Tang Sanzang chants the spell again; in the end Sun Wukong takes his leave and returns to the Water Curtain Cave.

short_description.id: Baigujing (Siluman Tulang Putih) adalah iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dalam novel Journey to the West. Wujud aslinya kerangka; ia menyamar tiga kali untuk memakan daging Tang Sanzang tetapi dikenali Sun Wukong.
short_description.en: Baigujing (White Bone Spirit) is a shapeshifting demoness in the novel Journey to the West. Her true form is a skeleton; she disguises herself three times to eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang but is recognized by Sun Wukong.

long_description.id: Baigujing adalah tokoh sastra dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat), yang oleh Wikipedia disebut iblis perempuan pengubah wujud dengan wujud asli berupa kerangka. Terjemahan William John Francis Jenner menamainya White Bone Spirit. Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menyebutnya jiangshi yang menjelma pengacau, dan di punggungnya tertulis nama Baigu Furen.
long_description.en: Baigujing is a literary character from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West, called by Wikipedia a shapeshifting demoness whose true form is a skeleton. The William John Francis Jenner translation names her White Bone Spirit. In the novel, Sun Wukong calls her a jiangshi that has turned into a troublemaker, and her back bears the name Baigu Furen.

long_description.id: Dalam novel, ia mengetahui bahwa memakan sepotong daging Tang Sanzang memberi umur panjang. Ia lalu menyamar sebagai gadis cantik dengan kendi dan botol, kemudian sebagai perempuan tua dan seorang kakek. Isi kendi ternyata belatung, katak, dan kodok. Sun Wukong, dengan mata api bermata emasnya, mengenali penyamaran itu; ia memakai jieshi fa untuk meninggalkan mayat palsu ketika dipukul.
long_description.en: In the novel, she learns that eating a piece of the flesh of Tang Sanzang grants long life. She disguises herself as a beautiful girl with a jar and bottle, then as an old woman and an old man. The contents of the jar turn out to be maggots, frogs, and toads. Sun Wukong, with his fiery golden eyes, recognizes the disguise; she uses the jieshi fa technique to leave a false corpse when struck.

long_description.id: Pada akhirnya Sun Wukong memukul mati sosok itu dan tubuhnya menjadi setumpuk tengkorak. Zhu Bajie menghasut Tang Sanzang agar tidak percaya bahwa itu siluman, dan Tang Sanzang kembali merapal mantra; akhirnya Sun Wukong berpamitan dan kembali ke Gua Tirai Air.
long_description.en: In the end Sun Wukong strikes the figure dead and its body becomes a pile of skeleton. Zhu Bajie goads Tang Sanzang into doubting that it was a demon, and Tang Sanzang chants the spell again; in the end Sun Wukong takes his leave and returns to the Water Curtain Cave.

short_description.id: Princess Iron Fan (Tieshan Gongzhu) adalah iblis perempuan atau raksasi (Rākṣasī) dalam novel Journey to the West. Ia istri Bull Demon King, ibu Red Boy, dan pemilik kipas pisang yang bisa memadamkan api dan mengibaskan orang jauh-jauh.
short_description.en: Princess Iron Fan (Tieshan Gongzhu) is a demoness, or female rakshasa (Rākṣasī), in the novel Journey to the West. She is the wife of Bull Demon King, the mother of Red Boy, and the owner of a banana-leaf fan that puts out fire and blows people far away.

long_description.id:
Princess Iron Fan adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat). Wikipedia menyebutnya iblis perempuan yang cantik, istri Bull Demon King, dan ibu Red Boy. Dalam novel ia juga disebut Luocha Nü (羅剎女), yaitu Rākṣasī, sehingga wujudnya adalah raksasi, bukan manusia biasa.

Ia memiliki kipas pisang (芭蕉扇). Menurut novel, kipas itu bila dimohon memadamkan api dengan satu kibasan, membangkitkan angin dengan dua, dan menurunkan hujan dengan tiga. Orang yang terkena kibasannya terbawa delapan puluh empat ribu li. Ketika Sun Wukong datang untuk meminjamnya, ia bertarung dengannya dan menyapu Sun Wukong dengan kibasan itu. Dalam bab yang sama Sun Wukong juga berkata bahwa ia sudah berada di dalam perutnya.

Menurut dewa bumi dalam novel, suaminya telah meninggalkannya dan tinggal di Gua Moyun di Gunung Jilei, tempat Yumian Gongzhu berada. Dalam bab berikutnya, setelah para dewa menaklukkan suaminya, ia keluar membawa kipas dan menyerahkannya kepada Sun Wukong; ia juga memberi tahu bahwa kipas itu harus dikibaskan 49 kali untuk memutus akar api.
long_description.en:
Princess Iron Fan is a literary character from the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. Wikipedia calls her a beautiful demoness, the wife of Bull Demon King, and the mother of Red Boy. In the novel she is also called Luocha Nü (羅剎女), that is Rākṣasī, so she is a female rakshasa rather than an ordinary human.

She owns a banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇). According to the novel, the fan, if obtained, puts out fire with one fanning, raises wind with two, and brings rain with three. A person fanned by it is carried eighty-four thousand li. When Sun Wukong comes to borrow it, she fights him and sweeps him away with the fan. In the same chapter Sun Wukong also says he is already inside her belly.

According to the earth deity in the novel, her husband has abandoned her and lives at Moyun Cave on Jilei Mountain, where Yumian Gongzhu lives. In the following chapter, after the gods subdue her husband, she comes out with the fan and hands it to Sun Wukong; she also tells him the fan must be waved 49 times to cut the root of the fire.

summary.id: Sun Wukong mendatangi Gua Pisang di Gunung Cuiyun untuk meminjam kipas. Luocha Nü bertarung dengannya dan menyapunya dengan kipas, dan Sun Wukong berkata bahwa ia sudah berada di dalam perutnya. Pada akhirnya, setelah para dewa menaklukkan suaminya, ia menyerahkan kipas itu dan menjelaskan cara memutus akar api.
summary.en: Sun Wukong goes to the Banana Cave on Cuiyun Mountain to borrow the fan. Luocha Nü fights him and sweeps him away with the fan, and Sun Wukong says he is already inside her belly. In the end, after the gods subdue her husband, she hands over the fan and explains how to cut the root of the fire.

short_description.id: Akabeko adalah sapi merah misterius dalam legenda Aizu yang membantu pembangunan Kuil Enzoji. Kisahnya mengilhami mainan rakyat setempat.
short_description.en: Akabeko is a mysterious red cow in an Aizu legend that helped build Enzoji Temple. Its story inspired a local folk toy.

long_description.id:
Salah satu cerita asal-usul Akabeko berpusat pada pembangunan Kuil Enzoji di Aizu. Menurut cerita itu, seekor sapi merah yang tidak dikenal muncul, memimpin ternak lain, dan terus bekerja sampai pengangkutan bahan bangunan selesai. Penduduk yang berterima kasih kemudian mendirikan arca sapi tersebut di lingkungan kuil.

Cerita sapi itu kemudian menjadi dasar pembuatan mainan kecil Akabeko di Aizu. Mainan dari bubur kertas tersebut memiliki kepala yang dapat bergoyang. Dalam tradisi setempat, mainan ini juga dipandang sebagai pembawa keberuntungan dan pelindung dari penyakit.
long_description.en:
One origin story places Akabeko at the building of Enzoji Temple in Aizu. In this account, an unknown red cow appeared, led the other cattle, and worked until the transport of building materials was finished. Grateful residents then erected statues of the cow in the temple grounds.

The cow story later inspired small Akabeko toys in Aizu. These papier-mâché toys have bobbing heads. In local tradition, the toys have also been regarded as good-luck charms and protection from illness.

era: The temple-building legend is set around 807.

long_description.id: Salah satu cerita asal-usul Akabeko berpusat pada pembangunan Kuil Enzoji di Aizu. Menurut cerita itu, seekor sapi merah yang tidak dikenal muncul, memimpin ternak lain, dan terus bekerja sampai pengangkutan bahan bangunan selesai. Penduduk yang berterima kasih kemudian mendirikan arca sapi tersebut di lingkungan kuil.
long_description.en: One origin story places Akabeko at the building of Enzoji Temple in Aizu. In this account, an unknown red cow appeared, led the other cattle, and worked until the transport of building materials was finished. Grateful residents then erected statues of the cow in the temple grounds.

long_description.id: Cerita sapi itu kemudian menjadi dasar pembuatan mainan kecil Akabeko di Aizu. Mainan dari bubur kertas tersebut memiliki kepala yang dapat bergoyang. Dalam tradisi setempat, mainan ini juga dipandang sebagai pembawa keberuntungan dan pelindung dari penyakit.
long_description.en: The cow story later inspired small Akabeko toys in Aizu. These papier-mâché toys have bobbing heads. In local tradition, the toys have also been regarded as good-luck charms and protection from illness.

short_description.id: Ōyamatsumi adalah kami pegunungan dalam tradisi Jepang, dengan kisah asal-usul berbeda dalam Kojiki dan Nihongi.
short_description.en: Ōyamatsumi is a mountain kami of Japanese tradition whose origins differ between the Kojiki and Nihongi.

long_description.id:
Ōyamatsumi adalah kami yang namanya terkait dengan roh penghuni gunung; ensiklopedia Shinto menafsirkannya sebagai dewa agung yang menguasai pegunungan. Kojiki menyebutnya salah satu dewa yang muncul ketika Izanagi dan Izanami melahirkan daratan. Sebuah varian dalam Nihongi justru menyebutnya terlahir dari salah satu bagian Kagutsuchi setelah dipotong Izanagi. Kedua kisah itu dicatat sebagai versi asal-usul yang berbeda.

Kuil untuk kami bernama Ōyamatsumi terdapat di berbagai tempat di Jepang. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat, nama itu juga dapat dipakai bagi kami suatu gunung atau roh orang yang meninggal di pegunungan. Sebuah kuil di Toba memujanya sebagai dewa gunung dan laut; menurut catatan setempat, kuil itu dipindahkan ketika pembangunan Kastel Toba berlangsung. Dua festival musim semi di sana menampilkan tarian berkostum serta arak-arakan mikoshi.
long_description.en:
Ōyamatsumi is a kami whose name relates to a spirit dwelling in a mountain; a Shinto encyclopedia explains it as a great deity with authority over mountains. The Kojiki names him among the deities born when Izanagi and Izanami produced the land. An alternate account in the Nihongi says he arose from a part of Kagutsuchi after Izanagi cut him up. These are distinct accounts of his origin.

Shrines to kami named Ōyamatsumi are found across Japan. In folk religion, the name can also denote the kami of a particular mountain or the spirit of someone who died there. A shrine in Toba honors him as a deity of mountains and seas; a local account says it was moved during construction of Toba Castle. Two spring festivals there include a costumed dance and a mikoshi procession.

short_description.id: Tenjin adalah nama ilahi bagi Sugawara no Michizane yang dipuja sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan setelah wafat dalam pembuangan.
short_description.en: Tenjin is the deified Sugawara no Michizane, revered as a patron of scholarship after his death in exile.

long_description.id:
Tenjin mula-mula berarti “dewa langit”, tetapi kemudian terutama merujuk pada roh cendekiawan istana Sugawara no Michizane. Ia dibuang karena intrik politik dan wafat dalam pembuangan. Kemudian bencana dikaitkan dengan rohnya yang murka; istana memulihkan kedudukannya secara anumerta dan ia akhirnya didewakan. Dalam kepercayaan sesudahnya, ia dihormati sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan.

Istilah tenjin juga pernah dipakai untuk dewa langit sebelum pemujaan Michizane berkembang, sehingga makna awalnya perlu dibedakan dari tokoh ini. Sebuah ensiklopedia menjelaskan bahwa sosok Tenjin memadukan roh Michizane dengan gambaran dewa guntur dan beberapa unsur keagamaan lain. Kuil Kitano Tenmangū didedikasikan kepadanya pada 947; pemujaannya kemudian menyebar lewat kuil cabang. Kini para pelajar juga mendatanginya berkaitan dengan ujian masuk sekolah dan universitas.
long_description.en:
Tenjin originally meant “heavenly god” but later referred chiefly to the spirit of the court scholar Sugawara no Michizane. Political intrigue sent him into exile, where he died. Later disasters were attributed to his angry spirit; the court restored his rank after death and he was eventually deified. In later devotion he is revered as a patron of scholarship.

The word tenjin was also used for heavenly deities before devotion to Michizane developed, so its earlier sense should be distinguished from this figure. An encyclopedia describes Tenjin as combining Michizane’s spirit with a thunder deity and other religious elements. Kitano Tenmangū was dedicated to him in 947, followed by branch shrines. Students today also turn to him in connection with school and university entrance exams.

short_description.id: Tenjin adalah nama ilahi bagi Sugawara no Michizane yang dipuja sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan setelah wafat dalam pembuangan.
short_description.en: Tenjin is the deified Sugawara no Michizane, revered as a patron of scholarship after his death in exile.

long_description.id: Tenjin mula-mula berarti “dewa langit”, tetapi kemudian terutama merujuk pada roh cendekiawan istana Sugawara no Michizane. Ia dibuang karena intrik politik dan wafat dalam pembuangan. Kemudian bencana dikaitkan dengan rohnya yang murka; istana memulihkan kedudukannya secara anumerta dan ia akhirnya didewakan. Dalam kepercayaan sesudahnya, ia dihormati sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan.
long_description.en: Tenjin originally meant “heavenly god” but later referred chiefly to the spirit of the court scholar Sugawara no Michizane. Political intrigue sent him into exile, where he died. Later disasters were attributed to his angry spirit; the court restored his rank after death and he was eventually deified. In later devotion he is revered as a patron of scholarship.

long_description.id: Istilah tenjin juga pernah dipakai untuk dewa langit sebelum pemujaan Michizane berkembang, sehingga makna awalnya perlu dibedakan dari tokoh ini. Sebuah ensiklopedia menjelaskan bahwa sosok Tenjin memadukan roh Michizane dengan gambaran dewa guntur dan beberapa unsur keagamaan lain. Kuil Kitano Tenmangū didedikasikan kepadanya pada 947; pemujaannya kemudian menyebar lewat kuil cabang. Kini para pelajar juga mendatanginya berkaitan dengan ujian masuk sekolah dan universitas.
long_description.en: The word tenjin was also used for heavenly deities before devotion to Michizane developed, so its earlier sense should be distinguished from this figure. An encyclopedia describes Tenjin as combining Michizane’s spirit with a thunder deity and other religious elements. Kitano Tenmangū was dedicated to him in 947, followed by branch shrines. Students today also turn to him in connection with school and university entrance exams.

cultural_context.id: Tenjin dipuja sebagai pelindung ilmu pengetahuan di kuil-kuil, dan pelajar mendatangi kuilnya menjelang ujian.
cultural_context.en: Tenjin is venerated as a patron of scholarship, and students visit his shrine when preparing for examinations.
