claim.en: According to this text even the omniscient Ganesa took a moment to consider, while Vyasa continued to compose many other verses.

claims_provenance.quote: Even the omniscient Ganesa took a moment to consider; while Vyasa, however, continued to compose other verses in great abundance.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Project Gutenberg — The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, Volume 1 (Books 1, 2 and 3)

claim.id: Nama Ganesha adalah gabungan kata Sanskerta gana, berarti "kelompok, kumpulan, atau sistem kategori", dan isha, berarti "tuan atau penguasa".
claim.en: The name Ganesha is a Sanskrit compound of gana, meaning "group, multitude, or categorical system", and isha, meaning "lord or master".

claims_provenance.quote: The name Ganesha is a Sanskrit compound, joining the words gana (gaṇa), meaning a 'group, multitude, or categorical system' and isha (īśa), meaning 'lord or master'.

claim.id: Ganesha juga dikenal sebagai Ganapati, Vinayaka, dan Pillaiyar; ia salah satu dewa Hindu yang paling terkenal dan dipuja, serta Dewa Tertinggi dalam sekte Ganapatya.
claim.en: Ganesha, also known as Ganapati, Vinayaka and Pillaiyar, is one of the best-known and most revered deities in the Hindu pantheon and the Supreme god in the Ganapatya sect.

claims_provenance.quote: also known as Ganapati, Vinayaka and Pillaiyar, is one of the best-known and most revered and worshipped deities in the Hindu pantheon and is the Supreme god in the Ganapatya sect.

claim.id: Ganesha juga bergelar "Pratham Pujya", dewa yang dipuja lebih dulu sebelum pemujaan dewa lain.
claim.en: Ganesha also holds the title "Pratham Pujya", the god to be worshipped first before any other deity.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha also holds the Title of "Pratham Pujya" (the god to be worshipped initially before the worship of any other Deity).

claim.id: Sebagai dewa permulaan, Ganesha dihormati pada awal upacara dan ritus; ia juga diseru saat menulis sebagai pelindung huruf dan ilmu.
claim.en: As god of beginnings Ganesha is honoured at the start of rites and ceremonies, and invoked during writing sessions as patron of letters and learning.

claims_provenance.quote: As the god of beginnings, he is honoured at the start of rites and ceremonies. Ganesha is also invoked during writing sessions as a patron of letters and learning.

claim.id: Teks-teks utama tentang Ganesha mencakup Ganesha Purana, Mudgala Purana, dan Ganapati Atharvasirsha.
claim.en: The principal texts on Ganesha include the Ganesha Purana, the Mudgala Purana, and the Ganapati Atharvasirsha.

claims_provenance.quote: The principal texts on Ganesha include the Ganesha Purana, the Mudgala Purana, and the Ganapati Atharvasirsha.

claim.id: Amarakosha, kamus Sanskerta awal, mencantumkan delapan sinonim Ganesha, di antaranya Vinayaka, Vighnarāja, Dvaimātura (berbunda dua), Gaṇādhipa, dan Ekadanta (bergading satu).
claim.en: The Amarakosha, an early Sanskrit lexicon, lists eight synonyms of Ganesha, including Vinayaka, Vighnarāja, Dvaimātura (one who has two mothers), Gaṇādhipa, and Ekadanta (one who has one tusk).

claims_provenance.quote: The Amarakosha, an early Sanskrit lexicon, lists eight synonyms of Ganesha: Vinayaka, Vighnarāja (equivalent to Vighnesha), Dvaimātura (one who has two mothers), Gaṇādhipa (equivalent to Ganapati and Ganesha), Ekadanta (one who has one tusk)

claim.id: Ganesha dipuja secara populer sebagai penyingkir rintangan, meski menurut tradisi ia juga menaruh rintangan di jalan orang yang perlu dihentikan; karena itu ia sering dipuja sebelum memulai sesuatu yang baru.
claim.en: Ganesha is popularly worshipped as a remover of obstacles, though traditionally he also places obstacles in the path of those who need to be checked; hence he is often worshipped before beginning anything new.

claims_provenance.quote: He is popularly worshipped as a remover of obstacles, though traditionally he also places obstacles in the path of those who need to be checked. Hence, he is often worshipped by the people before they begin anything new.

claim.id: Gambar dan sebutan paling awal mencatat Ganesha sebagai dewa utama di wilayah Indonesia, Thailand, Kamboja, dan Vietnam masa kini, berasal dari abad ke-7 dan ke-8, dan mencerminkan contoh India abad ke-5 atau lebih awal.
claim.en: The earliest images and mentions list Ganesha as a major deity in present-day Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam, dating to the 7th and 8th centuries and mirroring Indian examples of the 5th century or earlier.

claims_provenance.quote: The earliest images and mention lists Ganesha as a major deity in present-day Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam dating to the 7th and 8th centuries, and these mirror Indian examples of the 5th century or earlier.

claim.id: Sebagian teks menyebut Ganesha lahir berkepala gajah, tetapi dalam kebanyakan kisah ia memperolehnya kemudian; motif paling sering adalah Parvati menciptakannya dari tanah liat dan Shiva memenggalnya.
claim.en: Some texts say Ganesha was born with an elephant head, but in most stories he acquires it later; the most recurrent motif is that Parvati created him from clay and Shiva beheaded him.

claims_provenance.quote: While some texts say that Ganesha was born with an elephant head, he acquires the head later in most stories. The most recurrent motif in these stories is that Ganesha was created by Parvati using clay to protect her and Shiva beheaded him when Ganesha came between Shiva and Parvati.

claim.id: Kisah lain menyebut Ganesha tercipta langsung dari tawa Shiva; karena Shiva menganggapnya terlalu memikat, ia memberinya kepala gajah dan perut buncit.
claim.en: Another story says Ganesha was created directly by Shiva's laughter; because Shiva considered him too alluring, he gave him an elephant head and a protruding belly.

claims_provenance.quote: Another story says that Ganesha was created directly by Shiva's laughter. Because Shiva considered Ganesha too alluring, he gave him the head of an elephant and a protruding belly.

claim.id: Nama paling awal Ganesha adalah Ekadanta (Bergading Satu), merujuk pada satu gading utuhnya karena yang lain patah; beberapa arca paling awal memperlihatkannya memegang gading patah itu.
claim.en: Ganesha's earliest name was Ekadanta (One Tusked), referring to his single whole tusk, the other being broken; some of the earliest images show him holding his broken tusk.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha's earliest name was Ekadanta (One Tusked), referring to his single whole tusk, the other being broken. Some of the earliest images of Ganesha show him holding his broken tusk.

claim.id: Dalam wujud baku, Ganesha biasanya memegang kapak atau pengait di satu lengan atas dan pasha (jerat) di lengan atas lainnya.
claim.en: In the standard configuration Ganesha typically holds an axe or a goad in one upper arm and a pasha (noose) in the other.

claims_provenance.quote: In the standard configuration, Ganesha typically holds an axe or a goad in one upper arm and a pasha (noose) in the other upper arm.

claim.id: Ganesha sering digambarkan menunggangi atau ditemani seekor tikus; menurut Martin-Dubost, tikus mulai tampil sebagai kendaraan utama dalam arca Ganesha di India tengah dan barat pada abad ke-7.
claim.en: Ganesha is often shown riding on or attended by a mouse; per Martin-Dubost the rat began to appear as principal vehicle in sculptures in central and western India during the 7th century.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha is often shown riding on or attended by a mouse. ... Martin-Dubost says that the rat began to appear as the principal vehicle in sculptures of Ganesha in central and western India during the 7th century; the rat was always placed close to his feet.

claim.id: Para pemuja mempersembahkan manisan seperti modaka dan bola manis kecil bernama laddu kepada Ganesha; ia sering digambarkan membawa mangkuk manisan yang disebut modakapātra.
claim.en: Devotees offer Ganesha sweets such as modaka and small sweet balls called laddus; he is often shown carrying a bowl of sweets called a modakapātra.

claims_provenance.quote: Devotees offer Ganesha sweets such as modaka and small sweet balls called laddus. He is often shown carrying a bowl of sweets, called a modakapātra.

claim.id: Festival tahunan menghormati Ganesha selama sepuluh hari, dimulai pada Ganesh Chaturthi yang biasanya jatuh pada akhir Agustus atau awal September, dengan membawa masuk arca tanah liat sebagai lambang kunjungan sang dewa.
claim.en: An annual festival honours Ganesha for ten days, starting on Ganesh Chaturthi in late August or early September, beginning with clay idols brought in to symbolise the god's visit.

claims_provenance.quote: An annual festival honours Ganesha for ten days, starting on Ganesh Chaturthi, which typically falls in late August or early September. The festival begins with people bringing in clay idols of Ganesha, symbolising the god's visit.

claim.id: Pada 1893, Lokmanya Tilak mengubah festival tahunan Ganesha dari perayaan keluarga yang bersifat pribadi menjadi acara publik yang besar.
claim.en: In 1893 Lokmanya Tilak transformed this annual Ganesha festival from private family celebrations into a grand public event.

claims_provenance.quote: In 1893, Lokmanya Tilak transformed this annual Ganesha festival from private family celebrations into a grand public event.

claim.id: Sebagai dewa peralihan, Ganesha ditempatkan di pintu banyak kuil Hindu untuk menolak yang tak layak, selaras dengan perannya sebagai penjaga pintu Parvati.
claim.en: As god of transitions Ganesha is placed at the doorway of many Hindu temples to keep out the unworthy, analogous to his role as Parvati's doorkeeper.

claims_provenance.quote: As the god of transitions, he is placed at the doorway of many Hindu temples to keep out the unworthy, which is analogous to his role as Parvati's doorkeeper.

claim.id: Delapan kuil Ashtavinayak terletak dalam radius 100 kilometer dari kota Pune; masing-masing merayakan satu bentuk Ganapati dengan kisahnya sendiri: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar, dan Ranjangaon.
claim.en: The eight Ashtavinayak shrines lie within a 100-kilometre radius of Pune; each celebrates a particular form of Ganapati with its own lore: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar, and Ranjangaon.

claims_provenance.quote: Located within a 100-kilometer radius of the city of Pune, each of the eight shrines celebrates a particular form of Ganapati, complete with its own lore. The eight shrines are: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar and Ranjangaon.

claim.id: Ganesha tampil dalam wujud klasiknya sebagai dewa yang mudah dikenali dengan atribut ikonografi yang jelas pada awal abad ke-4 hingga ke-5 M.
claim.en: Ganesha appeared in his classic form as a clearly recognizable deity with well-defined iconographic attributes in the early 4th to 5th centuries CE.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha appeared in his classic form as a clearly-recognizable deity with well-defined iconographic attributes in the early 4th to 5th centuries CE.

claim.id: Kultus mandiri dengan Ganesha sebagai dewa utama telah mapan pada sekitar abad ke-10.
claim.en: An independent cult with Ganesha as the primary deity was well established by about the 10th century.

claims_provenance.quote: An independent cult with Ganesha as the primary deity was well established by about the 10th century.

claim.id: Para pemuja percaya bahwa bila Ganesha diambil hatinya, ia memberi keberhasilan, kemakmuran, dan perlindungan dari kesulitan.
claim.en: Devotees believe that if Ganesha is propitiated he grants success, prosperity, and protection against adversity.

claims_provenance.quote: Devotees believe that if Ganesha is propitiated, he grants success, prosperity and protection against adversity.

claim.id: Ganesha dipandang sebagai dewa lintas sekte: umat Hindu dari semua aliran menyerunya pada awal doa, kegiatan penting, dan upacara; penari dan pemusik, terutama di India selatan, memulai pertunjukan dengan doa kepadanya.
claim.en: Ganesha is a non-sectarian deity: Hindus of all denominations invoke him at the start of prayers, important undertakings, and ceremonies, and dancers and musicians, particularly in southern India, begin performances with a prayer to him.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha is a non-sectarian deity. Hindus of all denominations invoke him at the beginning of prayers, important undertakings, and religious ceremonies. Dancers and musicians, particularly in southern India, begin art performances such as the Bharatanatyam dance with a prayer to Ganesha.

claim.id: Di kalangan orang Indonesia yang mayoritas beragama Islam, Ganesha tidak dipuja tetapi dipandang sebagai simbol pengetahuan, kebijaksanaan, dan pendidikan; banyak universitas negeri Indonesia memuat gambarnya di kampus atau logo.
claim.en: Among predominantly Muslim Indonesians Ganesha is not worshipped but seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and education, and many Indonesian public universities feature his likeness in their grounds or logo.

claims_provenance.quote: Amongst Indonesians who predominantly profess the Islamic faith, Ganesha is not worshipped, but seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom and education. Many Indonesian public universities feature Ganesha's likeness in their grounds or logo.

claim.id: Arca Ganesha ditemukan di seluruh kawasan Asia Tenggara maritim, sering di samping tempat suci Shiva; bentuk Ganesha dalam seni Hindu di Filipina, Jawa, Bali, dan Kalimantan menunjukkan pengaruh khas daerah.
claim.en: Statues of Ganesha are found throughout the region of Maritime Southeast Asia, often beside Shiva sanctuaries; his forms in the Hindu art of the Philippines, Java, Bali, and Borneo show specific regional influences.

claims_provenance.quote: Statues of Ganesha are found throughout the region, often beside Shiva sanctuaries. The forms of Ganesha found in the Hindu art of the Philippines, Java, Bali, and Borneo show specific regional influences.

claim.id: Di Jepang, tempat Ganesha dikenal sebagai Kangiten, kultus Ganesha pertama kali disebut pada 806.
claim.en: In Japan, where Ganesha is known as Kangiten, the Ganesha cult was first mentioned in 806.

claims_provenance.quote: In Japan, where Ganesha is known as Kangiten, the Ganesha cult was first mentioned in 806.

claim.id: Salah satu bentuk populernya, Heramba-Ganapati, berkepala gajah lima, dan variasi lain jumlah kepala yang lebih jarang diketahui.
claim.en: One of his popular forms, Heramba-Ganapati, has five elephant heads, and other less common variations in the number of heads are known.

claims_provenance.quote: One of his popular forms, Heramba-Ganapati, has five elephant heads, and other less-common variations in the number of heads are known.

claim.id: Ganesha disebut dalam teks Hindu antara abad ke-1 SM dan abad ke-2 M, dan beberapa arca Ganesha dari abad ke-4 dan ke-5 M telah didokumentasikan para sarjana.
claim.en: Ganesha is mentioned in Hindu texts between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE, and a few Ganesha images from the 4th and 5th centuries CE have been documented by scholars.

claims_provenance.quote: Ganesha is mentioned in Hindu texts between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE, and a few Ganesha images from the 4th and 5th centuries CE have been documented by scholars.

claim.id: Dari delapan inkarnasi Ganesha dalam Mudgala Purana, ia memakai tikus bernama Mushaka pada lima inkarnasi, singa sebagai Vakratunda, merak sebagai Vikata, dan Shesha sang ular ilahi sebagai Vighnaraja.
claim.en: Of the eight incarnations of Ganesha in the Mudgala Purana, he uses a mouse named Mushaka in five, a lion as Vakratunda, a peacock as Vikata, and Shesha, the divine serpent, as Vighnaraja.

claims_provenance.quote: Of the eight incarnations of Ganesha described in the Mudgala Purana, Ganesha uses a mouse (shrew) named Mushaka in five of them, a lion in his incarnation as Vakratunda, a peacock in his incarnation as Vikata, and Shesha, the divine serpent, in his incarnation as Vighnaraja.

short_description.id: Ganesha adalah dewa Hindu berkepala gajah, putra Shiva dan Parvati, yang dipuja sebagai penyingkir rintangan dan dihormati di awal banyak kegiatan.
short_description.en: Ganesha is an elephant-headed Hindu deity, son of Shiva and Parvati, worshipped as a remover of obstacles and honoured at the start of many undertakings.

long_description.id: Ganesha adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam agama Hindu. Ia dikenali dari kepala gajah dan tubuh manusia, dikaitkan dengan penulis, pelancong, pelajar, dan perdagangan, serta dipuja sebagai penyingkir rintangan. Ia juga dikenal sebagai Ganapati, Vinayaka, dan Pillaiyar, dan menurut tradisi ia dipuja lebih dulu sebelum dewa lain. Sebuah deskripsi museum menyebutnya putra Shiva dan Parvati, dan umat percaya ia memberi keberhasilan serta kemakmuran. Para pemuja mempersembahkan manisan seperti modaka dan laddu kepadanya.
long_description.en: Ganesha is one of the most important gods in Hinduism. He is recognized by his elephant head and human body, associated with writers, travellers, students, and commerce, and worshipped as a remover of obstacles. He is also known as Ganapati, Vinayaka, and Pillaiyar, and tradition holds that he is worshipped before other gods. A museum description calls him the son of Shiva and Parvati, and devotees believe he grants success and prosperity. Devotees offer him sweets such as modaka and laddus.

long_description.id: Sebuah patung museum menunjukkan tali jerat, kapak, manisan, dan gading di keempat tangannya. Dalam ikonografi ia sering digambarkan membawa gading patah, kapak atau pengait, jerat, dan mangkuk manisan, dan menunggangi atau ditemani seekor tikus. Beberapa kisah menjelaskan kepala gajahnya: dalam kisah yang paling sering, Parvati menciptakannya dari tanah liat dan Shiva memenggalnya lalu menggantikan kepalanya dengan kepala gajah; kisah lain menyebut ia tercipta dari tawa Shiva. Tentang gadingnya yang patah, sumber menyebut ia melemparkannya kepada Bulan yang menertawakannya, atau mematahkannya untuk menyalin Mahabharata yang didiktekan Vyasa.
long_description.en: A museum sculpture shows a lasso, battle-ax, sweet, and tusk in his four hands. In iconography he is often shown with a broken tusk, an axe or goad, a noose, and a bowl of sweets, and riding or attended by a mouse. Several stories explain his elephant head: in the most recurrent one Parvati created him from clay and Shiva beheaded him and replaced the head with an elephant's; another says he was created from Shiva's laughter. For his broken tusk, sources say he hurled it at the laughing Moon, or snapped it off to transcribe the Mahabharata dictated by Vyasa.

long_description.id: Dalam Mahabharata terjemahan Ganguli, Vyasa memanggil Ganesa untuk menuliskan karyanya dan Ganesa bersedia asalkan penanya tidak berhenti. Ganesha juga dipuja dalam tradisi Jain dan Buddha, dan di Jepang dikenal sebagai Kangiten. Gambar dan sebutan paling awal di wilayah Indonesia masa kini berasal dari abad ke-7 dan ke-8, dan di Indonesia ia dipandang sebagai simbol pengetahuan, kebijaksanaan, dan pendidikan.
long_description.en: In Ganguli's translation of the Mahabharata, Vyasa calls Ganesa to write his work and Ganesa agrees provided his pen does not cease. Ganesha is also worshipped in Jain and Buddhist traditions, and in Japan he is known as Kangiten. The earliest images and mentions in present-day Indonesia date to the 7th and 8th centuries, and in Indonesia he is seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and education.

long_description.id: Ganesha dihormati pada awal doa dan upacara oleh umat Hindu dari semua aliran, dan ia ditempatkan di pintu banyak kuil. Festival Ganesh Chaturthi berlangsung sepuluh hari dengan arca tanah liat, dan pada 1893 Lokmanya Tilak mengubahnya dari perayaan keluarga menjadi acara publik besar. Teks-teks utama tentang Ganesha mencakup Ganesha Purana, Mudgala Purana, dan Ganapati Atharvasirsha. Teks Hindu menyebut Ganesha antara abad ke-1 SM dan abad ke-2 M, dan wujud klasiknya muncul pada awal abad ke-4 hingga ke-5 M.
long_description.en: Ganesha is honoured at the start of prayers and ceremonies by Hindus of all denominations, and stands at the doorway of many temples. The Ganesh Chaturthi festival lasts ten days with clay idols, and in 1893 Lokmanya Tilak transformed it from family celebrations into a grand public event. Among the main texts about Ganesha are the Ganesha Purana, the Mudgala Purana, and the Ganapati Atharvasirsha. Hindu texts mention Ganesha between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE, and his classic form appears in the early 4th to 5th centuries CE.

cultural_context.id: Ganesha dipandang sebagai dewa lintas sekte: umat Hindu dari semua aliran menyerunya pada awal doa, kegiatan penting, dan upacara. Di Indonesia, di kalangan yang mayoritas beragama Islam, ia tidak dipuja tetapi dipandang sebagai simbol pengetahuan, kebijaksanaan, dan pendidikan.
cultural_context.en: Ganesha is not tied to a single sect: Hindus of every denomination call on him when beginning prayers, major undertakings, and ceremonies. Among predominantly Muslim Indonesians he is not worshipped but is seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and education.

description.en: In Japan Ganesha is known as Kangiten; the cult was first mentioned in 806.

role.id: Anak Parvati yang berjaga di pintu

summary.id: Dalam salah satu kisah, Parvati membuat Ganesha dari tanah dan menempatkannya sebagai penjaga saat mandi. Shiva pulang dan murka, para bhutagana bertarung dengan sang anak hingga kepalanya terpenggal. Shiva yang menyesal memerintahkan kepala baru dicari dan hewan pertama yang ada adalah gajah. Sebagai ganjaran atas keberaniannya, Shiva menjadikannya pemimpin para bhutagana.
summary.en: In one account, Parvati made Ganesha from earth and set him as guard while she bathed. Shiva returned and was outraged, the bhutaganas fought the boy and his head was cut off. Repentant, Shiva ordered a new head to be found and the first animal available was an elephant. As a reward for his courage Shiva made him leader of the bhutaganas.

summary.id: Dalam kisah yang menjelaskan kaitan Ganesha dengan kecerdasan dan kebijaksanaan, ia bersaing dengan Karthikeya untuk menikah lebih dulu. Ia dinyatakan menang dan menikahi Buddhi (Kebijaksanaan) dan Siddhi (Keberhasilan), putri-putri Prajapati.
summary.en: In a story explaining Ganesha's association with intelligence and wisdom, he competes with Karthikeya to marry first. He is declared the winner and marries Buddhi (Wisdom) and Siddhi (Success), daughters of Prajapati.

title.en: The modakas, the rat, the snake, and the Moon

role.id: Tokoh utama yang jatuh lalu membalas Bulan
role.en: Protagonist who falls, then answers the Moon

summary.id: Dalam salah satu kisah, setelah makan terlalu banyak modaka, Ganesha menunggangi tikus raksasanya, Kroncha. Perutnya pecah saat jatuh dan ia melilitkan ular di perutnya agar tertutup. Ketika Bulan menertawakannya, Ganesha mematahkan ujung salah satu gadingnya dan melemparnya ke wajah Bulan hingga menghitam.
summary.en: In another account, after eating too many modakas Ganesha rode his giant rat Kroncha. His belly burst when he fell and he wound the snake around his midriff to close it. When the Moon laughed at him, Ganesha snapped the tip off one tusk and threw it at the Moon's face, which was struck black.

title.en: Ganesa as scribe of the Mahabharata

summary.id: Dalam terjemahan Ganguli, Vyasa mengingat Ganesa untuk menulis karyanya. Ganesa bersedia asalkan penanya tidak berhenti, dan Vyasa meminta ia berhenti menulis bila ada yang tidak dipahaminya. Ganesa menyetujui dengan mengucapkan Om lalu mulai menulis.
summary.en: In Ganguli's translation, Vyasa calls Ganesa to mind to write his work. Ganesa agrees provided his pen does not cease, and Vyasa asks him to stop writing wherever he does not comprehend. Ganesa assents by saying Om and begins to write.

name.en: The eight Ashtavinayak shrines near Pune

description.id: Delapan kuil dalam radius 100 kilometer dari kota Pune, masing-masing merayakan satu bentuk Ganapati dengan kisahnya sendiri.
description.en: Eight shrines within a 100-kilometre radius of Pune, each celebrating a particular form of Ganapati with its own lore.

description.en: Ganesha appears as a clearly recognizable deity with well-defined iconographic attributes.

description.id: Tikus mulai tampil sebagai kendaraan utama dalam arca Ganesha di India tengah dan barat.
description.en: The rat begins to appear as the principal vehicle in sculptures of Ganesha in central and western India.

description.en: A cult with Ganesha as the primary deity was well established.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Ganesha diseru pada awal banyak upacara dan kegiatan?
learning_questions.en: Why is Ganesha invoked at the start of so many ceremonies and undertakings?

learning_questions.id: Bagaimana berbagai kisah menjelaskan kepala gajah dan gading Ganesha yang patah?
learning_questions.en: How do the different stories explain Ganesha's elephant head and broken tusk?

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Ganesha dipandang sebagai simbol pendidikan di Indonesia meskipun tidak dipuja di sana?
learning_questions.en: Why is Ganesha seen as a symbol of education in Indonesia even where he is not worshipped?

sources.title: The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, Volume 1 (Books 1, 2 and 3)
sources.author: Kisari Mohan Ganguli (trans.)

claims.quote: Ganesha (also Ganesa or Ganapati) is one of the most important gods in Hinduism.

statement.id: Ganesha termasuk dewa penting dalam agama Hindu.
statement.en: Ganesha is an important Hindu deity.

claims.quote: Ganesha is easily recognized with his elephant head and human body

statement.id: Ganesha digambarkan dengan kepala gajah dan tubuh manusia.
statement.en: Ganesha is depicted with an elephant head and human body.

claims.quote: Ganesha is the patron of writers, travellers, students, and commerce, and he removes obstacles blocking new projects.

statement.id: Ganesha melindungi penulis, pengelana, pelajar, dan perdagangan serta menyingkirkan rintangan.
statement.en: Ganesha is patron of writers, travellers, students, and commerce, and removes obstacles.

claims.quote: The potbellied, elephant-headed Hindu god Ganesha, son of Shiva and Parvati, is venerated throughout India. He is believed to bestow success and abundance through his removal of obstacles. Before any important task is begun, an offering is made to Ganesha.

statement.id: Ganesha adalah putra Shiva dan Parvati dan diberi persembahan sebelum tugas penting dimulai.
statement.en: Ganesha is Shiva and Parvati's son and receives offerings before important undertakings.

claims.quote: Repentant, Shiva ordered a new head to be found for the boy and, as the first animal available was an elephant, so Ganesha gained a new elephant head

statement.id: Dalam suatu kisah, Shiva mengganti kepala Ganesha dengan kepala gajah.
statement.en: In one story Shiva had Ganesha's head replaced with an elephant's.

claims.quote: Ganesha is also worshipped as a principal deity in both Jainism and Buddhism.

statement.id: Ganesha juga dipuja dalam tradisi Jain dan Buddha.
statement.en: Ganesha is also worshipped in Jain and Buddhist traditions.

claims.quote: Here, his upper left hand holds a lasso; the upper right, a battle-ax; the lower left, a sweet; and the lower right, one of his own tusks

statement.id: Pada patung museum Ganesha memegang tali, kapak, manisan, dan gadingnya sendiri.
statement.en: In a museum sculpture Ganesha holds a lasso, axe, sweet, and one of his tusks.

claims.quote: Ganesha is mentioned in Hindu texts between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE

statement.id: Teks Hindu menyebut Ganesha antara abad pertama sebelum Masehi dan abad kedua Masehi.
statement.en: Hindu texts mention Ganesha between the first century BCE and the second century CE.

claims.quote: Ganesha is the son of Shiva and Parvati and he is the brother of Karthikeya (or Subrahmanya), the god of war. He was created by his mother using earth which she moulded into the shape of a boy.

statement.id: Ganesha adalah putra Shiva dan Parvati serta saudara Karthikeya (Subrahmanya), dewa perang; menurut kisah ini ia dibuat ibunya dari tanah yang dibentuk menjadi seorang anak laki-laki.
statement.en: Ganesha is the son of Shiva and Parvati and brother of Karthikeya (Subrahmanya), the god of war; in this account his mother created him from earth moulded into the shape of a boy.

claims.quote: As Shiva was away on his meditative wanderings, Parvati set her new son as guard while she bathed. Unexpectedly, Shiva returned home and, on finding the boy, and outraged at his impudence in claiming he was Parvati's son, Shiva called for his gang of demons, the bhutaganas, who fought ferociously with the boy.

statement.id: Saat Shiva pergi bertapa, Parvati menempatkan putranya sebagai penjaga ketika ia mandi. Shiva pulang dan murka, lalu memanggil para bhutagana yang bertarung sengit melawan sang anak.
statement.en: While Shiva was away on meditative wanderings, Parvati set her son as guard while she bathed. Shiva returned, was outraged, and called his bhutaganas, who fought ferociously with the boy.

claims.quote: However, the youngster easily held his own against such fearsome adversaries and Vishnu was forced to intervene in the form of Maya and, whilst the boy was distracted by her beauty, the demons, or Shiva himself, lopped off his head.

statement.id: Sang anak mampu menahan lawan-lawannya hingga Vishnu turun tangan dalam wujud Maya; saat anak itu terpikat kecantikannya, para bhutagana atau Shiva sendiri memenggal kepalanya.
statement.en: The boy held his own until Vishnu intervened in the form of Maya; while he was distracted by her beauty, the demons, or Shiva himself, cut off his head.

claims.quote: As a reward for his great courage in fighting the demons, Shiva made Ganesha the leader of the bhutaganas, hence his name.

statement.id: Sebagai ganjaran atas keberaniannya melawan para bhutagana, Shiva menjadikan Ganesha pemimpin mereka, dan dari situlah namanya.
statement.en: As a reward for his courage in fighting the bhutaganas, Shiva made Ganesha their leader, hence his name.

claims.quote: A story which explains the god's association with intelligence and wisdom is his competition with Karthikeya to be the first to marry. ... Declared the winner, Ganesha promptly married not one but two daughters of Prajapati: Buddhi (Wisdom) and Siddhi (Success), with whom he had two sons: Kshema and Laabha.

statement.id: Kisah yang menjelaskan kaitan Ganesha dengan kecerdasan dan kebijaksanaan adalah perlombaannya dengan Karthikeya untuk menikah lebih dulu; ia dinyatakan menang dan menikahi Buddhi dan Siddhi, putri-putri Prajapati.
statement.en: A story explaining Ganesha's association with intelligence and wisdom is his competition with Karthikeya to marry first; declared the winner, he married Buddhi and Siddhi, daughters of Prajapati.

claims.quote: One day, after eating a few too many modakas (sacrificial cakes), Ganesha decided to take a ride on his giant rat, Kroncha, to aid his digestion.

statement.id: Suatu hari, setelah memakan terlalu banyak modaka (kue persembahan), Ganesha menunggangi tikus raksasanya, Kroncha, untuk membantu pencernaannya.
statement.en: One day, after eating too many modakas (sacrificial cakes), Ganesha rode his giant rat Kroncha to aid his digestion.

claims.quote: Ganesha landed on his full belly and it burst on hitting the ground. The cakes from his stomach rolled left, right and centre but Ganesha, unperturbed, carefully gathered them in, stuffed them all back into his belly and wound the snake around his midriff to keep it closed.

statement.id: Dalam kisah ini perut Ganesha pecah saat ia jatuh, lalu ia memasukkan kembali kue-kuenya dan melilitkan ular di perutnya agar tertutup.
statement.en: In this story Ganesha's belly burst when he fell; he stuffed the cakes back in and wound the snake around his midriff to keep it closed.

claims.quote: Outraged, Ganesha broke off the end of one of his tusks and hurled it at the laughing Moon who, hit full in the face, was struck black.

statement.id: Karena murka pada Bulan yang menertawakannya, Ganesha mematahkan ujung salah satu gadingnya dan melemparkannya ke wajah Bulan hingga menghitam.
statement.en: Outraged at the laughing Moon, Ganesha broke off the end of one of his tusks and hurled it at the Moon's face, which was struck black.

claims.quote: Yet another but less picturesque explanation of Ganesha's broken tusk was that he snapped it off in order to transcribe the epic poem Mahabharata, dictated by the sage Vyasa who wished to preserve the story for all time. This version explains Ganesha's association with writers and intellectuals.

statement.id: Penjelasan lain tentang gading Ganesha yang patah adalah bahwa ia mematahkannya untuk menyalin Mahabharata yang didiktekan resi Vyasa; versi ini menjelaskan kaitannya dengan penulis dan kaum intelektual.
statement.en: Another explanation of Ganesha's broken tusk is that he snapped it off to transcribe the Mahabharata dictated by the sage Vyasa; this version explains his association with writers and intellectuals.

claims.quote: In his hands he often carries a broken tusk, an axe, a ladle, a noose, prayer beads and a tray or bowl of sweets. He sometimes also wields an elephant goad in order to master life's obstacles.
claims.locator: How is Ganesha Represented in Art?

statement.id: Di tangannya ia sering membawa gading patah, kapak, sendok sayur, jerat, untaian doa, serta nampan atau mangkuk manisan, dan kadang pengait gajah untuk menguasai rintangan hidup.
statement.en: In his hands he often carries a broken tusk, an axe, a ladle, a noose, prayer beads, and a tray or bowl of sweets, and sometimes an elephant goad to master life's obstacles.

claims.quote: Ganesha is often depicted riding Kroncha, his giant rat, famed for its agility and also symbolic of the god's ability to circumvent obstacles.
claims.locator: How is Ganesha Represented in Art?

statement.id: Ganesha sering digambarkan menunggangi Kroncha, tikus raksasanya yang terkenal lincah dan melambangkan kemampuan sang dewa menghindari rintangan.
statement.en: Ganesha is often depicted riding Kroncha, his giant rat, famed for its agility and symbolic of his ability to circumvent obstacles.

claims.quote: Then Vyasa began to call to mind Ganesa. And Ganesa, obviator of obstacles, ready to fulfil the desires of his votaries, was no sooner thought of, than he repaired to the place where Vyasa was seated.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Ganguli, Vyasa mengingat Ganesa, "penyingkir rintangan" yang siap memenuhi keinginan para pemujanya, dan Ganesa segera datang ke tempat Vyasa duduk.
statement.en: In Ganguli's translation Vyasa calls Ganesa to mind, "obviator of obstacles" ready to fulfil the desires of his votaries, and Ganesa promptly comes to where Vyasa sits.

claims.quote: I will become the writer of thy work, provided my pen do not for a moment cease writing. ... Wherever there be anything thou dost not comprehend, cease to continue writing. ... Ganesa having signified his assent, by repeating the word Om! proceeded to write

statement.id: Ganesa bersedia menjadi penulis karya Vyasa dengan syarat penanya tidak berhenti; Vyasa meminta ia berhenti menulis bila ada yang tidak dipahaminya, dan Ganesa menyetujui dengan mengucapkan Om lalu mulai menulis.
statement.en: Ganesa agrees to be the writer of Vyasa's work provided his pen never ceases; Vyasa asks him to stop writing wherever he does not comprehend, and Ganesa assents by saying Om and begins to write.

claims.quote: Even the omniscient Ganesa took a moment to consider; while Vyasa, however, continued to compose other verses in great abundance.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, bahkan Ganesa yang mahatahu sempat berpikir sejenak, sementara Vyasa terus menggubah banyak bait lain.
statement.en: According to this text even the omniscient Ganesa took a moment to consider, while Vyasa continued to compose many other verses.

claims.quote: The name Ganesha is a Sanskrit compound, joining the words gana (gaṇa), meaning a 'group, multitude, or categorical system' and isha (īśa), meaning 'lord or master'.

statement.id: Nama Ganesha adalah gabungan kata Sanskerta gana, berarti "kelompok, kumpulan, atau sistem kategori", dan isha, berarti "tuan atau penguasa".
statement.en: The name Ganesha is a Sanskrit compound of gana, meaning "group, multitude, or categorical system", and isha, meaning "lord or master".

claims.quote: also known as Ganapati, Vinayaka and Pillaiyar, is one of the best-known and most revered and worshipped deities in the Hindu pantheon and is the Supreme god in the Ganapatya sect.

statement.id: Ganesha juga dikenal sebagai Ganapati, Vinayaka, dan Pillaiyar; ia salah satu dewa Hindu yang paling terkenal dan dipuja, serta Dewa Tertinggi dalam sekte Ganapatya.
statement.en: Ganesha, also known as Ganapati, Vinayaka and Pillaiyar, is one of the best-known and most revered deities in the Hindu pantheon and the Supreme god in the Ganapatya sect.

claims.quote: Ganesha also holds the Title of "Pratham Pujya" (the god to be worshipped initially before the worship of any other Deity).

statement.id: Ganesha juga bergelar "Pratham Pujya", dewa yang dipuja lebih dulu sebelum pemujaan dewa lain.
statement.en: Ganesha also holds the title "Pratham Pujya", the god to be worshipped first before any other deity.

claims.quote: As the god of beginnings, he is honoured at the start of rites and ceremonies. Ganesha is also invoked during writing sessions as a patron of letters and learning.

statement.id: Sebagai dewa permulaan, Ganesha dihormati pada awal upacara dan ritus; ia juga diseru saat menulis sebagai pelindung huruf dan ilmu.
statement.en: As god of beginnings Ganesha is honoured at the start of rites and ceremonies, and invoked during writing sessions as patron of letters and learning.

claims.quote: The principal texts on Ganesha include the Ganesha Purana, the Mudgala Purana, and the Ganapati Atharvasirsha.

statement.id: Teks-teks utama tentang Ganesha mencakup Ganesha Purana, Mudgala Purana, dan Ganapati Atharvasirsha.
statement.en: The principal texts on Ganesha include the Ganesha Purana, the Mudgala Purana, and the Ganapati Atharvasirsha.

claims.quote: The Amarakosha, an early Sanskrit lexicon, lists eight synonyms of Ganesha: Vinayaka, Vighnarāja (equivalent to Vighnesha), Dvaimātura (one who has two mothers), Gaṇādhipa (equivalent to Ganapati and Ganesha), Ekadanta (one who has one tusk)

statement.id: Amarakosha, kamus Sanskerta awal, mencantumkan delapan sinonim Ganesha, di antaranya Vinayaka, Vighnarāja, Dvaimātura (berbunda dua), Gaṇādhipa, dan Ekadanta (bergading satu).
statement.en: The Amarakosha, an early Sanskrit lexicon, lists eight synonyms of Ganesha, including Vinayaka, Vighnarāja, Dvaimātura (one who has two mothers), Gaṇādhipa, and Ekadanta (one who has one tusk).

claims.quote: He is popularly worshipped as a remover of obstacles, though traditionally he also places obstacles in the path of those who need to be checked. Hence, he is often worshipped by the people before they begin anything new.

statement.id: Ganesha dipuja secara populer sebagai penyingkir rintangan, meski menurut tradisi ia juga menaruh rintangan di jalan orang yang perlu dihentikan; karena itu ia sering dipuja sebelum memulai sesuatu yang baru.
statement.en: Ganesha is popularly worshipped as a remover of obstacles, though traditionally he also places obstacles in the path of those who need to be checked; hence he is often worshipped before beginning anything new.

claims.quote: The earliest images and mention lists Ganesha as a major deity in present-day Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam dating to the 7th and 8th centuries, and these mirror Indian examples of the 5th century or earlier.

statement.id: Gambar dan sebutan paling awal mencatat Ganesha sebagai dewa utama di wilayah Indonesia, Thailand, Kamboja, dan Vietnam masa kini, berasal dari abad ke-7 dan ke-8, dan mencerminkan contoh India abad ke-5 atau lebih awal.
statement.en: The earliest images and mentions list Ganesha as a major deity in present-day Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam, dating to the 7th and 8th centuries and mirroring Indian examples of the 5th century or earlier.

claims.quote: While some texts say that Ganesha was born with an elephant head, he acquires the head later in most stories. The most recurrent motif in these stories is that Ganesha was created by Parvati using clay to protect her and Shiva beheaded him when Ganesha came between Shiva and Parvati.

statement.id: Sebagian teks menyebut Ganesha lahir berkepala gajah, tetapi dalam kebanyakan kisah ia memperolehnya kemudian; motif paling sering adalah Parvati menciptakannya dari tanah liat dan Shiva memenggalnya.
statement.en: Some texts say Ganesha was born with an elephant head, but in most stories he acquires it later; the most recurrent motif is that Parvati created him from clay and Shiva beheaded him.

claims.quote: Another story says that Ganesha was created directly by Shiva's laughter. Because Shiva considered Ganesha too alluring, he gave him the head of an elephant and a protruding belly.

statement.id: Kisah lain menyebut Ganesha tercipta langsung dari tawa Shiva; karena Shiva menganggapnya terlalu memikat, ia memberinya kepala gajah dan perut buncit.
statement.en: Another story says Ganesha was created directly by Shiva's laughter; because Shiva considered him too alluring, he gave him an elephant head and a protruding belly.

claims.quote: Ganesha's earliest name was Ekadanta (One Tusked), referring to his single whole tusk, the other being broken. Some of the earliest images of Ganesha show him holding his broken tusk.

statement.id: Nama paling awal Ganesha adalah Ekadanta (Bergading Satu), merujuk pada satu gading utuhnya karena yang lain patah; beberapa arca paling awal memperlihatkannya memegang gading patah itu.
statement.en: Ganesha's earliest name was Ekadanta (One Tusked), referring to his single whole tusk, the other being broken; some of the earliest images show him holding his broken tusk.

claims.quote: In the standard configuration, Ganesha typically holds an axe or a goad in one upper arm and a pasha (noose) in the other upper arm.

statement.id: Dalam wujud baku, Ganesha biasanya memegang kapak atau pengait di satu lengan atas dan pasha (jerat) di lengan atas lainnya.
statement.en: In the standard configuration Ganesha typically holds an axe or a goad in one upper arm and a pasha (noose) in the other.

claims.quote: Ganesha is often shown riding on or attended by a mouse. ... Martin-Dubost says that the rat began to appear as the principal vehicle in sculptures of Ganesha in central and western India during the 7th century; the rat was always placed close to his feet.

statement.id: Ganesha sering digambarkan menunggangi atau ditemani seekor tikus; menurut Martin-Dubost, tikus mulai tampil sebagai kendaraan utama dalam arca Ganesha di India tengah dan barat pada abad ke-7.
statement.en: Ganesha is often shown riding on or attended by a mouse; per Martin-Dubost the rat began to appear as principal vehicle in sculptures in central and western India during the 7th century.

claims.quote: Devotees offer Ganesha sweets such as modaka and small sweet balls called laddus. He is often shown carrying a bowl of sweets, called a modakapātra.

statement.id: Para pemuja mempersembahkan manisan seperti modaka dan bola manis kecil bernama laddu kepada Ganesha; ia sering digambarkan membawa mangkuk manisan yang disebut modakapātra.
statement.en: Devotees offer Ganesha sweets such as modaka and small sweet balls called laddus; he is often shown carrying a bowl of sweets called a modakapātra.

claims.quote: An annual festival honours Ganesha for ten days, starting on Ganesh Chaturthi, which typically falls in late August or early September. The festival begins with people bringing in clay idols of Ganesha, symbolising the god's visit.

statement.id: Festival tahunan menghormati Ganesha selama sepuluh hari, dimulai pada Ganesh Chaturthi yang biasanya jatuh pada akhir Agustus atau awal September, dengan membawa masuk arca tanah liat sebagai lambang kunjungan sang dewa.
statement.en: An annual festival honours Ganesha for ten days, starting on Ganesh Chaturthi in late August or early September, beginning with clay idols brought in to symbolise the god's visit.

claims.quote: In 1893, Lokmanya Tilak transformed this annual Ganesha festival from private family celebrations into a grand public event.

statement.id: Pada 1893, Lokmanya Tilak mengubah festival tahunan Ganesha dari perayaan keluarga yang bersifat pribadi menjadi acara publik yang besar.
statement.en: In 1893 Lokmanya Tilak transformed this annual Ganesha festival from private family celebrations into a grand public event.

claims.quote: As the god of transitions, he is placed at the doorway of many Hindu temples to keep out the unworthy, which is analogous to his role as Parvati's doorkeeper.

statement.id: Sebagai dewa peralihan, Ganesha ditempatkan di pintu banyak kuil Hindu untuk menolak yang tak layak, selaras dengan perannya sebagai penjaga pintu Parvati.
statement.en: As god of transitions Ganesha is placed at the doorway of many Hindu temples to keep out the unworthy, analogous to his role as Parvati's doorkeeper.

claims.quote: Located within a 100-kilometer radius of the city of Pune, each of the eight shrines celebrates a particular form of Ganapati, complete with its own lore. The eight shrines are: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar and Ranjangaon.

statement.id: Delapan kuil Ashtavinayak terletak dalam radius 100 kilometer dari kota Pune; masing-masing merayakan satu bentuk Ganapati dengan kisahnya sendiri: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar, dan Ranjangaon.
statement.en: The eight Ashtavinayak shrines lie within a 100-kilometre radius of Pune; each celebrates a particular form of Ganapati with its own lore: Morgaon, Siddhatek, Pali, Mahad, Theur, Lenyadri, Ozar, and Ranjangaon.

claims.quote: Ganesha appeared in his classic form as a clearly-recognizable deity with well-defined iconographic attributes in the early 4th to 5th centuries CE.

statement.id: Ganesha tampil dalam wujud klasiknya sebagai dewa yang mudah dikenali dengan atribut ikonografi yang jelas pada awal abad ke-4 hingga ke-5 M.
statement.en: Ganesha appeared in his classic form as a clearly recognizable deity with well-defined iconographic attributes in the early 4th to 5th centuries CE.

claims.quote: An independent cult with Ganesha as the primary deity was well established by about the 10th century.

statement.id: Kultus mandiri dengan Ganesha sebagai dewa utama telah mapan pada sekitar abad ke-10.
statement.en: An independent cult with Ganesha as the primary deity was well established by about the 10th century.

claims.quote: Devotees believe that if Ganesha is propitiated, he grants success, prosperity and protection against adversity.

statement.id: Para pemuja percaya bahwa bila Ganesha diambil hatinya, ia memberi keberhasilan, kemakmuran, dan perlindungan dari kesulitan.
statement.en: Devotees believe that if Ganesha is propitiated he grants success, prosperity, and protection against adversity.

claims.quote: Ganesha is a non-sectarian deity. Hindus of all denominations invoke him at the beginning of prayers, important undertakings, and religious ceremonies. Dancers and musicians, particularly in southern India, begin art performances such as the Bharatanatyam dance with a prayer to Ganesha.

statement.id: Ganesha dipandang sebagai dewa lintas sekte: umat Hindu dari semua aliran menyerunya pada awal doa, kegiatan penting, dan upacara; penari dan pemusik, terutama di India selatan, memulai pertunjukan dengan doa kepadanya.
statement.en: Ganesha is a non-sectarian deity: Hindus of all denominations invoke him at the start of prayers, important undertakings, and ceremonies, and dancers and musicians, particularly in southern India, begin performances with a prayer to him.

claims.quote: Amongst Indonesians who predominantly profess the Islamic faith, Ganesha is not worshipped, but seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom and education. Many Indonesian public universities feature Ganesha's likeness in their grounds or logo.

statement.id: Di kalangan orang Indonesia yang mayoritas beragama Islam, Ganesha tidak dipuja tetapi dipandang sebagai simbol pengetahuan, kebijaksanaan, dan pendidikan; banyak universitas negeri Indonesia memuat gambarnya di kampus atau logo.
statement.en: Among predominantly Muslim Indonesians Ganesha is not worshipped but seen as a symbol of knowledge, wisdom, and education, and many Indonesian public universities feature his likeness in their grounds or logo.

claims.quote: Statues of Ganesha are found throughout the region, often beside Shiva sanctuaries. The forms of Ganesha found in the Hindu art of the Philippines, Java, Bali, and Borneo show specific regional influences.

statement.id: Arca Ganesha ditemukan di seluruh kawasan Asia Tenggara maritim, sering di samping tempat suci Shiva; bentuk Ganesha dalam seni Hindu di Filipina, Jawa, Bali, dan Kalimantan menunjukkan pengaruh khas daerah.
statement.en: Statues of Ganesha are found throughout the region of Maritime Southeast Asia, often beside Shiva sanctuaries; his forms in the Hindu art of the Philippines, Java, Bali, and Borneo show specific regional influences.

claims.quote: In Japan, where Ganesha is known as Kangiten, the Ganesha cult was first mentioned in 806.

statement.id: Di Jepang, tempat Ganesha dikenal sebagai Kangiten, kultus Ganesha pertama kali disebut pada 806.
statement.en: In Japan, where Ganesha is known as Kangiten, the Ganesha cult was first mentioned in 806.

claims.quote: One of his popular forms, Heramba-Ganapati, has five elephant heads, and other less-common variations in the number of heads are known.

statement.id: Salah satu bentuk populernya, Heramba-Ganapati, berkepala gajah lima, dan variasi lain jumlah kepala yang lebih jarang diketahui.
statement.en: One of his popular forms, Heramba-Ganapati, has five elephant heads, and other less common variations in the number of heads are known.

statement.en: Ganesha's name is written गणेश in Sanskrit, with the IAST transliteration Gaṇeśa.

claims.quote: Ganesha is mentioned in Hindu texts between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE, and a few Ganesha images from the 4th and 5th centuries CE have been documented by scholars.

statement.id: Ganesha disebut dalam teks Hindu antara abad ke-1 SM dan abad ke-2 M, dan beberapa arca Ganesha dari abad ke-4 dan ke-5 M telah didokumentasikan para sarjana.
statement.en: Ganesha is mentioned in Hindu texts between the 1st century BCE and 2nd century CE, and a few Ganesha images from the 4th and 5th centuries CE have been documented by scholars.

claims.quote: Of the eight incarnations of Ganesha described in the Mudgala Purana, Ganesha uses a mouse (shrew) named Mushaka in five of them, a lion in his incarnation as Vakratunda, a peacock in his incarnation as Vikata, and Shesha, the divine serpent, in his incarnation as Vighnaraja.

statement.id: Dari delapan inkarnasi Ganesha dalam Mudgala Purana, ia memakai tikus bernama Mushaka pada lima inkarnasi, singa sebagai Vakratunda, merak sebagai Vikata, dan Shesha sang ular ilahi sebagai Vighnaraja.
statement.en: Of the eight incarnations of Ganesha in the Mudgala Purana, he uses a mouse named Mushaka in five, a lion as Vakratunda, a peacock as Vikata, and Shesha, the divine serpent, as Vighnaraja.

summary.id: Sebagian teks menyebut Ganesha lahir berkepala gajah, tetapi dalam kebanyakan kisah ia memperolehnya kemudian setelah dipenggal Shiva.
summary.en: Some texts say Ganesha was born with an elephant head, but in most stories he acquires it later after Shiva beheads him.

summary.id: Kisah lain menyebut ia tercipta langsung dari tawa Shiva, yang lalu memberinya kepala gajah karena menganggapnya terlalu memikat.
summary.en: Another story says he was created directly by Shiva's laughter, who then gave him an elephant head because he found him too alluring.

summary.id: Ia mematahkan gadingnya dan melemparkannya kepada Bulan yang menertawakannya.
summary.en: He broke off his tusk and hurled it at the laughing Moon.

summary.id: Ia mematahkannya untuk menyalin Mahabharata yang didiktekan Vyasa.
summary.en: He snapped it off to transcribe the Mahabharata dictated by Vyasa.

short_description.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dalam mitologi Yunani yang lahir dari leher Medusa dan menjadi tunggangan Bellerophon serta pembawa petir Zeus.
short_description.en: Pegasus is the immortal winged horse of Greek mythology, born from Medusa's neck, ridden by Bellerophon and later bearer of Zeus's thunderbolts.

long_description.id:
Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dalam mitologi Yunani. Ia dikisahkan lahir dari leher Medusa ketika Perseus memenggalnya, dan menurut sumber ia dilahirkan bersama Chrysaor. Poseidon disebut sebagai ayahnya, meski Theoi juga mencatat tradisi yang hanya menyebut Medusa.

Bellerophon mendapatkan Pegasus dan, dengan bantuan Athena, menjinakkannya, lalu menungganginya dalam pertempuran melawan Chimaera. Kisah tentang cara Bellerophon memperolehnya berbeda-beda: ada yang menyebut kekang emas dari Athena, ada yang menyebut Athena sendiri yang menjinakkannya, dan ada yang menyebut Poseidon memberikannya kepada putranya. Setelah itu Bellerophon mencoba terbang menuju para dewa, tetapi Pegasus melemparkannya.

Pegasus melanjutkan perjalanan ke Olympos. Menurut satu tradisi ia menjadi pembawa petir Zeus dan, dalam tradisi lain, diserahkan kepada Eos. Ia juga dikreditkan dengan menciptakan mata air lewat hentakan kukunya, yang paling terkenal adalah Hippocrene di Gunung Helicon, dan dikenang sebagai rasi bintang.

Gambar Pegasus muncul pada tembikar Yunani dan koin, dan salah satu penggambaran pahatnya yang terkenal berasal dari sebuah pedimen kuil. Dalam seni Romawi, kuda itu menjadi lambang keabadian. Pada 1941, siluet Bellerophon di atas Pegasus dipakai sebagai lambang pasukan penerjun payung United Kingdom.
long_description.en:
Pegasus is the immortal winged horse of Greek mythology. He is said to have been born from Medusa's neck when Perseus beheaded her, and according to the source he was born together with Chrysaor. Poseidon is named as his father, although Theoi also records a tradition naming only Medusa.

Bellerophon obtained Pegasus and, with Athena's help, tamed him and rode him against the Chimaera. Accounts of how Bellerophon acquired him differ: some mention a golden bridle from Athena, some say Athena herself tamed him, and some say Poseidon gave him to his son. Afterwards Bellerophon tried to fly toward the gods, but Pegasus threw him.

Pegasus went on to Olympos. According to one tradition he became Zeus's thunderbolt-bearer, and in another he was given to Eos. He is also credited with creating springs with a stamp of his hoof, the most famous being Hippocrene on Mount Helicon, and he was commemorated as a constellation.

Pegasus appears on Greek pottery and coins, and one famous sculptural depiction comes from a temple pediment. In Roman art the horse became a symbol of immortality. In 1941 a silhouette of Bellerophon on Pegasus was adopted as the insignia of the United Kingdom's parachute troops.

literal_meaning.id: Menurut Theoi berarti 'dari mata air' atau 'memancar keluar'; usulan lain mengaitkannya dengan kata Luwian untuk 'kilat'.
literal_meaning.en: According to Theoi it means 'of the spring' or 'sprung forth'; another proposal links it to a Luwian word for 'lightning'.

who.id: Pegasus adalah kuda bersayap abadi dari mitologi Yunani.
who.en: Pegasus is an immortal winged horse of Greek mythology.

origin.id: Ia dikisahkan lahir dari leher Medusa yang dipenggal Perseus.
origin.en: He is said to have sprung from the neck of Medusa after Perseus beheaded her.

role.id: Ia menjadi tunggangan Bellerophon melawan Chimaera dan kemudian pembawa petir Zeus.
role.en: He served as Bellerophon's mount against the Chimaera and later as bearer of Zeus's thunderbolts.

famous_for.id: Pegasus paling dikenal sebagai kuda bersayap yang menciptakan mata air dengan hentakan kukunya.
famous_for.en: Pegasus is best known as the winged horse who made springs with a stamp of his hoof.

did_you_know.id: Menurut Theoi, gagasan Pegasus sebagai kuda para Muse lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno, sebab bagi orang kuno hubungannya dengan para Muse hanya lewat Hippocrene.
did_you_know.en: According to Theoi, Pegasus as the horse of the Muses is better known in modern times than in antiquity, since for the ancients his only link to the Muses was Hippocrene.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Theoi, terbitnya rasi bintang Pegasus menandai datangnya musim semi dan, di Yunani, badai petir musiman. Sumber yang sama mencatat bahwa gagasan Pegasus sebagai kuda para Muse lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno.
cultural_context.en: According to Theoi, the rising of the Pegasus constellation marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms. The same source notes that Pegasus as the horse of the Muses is more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity.

description.id: Bellerophon menunggangi dan menerbangkan Pegasus; Pegasos juga terbang ke Olympos.
description.en: Bellerophon rode and flew Pegasus, and Pegasos flew on to Olympos.

description.id: Pegasos disebut kuda bersayap yang abadi.
description.en: Pegasos is described as an immortal winged horse.

description.id: Menurut Hesiod dalam Theogony, Pegasus membawakan petir dan kilat kepada Zeus kapan pun diperlukan.
description.en: According to Hesiod's Theogony, Pegasus brought Zeus his thunder and lightning whenever needed.

description.id: Pegasus dikreditkan menciptakan sejumlah mata air dengan hentakan kukunya, termasuk Hippocrene.
description.en: Pegasus is credited with creating a number of springs with a stamp of his hoof, including Hippocrene.

role.en: Pegasus is born from Medusa's neck.

summary.id: Ketika Perseus memenggal kepala Medusa, Pegasos dan Khrysaor melompat dari darah atau tubuhnya. Hesiod menyatakan Pegasos dinamai dari mata air Okeanos tempat ia lahir.
summary.en: When Perseus beheaded Medusa, Pegasos and Khrysaor sprang from her blood or body. Hesiod says Pegasos was named after the springs of Okeanos where he was born.

role.en: Pegasus helps Bellerophon kill the Chimaera.

summary.id: Dengan bantuan Athena, Bellerophon menjinakkan Pegasus dan menunggangi serta menerbangkannya untuk membunuh Chimaera dengan tombaknya. Hesiod menyatakan Khimaira dibunuh oleh Pegasos dan Bellerophon.
summary.en: With Athena's help, Bellerophon tamed Pegasus and rode and flew him to kill the Chimaera with his spear. Hesiod states that Khimaira was killed by Pegasos and Bellerophon.

role.id: Pegasus melempar Bellerophon yang hendak terbang ke tempat para dewa.
role.en: Pegasus throws Bellerophon, who tried to fly to the gods.

summary.id: Karena menyangka bisa terbang cukup tinggi untuk bergabung dengan para dewa, Bellerophon dilempar Pegasus dan jatuh ke bumi, sedangkan Pegasus terus terbang ke Gunung Olympus. Sumber lain menyebut Zeus yang membuat kuda itu meronta, atau lalat pengganggu kiriman Zeus yang membuatnya murka.
summary.en: Thinking he could fly high enough to join the gods, Bellerophon was thrown by Pegasus and fell to earth, while Pegasus kept on flying to Mount Olympus. Other sources say Zeus made the horse buck, or that a gad-fly sent by Zeus enraged him.

role.id: Hentakan kuku Pegasus memunculkan mata air.
role.en: Pegasus's hoofstamp brings forth a spring.

summary.id: Pegasus dikreditkan menciptakan mata air Hippocrene di Gunung Helicon. Antoninus Liberalis menyebut ia menghentak puncak gunung itu atas kehendak Poseidon agar gunung tidak terus membengkak, sedangkan Pausanias menyebutnya dibuat oleh kuku kuda Bellerophon.
summary.en: Pegasus is credited with creating the Hippocrene spring on Mount Helicon. Antoninus Liberalis says he struck the mountain's summit by Poseidon's will to stop it swelling, while Pausanias says it was made by the hoof of Bellerophon's horse.

description.id: Tempat mata air Hippocrene, dekat hutan suci para Muse.
description.en: Site of the Hippocrene spring, close to the grove sacred to the Muses.

description.id: Tempat mata air lain yang dikaitkan dengan hentakan kuku Pegasus.
description.en: Site of another spring credited to Pegasus's hoofstamp.

description.en: In some accounts, where Bellerophon found Pegasus, near Corinth.

description.en: Its pediment carries a famous sculptural depiction of Pegasus.

description.en: Theoi classes Hesiod's Theogony, with its account of Pegasos's birth, as Greek epic of the 8th or 7th century BCE.

description.en: Pegasus was a popular coin design, in particular from Corinth from the 6th century BCE.

description.id: Benvenuto Cellini memasukkan Pegasus pada koin yang dibuat untuk menghormati Kardinal Pietro Bembo; sejak itu Pegasus menjadi simbol Toskana.
description.en: Benvenuto Cellini included Pegasus on a coin made to honor Cardinal Pietro Bembo; Pegasus has been a symbol of Tuscany since.

traditional_summary.en: For the ancients, Pegasus's link to the Muses was only the Hippocrene well that his hoof called forth.

modern_depiction.id: Pegasus dianggap kuda para Muse, dan peran ini lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di zaman kuno.
modern_depiction.en: Pegasus is regarded as the horse of the Muses, a role more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity.

summary.en: Hesiod, Apollodorus, Hyginus, and Ovid name Poseidon and Medousa as his parents.

summary.id: Dari kata Yunani untuk mata air (pēgē), seperti kata Hesiod, atau dari 'memancar keluar'.
summary.en: From the Greek word for spring (pēgē), as Hesiod has it, or from 'sprung forth'.

summary.id: Dari kata Luwian pihassas ('kilat'); tafsiran ini diterima luas tetapi dikritik Robin Lane Fox.
summary.en: From Luwian pihassas ('lightning'); this reading is widely accepted but criticized by Robin Lane Fox.

claims_provenance.quote: At the same time and in the same way, Chryasor was also born.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Poseidon memberikan Pegasus kepada putranya, Bellerophon, yang memanfaatkannya dalam pertempuran terkenal melawan Chimaera.
claim.en: Poseidon gave Pegasus to his son Bellerophon, who put Pegasus to good use in his famous battle with the Chimaera.

claims_provenance.quote: Poseidon gave Pegasus to his son Bellerophon who put Pegasus to good use in his famous battle with the Chimaera.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Dalam sebagian kisah Bellerophon menemukan kuda itu di mata air Pirene dekat Corinth, dan Hesiod menyiratkan hal ini menjelaskan nama Pegasus, yang diturunkan dari pēgē ('air').
claim.en: In some accounts Bellerophon found the horse at the fountain of Pirene near Corinth, and Hesiod suggests this explains the name Pegasus, derived from pēgē ('water').

claims_provenance.quote: To aid him in this task, Bellerophon was fortunate to have at his disposal Pegasus. In some accounts he found the horse at the fountain of Pirene near Corinth, and Hesiod suggests this fact explains the name Pegasus, derived from 'water'- pēgē.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Pegasus terus terbang dan setibanya di Gunung Olympus ia diserahkan kepada Eos, yang bertugas membawa fajar melintasi langit setiap hari.
claim.en: Pegasus flew on and, on reaching Mt. Olympus, was given to Eos, who was responsible for bringing Dawn across the sky each day.

claims_provenance.quote: Meanwhile, Pegasus kept on going and on reaching Mt. Olympus, he was given to Eos who was responsible for bringing Dawn across the sky each day.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Salah satu penggambaran terkenal dalam seni pahat berasal dari pedimen Kuil Artemis di Corcyra (sekitar 580 SM).
claim.en: A famous sculptural representation comes from the pediment of the Temple of Artemis on Corcyra (c. 580 BCE).

claims_provenance.quote: A famous representation in sculpture is from the pediment of the Temple of Artemis on Corcyra (c. 580 BCE).
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Mitos Bellerophon dan Pegasus juga populer dalam seni Romawi, terutama kamei batu semimulia dan mozaik lantai, tempat kuda itu menjadi lambang keabadian.
claim.en: The Bellerophon and Pegasus myth was also popular in Roman art, especially engraved semi-precious stone cameos and floor mosaics, where the horse became symbolic of immortality.

claims_provenance.quote: The Bellerophon and Pegasus myth was also a popular subject in Roman art - especially engraved semi-precious stone cameos and floor mosaics - where the horse became symbolic of immortality.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Pegasus: The Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Menurut Theoi, nama Pegasos berarti 'dari mata air' atau 'memancar keluar'; yang pertama merujuk pada kaitan kuda itu dengan berbagai mata air, yang kedua pada kelahirannya dari leher Gorgon.
claim.en: According to Theoi, Pegasos' name means either 'of the spring' or 'sprung forth'; the first alludes to the steed's link with various springs, the second to its birth from the Gorgon's neck.

claims_provenance.quote: Pegasos' name means either "of the spring" from the Greek word ... "sprung forth" from the word ... The first alludes to the steed's connection with various springs, and the latter to its birth from the Gorgon's neck.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Bellerophon kemudian mencoba terbang ke surga, tetapi Zeus membuat kuda itu meronta sehingga sang pahlawan terlempar ke bumi; Pegasos terbang ke Olympos dan menjadi pembawa petir Zeus.
claim.en: Later the hero tried to fly to heaven, but Zeus made the horse buck and throw him back to earth; Pegasos flew on to Olympos and became Zeus's thunderbolt-bearer.

claims_provenance.quote: Later the hero attempted to fly to heaven but Zeus caused the horse to buck throwing him back down to earth in disgrace. Pegasos winged his way on to Olympos where he became the thunderbolt-bearer of Zeus.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Terbitnya rasi bintang Pegasus menandai datangnya musim semi dan, di Yunani, badai petir musiman.
claim.en: The rising of the Pegasus constellation marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms.

claims_provenance.quote: Pegasos was commemorated amongst the stars as the constellation of the same name. Its rising marks the arrival of spring and, in Greece, of seasonal thunderstorms.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Menurut pandangan yang tampaknya paling kuno, Pegasus adalah kuda petir milik Zeus, sedangkan penulis yang lebih belakangan menyebutnya kuda Eos.
claim.en: On the view that seems the most ancient, Pegasus was the thundering horse of Zeus, whereas later writers describe him as the horse of Eos.

claims_provenance.quote: According to this view, which is apparently the most ancient, Pegasus was the thundering horse of Zeus; but later writers describe him as the horse of Eos
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Menurut salah satu kisah, Athena menampakkan diri kepada Bellerophon dalam mimpi, memerintahkannya berkurban kepada Poseidon, dan memberinya kekang emas.
claim.en: In one account Athena appeared to Bellerophon in a dream, told him to sacrifice to Poseidon, and gave him a golden bridle.

claims_provenance.quote: The latter advised him to spend a night in the temple of Athena, and, as Bellerophon was sleeping, the goddess appeared to him in a dream, commanding him to sacrifice to Poseidon, and gave him a golden bridle.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Menurut sebagian kisah, Athena sendiri yang menjinakkan dan memasang kekang pada Pegasus lalu menyerahkannya kepada Bellerophon.
claim.en: According to some accounts, Athena herself tamed and bridled Pegasus and handed him over to Bellerophon.

claims_provenance.quote: According to some Athena herself tamed and bridled Pegasus, and surrendered him to Bellerophon
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Setelah menaklukkan Chimaera, ia berusaha naik ke surga dengan kuda bersayapnya tetapi jatuh ke bumi, entah karena takut atau pusing, entah karena dilempar Pegasus yang dibuat murka oleh seekor lalat pengganggu kiriman Zeus.
claim.en: After conquering the Chimaera, he tried to rise to heaven on his winged horse but fell to earth, whether from fear or giddiness or because Pegasus, enraged by a gad-fly Zeus had sent, threw him.

claims_provenance.quote: After he had conquered the Chimaera ... he endeavoured to rise up to heaven with his winged horse, but fell down upon the earth, either from fear or from giddiness, or being thrown off by Pegasus, who was rendered furious by a gad-fly which Zeus had sent.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Pegasus belakangan juga dianggap kuda para Muse; dalam peran ini ia lebih terkenal di zaman modern daripada di masa kuno, sebab bagi orang kuno hubungannya dengan para Muse hanya lewat hentakan kukunya yang memunculkan mata air Hippocrene.
claim.en: Pegasus was also later regarded as the horse of the Muses; in this role he is more celebrated in modern times than in antiquity, since for the ancients his only link to the Muses was that his hoof called forth the Hippocrene well.

claims_provenance.quote: Pegasus lastly was also regarded as the horse of the Muses, and in this capacity he is more celebrated in modern times than he ever was in antiquity ; for with the ancients he had no connection with the Muses, except that by his hoof he called forth the inspiring well Hippocrene.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Hesiod, Theogony: setelah Perseus memenggal kepala Medusa, Khrysaor dan kuda Pegasos melompat dari darahnya; Pegasos dinamai dari mata air (pegai) Okeanos tempat ia lahir.
claim.en: Hesiod, Theogony: when Perseus cut off Medusa's head, Khrysaor and the horse Pegasos sprang from her blood; Pegasos was named after the springs (pegai) of Okeanos where he was born.

claims_provenance.quote: But when Perseus had cut off the head of Medousa (Medusa) there sprang from her blood stout-hearted Khrysaor (Chrysaor) and the horse Pegasos so named from the springs (pegai) of Okeanos (Oceanus), where he was born.

claim.en: Theoi lists Poseidon and Medousa as Pegasos's parents according to Hesiod, Apollodorus, Hyginus, and Ovid.

claims_provenance.quote: [1.1] POSEIDON & MEDOUSA (Hesiod Theogony 278, Apollodorus 2.32 & 2.42, Hyginus Fabulae 151 & Astronomica 2.18, Ovid Metamorphoses 4.781 & 6.119)

claim.en: Theoi also records a tradition (Pindar, Nonnus) naming only Medousa as Pegasos's parent.

claims_provenance.quote: [1.2] MEDOUSA (Pindar Olympian Ode, Nonnus Dionysiaca 24.270)
claims_provenance.source_citation: Theoi Project — PEGASUS (Pegasos) - Winged Horse of Greek Mythology

claim.id: Hesiod (Catalogues of Women): ayah Bellerophon, Poseidon, memberinya Pegasos yang membawanya secepat kilat dengan sayapnya dan terbang tak kenal lelah ke mana-mana di bumi.
claim.en: Hesiod (Catalogues of Women): Bellerophon's father Poseidon gave him Pegasos, who bore him swiftly on his wings and flew unwearying everywhere over the earth.

claims_provenance.quote: his father [Poseidon] gave him Pegasos who would bear him most swiftly on his wings, and flew unwearying everywhere over the earth

claim.en: Hesiod, Theogony: Khimaira (Chimera) was killed by Pegasos and gallant Bellerophon.

claims_provenance.quote: But Khimaira (Chimera) was killed by Pegasos and gallant Bellerophon.

claim.en: Pindar: Bellerophon long strove to yoke Pegasos, the snake-haired Gorgo's offspring, until Pallas (Athena) brought him the bridle and golden headband.

claims_provenance.quote: seeking to yoke the snake-haired Gorgo's offspring, Pegasos. Till Pallas [Athena], goddess maid, brought him the bridle and golden headband

claim.id: Antoninus Liberalis: Gunung Helikon, terpikat kenikmatan nyanyian para Muse, membengkak ke langit sampai Pegasos, atas kehendak Poseidon, menghentikannya dengan menghentak puncaknya.

claim.id: Salah satu etimologi yang diusulkan untuk nama itu adalah kata Luwian pihassas ('kilat') dan Pihassassi, nama Luwian-Het setempat di Kilikia selatan untuk dewa cuaca yang dikaitkan dengan guntur dan kilat.
claim.en: One proposed etymology of the name is Luwian pihassas 'lightning' and Pihassassi, a local Luwian-Hittite name in southern Cilicia for a weather deity associated with thunder and lightning.

claims_provenance.quote: A proposed etymology of the name is Luwian pihassas 'lightning', and Pihassassi, a local Luwian-Hittite name in southern Cilicia of a weather deity associated with thunder and lightning.

claim.id: Tafsiran Luwian itu pertama kali diajukan pada 1952 dan masih diterima luas, tetapi Robin Lane Fox (2009) mengkritiknya sebagai tidak masuk akal.

claim.en: During World War II the silhouette of Bellerophon mounted on the winged Pegasus was adopted in 1941 by the United Kingdom's newly raised parachute troops as their upper-sleeve insignia.
