short_description.id: Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan penguasa alam bawah dalam agama serta mitologi Yunani kuno, yang juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan bumi.
short_description.en: Hades is the god of the dead and ruler of the underworld in ancient Greek religion and mythology, also associated with the wealth of the earth.

long_description.id:
Dalam agama Yunani kuno, Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan kekayaan serta raja alam bawah. Namanya juga dipakai untuk menyebut wilayah alam bawah itu sendiri. Ia putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, ditelan ayahnya sejak lahir, lalu bersama Zeus dan Poseidon mengalahkan para Titan. Dalam pembagian kosmos ia memperoleh alam bawah, Zeus langit, dan Poseidon laut.

Hades memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan yang layak. Ia juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan tersembunyi di dalam bumi, dan Plouton berarti pemberi kekayaan. Karena ditakuti, namanya dihindari dan orang memakai gelar seperti Eubuleus, kurban baginya dilakukan malam hari, dan Hesiodos menyebutnya tanpa belas kasih di hatinya; satu sumber lain menyebutnya garang dan tak kenal ampun.

Persephone disebut istrinya, yang ia culik ke alam bawah. Ketika Demeter menimpakan paceklik, Persephone dijemput, tetapi karena telah memakan biji delima ia harus kembali selama sebagian tiap tahun. Hades sendiri digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olimpus.

Dalam seni, Hades digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, kadang duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta berkuda hitam. Ia juga memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; sumber-sumber berbeda tentang siapa yang membuatnya. Orang Romawi mengenalnya sebagai Dis atau Pluto.

Dunia bawah dipercaya dimasuki melalui Sungai Styx, tempat Hermes menuntun jiwa dan Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang yang dijaga Kerberos. Jiwa dinilai oleh Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos: yang baik ke Padang Elysium, yang buruk ke Tartarus. Beberapa pahlawan mengunjunginya, antara lain Hercules, Odiseus, dan Orpheus.
long_description.en:
In ancient Greek religion Hades is god of the dead and riches and king of the underworld. His name also refers to the underworld itself. He is the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by his father at birth, and with Zeus and Poseidon he overcame the Titans. In the division of the cosmos he received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea.

Hades presides over funeral rites and defends the dead's right to due burial. He is also associated with hidden wealth beneath the earth, and Plouton means the giver of wealth. Because he was feared, his name was avoided and epithets such as Eubuleus were used, sacrifices to him were made at night, and Hesiod calls him pitiless in heart; another source calls him fierce and inexorable.

Persephone is named as his wife, whom he abducted to the underworld. When Demeter brought famine, Persephone was fetched back, but since she had eaten the pomegranate seed she had to return for part of each year. Hades himself is portrayed as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.

Greek artists most often show Hades as a mature bearded man with a cornucopia, a libation vase, a sceptre, or a two-pronged spear, and at times on an ebony throne or in a chariot with black horses. He also has a helmet that makes the wearer invisible; sources differ on who made it. The Romans knew him as Dis or Pluto.

The underworld was believed to be entered across the river Styx, where Hermes leads souls and Charon ferries them to gates guarded by Kerberos. Souls are judged by Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos: the good go to the Elysian Fields, the bad to Tartarus. Several heroes visited it, among them Hercules, Odysseus, and Orpheus.

literal_meaning.id: Asalnya tidak pasti; sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
literal_meaning.en: Its origin is uncertain; since antiquity it has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one".

who.id: Dewa orang mati dan penguasa alam bawah.
who.en: God of the dead and ruler of the underworld.

role.id: Memerintah alam bawah dan berkaitan dengan upacara pemakaman.
role.en: Rules the underworld and is linked to funerary rites.

famous_for.id: Mendapat alam bawah saat pembagian kosmos dan menculik Persephone.
famous_for.en: Receiving the underworld in the division of the cosmos and abducting Persephone.

did_you_know.id: Hades adalah satu-satunya dewa yang tidak tinggal di Gunung Olimpus; ia berdiam di istana gelap di bawah bumi.
did_you_know.en: Of the Greek gods, only Hades did not live on Mount Olympus; his home was a dark palace under the earth.

cultural_context.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, keyakinan bahwa orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar juru perahu mengembara sebagai hantu menunjukkan sifat Hades yang ambigu; alam bawah tidak selalu tempat siksa, tetapi pada umumnya tempat peristirahatan terakhir jiwa.
cultural_context.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, the belief that the unburied or those unable to pay the boatman wandered as ghosts points to an ambiguous view of Hades: the realm was not necessarily a place of torment, but in most cases just the soul's final resting place.

description.id: Hades memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; Athena dan Perseus memakainya dalam kisah-kisah.
description.en: Hades has a helmet that makes the wearer invisible; Athena and Perseus used it in stories.

description.id: Ia memerintah alam bawah, dan satu sumber menyebut ia menjaga gerbangnya tertutup agar tak ada arwah lolos atau kembali.
description.en: He rules the underworld, and one source says he kept its gates closed so no shade could escape or return.

description.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan kekayaan tersembunyi bumi, dari tanah subur hingga emas, perak, dan logam lain.
description.en: He is associated with the earth's hidden wealth, from fertile soil to gold, silver, and other metals.

description.id: Ia memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan layak.
description.en: He presides over funeral rites and defends the dead's right to due burial.

description.id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkannya menjadi Pluto.
description.en: Roman-era mythographers equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades and merged them into Pluto.

title.en: Birth and the war against the Titans

role.id: Putra Kronos yang ditelan lalu dimuntahkan.
role.en: The son of Kronos who is swallowed and then disgorged.

summary.id: Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir; Zeus membuat Kronos memuntahkan mereka, dan para dewa mengusir Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di Tartaros. Kiklops juga menghadiahkan helm untuk Haides.
summary.en: Haides is swallowed by Kronos at birth; Zeus makes Kronos disgorge them, and the gods drive the Titans from heaven and lock them in Tartaros. The Kyklopes also give a helmet for Haides.

role.id: Saudara yang memperoleh alam bawah lewat undian.
role.en: The brother who receives the underworld by lot.

summary.id: Setelah menggulingkan Titan, Hades mengundi dengan Zeus dan Poseidon, dan Hades memperoleh alam bawah, Zeus langit, Poseidon laut.
summary.en: After overthrowing the Titans, Hades drew lots with Zeus and Poseidon and received the underworld, Zeus the sky, Poseidon the sea.

summary.id: Hades menginginkan pengantin dan Zeus menyetujui penculikan Persephone. Demeter menimpakan paceklik sampai Persephone dikembalikan, tetapi karena sudah memakan biji delima ia harus kembali selama sebagian tiap tahun.
summary.en: Hades wants a bride and Zeus assents to the abduction of Persephone. Demeter brings famine until Persephone is returned, but because she ate the pomegranate seed she must return for part of each year.

role.en: The ruler of the place where souls are judged.

summary.id: Di gerbang Hades, jiwa dinilai oleh Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos; yang baik minum dari Lethe dan masuk Padang Elysium, yang buruk dibawa ke Tartarus.
summary.en: At the gates of Hades souls are judged by Minos, Rhadamanthys and Aiakos; the good drink from Lethe and enter the Elysian Fields, the bad are taken to Tartarus.

role.id: Penguasa yang dikunjungi, dan kadang memenjarakan, para pahlawan.
role.en: The ruler visited by, and sometimes imprisoning, heroes.

summary.id: Hercules, Odiseus, dan Orpheus mengunjungi alam bawah; Theseus dan Peirithoos berusaha menculik Persephone sehingga Hades memenjarakan mereka, dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian dibebaskan Hercules.
summary.en: Hercules, Odysseus and Orpheus visit the underworld; Theseus and Peirithoos try to capture Persephone and Hades imprisons them, and only Theseus is later released by Hercules.

role.id: Dewa yang gemetar di dunia bawah.
role.en: The god who trembles in the underworld.

summary.id: Ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati.
summary.en: As Zeus battles Typhoeus, Haides trembles where he rules over the dead.

description.id: Wilayah di bawah bumi yang diperintah Hades dan dianggap tujuan akhir jiwa orang mati.
description.en: The region below the earth ruled by Hades, regarded as the final destination for the souls of the dead.

description.id: Sungai di dunia bawah tempat Hermes menuntun jiwa dan Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades.
description.en: The underworld river to which Hermes leads souls and from which Charon ferries them to the gates of Hades.

description.id: Tingkat terendah Hades, tempat jiwa yang dinilai buruk menerima hukuman.
description.en: The lowest level of Hades, where souls judged to have led bad lives are punished.

description.id: Tempat indah tujuan jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik.
description.en: The idyllic destination of souls judged to have led especially good lives.

description.id: Tempat Hades memiliki pelataran suci dan kuil yang hanya dibuka setahun sekali.
description.en: Where Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple opened only once a year.

note.id: Istri Hades.
note.en: Hades's wife.

note.id: Ayah Hades, yang menelannya sejak lahir.
note.en: Hades's father, who swallowed him at birth.

note.id: Ibu Hades.
note.en: Hades's mother.

note.id: Saudara Hades yang memperoleh langit.
note.en: Hades's brother who received the sky.

note.id: Saudara Hades yang memperoleh laut.
note.en: Hades's brother who received the sea.

caption.en: Hades — AI artistic interpretation based on features in folklore sources.

claim.id: Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan kekayaan serta raja alam bawah dalam agama Yunani kuno.
claim.en: Hades is the ancient Greek god of the dead and riches and king of the underworld.

claims_provenance.quote: in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous.

claim.id: Hades mendapat alam bawah, Zeus langit, dan Poseidon laut.
claim.en: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea.

claims_provenance.quote: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea

claim.id: Hades memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan layak.
claim.en: Hades presided over funerary rites and defended the dead's right to burial.

claims_provenance.quote: He presided over funeral rites and defended the right of the dead to due burial.

claim.id: Hades juga dewa kekayaan tersembunyi di bumi, dari tanah subur hingga logam.
claim.en: Hades was also god of the earth's hidden wealth, including fertile soil and metals.

claims_provenance.quote: Haides was also the god of the hidden wealth of the earth, from the fertile soil with nourished the seed-grain, to the mined wealth of gold, silver and other metals.

claim.id: Hades adalah nama dewa sekaligus nama tempat alam bawah yang dianggap tujuan akhir jiwa orang mati.
claim.en: Hades names both the god and the underworld considered the destination of dead souls.

claims_provenance.quote: Hades was both the name of the ancient Greek god of the underworld (Roman name: Pluto) and the name of the shadowy place below the earth which was considered the final destination for the souls of the dead.

claim.id: Persephone disebut sebagai istri Hades yang dibawanya ke alam bawah.
claim.en: Persephone is named as Hades's wife whom he brought to the underworld.

claims_provenance.quote: The god's wife was Persephone whom he abducted to join him in the underworld

claim.id: Hades digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olympus.
claim.en: Hades is described as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.

claims_provenance.quote: Hades was the only god not to reside on Mount Olympus, dwelling instead in a dark palace beneath the earth.

claim.id: Menurut Theoi, Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir bersama empat saudaranya; Zeus kemudian membuat sang Titan memuntahkan mereka, dan bersama-sama mereka mengusir para dewa Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di jurang Tartaros.
claim.en: According to Theoi, Haides was devoured by Kronos as soon as he was born along with four siblings; Zeus later made the Titan disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them in the pit of Tartaros.

claims_provenance.quote: Haides was devoured by Kronos (Cronus) as soon as he was born, along with four of his siblings. Zeus later caused the Titan to disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them away in the pit of Tartaros.

claim.id: Dalam Iliad (terjemahan Lattimore), Poseidon berkata bahwa ketika undi dikocok ia mendapat laut kelabu, Aides mendapat undi kabut dan kegelapan, dan Zeus mendapat langit luas.
claim.en: In the Iliad (Lattimore's translation), Poseidon says that when the lots were shaken he drew the grey sea, Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky.

claims_provenance.quote: I [Poseidon] when the lots were shaken drew the grey sea to live in forever; Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky, in the cloud and the bright air.
claims_provenance.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Homer Iliad 15.187 ff (trans. Lattimore)

claim.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides digambarkan kuat, tanpa belas kasih di hatinya, dan berdiam di bawah bumi.
claim.en: In Hesiod's Theogony Haides is described as strong, pitiless in heart, and dwelling under the earth.

claims_provenance.quote: strong Haides (Hades), pitiless in heart, who dwells under the earth
claims_provenance.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 453 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

claim.id: Haides menginginkan pengantin dan memohon kepada saudaranya Zeus agar memberinya salah satu putrinya; Zeus menawarkan Persephone, putri Demeter, dan karena tahu Demeter akan menolak, ia menyetujui penculikan paksa gadis itu.
claim.en: Haides desired a bride and asked his brother Zeus for one of his daughters; Zeus offered Persephone, daughter of Demeter, and, knowing Demeter would resist, assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

claims_provenance.quote: Haides desired a bride and petitioned his brother Zeus to grant him one of his daughters. The god offered him Persephone, the daughter of Demeter. However, knowing that the goddess would resist the marriage, he assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

claim.id: Demeter murka dan menimpakan paceklik besar ke bumi sampai putrinya dikembalikan; Zeus terpaksa mengalah dan gadis itu dijemput dari dunia bawah, tetapi karena telah mencicipi biji delima ia harus kembali kepada Haides selama sebagian tiap tahun.
claim.en: Demeter was furious and brought a great dearth upon the earth until her daughter was returned; Zeus was forced to concede and the girl was fetched from the underworld, but since she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return to Haides for a portion of each year.

claims_provenance.quote: When Demeter learned of this, she was furious and caused a great dearth to fall upon the earth until her daughter was returned. Zeus was forced to concede lest mankind perish, and the girl was fetched forth from the underworld. However, since she had tasted of the pomegranate seed, she was forced to return to him for a portion of each year.

claim.id: Haides digambarkan sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap yang agung, entah sebagai Aidoneus yang bertakhta di dunia bawah dengan tongkat berujung burung, atau sebagai Plouton, pemberi kekayaan, yang mencurahkan kesuburan dari cornucopia.
claim.en: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god, either as Aidoneus enthroned in the underworld holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton, the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

claims_provenance.quote: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god. He was depicted as either Aidoneus, enthroned in the underworld, holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton (Pluton), the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

claim.id: Bangsa Romawi menamainya Dis atau Pluto, bentuk Latin dari gelar Yunaninya Plouton, "Penguasa Kekayaan".
claim.en: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

claims_provenance.quote: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat, dan tradisi kemudian menyebut helm itu hadiah dari para Kiklops setelah mereka dibebaskan dari Tartarus.
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades possessed a helmet that rendered the wearer invisible, and later traditions said it was a gift from the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.

claims_provenance.quote: He possessed a helmet which rendered the wearer invisible (Il. v. 845), and later traditions stated that this helmet was given him as a present by the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup agar tak ada arwah yang dapat lolos atau kembali ke wilayah cahaya.
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed so that no shade could escape or return to the region of light.

claims_provenance.quote: He kept the gates of the lower world closed (whence he is called ... that no shade might be able to escape or return to the region of light.
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, wataknya digambarkan garang dan tak kenal ampun sehingga di antara semua dewa ia paling dibenci manusia.
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, his character is described as fierce and inexorable, so that of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.

claims_provenance.quote: His character is described as fierce and inexorable, whence of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Di Elis Haides memiliki pelataran suci dan sebuah kuil yang hanya dibuka sekali setiap tahun.
claim.en: In Elis Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple that was opened only once every year.

claims_provenance.quote: In Elis he had a sacred enclosure and a temple, which was opened only once in every year
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Plato mencatat bahwa orang lebih suka menyebutnya Pluton (pemberi kekayaan) daripada mengucapkan nama Hades atau Aides yang ditakuti.
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Plato observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.

claims_provenance.quote: Plato (Cratyl. p. 403) observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, asal-usul kata Hades tidak pasti; sebagian menurunkannya dari a-idein sehingga berarti "dewa yang membuat tak terlihat".
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, the etymology of Hades is uncertain; some derive it from a-idein, so that it would signify "the god who makes invisible".

claims_provenance.quote: The etymology of Hades is uncertain: some derive it from a-idein, whence it would signify "the god who makes invisible,"
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, dalam Homeros Aides selalu nama sang dewa, tetapi kemudian dialihkan ke rumah, tempat tinggal, atau kerajaannya sehingga menjadi nama dunia bawah itu sendiri.
claim.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, in Homer Aides is always the name of the god, but later it was transferred to his house, abode or kingdom and became a name for the lower world itself.

claims_provenance.quote: In Homer Aides is invariably the name of the god; but in later times it was transferred to his house, his abode or kingdom, so that it became a name for the lower world itself.
claims_provenance.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

claim.id: Menurut Theoi, tiga dewi murka bumi kadang digambarkan sebagai putri Haides, tetapi kisah yang lazim menyebut mereka lahir dari bumi.
claim.en: According to Theoi, the three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides, but the usual account describes them as earth-born.

claims_provenance.quote: The three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides. The usual account, however, describes them as earth-born.
claims_provenance.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Offspring of Hades

claim.id: Dalam Bibliotheca Pseudo-Apollodoros, para Kiklops memberi Zeus guntur dan petir, serta helm untuk Plouton (Haides) dan trisula untuk Poseidon.
claim.en: In Pseudo-Apollodorus's Bibliotheca the Kyklopes gave Zeus thunder, lightning and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Haides) and a trident for Poseidon.

claims_provenance.quote: In return the Kyklopes (Cyclopes) gave Zeus thunder, lightning, and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Pluton) [Haides] and a trident for Poseidon.
claims_provenance.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1.6-7 (trans. Aldrich)

claim.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati di bawah ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus.
claim.en: In Hesiod's Theogony, Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below as Zeus battled Typhoeus.

claims_provenance.quote: Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below.
claims_provenance.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 820 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

claim.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades mungkin dewa yang paling ditakuti dan oleh Homeros maupun Hesiodos disebut 'tanpa belas kasih', 'menjijikkan', dan 'mengerikan'.
claim.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades was perhaps the most feared of the gods and is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous'.

claims_provenance.quote: Perhaps the most feared of the gods, he is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous' Hades.

claim.id: Bahkan menyebut namanya dihindari; sebagai gantinya dipakai gelar seperti Eubuleus (pemberi nasihat baik).
claim.en: Even speaking his name was avoided; epithets such as Eubuleus (giving good advice) were used instead.

claims_provenance.quote: Indeed, even to speak his name was avoided; instead epithets were used such as Eubuleus (giving good advice).

claim.id: Ada pula catatan tentang praktik kurban untuk Hades yang dilakukan malam hari dengan darah korban dibiarkan meresap ke tanah agar sampai ke dewa dunia bawah.
claim.en: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices in honour of Hades, carried out at night, with the victims' blood left to seep into the earth to reach the underworld god.

claims_provenance.quote: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices made in honour of Hades, carried out at night and where the blood of victims was left to seep down into the earth to reach the underworld god.

claim.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades memiliki helm buatan Hephaistos yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; helm itu dipakai Athena saat melawan Ares dalam Iliad dan oleh Perseus dalam perburuan kepala Medusa.
claim.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades had a helmet made by Hephaistos that rendered the wearer invisible; it was used by Athena when she fought Ares in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for Medusa's head.

claims_provenance.quote: The god also had a helmet made by Hephaistos which rendered the wearer invisible, and it was this helmet that was used by Athena when she fought Ares in Homer's account of the Trojan War in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for the head of Medusa.

claim.id: Dalam mitologi, Hades jatuh cinta pada Persephone, putri Zeus dan Demeter, dan menculiknya untuk tinggal bersamanya.
claim.en: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

claims_provenance.quote: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

claim.id: Hades menipu gadis itu agar memakan biji delima sehingga ia hanya dapat kembali kepada yang hidup selama setengah tahun; mitos ini mungkin melambangkan siklus hidup dan mati, penanaman dan panen.
claim.en: Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed so that she could only return to the living for half of the year; the myth was perhaps symbolic of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

claims_provenance.quote: However, Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed and therefore she could only return to the living for half of the year. This myth was symbolic perhaps of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

claim.id: Ketika Hermes mengetahuinya, ia menuntut Persephone dikembalikan kepada Demeter dan diputuskan bahwa jika ia belum makan apa pun dari Hades, ia boleh kembali ke dunia atas.
claim.en: When Hermes discovered this he demanded that Persephone be returned to Demeter, and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades she could return to the upper world.

claims_provenance.quote: When Hermes discovered this, he demanded Persephone be returned to Demeter and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades, she could return to the upper world.

claim.id: Dalam seni Yunani Arkais dan Klasik, Hades paling sering digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, lambang kekayaan mineral dan nabati dari tanah.
claim.en: In Archaic and Classical Greek art Hades is most often a mature bearded man holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia, symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth that comes from the ground.

claims_provenance.quote: In Archaic and Classical Greek art, Hades is most often represented as a more mature man, bearded and holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia - symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth which comes from the ground.

claim.id: Kadang ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta yang ditarik kuda hitam, sering dengan Persephone di sisinya.
claim.en: On occasion he is shown seated on an ebony throne or riding a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

claims_provenance.quote: On occasion he is seated on an ebony throne or rides a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

claim.id: Hermes dipercaya menuntun jiwa ke Sungai Styx di dunia bawah, tempat juru perahu tua Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades, yang dijaga Kerberos, anjing ganas berkepala tiga (atau lima puluh menurut Hesiodos) yang menjaga agar jiwa tetap di dalam.
claim.en: Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx, where the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades, guarded by Kerberos, a ferocious three-headed dog (fifty-headed according to Hesiod) who kept souls in rather than others out.

claims_provenance.quote: The god Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx in the underworld, at which point the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades where Kerberos - the ferocious three-headed dog (or fifty-headed according to Hesiod) with serpents coming out of its body - stood guard to keep souls in rather than to keep others out.

claim.id: Untuk membayar Charon, keluarga yang berduka menaruh koin di mulut jenazah (bagi orang Yunani koin tradisionalnya obol bernilai rendah); orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar dihukum mengembara di bumi sebagai hantu.
claim.en: To pay Charon, bereaved families put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (the traditional Greek coin was the low-value obol); the unburied or those unable to pay were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

claims_provenance.quote: It was for payment to Charon that bereaved family members put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (for Greeks the traditional coin was the low-value obol). The unburied or those without the means to pay the boatman were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

claim.id: Secara tradisional, tiga hakim jiwa adalah Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos, yang terkenal karena hidup terhormat.
claim.en: Traditionally the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

claims_provenance.quote: Traditionally, the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

claim.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik lebih dulu diajak minum air Sungai Lethe yang membuat mereka melupakan semua hal buruk, lalu dibawa ke Padang Elysium yang indah.
claim.en: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe, which made them forget all bad things, and then to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

claims_provenance.quote: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe which made them forget all bad things, and then they were taken to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

claim.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup buruk diserahkan kepada para Furia dan dibawa ke Tartarus, tingkat terendah Hades, untuk menerima hukuman atas perbuatan mereka.
claim.en: Souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to be punished for their misdeeds.

claims_provenance.quote: Those souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to receive punishment for their misdeeds.

claim.id: Meski menakutkan bagi yang hidup, Hades dikunjungi beberapa pahlawan: Hercules untuk menangkap Kerberos pada pekerjaan kedua belasnya, Odiseus untuk meminta nasihat Tiresias, Orpheus untuk mencari Eurydice, dan Theseus serta Peirithoos untuk menculik Persephone agar dinikahi Peirithoos.
claim.en: Though fearful to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes: Hercules to capture Kerberos in his last labour, Odysseus to seek Tiresias's advice, Orpheus to find Eurydice, and Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that Peirithoos might marry her.

claims_provenance.quote: Although a fearful place to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes in the course of their various adventures, including Hercules to capture Kerberos in the last of his twelve labours, by Odysseus to seek the advice of wise Tiresias, by Orpheus to find Eurydice, and by Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that she might marry the latter.

claim.id: Kedua pahlawan terakhir itu kurang beruntung karena Hades memenjarakan mereka di dua singgasana (atau mengikat mereka pada dua batu menurut kisah lain), dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian lolos ketika Hercules membebaskannya.
claim.en: The last two heroes were less fortunate: Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied them to two rocks in other accounts), and only Theseus later escaped when Hercules released him.

claims_provenance.quote: These last two heroes were, however, less fortunate than the others in that Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied to two rocks in other accounts) and only Theseus would later escape from the underworld when Hercules released him.

claim.id: Setelah para dewa Olimpus menggulingkan Titan lalu Raksasa, Hades mengundi dengan saudara-saudaranya, Zeus dan Poseidon, untuk menentukan bagian dunia yang akan diperintah masing-masing.
claim.en: After the Olympian gods overthrew first the Titans and then the Giants, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

claims_provenance.quote: Following the overthrow of first the Titans and then the Giants by the Olympian gods, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

claim.id: Asal-usul nama Hades tidak pasti, tetapi sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
claim.en: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

claims_provenance.quote: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

claim.id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi akhirnya menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkan semuanya menjadi Pluto, Latinisasi dari Plouton.
claim.en: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades, merging them all into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton.

claims_provenance.quote: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita, and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus, with Hades, and merged all these figures into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton

claim.id: Hades adalah putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, meski itu juga membuatnya putra terakhir yang dimuntahkan ayahnya.
claim.en: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

short_description.id: Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan penguasa alam bawah dalam agama serta mitologi Yunani kuno, yang juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan bumi.
short_description.en: Hades is the god of the dead and ruler of the underworld in ancient Greek religion and mythology, also associated with the wealth of the earth.

long_description.id: Dalam agama Yunani kuno, Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan kekayaan serta raja alam bawah. Namanya juga dipakai untuk menyebut wilayah alam bawah itu sendiri. Ia putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, ditelan ayahnya sejak lahir, lalu bersama Zeus dan Poseidon mengalahkan para Titan. Dalam pembagian kosmos ia memperoleh alam bawah, Zeus langit, dan Poseidon laut.
long_description.en: In ancient Greek religion Hades is god of the dead and riches and king of the underworld. His name also refers to the underworld itself. He is the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, swallowed by his father at birth, and with Zeus and Poseidon he overcame the Titans. In the division of the cosmos he received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea.

long_description.id: Hades memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan yang layak. Ia juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan tersembunyi di dalam bumi, dan Plouton berarti pemberi kekayaan. Karena ditakuti, namanya dihindari dan orang memakai gelar seperti Eubuleus, kurban baginya dilakukan malam hari, dan Hesiodos menyebutnya tanpa belas kasih di hatinya; satu sumber lain menyebutnya garang dan tak kenal ampun.
long_description.en: Hades presides over funeral rites and defends the dead's right to due burial. He is also associated with hidden wealth beneath the earth, and Plouton means the giver of wealth. Because he was feared, his name was avoided and epithets such as Eubuleus were used, sacrifices to him were made at night, and Hesiod calls him pitiless in heart; another source calls him fierce and inexorable.

long_description.id: Persephone disebut istrinya, yang ia culik ke alam bawah. Ketika Demeter menimpakan paceklik, Persephone dijemput, tetapi karena telah memakan biji delima ia harus kembali selama sebagian tiap tahun. Hades sendiri digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olimpus.
long_description.en: Persephone is named as his wife, whom he abducted to the underworld. When Demeter brought famine, Persephone was fetched back, but since she had eaten the pomegranate seed she had to return for part of each year. Hades himself is portrayed as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.

long_description.id: Dalam seni, Hades digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, kadang duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta berkuda hitam. Ia juga memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; sumber-sumber berbeda tentang siapa yang membuatnya. Orang Romawi mengenalnya sebagai Dis atau Pluto.
long_description.en: Greek artists most often show Hades as a mature bearded man with a cornucopia, a libation vase, a sceptre, or a two-pronged spear, and at times on an ebony throne or in a chariot with black horses. He also has a helmet that makes the wearer invisible; sources differ on who made it. The Romans knew him as Dis or Pluto.

long_description.id: Dunia bawah dipercaya dimasuki melalui Sungai Styx, tempat Hermes menuntun jiwa dan Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang yang dijaga Kerberos. Jiwa dinilai oleh Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos: yang baik ke Padang Elysium, yang buruk ke Tartarus. Beberapa pahlawan mengunjunginya, antara lain Hercules, Odiseus, dan Orpheus.
long_description.en: The underworld was believed to be entered across the river Styx, where Hermes leads souls and Charon ferries them to gates guarded by Kerberos. Souls are judged by Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos: the good go to the Elysian Fields, the bad to Tartarus. Several heroes visited it, among them Hercules, Odysseus, and Orpheus.

cultural_context.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, keyakinan bahwa orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar juru perahu mengembara sebagai hantu menunjukkan sifat Hades yang ambigu; alam bawah tidak selalu tempat siksa, tetapi pada umumnya tempat peristirahatan terakhir jiwa.
cultural_context.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, the belief that the unburied or those unable to pay the boatman wandered as ghosts points to an ambiguous view of Hades: the realm was not necessarily a place of torment, but in most cases just the soul's final resting place.

literal_meaning.id: Asalnya tidak pasti; sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
literal_meaning.en: Its origin is uncertain; since antiquity it has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one".

who.id: Dewa orang mati dan penguasa alam bawah.
who.en: God of the dead and ruler of the underworld.

role.id: Memerintah alam bawah dan berkaitan dengan upacara pemakaman.
role.en: Rules the underworld and is linked to funerary rites.

famous_for.id: Mendapat alam bawah saat pembagian kosmos dan menculik Persephone.
famous_for.en: Receiving the underworld in the division of the cosmos and abducting Persephone.

did_you_know.id: Hades adalah satu-satunya dewa yang tidak tinggal di Gunung Olimpus; ia berdiam di istana gelap di bawah bumi.
did_you_know.en: Of the Greek gods, only Hades did not live on Mount Olympus; his home was a dark palace under the earth.

description.id: Hades memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; Athena dan Perseus memakainya dalam kisah-kisah.
description.en: Hades has a helmet that makes the wearer invisible; Athena and Perseus used it in stories.

description.id: Ia memerintah alam bawah, dan satu sumber menyebut ia menjaga gerbangnya tertutup agar tak ada arwah lolos atau kembali.
description.en: He rules the underworld, and one source says he kept its gates closed so no shade could escape or return.

description.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan kekayaan tersembunyi bumi, dari tanah subur hingga emas, perak, dan logam lain.
description.en: He is associated with the earth's hidden wealth, from fertile soil to gold, silver, and other metals.

description.id: Ia memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan layak.
description.en: He presides over funeral rites and defends the dead's right to due burial.

description.id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkannya menjadi Pluto.
description.en: Roman-era mythographers equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades and merged them into Pluto.

title.en: Birth and the war against the Titans

role.id: Putra Kronos yang ditelan lalu dimuntahkan.
role.en: The son of Kronos who is swallowed and then disgorged.

summary.id: Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir; Zeus membuat Kronos memuntahkan mereka, dan para dewa mengusir Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di Tartaros. Kiklops juga menghadiahkan helm untuk Haides.
summary.en: Haides is swallowed by Kronos at birth; Zeus makes Kronos disgorge them, and the gods drive the Titans from heaven and lock them in Tartaros. The Kyklopes also give a helmet for Haides.

role.id: Saudara yang memperoleh alam bawah lewat undian.
role.en: The brother who receives the underworld by lot.

summary.id: Setelah menggulingkan Titan, Hades mengundi dengan Zeus dan Poseidon, dan Hades memperoleh alam bawah, Zeus langit, Poseidon laut.
summary.en: After overthrowing the Titans, Hades drew lots with Zeus and Poseidon and received the underworld, Zeus the sky, Poseidon the sea.

summary.id: Hades menginginkan pengantin dan Zeus menyetujui penculikan Persephone. Demeter menimpakan paceklik sampai Persephone dikembalikan, tetapi karena sudah memakan biji delima ia harus kembali selama sebagian tiap tahun.
summary.en: Hades wants a bride and Zeus assents to the abduction of Persephone. Demeter brings famine until Persephone is returned, but because she ate the pomegranate seed she must return for part of each year.

role.en: The ruler of the place where souls are judged.

summary.id: Di gerbang Hades, jiwa dinilai oleh Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos; yang baik minum dari Lethe dan masuk Padang Elysium, yang buruk dibawa ke Tartarus.
summary.en: At the gates of Hades souls are judged by Minos, Rhadamanthys and Aiakos; the good drink from Lethe and enter the Elysian Fields, the bad are taken to Tartarus.

role.id: Penguasa yang dikunjungi, dan kadang memenjarakan, para pahlawan.
role.en: The ruler visited by, and sometimes imprisoning, heroes.

summary.id: Hercules, Odiseus, dan Orpheus mengunjungi alam bawah; Theseus dan Peirithoos berusaha menculik Persephone sehingga Hades memenjarakan mereka, dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian dibebaskan Hercules.
summary.en: Hercules, Odysseus and Orpheus visit the underworld; Theseus and Peirithoos try to capture Persephone and Hades imprisons them, and only Theseus is later released by Hercules.

role.id: Dewa yang gemetar di dunia bawah.
role.en: The god who trembles in the underworld.

summary.id: Ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati.
summary.en: As Zeus battles Typhoeus, Haides trembles where he rules over the dead.

description.id: Wilayah di bawah bumi yang diperintah Hades dan dianggap tujuan akhir jiwa orang mati.
description.en: The region below the earth ruled by Hades, regarded as the final destination for the souls of the dead.

description.id: Sungai di dunia bawah tempat Hermes menuntun jiwa dan Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades.
description.en: The underworld river to which Hermes leads souls and from which Charon ferries them to the gates of Hades.

description.id: Tingkat terendah Hades, tempat jiwa yang dinilai buruk menerima hukuman.
description.en: The lowest level of Hades, where souls judged to have led bad lives are punished.

description.id: Tempat indah tujuan jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik.
description.en: The idyllic destination of souls judged to have led especially good lives.

description.id: Tempat Hades memiliki pelataran suci dan kuil yang hanya dibuka setahun sekali.
description.en: Where Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple opened only once a year.

claims.quote: in the ancient Greek religion and mythology, is the god of the dead and riches and the King of the underworld, with which his name became synonymous.

statement.id: Hades adalah dewa orang mati dan kekayaan serta raja alam bawah dalam agama Yunani kuno.
statement.en: Hades is the ancient Greek god of the dead and riches and king of the underworld.

claims.quote: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea

statement.id: Hades mendapat alam bawah, Zeus langit, dan Poseidon laut.
statement.en: Hades received the underworld, Zeus the sky, and Poseidon the sea.

claims.quote: He presided over funeral rites and defended the right of the dead to due burial.

statement.id: Hades memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan layak.
statement.en: Hades presided over funerary rites and defended the dead's right to burial.

claims.quote: Haides was also the god of the hidden wealth of the earth, from the fertile soil with nourished the seed-grain, to the mined wealth of gold, silver and other metals.

statement.id: Hades juga dewa kekayaan tersembunyi di bumi, dari tanah subur hingga logam.
statement.en: Hades was also god of the earth's hidden wealth, including fertile soil and metals.

claims.quote: Hades was both the name of the ancient Greek god of the underworld (Roman name: Pluto) and the name of the shadowy place below the earth which was considered the final destination for the souls of the dead.

statement.id: Hades adalah nama dewa sekaligus nama tempat alam bawah yang dianggap tujuan akhir jiwa orang mati.
statement.en: Hades names both the god and the underworld considered the destination of dead souls.

claims.quote: The god's wife was Persephone whom he abducted to join him in the underworld

statement.id: Persephone disebut sebagai istri Hades yang dibawanya ke alam bawah.
statement.en: Persephone is named as Hades's wife whom he brought to the underworld.

claims.quote: Hades was the only god not to reside on Mount Olympus, dwelling instead in a dark palace beneath the earth.

statement.id: Hades digambarkan tinggal di istana gelap di bawah bumi, bukan di Olympus.
statement.en: Hades is described as dwelling in a dark palace beneath the earth rather than on Olympus.

claims.quote: Haides was devoured by Kronos (Cronus) as soon as he was born, along with four of his siblings. Zeus later caused the Titan to disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them away in the pit of Tartaros.

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, Haides ditelan Kronos begitu lahir bersama empat saudaranya; Zeus kemudian membuat sang Titan memuntahkan mereka, dan bersama-sama mereka mengusir para dewa Titan dari langit dan mengurung mereka di jurang Tartaros.
statement.en: According to Theoi, Haides was devoured by Kronos as soon as he was born along with four siblings; Zeus later made the Titan disgorge them, and together they drove the Titan gods from heaven and locked them in the pit of Tartaros.

claims.quote: I [Poseidon] when the lots were shaken drew the grey sea to live in forever; Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky, in the cloud and the bright air.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Homer Iliad 15.187 ff (trans. Lattimore)

statement.id: Dalam Iliad (terjemahan Lattimore), Poseidon berkata bahwa ketika undi dikocok ia mendapat laut kelabu, Aides mendapat undi kabut dan kegelapan, dan Zeus mendapat langit luas.
statement.en: In the Iliad (Lattimore's translation), Poseidon says that when the lots were shaken he drew the grey sea, Aides drew the lot of the mists and the darkness, and Zeus was allotted the wide sky.

claims.quote: strong Haides (Hades), pitiless in heart, who dwells under the earth
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 453 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

statement.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides digambarkan kuat, tanpa belas kasih di hatinya, dan berdiam di bawah bumi.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony Haides is described as strong, pitiless in heart, and dwelling under the earth.

claims.quote: Haides desired a bride and petitioned his brother Zeus to grant him one of his daughters. The god offered him Persephone, the daughter of Demeter. However, knowing that the goddess would resist the marriage, he assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

statement.id: Haides menginginkan pengantin dan memohon kepada saudaranya Zeus agar memberinya salah satu putrinya; Zeus menawarkan Persephone, putri Demeter, dan karena tahu Demeter akan menolak, ia menyetujui penculikan paksa gadis itu.
statement.en: Haides desired a bride and asked his brother Zeus for one of his daughters; Zeus offered Persephone, daughter of Demeter, and, knowing Demeter would resist, assented to the forceful abduction of the girl.

claims.quote: When Demeter learned of this, she was furious and caused a great dearth to fall upon the earth until her daughter was returned. Zeus was forced to concede lest mankind perish, and the girl was fetched forth from the underworld. However, since she had tasted of the pomegranate seed, she was forced to return to him for a portion of each year.

statement.id: Demeter murka dan menimpakan paceklik besar ke bumi sampai putrinya dikembalikan; Zeus terpaksa mengalah dan gadis itu dijemput dari dunia bawah, tetapi karena telah mencicipi biji delima ia harus kembali kepada Haides selama sebagian tiap tahun.
statement.en: Demeter was furious and brought a great dearth upon the earth until her daughter was returned; Zeus was forced to concede and the girl was fetched from the underworld, but since she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return to Haides for a portion of each year.

claims.quote: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god. He was depicted as either Aidoneus, enthroned in the underworld, holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton (Pluton), the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

statement.id: Haides digambarkan sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap yang agung, entah sebagai Aidoneus yang bertakhta di dunia bawah dengan tongkat berujung burung, atau sebagai Plouton, pemberi kekayaan, yang mencurahkan kesuburan dari cornucopia.
statement.en: Haides was depicted as a dark-bearded, regal god, either as Aidoneus enthroned in the underworld holding a bird-tipped sceptre, or as Plouton, the giver of wealth, pouring fertility from a cornucopia.

claims.quote: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

statement.id: Bangsa Romawi menamainya Dis atau Pluto, bentuk Latin dari gelar Yunaninya Plouton, "Penguasa Kekayaan".
statement.en: The Romans named him Dis, or Pluto, the Latin form of his Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches."

claims.quote: He possessed a helmet which rendered the wearer invisible (Il. v. 845), and later traditions stated that this helmet was given him as a present by the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat, dan tradisi kemudian menyebut helm itu hadiah dari para Kiklops setelah mereka dibebaskan dari Tartarus.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades possessed a helmet that rendered the wearer invisible, and later traditions said it was a gift from the Cyclopes after their delivery from Tartarus.

claims.quote: He kept the gates of the lower world closed (whence he is called ... that no shade might be able to escape or return to the region of light.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Haides menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup agar tak ada arwah yang dapat lolos atau kembali ke wilayah cahaya.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed so that no shade could escape or return to the region of light.

claims.quote: His character is described as fierce and inexorable, whence of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, wataknya digambarkan garang dan tak kenal ampun sehingga di antara semua dewa ia paling dibenci manusia.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, his character is described as fierce and inexorable, so that of all the gods he was most hated by mortals.

claims.quote: In Elis he had a sacred enclosure and a temple, which was opened only once in every year
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Di Elis Haides memiliki pelataran suci dan sebuah kuil yang hanya dibuka sekali setiap tahun.
statement.en: In Elis Hades had a sacred enclosure and a temple that was opened only once every year.

claims.quote: Plato (Cratyl. p. 403) observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, Plato mencatat bahwa orang lebih suka menyebutnya Pluton (pemberi kekayaan) daripada mengucapkan nama Hades atau Aides yang ditakuti.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, Plato observes that people preferred calling him Pluton (the giver of wealth) to pronouncing the dreaded name of Hades or Aides.

claims.quote: The etymology of Hades is uncertain: some derive it from a-idein, whence it would signify "the god who makes invisible,"
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, asal-usul kata Hades tidak pasti; sebagian menurunkannya dari a-idein sehingga berarti "dewa yang membuat tak terlihat".
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, the etymology of Hades is uncertain; some derive it from a-idein, so that it would signify "the god who makes invisible".

claims.quote: In Homer Aides is invariably the name of the god; but in later times it was transferred to his house, his abode or kingdom, so that it became a name for the lower world itself.
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, dalam Homeros Aides selalu nama sang dewa, tetapi kemudian dialihkan ke rumah, tempat tinggal, atau kerajaannya sehingga menjadi nama dunia bawah itu sendiri.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, in Homer Aides is always the name of the god, but later it was transferred to his house, abode or kingdom and became a name for the lower world itself.

claims.quote: The three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides. The usual account, however, describes them as earth-born.
claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Offspring of Hades

statement.id: Menurut Theoi, tiga dewi murka bumi kadang digambarkan sebagai putri Haides, tetapi kisah yang lazim menyebut mereka lahir dari bumi.
statement.en: According to Theoi, the three goddesses of earthly wrath were sometimes represented as daughters of Haides, but the usual account describes them as earth-born.

claims.quote: In return the Kyklopes (Cyclopes) gave Zeus thunder, lightning, and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Pluton) [Haides] and a trident for Poseidon.

statement.id: Dalam Bibliotheca Pseudo-Apollodoros, para Kiklops memberi Zeus guntur dan petir, serta helm untuk Plouton (Haides) dan trisula untuk Poseidon.
statement.en: In Pseudo-Apollodorus's Bibliotheca the Kyklopes gave Zeus thunder, lightning and a thunderbolt, as well as a helmet for Plouton (Haides) and a trident for Poseidon.

claims.locator: Classical Literature Quotes, Hesiod Theogony 820 ff (trans. Evelyn-White)

statement.id: Dalam Theogony Hesiodos, Haides gemetar di tempat ia memerintah orang mati di bawah ketika Zeus bertarung melawan Typhoeus.
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony, Haides trembled where he rules over the dead below as Zeus battled Typhoeus.

claims.quote: Perhaps the most feared of the gods, he is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous' Hades.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades mungkin dewa yang paling ditakuti dan oleh Homeros maupun Hesiodos disebut 'tanpa belas kasih', 'menjijikkan', dan 'mengerikan'.
statement.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades was perhaps the most feared of the gods and is described by both Homer and Hesiod as 'pitiless', 'loathsome', and 'monstrous'.

claims.quote: Indeed, even to speak his name was avoided; instead epithets were used such as Eubuleus (giving good advice).

statement.id: Bahkan menyebut namanya dihindari; sebagai gantinya dipakai gelar seperti Eubuleus (pemberi nasihat baik).
statement.en: Even speaking his name was avoided; epithets such as Eubuleus (giving good advice) were used instead.

claims.quote: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices made in honour of Hades, carried out at night and where the blood of victims was left to seep down into the earth to reach the underworld god.

statement.id: Ada pula catatan tentang praktik kurban untuk Hades yang dilakukan malam hari dengan darah korban dibiarkan meresap ke tanah agar sampai ke dewa dunia bawah.
statement.en: There are also accounts of sacrificial practices in honour of Hades, carried out at night, with the victims' blood left to seep into the earth to reach the underworld god.

claims.quote: The god also had a helmet made by Hephaistos which rendered the wearer invisible, and it was this helmet that was used by Athena when she fought Ares in Homer's account of the Trojan War in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for the head of Medusa.

statement.id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Hades memiliki helm buatan Hephaistos yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat; helm itu dipakai Athena saat melawan Ares dalam Iliad dan oleh Perseus dalam perburuan kepala Medusa.
statement.en: According to World History Encyclopedia, Hades had a helmet made by Hephaistos that rendered the wearer invisible; it was used by Athena when she fought Ares in the Iliad and by Perseus in his quest for Medusa's head.

claims.quote: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi, Hades jatuh cinta pada Persephone, putri Zeus dan Demeter, dan menculiknya untuk tinggal bersamanya.
statement.en: In mythology, Hades fell in love with Persephone, daughter of Zeus and Demeter, and abducted her to live with him.

claims.quote: However, Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed and therefore she could only return to the living for half of the year. This myth was symbolic perhaps of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

statement.id: Hades menipu gadis itu agar memakan biji delima sehingga ia hanya dapat kembali kepada yang hidup selama setengah tahun; mitos ini mungkin melambangkan siklus hidup dan mati, penanaman dan panen.
statement.en: Hades tricked the girl into eating a pomegranate seed so that she could only return to the living for half of the year; the myth was perhaps symbolic of the cycle of life and death, planting and harvest.

claims.quote: When Hermes discovered this, he demanded Persephone be returned to Demeter and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades, she could return to the upper world.

statement.id: Ketika Hermes mengetahuinya, ia menuntut Persephone dikembalikan kepada Demeter dan diputuskan bahwa jika ia belum makan apa pun dari Hades, ia boleh kembali ke dunia atas.
statement.en: When Hermes discovered this he demanded that Persephone be returned to Demeter, and it was decided that if she had not eaten any food from Hades she could return to the upper world.

claims.quote: In Archaic and Classical Greek art, Hades is most often represented as a more mature man, bearded and holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia - symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth which comes from the ground.

statement.id: Dalam seni Yunani Arkais dan Klasik, Hades paling sering digambarkan sebagai pria dewasa berjanggut yang memegang tongkat, tombak bermata dua, bejana libasi, atau cornucopia, lambang kekayaan mineral dan nabati dari tanah.
statement.en: In Archaic and Classical Greek art Hades is most often a mature bearded man holding a sceptre, a two-pronged spear, a libation vase, or a cornucopia, symbolic of the mineral and vegetable wealth that comes from the ground.

claims.quote: On occasion he is seated on an ebony throne or rides a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

statement.id: Kadang ia digambarkan duduk di singgasana eboni atau menunggang kereta yang ditarik kuda hitam, sering dengan Persephone di sisinya.
statement.en: On occasion he is shown seated on an ebony throne or riding a chariot pulled by black horses, often with Persephone at his side.

claims.quote: The god Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx in the underworld, at which point the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades where Kerberos - the ferocious three-headed dog (or fifty-headed according to Hesiod) with serpents coming out of its body - stood guard to keep souls in rather than to keep others out.

statement.id: Hermes dipercaya menuntun jiwa ke Sungai Styx di dunia bawah, tempat juru perahu tua Charon menyeberangkan mereka ke gerbang Hades, yang dijaga Kerberos, anjing ganas berkepala tiga (atau lima puluh menurut Hesiodos) yang menjaga agar jiwa tetap di dalam.
statement.en: Hermes was believed to lead souls to the river Styx, where the aged boatman Charon ferried them to the gates of Hades, guarded by Kerberos, a ferocious three-headed dog (fifty-headed according to Hesiod) who kept souls in rather than others out.

claims.quote: It was for payment to Charon that bereaved family members put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (for Greeks the traditional coin was the low-value obol). The unburied or those without the means to pay the boatman were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

statement.id: Untuk membayar Charon, keluarga yang berduka menaruh koin di mulut jenazah (bagi orang Yunani koin tradisionalnya obol bernilai rendah); orang yang tak dikubur atau tak mampu membayar dihukum mengembara di bumi sebagai hantu.
statement.en: To pay Charon, bereaved families put a coin in the mouth of the deceased (the traditional Greek coin was the low-value obol); the unburied or those unable to pay were condemned to wander the Earth as ghosts.

claims.quote: Traditionally, the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

statement.id: Secara tradisional, tiga hakim jiwa adalah Minos, Rhadamanthys, dan Aiakos, yang terkenal karena hidup terhormat.
statement.en: Traditionally the three judges of souls were Minos, Rhadamanthys, and Aiakos, themselves noted for their honourable lives.

claims.quote: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe which made them forget all bad things, and then they were taken to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

statement.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup sangat baik lebih dulu diajak minum air Sungai Lethe yang membuat mereka melupakan semua hal buruk, lalu dibawa ke Padang Elysium yang indah.
statement.en: Souls judged to have led especially good lives were first taken to drink the waters of the River Lethe, which made them forget all bad things, and then to the idyllic Elysian Fields.

claims.quote: Those souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to receive punishment for their misdeeds.

statement.id: Jiwa yang dinilai hidup buruk diserahkan kepada para Furia dan dibawa ke Tartarus, tingkat terendah Hades, untuk menerima hukuman atas perbuatan mereka.
statement.en: Souls judged to have led bad lives were put in the hands of the Furies and taken to Tartarus, the lowest level of Hades, to be punished for their misdeeds.

claims.quote: Although a fearful place to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes in the course of their various adventures, including Hercules to capture Kerberos in the last of his twelve labours, by Odysseus to seek the advice of wise Tiresias, by Orpheus to find Eurydice, and by Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that she might marry the latter.

statement.id: Meski menakutkan bagi yang hidup, Hades dikunjungi beberapa pahlawan: Hercules untuk menangkap Kerberos pada pekerjaan kedua belasnya, Odiseus untuk meminta nasihat Tiresias, Orpheus untuk mencari Eurydice, dan Theseus serta Peirithoos untuk menculik Persephone agar dinikahi Peirithoos.
statement.en: Though fearful to the living, Hades was visited by several heroes: Hercules to capture Kerberos in his last labour, Odysseus to seek Tiresias's advice, Orpheus to find Eurydice, and Theseus and Peirithoos to capture Persephone so that Peirithoos might marry her.

claims.quote: These last two heroes were, however, less fortunate than the others in that Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied to two rocks in other accounts) and only Theseus would later escape from the underworld when Hercules released him.

statement.id: Kedua pahlawan terakhir itu kurang beruntung karena Hades memenjarakan mereka di dua singgasana (atau mengikat mereka pada dua batu menurut kisah lain), dan hanya Theseus yang kemudian lolos ketika Hercules membebaskannya.
statement.en: The last two heroes were less fortunate: Hades imprisoned them in two thrones (or tied them to two rocks in other accounts), and only Theseus later escaped when Hercules released him.

claims.quote: Following the overthrow of first the Titans and then the Giants by the Olympian gods, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

statement.id: Setelah para dewa Olimpus menggulingkan Titan lalu Raksasa, Hades mengundi dengan saudara-saudaranya, Zeus dan Poseidon, untuk menentukan bagian dunia yang akan diperintah masing-masing.
statement.en: After the Olympian gods overthrew first the Titans and then the Giants, Hades drew lots with his brothers Zeus and Poseidon to decide which part of the world each would rule.

claims.quote: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

statement.id: Asal-usul nama Hades tidak pasti, tetapi sejak zaman kuno umumnya dianggap berarti "yang tak terlihat".
statement.en: The origin of Hades's name is uncertain but has generally been seen as meaning "the unseen one" since antiquity.

claims.quote: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita, and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus, with Hades, and merged all these figures into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton

statement.id: Para mitograf zaman Romawi akhirnya menyamakan dewa Etruria Aita serta dewa Romawi Dis Pater dan Orcus dengan Hades dan menggabungkan semuanya menjadi Pluto, Latinisasi dari Plouton.
statement.en: Roman-era mythographers eventually equated the Etruscan god Aita and the Roman gods Dis Pater and Orcus with Hades, merging them all into Pluto, a Latinisation of Plouton.

claims.quote: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

statement.id: Hades adalah putra sulung Kronos dan Rhea, meski itu juga membuatnya putra terakhir yang dimuntahkan ayahnya.
statement.en: Hades was the eldest son of Cronus and Rhea, although this also made him the last son to be regurgitated by his father.

claims.quote: Martin Litchfield West argues instead for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up" from the universality of death.

statement.id: Martin Litchfield West mengusulkan makna asli "yang memimpin pertemuan" yang berasal dari universalitas kematian.
statement.en: Martin Litchfield West instead argues for an original meaning of "the one who presides over meeting up", from the universality of death.

claims.quote: Hence he is called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios), or the king of the shades
claims.locator: Encyclopedia (Dictionary of Greek and Roman Biography and Mythology)

statement.id: Menurut kamus yang dikutip Theoi, karena itu ia disebut Zeus dunia bawah (Zeus katachthonios) atau raja para arwah.
statement.en: According to the dictionary reproduced on Theoi, he is hence called the infernal Zeus (Zeus katachthonios) or the king of the shades.
