short_description.id: Pluto adalah dewa dunia bawah Romawi dan padanan Hades dalam mitologi Yunani.
short_description.en: Pluto is the Roman underworld god and counterpart of Greek Hades.

long_description.id:
Pluto adalah anak Saturnus dan Ops, serta saudara Jupiter dan Neptunus. Ia berkuasa atas Tartarus dan dunia bawah. Theoi menjelaskan nama Pluto berkaitan dengan gelar Yunani Plouton, "penguasa kekayaan". Dalam uraian Theoi tentang Hades, padanannya dalam mitologi Yunani, ia memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan yang layak, serta dikenal sebagai dewa kekayaan tersembunyi di dalam bumi.

Proserpina menjadi ratunya setelah diculik Pluto. Sumber berbeda tentang lamanya ia berada di dunia bawah: satu sumber menyebut tiga atau enam bulan tiap tahun, sedangkan versi Ovid menyebut enam bulan bersama ibunya dan enam bulan bersama suaminya. Theoi mencatat bahwa karena telah mencicipi biji delima, ia harus kembali untuk sebagian tiap tahun.

Pluto dikisahkan mengendarai kereta emas dengan empat kuda hitam serta memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat. Cerberus menjaga pintu masuk dunia bawah. Theoi menggambarkan Hades sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap dan berwibawa seperti raja, dan mengutip uraian bahwa ia menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup, berwatak garang serta tak kenal ampun, sehingga paling dibenci manusia. Dalam kisah Orpheus, Pluto mengizinkan Eurydice dibawa kembali dengan syarat Orpheus tidak menoleh.
long_description.en:
Pluto is the son of Saturnus and Ops and brother of Jupiter and Neptunus. He rules Tartarus and the underworld. Theoi connects Pluto with the Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches". In Theoi's account of Hades, his Greek counterpart, he oversaw burial ceremonies and championed the entitlement of the dead to proper burial, and he was lord of the concealed riches of the earth.

Proserpina becomes his queen after Pluto abducts her. Sources differ over her time in the underworld: one source gives three or six months yearly, while Ovid's version gives six months with her mother and six with her husband. Theoi notes that because she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return for a portion of each year.

Pluto is said to drive a golden chariot with four black horses and own a helmet that makes its wearer invisible. Cerberus guards the underworld entrance. Theoi describes Hades as a dark-bearded, regal god, and quotes an account that Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed and was fierce and inexorable, so that mortals hated him most of all the gods. In the Orpheus tale, Pluto permits Eurydice's return if Orpheus does not look back.

summary.id: Dalam Metamorphoses karya Ovid, anak panah Cupid mengenai dada Pluto, lalu Proserpine dilihat dan dibawa pergi olehnya; bumi yang terhantam membuka jalan menuju Tartarus, dan Proserpine mengunyah tujuh butir yang dipetik dari kulit yang pucat. Menurut satu sumber, ia diculik dan terpaksa menghabiskan tiga (sebagian menyebut enam) bulan tiap tahun di dunia bawah; versi Ovid menyebut enam bulan bersama ibunya dan enam bulan bersama suaminya. Theoi mencatat bahwa karena telah mencicipi biji delima ia harus kembali untuk sebagian tiap tahun.
summary.en: In Ovid's Metamorphoses, Cupid's arrow strikes Pluto in the breast, and Proserpine is then seen and carried off by him; the smitten earth makes way to Tartarus, and Proserpine chews seven grains picked from the pallid rind. One source says she is kidnapped and forced to spend three (some claim six) months a year in the underworld; Ovid's version gives six months with her mother and six with her husband. Theoi notes that because she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return for a portion of each year.

short_description.id: Pluto adalah dewa dunia bawah Romawi dan padanan Hades dalam mitologi Yunani.
short_description.en: Pluto is the Roman underworld god and counterpart of Greek Hades.

long_description.id: Pluto adalah anak Saturnus dan Ops, serta saudara Jupiter dan Neptunus. Ia berkuasa atas Tartarus dan dunia bawah. Theoi menjelaskan nama Pluto berkaitan dengan gelar Yunani Plouton, "penguasa kekayaan". Dalam uraian Theoi tentang Hades, padanannya dalam mitologi Yunani, ia memimpin upacara pemakaman dan membela hak orang mati atas penguburan yang layak, serta dikenal sebagai dewa kekayaan tersembunyi di dalam bumi.
long_description.en: Pluto is the son of Saturnus and Ops and brother of Jupiter and Neptunus. He rules Tartarus and the underworld. Theoi connects Pluto with the Greek title Plouton, "the Lord of Riches". In Theoi's account of Hades, his Greek counterpart, he oversaw burial ceremonies and championed the entitlement of the dead to proper burial, and he was lord of the concealed riches of the earth.

long_description.id: Proserpina menjadi ratunya setelah diculik Pluto. Sumber berbeda tentang lamanya ia berada di dunia bawah: satu sumber menyebut tiga atau enam bulan tiap tahun, sedangkan versi Ovid menyebut enam bulan bersama ibunya dan enam bulan bersama suaminya. Theoi mencatat bahwa karena telah mencicipi biji delima, ia harus kembali untuk sebagian tiap tahun.
long_description.en: Proserpina becomes his queen after Pluto abducts her. Sources differ over her time in the underworld: one source gives three or six months yearly, while Ovid's version gives six months with her mother and six with her husband. Theoi notes that because she had tasted the pomegranate seed she had to return for a portion of each year.

long_description.id: Pluto dikisahkan mengendarai kereta emas dengan empat kuda hitam serta memiliki helm yang membuat pemakainya tak terlihat. Cerberus menjaga pintu masuk dunia bawah. Theoi menggambarkan Hades sebagai dewa berjanggut gelap dan berwibawa seperti raja, dan mengutip uraian bahwa ia menjaga gerbang dunia bawah tetap tertutup, berwatak garang serta tak kenal ampun, sehingga paling dibenci manusia. Dalam kisah Orpheus, Pluto mengizinkan Eurydice dibawa kembali dengan syarat Orpheus tidak menoleh.
long_description.en: Pluto is said to drive a golden chariot with four black horses and own a helmet that makes its wearer invisible. Cerberus guards the underworld entrance. Theoi describes Hades as a dark-bearded, regal god, and quotes an account that Hades kept the gates of the lower world closed and was fierce and inexorable, so that mortals hated him most of all the gods. In the Orpheus tale, Pluto permits Eurydice's return if Orpheus does not look back.

short_description.id: Tláloc adalah dewa hujan dalam agama Aztec, juga dewa kesuburan tanah dan air, yang dipuja sebagai pemberi kehidupan sekaligus ditakuti karena kuasanya atas hujan es, guntur, dan kilat.
short_description.en: Tláloc is the god of rain in Aztec religion, also a deity of earthly fertility and water, worshipped as a giver of life and feared for his power over hail, thunder and lightning.

long_description.id:
Tláloc adalah dewa hujan dalam agama Aztec dan juga dewa kesuburan tanah serta air. Ia dipuja sebagai pemberi kehidupan dan rezeki, dan banyak ritual serta korban dipersembahkan atas namanya. Ia ditakuti karena kuasanya atas hujan es, guntur, kilat, dan hujan, meskipun bukan sosok yang jahat.

Sumber lain menggambarkannya sebagai dewa yang berwajah ganda: murah hati ketika memberi hujan, tetapi tak kenal ampun ketika mengirim badai dan kekeringan. Dalam gambaran tentang kendi air, ia menurunkan hujan dari kendi di timur, sedangkan dari kendi lain ia menurunkan kekeringan, penyakit, dan embun beku. Hujan juga dipercaya turun ketika para Tláloc memukul pecah kendi di dalam gunung, dan guntur dianggap bunyi pecahnya kendi itu.

Tláloc dikaitkan dengan gua, mata air, dan gunung, terutama gunung suci tempat ia dipercaya bersemayam. Ia juga dianggap penguasa para Tlaloque dan surga Tlalocán, tempat korban banjir, badai, dan penyakit diterima setelah mati. Untuk menenangkannya dipersembahkan korban, termasuk anak-anak yang tangisnya dianggap pertanda baik. Di Tenochtitlán, ia memiliki kuil kembar di Templo Mayor yang kedudukannya setara dengan kuil Huitzilopochtli.

Dalam seni, Tláloc lazim digambarkan bersama ular, dengan mata bulat besar dan taring besar; sumber lain menyebut taring dan mata bercincin sebagai penandanya. Penggambaran tertuanya berasal dari vas abad ke-1 SM, dan di beberapa budaya Mesoamerika ia muncul dengan nama lain seperti Cocijo bagi Zapotec.
long_description.en:
Tláloc is the god of rain in Aztec religion and also a deity of earthly fertility and water. He was worshipped as a giver of life and sustenance, and many rituals and sacrifices were held in his name. He was feared for his power over hail, thunder, lightning and rain, although not as a malicious figure.

Another source describes him as two-sided: benevolent when giving rain but unforgiving when sending storms and drought. In the imagery of the water jars, he gave out rain from the jar of the East and drought, disease and frost from the other jars. Rain was also thought to come when the Tlálocs smashed the jars inside mountains, and thunder was taken to be the noise of the jars breaking.

Caves, springs and mountains are linked with Tláloc, above all the sacred mountain believed to be his home. He was also considered ruler of the Tlaloque and of the paradise of Tlalocán, the destination after death of those claimed by floods, storms and disease. To appease him, offerings were made, including child victims whose tears were read as a good sign. At Tenochtitlán he had a twin temple on the Templo Mayor, equal in status to that of Huitzilopochtli.

In art, Tláloc is commonly depicted with snakes, goggled eyes and large fangs; another source names fangs and ringed eyes as his identifiers. His earliest depictions are on 1st-century BCE vases, and in several Mesoamerican cultures he appears under other names, such as Cocijo for the Zapotec.

era: Earliest representations in art date to the 1st century BCE

claim.en: Tláloc is the god of rain in Aztec religion.

claims_provenance.quote: is the god of rain in Aztec religion.

claim.id: Ia adalah dewa kesuburan tanah dan air yang dipuja sebagai pemberi kehidupan.
claim.en: He was also a deity of earthly fertility and water, worshipped as a giver of life.

claims_provenance.quote: He was also a deity of earthly fertility and water, and worshipped as a giver of life and sustenance; many rituals and sacrifices predicated upon these aspects were held in his name.

claim.id: Ia ditakuti karena kekuasaannya atas hujan es, guntur, dan kilat.
claim.en: He was feared for his power over hail, thunder, and lightning.

claims_provenance.quote: He was feared—albeit not as a malicious figure—for his power over hail, thunder, lightning, and rain.

claim.id: Ia diasosiasikan dengan gua, mata air, dan puncak gunung tinggi.
claim.en: He is also associated with caves, springs, and mountains.

claims_provenance.quote: He is also associated with caves, springs, and mountains, most specifically the sacred mountain where he was believed to reside.

claim.id: Tláloc adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dan paling menakutkan dalam jajaran dewa Aztec, dianggap dewa hujan, air, petir, dan pertanian.
claim.en: Tláloc is one of the most important and formidable gods of the Aztec pantheon, considered the god of rain, water, lightning and agriculture.

claims_provenance.quote: is one of the most important and formidable gods in the Aztec pantheon. He was considered the god of rain, water, lightning and agriculture.

claim.id: Tlaloc dipandang sebagai dewa yang murah hati karena memberi hujan penghidupan, tetapi juga sebagai dewa yang tak kenal ampun dan merusak ketika mengirim badai dan kekeringan.
claim.en: Tlaloc was seen both as a benevolent god providing life-giving rain and as an unforgiving, destructive deity when he sent storms and drought.

claims_provenance.quote: Tlaloc was seen as both a benevolent god providing life-giving rain but also as an unforgiving and destructive deity when he sent storms and drought.

claim.id: Nama Tláloc berasal dari kata Nahuatl tlali yang berarti 'bumi' dan oc yang berarti 'sesuatu di permukaan'.
claim.en: The name Tláloc derives from the Nahuatl words tlali, meaning 'earth', and oc, meaning 'something on the surface'.

claims_provenance.quote: The name Tláloc derives from the Nahuatl words tlali meaning 'earth' and oc meaning 'something on the surface'.

claim.id: Dari kendi di arah timur, Tláloc mengirim hujan yang penting bagi kehidupan, sedangkan dari kendi-kendi lain ia menurunkan kekeringan, penyakit, dan embun beku yang mematikan bagi manusia dan tanaman.
claim.en: From the jar of the East Tláloc gave out the rains essential for life, whereas from the other jars he dispensed drought, disease and frost, deadly for mankind and crops.

claims_provenance.quote: From the jar of the East Tláloc gave out the rains so essential for life whilst from the other jars the god dispensed the terrible scourges of drought, disease and frost so deadly for mankind and crops.

claim.id: Hujan juga dipercaya turun ketika para Tláloc memukul kendi air di dalam gunung dengan tongkat, dan suara guntur dipercaya sebagai bunyi pecahnya kendi-kendi itu.
claim.en: Rain was also thought to come when the Tlálocs used sticks to smash the water jars inside mountains, and the sound of thunder was believed to be the noise of these jars being smashed.

claims_provenance.quote: Alternatively, rain was thought to come when the Tlálocs used sticks to smash the water jars which were inside mountains. Indeed, the sound of thunder was believed to be the noise made when these water jars were smashed.

claim.id: Tláloc juga dianggap penguasa para Tlaloque, sekelompok dewa hujan, cuaca, dan gunung yang beragam.
claim.en: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque, a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods.

claims_provenance.quote: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque - a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods

claim.id: Di ibu kota Aztec, Tenochtitlán, dua kuil kembar didirikan di piramida Templo Mayor: satu untuk Huitzilopochtli (musim kemarau) dan satu untuk Tláloc, yang diberi kedudukan setara.
claim.en: At the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, two twin temples were set up on the Templo Mayor pyramid, one for Huitzilopochtli (the dry season) and one for Tláloc, who was given equal status.

claims_provenance.quote: At the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán two twin temples were set up on the Templo Mayor pyramid, one dedicated to the great god Huitzilopochtli (representing the dry season) and the other to Tláloc who was given equal status.

claim.id: Untuk menenangkan dewa ini dipersembahkan korban, termasuk anak-anak, yang tangisnya dianggap pertanda baik dan dikaitkan dengan tetes hujan dari Tláloc sendiri.
claim.en: To appease the god, sacrificial victims were offered, including children, whose tears were seen as a favourable sign and linked to drops of rain from Tláloc himself.

claims_provenance.quote: More sinister offerings to appease the god and win his favour were sacrificial victims, including children, whose tears were seen as a favourable sign and linked to drops of rain from Tláloc himself.

claim.id: Tláloc dipercaya menguasai surga Tlalocán, tempat korban banjir, badai, dan penyakit seperti lepra diterima setelah mati.
claim.en: Tláloc was believed to rule the other-worldly paradise of Tlalocán, where victims of floods, storms and diseases such as leprosy were received after death.

claims_provenance.quote: Tláloc was also believed to rule the other-worldly paradise of Tlalocán where victims of floods, storms and diseases such as leprosy were received after death.

claim.id: Pada masa Pascaklasik di Meksiko, Tláloc dipercaya tinggal di gua-gua yang lembap dan penuh harta indah.
claim.en: In later Postclassical Mexico, Tláloc was believed to live in caves that were damp and filled with magnificent treasures.

claims_provenance.quote: In later Postclassical Mexico Tláloc was believed to live in caves which were suitably damp for a rain god but also filled with magnificent treasures.

claim.id: Penggambaran tertua Tláloc dalam seni berasal dari vas abad ke-1 SM di Tlapacoya, tempat sang dewa memegang petir.
claim.en: The earliest representations of Tláloc in art belong to 1st-century BCE vases from Tlapacoya, where the god wields a lightning bolt.

claims_provenance.quote: The earliest representations of Tláloc in art belong to 1st century BCE vases from Tlapacoya where the god wields a lightning bolt.

claim.id: Tláloc lazim digambarkan bersama ular; ia paling sering bermata bulat besar seperti kacamata renang dan bertaring besar seperti jaguar.
claim.en: Tláloc is commonly depicted in the company of snakes, most often with goggled eyes and large fangs like a jaguar.

short_description.id: Tláloc adalah dewa hujan dalam agama Aztec, juga dewa kesuburan tanah dan air, yang dipuja sebagai pemberi kehidupan sekaligus ditakuti karena kuasanya atas hujan es, guntur, dan kilat.
short_description.en: Tláloc is the god of rain in Aztec religion, also a deity of earthly fertility and water, worshipped as a giver of life and feared for his power over hail, thunder and lightning.

long_description.id: Tláloc adalah dewa hujan dalam agama Aztec dan juga dewa kesuburan tanah serta air. Ia dipuja sebagai pemberi kehidupan dan rezeki, dan banyak ritual serta korban dipersembahkan atas namanya. Ia ditakuti karena kuasanya atas hujan es, guntur, kilat, dan hujan, meskipun bukan sosok yang jahat.
long_description.en: Tláloc is the god of rain in Aztec religion and also a deity of earthly fertility and water. He was worshipped as a giver of life and sustenance, and many rituals and sacrifices were held in his name. He was feared for his power over hail, thunder, lightning and rain, although not as a malicious figure.

long_description.id: Sumber lain menggambarkannya sebagai dewa yang berwajah ganda: murah hati ketika memberi hujan, tetapi tak kenal ampun ketika mengirim badai dan kekeringan. Dalam gambaran tentang kendi air, ia menurunkan hujan dari kendi di timur, sedangkan dari kendi lain ia menurunkan kekeringan, penyakit, dan embun beku. Hujan juga dipercaya turun ketika para Tláloc memukul pecah kendi di dalam gunung, dan guntur dianggap bunyi pecahnya kendi itu.
long_description.en: Another source describes him as two-sided: benevolent when giving rain but unforgiving when sending storms and drought. In the imagery of the water jars, he gave out rain from the jar of the East and drought, disease and frost from the other jars. Rain was also thought to come when the Tlálocs smashed the jars inside mountains, and thunder was taken to be the noise of the jars breaking.

long_description.id: Tláloc dikaitkan dengan gua, mata air, dan gunung, terutama gunung suci tempat ia dipercaya bersemayam. Ia juga dianggap penguasa para Tlaloque dan surga Tlalocán, tempat korban banjir, badai, dan penyakit diterima setelah mati. Untuk menenangkannya dipersembahkan korban, termasuk anak-anak yang tangisnya dianggap pertanda baik. Di Tenochtitlán, ia memiliki kuil kembar di Templo Mayor yang kedudukannya setara dengan kuil Huitzilopochtli.
long_description.en: Caves, springs and mountains are linked with Tláloc, above all the sacred mountain believed to be his home. He was also considered ruler of the Tlaloque and of the paradise of Tlalocán, the destination after death of those claimed by floods, storms and disease. To appease him, offerings were made, including child victims whose tears were read as a good sign. At Tenochtitlán he had a twin temple on the Templo Mayor, equal in status to that of Huitzilopochtli.

long_description.id: Dalam seni, Tláloc lazim digambarkan bersama ular, dengan mata bulat besar dan taring besar; sumber lain menyebut taring dan mata bercincin sebagai penandanya. Penggambaran tertuanya berasal dari vas abad ke-1 SM, dan di beberapa budaya Mesoamerika ia muncul dengan nama lain seperti Cocijo bagi Zapotec.
long_description.en: In art, Tláloc is commonly depicted with snakes, goggled eyes and large fangs; another source names fangs and ringed eyes as his identifiers. His earliest depictions are on 1st-century BCE vases, and in several Mesoamerican cultures he appears under other names, such as Cocijo for the Zapotec.

cultural_context.id: Menurut salah satu sumber, Tlaloc penting bagi bangsa Aztec karena hujan yang dikuasainya sangat dibutuhkan untuk pertanian.
cultural_context.en: One source explains that Tlaloc mattered to the Aztecs because the rains he governed were vital for farming.

statement.id: Hujan juga dipercaya turun ketika para Tláloc memukul kendi air di dalam gunung dengan tongkat, dan suara guntur dipercaya sebagai bunyi pecahnya kendi-kendi itu.
statement.en: Rain was also thought to come when the Tlálocs used sticks to smash the water jars inside mountains, and the sound of thunder was believed to be the noise of these jars being smashed.

claims.quote: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque - a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods

statement.id: Tláloc juga dianggap penguasa para Tlaloque, sekelompok dewa hujan, cuaca, dan gunung yang beragam.
statement.en: Tláloc was also considered the ruler of the Tlaloque, a motley group of rain, weather and mountain gods.

claims.quote: At the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlán two twin temples were set up on the Templo Mayor pyramid, one dedicated to the great god Huitzilopochtli (representing the dry season) and the other to Tláloc who was given equal status.

statement.id: Di ibu kota Aztec, Tenochtitlán, dua kuil kembar didirikan di piramida Templo Mayor: satu untuk Huitzilopochtli (musim kemarau) dan satu untuk Tláloc, yang diberi kedudukan setara.
statement.en: At the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, two twin temples were set up on the Templo Mayor pyramid, one for Huitzilopochtli (the dry season) and one for Tláloc, who was given equal status.

claims.quote: More sinister offerings to appease the god and win his favour were sacrificial victims, including children, whose tears were seen as a favourable sign and linked to drops of rain from Tláloc himself.

statement.id: Untuk menenangkan dewa ini dipersembahkan korban, termasuk anak-anak, yang tangisnya dianggap pertanda baik dan dikaitkan dengan tetes hujan dari Tláloc sendiri.
statement.en: To appease the god, sacrificial victims were offered, including children, whose tears were seen as a favourable sign and linked to drops of rain from Tláloc himself.

claims.quote: Tláloc was also believed to rule the other-worldly paradise of Tlalocán where victims of floods, storms and diseases such as leprosy were received after death.

statement.id: Tláloc dipercaya menguasai surga Tlalocán, tempat korban banjir, badai, dan penyakit seperti lepra diterima setelah mati.
statement.en: Tláloc was believed to rule the other-worldly paradise of Tlalocán, where victims of floods, storms and diseases such as leprosy were received after death.

claims.quote: In later Postclassical Mexico Tláloc was believed to live in caves which were suitably damp for a rain god but also filled with magnificent treasures.

statement.id: Pada masa Pascaklasik di Meksiko, Tláloc dipercaya tinggal di gua-gua yang lembap dan penuh harta indah.
statement.en: In later Postclassical Mexico, Tláloc was believed to live in caves that were damp and filled with magnificent treasures.

claims.quote: The earliest representations of Tláloc in art belong to 1st century BCE vases from Tlapacoya where the god wields a lightning bolt.

statement.id: Penggambaran tertua Tláloc dalam seni berasal dari vas abad ke-1 SM di Tlapacoya, tempat sang dewa memegang petir.
statement.en: The earliest representations of Tláloc in art belong to 1st-century BCE vases from Tlapacoya, where the god wields a lightning bolt.

claims.quote: Tláloc is commonly depicted in the company of snakes. He most often has goggled eyes and large fangs like a jaguar

statement.id: Tláloc lazim digambarkan bersama ular; ia paling sering bermata bulat besar seperti kacamata renang dan bertaring besar seperti jaguar.
statement.en: Tláloc is commonly depicted in the company of snakes, most often with goggled eyes and large fangs like a jaguar.

claims.quote: In the various Mesoamerican cultures Tláloc appears as Dzahui for the Mixtec, Tajίn for the Totonac, Chupithripeme for the Tarascan and Cocijo for the Zapotec.

statement.id: Dalam berbagai budaya Mesoamerika, Tláloc muncul sebagai Dzahui bagi suku Mixtec, Tajín bagi Totonac, Chupithripeme bagi Tarasca, dan Cocijo bagi Zapotec.
statement.en: In the various Mesoamerican cultures Tláloc appears as Dzahui for the Mixtec, Tajín for the Totonac, Chupithripeme for the Tarascan and Cocijo for the Zapotec.

claims.quote: Tlaloc was important to the Aztecs because he was the god of vital rains needed for agriculture.

statement.id: Tlaloc penting bagi bangsa Aztec karena ia dewa hujan vital yang dibutuhkan untuk pertanian.
statement.en: Tlaloc was important to the Aztecs because he was the god of vital rains needed for agriculture.

claims.quote: Tláloc's two main identifiers are fangs, along with ringed eyes.

statement.id: Dua penanda utama Tláloc adalah taring dan mata bercincin.
statement.en: Tláloc's two main identifiers are fangs and ringed eyes.

claims.quote: In the Aztec Creation myth Tláloc was ruler of the 3rd Sun, he was linked to Mázatl (Deer) the 7th day

statement.id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Aztec, Tláloc adalah penguasa Matahari ke-3 dan dikaitkan dengan Mázatl (Rusa), hari ketujuh.
statement.en: In the Aztec creation myth, Tláloc was ruler of the 3rd Sun and was linked to Mázatl (Deer), the 7th day.

claims.quote: Born during the Creation when Quetzalcoatl and Huitzilpochtli (or in some versions Tezcatlipoca) dismembered the reptilian monster Cipactli

statement.id: Tláloc lahir pada masa penciptaan, ketika Quetzalcoatl dan Huitzilpochtli (atau dalam beberapa versi Tezcatlipoca) mencabik-cabik monster reptil Cipactli.
statement.en: Tláloc was born during the Creation, when Quetzalcoatl and Huitzilpochtli (or in some versions Tezcatlipoca) dismembered the reptilian monster Cipactli.

claims.quote: along with his sister Chalchiúhtlicue (or in some versions his wife or mother), herself a goddess of rivers, oceans and floods.

statement.id: Chalchiúhtlicue, dewi sungai, samudra, dan banjir, disebut sebagai saudari Tláloc atau, dalam beberapa versi, istri atau ibunya.
statement.en: Chalchiúhtlicue, a goddess of rivers, oceans and floods, is called the sister of Tláloc or, in some versions, his wife or mother.

topic.en: Who dismembered Cipactli at Tláloc's birth

short_description.id: Vulcan adalah dewa api dan penempaan Romawi, pelindung pandai besi yang dipadankan dengan Hephaestus Yunani.
short_description.en: Vulcan is the Roman god of fire and forge, patron of smiths and counterpart of Greek Hephaestus.

long_description.id:
Vulcan atau Volcanus adalah dewa api dan penempaan Romawi, putra Jupiter dan Juno serta pelindung pandai besi dan perajin. Ia dipadankan dengan Hephaestus Yunani, dan sebagai dewa tempa serta api yang menghancurkan, termasuk gunung berapi, ia mungkin termasuk dewa yang paling ditakuti. Sebuah catatan penerjemah mencatat bahwa ada yang menyebutnya putra Juno saja.

Festival Vulcanalia dirayakan pada 23 Agustus, dan salah satu kuilnya berdiri di Campus Martius di luar Roma; karena takut api, sebagian besar kuilnya berada di luar kota.

Dalam kisah Romawi, Jupiter melemparkan Vulcan dari surga, dan jatuhnya membuatnya pincang dan cacat; ia lalu mendirikan bengkel besar di Gunung Aetna bersama para Cyclopes. Menurut versi Yunani, justru Hera yang melemparkan Hephaestus yang baru lahir. Ia dinikahkan dengan Venus, yang kemudian meninggalkannya bagi Mars, dan keburukan rupanya disebut menghalangi kebahagiaannya dalam pernikahan.

Vulcan membuat takhta emas berperangkap bagi Juno dan melepaskannya setelah Bacchus membujuknya dengan anggur, lalu membangun istana bagi para dewa. Ia membuka kepala Jupiter dengan kapak sehingga Minerva lahir, dan menempa senjata untuk Aeneas atas permintaan Venus, lalu kembali ke bengkel tempat para Cyclopes mengerjakan petir Jupiter. Ia juga membuat jaring perunggu untuk menjebak Venus dan Mars. Seni Renaisans sering menampilkannya sebagai pandai besi pincang.
long_description.en:
Vulcan, or Volcanus, is the Roman god of fire and forge, son of Jupiter and Juno and patron of blacksmiths and artisans. He was identified with Greek Hephaestus, and as god of the forge and of devastating fire, including volcanoes, he was probably among the most dreaded of the gods. A translator's note records that some called him the son of Juno alone.

Vulcanalia was celebrated on 23 August, and one of his temples stood on the Campus Martius outside Rome; for fear of fire, most of his temples were located outside a city.

In the Roman account Jupiter threw Vulcan out of heaven, and the fall left him lame and deformed; he then established a great forge on Mount Aetna with the Cyclopes. In the Greek variation it was Hera who hurled the newborn Hephaestus down. He was married to Venus, who later left him for Mars, and his ugliness is said to have prevented him from finding happiness in marriage.

Vulcan made a trapped golden throne for Juno and freed her after Bacchus appealed to him with wine, then built palaces for the gods. He opened Jupiter's head with an axe so that Minerva sprang forth, and forged arms for Aeneas at Venus's request, then returned to his forge where the Cyclopes worked on Jupiter's thunderbolts. He also made a bronze net to trap Venus and Mars. Renaissance art often shows him as a lame blacksmith.

famous_for.id: Vulcan dikenal karena menempa karya agung bagi para dewa dan pahlawan, termasuk senjata Aeneas.
famous_for.en: Vulcan is known for forging masterworks for gods and heroes, including arms for Aeneas.

did_you_know.id: Vulcan tidak memiliki planet yang dinamai dengannya, hanya proses pengerasan karet: vulkanisasi.
did_you_know.en: No planet bears the name of Vulcan; the only thing named after him is vulcanization, the process of hardening rubber.

cultural_context.id: Karena takut api dan demi keselamatan, sebagian besar kuil Vulcan dibangun di luar kota, dan sebagai pelindung mereka yang bekerja dengan logam cair, ia tentu bermakna khusus bagi perajin perunggu.
cultural_context.en: For fear of fire and for safety, most of Vulcan's temples were located outside a city, and as patron of those who worked with molten metal he must have had a special meaning for the bronze artist.

description.id: Para Cyclopes di bengkel Vulcan mengerjakan petir Jupiter dan kereta Mars, dan Vulcan diminta membuat senjata dan baju zirah untuk Aeneas. Para penyair juga menyebut seekor anjing buatan Vulcan yang ia persembahkan kepada Jupiter, dan sebuah kereta emas disebut hadiah darinya.
description.en: The Cyclopes at Vulcan's forge worked on Jupiter's thunderbolts and Mars' chariot, and Vulcan was asked to make weapons and armor for Aeneas. The poets also say a dog was made by Vulcan and presented to Jupiter, and a golden chariot is called his gift.

description.en: Vulcan made a trapped golden throne for Juno and a very thin bronze net to catch Venus and Mars.

summary.en: At Jupiter's appeal Vulcan opened his head with an axe, and Minerva sprang forth fully grown and clad in armor.

summary.en: Venus asked her husband Vulcan to make weapons and armor for Aeneas; Vulcan went back to the forge, where the Cyclopes were busy with Jupiter's thunderbolts and Mars' chariot, and Aeneas' shield portrayed future events of Roman history.

short_description.id: Vulcan adalah dewa api dan penempaan Romawi, pelindung pandai besi yang dipadankan dengan Hephaestus Yunani.
short_description.en: Vulcan is the Roman god of fire and forge, patron of smiths and counterpart of Greek Hephaestus.

long_description.id: Vulcan atau Volcanus adalah dewa api dan penempaan Romawi, putra Jupiter dan Juno serta pelindung pandai besi dan perajin. Ia dipadankan dengan Hephaestus Yunani, dan sebagai dewa tempa serta api yang menghancurkan, termasuk gunung berapi, ia mungkin termasuk dewa yang paling ditakuti. Sebuah catatan penerjemah mencatat bahwa ada yang menyebutnya putra Juno saja.
long_description.en: Vulcan, or Volcanus, is the Roman god of fire and forge, son of Jupiter and Juno and patron of blacksmiths and artisans. He was identified with Greek Hephaestus, and as god of the forge and of devastating fire, including volcanoes, he was probably among the most dreaded of the gods. A translator's note records that some called him the son of Juno alone.

long_description.id: Festival Vulcanalia dirayakan pada 23 Agustus, dan salah satu kuilnya berdiri di Campus Martius di luar Roma; karena takut api, sebagian besar kuilnya berada di luar kota.
long_description.en: Vulcanalia was celebrated on 23 August, and one of his temples stood on the Campus Martius outside Rome; for fear of fire, most of his temples were located outside a city.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Romawi, Jupiter melemparkan Vulcan dari surga, dan jatuhnya membuatnya pincang dan cacat; ia lalu mendirikan bengkel besar di Gunung Aetna bersama para Cyclopes. Menurut versi Yunani, justru Hera yang melemparkan Hephaestus yang baru lahir. Ia dinikahkan dengan Venus, yang kemudian meninggalkannya bagi Mars, dan keburukan rupanya disebut menghalangi kebahagiaannya dalam pernikahan.
long_description.en: In the Roman account Jupiter threw Vulcan out of heaven, and the fall left him lame and deformed; he then established a great forge on Mount Aetna with the Cyclopes. In the Greek variation it was Hera who hurled the newborn Hephaestus down. He was married to Venus, who later left him for Mars, and his ugliness is said to have prevented him from finding happiness in marriage.

long_description.id: Vulcan membuat takhta emas berperangkap bagi Juno dan melepaskannya setelah Bacchus membujuknya dengan anggur, lalu membangun istana bagi para dewa. Ia membuka kepala Jupiter dengan kapak sehingga Minerva lahir, dan menempa senjata untuk Aeneas atas permintaan Venus, lalu kembali ke bengkel tempat para Cyclopes mengerjakan petir Jupiter. Ia juga membuat jaring perunggu untuk menjebak Venus dan Mars. Seni Renaisans sering menampilkannya sebagai pandai besi pincang.
long_description.en: Vulcan made a trapped golden throne for Juno and freed her after Bacchus appealed to him with wine, then built palaces for the gods. He opened Jupiter's head with an axe so that Minerva sprang forth, and forged arms for Aeneas at Venus's request, then returned to his forge where the Cyclopes worked on Jupiter's thunderbolts. He also made a bronze net to trap Venus and Mars. Renaissance art often shows him as a lame blacksmith.

cultural_context.id: Karena takut api dan demi keselamatan, sebagian besar kuil Vulcan dibangun di luar kota, dan sebagai pelindung mereka yang bekerja dengan logam cair, ia tentu bermakna khusus bagi perajin perunggu.
cultural_context.en: For fear of fire and for safety, most of Vulcan's temples were located outside a city, and as patron of those who worked with molten metal he must have had a special meaning for the bronze artist.

description.en: The Cyclopes at Vulcan's forge worked on Jupiter's thunderbolts and Mars' chariot, and Vulcan was asked to make weapons and armor for Aeneas. The poets also say a dog was made by Vulcan and presented to Jupiter, and a golden chariot is called his gift.

short_description.id: Ardhanarisvara adalah bentuk Shiva yang menyatu dengan Parvati.
short_description.en: Ardhanarishvara is a form of Shiva united with Parvati.

long_description.id:
Ardhanarisvara adalah bentuk Shiva yang menyatu dengan Parvati. Wujudnya dibagi sama rata menjadi setengah laki-laki dan setengah perempuan.

Ia melambangkan penyatuan energi maskulin dan feminin atau Purusha dan Prakriti. Bagian kanan biasanya Shiva laki-laki. Penggambaran awal berasal dari periode Kushan dan berkembang pada era Gupta. Nama Ardhanarisvara berarti Tuhan yang setengah perempuan. Deskripsi Cleveland tentang Ardhanarisvara memperlihatkan sisi kiri perempuan dan sisi kanan laki-laki.
long_description.en:
Ardhanarishvara is a form of Shiva united with Parvati. The form is divided equally into half male and half female.

It symbolizes the union of masculine and feminine energies or Purusha and Prakriti. The right half is usually male Shiva. Early depictions date to the Kushan period and develop in the Gupta era. The name Ardhanarishvara means the Lord who is half woman. Cleveland's description of Ardhanarishvara shows the left side female and the right side male.

short_description.id: Meretseger adalah dewi kobra Thebes yang melindungi nekropolis dan Lembah Para Raja.
short_description.en: Meretseger is a Theban cobra goddess protecting the necropolis and Valley of the Kings.

long_description.id:
Meretseger adalah dewi kobra Thebes yang melindungi nekropolis dan Lembah Para Raja. Namanya berarti Yang Mencintai Keheningan, dengan tafsir lain berkaitan dengan Osiris.

Ia menjadi pelindung perajin dan pekerja Deir el-Medina. Kuil batu kecil didedikasikan kepada Meretseger. Ia dipercaya menghukum pelanggaran dengan gigitan beracun tetapi menyembuhkan orang yang bertobat. Ensiklopedia pendamping menegaskan perlindungannya atas Lembah Para Raja.
long_description.en:
Meretseger is a Theban cobra goddess protecting the necropolis and Valley of the Kings. Her name means She Who Loves Silence, with another interpretation connected with Osiris.

She is patron of Deir el-Medina’s artisans and workers. Small rock temples are dedicated to Meretseger. She is believed to punish transgressions with a poisonous bite but heal the repentant. The accompanying encyclopedia confirms her protection of the Valley of the Kings.

short_description.id: Rhea adalah Titan perempuan dan dewi ibu Yunani, putri Gaia dan Uranus, yang menyelamatkan Zeus bayi dari Cronus.
short_description.en: Rhea is a Greek female Titan and mother goddess, daughter of Gaia and Uranus, who saved infant Zeus from Cronus.

long_description.id:
Rhea adalah Titan perempuan dan dewi ibu dalam mitologi Yunani, putri Gaia dan Uranus. Ia ibu Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, serta Zeus. Sumber klasik menyebutnya dewi bumi, dan namanya diterjemahkan sebagai "aliran, kemudahan".

Dalam kisah utamanya, Cronos menelan anak-anaknya; menurut sebuah sumber klasik hal itu karena Bumi dan Langit meramalkan ia akan digulingkan putranya sendiri. Untuk menyelamatkan Zeus, Rhea pergi ke Kreta, melahirkan di sebuah gua di Dicte, menitipkan bayi itu kepada Kouretes serta dua Nymph, dan menyerahkan batu berbalut kain kepada Cronos. Kouretes membenturkan perisai untuk menyembunyikan tangis Zeus. Orang-orang kuno tidak sepakat apakah Zeus dibesarkan di Gunung Ida atau Gunung Dicte.

Rhea dikaitkan dengan Cybele, dewi Frigia, walau keduanya semula tokoh berbeda; Cybele juga tercantum di antara nama-namanya. Ops adalah padanan Rhea di Romawi. Kreta disebut pusat pemujaannya yang paling awal, dan di Olympia ada kuil Metroön untuknya. Di Frigia para Corybantes menjadi imam-imamnya, dan dalam seni ia umumnya digambarkan duduk di singgasana yang diapit singa.

Sumber-sumber kuno juga mencatat versi yang berbeda tentang keluarganya, dan sebagian kisah menyebut Rhea bersama Cronos menggantikan Ophion dan Eurynome dalam kekuasaan atas dunia. Pohon ek dan singa dikeramatkan baginya. Homer hanya menyinggung Rhea sekilas, sehingga bagian dalam Hesiod dianggap legenda Yunani tertua tentang Rhea.
long_description.en:
Rhea is a female Titan and mother goddess of Greek myth, daughter of Gaia and Uranus. She is mother of Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, and Zeus. Classical sources describe her as a goddess of the earth, and her name is translated as "flow, ease".

In her best-known story Cronos swallows his children; in one classical source this is because Earth and Sky foretold that he would be dethroned by his own son. To save Zeus, Rhea goes to Crete, gives birth in a cave of Dicte, entrusts the infant to the Kouretes and two nymphs, and gives Cronos a swaddled stone. The Kouretes clash shields to hide Zeus's cries. The ancients were not agreed whether Zeus was reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.

Rhea became associated with Cybele, a Phrygian goddess, although the two began as separate figures; Cybele is also listed among her names. Ops is her Roman counterpart. Crete is called the earliest seat of her worship, and at Olympia there was a Metroön built for her. In Phrygia the Corybantes were her priests, and in art she is generally shown seated on a throne flanked by lions.

Ancient sources also record different versions of her family, and some accounts say Rhea and Cronos succeeded Ophion and Eurynome in sovereignty over the world. The oak and the lion were sacred to her. Homer makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, so the passage of Hesiod is regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about her.

short_description.id: Rhea adalah Titan perempuan dan dewi ibu Yunani, putri Gaia dan Uranus, yang menyelamatkan Zeus bayi dari Cronus.
short_description.en: Rhea is a Greek female Titan and mother goddess, daughter of Gaia and Uranus, who saved infant Zeus from Cronus.

long_description.id: Rhea adalah Titan perempuan dan dewi ibu dalam mitologi Yunani, putri Gaia dan Uranus. Ia ibu Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, serta Zeus. Sumber klasik menyebutnya dewi bumi, dan namanya diterjemahkan sebagai "aliran, kemudahan".
long_description.en: Rhea is a female Titan and mother goddess of Greek myth, daughter of Gaia and Uranus. She is mother of Hestia, Demeter, Hera, Hades, Poseidon, and Zeus. Classical sources describe her as a goddess of the earth, and her name is translated as "flow, ease".

long_description.id: Dalam kisah utamanya, Cronos menelan anak-anaknya; menurut sebuah sumber klasik hal itu karena Bumi dan Langit meramalkan ia akan digulingkan putranya sendiri. Untuk menyelamatkan Zeus, Rhea pergi ke Kreta, melahirkan di sebuah gua di Dicte, menitipkan bayi itu kepada Kouretes serta dua Nymph, dan menyerahkan batu berbalut kain kepada Cronos. Kouretes membenturkan perisai untuk menyembunyikan tangis Zeus. Orang-orang kuno tidak sepakat apakah Zeus dibesarkan di Gunung Ida atau Gunung Dicte.
long_description.en: In her best-known story Cronos swallows his children; in one classical source this is because Earth and Sky foretold that he would be dethroned by his own son. To save Zeus, Rhea goes to Crete, gives birth in a cave of Dicte, entrusts the infant to the Kouretes and two nymphs, and gives Cronos a swaddled stone. The Kouretes clash shields to hide Zeus's cries. The ancients were not agreed whether Zeus was reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.

long_description.id: Rhea dikaitkan dengan Cybele, dewi Frigia, walau keduanya semula tokoh berbeda; Cybele juga tercantum di antara nama-namanya. Ops adalah padanan Rhea di Romawi. Kreta disebut pusat pemujaannya yang paling awal, dan di Olympia ada kuil Metroön untuknya. Di Frigia para Corybantes menjadi imam-imamnya, dan dalam seni ia umumnya digambarkan duduk di singgasana yang diapit singa.
long_description.en: Rhea became associated with Cybele, a Phrygian goddess, although the two began as separate figures; Cybele is also listed among her names. Ops is her Roman counterpart. Crete is called the earliest seat of her worship, and at Olympia there was a Metroön built for her. In Phrygia the Corybantes were her priests, and in art she is generally shown seated on a throne flanked by lions.

long_description.id: Sumber-sumber kuno juga mencatat versi yang berbeda tentang keluarganya, dan sebagian kisah menyebut Rhea bersama Cronos menggantikan Ophion dan Eurynome dalam kekuasaan atas dunia. Pohon ek dan singa dikeramatkan baginya. Homer hanya menyinggung Rhea sekilas, sehingga bagian dalam Hesiod dianggap legenda Yunani tertua tentang Rhea.
long_description.en: Ancient sources also record different versions of her family, and some accounts say Rhea and Cronos succeeded Ophion and Eurynome in sovereignty over the world. The oak and the lion were sacred to her. Homer makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, so the passage of Hesiod is regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about her.

cultural_context.id: Rhea dan Cybele pada mulanya dua tokoh terpisah, tetapi pada dasarnya menjadi dua perwujudan dewi yang sama; pemujaan Rhea tercermin pada kuil Metroön di Olympia yang dibangun untuk menghormatinya sebagai ibu para dewa.
cultural_context.en: Rhea and Cybele began as two separate figures but essentially became two manifestations of the same deity; the cult of Rhea is reflected in the Metroön at Olympia, built to honor her as mother of the gods.

statement.id: Menurut sebagian kisah, Cronos dan Rhea didahului dalam kekuasaan atas dunia oleh Ophion dan Eurynome; Ophion dikalahkan Cronos, dan Rhea melempar Eurynome ke Tartarus.
statement.en: According to some accounts Cronos and Rhea were preceded in sovereignty over the world by Ophion and Eurynome; Ophion was overpowered by Cronos, and Rhea cast Eurynome into Tartarus.

claims.quote: she was seldom represented in a standing posture, but generally seated on a throne, adorned with the mural crown, from which a veil hangs down. Lions usually appear crouching on the right and left of her throne

statement.id: Rhea jarang digambarkan berdiri, umumnya duduk di singgasana dengan mahkota tembok dan cadar menjuntai; singa biasanya berjongkok di kanan dan kiri singgasananya.
statement.en: She was seldom represented standing, but generally seated on a throne, wearing the mural crown with a veil hanging down; lions usually appear crouching to the right and left of her throne.

claims.quote: Rhea Translation Flow, Ease (rhea)

statement.id: Nama Rhea diterjemahkan sebagai "aliran, kemudahan".
statement.en: The name Rhea is translated as "flow, ease".

claims.quote: [1.2] AITHER (or OURANOS) & GAIA (Hyginus Pref)

statement.id: Menurut Hyginus (Pref), orang tua Rhea adalah Aither (atau Ouranos) dan Gaia.
statement.en: In Hyginus (Preface), Rhea's parents are Aither (or Ouranos) and Gaia.

claims.quote: [1.2] ZEUS, POSEIDON, HAIDES (by Kronos) (Homer Iliad 15.187)

statement.id: Menurut Homer, Iliad 15.187, anak Rhea dari Kronos adalah Zeus, Poseidon, dan Hades.
statement.en: In Homer, Iliad 15.187, Rhea's children by Kronos are Zeus, Poseidon, and Haides.

claims.quote: [1.3] ZEUS, DEMETER, HAIDES (Homeric Hymn 2.69)

statement.id: Menurut Homeric Hymn 2.69, anak Rhea adalah Zeus, Demeter, dan Hades.
statement.en: In Homeric Hymn 2.69, Rhea's children are Zeus, Demeter, and Haides.

claims.quote: wedded his sister Rhea; and since both Earth and Sky foretold him that he would be dethroned by his own son, he used to swallow his offspring at birth. His firstborn Hestia he swallowed, then Demeter and Hera, and after them Pluto and Poseidon.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah sumber klasik, ia menikahi saudarinya Rhea, dan karena Bumi dan Langit meramalkan ia akan digulingkan putranya sendiri, ia menelan anak-anaknya saat lahir: Hestia, lalu Demeter dan Hera, kemudian Pluto dan Poseidon.
statement.en: In a classical source, he wedded his sister Rhea, and since Earth and Sky foretold he would be dethroned by his own son, he swallowed his offspring at birth: Hestia, then Demeter and Hera, then Pluto and Poseidon.

claims.quote: Rhea repaired to Crete, when she was big with Zeus, and brought him forth in a cave of Dicte.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah sumber klasik, Rhea pergi ke Kreta ketika mengandung Zeus dan melahirkannya di sebuah gua di Dicte.
statement.en: In a classical source, Rhea went to Crete when big with Zeus and brought him forth in a cave of Dicte.

claims.quote: The ancients were not agreed as to whether the infant god had been reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.

statement.id: Orang-orang kuno tidak sepakat apakah dewa bayi itu dibesarkan di Gunung Ida atau Gunung Dicte.
statement.en: The ancients were not agreed whether the infant god had been reared on Mount Ida or Mount Dicte.

claims.quote: Homer (Il. xv. 187) makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, and the passage of Hesiod, which accordingly must be regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about Rhea

statement.id: Homer hanya menyinggung Rhea sekilas, sehingga bagian dalam Hesiod harus dianggap sebagai legenda Yunani tertua tentang Rhea.
statement.en: Homer makes only a passing allusion to Rhea, so the passage of Hesiod must be regarded as the most ancient Greek legend about Rhea.

short_description.id: Hubal adalah dewa Arab pra-Islam yang terutama dipuja Quraisy di Mekah.
short_description.en: Hubal is a pre-Islamic Arabian god particularly worshipped by the Quraysh in Mecca.

long_description.id:
Hubal adalah dewa Arab pra-Islam yang terutama dipuja Quraisy di Mekah. Hubal dipuja melalui arca menyerupai manusia di Ka’bah.

Ramalan dilakukan menggunakan anak panah di depan arca Hubal. Quraisy mengendalikan akses menuju arca Hubal. Ibn al-Kalbi menggambarkan arca Hubal sebagai sosok manusia dengan tangan kanan yang patah dan diganti emas, dan arca itu disebut terbuat dari akik merah.

Britannica 1911 mencatat bahwa Hobal ditempatkan di dalam Bait di atas lubang yang berisi harta suci, dan fungsi utamanya terkait undian suci. Sumber berbeda tentang siapa yang mendirikan arcanya: Ibn Al-Kalbi menyebut Khuzayma ibn Mudrika, sedangkan tradisi lain menyebut Amr ibn Luhayy. Mircea Eliade dan Charles J. Adams menyebutnya dewa hujan dan dewa perang, sementara dugaan Hugo Winckler bahwa ia dewa bulan ditolak sarjana yang lebih baru. Menurut salah satu sumber, Muhammad menghancurkan arcanya saat menaklukkan Mekah pada 630.
long_description.en:
Hubal is a pre-Islamic Arabian god particularly worshipped by the Quraysh in Mecca. Hubal is worshipped through a human-shaped statue in the Kaaba.

Divination uses arrows placed before Hubal's statue. The Quraysh control access to Hubal's statue. Ibn al-Kalbi describes the statue as a human figure whose broken right hand is replaced by gold, and the statue is said to be made of red agate.

The 1911 Britannica notes that Hobal was set up within the Temple over the pit containing the sacred treasures and that his chief function was connected with the sacred lot. Sources differ on who set up his statue: Ibn Al-Kalbi names Khuzayma ibn Mudrika, while another tradition names Amr ibn Luhayy. Mircea Eliade and Charles J. Adams call him a rain god and a warrior god, while Hugo Winckler's guess that he was a lunar deity has been rejected by more recent scholars. According to one source, Muhammad broke his statue when he conquered Mecca in 630.

statement.id: Kitab al-Asnam karya Hisham Ibn Al-Kalbi menggambarkan arca itu berbentuk manusia, dengan tangan kanan yang patah diganti tangan emas.
statement.en: Hisham Ibn Al-Kalbi's Book of Idols describes the image as human-shaped, with the broken right hand replaced by a golden one.

claims.quote: The god's icon was a human figure believed to control acts of divination, which was performed by tossing arrows before the statue.

statement.id: Arca Hubal berupa sosok manusia yang diyakini mengendalikan ramalan, yang dilakukan dengan melemparkan anak panah di hadapan arca.
statement.en: Hubal's icon was a human figure believed to control divination, performed by tossing arrows before the statue.

claims.quote: The name Hubal may be ultimately derivative of the name Baal from the Canaanite pantheon. In particular, the name could derive from the Aramaic hu bel, meaning "he is Baal".

statement.id: Nama Hubal mungkin pada akhirnya berasal dari nama Baal dalam jajaran dewa Kanaan; secara khusus bisa dari bahasa Aram hu bel, "dia adalah Baal".
statement.en: The name Hubal may ultimately derive from the name Baal of the Canaanite pantheon; in particular from Aramaic hu bel, 'he is Baal'.

claims.quote: According to Ibn Al-Kalbi, the image was first set up by Khuzayma ibn Mudrika, but another tradition, recorded by Ibn Ishaq, holds that Amr ibn Luhayy, a leader of the Khuza'a tribe, put an image of Hubal into the Kaaba

statement.id: Menurut Ibn Al-Kalbi, arca itu pertama didirikan oleh Khuzayma ibn Mudrika, tetapi tradisi lain yang dicatat Ibn Ishaq menyebut Amr ibn Luhayy, pemimpin suku Khuza'a, menempatkan arca Hubal di Ka'bah.
statement.en: According to Ibn Al-Kalbi the image was first set up by Khuzayma ibn Mudrika, but another tradition recorded by Ibn Ishaq says Amr ibn Luhayy, a leader of the Khuza'a tribe, put an image of Hubal in the Kaaba.

claims.quote: A tale recorded by Ibn Al-Kalbi has Muhammad's grandfather Abdul Mutallib vowing to sacrifice one of his ten children. He consulted the arrows of Hubal to find out which child he should choose.

statement.id: Sebuah kisah yang dicatat Ibn Al-Kalbi menuturkan kakek Muhammad, Abdul Mutallib, bersumpah mengorbankan salah satu dari sepuluh anaknya dan menanyakan anak panah Hubal untuk memilihnya.
statement.en: A tale recorded by Ibn Al-Kalbi has Muhammad's grandfather Abdul Mutallib vow to sacrifice one of his ten children and consult the arrows of Hubal to choose which.

claims.quote: When Muhammad conquered Mecca in 630, he broke the statue of Hubal, along with the other 360 images at the Kaaba, and dedicated the structure to Allah.

statement.id: Ketika Muhammad menaklukkan Mekah pada 630, ia menghancurkan arca Hubal beserta 360 arca lain di Ka'bah dan mengabdikan bangunan itu kepada Allah.
statement.en: When Muhammad conquered Mecca in 630 he broke the statue of Hubal, with the other 360 images at the Kaaba, and dedicated the structure to Allah.

claims.quote: Mircea Eliade and Charles J. Adams assert that he was "a god of rain and a warrior god. Towards the end of the pre-Islamic era he emerged as an intertribal warrior god worshipped by the Quraysh and the allied tribes of the Kinana and Tihama."

statement.id: Mircea Eliade dan Charles J. Adams menyatakan Hubal adalah dewa hujan dan dewa perang yang menjelang akhir masa pra-Islam menjadi dewa perang antarsuku yang dipuja Quraisy serta suku-suku sekutu Kinana dan Tihama.
statement.en: Mircea Eliade and Charles J. Adams assert he was a god of rain and a warrior god who emerged toward the end of the pre-Islamic era as an intertribal warrior god worshipped by the Quraysh and the allied tribes of the Kinana and Tihama.

claims.quote: Hugo Winckler in the early twentieth century speculated that Hubal was a lunar deity, a view that was repeated by other scholars.

statement.id: Hugo Winckler pada awal abad kedua puluh menduga Hubal adalah dewa bulan, pandangan yang diulang oleh sarjana lain.
statement.en: In the early twentieth century Hugo Winckler speculated that Hubal was a lunar deity, a view repeated by other scholars.

claims.quote: More recent scholars have rejected this view, partly because it is speculation

statement.id: Sarjana yang lebih baru menolak pandangan dewa bulan itu, antara lain karena sifatnya spekulatif.
statement.en: More recent scholars have rejected the lunar-deity view, partly because it is speculation.

claims.quote: The paucity of evidence concerning Hubal makes it difficult to characterise his role or identity in pagan Arabian mythologies.

statement.id: Sedikitnya bukti tentang Hubal menyulitkan penggambaran peran atau identitasnya dalam mitologi Arab pagan.
statement.en: The paucity of evidence about Hubal makes it difficult to characterise his role or identity in pagan Arabian mythologies.

short_description.id: Shesha adalah naga ilahi, raja ular, dan makhluk primordial penciptaan dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Shesha is a divine naga, king of serpents, and primordial creation being in Hinduism.

long_description.id:
Shesha adalah naga ilahi, raja ular, dan makhluk primordial penciptaan dalam Hindu. Shesha juga dikenal sebagai Ananta atau Ananta Shesha.

Vishnu dalam bentuk Narayana lazim digambarkan beristirahat di atas Shesha bersama Lakshmi. Dalam tradisi, ia berinkarnasi sebagai Lakshmana dan Balarama. Ikonografinya dapat berkepala lima, tujuh, atau sepuluh, sementara teks klasik sering menyebut seribu kepala. Mackenzie juga menyebut Balarama sebagai inkarnasi ular dunia Shesha.
long_description.en:
Shesha is a divine naga, king of serpents, and primordial creation being in Hinduism. Shesha is also known as Ananta or Ananta Shesha.

Vishnu as Narayana is commonly depicted resting on Shesha with Lakshmi. In tradition he incarnates as Lakshmana and Balarama. His iconography can have five, seven, or ten hoods, while classical texts often describe a thousand heads. Mackenzie also calls Balarama an incarnation of the world serpent Shesha.

short_description.id: Adad adalah dewa badai Babilonia.
short_description.en: Adad is a Babylonian storm deity.

long_description.id:
Adad adalah dewa badai Babilonia. Bangsa Sumeria menyebutnya Ishkur.

Adad digambarkan bersama naga berkepala singa atau banteng. Adad digambarkan membawa palu atau petir. Shala disebut sebagai pasangan Adad. Uraian keluarga Enlil memasukkan Ishkur atau Adad sebagai dewa cuaca.
long_description.en:
Adad is a Babylonian storm deity. The Sumerians call him Ishkur.

Adad is depicted with a lion-headed dragon or a bull. Adad is depicted carrying a hammer or lightning bolt. Shala is named as Adad’s consort. The account of Enlil’s family includes Ishkur, or Adad, as a weather deity.

short_description.id: Black Tortoise atau Xuanwu adalah lambang rasi Tiongkok berupa kura-kura yang dililit ular.
short_description.en: Black Tortoise, or Xuanwu, is a Chinese constellation symbol showing a turtle intertwined with a snake.

long_description.id:
Black Tortoise atau Black Turtle-Snake (玄武, Xuánwǔ) adalah salah satu dari empat simbol rasi bintang Tiongkok. Biasanya digambarkan sebagai kura-kura yang berlilit dengan seekor ular. Ia mewakili utara sehingga kadang disebut prajurit hitam dari utara, dan mewakili musim dingin karena kura-kura dan ular berhibernasi pada musim dingin. Menurut Xu Shen, aksara wu (武) berarti "kesatria" dalam dialek Jianghuai.

Teks Liji menempatkan Xuanwu di belakang dalam susunan arak-arakan, dengan Naga Biru-Hijau di kiri dan Harimau Putih di kanan. Dalam syair Yuan You (Chu Ci), tokoh yang bepergian memanggil Xuanwu untuk mengikutinya.

Di Tiongkok kuno, kura-kura dan ular dianggap makhluk spiritual yang melambangkan umur panjang. Dalam novel klasik Journey to the West, Xuanwu adalah raja utara dengan dua jenderal, Jenderal Kura-kura dan Jenderal Ular. Di Jepang, xuanwu dilafalkan Genbu; ia dikatakan melindungi sisi utara Kyoto sebagai satu dari empat roh penjaga kota, dan diwakili oleh Kuil Kenkun di puncak Gunung Funaoka.
long_description.en:
The Black Turtle-Snake, or Black Tortoise (玄武, Xuánwǔ), is among the four symbols of the Chinese constellations and is normally drawn as a tortoise or turtle coiled together with a snake. It stands for the north, which is why it is at times named the black warrior of the north, and for winter, since tortoises and snakes hibernate in the cold season. Xu Shen explained the character wu (武) as meaning "knight" in the Jianghuai dialect.

The Liji text puts Xuanwu at the rear of a marching order, with the Azure Dragon on the left and the White Tiger on the right. In the poem Yuan You (Chu Ci), the traveller calls Xuanwu to follow him.

In ancient China the tortoise and the serpent were regarded as spiritual creatures standing for long life. In the classic novel Journey to the West, Xuanwu is a king of the north served by two generals, a Tortoise General and a Snake General. In Japan the name is read Genbu; he is said to guard the north of Kyoto as one of the city's four guardian spirits and is represented by the Kenkun Shrine on top of Mount Funaoka.

description.id: Di Jepang, Genbu diwakili oleh Kuil Kenkun di puncak Gunung Funaoka, Kyoto.
description.en: In Japan, Genbu is represented by the Kenkun Shrine on top of Mount Funaoka in Kyoto.

claims_provenance.quote: The Black Turtle-Snake (Chinese: 玄武; pinyin: Xuánwǔ) is one of the Four Symbols of the Chinese constellations. It is usually depicted as a tortoise or turtle, intertwined with a snake.

claim.id: Penjelasan Xu Shen mengaitkan kata wu dengan kesatria dalam dialek Jianghuai.
claim.en: Xu Shen's explanation links wu to the word for knight in the Jianghuai dialect.

claims_provenance.quote: According to Eastern Han philologist Xu Shen, the character wu (武) meant "knight" (士; shì ) in the Jianghuai dialect.  So the English translation Black ~ Dark ~ Mysterious Warrior is a more faithful translation.

claim.id: Xuanwu dikaitkan dengan arah utara.
claim.en: Xuanwu is associated with the northern direction.

claims_provenance.quote: It represents the north, thus it is sometimes called Black Warrior of the North (北方玄武; Běifāng Xuánwǔ).

claim.id: Kura-kura dan ular yang berhibernasi mendasari hubungannya dengan musim dingin.
claim.en: The winter association draws on the hibernation of turtles and snakes.

claims_provenance.quote: While neither character xuan (玄) or wu (武) literally means turtle, tortoise or snake, tortoises and snakes are known to hibernate during winter, so xuanwu (玄武) as a whole represents the season of winter.

claim.id: Di Jepang, Genbu dipercaya menjaga sisi utara Kyoto.

short_description.id: Black Tortoise atau Xuanwu adalah lambang rasi Tiongkok berupa kura-kura yang dililit ular.
short_description.en: Black Tortoise, or Xuanwu, is a Chinese constellation symbol showing a turtle intertwined with a snake.

long_description.id: Black Tortoise atau Black Turtle-Snake (玄武, Xuánwǔ) adalah salah satu dari empat simbol rasi bintang Tiongkok. Biasanya digambarkan sebagai kura-kura yang berlilit dengan seekor ular. Ia mewakili utara sehingga kadang disebut prajurit hitam dari utara, dan mewakili musim dingin karena kura-kura dan ular berhibernasi pada musim dingin. Menurut Xu Shen, aksara wu (武) berarti "kesatria" dalam dialek Jianghuai.
long_description.en: The Black Turtle-Snake, or Black Tortoise (玄武, Xuánwǔ), is among the four symbols of the Chinese constellations and is normally drawn as a tortoise or turtle coiled together with a snake. It stands for the north, which is why it is at times named the black warrior of the north, and for winter, since tortoises and snakes hibernate in the cold season. Xu Shen explained the character wu (武) as meaning "knight" in the Jianghuai dialect.

long_description.id: Teks Liji menempatkan Xuanwu di belakang dalam susunan arak-arakan, dengan Naga Biru-Hijau di kiri dan Harimau Putih di kanan. Dalam syair Yuan You (Chu Ci), tokoh yang bepergian memanggil Xuanwu untuk mengikutinya.
long_description.en: The Liji text puts Xuanwu at the rear of a marching order, with the Azure Dragon on the left and the White Tiger on the right. In the poem Yuan You (Chu Ci), the traveller calls Xuanwu to follow him.

long_description.id: Di Tiongkok kuno, kura-kura dan ular dianggap makhluk spiritual yang melambangkan umur panjang. Dalam novel klasik Journey to the West, Xuanwu adalah raja utara dengan dua jenderal, Jenderal Kura-kura dan Jenderal Ular. Di Jepang, xuanwu dilafalkan Genbu; ia dikatakan melindungi sisi utara Kyoto sebagai satu dari empat roh penjaga kota, dan diwakili oleh Kuil Kenkun di puncak Gunung Funaoka.
long_description.en: In ancient China the tortoise and the serpent were regarded as spiritual creatures standing for long life. In the classic novel Journey to the West, Xuanwu is a king of the north served by two generals, a Tortoise General and a Snake General. In Japan the name is read Genbu; he is said to guard the north of Kyoto as one of the city's four guardian spirits and is represented by the Kenkun Shrine on top of Mount Funaoka.

short_description.id: Inti adalah dewa matahari Inca kuno yang dimuliakan sebagai pelindung negara Inca. Ia umumnya dianggap dewa yang murah hati, meski dapat murka.
short_description.en: Inti is the ancient Inca sun god, revered as the national patron of the Inca state. He was generally considered benevolent, although he could be angered.

long_description.id:
Inti adalah dewa matahari Inca kuno dan dimuliakan sebagai pelindung negara Inca. Sebagian besar orang menganggapnya dewa matahari, tetapi ia lebih tepat dipandang sebagai gugusan aspek surya, karena bangsa Inca membagi identitasnya menurut tahap-tahap matahari, menjadi tiga subkompleks: ayah, putra, dan saudara. Ia dianggap mahakuasa sekaligus murah hati, namun dapat menunjukkan murkanya lewat gerhana matahari.

Menurut kepercayaan yang paling umum, Inti lahir dari Viracocha; sumber lain menyebut Viracocha menciptakan matahari dari sebuah pulau di Danau Titicaca. Inti juga disebut saudara dan, menurut sumber lain, suami Quilla, dewi bulan. Penguasa Inca menganggap diri keturunan langsungnya dan penguasa Inca dipandang sebagai perwakilan hidupnya, sedangkan Manco Capac dipercaya diajari atau malah putranya.

Kuil Coricancha di Cuzco dipersembahkan kepada Inti, dan ia dipuja terutama pada festival Inti Raymi. Pachacuti sering dikaitkan dengan asal dan perluasan Kultus Matahari Inca. Salah satu persembahan yang paling umum adalah llama putih. Dalam seni, ia jarang digambarkan; bila ada, wujudnya berupa patung emas, cakram matahari, atau topeng emas, dan salah satu patung menampilkannya sebagai anak kecil duduk bernama Punchao.
long_description.en:
Inti is the ancient Inca sun god, held up as patron of the Inca state. Most people regard him as the sun god, yet he is better seen as a cluster of solar aspects, since the Inca split his identity along the stages of the sun into three sub-complexes: father, son and brother. He was thought all-powerful and generous, yet able to show anger through solar eclipses.

The most common belief was that Inti was born of Viracocha, though another source says Viracocha made the sun from an island on Lake Titicaca. Inti is also called the brother of Quilla, goddess of the moon, and by another source her husband. Inca rulers saw themselves as his direct descendants and the Inca ruler was regarded as his living representative, while Manco Capac was believed to have been taught by him or even to be his son.

The Coricancha temple at Cuzco was dedicated to Inti, and he was worshipped above all at the Inti Raymi festival. Pachacuti is often linked with the origin and spread of the Inca Sun Cult. White llamas were among the commonest offerings. In art he was seldom portrayed; when he was, the form was a gold statue, a sun disk or a golden mask, and one statue showed him as a small seated boy called Punchao.

short_description.id: Inti adalah dewa matahari Inca kuno yang dimuliakan sebagai pelindung negara Inca. Ia umumnya dianggap dewa yang murah hati, meski dapat murka.
short_description.en: Inti is the ancient Inca sun god, revered as the national patron of the Inca state. He was generally considered benevolent, although he could be angered.

long_description.id: Inti adalah dewa matahari Inca kuno dan dimuliakan sebagai pelindung negara Inca. Sebagian besar orang menganggapnya dewa matahari, tetapi ia lebih tepat dipandang sebagai gugusan aspek surya, karena bangsa Inca membagi identitasnya menurut tahap-tahap matahari, menjadi tiga subkompleks: ayah, putra, dan saudara. Ia dianggap mahakuasa sekaligus murah hati, namun dapat menunjukkan murkanya lewat gerhana matahari.
long_description.en: Inti is the ancient Inca sun god, held up as patron of the Inca state. Most people regard him as the sun god, yet he is better seen as a cluster of solar aspects, since the Inca split his identity along the stages of the sun into three sub-complexes: father, son and brother. He was thought all-powerful and generous, yet able to show anger through solar eclipses.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan yang paling umum, Inti lahir dari Viracocha; sumber lain menyebut Viracocha menciptakan matahari dari sebuah pulau di Danau Titicaca. Inti juga disebut saudara dan, menurut sumber lain, suami Quilla, dewi bulan. Penguasa Inca menganggap diri keturunan langsungnya dan penguasa Inca dipandang sebagai perwakilan hidupnya, sedangkan Manco Capac dipercaya diajari atau malah putranya.
long_description.en: The most common belief was that Inti was born of Viracocha, though another source says Viracocha made the sun from an island on Lake Titicaca. Inti is also called the brother of Quilla, goddess of the moon, and by another source her husband. Inca rulers saw themselves as his direct descendants and the Inca ruler was regarded as his living representative, while Manco Capac was believed to have been taught by him or even to be his son.

long_description.id: Kuil Coricancha di Cuzco dipersembahkan kepada Inti, dan ia dipuja terutama pada festival Inti Raymi. Pachacuti sering dikaitkan dengan asal dan perluasan Kultus Matahari Inca. Salah satu persembahan yang paling umum adalah llama putih. Dalam seni, ia jarang digambarkan; bila ada, wujudnya berupa patung emas, cakram matahari, atau topeng emas, dan salah satu patung menampilkannya sebagai anak kecil duduk bernama Punchao.
long_description.en: The Coricancha temple at Cuzco was dedicated to Inti, and he was worshipped above all at the Inti Raymi festival. Pachacuti is often linked with the origin and spread of the Inca Sun Cult. White llamas were among the commonest offerings. In art he was seldom portrayed; when he was, the form was a gold statue, a sun disk or a golden mask, and one statue showed him as a small seated boy called Punchao.

cultural_context.en: The sun mattered to the Incas, especially highlanders, because crops such as maize depended on it, and its heat was also thought to bring rain.

statement.id: Inti jarang digambarkan dalam seni Inca, dan bila digambarkan biasanya sebagai patung emas, cakram matahari, atau topeng emas; emas dikaitkan dengan sang dewa karena dipercaya sebagai keringat matahari.
statement.en: Inti was not often represented in Inca art, and when he was it was usually as a gold statue, a sun disk or a golden mask; gold was associated with the god because it was believed to be the sweat of the sun.

claims.quote: The statue represented Inti as a small seated boy, called Punchao (Day or Midday Sun).

statement.id: Patung itu menggambarkan Inti sebagai anak kecil yang duduk, bernama Punchao (Matahari Siang atau Tengah Hari).
statement.en: The statue represented Inti as a small seated boy, called Punchao (Day or Midday Sun).

claims.quote: One curious story is when an eagle was attacked by buzzards and fell from the skies during a ceremony in honour of Inti held in c. 1526 CE which was thought to foretell the collapse of the Inca empire.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, seekor elang diserang burung nasar kecil dan jatuh dari langit saat upacara untuk Inti sekitar 1526 M, yang dianggap meramalkan runtuhnya Kekaisaran Inca.
statement.en: In one story an eagle was attacked by buzzards and fell from the skies during a ceremony in honour of Inti in c. 1526 CE, which was thought to foretell the collapse of the Inca empire.

claims.quote: The god's worshippers and the vast majority of the art made in his name have long since disappeared but Inti lives on in several present day South American cultures.

statement.id: Para pemuja sang dewa dan sebagian besar seni yang dibuat atas namanya telah lama lenyap, tetapi Inti masih hidup dalam beberapa budaya Amerika Selatan masa kini.
statement.en: The god's worshippers and most of the art made in his name have long since disappeared, but Inti lives on in several present-day South American cultures.

claims.quote: The festival of Inti Raymi has been revived as a great yearly festival in Cuzco, several national flags bear an image of him in the form of a flaming sun

statement.id: Festival Inti Raymi dihidupkan kembali sebagai festival tahunan besar di Cuzco, dan beberapa bendera nasional memuat gambarnya berupa matahari yang menyala.
statement.en: The Inti Raymi festival has been revived as a great yearly festival in Cuzco, and several national flags bear an image of him as a flaming sun.

claims.quote: Other important temples were at Pisac (north-east of Cuzco), Ingapirca (in modern Ecuador), and on the Island of the Sun on Lake Titicaca which Inca rulers visited once a year in pilgrimage.

statement.id: Kuil penting lain berada di Pisac, Ingapirca (di Ekuador masa kini), dan di Pulau Matahari di Danau Titicaca, yang dikunjungi para penguasa Inca setahun sekali dalam ziarah.
statement.en: Other important temples were at Pisac, Ingapirca (in modern Ecuador) and on the Island of the Sun on Lake Titicaca, which Inca rulers visited once a year in pilgrimage.

claims.quote: Inti (Quechua: inti, lit. 'sun' ) is the ancient Inca sun god. He is revered as the national patron of the Inca state.

statement.id: Inti (Quechua: inti, secara harfiah 'matahari') adalah dewa matahari Inca kuno, dimuliakan sebagai pelindung nasional negara Inca.
statement.en: Inti (Quechua: inti, literally 'sun') is the ancient Inca sun god, revered as the national patron of the Inca state.

claims.quote: The word inti is not of Quechua origin but a loanword from Puquina.

statement.id: Kata inti bukan berasal dari bahasa Quechua, melainkan kata serapan dari bahasa Puquina.
statement.en: The word inti is not of Quechua origin but a loanword from Puquina.

claims.quote: According to myth, Inti taught Manco Cápac and his daughter Mama Ocllo the arts of civilization.

statement.id: Menurut mitos, Inti mengajarkan seni peradaban kepada Manco Cápac dan putrinya, Mama Ocllo.
statement.en: According to myth, Inti taught Manco Cápac and his daughter Mama Ocllo the arts of civilization.

claims.quote: The sun was also important to the Incas, particularly the people of the highlands, because it was necessary for the production of crops like maize and other grains. The sun's heat was also thought to cause rain.

statement.id: Matahari penting bagi bangsa Inca, terutama penduduk dataran tinggi, karena diperlukan untuk menghasilkan jagung dan biji-bijian lain; panas matahari juga dianggap menyebabkan hujan.
statement.en: The sun was important to the Incas, particularly highland people, because it was necessary for producing maize and other grains; the sun's heat was also thought to cause rain.

claims.quote: Inti's identity is also divided into three primary subcomplexes, which are the father, son, and brother.

statement.id: Identitas Inti juga dibagi menjadi tiga subkompleks utama, yaitu ayah, putra, dan saudara.
statement.en: Inti's identity is also divided into three primary subcomplexes: the father, the son and the brother.

claims.quote: The first of these is Apu Inti ("supreme Inti"). He represents the father and is sometimes known as "The Lord Sun". The second is Churi Inti, or "Son Inti", who represents the son of Inti and is often known as "Daylight". The third and final division of Inti is Inti Wawqi ("Sun brother", or "Inti brother", also spelled Inti-Guauqui, Inti-Huaoqui).

statement.id: Ketiganya adalah Apu Inti ("Inti tertinggi"), Churi Inti ("Inti putra", sering disebut "Cahaya Siang"), dan Inti Wawqi ("saudara matahari").
statement.en: The three are Apu Inti ("supreme Inti"), Churi Inti ("Son Inti", often known as "Daylight") and Inti Wawqi ("Sun brother").

claims.quote: Some sources identify the central figure of the Gateway of the Sun as Inti and others as Viracocha

statement.id: Sebagian sumber mengidentifikasi tokoh utama pada Gerbang Matahari sebagai Inti dan sebagian lain sebagai Viracocha.
statement.en: Some sources identify the central figure of the Gateway of the Sun as Inti and others as Viracocha.

claims.quote: The Sun is also depicted on the coat of arms of Bolivia and coat of arms of Ecuador, the Flag of the Hispanic people, as well as the historical flag of Peru. All these countries (including the North region of Chile, Northeast and parts of Cuyo (Argentina)) were historically part of the Inca Empire.

statement.id: Matahari juga digambarkan pada lambang negara Bolivia dan Ekuador serta bendera historis Peru; semua negara itu (termasuk Chile utara dan bagian Argentina) dahulu bagian dari Kekaisaran Inca.
statement.en: The Sun is also depicted on the coats of arms of Bolivia and Ecuador and the historical flag of Peru; all these countries (including northern Chile and parts of Argentina) were historically part of the Inca Empire.

claims.quote: The Inca ruler was considered to be the living representative of Inti.

statement.id: Penguasa Inca dianggap perwakilan hidup Inti.
statement.en: The Inca ruler was considered to be the living representative of Inti.

claims.quote: Spanish conquistadors captured a great golden disk representing Inti in 1571

statement.id: Para penakluk Spanyol merebut sebuah cakram emas besar yang melambangkan Inti pada 1571.
statement.en: Spanish conquistadors captured a great golden disk representing Inti in 1571.

summary.en: The most common belief: Inti was born of Viracocha.

summary.en: According to another source, Viracocha created the sun from an island on Lake Titicaca.
