short_description.id: Pachamama atau Mama Pacha adalah dewa Andes yang mewakili ruang-waktu, dipuja bangsa-bangsa Andes sebagai dewi ibu yang menopang kehidupan dan kesuburan.
short_description.en: Pachamama, also called Mama Pacha, is an Andean deity who stands for space-time and is honoured by Andean peoples as a mother goddess sustaining life and fertility.

long_description.id:
Pachamama atau Mama Pacha adalah dewa Andes yang mewakili ruang-waktu dan dipuja oleh bangsa-bangsa Andes. Dalam mitologi dan agama Inca, ia dipandang sebagai dewi ibu yang terkait kehidupan, kesuburan, dan alam, dan dianggap hadir di mana-mana serta berdaya cipta untuk menopang kehidupan. Empat prinsip kosmologis Quechua (Air, Bumi, Matahari, dan Bulan) menganggapnya asal utama, dan dari kesuburannya kosmos dikatakan lahir dan bumi disuburkan.

Ia biasanya dewi yang penuh kasih dan murah hati, tetapi dapat menjadi mengerikan dan merusak ketika tersinggung. Pachamama umum dipuja dalam wujud duniawinya, Allpamama atau Mama Allpa; kuilnya berupa batu keramat atau batang pohon legendaris, dan ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan pembawa hasil panen kentang atau daun koka. Para imam mempersembahkan llama, marmut, dan pakaian mini yang dibakar kepadanya. Ia juga digambarkan sebagai dewi purba yang tidak membutuhkan kuil khusus.

Pemujaannya berlangsung lewat persembahan. Pemuka Andes bernama Rufino Turpo menceritakan keluarganya berkumpul pada awal Agustus untuk membuat "pembayaran" kepada Pachamama, yang seperti manusia perlu makan dan minum; sang Ibu dikatakan marah bila orang membayar tanpa hormat, dan persembahan dibakar sehingga asapnya membawa doa. Di beberapa daerah, orang menumpahkan sedikit chicha ke tanah setiap hari sebagai challa.

Program Peru pada Festival Folklife 2015 memakai nama Pachamama, "Ibu Bumi" dalam bahasa Quechua dan Aymara. Menurut kajian, kronik Peru abad keenam belas dan ketujuh belas memuat rincian tentang kultus bumi pra-Hispanik dan kelangsungannya pada dekade awal kolonisasi. Melalui sinkretisme, Perawan Maria dikaitkan dengan Pachamama, dan pada abad ke-21 banyak masyarakat adat mendasarkan kepedulian lingkungan pada kepercayaan ini.
long_description.en:
Pachamama, also called Mama Pacha, is an Andean deity who stands for space-time and is honoured by Andean peoples. Inca mythology and religion treat her as a mother goddess connected with life, fertility and nature, thought to be ever-present and able to create and sustain life. Four cosmological Quechua principles (Water, Earth, Sun and Moon) trace their origin to her, and the cosmos is said to be born from her fertility, with the earth made fertile.

She is normally loving and generous, yet can turn terrible and destructive when offended. Pachamama was commonly worshipped in her earthly form, Allpamama or Mama Allpa; her shrines were sacred rocks or the trunks of legendary trees, and she was pictured as a woman carrying potato or coca-leaf harvests. Priests offered llamas, guinea pigs and small burned garments to her. She is also described as an ancient goddess who needs no special temples.

Her worship proceeds through offerings. An Andean writer, Rufino Turpo, recounts his family gathering at the start of August to make a "payment" to Pachamama, who like people needs to eat and drink; the Mother is said to be angered by payment made without respect, and the offering is burned so that the smoke carries prayers. In some regions people spill a little chicha on the ground daily as a challa.

The Peru program of the 2015 Folklife Festival took its name from Pachamama, "Mother Earth" in Quechua and Aymara. Scholarship notes that Peruvian chronicles of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries record details of pre-Hispanic earth cults and their persistence in the early decades of colonization. Through syncretism the Virgin Mary was associated with Pachamama, and in the 21st century many Indigenous peoples ground environmental concerns in these beliefs.

claim.en: Pachamama and her sun-husband Inti are worshipped as benevolent deities in the area known as Tawantinsuyu, the former Inca Empire, stretching through the Andean mountains in present-day Bolivia, Ecuador, Chile, Peru, Colombia and northern Argentina.

claim.en: The central ritual to Pachamama is the Challa or Pago (payment), carried out during all of August and in many places also on the first Friday of each month.

short_description.id: Pachamama atau Mama Pacha adalah dewa Andes yang mewakili ruang-waktu, dipuja bangsa-bangsa Andes sebagai dewi ibu yang menopang kehidupan dan kesuburan.
short_description.en: Pachamama, also called Mama Pacha, is an Andean deity who stands for space-time and is honoured by Andean peoples as a mother goddess sustaining life and fertility.

long_description.id: Pachamama atau Mama Pacha adalah dewa Andes yang mewakili ruang-waktu dan dipuja oleh bangsa-bangsa Andes. Dalam mitologi dan agama Inca, ia dipandang sebagai dewi ibu yang terkait kehidupan, kesuburan, dan alam, dan dianggap hadir di mana-mana serta berdaya cipta untuk menopang kehidupan. Empat prinsip kosmologis Quechua (Air, Bumi, Matahari, dan Bulan) menganggapnya asal utama, dan dari kesuburannya kosmos dikatakan lahir dan bumi disuburkan.
long_description.en: Pachamama, also called Mama Pacha, is an Andean deity who stands for space-time and is honoured by Andean peoples. Inca mythology and religion treat her as a mother goddess connected with life, fertility and nature, thought to be ever-present and able to create and sustain life. Four cosmological Quechua principles (Water, Earth, Sun and Moon) trace their origin to her, and the cosmos is said to be born from her fertility, with the earth made fertile.

long_description.id: Ia biasanya dewi yang penuh kasih dan murah hati, tetapi dapat menjadi mengerikan dan merusak ketika tersinggung. Pachamama umum dipuja dalam wujud duniawinya, Allpamama atau Mama Allpa; kuilnya berupa batu keramat atau batang pohon legendaris, dan ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan pembawa hasil panen kentang atau daun koka. Para imam mempersembahkan llama, marmut, dan pakaian mini yang dibakar kepadanya. Ia juga digambarkan sebagai dewi purba yang tidak membutuhkan kuil khusus.
long_description.en: She is normally loving and generous, yet can turn terrible and destructive when offended. Pachamama was commonly worshipped in her earthly form, Allpamama or Mama Allpa; her shrines were sacred rocks or the trunks of legendary trees, and she was pictured as a woman carrying potato or coca-leaf harvests. Priests offered llamas, guinea pigs and small burned garments to her. She is also described as an ancient goddess who needs no special temples.

long_description.id: Pemujaannya berlangsung lewat persembahan. Pemuka Andes bernama Rufino Turpo menceritakan keluarganya berkumpul pada awal Agustus untuk membuat "pembayaran" kepada Pachamama, yang seperti manusia perlu makan dan minum; sang Ibu dikatakan marah bila orang membayar tanpa hormat, dan persembahan dibakar sehingga asapnya membawa doa. Di beberapa daerah, orang menumpahkan sedikit chicha ke tanah setiap hari sebagai challa.
long_description.en: Her worship proceeds through offerings. An Andean writer, Rufino Turpo, recounts his family gathering at the start of August to make a "payment" to Pachamama, who like people needs to eat and drink; the Mother is said to be angered by payment made without respect, and the offering is burned so that the smoke carries prayers. In some regions people spill a little chicha on the ground daily as a challa.

long_description.id: Program Peru pada Festival Folklife 2015 memakai nama Pachamama, "Ibu Bumi" dalam bahasa Quechua dan Aymara. Menurut kajian, kronik Peru abad keenam belas dan ketujuh belas memuat rincian tentang kultus bumi pra-Hispanik dan kelangsungannya pada dekade awal kolonisasi. Melalui sinkretisme, Perawan Maria dikaitkan dengan Pachamama, dan pada abad ke-21 banyak masyarakat adat mendasarkan kepedulian lingkungan pada kepercayaan ini.
long_description.en: The Peru program of the 2015 Folklife Festival took its name from Pachamama, "Mother Earth" in Quechua and Aymara. Scholarship notes that Peruvian chronicles of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries record details of pre-Hispanic earth cults and their persistence in the early decades of colonization. Through syncretism the Virgin Mary was associated with Pachamama, and in the 21st century many Indigenous peoples ground environmental concerns in these beliefs.

cultural_context.id: Pada abad ke-21, banyak masyarakat adat di Amerika Selatan mendasarkan kepedulian lingkungan pada kepercayaan kepada Pachamama, dengan mengatakan bahwa mengambil terlalu banyak dari alam berarti mengambil terlalu banyak dari Pachamama.
cultural_context.en: In the 21st century, many Indigenous peoples of South America ground their environmental concerns in belief in Pachamama, holding that over-taking from nature means over-taking from Pachamama.

claims.quote: or Mama Pacha ... is the Andean deity representing space-time, revered by the peoples of the Andes.

statement.id: Pachamama atau Mama Pacha adalah dewa Andes yang mewakili ruang-waktu dan dipuja oleh bangsa-bangsa Andes.
statement.en: Pachamama or Mama Pacha is the Andean deity representing space-time, revered by the peoples of the Andes.

claims.quote: The four cosmological Quechua principles—Water, Earth, Sun, and Moon—claim Pachamama as their prime origin.

statement.id: Empat prinsip kosmologi Quechua—Air, Bumi, Matahari, dan Bulan—berasal dari Pachamama.
statement.en: The four cosmological Quechua principles claim Pachamama as their origin.

claims.quote: She is considered an omnipresent deity with creative power, capable of sustaining life in the cosmos.

statement.id: Ia dianggap dewa yang hadir di mana-mana dan memiliki daya cipta untuk menopang kehidupan di kosmos.
statement.en: She is considered an omnipresent deity with creative power, capable of sustaining life in the cosmos.

claims.quote: In Inca mythology and religion, she is a "mother goddess" type deity, representing the universal energy that connects everything, linked to space, time, the universe, totality, life, fertility, and nature.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi dan agama Inca, ia adalah dewa bertipe "dewi ibu" yang mewakili energi universal yang menghubungkan segalanya, terkait ruang, waktu, alam semesta, totalitas, kehidupan, kesuburan, dan alam.
statement.en: In Inca mythology and religion, she is a "mother goddess" type deity representing the universal energy that connects everything, linked to space, time, the universe, totality, life, fertility and nature.

claims.quote: She is attributed with the role of mother of the world, from whom the material and spiritual sustenance of human beings comes.

statement.id: Ia dianggap berperan sebagai ibu dunia, tempat asal sumber penghidupan material dan spiritual manusia.
statement.en: She is attributed with the role of mother of the world, from whom the material and spiritual sustenance of human beings comes.

claims.quote: In various myths, Pachamama is described as the wife of Pachacámac and mother of Mama Quilla (the goddess of the moon) and Inti (the god of the sun).

statement.id: Dalam berbagai mitos, Pachamama digambarkan sebagai istri Pachacámac dan ibu Mama Quilla (dewi bulan) dan Inti (dewa matahari).
statement.en: In various myths, Pachamama is described as the wife of Pachacámac and mother of Mama Quilla (the goddess of the moon) and Inti (the god of the sun).

claims.quote: Pachamama was commonly worshipped in her earthly manifestation or form called Allpamama or Mama Allpa (goddess of the earth), her shrines consisted of sacred rocks or the trunks of legendary trees, and artists depicted her as a woman bearing harvests of potatoes or coca leaves.

statement.id: Pachamama umum dipuja dalam wujud duniawinya yang disebut Allpamama atau Mama Allpa (dewi bumi); kuilnya berupa batu keramat atau batang pohon legendaris, dan seniman menggambarkannya sebagai perempuan pembawa hasil panen kentang atau daun koka.
statement.en: Pachamama was commonly worshipped in her earthly form called Allpamama or Mama Allpa (goddess of the earth); her shrines were sacred rocks or the trunks of legendary trees, and artists depicted her as a woman bearing harvests of potatoes or coca leaves.

claims.quote: Priests sacrifice offerings of llamas, cuy (guinea pigs), and elaborate, miniature, burned garments to her.

statement.id: Para imam mempersembahkan llama, cuy (marmut), dan pakaian mini yang rumit yang dibakar kepadanya.
statement.en: Priests sacrifice offerings of llamas, cuy (guinea pigs) and elaborate miniature burned garments to her.

claims.quote: She is normally a loving and generous goddess, but she can be terrible, cruel, and destructive when she is upset or feels hurt, capable of destroying men and everything above or within her.

statement.id: Ia biasanya dewi yang penuh kasih dan murah hati, tetapi bisa mengerikan, kejam, dan merusak ketika marah atau merasa terluka, mampu menghancurkan manusia dan segala yang ada di atas atau di dalamnya.
statement.en: She is normally a loving and generous goddess, but she can be terrible, cruel and destructive when upset or hurt, capable of destroying men and everything above or within her.

claims.quote: Pachamama is an ancient and primordial goddess who does not need temples or specific places of worship, although she likes springs, simply because she is everywhere and at all times.

statement.id: Pachamama adalah dewi purba dan primordial yang tidak membutuhkan kuil atau tempat ibadah khusus, meskipun ia menyukai mata air, karena ia ada di mana-mana dan sepanjang waktu.
statement.en: Pachamama is an ancient and primordial goddess who does not need temples or specific places of worship, although she likes springs, simply because she is everywhere and at all times.

claims.quote: The word Pachamama comes from the Quechua language and is composed of two terms: Pacha: a complex word meaning 'world, universe, space-time, totality, era, cosmos'.

statement.id: Kata Pachamama berasal dari bahasa Quechua dan terdiri atas dua unsur; yang pertama, pacha, adalah kata kompleks yang berarti 'dunia, alam semesta, ruang-waktu, totalitas, zaman, kosmos'.
statement.en: The word Pachamama comes from the Quechua language and has two parts; the first, pacha, is a complex word meaning 'world, universe, space-time, totality, era, cosmos'.

claims.quote: Mama: means mother, but also represents the feminine principle that generates and nourishes life.

statement.id: Unsur kedua, mama, berarti ibu, tetapi juga mewakili prinsip feminin yang melahirkan dan memelihara kehidupan.
statement.en: The second part, mama, means mother, but also represents the feminine principle that generates and nourishes life.

claims.quote: Pachamama plays the role of cosmic mother; from Pachamama's fertility, the cosmos is born, the earth is fertilized, and then it flourishes.

statement.id: Pachamama berperan sebagai ibu kosmik; dari kesuburannya kosmos lahir, bumi disuburkan, dan kemudian berkembang.
statement.en: Pachamama plays the role of cosmic mother; from her fertility the cosmos is born, the earth is fertilized, and it then flourishes.

claims.quote: Allpamama is often hungry, and if she is not nourished with offerings or if she is offended, she can cause a cosmic imbalance that breaks the universal harmony affecting all worlds

statement.id: Allpamama sering lapar, dan bila tidak diberi persembahan atau tersinggung, ia dapat menimbulkan ketidakseimbangan kosmik yang merusak keharmonisan semesta yang memengaruhi semua dunia.
statement.en: Allpamama is often hungry, and if she is not nourished with offerings or is offended, she can cause a cosmic imbalance that breaks the universal harmony affecting all worlds.

claims.quote: Pachamama and her sun-husband, Inti, are worshipped as benevolent deities in the area known as Tawantinsuyu. Tawantinsuyu is the name of the former Inca Empire, and the region stretches through the Andean mountains in present-day Bolivia, Ecuador, Chile, Peru, Colombia and northern Argentina.

statement.id: Pachamama dan suaminya, sang matahari Inti, dipuja sebagai dewa-dewi yang murah hati di wilayah yang dikenal sebagai Tawantinsuyu, bekas Kekaisaran Inca yang membentang melintasi pegunungan Andes di Bolivia, Ekuador, Chile, Peru, Kolombia, dan Argentina utara masa kini.
statement.en: Pachamama and her sun-husband Inti are worshipped as benevolent deities in the area known as Tawantinsuyu, the former Inca Empire, stretching through the Andean mountains in present-day Bolivia, Ecuador, Chile, Peru, Colombia and northern Argentina.

statement.id: Pada hari pertama Chajrayapuy (Agustus), keluarga berkumpul untuk membuat "pembayaran" atau persembahan kepada Pachamama; seperti manusia, ia perlu makan dan minum, dan setiap kali minum chicha, bir, atau anggur, minuman itu harus dibagikan kepadanya.
statement.en: On the first day of Chajrayapuy (August) the family gathers to make a "payment" or offering to Pachamama; like people, she needs to eat and drink, and whenever chicha, beer or wine is drunk it must be shared with her.

claims.quote: We offer all this for Pachamama to eat, and in return she provides for us and protects us. Finally, we burn the offering. Smoke rises, taking our prayers.

statement.id: Semua persembahan itu diberikan agar Pachamama makan, dan sebagai balasannya ia menyediakan kebutuhan dan melindungi; persembahan lalu dibakar dan asapnya membawa doa.
statement.en: All this is offered for Pachamama to eat, and in return she provides for the people and protects them; the offering is then burned and the smoke carries the prayers.

claims.quote: The Mother gets angry when you want to pay without respect, without knowing why.

statement.id: Sang Ibu marah bila orang membayar tanpa hormat dan tanpa tahu alasannya.
statement.en: The Mother gets angry when you want to pay without respect, without knowing why.

claims.quote: This article analyzes the cult to Andean Mother Earth known as Pachamama, starting from the references contained in those Peruvian chronicles of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries

claims.quote: We emphasize, in particular, the peculiarity of the details that they provide about terminology, representations, beliefs and rituals associated with telluric cults in the Prehispanic period, and their persistence throughout the first decades of colonization of the central Andes.

statement.id: Kronik-kronik itu memberi rincian khas tentang istilah, penggambaran, kepercayaan, dan ritual kultus bumi pada masa pra-Hispanik, serta kelangsungannya selama beberapa dekade pertama kolonisasi Andes tengah.
statement.en: The chronicles give distinctive details about terminology, representations, beliefs and rituals of the telluric cults of the Prehispanic period, and their persistence through the first decades of colonization of the central Andes.

short_description.id: Vajrapani adalah bodhisatwa dalam Buddhisme Mahayana dan pelindung serta pembimbing Buddha Gautama.
short_description.en: Vajrapani is a Mahayana bodhisattva and protector and guide of Gautama Buddha.

long_description.id:
Vajrapani adalah bodhisatwa dalam Buddhisme Mahayana dan pelindung serta pembimbing Buddha Gautama. Nama lain yang digunakan adalah Chana Dorje dan Chador.

Ia melambangkan daya Buddha, bersama Manjushri yang melambangkan kebijaksanaan dan Avalokiteshvara yang melambangkan belas kasih. Nama Sanskertanya dijelaskan sebagai pemegang vajra atau halilintar. Wujud manusianya digambarkan memegang vajra di tangan kanan. HAR menyatakan Vajrapani dalam tradisi Vajrayana sering digambarkan murka dan dikenal sebagai Guhyapati.
long_description.en:
Vajrapani is a Mahayana bodhisattva and protector and guide of Gautama Buddha. Other names used are Chana Dorje and Chador.

He symbolizes the Buddha's power alongside Manjushri symbolizing wisdom and Avalokiteshvara symbolizing compassion. His Sanskrit name is explained as holder of the vajra or thunderbolt. His human form is depicted holding a vajra in the right hand. HAR states that Vajrapani in Vajrayana is often depicted wrathfully and known as Guhyapati.

short_description.id: Mahishasura adalah asura berwujud kerbau dalam Hindu.
short_description.en: Mahishasura is a bovine asura in Hinduism.

long_description.id:
Mahishasura adalah asura berwujud kerbau dalam Hindu. Cerita menggambarkannya menggunakan perubahan wujud untuk menjalankan niat jahat.

Ia disebut putra Rambha dan saudara Mahishi. Durga membunuhnya dengan trisula dan memperoleh epitet Mahishasuramardini. Navaratri merayakan pertempuran itu dan berakhir dengan perayaan kekalahannya pada Vijayadashami. Dalam kisah, ia memperoleh anugerah bahwa tidak ada laki-laki yang dapat membunuhnya. Versi WHE menggambarkan Mahisa bertubuh manusia dan berkepala kerbau.
long_description.en:
Mahishasura is a bovine asura in Hinduism. The narrative depicts him using shape shifting to pursue evil intentions.

He is called Rambha's son and Mahishi's brother. Durga kills him with a trident and gains the epithet Mahishasuramardini. Navaratri celebrates the battle and culminates in celebrating his defeat at Vijayadashami. In the narrative he obtains a boon that no man can kill him. WHE's version depicts Mahisa with a human body and buffalo head.

short_description.id: Rahu adalah salah satu Navagraha dan personifikasi titik simpul Bulan utara dalam tradisi Hindu.
short_description.en: Rahu is one of the Navagraha and personifies the north lunar node in Hindu tradition.

long_description.id:
Rahu adalah salah satu Navagraha dan personifikasi titik simpul Bulan utara dalam tradisi Hindu. Ia dipasangkan dengan Ketu, titik simpul Bulan selatan.

Rahu kala merupakan waktu yang dianggap tidak menguntungkan dalam tradisi astrologi. Kisah Purana menuturkan Svarbhanu menyamar untuk meminum amrita. Kepala yang dipotong Vishnu disebut Rahu, sedangkan tubuhnya disebut Ketu. Mackenzie menggambarkan Rahu sebagai demon yang menyebabkan gerhana dengan menelan Matahari dan Bulan.
long_description.en:
Rahu is one of the Navagraha and personifies the north lunar node in Hindu tradition. He is paired with Ketu, the south lunar node.

Rahu kala is a time considered inauspicious in the astrological tradition. The Puranic narrative recounts Svarbhanu disguising himself to drink amrita. The head severed by Vishnu is called Rahu, while the body is called Ketu. Mackenzie depicts Rahu as a demon causing eclipses by swallowing the sun and moon.

role.en: The asura who stole the amrita and was beheaded by Mohini

summary.id: Svarbhanu duduk di barisan dewa dan meminum amrita; Surya dan Chandra memergokinya, tetapi ia sudah abadi ketika Mohini memenggalnya dengan cakra. Kepalanya menjadi Rahu, tubuhnya Ketu, dan Rahu menelan Matahari dan Bulan dalam gerhana.
summary.en: Svarbhanu sat among the gods and drank the amrita; Surya and Chandra caught him, but he was already immortal when Mohini cut off his head with the discus. The head became Rahu, the body Ketu, and Rahu swallows the Sun and Moon in eclipses.

short_description.id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh novel klasik Tiongkok Journey to the West: pangeran naga yang dihukum, lalu diubah menjadi kuda putih untuk membawa biksu Tang Sanzang dalam perjalanannya.
short_description.en: The White Dragon Horse is a character of the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West: a dragon prince who is punished and then turned into a white horse to carry the monk Tang Sanzang on his journey.

long_description.id:
White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Journey to the West, yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en. Dalam novel itu ia pangeran naga, putra ketiga Raja Naga Laut Barat, yang kemudian menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang; ia juga dikenal sebagai Ao Lie.

Menurut teks bab 8, ia digantung di udara dan dipukul karena membakar mutiara, hingga Guanyin menyelamatkannya dan menaruhnya di ngarai untuk menunggu pengambil sutra. Pada bab 15 ia menelan kuda putih Tang Sanzang, melawan Sun Wukong, lalu diubah Guanyin menjadi kuda putih pengganti.

Di akhir novel ia dinaikkan menjadi Kuda Naga Delapan Bagian Surgawi, kembali ke wujud naga, dan melingkari tiang di kuil. Ia sering digambarkan pendiam dan cerdas, dan dalam tafsir tradisional dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran"; ia juga dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok.
long_description.en:
The White Dragon Horse is a literary character from Journey to the West, a novel that appeared in the 16th century under the Ming dynasty and is credited to Wu Cheng'en. In the novel he is a dragon prince, third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea, who later becomes Tang Sanzang's steed; he is also known as Ao Lie.

According to the chapter 8 text he is hung in the air and beaten for burning a pearl until Guanyin rescues him and places him in a gorge to wait for the scripture seeker. In chapter 15 he swallows Tang Sanzang's white horse, fights Sun Wukong, and is then turned by Guanyin into a white horse as a replacement.

At the end of the novel he is raised to the Dragon Horse of the Eight Heavenly Sections, returns to dragon form and coils around a pillar in the temple. He is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and in traditional interpretation is linked with the "Horse of the Mind"; he is also worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion.

cultural_context.id: Dalam kritik sastra tradisional dan tafsir Neidan, White Dragon Horse dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran" atau "Kuda Kehendak"; dan Bai Longma dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok. cultural_context.en: In traditional literary criticism and Neidan interpretation the White Dragon Horse is linked with the "Horse of the Mind" or "Horse of the Will", and Bai Longma is worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion. In his 1913 introduction Timothy Richard presents him as a dragon who sinned and was degraded into a horse.

claim.en: In chapter 8 the dragon hanging in the air says he is the son of the Dragon King of the West Sea, Ao Run (敖閏); for setting fire to the pearl in the hall his father reported him to heaven as unfilial, and the Jade Emperor hung him up and had him struck three hundred times, soon to be executed.

claim.en: The bodhisattva places him in a deep gorge to wait for the scripture seeker, to become a white horse and win merit going west; the little dragon accepts the order and hides himself.

claims_provenance.quote: 菩薩把他送在深澗之中，只等取經人來，變做白馬，上西方立功。小龍領命潛身不題。

claim.id: Dalam bab 15, sang naga tidak berhasil mengejar Tang Sanzang tetapi menelan kuda putihnya beserta pelana dan kekang dalam satu suapan, lalu bersembunyi lagi di air.
claim.en: In chapter 15 the dragon cannot catch up with the elder but swallows his white horse with saddle and bridle in one gulp and hides again in the water.

claims_provenance.quote: 那條龍就趕不上，把他的白馬連鞍轡一口吞下肚去，依然伏水潛蹤。

claim.id: Guanyin menjelaskan bahwa ia sendiri meminta naga itu kepada Kaisar Giok untuk menjadi tunggangan para pengambil sutra, karena kuda biasa tak akan sanggup menempuh ribuan gunung dan sungai ke Tanah Buddha tanpa kuda naga ini.
claim.en: The bodhisattva explains that she herself asked the Jade Emperor for the dragon to serve as a mount for scripture seekers, since an ordinary horse could not cross the myriad mountains and rivers to the Buddha land without this dragon horse.

claims_provenance.quote: 那條龍，是我親奏玉帝，討他在此，專為求經人做個腳力。你想那東土來的凡馬，怎歷得這萬水千山？怎到得那靈山佛地？須是得這個龍馬，方才去得。

claim.id: Guanyin menyuruh pengawal memanggilnya dengan sebutan "敖閏龍王玉龍三太子" (Pangeran Ketiga Naga Giok dari Raja Naga Ao Run) agar keluar.
claim.en: The bodhisattva has an attendant call him by the title "敖閏龍王玉龍三太子" (third prince Jade Dragon of the Dragon King Ao Run) to come out.

claims_provenance.quote: 菩薩叫揭諦道：「你去澗邊叫一聲『敖閏龍王玉龍三太子，你出來，有南海菩薩在此。』他就出來了。

claim.id: Di akhir novel, Buddha memanggil kuda putih itu dan berkata ia putra Raja Naga Guangjin (廣晉) dari Samudra Barat, bersalah tidak berbakti karena melawan perintah ayahnya; karena jasanya memikul biksu ke barat dan kitab ke timur, ia dinaikkan menjadi Kuda Naga Delapan Bagian Surgawi (八部天龍馬).
claim.en: At the end of the novel the Buddha addresses the white horse and says he is a son of the Dragon King Guangjin (廣晉) of the Western Ocean, guilty of unfilial conduct for defying his father's order; for carrying the holy monk west and the scriptures east he is raised to the Dragon Horse of the Eight Heavenly Sections (八部天龍馬).

short_description.id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh novel klasik Tiongkok Journey to the West: pangeran naga yang dihukum, lalu diubah menjadi kuda putih untuk membawa biksu Tang Sanzang dalam perjalanannya.
short_description.en: The White Dragon Horse is a character of the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West: a dragon prince who is punished and then turned into a white horse to carry the monk Tang Sanzang on his journey.

long_description.id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Journey to the West, yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en. Dalam novel itu ia pangeran naga, putra ketiga Raja Naga Laut Barat, yang kemudian menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang; ia juga dikenal sebagai Ao Lie.
long_description.en: The White Dragon Horse is a literary character from Journey to the West, a novel that appeared in the 16th century under the Ming dynasty and is credited to Wu Cheng'en. In the novel he is a dragon prince, third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea, who later becomes Tang Sanzang's steed; he is also known as Ao Lie.

long_description.id: Menurut teks bab 8, ia digantung di udara dan dipukul karena membakar mutiara, hingga Guanyin menyelamatkannya dan menaruhnya di ngarai untuk menunggu pengambil sutra. Pada bab 15 ia menelan kuda putih Tang Sanzang, melawan Sun Wukong, lalu diubah Guanyin menjadi kuda putih pengganti.
long_description.en: According to the chapter 8 text he is hung in the air and beaten for burning a pearl until Guanyin rescues him and places him in a gorge to wait for the scripture seeker. In chapter 15 he swallows Tang Sanzang's white horse, fights Sun Wukong, and is then turned by Guanyin into a white horse as a replacement.

long_description.id: Di akhir novel ia dinaikkan menjadi Kuda Naga Delapan Bagian Surgawi, kembali ke wujud naga, dan melingkari tiang di kuil. Ia sering digambarkan pendiam dan cerdas, dan dalam tafsir tradisional dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran"; ia juga dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok.
long_description.en: At the end of the novel he is raised to the Dragon Horse of the Eight Heavenly Sections, returns to dragon form and coils around a pillar in the temple. He is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and in traditional interpretation is linked with the "Horse of the Mind"; he is also worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion.

cultural_context.id: Dalam kritik sastra tradisional dan tafsir Neidan, White Dragon Horse dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran" atau "Kuda Kehendak"; dan Bai Longma dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok. Dalam pengantar tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menafsirkannya sebagai naga yang berdosa lalu direndahkan menjadi kuda.
cultural_context.en: In traditional literary criticism and Neidan interpretation the White Dragon Horse is linked with the "Horse of the Mind" or "Horse of the Will", and Bai Longma is worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion. In his 1913 introduction Timothy Richard presents him as a dragon who sinned and was degraded into a horse.

literal_meaning.id: Bai Longma secara harfiah berarti "kuda naga putih"; Yulong berarti "naga giok".
literal_meaning.en: Bai Longma literally means "white dragon horse"; Yulong means "jade dragon".

short_description.id: Nukekubi adalah jenis rokurokubi yang kepalanya terlepas sepenuhnya dari tubuh dan dapat terbang; kisah tentangnya populer pada zaman Edo.
short_description.en: Nukekubi is the kind of rokurokubi whose head detaches completely from the body and can fly; tales about it became popular in the Edo period.

long_description.id:
Nukekubi adalah rokurokubi yang kepalanya terlepas sepenuhnya dari tubuh. Pada rokurokubi, kepala dapat terbang, entah di ujung leher panjang seperti ular atau terlepas sama sekali dari tubuh. Menurut Yokai.com, nukekubi lebih ganas dan haus darah daripada rokurokubi berleher panjang.

Kisah dan gambar rokurokubi menjadi sangat populer pada zaman Edo, dan kamus mencatat banyak pustaka zaman Edo yang memuatnya. Lafcadio Hearn memuat kisah "Rokuro-kubi" dalam Kwaidan tentang seorang pendeta yang menginap bersama keluarga makhluk semacam itu. Sebuah kisah zaman Edo bahkan memuat nukekubi lelaki.

Pustaka zaman Edo kerap menafsirkan kepala yang terlepas sebagai jiwa yang mengembara keluar tubuh, seperti dalam Sorori Monogatari (1663). Yokai.com menyebut para ilmuwan zaman Edo mengira penderitanya mengidap penyakit mirip berjalan dalam tidur. Diteorikan pula bahwa bila tubuh yang tidur dipindahkan saat kepala melayang, kepala tidak dapat menyatu kembali. Penulis ensiklopedia Jepang menduga kisah kepala terbang berasal dari Tiongkok.
long_description.en:
The nukekubi is a rokurokubi whose head detaches completely from the body. In a rokurokubi the head can fly off, either at the end of a long snake-like neck or fully detached from the body. According to Yokai.com, nukekubi are more violent and thirst for blood more than the long-necked rokurokubi.

Tales and pictures of rokurokubi became very popular in the Edo period, and a dictionary notes many Edo-period works that record them. Lafcadio Hearn included a story called "Rokuro-kubi" in Kwaidan about a priest who stays with a family of such creatures. An Edo-period tale even includes a male nukekubi.

Edo-period works often interpret the detached head as the soul wandering out of the body, as in the Sorori Monogatari (1663). Yokai.com says Edo-period scientists believed sufferers had an affliction like sleepwalking. It is also theorized that if the sleeping body is moved while the head floats, the head cannot rejoin it. The author of a Japanese encyclopedia entry suspects that tales of flying heads came from China.

short_description.id: Nukekubi adalah jenis rokurokubi yang kepalanya terlepas sepenuhnya dari tubuh dan dapat terbang; kisah tentangnya populer pada zaman Edo.
short_description.en: Nukekubi is the kind of rokurokubi whose head detaches completely from the body and can fly; tales about it became popular in the Edo period.

long_description.id: Nukekubi adalah rokurokubi yang kepalanya terlepas sepenuhnya dari tubuh. Pada rokurokubi, kepala dapat terbang, entah di ujung leher panjang seperti ular atau terlepas sama sekali dari tubuh. Menurut Yokai.com, nukekubi lebih ganas dan haus darah daripada rokurokubi berleher panjang.
long_description.en: The nukekubi is a rokurokubi whose head detaches completely from the body. In a rokurokubi the head can fly off, either at the end of a long snake-like neck or fully detached from the body. According to Yokai.com, nukekubi are more violent and thirst for blood more than the long-necked rokurokubi.

long_description.id: Kisah dan gambar rokurokubi menjadi sangat populer pada zaman Edo, dan kamus mencatat banyak pustaka zaman Edo yang memuatnya. Lafcadio Hearn memuat kisah "Rokuro-kubi" dalam Kwaidan tentang seorang pendeta yang menginap bersama keluarga makhluk semacam itu. Sebuah kisah zaman Edo bahkan memuat nukekubi lelaki.
long_description.en: Tales and pictures of rokurokubi became very popular in the Edo period, and a dictionary notes many Edo-period works that record them. Lafcadio Hearn included a story called "Rokuro-kubi" in Kwaidan about a priest who stays with a family of such creatures. An Edo-period tale even includes a male nukekubi.

long_description.id: Pustaka zaman Edo kerap menafsirkan kepala yang terlepas sebagai jiwa yang mengembara keluar tubuh, seperti dalam Sorori Monogatari (1663). Yokai.com menyebut para ilmuwan zaman Edo mengira penderitanya mengidap penyakit mirip berjalan dalam tidur. Diteorikan pula bahwa bila tubuh yang tidur dipindahkan saat kepala melayang, kepala tidak dapat menyatu kembali. Penulis ensiklopedia Jepang menduga kisah kepala terbang berasal dari Tiongkok.
long_description.en: Edo-period works often interpret the detached head as the soul wandering out of the body, as in the Sorori Monogatari (1663). Yokai.com says Edo-period scientists believed sufferers had an affliction like sleepwalking. It is also theorized that if the sleeping body is moved while the head floats, the head cannot rejoin it. The author of a Japanese encyclopedia entry suspects that tales of flying heads came from China.

short_description.en: Tarantasio is a legendary dragon that, in the lore of Lombardy, terrorized the people of Lake Gerundo near Lodi, devouring children, wrecking boats and spreading a disease-bearing breath.

long_description.id:
Tarantasio adalah naga legendaris yang menteror penghuni Danau Gerundo kuno dan hipotetis di sekitar Lodi, Lombardia. Menurut legenda rakyat, ia juga dikenal sebagai Tarànto dan terutama memakan anak-anak. Ia dipercaya menghancurkan perahu dan mencemari udara dengan napas pembawa wabah yang menyebabkan penyakit yang disebut febbre gialla.

Banyak legenda bersepakat bahwa pembunuhan naga itu bertepatan dengan pengeringan danau. Satu tradisi menyebut ia lahir dari daging busuk panglima Ezzelino III da Romano. Sebagian sumber rakyat menghubungkan pengeringan danau dengan Santo Kristoforus atau Federico Barbarossa, sedangkan versi yang paling memikat menyebut leluhur keluarga Visconti membunuh naga itu lalu memakai ular besar dengan anak di mulutnya sebagai lambang.

Legenda itu sudah dibicarakan pada tahun 1100 oleh biarawan Sabbio dalam memoarnya tentang Lodi, dan sebuah fresko di serambi gereja San Marco di Milan menggambarkan naga itu di latar danau. Sebuah kelurahan di Cassano d'Adda dinamai Taranta merujuk legenda tersebut, dan beberapa gereja konon menyimpan rusuk naga yang oleh naturalis Enrico Caffi diidentifikasi sebagai milik mamut. Dalam budaya populer, pembunuhan tarantasio membuka novel Donna di spade (1991) dan legenda ini disebut mengilhami logo Eni.
long_description.en:
Tarantasio is a legendary dragon that terrorized the inhabitants of the ancient, hypothetical Lake Gerundo near Lodi in Lombardy. In popular legend he is also known as Tarànto and fed above all on children. He was believed to wreck boats and foul the air with a pestilential breath that caused a disease called febbre gialla.

Many legends agree that the dragon's killing coincided with the draining of the lake. One tradition says he was born from the putrefying flesh of the commander Ezzelino III da Romano. Some popular sources link the draining to Saint Christopher or Frederick Barbarossa, while the most evocative version has the progenitor of the Visconti kill the dragon and adopt the biscione with a child in its mouth as an emblem.

The legend is already spoken of in 1100 by the monk Sabbio in his memoirs on Lodi, and a fresco in the cloister of the church of San Marco in Milan shows the dragon against the lake. A hamlet of Cassano d'Adda is named Taranta after the legend, and some churches are said to preserve dragon ribs, one of which the naturalist Enrico Caffi identified as a mammoth's. In popular culture the killing of a tarantasio opens the novel Donna di spade (1991), and the legend is said to have inspired the Eni logo.

statement.id: Konon beberapa tulang rusuk naga masih disimpan, antara lain di gereja San Bassiano di Pizzighettone, Cremona; salah satu rusuk itu diteliti naturalis Enrico Caffi pada abad ke-19, yang mengidentifikasinya sebagai milik mamut.
statement.en: Some ribs of the dragon are still preserved, among others at the church of San Bassiano in Pizzighettone, Cremona; one of the ribs was studied by the naturalist Enrico Caffi in the 19th century, who identified it as belonging to a mammoth.

statement.en: The killing of a tarantasio dragon (which in the story denotes a species rather than a single individual) is the opening episode of the fantasy novel Donna di spade by Giuseppe Pederiali, published in 1991.

short_description.id: Tigmamanukan adalah burung pertanda dalam kepercayaan Tagalog; arah terbang dan kicauannya menjadi pertanda perjalanan, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala.
short_description.en: The tigmamanukan is an omen bird of Tagalog belief; the direction of its flight and its song served as omens for journeys, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda. Di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya. Sebelum Kristenisasi, ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.

Sebuah teks lama menyebut burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon: bila bertemu burung itu, atau ular, tikus, atau orang yang bersin, orang segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda celaka, terutama saat burung itu berkicau. Kicaunya punya dua bentuk, satu dianggap pertanda buruk dan yang lain pertanda baik sehingga perjalanan dilanjutkan.

Menurut kamus bahasa Tagalog tahun 1613 karya San Buenaventura, bila tigmamanukan terbang melintas ke kanan di awal perjalanan, perjalanan itu akan berhasil; bila ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali, dan tanda itu disebut labay. Dikatakan pula bahwa pemburu yang menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil memohon agar burung itu berkicau di kanan.

Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan, Tigmamanukan membuka bambu tempat laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda, keluar; dikatakan ia dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut wujud burung Amihan yang mematuk bambu. Sebagian penjelajah Barat awal mengira burung ini burung biru peri (genus Irena), dan kebanyakan sumber sepakat bahwa ia berwarna biru; di Filipina kuno banyak burung pertanda lain juga berbulu biru.
long_description.en:
In Philippine mythology, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan to be an omen bird. Among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it. Before Christianisation it was believed to be sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

An early text mentions a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree: on meeting it, or a serpent, a rat or someone who sneezed, people returned home at once, taking it as an augury of harm, especially when the bird sang. Its song had two forms, one taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, after which the journey went on.

According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, if a tigmamanukan flew across the path to the right at the start of a journey the expedition would succeed, and if it flew to the left the travelers would surely never return; the sign was called labay. It was also said that a hunter who trapped a tigmamanukan cut its beak and released it, asking it to sing on the right.

In at least one telling of the creation myth, the Tigmamanukan opened the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged; it is said to have been named Manaul by Bathala, while other sources say it was Amihan's bird form that pecked the bamboo. Some early Western explorers took the bird to be a fairy bluebird (genus Irena), and most sources agree it was blue; many other omen birds of ancient Philippines were also blue-plumaged.

short_description.id: Tigmamanukan adalah burung pertanda dalam kepercayaan Tagalog; arah terbang dan kicauannya menjadi pertanda perjalanan, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala.
short_description.en: The tigmamanukan is an omen bird of Tagalog belief; the direction of its flight and its song served as omens for journeys, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda. Di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya. Sebelum Kristenisasi, ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan to be an omen bird. Among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it. Before Christianisation it was believed to be sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

long_description.id: Sebuah teks lama menyebut burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon: bila bertemu burung itu, atau ular, tikus, atau orang yang bersin, orang segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda celaka, terutama saat burung itu berkicau. Kicaunya punya dua bentuk, satu dianggap pertanda buruk dan yang lain pertanda baik sehingga perjalanan dilanjutkan.
long_description.en: An early text mentions a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree: on meeting it, or a serpent, a rat or someone who sneezed, people returned home at once, taking it as an augury of harm, especially when the bird sang. Its song had two forms, one taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, after which the journey went on.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus bahasa Tagalog tahun 1613 karya San Buenaventura, bila tigmamanukan terbang melintas ke kanan di awal perjalanan, perjalanan itu akan berhasil; bila ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali, dan tanda itu disebut labay. Dikatakan pula bahwa pemburu yang menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil memohon agar burung itu berkicau di kanan.
long_description.en: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, if a tigmamanukan flew across the path to the right at the start of a journey the expedition would succeed, and if it flew to the left the travelers would surely never return; the sign was called labay. It was also said that a hunter who trapped a tigmamanukan cut its beak and released it, asking it to sing on the right.

long_description.id: Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan, Tigmamanukan membuka bambu tempat laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda, keluar; dikatakan ia dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut wujud burung Amihan yang mematuk bambu. Sebagian penjelajah Barat awal mengira burung ini burung biru peri (genus Irena), dan kebanyakan sumber sepakat bahwa ia berwarna biru; di Filipina kuno banyak burung pertanda lain juga berbulu biru.
long_description.en: In at least one telling of the creation myth, the Tigmamanukan opened the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged; it is said to have been named Manaul by Bathala, while other sources say it was Amihan's bird form that pecked the bamboo. Some early Western explorers took the bird to be a fairy bluebird (genus Irena), and most sources agree it was blue; many other omen birds of ancient Philippines were also blue-plumaged.

short_description.id: Kucing bersayap adalah felid dengan sayap seperti burung atau kelelawar, tema seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah. Kucing domestik bersayap kini dikenal sebagai legenda urban dengan penjelasan medis.
short_description.en: The winged cat is a feline with bird-like or bat-like wings, a theme in art and legend since prehistory. Winged domestic cats are now known as an urban legend with medical explanations.

long_description.id:
Kucing bersayap adalah felid yang digambarkan bersayap seperti burung, kelelawar, atau makhluk terbang lain. Menurut sumber pertama, tema ini sudah ada dalam seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah, terutama pada gambaran kucing besar bersayap elang di Eurasia dan Afrika Utara.

Singa bersayap dan pantherin bersayap lain umum dalam seni religius dan mitologis bangsa Sumeria, Mesopotamia lain, Akkadia, Persia, dan Skithia. Aq Bars, macan tutul salju bersayap, adalah lambang berasal Turkic dan Bulgar kuno. Dalam Kitab Daniel, binatang pertama dalam penglihatan tentang binatang dari laut menyerupai singa bersayap, dan dalam Kekristenan abad pertengahan setan kadang digambarkan sebagai kucing bersayap kelelawar. Dalam gambaran Nordik, kucing-kucing dewi Freyja juga bersayap.

Kepercayaan akan kucing domestik bersayap bertahan sebagai legenda urban. Penampakannya dijelaskan secara medis oleh rambut kusut, kulit longgar, atau anggota tubuh tambahan di dekat bahu yang mengepak saat kucing berlari, dan tidak ada bukti sayap sungguhan seperti sayap burung atau kelelawar.

Laporan tertua yang diketahui berasal dari Henry David Thoreau, yang mencatat kunjungan pada Juni 1842 ke seekor kucing yang sedang berburu di hutan. Menurut pemiliknya, bulu kucing itu menebal dan memipih di sisi tubuhnya pada musim dingin; sebagian orang mengira ia sebagian tupai terbang atau hewan liar lain. Artikel berbahasa Jepang juga mencatat penangkapan hewan berwajah kucing yang bersayap pada 1826 di Jepang.
long_description.en:
The winged cat is a feline depicted with wings like those of a bird, a bat or another flying creature. According to the first source, the theme goes back to prehistory in art and legend, especially in pictures of large cats bearing eagle wings across Eurasia and North Africa.

Winged lions and other winged pantherines are common in the religious and mythological art of the Sumerians, other Mesopotamians, Akkadians, Persians and Scythians. Aq Bars, the winged snow leopard, is a symbol of ancient Turkic and Bulgar origin. In the Book of Daniel, the opening beast of the vision of creatures rising from the sea looks like a winged lion, and in medieval Christianity demons were sometimes depicted as bat-winged cats. In the Norse imagery the cats of the goddess Freyja are also winged.

Belief in winged domestic cats persists as an urban legend. Sightings are explained medically by matted hair, loose skin or extra limbs near the shoulders that flap as the cat runs, and there is no evidence of true bird-like or bat-like wings.

The earliest known report comes from Henry David Thoreau, who recorded a visit in June 1842 to a cat that was out hunting in the woods. According to its owner, the cat's fur grew thick and flattened along its sides in winter; some thought it partly a flying squirrel or other wild animal. The Japanese-language article also records the capture of a winged, cat-faced animal in Japan in 1826.

short_description.id: Balāha adalah kuda terbang dalam legenda Buddha, wujud bodhisattva yang menyelamatkan para pedagang dari pulau rakshasa.
short_description.en: Balāha is a flying horse of Buddhist legend, a bodhisattva's form that rescues merchants from an island of rākshasas.

long_description.id:
Balāha adalah kuda terbang legendaris dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Buddha, dengan versi berbahasa Tionghoa dan India. Seorang bodhisattva datang dalam wujud kuda terbang yang dapat berbicara, sering putih, kadang bersayap atau berkepala gagak, untuk menyelamatkan para pedagang yang terdampar di pulau rakshasa pemakan manusia. Para pedagang berpegangan pada sisinya seperti pada kapal untuk menyeberangi laut.

Dalam Valāhassa Jātaka kuda itu calon Buddha sendiri; versi lebih baru mengaitkannya dengan Avalokiteshvara, dan pulau itu menjadi Sri Lanka.

Teks Jātaka 196 menggambarkan Bodhisatta sebagai kuda terbang putih berparuh seperti gagak, berambut seperti rumput muñja, yang mampu terbang. Kisahnya berlatar pulau Ceylon, tempat kota Yakkha Sirīsavatthu dihuni para Yakkhini. Kuda itu tiga kali bertanya dengan suara manusia siapa yang ingin pulang, lalu membawa dua ratus lima puluh pedagang ke negeri mereka. Di akhir kisah sang Guru menyatakan bahwa ia sendiri adalah kuda itu.

Victor Goloubew (1927) menyebut kelompok arca kuda terbang Balâha sebagai yang paling mengesankan di antara arca dari penggalian Nâk Pân di Angkor, dan menafsirkan kuda batu itu sebagai lambang makhluk yang mendambakan pembebasan.
long_description.en:
Balāha is a legendary flying horse of Buddhist mythology and folklore, with versions in Chinese and Indian languages. A bodhisattva comes in the form of a flying horse that can speak, often white, sometimes winged or crow-headed, to deliver merchants stranded on an island of man-eating rakshasas. The merchants cling to its sides as to a ship to cross the sea.

In the Valāhassa Jātaka the horse is the future Buddha himself; a more recent version attributes the transformation to Avalokiteshvara, and the island becomes the future Ceylon.

The text of Jātaka 196 describes the Bodhisatta as a white flying horse beaked like a crow, with hair like muñja grass, able to fly through the air. The story is set on the island of Ceylon, where the Yakkha town Sirīsavatthu is peopled by Yakkhinis. The horse thrice asks in human speech who wants to go home, then conveys two hundred and fifty merchants to their own country. At the end the Teacher declares that he himself was the horse.

Victor Goloubew (1927) calls the flying-horse group Balâha the most remarkable of the sculptures from the Nâk Pân excavations at Angkor, and interprets the stone horse as a symbol of beings aspiring to deliverance.

short_description.id: Lembuswana adalah satwa mitologi rakyat Kutai yang berwujud lembu keemasan bermahkota, berbelalai gajah, bersayap garuda, bertaji ayam, dan bersisik naga, lambang Kerajaan Kutai hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara.
short_description.en: The lembuswana is a mythical beast of the Kutai people, a golden crowned bull with an elephant's trunk, garuda wings, rooster spurs and dragon scales, emblem of the Kutai kingdom through the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara.

long_description.id:
Lembuswana adalah satwa dalam mitologi kuno rakyat Kutai yang kemudian menjadi lambang sejak masa Kerajaan Kutai, kerajaan Hindu tertua, hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. Ia dianggap suci karena dipercaya sebagai tunggangan Dewa Wishnu, dan menurut artikel jurnal, ia merupakan simbol keperkasaan dan kekuasaan Raja Kutai. Namanya disebut berasal dari bahasa Sansekerta: lembu, yang berarti sapi, dan svarna, yang berarti emas; arsip keluarga yang dikutip sebuah jurnal menafsirkan "lembu" dan "suwana" dengan makna lain.

Lembuswana berwarna keemasan dan berwujud lembu yang bermahkota, berbelalai dan bergading seperti gajah, bersayap seperti garuda, berkuku dan bertaji seperti ayam jantan, serta bersisik seperti naga. Penggambaran lain menyebutnya bertaring seperti harimau dan bertubuh seperti kuda. Hewan ini diyakini memiliki kekuatan luar biasa dan dapat hidup di darat, air, maupun udara; dalam riwayat yang dikutip jurnal, ia dapat terbang secepat kilat di angkasa. Menurut kepercayaan masyarakat, ia adalah kendaraan Batara Guru sekaligus kendaraan spiritual Raja Mulawarman. Seorang penulis karya tugas akhir menyimpulkan bahwa ia adalah tunggangan sakral para dewa yang patuh, abdi yang setia, serta kuat dan perkasa.

Lembuswana dipercaya menjaga Sungai Mahakam dari bahaya, memastikan airnya tetap bersih, dan membantu nelayan menemukan tempat menangkap ikan. Legenda kemunculannya dari dasar sungai dihubungkan dengan kelahiran Putri Karang Melenuyang. Dalam De Kroniek van Koetai, seorang anak berbaring di atas gong yang dijunjung seekor naga, dan naga itu dijunjung Lembusuana yang berdiri di atas batu. Dalam cerita rakyat Kutai, naga itu disebut Ular Lembu, dan peristiwa itu digelar kembali setiap tahun pada upacara Erau.

Lembuswana memiliki falsafah Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso, yaitu bahwa seseorang seharusnya bersifat mulia sebagai pengayom rakyat; mahkotanya dapat diartikan sebagai kekuasaan dan belalainya menggambarkan Dewa Ganesha. Menurut Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana diukir berwarna di atas kulit kerbau yang disimpan di keraton Kutai sebagai pusaka. Patung lembuswana berdiri di halaman depan Museum Mulawarman di Tenggarong, tempat sepasang arca Lembusuana dari gangsa keemasan juga dapat dilihat. Menurut sebuah artikel jurnal, patung-patung lembuswana dibuat di Birma pada 1850, lalu sampai di istana Kutai Kartanegara pada 1900. Patung lembuswana raksasa karya I Nyoman Nuarta juga berdiri di Pulau Kumala; konon patung duduk di sana dianggap merusak filosofi Lembusuana yang berdiri gagah berani.
long_description.en:
The lembuswana is a creature of the ancient mythology of the Kutai people that became an emblem from the time of the Kutai kingdom, the oldest Hindu kingdom, to the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. It is considered sacred because it is believed to be the mount of the god Vishnu, and according to a journal article it is a symbol of the might and power of the King of Kutai. Its name is said to come from Sanskrit: lembu, meaning cow, and svarna, meaning gold; a family archive cited in a journal reads "lembu" and "suwana" differently.

The lembuswana is golden and bull-shaped, wearing a crown, with an elephant's trunk and tusks, wings like a garuda, a rooster's claws and spurs and scales like a dragon. Other descriptions give it fangs like a tiger and a body like a horse. The animal is believed to have extraordinary power and to be able to live on land, in water and in the air; in the account cited in a journal it can fly as fast as lightning through the sky. By popular belief it is the vehicle of Batara Guru and the spiritual vehicle of King Mulawarman. The author of a final-project paper concludes that it is a sacred steed of the gods, docile, a faithful servant, strong and mighty.

The lembuswana is believed to guard the Mahakam River from danger, keep its water clean and help fishermen find fishing spots. The legend of its emergence from the river bed is tied to the birth of Princess Karang Melenuyang. In De Kroniek van Koetai, a child lies on a gong carried by a dragon, and the dragon is carried by Lembusuana standing on a rock. In Kutai folk tales the dragon is called Ular Lembu, and the event is re-enacted every year at the Erau ceremony.

The lembuswana carries the philosophy Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso: one should be noble as protector of the people; its crown can be read as power and its trunk represents the god Ganesha. According to Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana was carved in colour on buffalo hide kept in the Kutai palace as a heirloom. A lembuswana statue stands in front of the Mulawarman Museum in Tenggarong, where a pair of golden-bronze Lembusuana statues can also be seen. A journal article says the statues were made in Burma in 1850 and reached the Kutai Kartanegara palace in 1900. A giant lembuswana statue by I Nyoman Nuarta also stands on Pulau Kumala; it is said that a seated statue there was seen as damaging the philosophy of Lembusuana, who stands bravely.

short_description.id: Lembuswana adalah satwa mitologi rakyat Kutai yang berwujud lembu keemasan bermahkota, berbelalai gajah, bersayap garuda, bertaji ayam, dan bersisik naga, lambang Kerajaan Kutai hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara.
short_description.en: The lembuswana is a mythical beast of the Kutai people, a golden crowned bull with an elephant's trunk, garuda wings, rooster spurs and dragon scales, emblem of the Kutai kingdom through the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara.

long_description.id: Lembuswana adalah satwa dalam mitologi kuno rakyat Kutai yang kemudian menjadi lambang sejak masa Kerajaan Kutai, kerajaan Hindu tertua, hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. Ia dianggap suci karena dipercaya sebagai tunggangan Dewa Wishnu, dan menurut artikel jurnal, ia merupakan simbol keperkasaan dan kekuasaan Raja Kutai. Namanya disebut berasal dari bahasa Sansekerta: lembu, yang berarti sapi, dan svarna, yang berarti emas; arsip keluarga yang dikutip sebuah jurnal menafsirkan "lembu" dan "suwana" dengan makna lain.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is a creature of the ancient mythology of the Kutai people that became an emblem from the time of the Kutai kingdom, the oldest Hindu kingdom, to the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. It is considered sacred because it is believed to be the mount of the god Vishnu, and according to a journal article it is a symbol of the might and power of the King of Kutai. Its name is said to come from Sanskrit: lembu, meaning cow, and svarna, meaning gold; a family archive cited in a journal reads "lembu" and "suwana" differently.

long_description.id: Lembuswana berwarna keemasan dan berwujud lembu yang bermahkota, berbelalai dan bergading seperti gajah, bersayap seperti garuda, berkuku dan bertaji seperti ayam jantan, serta bersisik seperti naga. Penggambaran lain menyebutnya bertaring seperti harimau dan bertubuh seperti kuda. Hewan ini diyakini memiliki kekuatan luar biasa dan dapat hidup di darat, air, maupun udara; dalam riwayat yang dikutip jurnal, ia dapat terbang secepat kilat di angkasa. Menurut kepercayaan masyarakat, ia adalah kendaraan Batara Guru sekaligus kendaraan spiritual Raja Mulawarman. Seorang penulis karya tugas akhir menyimpulkan bahwa ia adalah tunggangan sakral para dewa yang patuh, abdi yang setia, serta kuat dan perkasa.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is golden and bull-shaped, wearing a crown, with an elephant's trunk and tusks, wings like a garuda, a rooster's claws and spurs and scales like a dragon. Other descriptions give it fangs like a tiger and a body like a horse. The animal is believed to have extraordinary power and to be able to live on land, in water and in the air; in the account cited in a journal it can fly as fast as lightning through the sky. By popular belief it is the vehicle of Batara Guru and the spiritual vehicle of King Mulawarman. The author of a final-project paper concludes that it is a sacred steed of the gods, docile, a faithful servant, strong and mighty.

long_description.id: Lembuswana dipercaya menjaga Sungai Mahakam dari bahaya, memastikan airnya tetap bersih, dan membantu nelayan menemukan tempat menangkap ikan. Legenda kemunculannya dari dasar sungai dihubungkan dengan kelahiran Putri Karang Melenuyang. Dalam De Kroniek van Koetai, seorang anak berbaring di atas gong yang dijunjung seekor naga, dan naga itu dijunjung Lembusuana yang berdiri di atas batu. Dalam cerita rakyat Kutai, naga itu disebut Ular Lembu, dan peristiwa itu digelar kembali setiap tahun pada upacara Erau.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is believed to guard the Mahakam River from danger, keep its water clean and help fishermen find fishing spots. The legend of its emergence from the river bed is tied to the birth of Princess Karang Melenuyang. In De Kroniek van Koetai, a child lies on a gong carried by a dragon, and the dragon is carried by Lembusuana standing on a rock. In Kutai folk tales the dragon is called Ular Lembu, and the event is re-enacted every year at the Erau ceremony.

long_description.id: Lembuswana memiliki falsafah Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso, yaitu bahwa seseorang seharusnya bersifat mulia sebagai pengayom rakyat; mahkotanya dapat diartikan sebagai kekuasaan dan belalainya menggambarkan Dewa Ganesha. Menurut Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana diukir berwarna di atas kulit kerbau yang disimpan di keraton Kutai sebagai pusaka. Patung lembuswana berdiri di halaman depan Museum Mulawarman di Tenggarong, tempat sepasang arca Lembusuana dari gangsa keemasan juga dapat dilihat. Menurut sebuah artikel jurnal, patung-patung lembuswana dibuat di Birma pada 1850, lalu sampai di istana Kutai Kartanegara pada 1900. Patung lembuswana raksasa karya I Nyoman Nuarta juga berdiri di Pulau Kumala; konon patung duduk di sana dianggap merusak filosofi Lembusuana yang berdiri gagah berani.
long_description.en: The lembuswana carries the philosophy Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso: one should be noble as protector of the people; its crown can be read as power and its trunk represents the god Ganesha. According to Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana was carved in colour on buffalo hide kept in the Kutai palace as a heirloom. A lembuswana statue stands in front of the Mulawarman Museum in Tenggarong, where a pair of golden-bronze Lembusuana statues can also be seen. A journal article says the statues were made in Burma in 1850 and reached the Kutai Kartanegara palace in 1900. A giant lembuswana statue by I Nyoman Nuarta also stands on Pulau Kumala; it is said that a seated statue there was seen as damaging the philosophy of Lembusuana, who stands bravely.

statement.en: The lembuswana is a creature of the ancient mythology of the Kutai people, an emblem from the Kutai kingdom, the oldest Hindu kingdom, to the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura; it is considered sacred because it is believed to be the mount of the god Vishnu.
