short_description.id: Elang Kaukasus adalah elang raksasa, dalam satu versi anak Tifon dan Ekhidna, yang diutus Zeus memakan hati Prometheus setiap hari hingga dibunuh Herakles.
short_description.en: The Caucasian Eagle is a gigantic eagle, in one version child of Typhon and Echidna, sent by Zeus to eat Prometheus's liver every day until Herakles killed it.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah elang, anak Tifon dan Ekhidna. Setelah Zeus merantai Prometheus di tebing pegunungan Kaukasus, setiap hari seekor elang datang memakan hatinya. Elang itu digambarkan sebagai elang raksasa yang diutus Zeus sebagai hukuman karena Prometheus mencuri api dari para dewa.
long_description.en: In Greek mythology the Caucasian Eagle is an eagle, child of Typhon and Echidna. After Zeus chained Prometheus to a cliff in the Caucasus, an eagle came every day to eat his liver. It is described as a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus as punishment for Prometheus stealing fire from the gods.

long_description.id: Menurut satu sumber, elang itu juga digambarkan sebagai automaton perunggu buatan Hephaistos. Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos, hati Prometheus tumbuh kembali setiap malam sebanyak yang dimakan burung itu sepanjang hari. Dalam Prometheus Bound karya Aeschylus, elang itu disebut anjing bersayap Zeus yang mencabik tubuh Prometheus dan berpesta atas hatinya sepanjang hari, sedangkan dalam Argonautica karya Apollonius Rhodius bentuknya bukan bentuk burung biasa, dengan bulu sayap panjang yang naik turun seperti deretan dayung.
long_description.en: According to one source the eagle is also described as a bronze automaton built by Hephaistos. In Hesiod's Theogony Prometheus' liver grew as much again each night as the bird devoured in the day. In Aeschylus' Prometheus Bound the eagle is the winged hound of Zeus that tears Prometheus' body and feasts upon his liver all day long, while in Apollonius Rhodius' Argonautica its form is not that of an ordinary bird, its long quill-feathers rising and falling like a bank of oars.

long_description.id: Herakles menjatuhkan elang itu dengan hujan anak panah ketika ia datang membebaskan Prometheus.
long_description.en: Herakles felled the eagle with a volley of arrows when he came to free Prometheus.

description.id: Elang itu memakan hati Prometheus yang memulihkan diri; dalam Hesiodos hati itu tumbuh kembali setiap malam sebanyak yang dimakan sepanjang hari.
description.en: The eagle fed on Prometheus's regenerating liver; in Hesiod the liver grew back each night as much as was eaten in the day.

description.id: Herakles menjatuhkan elang itu dengan hujan anak panah; dalam Hesiodos ia membunuh burung itu.
description.en: Herakles felled the eagle with a volley of arrows; in Hesiod he slew the bird.

claims.quote: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah seekor burung elang yang merupakan anak dari Tifon dan Ekhidna.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah elang anak Tifon dan Ekhidna.
statement.en: In Greek mythology, the Caucasian Eagle is an eagle, child of Typhon and Echidna.

claims.quote: Zeus merantai Prometheus di sebuah tebing di pegunungan Kaukasus dan setiap hari akan datang seekor elang yang memakan hati Prometheus.

statement.id: Zeus merantai Prometheus di tebing pegunungan Kaukasus, dan setiap hari seekor elang datang memakan hatinya.
statement.en: Zeus chained Prometheus to a Caucasus cliff, and every day an eagle came to eat his liver.

claims.quote: THE AETOS KAUKASIOS (Caucasian Eagle) was a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus to feed upon the ever-regenerating liver of the Titan Prometheus after he was chained to a peak of the Kaukasos (Caucasus) Mountains as punishment for stealing fire from the gods.

statement.id: Aetos Kaukasios (Elang Kaukasus) adalah elang raksasa yang diutus Zeus untuk memakan hati Titan Prometheus yang terus memulihkan diri setelah ia dirantai di puncak pegunungan Kaukasos (Kaukasus) sebagai hukuman karena mencuri api dari para dewa.
statement.en: The Aetos Kaukasios (Caucasian Eagle) was a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus to feed upon the ever-regenerating liver of the Titan Prometheus after he was chained to a peak of the Kaukasos (Caucasus) Mountains as punishment for stealing fire from the gods.

claims.quote: The eagle was variously described as a bronze automaton constructed by the god Hephaistos (Hephaestus), or as a fell creature spawned by the drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).

statement.id: Elang itu digambarkan beragam: sebagai automaton perunggu buatan dewa Hephaistos (Hephaestus), atau sebagai makhluk ganas yang dilahirkan drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).
statement.en: The eagle was variously described as a bronze automaton constructed by the god Hephaistos (Hephaestus), or as a fell creature spawned by the drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).

claims.quote: When Herakles set out to free Prometheus from his bonds, he felled the eagle with a volley of arrows.

statement.id: Ketika Herakles berangkat membebaskan Prometheus dari belenggunya, ia menjatuhkan elang itu dengan hujan anak panah.
statement.en: When Herakles set out to free Prometheus from his bonds, he felled the eagle with a volley of arrows.

claims.quote: Hesiod, Theogony 507 ff (trans. Evelyn-White) ... Ready-witted Prometheus he [Zeus] bound with inextricable bonds, cruel chains ... set on him a long-winged eagle, which used to eat his immortal liver; but by night the liver grew as much again everyway as the long-winged bird devoured in the whole day. That bird Herakles (Heracles), the valiant son of shapely-ankled Alkmene (Alcmena), slew

statement.id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos (terjemahan Evelyn-White), seekor elang bersayap panjang yang biasa memakan hati abadi Prometheus ditempatkan padanya, tetapi pada malam hari hati itu tumbuh sebanyak yang dimakan burung itu sepanjang hari; burung itu dibunuh Herakles (Heracles), putra gagah Alkmene (Alcmena).
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony (trans. Evelyn-White), a long-winged eagle was set on Prometheus to eat his immortal liver, but by night the liver grew as much again as the bird devoured in the whole day; Herakles (Heracles), the valiant son of Alkmene (Alcmena), slew that bird.

claims.quote: Apollonius Rhodius, Argonautica 2. 1238 ff (trans. Rieu) ... They saw it in the afternoon flying high above the ship with a strident whirr. It was near the clouds, yet it made all their canvas quiver to its wings as it beat by. For its form was not that of an ordinary bird : the long quill-feathers of each wing rose and fell like a bank of polished oars.

statement.id: Dalam Argonautica karya Apollonius Rhodius (terjemahan Rieu), mereka melihat elang itu pada sore hari terbang tinggi di atas kapal dengan desing nyaring; ia dekat awan, tetapi sayapnya membuat seluruh layar mereka bergetar saat ia melintas. Bentuknya bukan bentuk burung biasa: bulu-bulu sayap panjangnya naik turun seperti deretan dayung yang digosok.
statement.en: In Apollonius Rhodius' Argonautica (trans. Rieu), they saw it in the afternoon flying high above the ship with a strident whirr; it was near the clouds, yet its wings made all their canvas quiver as it beat by. Its form was not that of an ordinary bird: the long quill-feathers of each wing rose and fell like a bank of polished oars.

claims.quote: Aeschylus, Prometheus Bound 1021 ff ... The winged hound of Zeus, the ravening eagle, coming an unbidden banqueter the whole day long, with savage appetite shall tear your body piecemeal into great rents and feast his fill upon your liver until it is black with gnawing.

statement.id: Dalam Prometheus Bound karya Aeschylus, anjing bersayap Zeus, elang yang rakus, datang sebagai tamu tak diundang sepanjang hari, dengan nafsu buas akan mencabik tubuhmu sepotong-sepotong dan berpesta atas hatimu sampai menghitam karena dikoyak.
statement.en: In Aeschylus' Prometheus Bound, the winged hound of Zeus, the ravening eagle, comes an unbidden banqueter the whole day long and with savage appetite shall tear the body piecemeal into great rents and feast his fill upon the liver until it is black with gnawing.

short_description.id: Katak puru raksasa adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo.
short_description.en: The giant toad is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections.

long_description.id:
Katak puru raksasa (Ōgama) adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo. Cerita Ehon Hyaku Monogatari menempatkannya di pegunungan Suō, dan menyebut panjangnya sekitar 2,4 meter. Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi dan memakan ular pada musim panas.

Kisah lain, dari kumpulan Hokuetsu Kidan, menuturkan bahwa benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap; diduga itu katak puru raksasa. Katak puru raksasa juga muncul dalam lakon kabuki tahun 1804 dan dalam gambar yang menunjukkan Jiraiya menungganginya atau katak itu muncul di belakang Takiyasha-hime.

Pada sekitar Meiji 33, surat kabar Osaka memberitakan katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda dan sebuah tiruan katak ditampilkan di kuil. Tradisinya ditafsirkan berasal dari hewan liar pegunungan yang bisa sangat besar, serta dari anggapan bahwa katak menyedot serangga dan jiwa manusia.
long_description.en:
The giant toad (Ōgama) is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections. An Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tale places it in the mountains of Suō and gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres. It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath and to eat snakes in summer.

Another tale, from the Hokuetsu Kidan collection, relates that the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished; it was surmised to be a giant toad. Giant toads also appear in an 1804 kabuki play and in pictures showing Jiraiya riding one or one appearing behind Takiyasha-hime.

Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported on the giant toad of Mount Shinoda and a model toad was shown at a shrine. The tradition is interpreted as stemming from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains and from the notion that toads suck in insects and human spirit.

cultural_context.id: Para pengkaji menafsirkan bahwa tradisi katak puru raksasa muncul dari hewan liar pegunungan yang kadang sangat besar, dan bahwa katak dipandang gaib karena tampak menyedot serangga ke mulutnya.
cultural_context.en: Interpretations hold that giant-toad traditions arose from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains, and that toads were seen as uncanny because they appear to suck insects into their mouths.

description.id: Dari mulutnya ia mengembuskan hawa seperti pelangi; burung dan serangga yang terkena hawa itu terisap ke mulutnya, dan pada musim panas ia memakan ular.
description.en: It breathes out a rainbow-like vapor from its mouth; birds and insects touched by it are drawn into its mouth, and in summer it eats snakes.

role.id: Katak puru raksasa yang tinggal di pegunungan Iwakuni.
role.en: A giant toad living deep in the mountains of Iwakuni.

summary.id: Menurut teks Ehon Hyaku Monogatari, ia tinggal jauh di pegunungan Gunung Iwakuni di Provinsi Suō dan panjangnya sekitar 2,4 meter. Gambar dalam buku itu menunjukkan katak ini memegang tombak, dan ada yang menyebut ia memakainya untuk menyerang orang.
summary.en: According to the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari text, it lives deep in the mountains of Iwakuni in Suō Province and is about 2.4 metres long. The illustration shows this toad holding a spear, and one view says it used the spear to attack people.

summary.en: The thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat is said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned; it then vanished without a trace, and it was surmised to have been a giant toad.

description.id: Tempat katak puru raksasa dalam Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tinggal jauh di pegunungan; kini Iwakuni, Prefektur Yamaguchi.
description.en: Where the giant toad of the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari lives deep in the mountains; now Iwakuni, Yamaguchi Prefecture.

claims_provenance.quote: 『絵本百物語』本文によれば、周防国の岩国山（現・山口県岩国市）の山奥に住む大蝦蟇で、体長は約8尺（約2.4メートル）。

claim.id: Cerita tersebut memberinya panjang sekitar 2,4 meter.
claim.en: That tale gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres.

claim.id: Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi.
claim.en: It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath.

claims_provenance.quote: 口から虹のような気を吐き、この気に触れた鳥や虫たちを口の中へと吸い込み、夏には蛇を食べるとある。

claim.id: Tradisi tentang katak puru sebesar itu dianggap muncul karena hewan liar yang hidup di pegunungan angker kadang jauh lebih besar daripada hewan di luar.
claim.en: Traditions of such giant toads are thought to have arisen because wild animals living in uncanny mountains can be much larger than those found in ordinary outdoor places.

claims_provenance.quote: 北陸地方の奇談集『北越奇談』などに見られる巨大なガマガエルの怪異。 妖山中に棲息する野生動物は通常の野外のものよりもずっと巨大なものもあることから、このような巨大なガマの伝承が生まれたと考えられている。

claim.id: Ada tafsiran bahwa katak puru dipandang sebagai yōkai karena cara katak menangkap serangga dengan lidah panjang tampak seperti serangga terisap ke mulutnya, sehingga katak dan katak puru dianggap punya kekuatan gaib seperti menyedot jiwa manusia.
claim.en: There is an interpretation that toads were regarded as yōkai because the way a frog catches insects with its long tongue looks as if the insects are sucked into its mouth, so frogs and toads came to be thought to have uncanny powers such as sucking the spirit from people.

claims_provenance.quote: ガマガエルが妖怪視されたことについては、カエルが長い舌で虫などを捕える様子が、あたかも虫がカエルの口の中に吸い込まれるようにも見えるため、こうしたカエルやガマが人間の精気を吸うなどの怪異のあるものと考えられたとの解釈もある。

claim.id: Dalam satu kisah, benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk dikatakan membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap tanpa bekas; diduga itu katak puru raksasa dan tonjolan yang dikira batu adalah kutil katak.
claim.en: In one tale, the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita had been sitting was said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished without a trace; it was surmised to have been a giant toad and the bumps taken for rock to have been its warts.

claims_provenance.quote:
「気づかなかったか? 貴行が先ほどまで乗っていたものが、火のように赤い目玉を開き、口をあけてあくびをしたのだ」と恐れながら答えた。
再び2人が元の場所へ戻ってみたところ、藤田の乗っていた岩とおぼしきものは跡形もなく消え失せていた。あれは岩ではなく大蝦蟇であり、突起と思ったものは蝦蟇のイボだったと推測されたという。

claim.id: Pada bulan ketujuh Kyōwa 4 (Agustus 1804), sebuah katak puru raksasa muncul dalam lakon "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" karya Tsuruya Nanboku yang dibintangi Onoe Matsusuke generasi pertama di Teater Kawarazaki, Edo, dan mendapat sambutan baik.
claim.en: In the seventh month of Kyōwa 4 (August 1804), a giant toad appeared in "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" by Tsuruya Nanboku, starring the first Onoe Matsusuke, at the Kawarazaki Theater in Edo, and was well received.

claims_provenance.quote: 享和4年7月（1804年8月）には江戸河原崎座で鶴屋南北作、初代尾上松助主演『天竺徳兵衛韓噺』（天竺徳兵衛）にて大蝦蟇が登場し好評を博した。

claim.id: Sekitar Meiji 33, sebuah surat kabar Osaka memberitakan "katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda" setiap hari; pada musim panas itu, sebuah tiruan katak sebesar manusia dengan mata besar bersinar di lembah rimbun dipamerkan di kuil di Setomono-chō (陶器神社) dan ditonton banyak orang.
claim.en: Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported daily on the "giant toad of Mount Shinoda"; that summer, a model of a human-sized toad with glaring big eyes in a thick gorge was shown at the shrine in Setomono-chō (陶器神社) and crowds gathered.

claims_provenance.quote: 明治33年ころ、大阪毎日新聞が三面記事で「信田山の大蝦蟇」について連日報道した。その夏、瀬戸物町陶器神社に、うっそうとした渓谷に人間ほどの大きさの大蝦蟇が大目玉を光らせている、という作り物が登場し、観客が群がった。

short_description.en: The giant toad is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections.

long_description.id: Katak puru raksasa (Ōgama) adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo. Cerita Ehon Hyaku Monogatari menempatkannya di pegunungan Suō, dan menyebut panjangnya sekitar 2,4 meter. Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi dan memakan ular pada musim panas.
long_description.en: The giant toad (Ōgama) is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections. An Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tale places it in the mountains of Suō and gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres. It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath and to eat snakes in summer.

long_description.id: Kisah lain, dari kumpulan Hokuetsu Kidan, menuturkan bahwa benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap; diduga itu katak puru raksasa. Katak puru raksasa juga muncul dalam lakon kabuki tahun 1804 dan dalam gambar yang menunjukkan Jiraiya menungganginya atau katak itu muncul di belakang Takiyasha-hime.
long_description.en: Another tale, from the Hokuetsu Kidan collection, relates that the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished; it was surmised to be a giant toad. Giant toads also appear in an 1804 kabuki play and in pictures showing Jiraiya riding one or one appearing behind Takiyasha-hime.

long_description.id: Pada sekitar Meiji 33, surat kabar Osaka memberitakan katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda dan sebuah tiruan katak ditampilkan di kuil. Tradisinya ditafsirkan berasal dari hewan liar pegunungan yang bisa sangat besar, serta dari anggapan bahwa katak menyedot serangga dan jiwa manusia.
long_description.en: Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported on the giant toad of Mount Shinoda and a model toad was shown at a shrine. The tradition is interpreted as stemming from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains and from the notion that toads suck in insects and human spirit.

cultural_context.id: Para pengkaji menafsirkan bahwa tradisi katak puru raksasa muncul dari hewan liar pegunungan yang kadang sangat besar, dan bahwa katak dipandang gaib karena tampak menyedot serangga ke mulutnya.
cultural_context.en: Interpretations hold that giant-toad traditions arose from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains, and that toads were seen as uncanny because they appear to suck insects into their mouths.

description.en: It breathes out a rainbow-like vapor from its mouth; birds and insects touched by it are drawn into its mouth, and in summer it eats snakes.

summary.en: According to the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari text, it lives deep in the mountains of Iwakuni in Suō Province and is about 2.4 metres long. The illustration shows this toad holding a spear, and one view says it used the spear to attack people.

summary.en: The thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat is said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned; it then vanished without a trace, and it was surmised to have been a giant toad.

claims.quote: 大蝦蟇（おおがま）は、江戸時代の奇談集『絵本百物語』、北陸地方の奇談集『北越奇談』などに見られる巨大なガマガエルの怪異。

statement.id: Katak puru raksasa adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo.
statement.en: The giant toad is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections.

claims.quote: 『絵本百物語』本文によれば、周防国の岩国山（現・山口県岩国市）の山奥に住む大蝦蟇で、体長は約8尺（約2.4メートル）。

statement.id: Cerita Ehon Hyaku Monogatari menempatkannya di pegunungan Suō.
statement.en: An Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tale places it in the mountains of Suō.

claims.quote: 『絵本百物語』本文によれば、周防国の岩国山（現・山口県岩国市）の山奥に住む大蝦蟇で、体長は約8尺（約2.4メートル）。

statement.id: Cerita tersebut memberinya panjang sekitar 2,4 meter.
statement.en: That tale gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres.

claims.quote: 口から虹のような気を吐き、この気に触れた鳥や虫たちを口の中へと吸い込み、夏には蛇を食べるとある。

statement.id: Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi.
statement.en: It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath.

claims.quote: 北陸地方の奇談集『北越奇談』などに見られる巨大なガマガエルの怪異。 妖山中に棲息する野生動物は通常の野外のものよりもずっと巨大なものもあることから、このような巨大なガマの伝承が生まれたと考えられている。

statement.id: Tradisi tentang katak puru sebesar itu dianggap muncul karena hewan liar yang hidup di pegunungan angker kadang jauh lebih besar daripada hewan di luar.
statement.en: Traditions of such giant toads are thought to have arisen because wild animals living in uncanny mountains can be much larger than those found in ordinary outdoor places.

claims.quote: ガマガエルが妖怪視されたことについては、カエルが長い舌で虫などを捕える様子が、あたかも虫がカエルの口の中に吸い込まれるようにも見えるため、こうしたカエルやガマが人間の精気を吸うなどの怪異のあるものと考えられたとの解釈もある。

statement.id: Ada tafsiran bahwa katak puru dipandang sebagai yōkai karena cara katak menangkap serangga dengan lidah panjang tampak seperti serangga terisap ke mulutnya, sehingga katak dan katak puru dianggap punya kekuatan gaib seperti menyedot jiwa manusia.
statement.en: There is an interpretation that toads were regarded as yōkai because the way a frog catches insects with its long tongue looks as if the insects are sucked into its mouth, so frogs and toads came to be thought to have uncanny powers such as sucking the spirit from people.

claims.quote:
「気づかなかったか? 貴行が先ほどまで乗っていたものが、火のように赤い目玉を開き、口をあけてあくびをしたのだ」と恐れながら答えた。
再び2人が元の場所へ戻ってみたところ、藤田の乗っていた岩とおぼしきものは跡形もなく消え失せていた。あれは岩ではなく大蝦蟇であり、突起と思ったものは蝦蟇のイボだったと推測されたという。

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk dikatakan membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap tanpa bekas; diduga itu katak puru raksasa dan tonjolan yang dikira batu adalah kutil katak.
statement.en: In one tale, the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita had been sitting was said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished without a trace; it was surmised to have been a giant toad and the bumps taken for rock to have been its warts.

claims.quote: 享和4年7月（1804年8月）には江戸河原崎座で鶴屋南北作、初代尾上松助主演『天竺徳兵衛韓噺』（天竺徳兵衛）にて大蝦蟇が登場し好評を博した。

statement.id: Pada bulan ketujuh Kyōwa 4 (Agustus 1804), sebuah katak puru raksasa muncul dalam lakon "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" karya Tsuruya Nanboku yang dibintangi Onoe Matsusuke generasi pertama di Teater Kawarazaki, Edo, dan mendapat sambutan baik.
statement.en: In the seventh month of Kyōwa 4 (August 1804), a giant toad appeared in "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" by Tsuruya Nanboku, starring the first Onoe Matsusuke, at the Kawarazaki Theater in Edo, and was well received.

claims.quote: 明治33年ころ、大阪毎日新聞が三面記事で「信田山の大蝦蟇」について連日報道した。その夏、瀬戸物町陶器神社に、うっそうとした渓谷に人間ほどの大きさの大蝦蟇が大目玉を光らせている、という作り物が登場し、観客が群がった。

statement.id: Sekitar Meiji 33, sebuah surat kabar Osaka memberitakan "katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda" setiap hari; pada musim panas itu, sebuah tiruan katak sebesar manusia dengan mata besar bersinar di lembah rimbun dipamerkan di kuil di Setomono-chō (陶器神社) dan ditonton banyak orang.
statement.en: Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported daily on the "giant toad of Mount Shinoda"; that summer, a model of a human-sized toad with glaring big eyes in a thick gorge was shown at the shrine in Setomono-chō (陶器神社) and crowds gathered.

claims.quote: 著作者 一魁芳年 主題 児雷也;ジライヤ,大蝦蟇;オオガマ 内容記述 蝦蟇の妖術を使う児雷也が、大蝦蟇の上に乗っている。

statement.en: Nichibunken image database description: this work by Ikkai Yoshitoshi shows Jiraiya, who uses toad sorcery, riding on a giant toad.

short_description.id: Kukulkan adalah dewa ular berbulu dalam mitologi Maya, dikaitkan erat dengan Quetzalcoatl bangsa Aztec. Ia dianggap dewa pencipta dan pembawa hujan serta angin, dengan kuil besar di Chichen Itza.
short_description.en: Kukulkan is the feathered serpent deity of Maya mythology, closely related to the Aztec Quetzalcoatl. He was seen as a creator god who brought rain and winds, with a large temple at Chichen Itza.

long_description.id:
Kukulkan adalah dewa ular dalam mitologi Maya dan sangat berkaitan dengan dewa Qʼuqʼumatz dari bangsa Kʼicheʼ serta Quetzalcoatl dalam mitologi Aztec. Namanya berarti harfiah 'ular berbulu'. Ia juga diidentifikasi sebagai Quetzalcóatl oleh bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, sebagai Gucumatz oleh Maya Quiché di Guatemala, dan sebagai Ehecatl, dewa angin bangsa Huastec.

Dewa utama Maya Yucatec ini adalah dewa pencipta serta dewa hujan, angin, badai, dan kehidupan. Kuil-kuil terkemuka Kukulkan terdapat di situs arkeologi di semenanjung Yucatán, seperti Chichen Itza, Uxmal, dan Mayapan. El Castillo di Chichen Itza berfungsi sebagai kuilnya, dan upacara di puncaknya mencakup pengorbanan manusia.

Penggambaran ular berbulu hadir di budaya Mesoamerika lain. Meskipun sangat dimeksikanisasi, Kukulkan berakar pada bangsa Maya Periode Klasik, ketika ia dikenal sebagai Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, Ular Perang. Pemujaannya adalah agama Mesoamerika pertama yang melampaui sekat bahasa dan etnis lama dan memudahkan perdagangan damai, dan menyebar dari Chichen Itza hingga Dataran Tinggi Guatemala dan Belize utara.

Rujukan pada dewa ini bercampur dengan rujukan pada seorang tokoh historis bernama Kukulkan, pahlawan budaya yang menurut Maya Yucatec adalah penguasa atau pendeta dan datang ke atau mendirikan Chichen Itza pada abad ke-10. Dalam cerita rakyat modern, Kukulkan dituturkan sebagai ular bersayap yang berjalan di depan dewa hujan Chaac; bagi Maya Lacandon di Chiapas, ia adalah ular jahat peliharaan dewa matahari.
long_description.en:
Kukulkan is the serpent deity of Maya mythology, with close ties to Qʼuqʼumatz of the Kʼicheʼ and to Quetzalcoatl of Aztec mythology. His name literally means 'feathered snake'. The Toltecs and Aztecs identify him with Quetzalcóatl, the Quiché Maya of Guatemala with Gucumatz, and the Huastecs with Ehecatl, their wind god.

The chief god of the Yucatec Maya, he was a creator and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life. Major temples to Kukulkan stand at archaeological sites on the Yucatán Peninsula, including Chichen Itza, Uxmal and Mayapan. El Castillo at Chichen Itza served as his temple, and ceremonies at its summit included human sacrifices.

Images of the Feathered Serpent also occur in other Mesoamerican cultures. Though strongly Mexicanised, Kukulkan began among the Classic Period Maya, who knew him as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, the War Serpent. His cult was the first Mesoamerican religion to transcend the old linguistic and ethnic divisions and facilitated peaceful trade, and it spread from Chichen Itza as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.

References to the deity are confused with references to a historical figure named Kukulkan, a cultural hero who the Yucatec Maya believed was a ruler or priest and who came to or founded Chichen Itza in the 10th century. In modern folklore Kukulkan is told of as a winged serpent that travels ahead of the rain god Chaac; to the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas he is an evil snake, the pet of the sun god.

claim.id: Kukulcan adalah nama dewa ular berbulu dalam mitologi dan agama Mesoamerika, khususnya Maya Yucatec. Ia juga diidentifikasi sebagai dewa ular berbulu Quetzalcóatl oleh bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, sebagai Gucumatz oleh Maya Quiché di Guatemala, dan sebagai Ehecatl, dewa angin bangsa Huastec di Pesisir Teluk.
claim.en: Kukulcan is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular the Yucatec Maya; he is also identified as Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and as Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.

claims_provenance.quote: Kukulcan (pron. Koo-kool-kan) is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular, the Yucatec Maya. He is also identified as the feathered serpent god Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.

claim.id: Dewa utama Maya Yucatec, yang menetap di semenanjung Yucatan di utara Mesoamerika kuno, adalah ular berbulu Kukulcan, yang namanya berarti 'berbulu' (k'uk'ul) dan 'ular' (kan). Ia adalah dewa pencipta serta dewa hujan, angin, badai, dan kehidupan.
claim.en: The chief god of the Yucatec Maya, who settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica, was the feathered serpent Kukulcan, whose name means feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan); he was a creator god and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.

claims_provenance.quote: The Yucatec Maya were (and still are) speakers of the Yucatec language, and they settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica. Their chief god was the feathered serpent Kukulcan whose name means just that: feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan). He was a creator god, and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Kukulcan: The Feathered-Serpent God of Mesoamerica

claim.id: Kukulcan dan wujud-wujud lainnya dipersatukan oleh keyakinan bahwa masing-masing dianggap dewa pencipta dan pembawa hujan serta angin. Sang dewa terutama dikaitkan dengan Chichen Itza, tempat kuil besar dibangun untuk menghormatinya.
claim.en: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds; the god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza, where a large temple was built in his honour.

claims_provenance.quote: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are all unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds. The god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza where a large temple was built in his honour.

claim.id: Selain dewa Kukulcan, Maya Yucatec meyakini seorang pria bernama Kukulcan, pahlawan budaya yang berstatus penguasa atau pendeta, pada suatu waktu di abad ke-10 M (mungkin 987 M) datang ke atau bahkan mendirikan Chichen Itza di ujung utara semenanjung Yucatan.
claim.en: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan, a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest, had some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE) come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.

claims_provenance.quote: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan - a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest - had, some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE), come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.

claim.id: Pada piramida itu, sebuah tangga di tiap sisi naik melalui sembilan tingkat ke puncak dengan bangunan persegi kecil berisi dua ruang. Tiga tangga memiliki 91 anak tangga dan yang keempat 92, sehingga totalnya 365, satu untuk setiap hari dalam setahun.
claim.en: On the pyramid, a staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit with a small square structure of two chambers; three stairways have 91 steps and the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.

claims_provenance.quote: A staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit where there is a small square structure consisting of two chambers. The pyramid is a marvel of architectural symmetry and design intention. Three stairways have 91 steps while the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Kukulcan: The Feathered-Serpent God of Mesoamerica

claim.id: Pelataran di puncak piramida dipakai untuk upacara keagamaan menghormati Kukulcan yang mencakup pengorbanan manusia, pengingat bahwa dalam budaya Mesoamerika para dewa harus terus diberi makan dan ditenangkan demi kelangsungan dan kemakmuran umat manusia.
claim.en: The platform at the pyramid's top was used for religious ceremonies in honour of Kukulcan which included human sacrifices, a reminder that in Mesoamerican culture the gods had to be continuously fed and appeased to ensure the continuance and prosperity of the human race.

short_description.id: Kukulkan adalah dewa ular berbulu dalam mitologi Maya, dikaitkan erat dengan Quetzalcoatl bangsa Aztec. Ia dianggap dewa pencipta dan pembawa hujan serta angin, dengan kuil besar di Chichen Itza.
short_description.en: Kukulkan is the feathered serpent deity of Maya mythology, closely related to the Aztec Quetzalcoatl. He was seen as a creator god who brought rain and winds, with a large temple at Chichen Itza.

long_description.id: Kukulkan adalah dewa ular dalam mitologi Maya dan sangat berkaitan dengan dewa Qʼuqʼumatz dari bangsa Kʼicheʼ serta Quetzalcoatl dalam mitologi Aztec. Namanya berarti harfiah 'ular berbulu'. Ia juga diidentifikasi sebagai Quetzalcóatl oleh bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, sebagai Gucumatz oleh Maya Quiché di Guatemala, dan sebagai Ehecatl, dewa angin bangsa Huastec.
long_description.en: Kukulkan is the serpent deity of Maya mythology, with close ties to Qʼuqʼumatz of the Kʼicheʼ and to Quetzalcoatl of Aztec mythology. His name literally means 'feathered snake'. The Toltecs and Aztecs identify him with Quetzalcóatl, the Quiché Maya of Guatemala with Gucumatz, and the Huastecs with Ehecatl, their wind god.

long_description.id: Dewa utama Maya Yucatec ini adalah dewa pencipta serta dewa hujan, angin, badai, dan kehidupan. Kuil-kuil terkemuka Kukulkan terdapat di situs arkeologi di semenanjung Yucatán, seperti Chichen Itza, Uxmal, dan Mayapan. El Castillo di Chichen Itza berfungsi sebagai kuilnya, dan upacara di puncaknya mencakup pengorbanan manusia.
long_description.en: The chief god of the Yucatec Maya, he was a creator and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life. Major temples to Kukulkan stand at archaeological sites on the Yucatán Peninsula, including Chichen Itza, Uxmal and Mayapan. El Castillo at Chichen Itza served as his temple, and ceremonies at its summit included human sacrifices.

long_description.id: Penggambaran ular berbulu hadir di budaya Mesoamerika lain. Meskipun sangat dimeksikanisasi, Kukulkan berakar pada bangsa Maya Periode Klasik, ketika ia dikenal sebagai Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, Ular Perang. Pemujaannya adalah agama Mesoamerika pertama yang melampaui sekat bahasa dan etnis lama dan memudahkan perdagangan damai, dan menyebar dari Chichen Itza hingga Dataran Tinggi Guatemala dan Belize utara.
long_description.en: Images of the Feathered Serpent also occur in other Mesoamerican cultures. Though strongly Mexicanised, Kukulkan began among the Classic Period Maya, who knew him as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, the War Serpent. His cult was the first Mesoamerican religion to transcend the old linguistic and ethnic divisions and facilitated peaceful trade, and it spread from Chichen Itza as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.

long_description.id: Rujukan pada dewa ini bercampur dengan rujukan pada seorang tokoh historis bernama Kukulkan, pahlawan budaya yang menurut Maya Yucatec adalah penguasa atau pendeta dan datang ke atau mendirikan Chichen Itza pada abad ke-10. Dalam cerita rakyat modern, Kukulkan dituturkan sebagai ular bersayap yang berjalan di depan dewa hujan Chaac; bagi Maya Lacandon di Chiapas, ia adalah ular jahat peliharaan dewa matahari.
long_description.en: References to the deity are confused with references to a historical figure named Kukulkan, a cultural hero who the Yucatec Maya believed was a ruler or priest and who came to or founded Chichen Itza in the 10th century. In modern folklore Kukulkan is told of as a winged serpent that travels ahead of the rain god Chaac; to the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas he is an evil snake, the pet of the sun god.

statement.en: The cult of Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl was the first Mesoamerican religion to transcend the old Classic Period linguistic and ethnic divisions and facilitated communication and peaceful trade among peoples of many different social and ethnic backgrounds.

claims.quote: The cult of Kukulkan/Quetzalcoatl ... Although the cult was originally centred on the ancient city of Chichen Itza in the modern Mexican state of Yucatán, it spread as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.

statement.id: Pemujaan itu semula berpusat di kota kuno Chichen Itza di negara bagian Yucatán, Meksiko modern, lalu menyebar sampai Dataran Tinggi Guatemala dan Belize utara.
statement.en: The cult was originally centred on the ancient city of Chichen Itza in the modern Mexican state of Yucatán and spread as far as the Guatemalan Highlands and northern Belize.

claims.quote: In Yucatán, references to the deity Kukulkan are confused by references to a historical individual who bore the name of the god. ... This individual appears to have been a ruler or priest at Chichen Itza who first appeared around the 10th century.

statement.id: Di Yucatán, rujukan pada dewa Kukulkan bercampur dengan rujukan pada seorang tokoh historis yang memakai nama sang dewa; tokoh ini tampaknya penguasa atau pendeta di Chichen Itza yang pertama muncul sekitar abad ke-10.
statement.en: In Yucatán, references to the deity Kukulkan are confused with references to a historical individual who bore the god's name, who appears to have been a ruler or priest at Chichen Itza who first appeared around the 10th century.

claims.quote: El Castillo, Chichen Itza served as a temple to Kukulkan. During the spring and fall equinoxes the shadow cast by the angle of the sun and edges of the nine steps of the pyramid combined with the northern stairway and the stone serpent head carvings create the illusion of a massive serpent descending the pyramid.

statement.id: El Castillo di Chichen Itza berfungsi sebagai kuil Kukulkan. Pada ekuinoks musim semi dan gugur, bayangan dari sudut matahari dan tepi sembilan undakan piramida, dipadukan dengan tangga utara dan ukiran kepala ular batu, menciptakan ilusi ular raksasa yang menuruni piramida.
statement.en: El Castillo at Chichen Itza served as a temple to Kukulkan. At the spring and fall equinoxes the shadow cast by the sun on the edges of the nine steps of the pyramid, combined with the northern stairway and the stone serpent head carvings, creates the illusion of a massive serpent descending the pyramid.

claims.quote: A modern collection of folklore from Yucatán tells how Kukulkan was a winged serpent that flew to the sun and tried to speak to it but the sun, in its pride, burnt his tongue. The same source relates how Kukulkan always travels ahead of the Yucatec Maya rain god Chaac, helping to predict the rains as his tail moves the winds and sweeps the earth clean.

statement.id: Kumpulan cerita rakyat modern dari Yucatán menuturkan Kukulkan sebagai ular bersayap yang terbang ke matahari dan mencoba berbicara dengannya, tetapi matahari yang congkak membakar lidahnya. Sumber yang sama menyebut Kukulkan selalu berjalan di depan dewa hujan Maya Yucatec, Chaac, membantu meramalkan hujan karena ekornya menggerakkan angin dan menyapu bumi hingga bersih.
statement.en: A modern collection of folklore from Yucatán tells how Kukulkan was a winged serpent that flew to the sun and tried to speak to it, but the sun, in its pride, burnt his tongue; the same source says Kukulkan always travels ahead of the Yucatec Maya rain god Chaac, helping to predict the rains as his tail moves the winds and sweeps the earth clean.

claims.quote: Among the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas, Kukulkan is an evil, monstrous snake that is the pet of the sun god.

statement.id: Di kalangan Maya Lacandon di Chiapas, Kukulkan adalah ular jahat dan menyeramkan yang menjadi peliharaan dewa matahari.
statement.en: Among the Lacandon Maya of Chiapas, Kukulkan is an evil, monstrous snake that is the pet of the sun god.

claims.quote: In one tale, Kukulkan is a boy who was born as a snake. As he grew older it became obvious that he was the plumed serpent and his sister cared for him in a cave.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, Kukulkan adalah anak lelaki yang lahir sebagai ular; seiring ia tumbuh, jelas bahwa ia adalah ular berbulu, dan saudara perempuannya merawatnya di sebuah gua.
statement.en: In one tale, Kukulkan is a boy who was born as a snake; as he grew older it became obvious that he was the plumed serpent, and his sister cared for him in a cave.

claims.quote: In the 2006 film Apocalypto, the high priest in charge of human sacrifice prays to Kukulkan.

statement.id: Dalam film Apocalypto (2006), imam agung yang bertanggung jawab atas pengorbanan manusia berdoa kepada Kukulkan.
statement.en: In the 2006 film Apocalypto, the high priest in charge of human sacrifice prays to Kukulkan.

claims.quote: In the 2002 video game Serious Sam: The Second Encounter, Kukulkan serves as a guardian of the time portal in Teotihuacan and is fought as that game's first boss.

statement.id: Dalam gim video Serious Sam: The Second Encounter (2002), Kukulkan menjadi penjaga portal waktu di Teotihuacan dan dilawan sebagai bos pertama gim itu.
statement.en: In the 2002 video game Serious Sam: The Second Encounter, Kukulkan serves as a guardian of the time portal in Teotihuacan and is fought as that game's first boss.

claims.quote: Kukulcan (pron. Koo-kool-kan) is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular, the Yucatec Maya. He is also identified as the feathered serpent god Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.

statement.id: Kukulcan adalah nama dewa ular berbulu dalam mitologi dan agama Mesoamerika, khususnya Maya Yucatec. Ia juga diidentifikasi sebagai dewa ular berbulu Quetzalcóatl oleh bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, sebagai Gucumatz oleh Maya Quiché di Guatemala, dan sebagai Ehecatl, dewa angin bangsa Huastec di Pesisir Teluk.
statement.en: Kukulcan is the name of a feathered serpent god in the mythology and religion of Mesoamerica, in particular the Yucatec Maya; he is also identified as Quetzalcóatl by the Toltecs and Aztecs, as Gucumatz to the Quiché Maya of Guatemala, and as Ehecatl, the wind god of the Huastecs of the Gulf Coast.

claims.quote: The Yucatec Maya were (and still are) speakers of the Yucatec language, and they settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica. Their chief god was the feathered serpent Kukulcan whose name means just that: feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan). He was a creator god, and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.

statement.id: Dewa utama Maya Yucatec, yang menetap di semenanjung Yucatan di utara Mesoamerika kuno, adalah ular berbulu Kukulcan, yang namanya berarti 'berbulu' (k'uk'ul) dan 'ular' (kan). Ia adalah dewa pencipta serta dewa hujan, angin, badai, dan kehidupan.
statement.en: The chief god of the Yucatec Maya, who settled the Yucatan peninsula in the north of ancient Mesoamerica, was the feathered serpent Kukulcan, whose name means feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan); he was a creator god and the god of rain, wind, storms, and life.

claims.quote: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are all unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds. The god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza where a large temple was built in his honour.

statement.id: Kukulcan dan wujud-wujud lainnya dipersatukan oleh keyakinan bahwa masing-masing dianggap dewa pencipta dan pembawa hujan serta angin. Sang dewa terutama dikaitkan dengan Chichen Itza, tempat kuil besar dibangun untuk menghormatinya.
statement.en: Kukulcan and his other manifestations are unified by the belief that each was considered a creator god and a bringer of rain and winds; the god is particularly associated with Chichen Itza, where a large temple was built in his honour.

claims.quote: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan - a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest - had, some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE), come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.

statement.id: Selain dewa Kukulcan, Maya Yucatec meyakini seorang pria bernama Kukulcan, pahlawan budaya yang berstatus penguasa atau pendeta, pada suatu waktu di abad ke-10 M (mungkin 987 M) datang ke atau bahkan mendirikan Chichen Itza di ujung utara semenanjung Yucatan.
statement.en: In addition to the god Kukulcan, the Yucatec Maya believed that a man called Kukulcan, a cultural hero who is either a ruler or priest, had some time in the 10th century CE (perhaps 987 CE) come to or even founded Chichen Itza in the northern tip of the Yucatan peninsula.

claims.quote: A staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit where there is a small square structure consisting of two chambers. The pyramid is a marvel of architectural symmetry and design intention. Three stairways have 91 steps while the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.

statement.id: Pada piramida itu, sebuah tangga di tiap sisi naik melalui sembilan tingkat ke puncak dengan bangunan persegi kecil berisi dua ruang. Tiga tangga memiliki 91 anak tangga dan yang keempat 92, sehingga totalnya 365, satu untuk setiap hari dalam setahun.
statement.en: On the pyramid, a staircase on each side rises the nine levels to a summit with a small square structure of two chambers; three stairways have 91 steps and the fourth has 92, making a total of 365, one step for each day of the year.

claims.quote: The platform at the pyramid's top was used for religious ceremonies in honour of Kukulcan which included human sacrifices, a reminder that in Mesoamerican culture the gods had to be continuously fed and appeased in order to ensure the continuance and prosperity of the human race.

statement.id: Pelataran di puncak piramida dipakai untuk upacara keagamaan menghormati Kukulcan yang mencakup pengorbanan manusia, pengingat bahwa dalam budaya Mesoamerika para dewa harus terus diberi makan dan ditenangkan demi kelangsungan dan kemakmuran umat manusia.
statement.en: The platform at the pyramid's top was used for religious ceremonies in honour of Kukulcan which included human sacrifices, a reminder that in Mesoamerican culture the gods had to be continuously fed and appeased to ensure the continuance and prosperity of the human race.

short_description.id: Limokon adalah burung pertanda bagi orang Mandaya, Bagobo, dan Manobo di Mindanao, burung merpati hutan yang suaranya dipercaya menyampaikan peringatan para roh.
short_description.en: The limokon is an omen bird of the Mandaya, Bagobo and Manobo of Mindanao, a wild pigeon whose call is believed to carry warnings from the spirits.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Mandaya, Bagobo, dan Manobo di Mindanao meyakini limokon sebagai burung pertanda, seperti tigmamanukan bagi orang Tagalog di Luzon. Nama limokon kemungkinan dipakai untuk berbagai jenis merpati hutan di Filipina, sebagian di antaranya dianggap sakti atau sebagai burung pertanda. Sebuah catatan kaki dalam buku etnografi tentang orang Manobo mencantumkan nama Li-mo-kon dengan nama ilmiah Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, yang umumnya disebut merpati buah.

Francisco Combes (1667) mencatat bahwa orang-orang sangat memercayai pertanda, antara lain dari burung seperti limocon. Menurut Fay Cooper Cole (1913), roh biasa berbicara kepada manusia lewat suara limokon, dan jual beli dihentikan bila burung itu memberi peringatan. Burung ini disebut juga limokan, dan Juan de Plasencia pada 1589 menyebut kepercayaan serupa pada orang Tagalog. Garvan menyebut burung ini dianggap pembawa pertanda baik dan buruk yang dimintai petunjuk pada awal setiap perjalanan dan usaha.

Bila limokon berbunyi ketika seseorang berada di jalan setapak, ia mengepalkan tinju dan mengacungkannya ke arah datangnya peringatan itu. Bila arah bunyinya tidak jelas, ia menoleh ke kanan dan memeriksa apakah pohon di sana kuat atau lemah. Orang Mandaya membaca arah tinju itu: ke kanan berarti keberhasilan, ke kiri, depan, atau belakang berarti peringatan akan bahaya atau kegagalan, sehingga tugas ditunda atau dibatalkan. Dalam satu kisah, para peladang meninggalkan lahan karena bunyi limokon di sebelah kiri pemilik tanah. Pada orang Mandaya di Cateel, arti kanan dan kiri disebut berlawanan.

Limokon tidak dianggap roh, melainkan utusan dari dunia roh, dan burung ini tidak pernah dibunuh karena membunuhnya akan mendatangkan kemalangan. Garvan juga menyebut burung pertanda ini dipelihara dalam sangkar untuk tujuan keagamaan dan dibujuk dengan makanan agar bernyanyi bagi pelancong. Menurut sebagian informan, lelaki dan perempuan pertama keluar dari telur limokon.
long_description.en:
In Philippine mythology, the Mandaya, Bagobo and Manobo of Mindanao believed the limokon to be an omen bird, like the tigmamanukan among the Tagalog of Luzon. The name limokon was likely applied to various wild pigeons in the Philippines, some considered magical or omen birds. A footnote in an ethnography of the Manobo gives the name Li-mo-kon with the scientific name Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, generally called fruit dove.

Francisco Combes (1667) recorded that the people firmly believed in omens, including from birds like the limocon. According to Fay Cooper Cole (1913), spirits commonly speak to mortals through the limokon's call, and a sale is stopped if the bird warns. It is also spelled limokan, and Juan de Plasencia mentioned similar beliefs among the Tagalog in 1589. Garvan says the bird is considered a harbinger of good and evil, consulted at the start of every journey and undertaking.

When the limokon calls while someone is on the trail, he doubles his fist and thrusts it toward the direction of the warning. If the direction of the note is unclear, he looks to the right and checks whether the trees there are strong or weak. The Mandaya read the direction of the fist: right means success, left, front or back a warning of danger or failure, so the mission is delayed or given up. In one account, planters left a plot because the limokon called to the left of the landowner. Among the Mandaya of Cateel, right and left are said to mean the opposite.

The limokon is not regarded as a spirit but as a messenger from the spirit world, and the bird is never killed because killing it would bring misfortune. Garvan also says the omen bird is kept in cages for religious purposes and coaxed with food to sing for the traveler. According to some informants, the first man and woman emerged from limokon eggs.

summary.en: When the limokon's call was heard to the left of an owner clearing a field, the men left at once, believing the bird had warned that rats would eat their crop.

claim.en: The Mandaya, Bagobo and Manobo of Mindanao believed the limokon an omen bird, like the tigmamanukan among the Tagalog of Luzon.

claims_provenance.quote: In Philippine mythology, the Limokon was believed by the Mandaya, Bagobo, and Manobo people of Mindanao to be an omen bird. In Luzon, a blue bird called the Tigmamanukan was similarly believed by the Tagalog people to be an omen bird.

claim.id: Francisco Combes (1667) mencatat bahwa orang-orang sangat memercayai pertanda, antara lain dari burung seperti limocon.
claim.en: Francisco Combes (1667) recorded that the people firmly believed in omens, including from birds like the limocon.

claims_provenance.quote: What they believe in thoroughly are omens, which are almost general in all the islands. There are many of them: of birds, like the limocon

claim.id: Istilah limokon kemungkinan dipakai untuk berbagai merpati hutan dalam berbagai bahasa di Filipina, sebagian dianggap sakti atau burung pertanda.
claim.en: The term limokon likely named various wild pigeons in the Philippine languages, some thought magical or omen birds.

claims_provenance.quote: Likely the term 'limokon' applied to various types of wild pigeons in the various languages in the Philippines, some of which were considered 'magical' and or 'omen birds'.

claim.id: Menurut Fay Cooper Cole (1913), roh biasa berbicara kepada manusia lewat suara limokon; semua orang memahami dan menghormati peringatannya, dan jual beli dihentikan bila ia memberi peringatan.
claim.en: According to Fay Cooper Cole (1913), spirits commonly speak to mortals through the limokon's call; all understand and respect its warnings, and a sale is stopped if it warns.

claims_provenance.quote: A common method used by the spirits to communicate with mortals is through the call of the limokon. All the people know the meaning of its calls and all respect its warnings. If a man is starting to buy or trade for an article and this bird gives its warning the sale is stopped.

claim.id: Jika limokon berbunyi ketika seseorang berada di jalan setapak, ia segera mengepalkan tinju dan mengacungkannya ke arah datangnya peringatan itu.
claim.en: If the limokon calls when a person is on the trail, he at once doubles his fist and thrusts it in the direction from which the warning comes.

claims_provenance.quote: Should the limokon call when a person is on the trail he at ones doubles his fist and thrusts it in the direction from which the warning comes.

claim.id: Bila tidak jelas dari mana bunyinya datang, pelancong menoleh ke sisi kanan; jika di sana ada pohon yang kuat dan kokoh, semuanya baik, tetapi jika pohon itu ditebang atau lemah, ia harus sangat berhati-hati terhadap bahaya yang mengancam.
claim.en: When it is not clear where the note came from, the traveler looks to the right side; if he sees strong, sturdy trees there, all is well, but if they are cut or weak, he should take great care to avoid impending danger.

claims_provenance.quote: When it is not clear from whence the note came, the traveler looks toward the right side. If he sees there strong, sturdy trees, he knows that all is well, but if they are cut or weaklings, he should use great care to avoid impending danger.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Project Gutenberg (Field Museum of Natural History, 1913) — The Wild Tribes of Davao District, Mindanao

claim.id: Ketika ditanya mengapa orang hanya melihat ke kanan, seorang lelaki tua menjawab bahwa sisi kanan milik si pelancong, sedangkan sisi kiri buruk dan milik orang lain.
claim.en: Asked why one should look only to the right, an old man replied that the right side belongs to you, while the left side is bad and belongs to someone else.

claims_provenance.quote: When questioned as to why one should look only to the right, an old man quickly replied: "The right side belongs to you; the left side is bad and belongs to someone else."
claims_provenance.source_citation: Project Gutenberg (Field Museum of Natural History, 1913) — The Wild Tribes of Davao District, Mindanao

claim.id: Jika merpati limokan (ejaan lain limokon) berbunyi di sisi kiri jalan, rombongan menolak melanjutkan perjalanan, kecuali limokan lain menjawab dari sisi kanan jalan.
claim.en: If the dove limokan (a variant spelling of limokon) calls on the left side of the trail, the party will refuse to proceed unless another limokan answers from the right side of the path.

claims_provenance.quote: Likewise, if the dove limokan calls on the left side of the trail the party will refuse to proceed, unless another limokan answers the call from the right side of the path.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Project Gutenberg (Field Museum of Natural History, 1913) — The Wild Tribes of Davao District, Mindanao

claim.id: Hubungan dekat limokon dengan orang Mandaya disebut sebagai alasan mengapa bunyinya begitu diindahkan; pelancong yang mendengar kicau burung ini segera mengepalkan tinju dan mengarahkannya ke arah suara itu.
claim.en: The close relationship of the limokon to the Mandaya is given as the reason its calls are heeded so closely; a traveler hearing the cooing of this bird at once doubles his fist and points it toward the sound.

short_description.id: Limokon adalah burung pertanda bagi orang Mandaya, Bagobo, dan Manobo di Mindanao, burung merpati hutan yang suaranya dipercaya menyampaikan peringatan para roh.
short_description.en: The limokon is an omen bird of the Mandaya, Bagobo and Manobo of Mindanao, a wild pigeon whose call is believed to carry warnings from the spirits.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Mandaya, Bagobo, dan Manobo di Mindanao meyakini limokon sebagai burung pertanda, seperti tigmamanukan bagi orang Tagalog di Luzon. Nama limokon kemungkinan dipakai untuk berbagai jenis merpati hutan di Filipina, sebagian di antaranya dianggap sakti atau sebagai burung pertanda. Sebuah catatan kaki dalam buku etnografi tentang orang Manobo mencantumkan nama Li-mo-kon dengan nama ilmiah Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, yang umumnya disebut merpati buah.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology, the Mandaya, Bagobo and Manobo of Mindanao believed the limokon to be an omen bird, like the tigmamanukan among the Tagalog of Luzon. The name limokon was likely applied to various wild pigeons in the Philippines, some considered magical or omen birds. A footnote in an ethnography of the Manobo gives the name Li-mo-kon with the scientific name Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, generally called fruit dove.

long_description.id: Francisco Combes (1667) mencatat bahwa orang-orang sangat memercayai pertanda, antara lain dari burung seperti limocon. Menurut Fay Cooper Cole (1913), roh biasa berbicara kepada manusia lewat suara limokon, dan jual beli dihentikan bila burung itu memberi peringatan. Burung ini disebut juga limokan, dan Juan de Plasencia pada 1589 menyebut kepercayaan serupa pada orang Tagalog. Garvan menyebut burung ini dianggap pembawa pertanda baik dan buruk yang dimintai petunjuk pada awal setiap perjalanan dan usaha.
long_description.en: Francisco Combes (1667) recorded that the people firmly believed in omens, including from birds like the limocon. According to Fay Cooper Cole (1913), spirits commonly speak to mortals through the limokon's call, and a sale is stopped if the bird warns. It is also spelled limokan, and Juan de Plasencia mentioned similar beliefs among the Tagalog in 1589. Garvan says the bird is considered a harbinger of good and evil, consulted at the start of every journey and undertaking.

long_description.id: Bila limokon berbunyi ketika seseorang berada di jalan setapak, ia mengepalkan tinju dan mengacungkannya ke arah datangnya peringatan itu. Bila arah bunyinya tidak jelas, ia menoleh ke kanan dan memeriksa apakah pohon di sana kuat atau lemah. Orang Mandaya membaca arah tinju itu: ke kanan berarti keberhasilan, ke kiri, depan, atau belakang berarti peringatan akan bahaya atau kegagalan, sehingga tugas ditunda atau dibatalkan. Dalam satu kisah, para peladang meninggalkan lahan karena bunyi limokon di sebelah kiri pemilik tanah. Pada orang Mandaya di Cateel, arti kanan dan kiri disebut berlawanan.
long_description.en: When the limokon calls while someone is on the trail, he doubles his fist and thrusts it toward the direction of the warning. If the direction of the note is unclear, he looks to the right and checks whether the trees there are strong or weak. The Mandaya read the direction of the fist: right means success, left, front or back a warning of danger or failure, so the mission is delayed or given up. In one account, planters left a plot because the limokon called to the left of the landowner. Among the Mandaya of Cateel, right and left are said to mean the opposite.

long_description.id: Limokon tidak dianggap roh, melainkan utusan dari dunia roh, dan burung ini tidak pernah dibunuh karena membunuhnya akan mendatangkan kemalangan. Garvan juga menyebut burung pertanda ini dipelihara dalam sangkar untuk tujuan keagamaan dan dibujuk dengan makanan agar bernyanyi bagi pelancong. Menurut sebagian informan, lelaki dan perempuan pertama keluar dari telur limokon.
long_description.en: The limokon is not regarded as a spirit but as a messenger from the spirit world, and the bird is never killed because killing it would bring misfortune. Garvan also says the omen bird is kept in cages for religious purposes and coaxed with food to sing for the traveler. According to some informants, the first man and woman emerged from limokon eggs.

statement.en: Some informants stated that this is the name given to the first man and woman, who emerged from the limokon eggs.

claims.quote: The limokon warns or encourages the traveler, while certain acts of the individual, such as sneezing, are looked upon as warnings from unseen beings.

statement.id: Limokon memperingatkan atau menyemangati pelancong, sedangkan perbuatan tertentu seperti bersin dipandang sebagai peringatan dari makhluk tak kasatmata.
statement.en: The limokon warns or encourages the traveler, while certain acts of the individual, such as sneezing, are seen as warnings from unseen beings.

claims.quote: Similar beliefs held by the Tagalog were mentioned by Juan de Plasencia in 1589.

statement.id: Kepercayaan serupa pada orang Tagalog disebut oleh Juan de Plasencia pada 1589.
statement.en: Similar beliefs held by the Tagalog were mentioned by Juan de Plasencia in 1589.

claims.quote: Li-mo-kon. (Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale). Generally called fruit dove.

statement.id: Catatan kaki dalam buku ini mencantumkan nama Li-mo-kon dengan nama ilmiah Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, yang umumnya disebut merpati buah.
statement.en: A footnote in this book gives the name Li-mo-kon with the scientific name Phabitreron brevirostris Tweedale, generally called fruit dove.

claims.quote: This homely inert creature is considered the harbinger of good and evil, and is consulted at the beginning of every journey and of every undertaking where its prophetic voice can be heard.

statement.id: Burung yang sederhana dan pendiam ini dianggap pembawa pertanda baik dan buruk, dan dimintai petunjuk pada awal setiap perjalanan dan setiap usaha di tempat suaranya yang bernubuat dapat terdengar.
statement.en: This homely, inert bird is considered the harbinger of good and evil, and is consulted at the start of every journey and undertaking where its prophetic voice can be heard.

claims.quote: Should its cry forebode ill, the undertaking is discontinued no matter how urgent it may be. But should the cry presage good, then the project is taken up or continued with renewed assurance and a glad heart

statement.id: Jika bunyinya menandakan celaka, usaha dihentikan seberapa pun mendesaknya; jika menandakan baik, usaha dimulai atau dilanjutkan dengan keyakinan baru dan hati gembira.
statement.en: If its cry forebodes ill, the undertaking is discontinued however urgent it may be; if the cry presages good, the project is taken up or continued with renewed assurance and a glad heart.

claims.quote: for is not this bird the envoy of the deities and its voice a divine message?

statement.id: Burung ini dipandang sebagai utusan para dewa, dan suaranya sebagai pesan ilahi.
statement.en: The bird is regarded as the envoy of the deities and its voice as a divine message.

claims.quote: The omen bird is never killed, for to kill it would draw down unmitigated misfortune.
claims.locator: Ornitoskopi, sikap hormat terhadap burung pertanda

statement.id: Burung pertanda tidak pernah dibunuh, karena membunuhnya akan mendatangkan kemalangan besar.
statement.en: The omen bird is never killed, because killing it would bring down great misfortune.

claims.quote: The cage is usually hung from the roof under the eaves outside the wall. The turtledove is kept for religious purposes

statement.id: Sangkar biasanya digantung pada atap di bawah cucuran atap di luar dinding, dan merpati tekukur dipelihara untuk tujuan keagamaan.
statement.en: The cage is usually hung from the roof under the eaves outside the wall, and the turtledove is kept for religious purposes.

claims.quote: The prospective traveler takes a little camote or banana and, placing it in the cage, addresses the captive bird and asks it to sing to its companions of the woods that they too in turn may sing to him the song of success and safe return.
claims.locator: Ornitoskopi, sikap hormat terhadap burung pertanda

statement.id: Calon pelancong menaruh sedikit ubi jalar atau pisang di sangkar dan meminta burung tangkapan itu bernyanyi kepada kawan-kawannya di hutan agar mereka pun menyanyikan lagu keberhasilan dan keselamatan pulang baginya.
statement.en: The prospective traveler places a little sweet potato or banana in the cage and asks the captive bird to sing to its companions in the woods so that they in turn may sing to him the song of success and safe return.

claims.quote: Maxey states exactly the opposite, for the Mandaya of Cateel, i. e., the right side is bad, the left good.

statement.id: Maxey menyatakan hal yang persis berlawanan bagi orang Mandaya di Cateel: sisi kanan buruk dan sisi kiri baik.
statement.en: Maxey states exactly the opposite for the Mandaya of Cateel: the right side is bad and the left good.

short_description.id: Mujina adalah istilah Jepang lama untuk teledu atau tanuki; dalam cerita rakyat mujina digambarkan sebagai yōkai pengubah wujud yang menipu manusia.
short_description.en: Mujina is an old Japanese term for the badger or tanuki; in folklore the mujina is depicted as a shapeshifting yōkai that deceives humans.

long_description.id:
Mujina adalah istilah Jepang lama yang terutama merujuk pada teledu Jepang tetapi secara tradisional pada tanuki, sehingga menimbulkan kebingungan. Dalam wujud aslinya mujina dikatakan berwajah seperti rakun dengan tubuh teledu. Sebuah ensiklopedia Jepang mencatat bahwa dahulu tanuki disebut muji atau mujina, namun hal itu tidak selalu pasti dan ada daerah yang menyebut keduanya mujina.

Dalam cerita rakyat, mujina seperti kitsune dan tanuki digambarkan sebagai yōkai yang menipu manusia. Mujina dapat berubah menjadi komet, tiang pagar, batu, pohon, dan sebagainya, dan salah satu wujud kesukaannya adalah pendeta Buddha berjubah hitam. Ia juga dikatakan menggembungkan perutnya dan menabuhnya sambil bernyanyi, serta menciptakan "api hantu" yang menyerupai will-o'-the-wisp. Wujud ubahannya tidak selalu stabil: bila tertidur, penampilannya dapat terurai.

Mujina pertama kali tampak dalam sastra di Nihon Shoki, pada bagian tentang tahun ke-35 Permaisuri Suiko (627). Di wilayah Shimōsa mereka disebut kabukiri-kozō, dan di Sado disebut Tonchibō dan juga dianggap seperti wujud dewa gunung. Mujina dikenal sebagai penipu yang gemar bercanda tanpa niat jahat, namun dipercaya berhati lembut dan tahu berterima kasih. Kebingungan istilah ini pernah berdampak hukum: pada 1924 di Prefektur Tochigi seorang pemburu membunuh anjing rakun yang ia kira bernama mujina.
long_description.en:
Mujina is an old Japanese term primarily for the Japanese badger but traditionally for the tanuki, which causes confusion. In its natural form the mujina is said to have a raccoon-like face and a badger's body. A Japanese encyclopedia notes that the tanuki was anciently called muji or mujina, but this is not certain and some regions call both animals mujina.

In folklore the mujina, like the tanuki, is depicted as a yōkai that deceives humans. It can turn into comets, fence posts, stones, trees and more, and one of its favorite forms is a black-garbed Buddhist priest. It is also said to inflate its belly and drum on it while singing, and to create a "ghost-fire" resembling will-o'-the-wisps. Its transformation is not always stable: if it falls asleep its appearance can come undone.

The earliest literary appearance is in the Nihon Shoki, in the section on the 35th year of Empress Suiko (627). In the Shimōsa region they are called kabukiri-kozō, and on Sado they are called Tonchibō and also thought of as resembling a mountain deity. The mujina is known as a trickster fond of harmless pranks, yet is believed to have a gentle heart and to know gratitude. The confusion over the term once had legal consequences: in 1924 in Tochigi Prefecture a hunter killed a raccoon dog he believed to be called a mujina.

claims.quote: is an old Japanese term primarily referring to the Japanese badger, but traditionally to the Japanese raccoon dog (tanuki), causing confusion.

statement.id: Mujina adalah istilah Jepang lama yang terutama merujuk pada teledu Jepang, tetapi secara tradisional pada anjing rakun Jepang (tanuki), sehingga menimbulkan kebingungan.
statement.en: Mujina is an old Japanese term primarily referring to the Japanese badger, but traditionally to the Japanese raccoon dog (tanuki), causing confusion.

claims.quote: The mujina is said to be a raccoon-faced creature in its natural form, with the main body being that of a Japanese badger.

statement.id: Mujina dikatakan berwajah seperti rakun dalam wujud aslinya, dengan tubuh utama berupa teledu Jepang.
statement.en: The mujina is said to be a raccoon-faced creature in its natural form, with a Japanese badger's body.

claims.quote: The mujina in specific are known to be able to inflate their bellies, creating music by drumming on it whilst singing.

statement.id: Mujina dikenal dapat menggembungkan perutnya dan menciptakan musik dengan menabuhnya sambil bernyanyi.
statement.en: Mujina are known to be able to inflate their bellies, creating music by drumming on them while singing.

claims.quote: At times, the mujina will also create a "ghost-fire", also called tanuki-bi (狸火), which resembles will-o'-the-wisps.

statement.id: Kadang-kadang mujina juga menciptakan "api hantu", disebut juga tanuki-bi (狸火), yang menyerupai will-o'-the-wisp.
statement.en: At times the mujina will also create a "ghost-fire", also called tanuki-bi (狸火), which resembles will-o'-the-wisps.

claims.quote: One of its favorite appearances is that of a black-garbed Buddhist priest, also called the tanuki-bôzu.

statement.id: Salah satu wujud kesukaannya adalah pendeta Buddha berjubah hitam, disebut juga tanuki-bōzu.
statement.en: One of its favorite appearances is that of a black-garbed Buddhist priest, also called the tanuki-bôzu.

claims.quote: they have been able to transform into dazzling comets, fence posts, stones, trees, and so on.

statement.id: Mujina dikatakan mampu berubah menjadi komet yang menyilaukan, tiang pagar, batu, pohon, dan sebagainya.
statement.en: Mujina are said to have been able to transform into dazzling comets, fence posts, stones, trees, and so on.

claims.quote: The appearance of a mujina's transformation isn't always stable; if the badger were to drift to sleep, their appearance can become wholly or even partially undone.

statement.id: Wujud hasil perubahan mujina tidak selalu stabil; bila teledu itu tertidur, penampilannya dapat terurai seluruhnya atau sebagian.
statement.en: A mujina's transformation is not always stable; if the badger drifts to sleep, its appearance can become wholly or partially undone.

claims.quote: They are first seen in literature in the Nihon Shoki in the part about Empress Suiko's 35th year (627)

statement.id: Mujina pertama kali tampak dalam sastra di Nihon Shoki, pada bagian tentang tahun ke-35 Permaisuri Suiko (627).
statement.en: Their earliest appearance in literature is in the Nihon Shoki, in the part about Empress Suiko's 35th year (627).

claims.quote: In the Shimōsa region, they are called kabukiri-kozō ... and they would shapeshift into a kozō (little monk) wearing a strangely short kimono with a kappa-like bobbed head

statement.id: Di wilayah Shimōsa, mereka disebut kabukiri-kozō dan berubah menjadi kozō (biksu cilik) yang mengenakan kimono aneh yang pendek dan berkepala potongan pendek seperti kappa.
statement.en: In the Shimōsa region they are called kabukiri-kozō and would shapeshift into a kozō (little monk) wearing a strangely short kimono and a kappa-like bobbed head.

claims.quote: 民俗 ムジナはタヌキと同じく人間を化かす，また大入道その他の怪物の姿で人をおどすともいう。

statement.id: Seperti tanuki, mujina menipu manusia, dan dikatakan pula menakuti orang dengan menyamar sebagai 大入道 atau monster lain.
statement.en: Like the tanuki, the mujina deceives humans, and is also said to frighten people in the form of a 大入道 or other monsters.

claims.quote: 佐渡ではトンチボウと呼んで山の神の姿のようにも考え，またこれにまつわる伝承が残っていた。また，長野県北境の山中ではバンブクといって腹に毛のないものが化けるなどともいっていた。

statement.id: Di Sado, mujina disebut Tonchibō dan juga dianggap seperti wujud dewa gunung, dan ada cerita yang berkaitan dengannya; di pegunungan perbatasan utara Prefektur Nagano disebut Banbuku, dikatakan yang perutnya tak berbulu dapat berubah wujud.
statement.en: On Sado it was called Tonchibō and also thought of as resembling a mountain deity, with related traditions preserved; in the mountains on the northern border of Nagano Prefecture it was called Banbuku, and one with a hairless belly was said to transform.

claims.quote: 古くはタヌキを指してムジあるいはムジナと呼び，アナグマをマミあるいはササグマと呼んだという。しかし，これは必ずしも確かではなく，タヌキとアナグマの双方をムジナと呼ぶ地方もある。

statement.id: Konon dahulu tanuki disebut muji atau mujina dan teledu disebut mami atau sasaguma, tetapi hal itu tidak selalu pasti, dan ada daerah yang menyebut tanuki maupun teledu sebagai mujina.
statement.en: It is said that anciently the tanuki was called muji or mujina and the badger mami or sasaguma, but this is not necessarily certain, and in some regions both tanuki and badger are called mujina.

claims.quote: In Tochigi Prefecture in 1924, a hunter killed a raccoon dog, which he believed to be called a mujina.

statement.id: Pada 1924 di Prefektur Tochigi, seorang pemburu membunuh seekor anjing rakun yang ia kira bernama mujina.
statement.en: In 1924 in Tochigi Prefecture, a hunter killed a raccoon dog which he believed to be called a mujina.

claims.quote: Like the other yōkai, the mujina is a notorious trickster, and enjoys using their shapeshifting to play harmless pranks.

statement.id: Seperti yōkai lain, mujina adalah penipu yang terkenal dan gemar memakai kemampuan berubah wujud untuk bercanda tanpa niat jahat.
statement.en: Like other yōkai, the mujina is a notorious trickster and enjoys using its shapeshifting to play harmless pranks.

claims.quote: It is believed that although these creatures can be extremely chaotic, they have a gentle heart, and know how to be grateful.

statement.id: Dipercaya bahwa walau bisa sangat kacau, makhluk ini berhati lembut dan tahu berterima kasih.
statement.en: It is believed that although these creatures can be extremely chaotic, they have a gentle heart and know how to be grateful.

short_description.id: Ninki Nanka adalah makhluk legenda mirip naga dari cerita rakyat Gambia, yang dipercaya menghuni rawa dan hutan lebat serta membawa maut bagi siapa pun yang menatapnya.
short_description.en: The Ninki Nanka is a dragon-like legendary creature of the folklore of Gambia, believed to haunt swamps and dense bush and to bring death to anyone who meets its gaze.

long_description.id:
Ninki Nanka dikenal dalam cerita rakyat orang Mandinka di Gambia. Banyak penduduk Gambia hilir konon menghindari rawa, sungai, bukit, dan anak sungai yang subur karena takut padanya. Ia dipercaya tinggal di hutan berawa dan gua, dan sering disebut naga sungai atau naga rawa.

Wujudnya berbeda menurut tiap suku, tetapi umumnya reptil. Ada yang menyebut kepala buaya pada tubuh keledai, ada yang menyebut campuran kuda nil dan jerapah, ada pula yang menganggapnya ular besar. Kisah lain melukiskan binatang rawa sepanjang 9 m bertubuh mirip buaya, bersisik bagai cermin, berleher jerapah, berkepala kuda, dan bertanduk tiga.

Ciri yang paling sering disebut adalah tatapannya yang mematikan, sehingga orang dianjurkan membawa cermin untuk menangkisnya. Sisiknya konon berkilau aneka warna sehingga ia bisa menyamar. Laporan komisaris tahun 1906 menyamakannya dengan ular raksasa bermahkota di semak paling lebat: melihat tubuhnya membawa penyakit, melihat mata atau mahkotanya berarti mati seketika.

Sebagai roh jahat, Ninki Nanka juga dipercaya mendatangkan kekeringan dan kelaparan. Di masa kini makhluk ini dibandingkan dengan monster Loch Ness, dan pada Juli 2006 Centre for Fortean Zoology mengirim ekspedisi ke Gambia untuk mencarinya.
long_description.en:
The Ninki Nanka belongs to the folklore of the Mandinka of Gambia. Many people of the lower Gambia were said to shun fertile swamps, rivers, hills and creeks out of fear of it. It was believed to live in swampy forests and caves and is often called a river or swamp dragon.

Its form varies from tribe to tribe, though most see it as a reptile. Some speak of a crocodile's head on a donkey's body, others of a hippopotamus-giraffe mix, others again of a large snake. Another account pictures a 9m marsh beast with a crocodile-like body, mirror-like scales, a giraffe's neck, a horse's head and three horns.

The trait most often mentioned is its deadly stare, and people are advised to carry mirrors to turn it aside. Its scales are said to shimmer in many colours, letting it blend in. A 1906 commissioner's report compared it to a giant crowned serpent of the thickest bush: sighting its body brought illness, while sighting its eyes or crown meant sudden death.

As an evil spirit, the Ninki Nanka was also believed to cause drought and famine. Today it is compared with the Loch Ness monster, and in July 2006 the Centre for Fortean Zoology sent an expedition to Gambia to look for it.
