claims.quote: Tangaroa (Māori; Takaroa in the South Island dialect; cognate with Tagaloa in Sāmoan) is the great atua of the sea, lakes, rivers, and creatures that live within them, especially fish, in Māori mythology.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah atua laut, danau, sungai, dan ikan dalam mitologi Māori.
statement.en: Tangaroa is the great atua of the sea, lakes, rivers, and fish in Māori mythology.

claims.quote: As Tangaroa-whakamau-tai, he exercises control over the tides. He is sometimes depicted as a whale.

statement.id: Sebagai Tangaroa-whakamau-tai ia mengatur pasang surut dan terkadang digambarkan sebagai paus.
statement.en: As Tangaroa-whakamau-tai he governs tides and is sometimes depicted as a whale.

claims.quote: Tangaroa is son of Ranginui and Papatūānuku, Sky and Earth. After joining his brothers Rongo, Tū, Haumia, and Tāne in the forcible separation of their parents, he is attacked by his brother Tāwhirimātea, the atua of storms, and forced to hide in the sea.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah putra Ranginui dan Papatūānuku yang bersembunyi di laut akibat serangan Tāwhirimātea.
statement.en: Tangaroa is son of Sky and Earth who hid in the sea when attacked by storm god Tāwhirimātea.

claims.quote: Tangaroa is the father of many sea creatures. Tangaroa's son, Punga, has two children, Ikatere, the ancestor of fish, and Tū-te-wehiwehi (or Tū-te-wanawana), the ancestor of reptiles.

statement.id: Tangaroa adalah ayah dari banyak makhluk laut. Punga, putra Tangaroa, memiliki dua anak: Ikatere, leluhur ikan, dan Tū-te-wehiwehi (atau Tū-te-wanawana), leluhur reptil.
statement.en: Tangaroa is the father of many sea creatures. His son Punga has two children: Ikatere, the ancestor of fish, and Tū-te-wehiwehi (or Tū-te-wanawana), the ancestor of reptiles.

claims.quote: The contention between Tangaroa and Tāne Mahuta, the father of birds, trees, and humans, is an indication that the Māori thought of the ocean and the land as opposed realms.

statement.id: Pertentangan antara Tangaroa dan Tāne Mahuta, ayah burung, pohon, dan manusia, menandakan bahwa orang Māori memandang lautan dan daratan sebagai ranah yang berlawanan.
statement.en: The contention between Tangaroa and Tāne Mahuta, the father of birds, trees and humans, indicates that the Māori thought of the ocean and the land as opposed realms.

claims.quote: When people go out to sea to fish or to travel, they are, in effect, representatives of Tāne Mahuta, entering the realm of Tāne Mahuta's enemy. For this reason, offerings need to be made to Tangaroa before any such expedition.

statement.id: Ketika orang pergi ke laut untuk menangkap ikan atau bepergian, mereka pada dasarnya mewakili Tāne Mahuta yang memasuki ranah musuh Tāne Mahuta. Karena itu, persembahan perlu diberikan kepada Tangaroa sebelum ekspedisi semacam itu.
statement.en: When people go out to sea to fish or travel, they are in effect representatives of Tāne Mahuta entering the realm of his enemy. For this reason, offerings need to be made to Tangaroa before any such expedition.

claims.quote: In Rarotonga, Tangaroa is god of the sea and fertility. He is the most important of all the departmental gods.

statement.id: Di Rarotonga, Tangaroa adalah dewa laut dan kesuburan, serta yang terpenting di antara semua dewa departemental.
statement.en: In Rarotonga, Tangaroa is god of the sea and fertility and the most important of all the departmental gods.

claims.quote: Tangaloa is one of the oldest Polynesian deities. In Western Polynesian traditions such as Samoa and Tonga, Tangaloa is considered the supreme and creator deity. In Eastern Polynesian cultures, however, he is usually considered of equal status to Tāne and thus not supreme.

statement.id: Tangaloa adalah salah satu dewa Polinesia tertua. Dalam tradisi Polinesia Barat seperti Samoa dan Tonga, Tangaloa dianggap dewa tertinggi dan pencipta; dalam budaya Polinesia Timur ia biasanya dianggap setara dengan Tāne dan karena itu tidak tertinggi.
statement.en: Tangaloa is one of the oldest Polynesian deities. In Western Polynesian traditions such as Samoa and Tonga he is considered the supreme and creator deity; in Eastern Polynesian cultures he is usually considered equal in status to Tāne and thus not supreme.

claims.quote: The Kāi Tahu version of the origin of Takaroa maintains that he is the son of Temoretu and that Papatūānuku is his wife. Papatūānuku commits adultery with Rakinui while Takaroa is away, and in the resulting battle on the beach, Takaroa's spear pierces Rakinui through both his thighs. Papatūānuku then marries Rakinui.

statement.id: Versi Kāi Tahu tentang asal Takaroa menyatakan bahwa ia putra Temoretu dan Papatūānuku adalah istrinya. Papatūānuku berzina dengan Rakinui saat Takaroa pergi; dalam pertempuran di pantai, tombak Takaroa menembus kedua paha Rakinui, lalu Papatūānuku menikah dengan Rakinui.
statement.en: The Kāi Tahu version of Takaroa's origin holds that he is the son of Temoretu and that Papatūānuku is his wife. Papatūānuku commits adultery with Rakinui while Takaroa is away; in the battle on the beach Takaroa's spear pierces Rakinui through both thighs, and Papatūānuku then marries Rakinui.

claims.quote: In Hawaiʻi, the god of ocean, healing, and long travels is called Kanaloa, the cognate term in the Hawaiian language

statement.id: Di Hawaiʻi, dewa samudra, penyembuhan, dan perjalanan jauh disebut Kanaloa, istilah sepadan (kognat) dalam bahasa Hawaii.
statement.en: In Hawaiʻi, the god of the ocean, healing and long travels is called Kanaloa, the cognate term in the Hawaiian language.

claims.quote: Tangaroa was ancestor of Fish and the Pounamu, which is classed with fish by the Maori.

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, Tangaroa adalah leluhur ikan dan pounamu, yang oleh orang Māori digolongkan bersama ikan.
statement.en: According to Shortland, Tangaroa was the ancestor of fish and of the pounamu, which the Maori classed with fish.

claims.quote: Tangaroa took to wife Te Anu-matao (=the chilly cold)

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, Tangaroa memperistri Te Anu-matao (= dingin yang menusuk).
statement.en: According to Shortland, Tangaroa took Te Anu-matao (= the chilly cold) as his wife.

claims.quote: Then Ihenga threw into the water some of his inanga. ... Then he called on Tangaroa, and Tangaroa sent the eels. The mode of calling was a karakia.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Ihenga yang dicatat Shortland, ketika memanggil Tangaroa, Tangaroa mengirim belut; cara memanggilnya adalah dengan karakia (mantra).
statement.en: In the story of Ihenga recorded by Shortland, when he called on Tangaroa, Tangaroa sent the eels; the mode of calling was a karakia (incantation).

claims.quote: Tangaroa warded it off, and it missed him. Then Tangaroa made a thrust at Rangi, and pierced him quite through the thigh, and he fell.

statement.id: Dalam versi yang dicatat Shortland, Tangaroa menangkis tusukan itu hingga meleset, lalu menusuk Rangi menembus pahanya hingga ia jatuh.
statement.en: In the version recorded by Shortland, Tangaroa warded off the thrust so that it missed him, then thrust at Rangi and pierced him quite through the thigh, so that he fell.

claims.quote: which Powers are regarded by the Maori as their own primitive ancestors, and are invoked in their karakia by all the Maori race; for we find the names of Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa, &c., mentioned as Atua or Gods of the Maori of the Sandwich Islands and other Islands of the Pacific inhabited by the same race.

statement.id: Menurut Shortland, kekuatan-kekuatan alam personifikasi itu dianggap orang Māori sebagai leluhur purba mereka dan dipanggil dalam karakia oleh seluruh bangsa Māori; nama Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa, dan lainnya disebut sebagai Atua atau dewa orang Māori di Kepulauan Sandwich dan pulau-pulau Pasifik lain yang dihuni ras yang sama.
statement.en: According to Shortland, these personified Powers of Nature are regarded by the Maori as their primitive ancestors and invoked in karakia by the whole Maori race; the names of Rangi, Rongo, Tangaroa and others are mentioned as Atua or gods of the Maori of the Sandwich Islands and other Pacific islands inhabited by the same race.

claims.quote: Lo, next Tangaroa, the god and father of fish and reptiles rises up, that he may rend apart the heavens and the earth, but he rends them not apart.
claims.locator: Myths of origins (account quoted from Grey)

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang dikutip Dixon, Tangaroa, dewa dan ayah ikan serta reptil, bangkit untuk memisahkan langit dan bumi tetapi tidak berhasil.
statement.en: In the account Dixon quotes, Tangaroa, the god and father of fish and reptiles, rises up to rend heaven and earth apart but does not succeed.

claims.quote: Now Papa-tu-a-nuku was the wife of Tangaroa, but had deserted him, coming to Rangi while Tangaroa was away. When the latter returned and learned of his wife's faithlessness, he attacked Rangi and speared him in the thigh

statement.id: Menurut Dixon, Papa-tu-a-nuku adalah istri Tangaroa tetapi meninggalkannya dan datang kepada Rangi saat Tangaroa pergi; ketika Tangaroa kembali dan mengetahui ketidaksetiaan istrinya, ia menyerang Rangi dan menombak pahanya.
statement.en: According to Dixon, Papa-tu-a-nuku was Tangaroa's wife but deserted him and came to Rangi while Tangaroa was away; when he returned and learned of her faithlessness, he attacked Rangi and speared him in the thigh.

claims.quote: In some of the Cook Islands, he has similar roles, though in Manihiki, he is the fire deity that Māui steals from, which in Māori mythology is instead Mahuika, a goddess of fire.

statement.id: Di sebagian Kepulauan Cook ia memiliki peran serupa, meskipun di Manihiki ia adalah dewa api tempat Māui mencuri api, yang dalam mitologi Māori justru adalah Mahuika, dewi api.
statement.en: In some of the Cook Islands he has similar roles, though in Manihiki he is the fire deity that Māui steals from, whereas in Māori mythology that figure is Mahuika, a goddess of fire.

claims.quote: Wooden figure of Tangaroa Upao Vahu,a sea-deity, represented in the act of creating other gods and men.

statement.en: A plate caption in Dixon's book describes a wooden figure of Tangaroa Upao Vahu, a sea-deity, shown in the act of creating other gods and men.

short_description.id: Scultone adalah makhluk mirip naga atau ular dalam legenda Sardinia yang tatapannya dapat membunuh dan yang menuntut korban manusia di sekitar Baunei, sebelum dikalahkan oleh Rasul Petrus.
short_description.en: The Scultone is a dragon-like or serpent creature of Sardinian legend whose gaze could kill and which demanded human sacrifices around Baunei before the apostle Peter defeated it.

long_description.id:
Legenda rakyat Sardinia menyebut Scultone sebagai hewan mirip reptil seperti naga yang membunuh manusia dan hewan; di dekat Baunei, kaburnya naga ini konon membuka jurang Golgo. Situs pariwisata Baunei menyebut monster itu "Sa Serpente", sejenis naga jahat yang kadang keluar dari jurang Golgo dan menuntut korban manusia. Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Korsika, ia hidup di antara semak-semak dan abadi.

Konon Rasul Petrus yang mengalahkannya. Satu versi menyebut tatapan Scultone mematikan sehingga Petrus memandangnya lewat cermin kecil dan membuatnya tenggelam ke perut bumi; versi lain menyebut Petrus melemparkan monster itu ke tanah sehingga Su Sterru membuka dan menelannya. Portal pariwisata Sardinia menyebut jurang itu sebagai sarang ular dan ancamannya dijauhkan dengan pembangunan gereja Santo Petrus di dekatnya.

Scultone muncul dalam wujud basilisk sebagai lawan utama dalam komik Martin Mystère dan menjadi salah satu tokoh buku La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. Sebuah artikel mencatat bahwa seperti basilisk, ia dapat membunuh dengan tatapan dan dilawan dengan cermin.
long_description.en:
Sardinian folk legends describe the Scultone as a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals; near Baunei its flight is said to have opened the Golgo chasm. The Baunei tourism site calls the monster "Sa Serpente", a sort of evil dragon that sometimes came out of the Golgo chasm demanding human sacrifices. According to the Corsican-language Wikipedia article, it lived among the shrubs and was immortal.

The apostle Peter is said to have defeated it. One version says the Scultone's gaze could kill, so Peter looked at it through a small mirror and sank it into the earth; another says Peter threw the monster to the ground so that Su Sterru opened and swallowed it. The Sardinian tourism portal calls the chasm a serpent's lair whose threat was averted by building the nearby church of Saint Peter.

It appears as a basilisk, the main antagonist of a Martin Mystère comic, and is one of the protagonists of the book La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. An article notes that, like the basilisk, it can kill with its gaze and is fought with a mirror.

short_description.id: Scultone adalah makhluk mirip naga atau ular dalam legenda Sardinia yang tatapannya dapat membunuh dan yang menuntut korban manusia di sekitar Baunei, sebelum dikalahkan oleh Rasul Petrus.
short_description.en: The Scultone is a dragon-like or serpent creature of Sardinian legend whose gaze could kill and which demanded human sacrifices around Baunei before the apostle Peter defeated it.

long_description.id: Legenda rakyat Sardinia menyebut Scultone sebagai hewan mirip reptil seperti naga yang membunuh manusia dan hewan; di dekat Baunei, kaburnya naga ini konon membuka jurang Golgo. Situs pariwisata Baunei menyebut monster itu "Sa Serpente", sejenis naga jahat yang kadang keluar dari jurang Golgo dan menuntut korban manusia. Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Korsika, ia hidup di antara semak-semak dan abadi.
long_description.en: Sardinian folk legends describe the Scultone as a reptile-like, dragon-like animal that killed people and animals; near Baunei its flight is said to have opened the Golgo chasm. The Baunei tourism site calls the monster "Sa Serpente", a sort of evil dragon that sometimes came out of the Golgo chasm demanding human sacrifices. According to the Corsican-language Wikipedia article, it lived among the shrubs and was immortal.

long_description.id: Konon Rasul Petrus yang mengalahkannya. Satu versi menyebut tatapan Scultone mematikan sehingga Petrus memandangnya lewat cermin kecil dan membuatnya tenggelam ke perut bumi; versi lain menyebut Petrus melemparkan monster itu ke tanah sehingga Su Sterru membuka dan menelannya. Portal pariwisata Sardinia menyebut jurang itu sebagai sarang ular dan ancamannya dijauhkan dengan pembangunan gereja Santo Petrus di dekatnya.
long_description.en: The apostle Peter is said to have defeated it. One version says the Scultone's gaze could kill, so Peter looked at it through a small mirror and sank it into the earth; another says Peter threw the monster to the ground so that Su Sterru opened and swallowed it. The Sardinian tourism portal calls the chasm a serpent's lair whose threat was averted by building the nearby church of Saint Peter.

long_description.id: Scultone muncul dalam wujud basilisk sebagai lawan utama dalam komik Martin Mystère dan menjadi salah satu tokoh buku La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. Sebuah artikel mencatat bahwa seperti basilisk, ia dapat membunuh dengan tatapan dan dilawan dengan cermin.
long_description.en: It appears as a basilisk, the main antagonist of a Martin Mystère comic, and is one of the protagonists of the book La Dottoressa Heja e il Drago dei Nuraghi. An article notes that, like the basilisk, it can kill with its gaze and is fought with a mirror.

short_description.id: Naga putih adalah naga Tiongkok yang secara tradisional melayani kaisar langit.
short_description.en: The white dragon is a Chinese dragon traditionally serving the celestial emperor.

long_description.id:
Naga putih adalah naga Tiongkok yang secara tradisional melayani kaisar langit. Kisah memberinya penerbangan sangat cepat dan perubahan sesekali menjadi ikan.

Novel Jepang memberi penerbangannya cahaya serta gelombang dan bahan yang dimuntahkannya efek pembentuk emas. Versi lain mengaitkan naga putih dengan perlindungan barat melalui simbolisme Lima Unsur.

Dalam Taoisme, naga putih yang dipersonifikasikan bernama Raja Naga Putih Laut Barat, Ao Run. Di Korea, naga putih lebih sering muncul dalam legenda dibanding naga lain, tampaknya karena puting beliung air putih di laut dianggap naga putih.
long_description.en:
The white dragon is a Chinese dragon traditionally serving the celestial emperor. Accounts give it especially fast flight and occasional transformations into a fish.

A Japanese novel gives its flight light and waves and its expelled material a gold-making effect. A variant associates the white dragon with western protection through Five Elements symbolism.

In Taoism, the personified white dragon is the White Dragon King of the Western Sea, Ao Run. In Korea the white dragon appears in legends more than other dragons, apparently because white waterspouts at sea were taken for white dragons.

claims_provenance.quote: 白竜（はくりゅう、白龍、拼音: báilóng パイロン）は、古代中国で、天上界の皇帝である天帝に仕えているとされた竜の一種。名前のとおり、全身の鱗が白い。

claim.id: Kisah memberinya penerbangan sangat cepat dan perubahan sesekali menjadi ikan.
claim.en: Accounts give it especially fast flight and occasional transformations into a fish.

claims_provenance.quote: 竜は基本的に空を飛べるが、白竜は特に空を飛ぶ速度が速く、これに乗っていれば他の竜に追いつかれないともいう。ときおり魚に化けて地上の泉などで泳いでいることもある。

claim.id: Novel Jepang memberi penerbangannya cahaya serta gelombang dan bahan yang dimuntahkannya efek pembentuk emas.
claim.en: A Japanese novel gives its flight light and waves and its expelled material a gold-making effect.

claims_provenance.quote: 曲亭馬琴の読本『南総里見八犬伝』にも登場し、白竜が光を放ち、波を巻きたてながら南の方へ飛んで行くという場面があり、白竜が物を吐くとそれが地面に入って金になるという解説がついている。

claim.id: Versi lain mengaitkan naga putih dengan perlindungan barat melalui simbolisme Lima Unsur.
claim.en: A variant associates the white dragon with western protection through Five Elements symbolism.

claims_provenance.quote: 五行思想においては、白は西を意味するため、白竜を白虎と同様、西方を守護する神聖な竜とする異説がある。

claim.id: Dalam Taoisme, naga putih yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai dewa bernama Raja Naga Putih Laut Barat, Ao Run (西海白龍王敖潤).
claim.en: In Taoism, the white dragon personified as a deity is named the White Dragon King of the Western Sea, Ao Run (西海白龍王敖潤).

claims_provenance.quote: 도교에서 백룡을 인격신화한 이름은 서해백룡왕오윤(西海白龍王敖潤)이다.

claim.id: Di Korea, naga putih lebih sering muncul dalam legenda dibanding naga lain; ini tampaknya karena puting beliung air putih di laut (용오름) dianggap naga putih.
claim.en: In Korea the white dragon appears in legends more often than other dragons, apparently because white waterspouts at sea (용오름) were thought to be white dragons.

claims_provenance.quote: 한국에는 유독 백룡이 다른 용에 비해 전설에 많이 전해지는 편이다. 이것은 바다의 흰색 물기둥인 용오름을 백룡으로 생각한 소산으로 보인다.

statement.id: Kisah memberinya penerbangan sangat cepat dan perubahan sesekali menjadi ikan.
statement.en: Accounts give it especially fast flight and occasional transformations into a fish.

claims.quote: 曲亭馬琴の読本『南総里見八犬伝』にも登場し、白竜が光を放ち、波を巻きたてながら南の方へ飛んで行くという場面があり、白竜が物を吐くとそれが地面に入って金になるという解説がついている。

statement.id: Novel Jepang memberi penerbangannya cahaya serta gelombang dan bahan yang dimuntahkannya efek pembentuk emas.
statement.en: A Japanese novel gives its flight light and waves and its expelled material a gold-making effect.

claims.quote: 五行思想においては、白は西を意味するため、白竜を白虎と同様、西方を守護する神聖な竜とする異説がある。

statement.id: Versi lain mengaitkan naga putih dengan perlindungan barat melalui simbolisme Lima Unsur.
statement.en: A variant associates the white dragon with western protection through Five Elements symbolism.

claims.quote: 도교에서 백룡을 인격신화한 이름은 서해백룡왕오윤(西海白龍王敖潤)이다.

statement.id: Dalam Taoisme, naga putih yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai dewa bernama Raja Naga Putih Laut Barat, Ao Run (西海白龍王敖潤).
statement.en: In Taoism, the white dragon personified as a deity is named the White Dragon King of the Western Sea, Ao Run (西海白龍王敖潤).

claims.quote: 한국에는 유독 백룡이 다른 용에 비해 전설에 많이 전해지는 편이다. 이것은 바다의 흰색 물기둥인 용오름을 백룡으로 생각한 소산으로 보인다.

statement.id: Di Korea, naga putih lebih sering muncul dalam legenda dibanding naga lain; ini tampaknya karena puting beliung air putih di laut (용오름) dianggap naga putih.
statement.en: In Korea the white dragon appears in legends more often than other dragons, apparently because white waterspouts at sea (용오름) were thought to be white dragons.

short_description.id: Fuxi (負屓) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang gemar membaca dan menulis; sosoknya dilukiskan melilit puncak atau sisi prasasti batu.
short_description.en: Fuxi (負屓) is one of the dragon's nine sons, fond of reading and writing; its likeness is shown coiling around the top or sides of stone steles.

long_description.id:
Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 負屓 adalah salah satu putra naga dalam uraian Li Dongyang di 懐麓堂集. Ia gemar membaca dan menulis, sehingga digambarkan melilit puncak prasasti batu. Tafsir harfiah aksara namanya mengacu pada memikul beban berat: 『贔』 menggambarkan banyaknya harta, sedangkan 『屓』 adalah 『贔』 yang ditambah 『尸』 dan bermakna menanggung harta.

Dalam Shuo Lüe karya Gu Qiyuan (Ming), putra naga yang gemar sastra dan berada di sisi prasasti ditulis 屓屭. Penulisnya menjelaskan bahwa aksara 屓 dan 屭 punya ragam tulisan lain, termasuk 贔, dan mengutip kamus Yunhui bahwa artinya perawakan besar atau kura-kura laut raksasa, sedangkan Guangyun menyebutnya "orang kuat yang mengerahkan tenaga". Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 负屃 sebagai putra kedelapan naga yang gemar sastra, dengan naga-naga bersastra di kedua sisi prasasti sebagai sosoknya.

Sumber-sumber tidak sepakat tentang kegemaran putra naga di prasasti. Yŏrha ilgi mengutip Zonggui bahwa 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di kedua sisi tulisan prasasti, tetapi Bowuzhi yipian menyebut 贔屭 gemar beban dan memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 yang gemar hiasan sastra berdiri di atas tulisan. Penulisnya mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan Gu Qiyuan sendiri tidak menemukan satu pun nama dalam daftar yang dibahasnya tercatat sebagai putra naga.
long_description.en:
According to Japanese Wikipedia, 負屓 is one of the dragon's sons in Li Dongyang's account in the 懐麓堂集. It is fond of reading and writing, which is why it is depicted coiling around the top of stone steles. A literal reading of the characters of its name refers to bearing a heavy load: 『贔』 conveys abundance of goods, while 『屓』 is 『贔』 with 『尸』 added and means holding on to treasure.

In Gu Qiyuan's Shuo Lüe (Ming), the dragon's son that likes literature and is at the sides of steles is written 屓屭. Its author explains that the characters 屓 and 屭 have variant forms, including 贔, and quotes the dictionary Yunhui that the word means a huge appearance or a giant sea turtle, while the Guangyun calls it "a strong man exerting strength". Chinese Wikipedia calls 负屃 the eighth son of the dragon, fond of literature, with the literary dragons at both sides of steles as its likeness.

Sources disagree about what the dragon's son at the stele likes. The Yŏrha ilgi quotes the Zonggui that 贔屭 likes literature and so is at both sides of the inscription, but the Bowuzhi yipian says 贔屭 likes heavy loads and carries the stele, while 螭虎, which likes literary ornament, stands on the inscription. Its author asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and Gu Qiyuan himself found none of the names in the list he discusses recorded as a dragon's son.

claim.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 屓屭 yang gemar sastra (好文) dan berada di sisi prasasti (在碑兩傍). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
claim.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 屓屭, which likes literature (好文) and is at the sides of steles (在碑兩傍). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

claims_provenance.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource — 說略/卷三十 | 維基文庫

claim.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe menjelaskan 屓屭: aksara 屓 dan 屭 punya ragam tulisan lain (termasuk 贔); menurut kamus Yunhui (韻會) artinya perawakan besar, juga 鼇 (kura-kura laut raksasa), dan menurut Guangyun (廣韻) "orang kuat yang mengerahkan tenaga"; ia mengutip Xijing fu (西京賦) dan Wu du fu (吳都賦) tentang 贔屓. Ia tidak menemukan satu pun nama yang dibahasnya dalam catatan sebagai putra naga; 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 ia tinggalkan untuk diteliti.
claim.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe glosses 屓屭: the characters 屓 and 屭 have variant forms (including 贔); according to the dictionary Yunhui (韻會) it means a huge appearance, also the 鼇 (giant sea turtle), and according to the Guangyun (廣韻) "a strong man exerting strength"; he cites the Xijing fu (西京賦) and the Wu du fu (吳都賦) on 贔屓. He found none of the names he discusses described in records as a dragon's son, and left 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 for further examination.

claims_provenance.quote: 屓屭，屓一作𤣂，一作贔。屭，一作㞒。《韻會》狀大貌。又鼇也。一曰雌鼇為屓。《廣韻》壯士作力貌。〈西京賦〉巨靈贔屓。〈吳都賦〉巨鼇贔屓。 ... 已上都不見有龍子之說，囚牛、嘲風、霸下，俟考。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource — 說略/卷三十 | 維基文庫

claim.id: Dalam Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) menyebut 贔屭 gemar beban sehingga memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 yang gemar hiasan sastra berdiri di atas tulisan prasasti; Zonggui (總龜) menyebut 覇夏 gemar memikul beban sehingga menjadi alas prasasti dan 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di kedua sisi tulisan prasasti. Penulisnya menyatakan pendapat-pendapat itu berbeda-beda, mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
claim.en: In the Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): the Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) says 贔屭 likes heavy things and so carries steles, while 螭虎, which likes literary ornament, stands on the inscription; the Zonggui (總龜) says 覇夏 likes bearing loads and so serves as a stele base, and 贔屭 likes literature and so is found at both sides of the inscription. The author says the accounts differ, asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and says old theories of this kind are mostly embellishment.

claims_provenance.quote: 又博物逸篇云。贔屭。性好重。故載碑。螭虎。形似龍。性好文釆。故立于碑文上。又總龜云。龍之九子。一名覇夏。好負重。故爲碑座。贔屭。好文故在碑文兩旁。諸說亦各不同。龍子名號及性情。何以知之。古說傅會多此類。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource — 熱河日記/卷17 | 維基文庫

claim.id: Catatan dalam Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 负屃 (Fùxì) sebagai putra kedelapan naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, berbentuk seperti naga, gemar sastra (平生好文), dan naga-naga bersastra di kedua sisi prasasti adalah sosoknya.
claim.en: A note in Chinese Wikipedia calls 负屃 (Fùxì) the eighth son of the dragon in Chinese mythology, dragon-shaped, fond of literature (平生好文), with the literary dragons at both sides of steles as its likeness.

claims_provenance.quote: 负屃是中国神话中龙的第八个儿子。似龙形，排行老八，平生好文，石碑两旁的文龙是其遗像。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikipedia — 負屭 | 維基百科

research_gaps.note: Belum ada berkas Wikimedia Commons yang diperiksa untuk entri ini.

Wikipedia bahasa Jepang dan Tionghoa dibaca; teks asli 懐麓堂集 di Wikisource tidak memakai tanda baca sehingga tidak bisa dikutip otomatis; dipakai teks bertanda baca yang memuat daftar serupa (說略, 熱河日記). Nama putra naga ini ditulis berbeda antar sumber (負屓/負屭/负屃 di Wikipedia; 屓屭 di Shuo Lüe; 贔屭 di Yŏrha ilgi): kesamaan didasarkan pada peran yang sama (gemar sastra, di prasasti) dan kesamaan aksara 屓, bukan pernyataan eksplisit satu sumber.

statement.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 屓屭 yang gemar sastra (好文) dan berada di sisi prasasti (在碑兩傍). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
statement.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 屓屭, which likes literature (好文) and is at the sides of steles (在碑兩傍). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

claims.quote: 屓屭，屓一作𤣂，一作贔。屭，一作㞒。《韻會》狀大貌。又鼇也。一曰雌鼇為屓。《廣韻》壯士作力貌。〈西京賦〉巨靈贔屓。〈吳都賦〉巨鼇贔屓。 ... 已上都不見有龍子之說，囚牛、嘲風、霸下，俟考。

statement.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe menjelaskan 屓屭: aksara 屓 dan 屭 punya ragam tulisan lain (termasuk 贔); menurut kamus Yunhui (韻會) artinya perawakan besar, juga 鼇 (kura-kura laut raksasa), dan menurut Guangyun (廣韻) "orang kuat yang mengerahkan tenaga"; ia mengutip Xijing fu (西京賦) dan Wu du fu (吳都賦) tentang 贔屓. Ia tidak menemukan satu pun nama yang dibahasnya dalam catatan sebagai putra naga; 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 ia tinggalkan untuk diteliti.
statement.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe glosses 屓屭: the characters 屓 and 屭 have variant forms (including 贔); according to the dictionary Yunhui (韻會) it means a huge appearance, also the 鼇 (giant sea turtle), and according to the Guangyun (廣韻) "a strong man exerting strength"; he cites the Xijing fu (西京賦) and the Wu du fu (吳都賦) on 贔屓. He found none of the names he discusses described in records as a dragon's son, and left 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 for further examination.

claims.quote: 又博物逸篇云。贔屭。性好重。故載碑。螭虎。形似龍。性好文釆。故立于碑文上。又總龜云。龍之九子。一名覇夏。好負重。故爲碑座。贔屭。好文故在碑文兩旁。諸說亦各不同。龍子名號及性情。何以知之。古說傅會多此類。

statement.id: Dalam Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) menyebut 贔屭 gemar beban sehingga memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 yang gemar hiasan sastra berdiri di atas tulisan prasasti; Zonggui (總龜) menyebut 覇夏 gemar memikul beban sehingga menjadi alas prasasti dan 贔屭 gemar sastra sehingga berada di kedua sisi tulisan prasasti. Penulisnya menyatakan pendapat-pendapat itu berbeda-beda, mempertanyakan bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
statement.en: In the Yŏrha ilgi (熱河日記): the Bowuzhi yipian (博物志逸篇) says 贔屭 likes heavy things and so carries steles, while 螭虎, which likes literary ornament, stands on the inscription; the Zonggui (總龜) says 覇夏 likes bearing loads and so serves as a stele base, and 贔屭 likes literature and so is found at both sides of the inscription. The author says the accounts differ, asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and says old theories of this kind are mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 负屃是中国神话中龙的第八个儿子。似龙形，排行老八，平生好文，石碑两旁的文龙是其遗像。

statement.id: Catatan dalam Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 负屃 (Fùxì) sebagai putra kedelapan naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok, berbentuk seperti naga, gemar sastra (平生好文), dan naga-naga bersastra di kedua sisi prasasti adalah sosoknya.
statement.en: A note in Chinese Wikipedia calls 负屃 (Fùxì) the eighth son of the dragon in Chinese mythology, dragon-shaped, fond of literature (平生好文), with the literary dragons at both sides of steles as its likeness.

topic.id: Apa yang digemari putra naga pada prasasti: sastra atau memikul beban
topic.en: What the dragon's son at the stele likes: literature or bearing loads

summary.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang dan Tionghoa, Shuo Lüe, serta Zonggui (dikutip Yŏrha ilgi): gemar sastra dan berada di sisi atau puncak prasasti.
summary.en: Japanese and Chinese Wikipedia, the Shuo Lüe and the Zonggui (quoted in the Yŏrha ilgi): fond of literature and at the sides or top of steles.

summary.id: Bowuzhi yipian (dikutip Yŏrha ilgi): 贔屭 gemar beban dan memikul prasasti, sedangkan 螭虎 gemar hiasan sastra; tafsir harfiah 負屓 pun mengacu pada memikul beban.
summary.en: Bowuzhi yipian (quoted in the Yŏrha ilgi): 贔屭 likes heavy loads and carries the stele, while 螭虎 likes literary ornament; the literal reading of 負屓 likewise refers to bearing a load.

short_description.id: Jiguang adalah hewan ajaib pembawa keberuntungan dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Jiguang is an auspicious fabulous animal in Chinese mythology.

long_description.id:
Jiguang adalah hewan ajaib pembawa keberuntungan dalam mitologi Tiongkok. Salah satu uraian memberinya bentuk kuda putih berpola dengan surai merah yang lahir di rawa besar.

Jiguang kerap dicampur dengan Tenghuang, sementara bentuk rubah dan kuda berbeda menurut versinya. Ungkapan Jiguang pianyu memakai sehelai bulunya sebagai kiasan untuk peninggalan atau dokumen langka.

Sumber-sumber klasik memberi gambaran yang beragam. 名馬記 mengutip 《山海經》 tentang kuda berpola bertubuh putih dan bersurai merah bernama 吉良, sedangkan kutipan 《瑞應圖》 menyebut 騰黃 yang kuning juga bernama 吉光. Baopuzi menyebut 騰黃之馬 dan 吉光之獸 sama-sama berumur tiga ribu tahun, dan 《海內十洲記》 menyebut mantel bulu 吉光 berwarna kuning, golongan kuda ajaib, yang tidak tenggelam di air dan tidak hangus di api.
long_description.en:
Jiguang is an auspicious fabulous animal in Chinese mythology. One description gives it the form of a patterned white horse with a red mane, born in a great marsh.

Jiguang is often confused with Tenghuang, while fox and horse forms differ between versions. The expression Jiguang pianyu uses a strand of its fur as a metaphor for rare relics or documents.

Classical sources give varied pictures. The 名馬記 quotes the 《山海經》 on a patterned horse with a white body and red mane named 吉良, while a quoted 《瑞應圖》 passage says the yellow 騰黃 is also named 吉光. The Baopuzi says both the 騰黃 horse and the 吉光 beast live three thousand years, and the 《海內十洲記》 says the 吉光 fur coat is yellow, of the divine-horse kind, and neither sinks in water nor scorches in fire.

topic.en: Colour and identity of 吉光

summary.en: The quoted 《瑞應圖》: 吉光 is another name of the yellow 騰黃; the 《海內十洲記》 calls its fur yellow.

short_description.id: Xolotl adalah dewa Aztec yang digambarkan berkepala anjing, pengantar jiwa orang mati, dan saudara kembar Quetzalcōātl.
short_description.en: Xolotl is an Aztec god depicted with a dog's head, a guide of the dead, and the twin brother of Quetzalcōātl.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp. Ia juga disebut dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan. Dalam kodeks dan arca Aztec ia tampil sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing, dan ia dikenal sebagai dewa anjing bangsa Mexica.

Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl, dan ia disebut personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja. Satu sumber menyebut tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut ia menemani Quetzalcoatl mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan manusia. Sebagai psikopomp ia menuntun orang mati ke Mictlān, dan anjing yang mungkin menjelmakan perannya dipercaya menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah dan membantu menyeberangi perairan.

Dalam mitos pengorbanan para dewa demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri. Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri: ia menjadi tanaman jagung ganda, lalu tanaman maguey ganda, lalu salamander yang hingga kini dinamai axolotl, tetapi akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lain. Versi lain menyebut ia menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
long_description.en:
In Aztec mythology Xolotl is a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp. He is also named god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities. In Aztec codices and statuary he appears as a dog or a god with a dog's head, and he is known as the dog god of the Mexica people.

Xolotl is the canine twin brother of Quetzalcōātl and is described as the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star. One source says his task was shielding the sun from underworld perils, while another says he went with Quetzalcoatl to fetch bones from the underworld so that people could be made. As a psychopomp he guides the dead to Mictlān, and dogs that may embody his role are said to have guided their masters into the Underworld and helped them cross water.

In the myth of the gods sacrificing themselves for the newly created sun, the gods decided to give their lives. Xolotl tried to escape: he turned into a double maize plant, then a doubled maguey plant, then a salamander still named axolotl, but he was ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the other gods. In the Teotihuacan legend he wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claim.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp (pengantar jiwa). Ia juga dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan.
claim.en: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl was a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp, and also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

claims_provenance.quote: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl ... was a god of fire and lightning. He was commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and was a psychopomp. He was also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

claim.id: Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl; keduanya putra Chīmalmā yang masih perawan. Ia adalah personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja (Evening Star) dan dikaitkan dengan api surgawi.
claim.en: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā; he is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star and was associated with heavenly fire.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā. He is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star, and was associated with heavenly fire.

claim.id: Xolotl disebut dewa kengerian (monstrosities) yang sinis dan mengenakan permata angin berbentuk kerang milik Quetzalcōātl. Tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah.
claim.en: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl, and his job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like ehēcailacacōcatl "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl. His job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

claim.id: Rongga matanya yang kosong dijelaskan dalam legenda Teotihuacan: ketika para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, Xolotl mundur dari pengorbanan itu dan menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
claim.en: Xolotl's empty eye sockets are explained by the Teotihuacan legend in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun; Xolotl withdrew from the sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claims_provenance.quote: His empty eye sockets are explained in the legend of Teotihuacan, in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun. Xolotl withdrew from this sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claim.id: Xolotl mengubah dirinya menjadi tanaman jagung muda berbatang dua (xolotl), tanaman maguey ganda (mexolotl), dan hewan amfibi (axolotl), sehingga disebut ahli transformasi. Pada akhirnya Ehecatl berhasil menemukan dan membunuhnya.
claim.en: Xolotl transformed himself into a young two-stalked maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and an amphibious animal (axolotl), and is thus a master transformer; in the end Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing him.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl transformed himself into a young maize plant with two stalks (xolotl), a doubled maguey plant (mexolotl), and an amphibious animal (axolotl). Xolotl is thus a master transformer. In the end, Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing Xolotl.

claim.id: Sebagai psikopomp, Xolotl menuntun orang mati dalam perjalanan ke Mictlān, alam baka dalam mitos. Dua wujud hewan rohnya adalah anjing ras xoloitzcuintle dan salamander air yang disebut axolotl.
claim.en: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths; his two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle dog breed and the aquatic salamander known as the axolotl.

claims_provenance.quote: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths. His two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle breed of dog and the aquatic salamander species known as the axolotl.

claim.id: Xolotl adalah dewa anjing bangsa Mexica, yang lazim dikenal sebagai Aztec. Dalam kodeks, arca, dan karya seni Aztec lain yang masih ada, ia digambarkan sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing.
claim.en: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs, and is represented in codices, statuary, and other surviving Aztec art as a dog or a god with a dog's head.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs. He is represented in codices, statuary, and other extant examples of Aztec art as a dog or a god with the head of a dog.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Meskipun kembar umumnya dianggap pertanda buruk dan dipandang dengan waswas dalam peradaban Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa pelindung kembar dan orang dengan kelainan fisik, yang menjadi bahan ketertarikan dalam budaya Mesoamerika.
claim.en: Although twins were generally seen as a bad omen in Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

claims_provenance.quote: While twins were generally seen as a bad omen and viewed with trepidation in the Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, which were a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl dalam misinya mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan umat manusia.
claim.en: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Ketika sebagian besar dewa rela mengorbankan diri, Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri.
claim.en: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

claims_provenance.quote: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, setting a mythic precedent for the Aztec culture of human sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Xolotl pertama kali mencoba kabur dengan menjadi tanaman jagung ganda. Ketika ketahuan, ia menjadi tanaman maguey ganda, dan ketika itu pun gagal menyembunyikannya, ia menjadi salamander yang hingga kini dikenal dengan nama Nahuatl axolotl.
claim.en: Xolotl first tries to escape by turning into a double maize plant; when discovered he becomes a doubled maguey plant, and when that fails to conceal him he becomes a salamander still known by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl makes his first attempt to escape by turning into a double maize plant. When he is discovered in that guise, he turns into a doubled maguey plant, and when that transformation fails to conceal him, he turns into a salamander still known today by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Bahkan dalam wujud axolotl, Xolotl akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lainnya.
claim.en: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods.

claims_provenance.quote: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Anjing, yang mungkin menjelmakan peran Xolotl, menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah setelah mati dan sangat berguna untuk menyeberangi perairan.
claim.en: Dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water.

claims_provenance.quote: dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Kata axolotl adalah gabungan istilah Nahuatl xolotl dan atl yang berarti "air", sehingga kira-kira dapat diterjemahkan sebagai "kembar air".
claim.en: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl and atl, meaning "water", and so could be roughly translated as "water twin".

claims_provenance.quote: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl (explained above) and atl, meaning "water," and so could be roughly translated as "water twin."
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Penghormatan kepada Xolotl juga muncul dalam film Disney Coco (2017) berupa seekor anjing bernama Dante.
claim.en: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog named Dante.

claims_provenance.quote: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog poignantly named Dante.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claim.id: Xolotl adalah pelindung permainan bola Mesoamerika. Sebagian sarjana berpendapat permainan itu melambangkan perjalanan malam Matahari yang berbahaya melalui dunia bawah; Xolotl dapat membantu kelahiran kembali Matahari karena ia berkuasa keluar-masuk dunia bawah.
claim.en: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame, which some scholars say symbolizes the Sun's perilous nighttime journey through the underworld; Xolotl can help the Sun's rebirth because he has the power to enter and exit the underworld.

claims_provenance.quote: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame. Some scholars argue the ballgame symbolizes the Sun's perilous and uncertain nighttime journey through the underworld. Xolotl is able to help in the Sun's rebirth since he possesses the power to enter and exit the underworld.

note.id: Saudara kembar berwujud anjing; keduanya putra Chīmalmā. Xolotl juga menemani Quetzalcoatl ke dunia bawah.
note.en: His twin brother; both are sons of Chīmalmā. Xolotl also accompanied Quetzalcoatl to the underworld.

description.en: The Disney film includes an homage to Xolotl in the form of a dog named Dante.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa dewa yang dihubungkan dengan anjing dan kembar bisa memiliki peran sebagai pengantar jiwa?
learning_questions.en: Why might a god linked to dogs and twins have a role as a guide of souls?

learning_questions.id: Apa arti perubahan wujud Xolotl menjadi beberapa makhluk dalam kisah pengorbanan para dewa?

sources.author: Jordy Samuels
sources.title: Xolotl: The Dog God of the Aztecs

claims.quote: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl ... was a god of fire and lightning. He was commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and was a psychopomp. He was also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa api dan petir yang lazim digambarkan sebagai pria berkepala anjing dan menjadi psikopomp (pengantar jiwa). Ia juga dewa kembar, monster, kematian, kemalangan, penyakit, dan kecacatan.
statement.en: In Aztec mythology, Xolotl was a god of fire and lightning, commonly depicted as a dog-headed man and a psychopomp, and also god of twins, monsters, death, misfortune, sickness, and deformities.

claims.quote: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā. He is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star, and was associated with heavenly fire.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah saudara kembar berwujud anjing dari Quetzalcōātl; keduanya putra Chīmalmā yang masih perawan. Ia adalah personifikasi gelap planet Venus sebagai Bintang Senja (Evening Star) dan dikaitkan dengan api surgawi.
statement.en: Xolotl is the canine brother and twin of Quetzalcōātl, the pair being sons of the virgin Chīmalmā; he is the dark personification of Venus as the Evening Star and was associated with heavenly fire.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like ehēcailacacōcatl "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl. His job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

statement.id: Xolotl disebut dewa kengerian (monstrosities) yang sinis dan mengenakan permata angin berbentuk kerang milik Quetzalcōātl. Tugasnya melindungi matahari dari bahaya dunia bawah.
statement.en: Xolotl was the sinister god of monstrosities who wears the conch-like "twisted wind jewel" of Quetzalcōātl, and his job was to protect the sun from the dangers of the underworld.

claims.quote: His empty eye sockets are explained in the legend of Teotihuacan, in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun. Xolotl withdrew from this sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

statement.id: Rongga matanya yang kosong dijelaskan dalam legenda Teotihuacan: ketika para dewa memutuskan mengorbankan diri demi matahari yang baru diciptakan, Xolotl mundur dari pengorbanan itu dan menangis begitu lama hingga matanya jatuh dari rongganya.
statement.en: Xolotl's empty eye sockets are explained by the Teotihuacan legend in which the gods decided to sacrifice themselves for the newly created sun; Xolotl withdrew from the sacrifice and wept so much that his eyes fell out of their sockets.

claims.quote: Xolotl transformed himself into a young maize plant with two stalks (xolotl), a doubled maguey plant (mexolotl), and an amphibious animal (axolotl). Xolotl is thus a master transformer. In the end, Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing Xolotl.

statement.id: Xolotl mengubah dirinya menjadi tanaman jagung muda berbatang dua (xolotl), tanaman maguey ganda (mexolotl), dan hewan amfibi (axolotl), sehingga disebut ahli transformasi. Pada akhirnya Ehecatl berhasil menemukan dan membunuhnya.
statement.en: Xolotl transformed himself into a young two-stalked maize plant, a doubled maguey plant, and an amphibious animal (axolotl), and is thus a master transformer; in the end Ehecatl succeeded in finding and killing him.

claims.quote: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths. His two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle breed of dog and the aquatic salamander species known as the axolotl.

statement.id: Sebagai psikopomp, Xolotl menuntun orang mati dalam perjalanan ke Mictlān, alam baka dalam mitos. Dua wujud hewan rohnya adalah anjing ras xoloitzcuintle dan salamander air yang disebut axolotl.
statement.en: As a psychopomp, Xolotl would guide the dead on their journey to Mictlān, the afterlife in myths; his two spirit animal forms are the xoloitzcuintle dog breed and the aquatic salamander known as the axolotl.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs. He is represented in codices, statuary, and other extant examples of Aztec art as a dog or a god with the head of a dog.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah dewa anjing bangsa Mexica, yang lazim dikenal sebagai Aztec. Dalam kodeks, arca, dan karya seni Aztec lain yang masih ada, ia digambarkan sebagai anjing atau dewa berkepala anjing.
statement.en: Xolotl was the dog god of the Mexica people, commonly known as the Aztecs, and is represented in codices, statuary, and other surviving Aztec art as a dog or a god with a dog's head.

claims.quote: While twins were generally seen as a bad omen and viewed with trepidation in the Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, which were a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

statement.id: Meskipun kembar umumnya dianggap pertanda buruk dan dipandang dengan waswas dalam peradaban Aztec, Xolotl adalah dewa pelindung kembar dan orang dengan kelainan fisik, yang menjadi bahan ketertarikan dalam budaya Mesoamerika.
statement.en: Although twins were generally seen as a bad omen in Aztec civilization, Xolotl was the patron god of twins and individuals with physical abnormalities, a subject of fascination in Mesoamerican cultures.

claims.quote: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity

statement.id: Xolotl menemani Quetzalcoatl dalam misinya mengambil tulang-tulang dari dunia bawah untuk menciptakan umat manusia.
statement.en: Xolotl accompanied Quetzalcoatl on his mission to retrieve bones from the underworld in order to create humanity.

claims.quote: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, setting a mythic precedent for the Aztec culture of human sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

statement.id: Ketika sebagian besar dewa rela mengorbankan diri, Xolotl berusaha melarikan diri.
statement.en: While most of the gods willingly offer themselves for sacrifice, Xolotl attempts to escape.

claims.quote: Xolotl makes his first attempt to escape by turning into a double maize plant. When he is discovered in that guise, he turns into a doubled maguey plant, and when that transformation fails to conceal him, he turns into a salamander still known today by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

statement.id: Xolotl pertama kali mencoba kabur dengan menjadi tanaman jagung ganda. Ketika ketahuan, ia menjadi tanaman maguey ganda, dan ketika itu pun gagal menyembunyikannya, ia menjadi salamander yang hingga kini dikenal dengan nama Nahuatl axolotl.
statement.en: Xolotl first tries to escape by turning into a double maize plant; when discovered he becomes a doubled maguey plant, and when that fails to conceal him he becomes a salamander still known by its Nahuatl name, axolotl.

claims.quote: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods

statement.id: Bahkan dalam wujud axolotl, Xolotl akhirnya tertangkap dan dikorbankan bersama dewa-dewa lainnya.
statement.en: Even in the form of an axolotl, Xolotl is ultimately caught and sacrificed along with the rest of the gods.

claims.quote: dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water

statement.id: Anjing, yang mungkin menjelmakan peran Xolotl, menuntun tuannya ke Dunia Bawah setelah mati dan sangat berguna untuk menyeberangi perairan.
statement.en: Dogs, perhaps embodying the role of Xolotl, guided their masters into the Underworld after death and were of particular use in crossing bodies of water.

claims.quote: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl (explained above) and atl, meaning "water," and so could be roughly translated as "water twin."

statement.id: Kata axolotl adalah gabungan istilah Nahuatl xolotl dan atl yang berarti "air", sehingga kira-kira dapat diterjemahkan sebagai "kembar air".
statement.en: The word axolotl is a combination of the Nahuatl terms xolotl and atl, meaning "water", and so could be roughly translated as "water twin".

claims.quote: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog poignantly named Dante.

statement.id: Penghormatan kepada Xolotl juga muncul dalam film Disney Coco (2017) berupa seekor anjing bernama Dante.
statement.en: An homage to Xolotl also appears in the 2017 Disney film Coco in the form of a dog named Dante.

claims.quote: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame. Some scholars argue the ballgame symbolizes the Sun's perilous and uncertain nighttime journey through the underworld. Xolotl is able to help in the Sun's rebirth since he possesses the power to enter and exit the underworld.

statement.id: Xolotl adalah pelindung permainan bola Mesoamerika. Sebagian sarjana berpendapat permainan itu melambangkan perjalanan malam Matahari yang berbahaya melalui dunia bawah; Xolotl dapat membantu kelahiran kembali Matahari karena ia berkuasa keluar-masuk dunia bawah.
statement.en: Xolotl was the patron of the Mesoamerican ballgame, which some scholars say symbolizes the Sun's perilous nighttime journey through the underworld; Xolotl can help the Sun's rebirth because he has the power to enter and exit the underworld.

short_description.id: Yazi adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok, berkepala anjing liar, garang, dan gemar bertarung serta membunuh; rupanya diukir pada senjata.
short_description.en: Yazi is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition, with a wild dog's head, fierce, and fond of fighting and killing; its image is carved on weapons.

long_description.id:
Yazi (睚眦; Jepang: Gaisai) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Ia berkepala anjing liar, berwatak garang, dan gemar bertarung serta membunuh. Karena itu rupanya diukir pada cincin pedang, mulut sarung pedang, serta sabit dan tombak untuk eksekusi, dan banyak dipakai dalam gambar panji militer pada zaman kuno.

Shuolue mencatat bahwa kesembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang. Teks itu juga menceritakan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana menanyakan nama mereka, daftar itu didapat dari catatan lama yang asalnya tak diketahui, dan penulisnya menilainya tidak berdasar.

Nama 睚眦 sendiri terdiri atas huruf yang berarti tepi atau rongga mata dan "melotot"; artinya adalah menatap marah, dan secara luas "sedikit". Ungkapan 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji berarti dendam sekecil dipelototi.
long_description.en:
Yazi (睚眦; Japanese: Gaisai) is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition. It has a wild dog's head, a fierce temper, and a fondness for fighting and killing. For that reason its image is carved on sword rings, scabbard mouths, and on sickles and halberds for executions, and was much used in military banner designs in antiquity.

The Shuolue records that the dragon's nine sons are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts. It also tells that in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked for their names, the list was obtained from an old register of unknown origin, and its author judged it unfounded.

The name 睚眦 itself consists of characters meaning the edge or socket of the eye and "to glare"; it means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight". The phrase 睚眦之怨 in the Shiji means a grudge as small as being glared at.

literal_meaning.id: Gabungan huruf yang berarti sudut atau rongga mata dan "melotot"; arti kiasannya menatap marah atau "sedikit".
literal_meaning.en: A compound of characters meaning the corner or socket of the eye and "to glare"; extended meanings are looking in anger, or "slight".

claims_provenance.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claim.id: Ia memiliki kepala anjing liar.
claim.en: It has a wild dog’s head.

claims_provenance.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claim.id: Sifatnya ganas dan dikaitkan dengan pertempuran.
claim.en: Its character is fierce and associated with combat.

claims_provenance.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claim.id: Gambarnya terdapat pada senjata dan panji militer.
claim.en: Its image appears on weapons and military banners.

claims_provenance.quote: よって、刀の環（刀を佩びるための輪）や、剣の鯉口、武器や罪人を処刑するための鎌や矛に彫られ、古代（三国志時代）には軍旗などの図案に多く用いられた。

claim.id: Menurut Shuolue, sembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang; delapan lainnya adalah Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi, dan Chiwen.
claim.en: According to the Shuolue, the nine sons of the dragon are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts; the others are Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi and Chiwen.

claims_provenance.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。

claim.id: Menurut Shuolue, pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana bertanya tentang nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang tidak dapat menyebutkannya; Liu Ji lalu mendapatkannya dari sebuah catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui, dan penulis menilai uraian itu tidak berdasar (bujing).
claim.en: According to the Shuolue, in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked Li Dongyang for the names of the dragon's nine sons; he could not give them all, Liu Ji obtained them from an old register of unknown origin, and the author judged the account unfounded (bujing).

claims_provenance.quote: 弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。余憶十一、二時，曾見其說於《對類總龜》中，近因歴考傳記，乃知其說為不經。

claim.id: Menurut Shuolue, istilah 睚眦 muncul dalam Zhanguoce dengan kalimat "Orang berbudi tergerak oleh sedikit kemarahan"; catatannya menjelaskan ya sebagai "mengangkat mata" dan zi sebagai "rongga mata".
claim.en: According to the Shuolue, the term 睚眦 appears in the Zhanguoce in a line about the worthy being moved by a slight resentment; the note explains ya as "raising the eyes" and zi as "the eye socket".

claims_provenance.quote: 睚眦，《戰國策》聶政曰：賢者以感忿睚眦之意。注：睚，舉眼也；眦，目匡也。

claim.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 睚 berasal dari tepi mata dan 眦 dari bagian mata yang baru mulai terbuka; keduanya berarti sudut mata.
claim.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the character 睚 derives from the edge of the eye and 眦 from the part where the eye just begins to open; both mean the corner of the eye.

claims_provenance.quote: 『睚』の字の由来は目のきわ、『眦』は目のわずかに開きはじめた部分、で、どちらも、まなじりや目じりという意味である。

claim.id: Kedua huruf itu juga berarti "melotot"; 睚眦 berarti menatap marah dan, secara luas, "sedikit"; 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji adalah dendam setingkat dipelototi sedikit.
claim.en: Both characters also mean "to glare"; 睚眦 means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight"; the 睚眦之怨 of the Shiji is a grudge as small as being glared at.

claims_provenance.quote: また、どちらに字にも『にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『睚眦』には『目を怒らして見る。にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『わずか』という意味もある。史記・范雎伝にある『睚眦之怨』（がいさいのうらみ）は、ちょっとにらまれた程度の恨み、という意味である。

cultural_context.id: Karena wataknya yang garang dan gemar bertarung, wujud Yazi diukir pada cincin dan gagang senjata serta dipakai pada panji perang kuno; Shuolue mencatat bahwa ia dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang.
cultural_context.en: Because of its fierce, combative character, Yazi's image is carved on rings and hilts of weapons and used on ancient military banners; the Shuolue records that it is used to adorn sword hilts.

literal_meaning.id: Gabungan huruf yang berarti sudut atau rongga mata dan "melotot"; arti kiasannya menatap marah atau "sedikit".
literal_meaning.en: A compound of characters meaning the corner or socket of the eye and "to glare"; extended meanings are looking in anger, or "slight".

statement.en: Yazi is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition.

statement.id: Ia memiliki kepala anjing liar.
statement.en: It has a wild dog’s head.

claims.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

statement.id: Sifatnya ganas dan dikaitkan dengan pertempuran.
statement.en: Its character is fierce and associated with combat.

claims.quote: よって、刀の環（刀を佩びるための輪）や、剣の鯉口、武器や罪人を処刑するための鎌や矛に彫られ、古代（三国志時代）には軍旗などの図案に多く用いられた。

statement.id: Gambarnya terdapat pada senjata dan panji militer.
statement.en: Its image appears on weapons and military banners.

claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, sembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang; delapan lainnya adalah Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi, dan Chiwen.
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, the nine sons of the dragon are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts; the others are Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi and Chiwen.

claims.quote: 弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。余憶十一、二時，曾見其說於《對類總龜》中，近因歴考傳記，乃知其說為不經。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana bertanya tentang nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang tidak dapat menyebutkannya; Liu Ji lalu mendapatkannya dari sebuah catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui, dan penulis menilai uraian itu tidak berdasar (bujing).
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked Li Dongyang for the names of the dragon's nine sons; he could not give them all, Liu Ji obtained them from an old register of unknown origin, and the author judged the account unfounded (bujing).

claims.quote: 睚眦，《戰國策》聶政曰：賢者以感忿睚眦之意。注：睚，舉眼也；眦，目匡也。

statement.id: Menurut Shuolue, istilah 睚眦 muncul dalam Zhanguoce dengan kalimat "Orang berbudi tergerak oleh sedikit kemarahan"; catatannya menjelaskan ya sebagai "mengangkat mata" dan zi sebagai "rongga mata".
statement.en: According to the Shuolue, the term 睚眦 appears in the Zhanguoce in a line about the worthy being moved by a slight resentment; the note explains ya as "raising the eyes" and zi as "the eye socket".

claims.quote: 『睚』の字の由来は目のきわ、『眦』は目のわずかに開きはじめた部分、で、どちらも、まなじりや目じりという意味である。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 睚 berasal dari tepi mata dan 眦 dari bagian mata yang baru mulai terbuka; keduanya berarti sudut mata.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the character 睚 derives from the edge of the eye and 眦 from the part where the eye just begins to open; both mean the corner of the eye.

claims.quote: また、どちらに字にも『にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『睚眦』には『目を怒らして見る。にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『わずか』という意味もある。史記・范雎伝にある『睚眦之怨』（がいさいのうらみ）は、ちょっとにらまれた程度の恨み、という意味である。

statement.id: Kedua huruf itu juga berarti "melotot"; 睚眦 berarti menatap marah dan, secara luas, "sedikit"; 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji adalah dendam setingkat dipelototi sedikit.
statement.en: Both characters also mean "to glare"; 睚眦 means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight"; the 睚眦之怨 of the Shiji is a grudge as small as being glared at.

short_description.id: Animikii adalah burung guntur mitologis raksasa dalam tradisi suku Ojibwe dan beberapa suku lain. Guntur disebabkan oleh kepakan sayapnya, dan ia diperlakukan dengan hormat.
short_description.en: The Animikii is a giant mythological thunderbird in the traditions of the Ojibwe and several other tribes. Thunder is caused by the beating of its wings, and it is treated with reverence.

long_description.id:
Animikii (juga Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi) adalah burung guntur mitologis raksasa yang dikenal di suku-suku utara dan barat, yaitu Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa, dan Shawnee. Mereka menimbulkan guntur dengan memukulkan sayap raksasa mereka.

Walaupun sangat kuat, burung guntur jarang mengganggu manusia, dan orang Ojibwe memperlakukannya dengan hormat. Animikii secara harfiah berarti "pembuat guntur", sedangkan Binesi berarti "burung besar". Salah satu kisah Ojibwe yang terkait menceritakan Nanabozho yang mencuri api dari Burung Guntur untuk dibagikan kepada manusia.
long_description.en:
The Animikii (also Binesi, Wapoothi, Waputhi) is a giant mythological thunderbird known among the northern and western tribes, namely the Ojibwe, Algonquin, Ottawa and Shawnee. They cause thunder by beating their enormous wings.

Although very powerful, thunderbirds rarely bother humans, and the Ojibwe treat them with reverence. Animikii literally means "thunderer" and Binesi means "the great bird". One related Ojibwe story tells of Nanabozho stealing fire from Thunderbird to share with the people.

short_description.id: Anka adalah burung raksasa dalam legenda Iran dan dongeng Turki, Kazakh, dan Altay yang tinggal di Gunung Kaf dan lahir kembali dari abunya.
short_description.en: Anka is a giant bird of Iranian legend and of Turkic, Kazakh and Altay tales that lives on Mount Kaf and is reborn from its ashes.

long_description.id:
Menurut legenda Iran, Anka adalah burung raksasa yang berkelana di Gunung Qaf; Wikipedia bahasa Kazakh menyebut jenis keduanya sebagai Samuryq, dan dalam dongeng Kazakh dan Altay burung dongeng seperti qartlan, kokzhore, dan qumai disetarakan dengannya.

Kamus Mitologi Turki karya Karakurt mendefinisikan Anka sebagai burung raksasa merah dari bahasa Persia yang tinggal di Gunung Kaf, kadang digambarkan berkepala anjing dan bercakar harimau, dan lahir kembali dari abunya. Ia menyebut dalam kepercayaan Turki lama Anka dikenal sebagai burung Toğrul dan Kongrul, yang melambangkan keabadian dan kebangkitan.

Karakurt menambahkan bahwa ciri Anka dalam budaya Persia dipindahkan seluruhnya kepada burung Kongrul, dan bahwa kepercayaan akan kematian harian dan kelahiran kembali dari abu, yang meluas karena pengaruh Persia dan Timur Tengah, sebenarnya melambangkan Matahari.
long_description.en:
According to Iranian legends, Anka is a giant bird that roams Mount Qaf; Kazakh Wikipedia gives its second kind as Samuryq, and in Kazakh and Altay tales fairy-tale birds such as qartlan, kokzhore and qumai are equated with it.

Karakurt's Dictionary of Turkic Mythology defines Anka as a giant red bird from Persian that lives on Mount Kaf, sometimes depicted with a dog's head and tiger claws, and is reborn from its ashes. It says that in old Turkic belief the Anka is known as the Toğrul and Kongrul birds, which symbolise immortality and resurrection.

Karakurt adds that the features of the Persian Anka were transferred entirely to the Kongrul bird, and that the belief in a daily death and rebirth from ashes, widespread through Persian and Middle Eastern influence, in fact symbolises the Sun.

short_description.id: Ball-tailed cat adalah "fearsome critter" mirip singa gunung dengan ekor panjang berujung gumpalan untuk memukul mangsa [ball-tailed-cat-c01].
short_description.en: The ball-tailed cat is a mountain-lion-like fearsome critter with a long, ball-tipped tail for striking prey [ball-tailed-cat-c01].

long_description.id:
Ball-tailed cat adalah "fearsome critter" Amerika Utara yang mirip singa gunung, tetapi berekor panjang dengan gumpalan padat untuk memukul mangsa [ball-tailed-cat-c01]. Kisahnya umum di kalangan penghuni hutan sekitar pergantian abad ke-20 [ball-tailed-cat-c02], dengan varian seperti Dingmaul dan Sliver Cat [ball-tailed-cat-c03]. Catatan tertulis tertuanya dari tahun 1939 [ball-tailed-cat-c04].

Ball-tailed cat digambarkan seperti puma, kecuali ekornya sangat panjang dan berujung bola padat untuk memukul mangsa [ball-tailed-cat-c01, ball-tailed-cat-c07]. Varian Sliver Cat dibedakan karena selain bola bersisi halus untuk memukul pingsan pejalan juga punya sisi berduri untuk menusuk dan mencengkeram korban [ball-tailed-cat-c05].

Ia termasuk fearsome critters [ball-tailed-cat-c01], bagian penting tradisi lisan di kamp penebangan kayu pada pergantian abad ke-20, terutama untuk mengisi waktu lewat cerita bual atau mengerjai pendatang baru [ball-tailed-cat-c06].
long_description.en:
The ball-tailed cat is a North American fearsome critter like a mountain lion, but with a long tail ending in a solid ball for striking prey [ball-tailed-cat-c01]. Its tales were common among woodsmen at the turn of the 20th century [ball-tailed-cat-c02], with variants such as the Dingmaul and Sliver Cat [ball-tailed-cat-c03]. The earliest written mention dates from 1939 [ball-tailed-cat-c04].

The ball-tailed cat is described like a mountain lion, except with an exceedingly long tail ending in a solid ball for striking its prey [ball-tailed-cat-c01, ball-tailed-cat-c07]. The Sliver Cat variant is distinguished by having, besides a smooth-sided ball for knocking wayfarers unconscious, a spiked side for piercing and grappling its victims [ball-tailed-cat-c05].

It is one of the fearsome critters [ball-tailed-cat-c01], an integral part of oral tradition in logging camps around the turn of the twentieth century, mainly to pass time through tall tales or to haze newcomers [ball-tailed-cat-c06].

cultural_context.en: The ball-tailed cat is a fearsome critter [ball-tailed-cat-c01], and such creatures served mainly to pass time through tall tales or to haze newcomers in logging camps [ball-tailed-cat-c06].

long_description.en: The ball-tailed cat is described like a mountain lion, except with an exceedingly long tail ending in a solid ball for striking its prey [ball-tailed-cat-c01, ball-tailed-cat-c07]. The Sliver Cat variant is distinguished by having, besides a smooth-sided ball for knocking wayfarers unconscious, a spiked side for piercing and grappling its victims [ball-tailed-cat-c05].

long_description.id: Ia termasuk fearsome critters [ball-tailed-cat-c01], bagian penting tradisi lisan di kamp penebangan kayu pada pergantian abad ke-20, terutama untuk mengisi waktu lewat cerita bual atau mengerjai pendatang baru [ball-tailed-cat-c06].
long_description.en: It is one of the fearsome critters [ball-tailed-cat-c01], an integral part of oral tradition in logging camps around the turn of the twentieth century, mainly to pass time through tall tales or to haze newcomers [ball-tailed-cat-c06].

cultural_context.id: Ball-tailed cat adalah fearsome critter [ball-tailed-cat-c01], dan makhluk jenis ini berfungsi terutama untuk mengisi waktu lewat cerita bual atau mengerjai pendatang baru di kamp penebangan kayu [ball-tailed-cat-c06].
cultural_context.en: The ball-tailed cat is a fearsome critter [ball-tailed-cat-c01], and such creatures served mainly to pass time through tall tales or to haze newcomers in logging camps [ball-tailed-cat-c06].

short_description.id: Caboclo de Agua adalah makhluk mitologi timur laut Brasil yang tinggal di dasar Sungai São Francisco dan menakut-nakuti nelayan [caboclo-de-agua-c01].
short_description.en: The Caboclo de Agua is a mythological being of northeastern Brazil that lives at the bottom of the São Francisco River and frightens fishermen [caboclo-de-agua-c01].

long_description.id:
Caboclo de Agua konon tinggal dalam gua emas di dasar Sungai São Francisco dan menakut-nakuti nelayan serta pelaut [caboclo-de-agua-c01]. Ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa berotot berkulit perunggu dengan satu mata besar [caboclo-de-agua-c02], berjantung tak tembus peluru [caboclo-de-agua-c03], dan dapat menyamar sebagai kuda [caboclo-de-agua-c04].

Ia mengosongkan jaring nelayan yang tidak disukainya dan memenuhi jaring yang disukainya [caboclo-de-agua-c05], serta sering membalikkan perahu [caboclo-de-agua-c06]. Nelayan memasang figur "carrancas" di haluan [caboclo-de-agua-c07] dan melukis bintang di dasar perahu untuk mengusirnya [caboclo-de-agua-c08].

Dalam kamus folklornya, Cascudo menyebut Caboclo-d'Água sebagai makhluk fantastis di Sungai São Francisco yang berkuasa atas air dan ikan [caboclo-de-agua-c09]. Ia berpihak pada sahabat-sahabatnya tetapi memburu nelayan yang tidak disukainya dengan membalikkan kano [caboclo-de-agua-c10]. Nama lainnya Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão, dan Romãozinho [caboclo-de-agua-c11].

Cascudo mengutip dua gambaran yang berbeda: tubuh monster berproporsi raksasa luar biasa [caboclo-de-agua-c12], dan tipe yang paling sering dilaporkan, yaitu pendek, tebal, berotot, berwarna tembaga, gesit, dan pemarah [caboclo-de-agua-c13]. Para pengayuh perahu di São Francisco mempersembahkan tembakau kepadanya [caboclo-de-agua-c14], dan penyeberang yang menancapkan pisau di dasar kano konon tidak diserangnya [caboclo-de-agua-c15].
long_description.en:
The Caboclo de Agua is said to live in a golden grotto at the bottom of the São Francisco River, frightening fishermen and boatmen [caboclo-de-agua-c01]. It is described as a muscular giant with bronze skin and a single huge eye [caboclo-de-agua-c02], with a bullet-proof heart [caboclo-de-agua-c03], able to appear as a horse [caboclo-de-agua-c04].

It empties the nets of fishermen it dislikes and fills those of men it likes [caboclo-de-agua-c05], and often capsizes boats [caboclo-de-agua-c06]. Fishermen mount "carrancas" figures on their bows [caboclo-de-agua-c07] and paint a star on the boat bottom to ward it off [caboclo-de-agua-c08].

In his folklore dictionary, Cascudo describes the Caboclo-d'Água as a fantastic creature of the São Francisco River with dominion over the waters and the fish [caboclo-de-agua-c09]. It favours its friends but pursues the fishermen it dislikes, overturning canoes [caboclo-de-agua-c10]. Its other names include Bicho-d'água, Rolão, Romão and Romãozinho [caboclo-de-agua-c11].

Cascudo quotes two different descriptions: a monstrous body with the proportions of an enormous giant [caboclo-de-agua-c12], and the type most often reported, short, thick, muscular, copper-coloured, quick and ill-tempered [caboclo-de-agua-c13]. The boatmen of the São Francisco offer it tobacco [caboclo-de-agua-c14], and a traveller who sticks a knife in the bottom of his canoe is said not to be attacked [caboclo-de-agua-c15].
