claim.id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong (共工) bernama Xiangliu (相柳氏) berkepala sembilan (九首) yang makan di sembilan gunung; tempat yang dijangkaunya (所抵) menjadi rawa dan lembah berair (澤谿); Yu (禹) membunuhnya dan darahnya berbau amis sehingga lima jenis biji-bijian tidak dapat ditanam di sana.
claim.en: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Haiwai bei jing, says Gonggong's (共工) minister is named Xiangliu (相柳氏), has nine heads (九首) and eats from nine mountains; where it reaches (所抵) there become marshes and watery valleys (澤谿); Yu (禹) killed it and its blood was foul, so the five grains could not be planted there.

claims_provenance.quote: 共工之臣曰相柳氏，九首，以食于九山。相柳之所抵，厥為澤谿。禹殺相柳，其血腥，不可以樹五穀種。

claim.id: Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, menggambarkan Xiangliu sebagai makhluk berkepala sembilan dan berwajah manusia (九首人面), bertubuh ular berwarna biru (蛇身而青); teks menambahkan frasa "tidak berani memanah ke utara" (不敢北射) karena segan pada menara Gonggong (共工之臺); menara itu persegi empat dan di sudutnya ada seekor ular berwarna harimau yang kepalanya menghadap ke selatan.
claim.en: The Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, describes Xiangliu as nine-headed with human faces (九首人面) and a blue snake body (蛇身而青); the text adds the phrase "dares not shoot northward" (不敢北射), in awe of Gonggong's terrace (共工之臺); the terrace is square and at a corner there is a tiger-coloured snake whose head faces south.

claims_provenance.quote: 相柳者，九首人面，蛇身而青。不敢北射，畏共工之臺。臺在其東，臺四方，隅有一蛇，虎色，首衝南方。

claim.id: Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong bernama Xiangyao (相繇) berkepala sembilan dan bertubuh ular, melingkar sendiri (自環) dan makan di sembilan negeri (九土); tempat yang dikenainya menjadi mata air dan rawa yang rasanya pahit (不辛乃苦) sehingga tak satu pun binatang dapat tinggal di sana. Yu membendung banjir dan membunuhnya; darahnya amis dan busuk, biji-bijian tak dapat tumbuh, dan tanahnya terlalu berair untuk dihuni.
claim.en: The Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, names a minister of Gonggong as Xiangyao (相繇), with nine heads and a snake body, coiling itself (自環) and eating from nine lands (九土); where it passes the places become springs and marshes whose water is bitter (不辛乃苦), so no beast can live there. Yu dammed the floods and killed it; its blood was rank, grain could not grow, and the land was too watery to inhabit.

claims_provenance.quote: 共工臣名曰相繇，九首蛇身，自環，食于九土。其所歍所尼，即為源澤，不辛乃苦，百獸莫能處。禹湮洪水，殺相繇，其血腥臭，不可生榖；其地多水，不可居也。

statement.id: Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, menggambarkan Xiangliu sebagai makhluk berkepala sembilan dan berwajah manusia (九首人面), bertubuh ular berwarna biru (蛇身而青); teks menambahkan frasa "tidak berani memanah ke utara" (不敢北射) karena segan pada menara Gonggong (共工之臺); menara itu persegi empat dan di sudutnya ada seekor ular berwarna harimau yang kepalanya menghadap ke selatan.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing, Haiwai bei jing, describes Xiangliu as nine-headed with human faces (九首人面) and a blue snake body (蛇身而青); the text adds the phrase "dares not shoot northward" (不敢北射), in awe of Gonggong's terrace (共工之臺); the terrace is square and at a corner there is a tiger-coloured snake whose head faces south.

claims.quote: 共工臣名曰相繇，九首蛇身，自環，食于九土。其所歍所尼，即為源澤，不辛乃苦，百獸莫能處。禹湮洪水，殺相繇，其血腥臭，不可生榖；其地多水，不可居也。

statement.id: Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, menyebut menteri Gonggong bernama Xiangyao (相繇) berkepala sembilan dan bertubuh ular, melingkar sendiri (自環) dan makan di sembilan negeri (九土); tempat yang dikenainya menjadi mata air dan rawa yang rasanya pahit (不辛乃苦) sehingga tak satu pun binatang dapat tinggal di sana. Yu membendung banjir dan membunuhnya; darahnya amis dan busuk, biji-bijian tak dapat tumbuh, dan tanahnya terlalu berair untuk dihuni.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing, Dahuang bei jing, names a minister of Gonggong as Xiangyao (相繇), with nine heads and a snake body, coiling itself (自環) and eating from nine lands (九土); where it passes the places become springs and marshes whose water is bitter (不辛乃苦), so no beast can live there. Yu dammed the floods and killed it; its blood was rank, grain could not grow, and the land was too watery to inhabit.

short_description.id: Aim adalah roh ke-23 dalam Goetia, adipati agung berkepala tiga yang menunggang ular beludak dan membawa obor menyala.
short_description.en: Aim is the twenty-third spirit in the Goetia, a great duke with three heads who rides a viper and carries a burning firebrand.

long_description.id:
Aim adalah roh ke-23 dalam Goetia, sebuah teks demonologi. Teks itu menyebutnya adipati agung yang kuat, tampil sebagai pria berbadan sangat tampan dengan tiga kepala.

Kepala pertama seperti ular, yang kedua seperti manusia dengan dua bintang di dahi, dan yang ketiga seperti kucing. Ia menunggang ular beludak sambil membawa obor menyala, yang dipakainya untuk membakar kota, kastil, dan tempat-tempat besar.

Goetia menyebut Aim membuat orang cerdik dalam segala hal, memberi jawaban benar tentang hal-hal tersembunyi, dan memimpin 26 legiun roh. Namanya juga tertulis Aym, Haborym, atau Haborim, dan Fred Gettings menduga asalnya dari mitologi Mesir dengan kaitan pada Bastet.
long_description.en:
Aim is the twenty-third spirit in the Goetia, a demonological text. The text calls him a great and strong duke, appearing as a very handsome man in body with three heads.

The first head is like a serpent, the second like a man with two stars on his forehead, and the third like a cat. He rides a viper carrying a burning firebrand, with which he sets cities, castles and great places on fire.

The Goetia says Aim makes one witty in all manner of ways, gives true answers to private matters, and governs 26 legions of spirits. His name is also written Aym, Haborym or Haborim, and Fred Gettings conjectures an Egyptian-mythology origin with a link to Bastet.

short_description.id: Ame no Wakahiko adalah dewa padi-padian (amatsukami) dalam mitologi Jepang yang diutus ke bumi, tidak melapor, dan mati terkena anak panah yang dilemparkan kembali.
short_description.en: Ame no Wakahiko is a god of grains (amatsukami) in Japanese mythology who is sent to earth, fails to report, and dies from an arrow thrown back at him.

long_description.id:
Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 atau 天若日子) adalah dewa padi-padian dan amatsukami dalam mitologi Jepang, putra Amatsukunitama. Namanya berarti "anak muda di surga", dan ia dianggap pemuda yang sangat tampan. Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menambahkan bahwa "Wakahiko" berarti pemuda dan menyebut teori bahwa nama ini kata benda umum, sehingga tanpa gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊.

Dalam banyak versi, ketika Ame no Hohi tidak mengirim kabar selama tiga tahun, para dewa memilih Ame no Wakahiko untuk menguasai bumi. Dalam sebagian versi ia jatuh cinta kepada Shitateruhime; delapan tahun kemudian burung Nakime dikirim menengoknya, tetapi ia memanah burung itu dan anak panahnya melesat ke surga. Takamimusubi melemparkannya kembali sehingga mengenai Ame no Wakahiko yang sedang tidur dan membunuhnya; versi lain menyebut Amaterasu yang melakukannya.

Setelah ia wafat, orang tuanya membangun gubuk duka. Ajisukitakahikone yang datang melayat disangka dirinya yang hidup kembali karena kemiripannya; tersinggung, ia menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya hingga jatuh di Mino dan menjadi Gunung Moyama. Mitos ini disebut sebagai asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali, dan mungkin juga mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaan atas negara tetangga.

Ia dimuliakan di Kuil Abiko di Aishō, Shiga, dan Kuil Iwakura di Shinshiro, Aichi. Sebuah kisah Otogi-zōshi zaman Muromachi, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, juga menampilkan pangeran bernama sama yang berwujud ular dan menjadi kisah asal-usul Tanabata.
long_description.en:
Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 or 天若日子), son of Amatsukunitama, is counted in Japanese mythology as a grain god and an amatsukami. His name is explained as "a young boy in heaven", and he is believed to have been a remarkably good-looking youth. Japanese Wikipedia adds that "Wakahiko" means a young man and notes a theory that it is a common noun, which would explain the lack of an honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊.

In many versions, when Ame no Hohi sent no word for three years, the gods chose Ame no Wakahiko to rule the earth. In some versions he fell in love with Shitateruhime; eight years later the bird Nakime was sent to check on him, but he shot the bird and the arrow flew to heaven. Takamimusubi threw it back so that it hit Ame no Wakahiko as he lay in bed and killed him; other versions say Amaterasu did this.

After his death his parents built a mourning hut. Ajisukitakahikone, who came to pay respects, was mistaken for him brought back to life because of their resemblance; offended, he destroyed the hut and kicked it so that it landed in Mino and became Mount Moyama. This myth is named as the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow, and is likely also a mythicisation of the Yamato state's attempts to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

Shrines that honor him include Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga, and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi. A Muromachi-period Otogi-zōshi story, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, also features a prince of the same name who takes the form of a serpent and serves as an origin tale for Tanabata.

summary.id: Setelah Ame no Hohi tak mengirim kabar, Ame no Wakahiko diutus menguasai bumi. Ia mengambil Shita-teru-hime sebagai istri dan tak melapor; ketika burung Nakime dikirim, ia memanahnya, dan anak panah itu dilemparkan kembali dari surga sehingga ia mati.
summary.en: After Ame no Hohi sent no word, Ame no Wakahiko was sent to rule the earth. He took Shita-teru-hime to wife and made no report; when the bird Nakime was sent he shot it, and the arrow was thrown back from heaven and he died.

role.en: The deceased mistaken for alive again

summary.id: Orang tuanya membangun gubuk duka. Ajisukitakahikone yang mirip dirinya datang melayat dan disangka dirinya yang hidup kembali; ia tersinggung, menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya hingga jatuh di Mino menjadi Gunung Moyama.
summary.en: His parents built a mourning hut. Ajisukitakahikone, who looked like him, came to pay respects and was mistaken for him alive again; offended, he destroyed the hut and kicked it so that it landed in Mino as Mount Moyama.

role.id: Pangeran berwujud ular, suami dalam kisah pencarian
role.en: The serpent-form prince, husband in a quest tale

summary.id: Dalam kisah Otogi-zōshi zaman Muromachi ini, Pangeran Ame no Wakahiko berwujud ular. Akhirnya ayah oni mengizinkannya bertemu sang istri sebulan sekali, tetapi sang istri mengira "setahun sekali", sehingga pasangan itu hanya bertemu saat Tanabata.
summary.en: In this Muromachi-period Otogi-zōshi tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent. In the end the oni father lets him meet his wife once a month, but she mistakes it for once a year, so the couple meet only at Tanabata.

claim.id: Ame no Wakahiko adalah dewa padi-padian dalam mitologi Jepang.
claim.en: Ame no Wakahiko is a grain deity in Japanese mythology.

claims_provenance.quote: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 or 天若日子) is a god of grains and an Amatsukami in Japanese mythology.

claim.id: Ia disebut sebagai putra Amatsukunitama.
claim.en: He is named as a son of Amatsukunitama.

claims_provenance.quote: He is the son of Amatsukunitama.

claim.id: Dalam beberapa versi, ia diutus menguasai bumi setelah utusan lain tak memberi kabar.
claim.en: Some versions send him to govern the earth after another envoy fails to report.

claims_provenance.quote: In many versions, when Ame no Hohi did not send word for three years, all the gods gathered up, and Ame no Wakahiko was the one who was chosen to rule the earth.

claim.id: Beberapa versi menyebut ia jatuh cinta kepada Shitateruhime.
claim.en: Some versions say he fell in love with Shitateruhime.

claims_provenance.quote: In some versions, Ame no Wakahiko fell in love with Shitateruhime.

claim.id: Nama Ame no Wakahiko berarti "anak muda di surga", dan ia dianggap pemuda yang sangat tampan.
claim.en: The name Ame no Wakahiko means "a young boy in heaven," and he is thought to be an exceptionally handsome youth.

claims_provenance.quote: The name Ame no Wakahiko means "a young boy in heaven," and he is thought to be an exceptionally handsome youth.

claim.id: Dalam sebagian versi, Ame no Wakahiko adalah putra Ame no Hohi dan dikirim ke bumi untuk mencarinya.
claim.en: In some versions, however, Ame no Wakahiko is the son of Ame no Hohi and was sent to earth to look for him.

claims_provenance.quote: In some versions, however, Ame no Wakahiko is the son of Ame no Hohi and Ame no Wakahiko was sent to earth to look for him.

claim.id: Delapan tahun kemudian, karena tak ada kabar, para dewa mengirim burung bernama Nakime ke bumi untuk menengoknya. Atas saran seorang perempuan bijak, Ame no Wakahiko memanah burung itu; burung itu mati, tetapi anak panahnya melesat hingga ke surga.
claim.en: Eight years later, with no report, the gods sent a bird named Nakime to earth to check on him. On a wise woman's advice Ame no Wakahiko shot the bird with his bow; the bird was killed but the arrow flew all the way to heaven.

claims_provenance.quote: Eight years later, after receiving no report back, the gods sent a bird named Nakime down to earth to check in on him. Following the advice of a wise woman, Ame no Wakahiko used his bow to shoot the bird. The bird was killed but the arrow flew all the way to heaven.

claim.id: Takamimusubi melihat anak panah itu dan melemparkannya kembali ke bumi hingga mengenai Ame no Wakahiko yang sedang berbaring di tempat tidur dan membunuhnya. Versi lain menyebut Amaterasu yang menembakkan panah itu kembali.
claim.en: Takamimusubi saw the arrow and threw it back at the earth, where it hit Ame no Wakahiko as he lay in bed and killed him. Other versions say Amaterasu shot the arrow back at him.

claims_provenance.quote: Takamimusubi saw the arrow and threw it back at the earth where it hit Ame no Wakahiko while he was lying in bed, killing him. Other versions state that Amaterasu was the one who shot the arrow back at him.

claim.id: Mitos ini adalah asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali.
claim.en: This myth is the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow.

claims_provenance.quote: This myth is the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow.

claim.id: Mitos ini kemungkinan juga merupakan mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaannya atas negara-negara tetangga.
claim.en: It is likely also a mythicisation of attempts by the Yamato state to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

claims_provenance.quote: It is likely also a mythicisation of attempts made by the Yamato state to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

claim.id: Setelah Ame no Wakahiko meninggal, orang tuanya membangun gubuk (喪屋 moya) untuknya. Ajisukitakahikone turun memberi penghormatan, tetapi karena mirip Ame no Wakahiko ia disangka Ame no Wakahiko yang dihidupkan kembali.
claim.en: After Ame no Wakahiko's death his parents built a mourning hut (喪屋 moya) for him. Ajisukitakahikone went down to pay respects, but because he looked like Ame no Wakahiko he was mistaken for Ame no Wakahiko brought back to life.

claims_provenance.quote: After Ame no Wakahiko's death, his parents built a hut (喪屋 moya) for their son. Ajisukitakahikone went down to pay his respect. However, due to Ajisukitakahikone looking similar to Ame no Wakahiko he was mistaken to be Ame no Wakahiko brought back to life.

claim.id: Ajisukitakahikone tersinggung, menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya; gubuk itu jatuh di tanah Mino dan menjadi gunung bernama Moyama.
claim.en: Ajisukitakahikone was offended, destroyed the hut and kicked it; the hut landed in the land of Mino and became a mountain called Moyama.

claims_provenance.quote: Ajisukitakahikone was offended by this and destroyed the hut and kicked it. The hut landed in the land of Mino and became a mountain called Moyama.

claim.id: Ame no Wakahiko dimuliakan di Kuil Abiko di Aishō, Shiga, dan Kuil Iwakura di Shinshiro, Aichi.
claim.en: Ame no Wakahiko is enshrined at Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga, and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi.

claims_provenance.quote: Ame no Wakahiko is enshrined at Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi.

claim.id: Kisah lain tentang Ame no Wakahiko muncul dalam sastra Jepang abad pertengahan zaman Muromachi (Otogi-zōshi), dengan alur yang sangat mirip tipe dongeng ATU 425 "Pencarian Suami yang Hilang" atau kisah Yunani-Romawi Cupid dan Psyche karya Apuleius.
claim.en: Another story of Ame no Wakahiko appears in medieval Japanese literature of the Muromachi period (Otogi-zōshi), in a narrative very similar to tale type ATU 425, "The Search for the Lost Husband", or to the Graeco-Roman story of Cupid and Psyche by Apuleius.

claims_provenance.quote: Another story of Ame no Wakahiko appears in Japanese medieval literature of the Muromachi period (Otogi-zōshi), in a narrative very similar to the Aarne-Thompson-Uther tale type ATU 425, "The Search for the Lost Husband", or to the Graeco-Roman story of Cupid and Psyche, by writer Apuleius.

claim.id: Kisah ini juga dikenal sebagai Ame no Wakahiko sōshi atau Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (Kisah Ame no Wakahiko), dan menjadi kisah asal-usul lain bagi festival Tanabata.
claim.en: The story is also known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

claims_provenance.quote: The story is alternatively known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

claim.id: Dalam kisah ini, Pangeran Ame no Wakahiko menjelma menjadi ular.
claim.en: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

claims_provenance.quote: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

claim.id: Di akhir kisah, ayah oni mengizinkan putranya dan sang istri bertemu sebulan sekali, tetapi sang istri salah mengira "setahun sekali", sehingga sepasang kekasih itu hanya bisa bersatu saat Tanabata.
claim.en: At the end of the tale the oni father lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year", so the lovers can only reunite at Tanabata.

claims_provenance.quote: At the end of this tale, the oni father  lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year" and thus, the lovers can only reunite during the Tanabata.

claim.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang, juga ditulis アメワカヒコ dan アマノワカヒコ.
claim.en: Japanese Wikipedia: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) is a deity in Japanese mythology, also written アメワカヒコ and アマノワカヒコ.

claims_provenance.quote: アメノワカヒコ（天若日子、天稚彦）は、日本神話に登場する神。アメワカヒコ、アマノワカヒコともする。

claim.id: "Wakahiko" dalam namanya berarti pemuda; ada teori bahwa karena itu kata benda umum, bukan nama dewa, ia tidak diberi gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊, dan teori lain karena ia memberontak kepada para amatsukami.
claim.en: "Wakahiko" in his name means a young man; one theory says that because it was a common noun rather than a divine name he carries no honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊, while another says it is because he rebelled against the amatsukami.

claims_provenance.quote: 名前の「ワカヒコ」は若い男の意味である。これが神名ではなく普通名詞だったため、「神」「命」「尊」の尊称が付かないとする説がある。また、天津神に反逆したためであるとする説もある。

claim.id: Menurut Kojiki, gubuk duka Ame no Wakahiko dibuat di bumi, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menyebut jenazah dinaikkan oleh angin kencang dan gubuk duka dibuat di surga.
claim.en: In the Kojiki the mourning hut of Ame no Wakahiko was built on earth, whereas in the Nihon Shoki a gale lifted the body and the hut was built in heaven.

claims_provenance.quote: 天若日子の喪屋は『古事記』では地上に作ったとあるが、『日本書紀』では疾風（はやち）に遺体を上げさせて、喪屋は天に作ったとある。

claim.id: Karena Ame no Wakahiko dan Ajisukitakahikone sangat mirip, ada teori bahwa mereka pada mulanya dewa yang sama: kematian Ame no Wakahiko dan kebangkitannya sebagai Ajisukitakahikone, yang melambangkan padi-padian yang layu di musim gugur lalu tumbuh kembali di musim semi, atau matahari yang melemah di musim dingin lalu bangkit di musim semi.
claim.en: Because Ame no Wakahiko and Ajisukitakahikone looked so alike, one theory holds they were originally the same god: Ame no Wakahiko's death and his revival as Ajisukitakahikone, representing grain withering in autumn and reviving in spring, or the sun weakening in winter and reviving in spring.

claims_provenance.quote: 天若日子と阿遅鉏高日子根神がそっくりだったということで、本来同一の神であったとする説もある。すなわち、アメノワカヒコの死とアヂスキタカヒコネとしての復活であり、これは穀物が秋に枯れて春に再生する、または太陽が冬に力が弱まり春に復活する様子を表したものであるとする。

claim.id: Dalam terjemahan Aston atas Nihongi, para dewa berkata: "Ame-waka-hiko, putra Ame no Kuni-dama. Ia orang yang gagah berani. Biarlah ia dicoba."
claim.en: In Aston's translation of the Nihongi, the gods say: "Ame-waka-hiko, son of Ame no Kuni-dama. He is a valorous person. Let him be tried."

short_description.id: Ame no Wakahiko adalah dewa padi-padian (amatsukami) dalam mitologi Jepang yang diutus ke bumi, tidak melapor, dan mati terkena anak panah yang dilemparkan kembali.
short_description.en: Ame no Wakahiko is a god of grains (amatsukami) in Japanese mythology who is sent to earth, fails to report, and dies from an arrow thrown back at him.

long_description.id: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 atau 天若日子) adalah dewa padi-padian dan amatsukami dalam mitologi Jepang, putra Amatsukunitama. Namanya berarti "anak muda di surga", dan ia dianggap pemuda yang sangat tampan. Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menambahkan bahwa "Wakahiko" berarti pemuda dan menyebut teori bahwa nama ini kata benda umum, sehingga tanpa gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊.
long_description.en: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 or 天若日子), son of Amatsukunitama, is counted in Japanese mythology as a grain god and an amatsukami. His name is explained as "a young boy in heaven", and he is believed to have been a remarkably good-looking youth. Japanese Wikipedia adds that "Wakahiko" means a young man and notes a theory that it is a common noun, which would explain the lack of an honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊.

long_description.id: Dalam banyak versi, ketika Ame no Hohi tidak mengirim kabar selama tiga tahun, para dewa memilih Ame no Wakahiko untuk menguasai bumi. Dalam sebagian versi ia jatuh cinta kepada Shitateruhime; delapan tahun kemudian burung Nakime dikirim menengoknya, tetapi ia memanah burung itu dan anak panahnya melesat ke surga. Takamimusubi melemparkannya kembali sehingga mengenai Ame no Wakahiko yang sedang tidur dan membunuhnya; versi lain menyebut Amaterasu yang melakukannya.
long_description.en: In many versions, when Ame no Hohi sent no word for three years, the gods chose Ame no Wakahiko to rule the earth. In some versions he fell in love with Shitateruhime; eight years later the bird Nakime was sent to check on him, but he shot the bird and the arrow flew to heaven. Takamimusubi threw it back so that it hit Ame no Wakahiko as he lay in bed and killed him; other versions say Amaterasu did this.

long_description.id: Setelah ia wafat, orang tuanya membangun gubuk duka. Ajisukitakahikone yang datang melayat disangka dirinya yang hidup kembali karena kemiripannya; tersinggung, ia menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya hingga jatuh di Mino dan menjadi Gunung Moyama. Mitos ini disebut sebagai asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali, dan mungkin juga mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaan atas negara tetangga.
long_description.en: After his death his parents built a mourning hut. Ajisukitakahikone, who came to pay respects, was mistaken for him brought back to life because of their resemblance; offended, he destroyed the hut and kicked it so that it landed in Mino and became Mount Moyama. This myth is named as the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow, and is likely also a mythicisation of the Yamato state's attempts to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

long_description.id: Ia dimuliakan di Kuil Abiko di Aishō, Shiga, dan Kuil Iwakura di Shinshiro, Aichi. Sebuah kisah Otogi-zōshi zaman Muromachi, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, juga menampilkan pangeran bernama sama yang berwujud ular dan menjadi kisah asal-usul Tanabata.
long_description.en: Shrines that honor him include Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga, and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi. A Muromachi-period Otogi-zōshi story, Ame no Wakahiko sōshi, also features a prince of the same name who takes the form of a serpent and serves as an origin tale for Tanabata.

cultural_context.id: Mitos ini adalah asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali, dan kemungkinan juga mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaan atas negara-negara tetangga.
cultural_context.en: The myth is given as the source of a Japanese proverb about the returning arrow, and probably also a mythic retelling of Yamato's efforts to assert its authority over neighbouring states.

summary.id: Setelah Ame no Hohi tak mengirim kabar, Ame no Wakahiko diutus menguasai bumi. Ia mengambil Shita-teru-hime sebagai istri dan tak melapor; ketika burung Nakime dikirim, ia memanahnya, dan anak panah itu dilemparkan kembali dari surga sehingga ia mati.
summary.en: After Ame no Hohi sent no word, Ame no Wakahiko was sent to rule the earth. He took Shita-teru-hime to wife and made no report; when the bird Nakime was sent he shot it, and the arrow was thrown back from heaven and he died.

role.en: The deceased mistaken for alive again

summary.id: Orang tuanya membangun gubuk duka. Ajisukitakahikone yang mirip dirinya datang melayat dan disangka dirinya yang hidup kembali; ia tersinggung, menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya hingga jatuh di Mino menjadi Gunung Moyama.
summary.en: His parents built a mourning hut. Ajisukitakahikone, who looked like him, came to pay respects and was mistaken for him alive again; offended, he destroyed the hut and kicked it so that it landed in Mino as Mount Moyama.

role.id: Pangeran berwujud ular, suami dalam kisah pencarian
role.en: The serpent-form prince, husband in a quest tale

summary.id: Dalam kisah Otogi-zōshi zaman Muromachi ini, Pangeran Ame no Wakahiko berwujud ular. Akhirnya ayah oni mengizinkannya bertemu sang istri sebulan sekali, tetapi sang istri mengira "setahun sekali", sehingga pasangan itu hanya bertemu saat Tanabata.
summary.en: In this Muromachi-period Otogi-zōshi tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent. In the end the oni father lets him meet his wife once a month, but she mistakes it for once a year, so the couple meet only at Tanabata.

claims.quote: Ame no Wakahiko (天稚彦 or 天若日子) is a god of grains and an Amatsukami in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Ame no Wakahiko adalah dewa padi-padian dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Ame no Wakahiko is a grain deity in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: He is the son of Amatsukunitama.

statement.id: Ia disebut sebagai putra Amatsukunitama.
statement.en: He is named as a son of Amatsukunitama.

claims.quote: In many versions, when Ame no Hohi did not send word for three years, all the gods gathered up, and Ame no Wakahiko was the one who was chosen to rule the earth.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa versi, ia diutus menguasai bumi setelah utusan lain tak memberi kabar.
statement.en: Some versions send him to govern the earth after another envoy fails to report.

claims.quote: In some versions, Ame no Wakahiko fell in love with Shitateruhime.

statement.id: Beberapa versi menyebut ia jatuh cinta kepada Shitateruhime.
statement.en: Some versions say he fell in love with Shitateruhime.

claims.quote: The name Ame no Wakahiko means "a young boy in heaven," and he is thought to be an exceptionally handsome youth.

statement.id: Nama Ame no Wakahiko berarti "anak muda di surga", dan ia dianggap pemuda yang sangat tampan.
statement.en: The name Ame no Wakahiko means "a young boy in heaven," and he is thought to be an exceptionally handsome youth.

claims.quote: In some versions, however, Ame no Wakahiko is the son of Ame no Hohi and Ame no Wakahiko was sent to earth to look for him.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian versi, Ame no Wakahiko adalah putra Ame no Hohi dan dikirim ke bumi untuk mencarinya.
statement.en: In some versions, however, Ame no Wakahiko is the son of Ame no Hohi and was sent to earth to look for him.

claims.quote: Eight years later, after receiving no report back, the gods sent a bird named Nakime down to earth to check in on him. Following the advice of a wise woman, Ame no Wakahiko used his bow to shoot the bird. The bird was killed but the arrow flew all the way to heaven.

statement.id: Delapan tahun kemudian, karena tak ada kabar, para dewa mengirim burung bernama Nakime ke bumi untuk menengoknya. Atas saran seorang perempuan bijak, Ame no Wakahiko memanah burung itu; burung itu mati, tetapi anak panahnya melesat hingga ke surga.
statement.en: Eight years later, with no report, the gods sent a bird named Nakime to earth to check on him. On a wise woman's advice Ame no Wakahiko shot the bird with his bow; the bird was killed but the arrow flew all the way to heaven.

claims.quote: Takamimusubi saw the arrow and threw it back at the earth where it hit Ame no Wakahiko while he was lying in bed, killing him. Other versions state that Amaterasu was the one who shot the arrow back at him.

statement.id: Takamimusubi melihat anak panah itu dan melemparkannya kembali ke bumi hingga mengenai Ame no Wakahiko yang sedang berbaring di tempat tidur dan membunuhnya. Versi lain menyebut Amaterasu yang menembakkan panah itu kembali.
statement.en: Takamimusubi saw the arrow and threw it back at the earth, where it hit Ame no Wakahiko as he lay in bed and killed him. Other versions say Amaterasu shot the arrow back at him.

claims.quote: This myth is the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow.

statement.id: Mitos ini adalah asal ungkapan Jepang tentang anak panah yang kembali.
statement.en: This myth is the origin of a Japanese saying about the returning arrow.

claims.quote: It is likely also a mythicisation of attempts made by the Yamato state to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

statement.id: Mitos ini kemungkinan juga merupakan mitologisasi upaya negara Yamato menegakkan kekuasaannya atas negara-negara tetangga.
statement.en: It is likely also a mythicisation of attempts by the Yamato state to impose its authority over neighbouring states.

claims.quote: After Ame no Wakahiko's death, his parents built a hut (喪屋 moya) for their son. Ajisukitakahikone went down to pay his respect. However, due to Ajisukitakahikone looking similar to Ame no Wakahiko he was mistaken to be Ame no Wakahiko brought back to life.

statement.id: Setelah Ame no Wakahiko meninggal, orang tuanya membangun gubuk (喪屋 moya) untuknya. Ajisukitakahikone turun memberi penghormatan, tetapi karena mirip Ame no Wakahiko ia disangka Ame no Wakahiko yang dihidupkan kembali.
statement.en: After Ame no Wakahiko's death his parents built a mourning hut (喪屋 moya) for him. Ajisukitakahikone went down to pay respects, but because he looked like Ame no Wakahiko he was mistaken for Ame no Wakahiko brought back to life.

claims.quote: Ajisukitakahikone was offended by this and destroyed the hut and kicked it. The hut landed in the land of Mino and became a mountain called Moyama.

statement.id: Ajisukitakahikone tersinggung, menghancurkan gubuk itu dan menendangnya; gubuk itu jatuh di tanah Mino dan menjadi gunung bernama Moyama.
statement.en: Ajisukitakahikone was offended, destroyed the hut and kicked it; the hut landed in the land of Mino and became a mountain called Moyama.

claims.quote: Ame no Wakahiko is enshrined at Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi.

statement.id: Ame no Wakahiko dimuliakan di Kuil Abiko di Aishō, Shiga, dan Kuil Iwakura di Shinshiro, Aichi.
statement.en: Ame no Wakahiko is enshrined at Abiko Shrine in Aishō, Shiga, and Iwakura Shrine in Shinshiro, Aichi.

claims.quote: Another story of Ame no Wakahiko appears in Japanese medieval literature of the Muromachi period (Otogi-zōshi), in a narrative very similar to the Aarne-Thompson-Uther tale type ATU 425, "The Search for the Lost Husband", or to the Graeco-Roman story of Cupid and Psyche, by writer Apuleius.

statement.id: Kisah lain tentang Ame no Wakahiko muncul dalam sastra Jepang abad pertengahan zaman Muromachi (Otogi-zōshi), dengan alur yang sangat mirip tipe dongeng ATU 425 "Pencarian Suami yang Hilang" atau kisah Yunani-Romawi Cupid dan Psyche karya Apuleius.
statement.en: Another story of Ame no Wakahiko appears in medieval Japanese literature of the Muromachi period (Otogi-zōshi), in a narrative very similar to tale type ATU 425, "The Search for the Lost Husband", or to the Graeco-Roman story of Cupid and Psyche by Apuleius.

claims.quote: The story is alternatively known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

statement.id: Kisah ini juga dikenal sebagai Ame no Wakahiko sōshi atau Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (Kisah Ame no Wakahiko), dan menjadi kisah asal-usul lain bagi festival Tanabata.
statement.en: The story is also known as Ame no Wakahiko sōshi or Ame no Wakahiko monogatari (The Tale of Ame no Wakahiko), and serves as another etiological tale for the Tanabata festival.

claims.quote: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

statement.id: Dalam kisah ini, Pangeran Ame no Wakahiko menjelma menjadi ular.
statement.en: In this tale, Prince Ame no Wakahiko takes the form of a serpent.

claims.quote: At the end of this tale, the oni father  lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year" and thus, the lovers can only reunite during the Tanabata.

statement.id: Di akhir kisah, ayah oni mengizinkan putranya dan sang istri bertemu sebulan sekali, tetapi sang istri salah mengira "setahun sekali", sehingga sepasang kekasih itu hanya bisa bersatu saat Tanabata.
statement.en: At the end of the tale the oni father lets his son and the wife meet once a month, but she mistakes it for "once a year", so the lovers can only reunite at Tanabata.

claims.quote: アメノワカヒコ（天若日子、天稚彦）は、日本神話に登場する神。アメワカヒコ、アマノワカヒコともする。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang, juga ditulis アメワカヒコ dan アマノワカヒコ.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia: アメノワカヒコ (天若日子, 天稚彦) is a deity in Japanese mythology, also written アメワカヒコ and アマノワカヒコ.

claims.quote: 名前の「ワカヒコ」は若い男の意味である。これが神名ではなく普通名詞だったため、「神」「命」「尊」の尊称が付かないとする説がある。また、天津神に反逆したためであるとする説もある。

statement.id: "Wakahiko" dalam namanya berarti pemuda; ada teori bahwa karena itu kata benda umum, bukan nama dewa, ia tidak diberi gelar kehormatan seperti 神, 命, atau 尊, dan teori lain karena ia memberontak kepada para amatsukami.
statement.en: "Wakahiko" in his name means a young man; one theory says that because it was a common noun rather than a divine name he carries no honorific such as 神, 命 or 尊, while another says it is because he rebelled against the amatsukami.

claims.quote: 天若日子の喪屋は『古事記』では地上に作ったとあるが、『日本書紀』では疾風（はやち）に遺体を上げさせて、喪屋は天に作ったとある。

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, gubuk duka Ame no Wakahiko dibuat di bumi, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menyebut jenazah dinaikkan oleh angin kencang dan gubuk duka dibuat di surga.
statement.en: In the Kojiki the mourning hut of Ame no Wakahiko was built on earth, whereas in the Nihon Shoki a gale lifted the body and the hut was built in heaven.

claims.quote: 天若日子と阿遅鉏高日子根神がそっくりだったということで、本来同一の神であったとする説もある。すなわち、アメノワカヒコの死とアヂスキタカヒコネとしての復活であり、これは穀物が秋に枯れて春に再生する、または太陽が冬に力が弱まり春に復活する様子を表したものであるとする。

statement.id: Karena Ame no Wakahiko dan Ajisukitakahikone sangat mirip, ada teori bahwa mereka pada mulanya dewa yang sama: kematian Ame no Wakahiko dan kebangkitannya sebagai Ajisukitakahikone, yang melambangkan padi-padian yang layu di musim gugur lalu tumbuh kembali di musim semi, atau matahari yang melemah di musim dingin lalu bangkit di musim semi.
statement.en: Because Ame no Wakahiko and Ajisukitakahikone looked so alike, one theory holds they were originally the same god: Ame no Wakahiko's death and his revival as Ajisukitakahikone, representing grain withering in autumn and reviving in spring, or the sun weakening in winter and reviving in spring.

claims.quote: Ame-waka-hiko, son of Ame no Kuni-dama. He is a valorous person. Let him be tried.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Aston atas Nihongi, para dewa berkata: "Ame-waka-hiko, putra Ame no Kuni-dama. Ia orang yang gagah berani. Biarlah ia dicoba."
statement.en: In Aston's translation of the Nihongi, the gods say: "Ame-waka-hiko, son of Ame no Kuni-dama. He is a valorous person. Let him be tried."

claims.quote: This God also was disloyal, and as soon as he arrived took to wife Shita-teru-hime

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, dewa ini juga tidak setia dan begitu tiba ia mengambil Shita-teru-hime sebagai istri.
statement.en: In the Nihongi this god too was disloyal and as soon as he arrived took Shita-teru-hime to wife.

claims.quote: Then Ame-waka-hiko took the heavenly deer-bow and the heavenly feathered arrows which had been given him by Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto, and shot the pheasant, so that it died.

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko mengambil busur rusa surgawi dan anak panah berbulu surgawi pemberian Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto, lalu memanah burung pegar itu hingga mati.
statement.en: In the Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko took the heavenly deer-bow and heavenly feathered arrows given him by Taka-mi-musubi no Mikoto and shot the pheasant so that it died.

claims.quote: Ame-waka-hiko was lying down after the feast of first-fruits, and when hit by the arrow died immediately.

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko sedang berbaring setelah pesta buah pertama, dan ketika terkena anak panah itu ia langsung meninggal.
statement.en: In the Nihongi, Ame-waka-hiko was lying down after the feast of first-fruits and died immediately when hit by the arrow.

claims.quote: and sent down a swift wind. to bring the body up to Heaven. Forthwith a mortuary house was made

statement.id: Dalam Nihongi, angin kencang dikirim turun untuk membawa jenazah naik ke Surga, lalu segera dibuat rumah duka.
statement.en: In the Nihongi a swift wind was sent down to bring the body up to Heaven, and a mortuary house was promptly made.

short_description.id: Ascapart adalah raksasa legenda dalam folklor Inggris yang ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, cukup besar untuk mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya.
short_description.en: Ascapart is a legendary giant of English folklore conquered by Bevis of Hampton, big enough to carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under one arm.

long_description.id:
Dalam folklor Inggris, Ascapart (juga Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) adalah raksasa legenda yang konon ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, begitu besar hingga dapat mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya. Tingginya 30 kaki tetapi ia yang terkecil di negerinya. Ia kalah setelah gadanya, sebatang pohon utuh, diayunkan ke arah Sir Bevis dan tertancap di tanah lunak; Bevis tidak membunuhnya melainkan menjadikannya pengawal.

Kemudian Ascapart mengkhianati Bevis dan membawa lari istrinya Josiane, lalu dibunuh sahabat-sahabat Bevis. Ia konon dikubur di bawah Bevis Mount, atau tubuhnya menjadi bagian South Downs saat ia jatuh. Raksasa ini juga muncul dalam folklor Hampshire dan New Forest; panel lukisan abad pertengahan Sir Bevis dan Ascupart ada di Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.

Halaman Taman Nasional South Downs menyebut Ascapart tergolong kecil dibanding raksasa zamannya, hanya sekitar 30 kaki, tetapi sangat mampu menakut-nakuti desa-desa di sekitar Southampton. Menurut sebagian penutur, ia hidup hanya karena Josain, istri Bevis, membujuk Bevis. Beberapa catatan menyebut ia memang mengkhianati Bevis dan menculik istrinya, lalu tewas di tangan para pendukung Bevis, dan tubuhnya menjadi bagian dari Downs.
long_description.en:
In English folklore Ascapart (also Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) is a legendary giant said to have been overcome by Bevis of Hampton, so huge he could carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under his arm. He was 30 feet tall, yet the smallest in his land. He lost when his club, a whole tree, was swung at Sir Bevis and stuck fast in soft ground; Bevis spared him and made him his squire.

Later Ascapart betrayed Bevis and carried off his wife Josiane, and Bevis's friends killed him. He is said to lie under Bevis Mount, or his body became part of the South Downs when he fell. The giant also figures in the folklore of Hampshire and the New Forest; medieval painted panels of Sir Bevis and Ascupart hang in the Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.

The South Downs National Park page says Ascapart was small for the giants of his day, a mere 30 feet tall, yet more than capable of terrifying the villages around Southampton. Some tellers say he lived only because Josain, Bevis's wife, persuaded Bevis. Some records say he did betray Bevis and kidnapped his wife, and met his death at the hands of Bevis's supporters, his body becoming part of the Downs.

short_description.id: Ascapart adalah raksasa legenda dalam folklor Inggris yang ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, cukup besar untuk mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya.
short_description.en: Ascapart is a legendary giant of English folklore conquered by Bevis of Hampton, big enough to carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under one arm.

long_description.id: Dalam folklor Inggris, Ascapart (juga Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) adalah raksasa legenda yang konon ditaklukkan Bevis dari Hampton, begitu besar hingga dapat mengepit Bevis, istrinya dan kudanya. Tingginya 30 kaki tetapi ia yang terkecil di negerinya. Ia kalah setelah gadanya, sebatang pohon utuh, diayunkan ke arah Sir Bevis dan tertancap di tanah lunak; Bevis tidak membunuhnya melainkan menjadikannya pengawal.
long_description.en: In English folklore Ascapart (also Ascupart, Ascapard, Ascopard, Ascopart, Asgapard) is a legendary giant said to have been overcome by Bevis of Hampton, so huge he could carry Bevis, his wife and his horse under his arm. He was 30 feet tall, yet the smallest in his land. He lost when his club, a whole tree, was swung at Sir Bevis and stuck fast in soft ground; Bevis spared him and made him his squire.

long_description.id: Kemudian Ascapart mengkhianati Bevis dan membawa lari istrinya Josiane, lalu dibunuh sahabat-sahabat Bevis. Ia konon dikubur di bawah Bevis Mount, atau tubuhnya menjadi bagian South Downs saat ia jatuh. Raksasa ini juga muncul dalam folklor Hampshire dan New Forest; panel lukisan abad pertengahan Sir Bevis dan Ascupart ada di Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.
long_description.en: Later Ascapart betrayed Bevis and carried off his wife Josiane, and Bevis's friends killed him. He is said to lie under Bevis Mount, or his body became part of the South Downs when he fell. The giant also figures in the folklore of Hampshire and the New Forest; medieval painted panels of Sir Bevis and Ascupart hang in the Southampton Bargate Monument Gallery.

long_description.id: Halaman Taman Nasional South Downs menyebut Ascapart tergolong kecil dibanding raksasa zamannya, hanya sekitar 30 kaki, tetapi sangat mampu menakut-nakuti desa-desa di sekitar Southampton. Menurut sebagian penutur, ia hidup hanya karena Josain, istri Bevis, membujuk Bevis. Beberapa catatan menyebut ia memang mengkhianati Bevis dan menculik istrinya, lalu tewas di tangan para pendukung Bevis, dan tubuhnya menjadi bagian dari Downs.
long_description.en: The South Downs National Park page says Ascapart was small for the giants of his day, a mere 30 feet tall, yet more than capable of terrifying the villages around Southampton. Some tellers say he lived only because Josain, Bevis's wife, persuaded Bevis. Some records say he did betray Bevis and kidnapped his wife, and met his death at the hands of Bevis's supporters, his body becoming part of the Downs.

short_description.id: Ayida Wedo adalah loa (roh ilahi) berwujud ular pelangi dalam Vodou Haiti, pasangan Damballa, yang juga dihormati di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey dan wilayah lain di Afrika.
short_description.en: Ayida Wedo is a rainbow-serpent loa, or divine spirit, of Haitian Vodou and the partner of Damballa, also honoured in the former Dahomey kingdom and nearby parts of Africa.

long_description.id:
Ayida Wedo, juga ditulis Ayida-Weddo atau Aida Wedo, adalah lwa yang kuat dalam vodou Haiti dan dihormati baik di Karibia maupun di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey/Benin, Togo, dan Ghana tenggara. Ia adalah dewi langit, awan, dan badai, dengan lambang ular dan pelangi. Ia dikaitkan dengan warna biru dan putih, warna langit dan awan.

Ia adalah istri Damballa dan melambangkan kekayaan, keberuntungan, serta kebahagiaan. Seperti suaminya ia tinggal dekat sungai dan menyukai pepohonan. Ia dianggap dewi yang jarang berbelas kasih dalam vaudou, yang kerap melawan Mami Wata untuk mencabut kutukannya atas orang yang tidak setia.

Menurut mitos penciptaan, para dewa ini sudah ada sebelum Bumi, dan Ayida Wedo membantu Mawu-Lisa membentuk dunia: ular itu membawa sang dewi di mulutnya, dan tubuhnya meninggalkan ngarai, sungai, lembah, dan gunung. Di Haiti dikisahkan bahwa ia menyeberangi samudra bersama Damballa; Damballa merayap di bawah laut sementara Ayida Wedo terbang di langit sebagai pelangi hingga keduanya bertemu lagi di Haiti.

Dalam Vodou Haiti ia disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. Dalam ritual kerasukan, mediumnya berpakaian putih dengan hiasan kepala berpermata dan merayap di tanah seperti ular.

Ellis mencatat bahwa orang Ewe memuja Anyi-ewo, dewa pelangi berwujud ular yang muncul ketika haus dan meminum air dalam jumlah besar sehingga tumpahannya turun sebagai hujan. Di Whydah dan Porto Novo, menurutnya, dewa ini punya nama lain yang ditulis Captain Burton sebagai Aydo-whe-do. Manik-manik Popo dipercaya dibuat olehnya.
long_description.en:
Ayida Wedo, also spelled Ayida-Weddo or Aida Wedo, is a mighty lwa of Haitian vodou who is honoured in the Caribbean as well as in the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin, Togo and southeastern Ghana. She rules sky, clouds and storms, and the snake and the rainbow are her emblems. Blue and white, the hues of sky and cloud, belong to her.

She is Damballa's wife and stands for wealth, luck and happiness. Like him she dwells near rivers and is fond of trees. She is counted a rare merciful deity of vodou, often opposing Mami Wata to undo the curses laid on the unfaithful.

In the creation myth these deities predate the Earth, and Ayida Wedo helped Mawu-Lisa form the world: the serpent bore the goddess in its mouth, and its body carved out canyons, rivers, valleys and mountains. Haitian lore tells that she crossed the ocean with Damballa, he gliding beneath the sea while she flew overhead as a rainbow, until they met again in Haiti.

Haitian Vodou identifies her with Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. In possession rites her medium dresses in white with a jeweled headdress and slithers along the ground like a snake.

Ellis records that the Ewe honoured Anyi-ewo, a rainbow-god in serpent form who appears when thirsty and drinks so much that what he spills comes down as rain. In Whydah and Porto Novo, he notes, the god seems to bear another name, written by Captain Burton as Aydo-whe-do. Popo beads were believed to be his work.

short_description.id: Ayida Wedo adalah loa (roh ilahi) berwujud ular pelangi dalam Vodou Haiti, pasangan Damballa, yang juga dihormati di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey dan wilayah lain di Afrika.
short_description.en: Ayida Wedo is a rainbow-serpent loa, or divine spirit, of Haitian Vodou and the partner of Damballa, also honoured in the former Dahomey kingdom and nearby parts of Africa.

long_description.id: Ayida Wedo, juga ditulis Ayida-Weddo atau Aida Wedo, adalah lwa yang kuat dalam vodou Haiti dan dihormati baik di Karibia maupun di bekas Kerajaan Dahomey/Benin, Togo, dan Ghana tenggara. Ia adalah dewi langit, awan, dan badai, dengan lambang ular dan pelangi. Ia dikaitkan dengan warna biru dan putih, warna langit dan awan.
long_description.en: Ayida Wedo, also spelled Ayida-Weddo or Aida Wedo, is a mighty lwa of Haitian vodou who is honoured in the Caribbean as well as in the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin, Togo and southeastern Ghana. She rules sky, clouds and storms, and the snake and the rainbow are her emblems. Blue and white, the hues of sky and cloud, belong to her.

long_description.id: Ia adalah istri Damballa dan melambangkan kekayaan, keberuntungan, serta kebahagiaan. Seperti suaminya ia tinggal dekat sungai dan menyukai pepohonan. Ia dianggap dewi yang jarang berbelas kasih dalam vaudou, yang kerap melawan Mami Wata untuk mencabut kutukannya atas orang yang tidak setia.
long_description.en: She is Damballa's wife and stands for wealth, luck and happiness. Like him she dwells near rivers and is fond of trees. She is counted a rare merciful deity of vodou, often opposing Mami Wata to undo the curses laid on the unfaithful.

long_description.id: Menurut mitos penciptaan, para dewa ini sudah ada sebelum Bumi, dan Ayida Wedo membantu Mawu-Lisa membentuk dunia: ular itu membawa sang dewi di mulutnya, dan tubuhnya meninggalkan ngarai, sungai, lembah, dan gunung. Di Haiti dikisahkan bahwa ia menyeberangi samudra bersama Damballa; Damballa merayap di bawah laut sementara Ayida Wedo terbang di langit sebagai pelangi hingga keduanya bertemu lagi di Haiti.
long_description.en: In the creation myth these deities predate the Earth, and Ayida Wedo helped Mawu-Lisa form the world: the serpent bore the goddess in its mouth, and its body carved out canyons, rivers, valleys and mountains. Haitian lore tells that she crossed the ocean with Damballa, he gliding beneath the sea while she flew overhead as a rainbow, until they met again in Haiti.

long_description.id: Dalam Vodou Haiti ia disinkretiskan dengan Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. Dalam ritual kerasukan, mediumnya berpakaian putih dengan hiasan kepala berpermata dan merayap di tanah seperti ular.
long_description.en: Haitian Vodou identifies her with Our Lady of Immaculate Conception. In possession rites her medium dresses in white with a jeweled headdress and slithers along the ground like a snake.

long_description.id: Ellis mencatat bahwa orang Ewe memuja Anyi-ewo, dewa pelangi berwujud ular yang muncul ketika haus dan meminum air dalam jumlah besar sehingga tumpahannya turun sebagai hujan. Di Whydah dan Porto Novo, menurutnya, dewa ini punya nama lain yang ditulis Captain Burton sebagai Aydo-whe-do. Manik-manik Popo dipercaya dibuat olehnya.
long_description.en: Ellis records that the Ewe honoured Anyi-ewo, a rainbow-god in serpent form who appears when thirsty and drinks so much that what he spills comes down as rain. In Whydah and Porto Novo, he notes, the god seems to bear another name, written by Captain Burton as Aydo-whe-do. Popo beads were believed to be his work.

statement.en: Ayida Wedo is a powerful loa spirit in Haitian vodou, revered in regions of Africa (including the former Dahomey kingdom/Benin, Togo and southeastern Ghana) and the Caribbean.

statement.en: In a cosmic mythical context the deities are thought to have existed before the Earth, and Ayida Wedo assisted the creator goddess Mawu-Lisa in forming the world.

statement.en: In Haitian Vodou, Ayida Wedo is syncretized with the Catholic figure of Our Lady of Immaculate Conception for her association with serpents and rainbow-colored cherubs.

short_description.id: Barak adalah anjing suci dalam mitologi Turk: anjing legendaris yang dianggap bukan anjing biasa, yang dalam sebagian legenda menetas dari telur burung Kerkes dan ditunggangi para dukun menuju langit.
short_description.en: Barak is the sacred dog of Turkic mythology: a legendary hound held to be no ordinary dog, which in some legends hatches from an egg of the bird Kerkes and is ridden by shamans up to the sky.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Turk, Barak dikenal sebagai anjing suci. Kedua sumber menyebutnya jenis anjing legendaris yang tidak dianggap anjing biasa, melainkan makhluk yang diberkati. Di Anadolu, nama yang sama juga dipakai untuk anjing pemburu yang berbulu lebat dan sangat cepat larinya.

Menurut sebagian legenda, ketika burung Kerkes menjadi tua ia meninggalkan dua telur: dari salah satunya lahir Barak, dari yang lain seekor anak burung. Para dukun dipercaya naik ke langit dengan menunggangi Barak dan konon mengenakan lambang-lambangnya di leher mereka.

Nama Barak juga dikenakan pada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda. Artikel pertama mencatat bahwa adanya seorang wali bernama Barak Ata atau Barak Baba di Anadolu tidak dianggap kebetulan.
long_description.en:
In Turkic mythology Barak is known as the sacred dog. Both sources describe it as a legendary kind of dog that is not regarded as an ordinary animal but as a blessed being. In Anadolu the same name is also used for shaggy hunting dogs that run very fast.

According to some legends, when the bird Kerkes grows old it leaves two eggs: Barak emerges from one of them and a chick from the other. Shamans are believed to rise to the sky mounted on Barak and are said to wear its symbols around their necks.

The name Barak is also applied to legendary dog-headed people. The first article notes that the presence of a saint called Barak Ata or Barak Baba in Anadolu is not regarded as a coincidence.

literal_meaning.id: Akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan; dalam bahasa Mongol Bar berarti harimau dan Barah berarti perdamaian.
literal_meaning.en: The root Bar carries meanings of joy and pride; in Mongolian Bar means tiger and Barah means peace.

claim.id: Barak adalah anjing suci (Kutsal Köpek) dalam mitologi Turk; di Anadolu nama ini juga dipakai untuk anjing pemburu berbulu.
claim.en: Barak is the Sacred Dog (Kutsal Köpek) in Turkic mythology (Türk mitolojisinde); in Anadolu the name is also given to hairy hunting dogs (tüylü av köpeklerine).

claims_provenance.quote: Barak - Türk mitolojisinde Kutsal Köpek. Anadoluda tüylü av köpeklerine de bu ad verilir.

claim.id: Barak adalah jenis anjing legendaris; ia bukan anjing biasa melainkan dianggap suci (kutlu).
claim.en: Barak is a legendary kind of dog (efsânevî bir köpek türü); it is not an ordinary dog (sıradan bir köpek) but is considered blessed (kutlu).

claims_provenance.quote: Efsânevî bir köpek türüdür. Barak sıradan bir köpek olmayıp kutlu sayılır.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Nama ini juga diberikan kepada anjing pemburu yang berbulu lebat dan berlari sangat cepat.
claim.en: The name is also given to hairy, shaggy hunting dogs (av köpeklerine) that run very fast (çok hızlı koşan).

claims_provenance.quote: Tüylü ve kıllı, çok hızlı koşan av köpeklerine de bu ad verilir.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Dalam sebagian legenda, burung bernama Kerkes bertelur dua butir ketika menua; dari satu telur menetas Barak, dari telur lainnya seekor anak burung.
claim.en: In some legends (bazı efsanelerde) the bird called Kerkes lays two eggs when it grows old; from one hatches Barak, from the other egg a chick (kuş yavrusu).

claims_provenance.quote: Bazı efsanelerde Kerkes adlı kuş yaşlanınca iki yumurta bırakır. Bunlardan birinden Barak, diğer yumurtadan ise bir kuş yavrusu çıkar.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Dipercaya bahwa para dukun (şaman) naik ke langit dengan menunggangi Barak, dan konon mereka mengalungkan lambang-lambangnya di leher.
claim.en: It is believed that shamans (şamanlar) ascend to the sky (göğe çıktıkları) riding Barak, and they are said to wear its symbols (simgelerini) on their necks.

claims_provenance.quote: Şamanların Barak'a binerek göğe çıktıklarına inanılır ve boyunlarına onun simgelerini taktıkları söylenir.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Keberadaan seorang wali (evliya) bernama Barak Ata (Barak Baba) di Anadolu dianggap bukan kebetulan.
claim.en: The presence in Anadolu of a saint (evliya) named Barak Ata (Barak Baba) is said to be no coincidence (tesadüfi değildir).

claims_provenance.quote: Anadolu'da Barak Ata (Barak Baba) adlı bir evliyanın yer alması tesadüfi değildir.

claim.id: Nama Barak juga diberikan kepada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda.
claim.en: The name Barak is also given to legendary dog-headed people (köpek başlı insanlara).

claims_provenance.quote: Efsânevî köpek başlı insanlara da Barak adı verilir.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Nama ini berasal dari akar Bar/Var; dalam bahasa Turk Kuno dan Altai Kuno akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan.
claim.en: The name is from the root Bar/Var; in Old Turkic (Eski Türkçe) and Old Altaic (eski Altayca) the root Bar carries meanings such as joy and pride (sevinç ve gurur).

claims_provenance.quote: Anlam: (Bar/Var). Eski Türkçe ve eski Altayca'da Bar kökü sevinç ve gurur gibi içeriklere sâhiptir.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Internet Archive (digital edition by the author) — Türk Söylence Sözlüğü

claim.id: Dalam bahasa Mongol kata Barah bermakna gencatan senjata dan perdamaian, sedangkan Bar berarti harimau.
claim.en: In Mongolian (Moğolcada) the word Barah means truce and peace (ateşkes, barış), while Bar means tiger (kaplan).

claims_provenance.quote: Moğolca'da Barah sözcüğü ateşkes, barış gibi anlamlar taşır. Bar ise kaplan demektir.

statement.id: Barak adalah anjing suci (Kutsal Köpek) dalam mitologi Turk; di Anadolu nama ini juga dipakai untuk anjing pemburu berbulu.
statement.en: Barak is the Sacred Dog (Kutsal Köpek) in Turkic mythology (Türk mitolojisinde); in Anadolu the name is also given to hairy hunting dogs (tüylü av köpeklerine).

claims.quote: Efsânevî bir köpek türüdür. Barak sıradan bir köpek olmayıp kutlu sayılır.

statement.id: Barak adalah jenis anjing legendaris; ia bukan anjing biasa melainkan dianggap suci (kutlu).
statement.en: Barak is a legendary kind of dog (efsânevî bir köpek türü); it is not an ordinary dog (sıradan bir köpek) but is considered blessed (kutlu).

claims.quote: Tüylü ve kıllı, çok hızlı koşan av köpeklerine de bu ad verilir.

statement.id: Nama ini juga diberikan kepada anjing pemburu yang berbulu lebat dan berlari sangat cepat.
statement.en: The name is also given to hairy, shaggy hunting dogs (av köpeklerine) that run very fast (çok hızlı koşan).

claims.quote: Bazı efsanelerde Kerkes adlı kuş yaşlanınca iki yumurta bırakır. Bunlardan birinden Barak, diğer yumurtadan ise bir kuş yavrusu çıkar.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian legenda, burung bernama Kerkes bertelur dua butir ketika menua; dari satu telur menetas Barak, dari telur lainnya seekor anak burung.
statement.en: In some legends (bazı efsanelerde) the bird called Kerkes lays two eggs when it grows old; from one hatches Barak, from the other egg a chick (kuş yavrusu).

claims.quote: Şamanların Barak'a binerek göğe çıktıklarına inanılır ve boyunlarına onun simgelerini taktıkları söylenir.

statement.id: Dipercaya bahwa para dukun (şaman) naik ke langit dengan menunggangi Barak, dan konon mereka mengalungkan lambang-lambangnya di leher.
statement.en: It is believed that shamans (şamanlar) ascend to the sky (göğe çıktıkları) riding Barak, and they are said to wear its symbols (simgelerini) on their necks.

claims.quote: Anadolu'da Barak Ata (Barak Baba) adlı bir evliyanın yer alması tesadüfi değildir.

statement.id: Keberadaan seorang wali (evliya) bernama Barak Ata (Barak Baba) di Anadolu dianggap bukan kebetulan.
statement.en: The presence in Anadolu of a saint (evliya) named Barak Ata (Barak Baba) is said to be no coincidence (tesadüfi değildir).

claims.quote: Efsânevî köpek başlı insanlara da Barak adı verilir.

statement.id: Nama Barak juga diberikan kepada manusia berkepala anjing dalam legenda.
statement.en: The name Barak is also given to legendary dog-headed people (köpek başlı insanlara).

claims.quote: Anlam: (Bar/Var). Eski Türkçe ve eski Altayca'da Bar kökü sevinç ve gurur gibi içeriklere sâhiptir.

statement.id: Nama ini berasal dari akar Bar/Var; dalam bahasa Turk Kuno dan Altai Kuno akar Bar memuat makna sukacita dan kebanggaan.
statement.en: The name is from the root Bar/Var; in Old Turkic (Eski Türkçe) and Old Altaic (eski Altayca) the root Bar carries meanings such as joy and pride (sevinç ve gurur).

claims.quote: Moğolca'da Barah sözcüğü ateşkes, barış gibi anlamlar taşır. Bar ise kaplan demektir.

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Mongol kata Barah bermakna gencatan senjata dan perdamaian, sedangkan Bar berarti harimau.
statement.en: In Mongolian (Moğolcada) the word Barah means truce and peace (ateşkes, barış), while Bar means tiger (kaplan).

short_description.id: Beast of Bodmin adalah hewan mirip kucing besar yang konon terlihat di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan dianggap sebagai salah satu "British big cats".
short_description.en: The Beast of Bodmin is a big-cat-like animal reportedly seen on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, counted among the 'British big cats'.

long_description.id:
Beast of Bodmin (atau Beast of Bodmin Moor) adalah salah satu kucing besar Britania (British big cats) yang paling terkenal, yang dituduh membunuh ternak. Menurut artikel ru, hewan mirip kucing besar ini terlihat lebih dari 60 kali sejak 1983 di Bodmin Moor, Cornwall, Inggris, dan diduga panther atau puma yang lepas dari kebun binatang atau koleksi pribadi. Penyelidikan pemerintah pada 1995 tidak menemukan bukti keberadaan hewan semacam itu, meski laporan penampakan terus berlanjut. Menurut artikel it, makhluk itu konon mirip puma berwarna abu-abu gelap hingga hitam dan juga terlihat di Devon dan Somerset.

Ketika sebuah tengkorak yang ditemukan di Sungai Fowey diserahkan kepada Natural History Museum sebagai bukti keberadaannya, tengkorak itu ternyata dipotong dari permadani kulit macan tutul. Menurut artikel ru, tengkorak yang ditemukan pada 1995 itu memang milik macan tutul jantan muda, tetapi hewan itu tidak dibunuh di Inggris. Para ilmuwan menyatakan laporan semacam itu biasanya tidak dapat dipercaya, karena kelangsungan populasi memerlukan jumlah individu yang tak masuk akal, sedangkan iklim dan sulitnya mencari makan membuat hewan yang lepas sulit bertahan.
long_description.en:
The Beast of Bodmin (or Beast of Bodmin Moor) is one of the best-known British big cats, blamed for killing livestock. According to the ru article this big-cat-like animal has been seen more than 60 times since 1983 on Bodmin Moor in Cornwall, England, and is thought to be a panther or puma escaped from a zoo or private collection. A government inquiry in 1995 found no evidence of such animals, though sightings continued. According to the it article it is said to look like a puma, dark grey to black, and has also been reported in Devon and Somerset.

When a skull found in the River Fowey was offered to the Natural History Museum as proof of the beast, it turned out to have been cut from a leopard-skin rug. According to the ru article that skull, found in 1995, did belong to a young male leopard, but the animal had not been killed in England. Scientists say such reports are usually unreliable, since a lasting population would need an implausible number of animals, while the climate and scarce prey make survival of escaped cats unlikely.

short_description.id: Beast of Exmoor adalah kucing besar misterius yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di Exmoor, Devon dan Somerset, dan terkenal sejak pembantaian domba tahun 1983.
short_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is a mysterious big cat reported to roam Exmoor in Devon and Somerset, famous since the sheep killings of 1983.

long_description.id:
Beast of Exmoor adalah salah satu kisah kucing besar Britania yang paling terkenal: kucing kriptozoologi berbulu abu-abu gelap atau hitam yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di pedesaan Exmoor, terutama Devon dan Somerset. Penampakan dilaporkan sejak 1970, dan kisahnya menjadi berita nasional pada 1983 ketika lebih dari seratus domba mati dengan leher terkoyak di South Molton.

Makhluk itu diduga macan tutul hitam atau puma yang dilepas secara ilegal, tetapi tidak ada kucing besar yang pernah dipastikan, dan pembantaian 1983 kini dikaitkan dengan penyebab lain seperti anjing besar. Bangkai yang pernah diberitakan sebagai Beast of Exmoor ternyata anjing laut mati.
long_description.en:
The Beast of Exmoor is one of the best-known British big cat stories: a cryptozoological cat with dark grey or black fur reported in rural Exmoor, especially Devon and Somerset. Sightings were reported from 1970, and the story became national news in 1983 when more than a hundred sheep were killed with torn throats at South Molton.

It was thought to be an illegally released black leopard or puma, but no big cat has ever been confirmed, and the 1983 killings are now attributed to causes such as large dogs. A carcass once reported as the Beast of Exmoor proved to be a dead seal.

short_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is a mysterious big cat reported to roam Exmoor in Devon and Somerset, famous since the sheep killings of 1983.

long_description.id: Beast of Exmoor adalah salah satu kisah kucing besar Britania yang paling terkenal: kucing kriptozoologi berbulu abu-abu gelap atau hitam yang dilaporkan berkeliaran di pedesaan Exmoor, terutama Devon dan Somerset. Penampakan dilaporkan sejak 1970, dan kisahnya menjadi berita nasional pada 1983 ketika lebih dari seratus domba mati dengan leher terkoyak di South Molton.
long_description.en: The Beast of Exmoor is one of the best-known British big cat stories: a cryptozoological cat with dark grey or black fur reported in rural Exmoor, especially Devon and Somerset. Sightings were reported from 1970, and the story became national news in 1983 when more than a hundred sheep were killed with torn throats at South Molton.

long_description.id: Makhluk itu diduga macan tutul hitam atau puma yang dilepas secara ilegal, tetapi tidak ada kucing besar yang pernah dipastikan, dan pembantaian 1983 kini dikaitkan dengan penyebab lain seperti anjing besar. Bangkai yang pernah diberitakan sebagai Beast of Exmoor ternyata anjing laut mati.
long_description.en: It was thought to be an illegally released black leopard or puma, but no big cat has ever been confirmed, and the 1983 killings are now attributed to causes such as large dogs. A carcass once reported as the Beast of Exmoor proved to be a dead seal.

short_description.id: Begu ganjang, atau hantu panjang, adalah roh jahat dalam kepercayaan Batak yang digambarkan besar, kurus, dan gelap seperti bayangan, tampak makin tinggi bila dipandang lebih lama, dan dipercaya dapat dipelihara untuk mencelakai orang.
short_description.en: Begu ganjang, the long ghost, is an evil spirit of Batak belief described as large, thin and shadow-dark, appearing to grow taller the longer it is looked at, and believed to be keepable to harm others.

long_description.id:
Dalam kepercayaan masyarakat Batak, begu ganjang termasuk jenis roh jahat yang digambarkan ganas. Tugasnya mencelakai orang, dan korbannya konon ditinggali lebam kebiruan di tenggorokan. Di kalangan Batak Karo ia dinamai begu jinujung, dan pemiliknya harus memberinya sajian berupa darah ayam merah.

Secara harfiah begu berarti roh atau hantu dan ganjang berarti panjang atau tinggi. Dalam berbagai cerita rakyat Batak ia dipaparkan besar, kurus, dan memanjang, gelap seperti bayangan, dan tampak makin tinggi serta besar bila dipandang lebih lama. Dalam kajian di Sumatra Utara, sebagian informan menyebut ia tampak seperti bayangan yang makin tinggi bila dilihat ke atas, sementara deskripsi populer lain menyebut bentuknya besar dan hitam, atau bahwa ia dipelihara untuk tujuan tertentu seperti menjaga ladang, atau bahwa ia tidak punya bentuk khusus.

Menurut budaya Batak, begu ganjang termasuk makhluk gaib yang dipercaya bermula dari manusia ataupun tempat tertentu. Menurut pemahaman Batak Toba, roh orang yang meninggal berubah menjadi begu, dan begu ganjang adalah salah satu jenisnya. Dalam sejumlah tradisi lisan ia dipercaya sebagai roh penjaga lahan pertanian; dalam perkembangan berikutnya ia lebih sering dikaitkan dengan ilmu hitam yang destruktif dan dengan dukun yang dipercaya dapat memanggil atau memeliharanya. Sebuah turi-turian Batak Toba menyebut begu ganjang sebagai satu dari nama yang diberikan Datu Tala kepada cucu-cucunya.

Kepercayaan ini dipakai untuk menjelaskan kejadian yang sulit dipahami, seperti penyakit misterius, kondisi fisik yang memburuk tanpa sebab jelas, dan kematian mendadak. Isu begu ganjang cenderung beredar ketika ada kematian mendadak tanpa penyebab yang tampak. Masyarakat mencurigai orang tertentu sebagai sigumoang, yang dianggap memiliki dan mengendalikannya, dan orang yang dicurigai memeliharanya pernah menjadi sasaran kekerasan; sebuah kajian menyatakan narasinya awalnya dihormati sebagai warisan budaya tetapi sering disalahgunakan untuk membenarkan tindakan kriminal.
long_description.en:
In Batak belief, the begu ganjang is counted among the evil spirits and is described as fierce. Its task is to harm people, and its victims are said to be left with a bluish bruise in the throat. Among the Karo Batak it is called begu jinujung, and its owner must give it offerings of red chicken blood.

Literally, begu means spirit or ghost and ganjang means long or tall. In various Batak folk tales it is depicted as large, thin and elongated, dark like a shadow, and appearing to grow taller and bigger the longer it is looked at. In a study in North Sumatra, some informants described it as a shadow that grows taller when looked up at, while other popular descriptions say its form is large and black, or that it is kept for certain purposes such as guarding fields, or that it has no particular form.

In Batak culture, begu ganjang is a supernatural being believed to originate from humans or certain places. In Batak Toba understanding, the spirits of the dead become begu, and begu ganjang is one kind. In some oral traditions it is believed to be a guardian spirit of farmland; in later developments it is more often linked with destructive black magic and with shamans believed able to summon or keep it. A Batak Toba turi-turian lists begu ganjang among the names Datu Tala gave to his grandchildren.

The belief is used to explain events that are hard to understand, such as mysterious illness, unexplained physical decline and sudden death. Rumors of begu ganjang tend to spread when a sudden death has no visible cause. People suspect certain persons of being sigumoang, regarded as owning and controlling it, and people suspected of keeping it have been targets of violence; one study states that the narrative was first respected as cultural heritage but is often misused to justify criminal acts.

role.en: An evil spirit tasked with harming others, and in some oral traditions a guardian spirit of farmland.

did_you_know.id: Dalam sebuah turi-turian Batak Toba, begu ganjang adalah salah satu dari enam nama yang diberikan Datu Tala kepada cucu-cucunya, sedangkan cucu ketujuh disebut jolma (manusia).
did_you_know.en: In a Batak Toba turi-turian, begu ganjang is one of six names Datu Tala gave to his grandchildren, while the seventh grandchild was called jolma (human).

cultural_context.id: Menurut sebuah kajian, narasi tentang begu yang diteliti berfungsi sebagai narasi persuasif untuk mencegah perilaku buruk dan merugikan, dan isu begu ganjang cenderung beredar ketika terjadi kematian mendadak tanpa sebab yang tampak. Suku Batak Toba juga meyakini bahwa arwah orang yang telah wafat tetap bisa mengawasi, melindungi, dan merawat anak cucunya.
cultural_context.en: According to one study, the begu narratives it examines serve as persuasive narratives to prevent bad and harmful behavior, and rumors of begu ganjang tend to spread when a sudden death has no visible cause. The Batak Toba people also believe the spirits of the dead can still watch over, protect and look after their descendants.

description.id: Dalam berbagai cerita rakyat Batak, ia tampak makin tinggi dan besar bila dipandang lebih lama; satu deskripsi populer menyebut ia akhirnya membunuh orang yang melihatnya.
description.en: In various Batak folk tales it appears to grow taller and bigger the longer it is looked at; one popular description says it finally kills the one who looks at it.

summary.en: Datu Tala Dibabana had seven grandchildren born at once; he named six of them with names including begu ganjang, while the seventh was called jolma (human). The study that reports it notes that this tale does not present the begu as evil.

description.en: Tempo magazine recorded a woman who died after a mob attacked her house because it was believed to bear the marks of a begu ganjang keeper's house.

claim.en: In Batak belief, the begu ganjang is a fierce evil spirit tasked with harming people and leaving a bruise on the victim's throat; the Karo Batak call it begu jinujung, which its owner must feed with red-chicken blood.

claims_provenance.quote: dalam kepercayaan masyarakat Batak adalah salah satu jenis roh jahat. Dalam masyarakat Batak, begu ganjang digambarkan sebagai roh ganas karena bertugas untuk mencelakakan orang lain dan menyisakan bekas biru di kerongkongan korbannya. Masyarakat Batak Karo menyebut begu ganjang sebagai "begu jinujung", yaitu roh yang harus diberikan sajian darah ayam merah oleh pemiliknya.

claim.id: Dalam budaya Batak, Begu Ganjang adalah makhluk gaib yang diyakini berasal dari manusia atau tempat tertentu; manusia dianggap punya jasad (pamatang) dan roh (tondi), dan setelah kematian roh dipercaya menjadi begu yang pergi ke parbeguan, tempat berkumpulnya roh orang yang telah meninggal.
claim.en: In Batak culture, Begu Ganjang is a supernatural being believed to originate from humans or certain places; a person is considered to have a body (pamatang) and a soul (tondi), and after death the soul is believed to become a begu that goes to the parbeguan, where the spirits of the dead gather.

claims_provenance.quote: Dalam budaya Batak, Begu Ganjang adalah makhluk gaib yang diyakini berasal dari manusia atau tempat tertentu. Manusia dianggap memiliki dua unsur yaitu jasad atau fisik, yang disebut pamatang, dan roh, yang disebut tondi. Setelah kematian, roh dipercaya berubah menjadi begu. Begu kemudian pergi ke parbeguan, tempat gaib di mana berkumpul roh-roh orang yang telah meninggal.

claim.id: Secara harfiah begu berarti "roh" atau "hantu" dan ganjang berarti "panjang" atau "tinggi", sehingga nama itu sering diterjemahkan sebagai hantu panjang.
claim.en: Literally, begu means "spirit" or "ghost" and ganjang means "long" or "tall", so the name is often translated as long ghost.

claim.en: According to this study, Siagian (1990: 7-11) tells that Datu Tala Dibabana had seven grandchildren born at once to his daughter.

claim.id: Dalam kisah itu, Datu Tala memanggil cucu-cucunya dan melibaskan tujuh lidi pada mereka sambil menamai keenam cucunya porhas, sibalik hunik, begu ngurngur, sombaon di laut, patuallang ni aji, dan begu ganjang, sedangkan cucu ketujuh disebut jolma (manusia).
claim.en: In the tale, Datu Tala called his grandchildren and struck seven lidi (palm ribs) on them while naming six of them porhas, sibalik hunik, begu ngurngur, sombaon di laut, patuallang ni aji and begu ganjang, while the seventh grandchild was called jolma (human).

claims_provenance.quote: Datu Tala memanggil semua cucunya itu dan melibaskan tujuh lidi pada mereka sambil menamai keenam cucunya dengan sebutan porhas, sibalik hunik, begu ngurngur, sombaon di laut, patuallang ni aji, dan begu ganjang sementara cucu ketujuh disebut jolma (manusia).

claim.en: According to this study, a tona (message) myth that also uses the term begu ganjang warns against envy leading to bad deeds.

claim.id: Menurut kajian ini, sebutan begu ganjang ada karena kemungkinan wujudnya bertubuh panjang atau tinggi sehingga langkahnya panjang, dan sosok itu dipercaya dapat dipelihara untuk mencelakakan orang lain.
claim.en: According to this study, the name begu ganjang exists possibly because its form has a long or tall body and so long strides, and the being is believed to be keepable in order to harm others.

claims_provenance.quote: sebutan begu ganjang eksis karena kemungkinan bentuk dari begu ganjang adalah bertubuh panjang atau tinggi sehingga langkahnya pun panjang. Sosok begu ganjang dipercaya dapat dipelihara guna mencelakakan orang lain

claim.id: Menurut kajian ini, Situmorang (2021: 8) menyatakan bahwa istilah "begu ganjang" menandakan adanya gerakan bawah tanah oleh kelompok tertentu untuk menghabisi lawan-lawannya.
claim.en: According to this study, Situmorang (2021: 8) states that the term "begu ganjang" signals an underground movement by certain groups to eliminate their opponents.

claims_provenance.quote: Terkait istilah “begu ganjang”, Situmorang (2021: 8) menyatakan bahwa istilah ... tersebut menandakan adanya sebuah gerakan bawah tanah oleh kelompok tertentu untuk menghabisi lawan-lawannya.

claim.id: Menurut informan yang mengaku pernah mengalaminya dalam kajian ini, begu ganjang tampak seperti bayangan yang semakin tinggi bila semakin dilihat ke atas, dan mereka percaya kematian mendadak disebabkan oleh begu ganjang.
claim.en: According to informants in this study who said they had experienced it, begu ganjang looks like a shadow that grows taller the more one looks up at it, and they believe sudden death is caused by begu ganjang.

claims_provenance.quote: begu ganjang tampak seperti bayangan yang semakin tinggi jika semakin dilihat ke atas dan percaya bahwa kematian orang secara mendadak disebabkan oleh begu ganjang.

claim.id: Menurut kajian ini, salah satu deskripsi populer adalah bahwa begu ganjang dipersepsi makin tinggi bila makin dilihat dan akhirnya membunuh orang yang melihatnya; deskripsi lain menyebut bentuknya besar dan hitam.
claim.en: According to this study, one popular description is that begu ganjang is perceived as growing taller the more it is looked at and finally killing the one who looks at it; another says its form is large and black.

claims_provenance.quote: begu ganjang dipersepsi akan semakin tinggi jika semakin dilihat dan akhirnya membunuh orang yang melihatnya. Kedua, bentuknya besar dan hitam.

claim.id: Menurut kajian ini, deskripsi populer lain adalah bahwa begu ganjang dipelihara untuk tujuan tertentu, misalnya menjaga ladang.
claim.en: According to this study, another popular description is that begu ganjang is kept for certain purposes, for example guarding fields.

claims_provenance.quote: Ketiga, begu ganjang dipelihara untuk tujuan tertentu, misalnya menjaga ladang

claim.id: Menurut kajian ini, ada pula persepsi bahwa begu ganjang tidak memiliki bentuk khusus.
claim.en: According to this study, there is also a perception that begu ganjang has no particular form.

claims_provenance.quote: Ada pula persepsi bahwa begu ganjang itu tidak memiliki bentuk khusus.
