short_description.id: Coatlicue ('Rok Ular') adalah dewi ibu bumi dalam panteon Aztec. Ia digambarkan mengenakan rok ular dan kalung jantung manusia, serta menjadi ibu dari dewa perang Huitzilopochtli.
short_description.en: Coatlicue ('Serpent Skirt') is the earth-mother goddess of the Aztec pantheon. She is shown in a skirt of snakes and a necklace of human hearts, and is mother of the war god Huitzilopochtli.

long_description.id: Coatlicue adalah dewa penting dalam panteon Aztec dan dianggap sebagai dewi ibu bumi. Ia dikenal sebagai pelindung persalinan dan dikaitkan dengan perang, pemerintahan, serta pertanian. Ia juga dianggap sebagai aspek perempuan dari dewa purba Ometeotl.
long_description.en: Coatlicue was a major deity in the Aztec pantheon and was regarded as the earth-mother goddess. She presided over childbirth and was linked to war, rule, and farming. She was also considered the female aspect of the primordial god Ometeotl.

long_description.id: Coatlicue digambarkan sebagai perempuan yang mengenakan rok ular menggeliat dan kalung dari jantung, tangan, dan tengkorak manusia. Kaki dan tangannya dihiasi cakar. Penggambarannya yang paling terkenal adalah patung basal raksasa yang ditemukan di Tenochtitlan dan kini berada di Museum Nasional Antropologi di Mexico City. Pada penggambaran itu, cakar besar di tangan dan kakinya dipakai untuk mencabik mayat manusia sebelum ia memakannya.
long_description.en: Coatlicue is shown as a woman in a skirt of writhing snakes, with a necklace of human hearts, hands, and skulls and claws on her hands and feet. Her best-known depiction is the colossal basalt statue found at Tenochtitlan, today kept in the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City. In that depiction, the large claws on her hands and feet are used to rip up human corpses before she eats them.

long_description.id: Menurut mitologi Aztec, Coatlicue adalah seorang pendeta perempuan yang merawat kuil di puncak gunung suci Coatepec. Saat ia menyapu, sebuah bola bulu jatuh dari langit dan membuatnya hamil secara ajaib. Anak itu adalah Huitzilopochtli, dewa perang. Putrinya Coyolxauhqui dan 400 saudara laki-lakinya menganggap kehamilan itu aib dan berencana membunuhnya, tetapi Huitzilopochtli lahir dengan senjata lengkap dan mengalahkan mereka.
long_description.en: According to Aztec mythology, Coatlicue was a priestess who tended the shrine on top of the sacred mountain Coatepec. As she swept, a ball of feathers fell from the sky and miraculously made her pregnant. The child was Huitzilopochtli, the god of war. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui and 400 brothers saw the pregnancy as dishonor and plotted to kill her, but Huitzilopochtli emerged fully armed and defeated them.

long_description.id: Dalam mitos lain, Coatlicue memperingatkan bangsa Mexica bahwa kota-kota Aztec akan jatuh satu per satu. Ia dipuja dalam ritual Tozozontli dan perayaan Quecholli, ketika seorang peniru sang dewi dikorbankan. Menurut satu tafsiran ilmiah, ia juga memiliki aspek penciptaan yang dapat mengimbangi tengkorak, jantung, tangan, dan cakar yang menghubungkannya dengan dewa bumi Tlaltecuhtli.
long_description.en: In another myth Coatlicue warned the Mexica that the Aztec cities would fall one by one. She was worshipped in the Tozozontli ritual and the Quecholli festival, when an impersonator of the goddess was sacrificed. One scholarly reading holds that her creative side may offset the skulls, hearts, hands, and claws that tie her to the earth deity Tlaltecuhtli.

short_description.id: Dakuwaqa adalah dewa hiu dalam mitologi Fiji yang tampil sebagai monster laut garang, menjaga kepulauan, dan dihormati nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari bahaya di laut.
short_description.en: Dakuwaqa is a shark god of Fijian mythology who appears as a fierce sea monster, guards the islands, and was respected by fishermen as their protector at sea.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Fiji, Dakuwaqa (juga ditulis Dakuwanga) adalah dewa hiu yang sering tampil sebagai monster laut yang garang dan menjaga kepulauan. Ia sangat dihormati nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari setiap bahaya di laut dan para penghuninya. Namanya berarti "bagian belakang perahu"; sebuah museum menyebutnya salah satu dari dua dewa hiu leluhur Fiji yang namanya dikaitkan dengan perahu dan layar.

Dakuwaqa dapat mengubah wujud menjadi apa pun, tetapi wujud aslinya adalah lelaki Fiji yang berotot dengan tubuh bagian atas hiu. Seorang warga desa menuturkan bahwa setiap kali Dakuwaqa datang ke desa, ia menjelma manusia.

Dalam satu mitos penciptaan, Dakuwaqa berencana menaklukkan Pulau Kadavu lewat sungai, tetapi dewi Rokobakaniceva menantangnya dalam wujud gurita. Gurita itu mencabut giginya dengan delapan lengan, menahan serangannya, dan memaksa Dakuwaqa berjanji tidak menyerang Kadavu lagi; demikianlah Dakuwaqa menjadi dewa dan pelindung Kadavu.

Kepercayaan itu hidup di masa modern. Sebuah catatan abad kedua puluh menggambarkan ikan besar berkepala hiu dan berekor paus yang nyaris membalikkan sebuah kapal; awak Fiji menuangkan kava ke laut dan menyebutnya Dakuwaqa. Menurut museum itu, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, presiden pertama Fiji setelah kemerdekaan, adalah keturunan Dakuwaqa, dan para pelayat melaporkan kawanan hiu mengiringi kapal pemakamannya ke laut.
long_description.en:
In Fijian mythology Dakuwaqa (also written Dakuwanga) is a shark god who often appears as a fierce sea monster guarding the islands. Fishermen held him in great respect because he protected them from every danger at sea and its creatures. His name means "back of the boat"; a museum lists him as one of two ancestral shark gods of Fiji whose names are linked to boats and sails.

Dakuwaqa can take any shape, but his real form is a muscular Fijian man with the upper body of a shark. A villager says that whenever Dakuwaqa comes to the village he turns himself into a human.

In one creation myth Dakuwaqa planned to take Kadavu Island by way of the river, but the goddess Rokobakaniceva challenged him as an octopus. She pulled out his teeth with her arms, held off his assault, and made him promise never to attack Kadavu again; so Dakuwaqa became the god and protector of Kadavu.

The belief has stayed alive. A twentieth-century account describes a huge fish, shark-headed and whale-tailed, nearly capsizing a ship; the Fijian crew poured kava into the sea and called it Dakuwaqa. According to the museum, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, Fiji's first president after independence, descends from Dakuwaqa, and mourners reported sharks escorting the vessel carrying him out to sea.

short_description.en: Dakuwaqa is a shark god of Fijian mythology who appears as a fierce sea monster, guards the islands, and was respected by fishermen as their protector at sea.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Fiji, Dakuwaqa (juga ditulis Dakuwanga) adalah dewa hiu yang sering tampil sebagai monster laut yang garang dan menjaga kepulauan. Ia sangat dihormati nelayan karena melindungi mereka dari setiap bahaya di laut dan para penghuninya. Namanya berarti "bagian belakang perahu"; sebuah museum menyebutnya salah satu dari dua dewa hiu leluhur Fiji yang namanya dikaitkan dengan perahu dan layar.
long_description.en: In Fijian mythology Dakuwaqa (also written Dakuwanga) is a shark god who often appears as a fierce sea monster guarding the islands. Fishermen held him in great respect because he protected them from every danger at sea and its creatures. His name means "back of the boat"; a museum lists him as one of two ancestral shark gods of Fiji whose names are linked to boats and sails.

long_description.id: Dakuwaqa dapat mengubah wujud menjadi apa pun, tetapi wujud aslinya adalah lelaki Fiji yang berotot dengan tubuh bagian atas hiu. Seorang warga desa menuturkan bahwa setiap kali Dakuwaqa datang ke desa, ia menjelma manusia.
long_description.en: Dakuwaqa can take any shape, but his real form is a muscular Fijian man with the upper body of a shark. A villager says that whenever Dakuwaqa comes to the village he turns himself into a human.

long_description.id: Dalam satu mitos penciptaan, Dakuwaqa berencana menaklukkan Pulau Kadavu lewat sungai, tetapi dewi Rokobakaniceva menantangnya dalam wujud gurita. Gurita itu mencabut giginya dengan delapan lengan, menahan serangannya, dan memaksa Dakuwaqa berjanji tidak menyerang Kadavu lagi; demikianlah Dakuwaqa menjadi dewa dan pelindung Kadavu.
long_description.en: In one creation myth Dakuwaqa planned to take Kadavu Island by way of the river, but the goddess Rokobakaniceva challenged him as an octopus. She pulled out his teeth with her arms, held off his assault, and made him promise never to attack Kadavu again; so Dakuwaqa became the god and protector of Kadavu.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan itu hidup di masa modern. Sebuah catatan abad kedua puluh menggambarkan ikan besar berkepala hiu dan berekor paus yang nyaris membalikkan sebuah kapal; awak Fiji menuangkan kava ke laut dan menyebutnya Dakuwaqa. Menurut museum itu, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, presiden pertama Fiji setelah kemerdekaan, adalah keturunan Dakuwaqa, dan para pelayat melaporkan kawanan hiu mengiringi kapal pemakamannya ke laut.

A twentieth-century account describes a huge fish, shark-headed and whale-tailed, nearly capsizing a ship; the Fijian crew poured kava into the sea and called it Dakuwaqa. According to the museum, Ratu Sir Penaia Ganilau, Fiji's first president after independence, descends from Dakuwaqa, and mourners reported sharks escorting the vessel carrying him out to sea.

short_description.id: Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame; suaranya diyakini terdengar lewat bullroarer dalam upacara inisiasi.
short_description.en: Daramulum is a sky hero of the Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, associated with Baiame; his voice is said to be heard through the bullroarer at initiation ceremonies.

long_description.id:
Dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara, Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame dan seorang istri emu, serta disebut pengubah wujud. Menurut catatan Howitt, kepercayaan kepada Daramulun, sang "bapa", dan Biamban, sang "tuan", dimiliki semua suku yang menghadiri Kuringal Yuin, dan agama yang berpusat pada Darhumulan menjadi ciri pengenal bangsa Yuin.

Suaranya terdengar melalui bullroarer yang diputar di udara dalam upacara inisiasi. Suku Yuin percaya guntur adalah suara Daramulun, dan anak-anak laki-laki diberi tahu bahwa ia akan melukai atau membunuh mereka jika membocorkan rahasia upacara.

Dalam salah satu catatan Howitt, figur Daramulun digambar di tanah sebagai "anak" Baiame yang berkaki satu, lengkap dengan kapak yang ia jatuhkan dan jejak kaki emu. Pada seni cadas di Taman Nasional Ku-ring-gai Chase ia digambarkan setengah profil dengan satu lengan, punggung emu, dan kaki besar, di dekat ukiran istri emu-nya; bagi suku Guringai ia diwakili bintang Alpha Crucis dari Salib Selatan.

Suku Ngarigo mengira roh orang mati naik ke langit dan disambut Daramulun, yang merawatnya. Dukun di mana-mana dipercaya menerima kekuatannya dari makhluk gaib seperti Baiame, Daramulun, atau Bunjil, dan satu bagian menyebut Daramulun tinggal di pohon dengan pembengkakan besar di sekeliling akarnya. Howitt sendiri menulis bahwa tidak ada pemujaan terhadap Daramulun, dan menganggap beberapa nama dewa dari berbagai suku mewakili satu sosok.
long_description.en:
In the Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum is a sky hero associated with Baiame and an emu-wife, and is described as a shapeshifter. In Howitt's record, belief in Daramulun, the "father", and Biamban, the "master", is shared by all the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal, and the Yuin nation is marked out by a religion built around Darhumulan.

His voice can be heard through the bullroarer whirled through the air during initiation ceremonies. The Yuin believe thunder is the voice of Daramulun, and boys are warned that he will harm or kill them should they reveal the secrets.

In one of Howitt's accounts, a figure of Daramulun is cut on the ground as the one-legged "boy" of Baiame, together with the tomahawk he let fall and emu footprints. In rock art in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park he is shown in semi-profile with one arm, an emu-back and a large foot, near a carving of his emu-wife; for the Guringai he is represented by Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross.

The Ngarigo thought the spirit of a dead person went up to the sky and was met by Daramulun, who takes care of it. Medicine-men are everywhere believed to receive their power from supernatural beings such as Baiame, Daramulun or Bunjil, and one passage says Daramulun lives in a tree with a great swelling round its roots. Howitt himself writes that there is not any worship of Daramulun, and regards several divine names from different tribes as representing one being.

sources.author: A. W. Howitt

claims.quote: In Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum ... is a sky hero associated with Baiame, and an emu-wife. He is a shapeshifter.

statement.id: Dalam budaya Aboriginal di Australia tenggara, Daramulum adalah pahlawan langit yang dikaitkan dengan Baiame dan seorang istri emu; ia disebut pengubah wujud.
statement.en: In Aboriginal cultures of south-east Australia, Daramulum is a sky hero associated with Baiame and an emu-wife, and is described as a shapeshifter.

claims.quote: He is depicted in semi-profile, with one arm, an emu-back (i.e. pointed buttocks), and a large foot.

statement.id: Daramulum digambarkan dalam setengah profil dengan satu lengan, punggung emu (bokong runcing), dan kaki besar.
statement.en: Daramulum is depicted in semi-profile with one arm, an emu-back (pointed buttocks), and a large foot.

claims.quote: His voice can be heard through the medium of the bullroarer which is whirled through the air during initiation ceremonies.

statement.id: Suara Daramulum terdengar melalui dengungan bullroarer dalam upacara inisiasi.
statement.en: His voice is heard through the bullroarer whirled during initiation ceremonies.

claims.quote: Daramulum is depicted on rock art off Elvina Track in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, near to a carving of his emu-wife.

statement.id: Daramulum digambarkan pada seni cadas di dekat Elvina Track di Taman Nasional Ku-ring-gai Chase, dekat ukiran istri emu-nya.
statement.en: Daramulum is depicted on rock art off Elvina Track in Ku-ring-gai Chase National Park, near to a carving of his emu-wife.

claims.quote: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by the Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the remainder of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife

statement.id: Bagi suku Guringai, Daramulum diwakili oleh bintang Alpha Crucis dari Salib Selatan, dan sisa rasi itu melambangkan kepala istri emu-nya.
statement.en: For the Guringai, Daramulum is represented by Alpha Crucis of the Southern Cross, with the rest of the Cross representing the head of his emu wife.

claims.quote: A religion centred on Darhumulan is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.

statement.id: Agama yang berpusat pada Darhumulan (ejaan lain nama ini) menjadi ciri pengenal bangsa Yuin.
statement.en: A religion centred on Darhumulan (a variant spelling of the name) is an identifying feature of the Yuin nation.

claims.quote: The belief in Daramulun, the " father," and Biamban, or " master," is common to all of the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.

statement.id: Kepercayaan kepada Daramulun, sang "bapa", dan Biamban, sang "tuan", dimiliki semua suku yang menghadiri Kuringal Yuin.
statement.en: Belief in Daramulun, the "father", and Biamban, the "master", is shared by all the tribes who attend the Yuin Kuringal.

claims.quote: The Yuin believe that the thunder is the voice of Daramulun.

statement.id: Suku Yuin percaya bahwa guntur adalah suara Daramulun.
statement.en: The Yuin believe that thunder is the voice of Daramulun.

claims.quote: Their neighbours the Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person ... went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as one of the old Ngarigo men said, takes care of it.

statement.id: Suku Ngarigo juga mengira roh orang mati naik ke langit, tempat ia disambut Daramulun, yang menurut seorang tetua Ngarigo merawatnya.
statement.en: The Ngarigo also thought that the spirit of a dead person went up to the sky, where it was met by Daramulun, who, as an old Ngarigo man said, takes care of it.

claims.quote: The general belief as to the powers of the medicine-man are much the same in all the tribes herein spoken of. He is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from some supernatural source, or being, such as Baiame, Daramulun, or Bunjil, or the ancestral ghosts.

statement.id: Dukun (medicine-man) di mana-mana dipercaya menerima kekuatannya dari sumber atau makhluk gaib seperti Baiame, Daramulun, atau Bunjil, atau dari hantu leluhur.
statement.en: The medicine-man is everywhere believed to have received his dreaded power from a supernatural source or being such as Baiame, Daramulun or Bunjil, or from the ancestral ghosts.

claims.quote: a tree with a great swelling round its roots. It is in such places that Daramulun lives.

statement.id: Menurut bagian ini, Daramulun tinggal di tempat-tempat semacam itu, yaitu pohon dengan pembengkakan besar di sekeliling akarnya.
statement.en: According to this passage, Daramulun lives in such places, namely a tree with a great swelling round its roots.

claims.quote: they cut on the ground the figure of Daramulun, who is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs, but the " boy," or son, of Baiame. He is always represented as having only one leg, the other terminating in a sharp point of bone.

statement.id: Dalam bagian ini, figur Daramulun digambar di tanah; ia di sini bukan Makhluk Gaib dalam kepercayaan Yuin melainkan "anak" atau putra Baiame, dan selalu digambarkan berkaki satu dengan ujung lainnya runcing dari tulang.
statement.en: In this passage a figure of Daramulun is cut on the ground; here he is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs but the "boy", or son, of Baiame, and is always shown with one leg, the other ending in a sharp point of bone.

claims.quote: There is also figured on the ground the tomahawk which Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree before mentioned to the ground ; then two footprints of an emu a little distance from each other, made when trying to escape from Daramulun.

statement.id: Di tanah juga digambar kapak yang dijatuhkan Daramulun ketika ia meluncur turun dari pohon ke tanah, lalu dua jejak kaki emu yang dibuat saat mencoba lolos dari Daramulun.
statement.en: Also figured on the ground are the tomahawk Daramulun let fall as he slipped down from the tree to the ground, and two emu footprints made when the emu tried to escape from Daramulun.

claims.quote: to imitate the bursting of stones heated in the fire, with which the boys are told Daramulun will injure or kill them if they tell any of the secrets.

statement.id: Anak-anak laki-laki diberi tahu bahwa Daramulun akan melukai atau membunuh mereka dengan batu yang dipanaskan di api jika mereka membocorkan rahasia.
statement.en: The boys are told that Daramulun will injure or kill them with stones heated in the fire if they tell any of the secrets.

claims.quote: There is not any worship of Daramulun

statement.id: Howitt menulis bahwa tidak ada pemujaan terhadap Daramulun.
statement.en: Howitt writes that there is not any worship of Daramulun.

claims.quote: It seems quite clear that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.

statement.id: Howitt menyimpulkan bahwa Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun, dan Baianie semuanya mewakili satu sosok yang sama dengan nama berbeda.
statement.en: Howitt concludes that Nurrundere, Nurelli, Bunjil, Mungan-ngaua, Daramulun and Baianie all represent the same being under different names.

summary.id: Dalam satu catatan, Daramulun bukan Makhluk Gaib dalam kepercayaan Yuin melainkan putra Baiame.
summary.en: In one account Daramulun is not the Supernatural Being of the Yuin beliefs but the son of Baiame.

summary.id: Howitt menyimpulkan beberapa nama, termasuk Daramulun dan Baianie, mewakili satu sosok yang sama.
summary.en: Howitt concludes that several names, including Daramulun and Baianie, represent one and the same being.

short_description.id: Daucina (juga ditulis Ndauthina) adalah dewa pelayaran dan penangkapan ikan di Fiji, dikenal sebagai sang pembawa obor yang berkeliaran di terumbu dengan kerudung api.
short_description.en: Daucina, also written Ndauthina, is the god of seafaring and fishing in Fiji, known as the torch-bearer who roams the reefs hooded with fire.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Fiji, Daucina berarti sang pembawa obor dan dikenal sebagai dewa agung pelayaran. Menurut Thomson, yang menulis namanya Ndauthina, ia adalah dewa komunitas pelaut dan nelayan di seluruh Fiji. Nelayan yang karam dikatakan selalu dapat berlindung di kuil yang dipersembahkan kepadanya.

Saat masih balita ia hanya tenang bila menatap lampu, sehingga ibunya mengikatkan alang-alang bernyala di kepalanya. Sejak itu ia berkeliaran di terumbu karang, pada malam hari, berkerudung tungku menyala.

Ia disebut pelindung para pezina dan pembawa pergi perempuan pada malam hari. Ia juga menyukai serangan malam dan menyorotkan cahaya ke pertahanan untuk memandu pengepung, tetapi tidak berbuat jahil terhadap para nelayan sahabatnya, yang diberinya angin baik dan tangkapan yang bagus.
long_description.en:
In Fijian mythology Daucina means the torch-bearer and is known as the great god of seafaring. According to Thomson, who writes the name Ndauthina, he is the god of the seafaring and fishing community throughout Fiji. A shipwrecked fisherman was said always to find refuge in a temple dedicated to him.

As a toddler he was quiet only when looking at a lamp, so his mother tied burning reeds to his head. Since then he is said to roam the reefs by night, hooded with a flaming brazier.

He is called the patron of adulterers and a carrier-off of women at night. He also loves night attacks, flashing light on defences to guide besiegers, yet plays no pranks on his friends the fishermen, to whom he gives fair winds and good catches.

short_description.id: Degei (Ndengei) adalah dewa tertinggi Fiji yang berwujud ular, pencipta dunia, buah-buahan, dan manusia, serta pengadil arwah orang mati.
short_description.en: Degei (Ndengei) is the supreme god of Fiji, enshrined as a serpent, creator of the world, fruits and men, and judge of the newly dead.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Fiji, Degei (dilafalkan Ndengei) berwujud ular dan dikenal sebagai dewa tertinggi Fiji. Ia pencipta dunia, buah-buahan, dan manusia, dan terutama berhubungan dengan wilayah Rakiraki. Satu catatan menyebut seekor burung bertelur dua yang dierami Ndengei, sang ular agung, lalu seorang anak laki-laki dan seorang anak perempuan keluar dari telur-telur itu.

Menurut tradisi, ia mula-mula bergerak bebas, lalu dalam wujud ular tumbuh menyatu dengan bumi dan sejak itu menjadi dewa gempa bumi, badai, dan musim. Bila ia mengguncang dirinya, hujan penyubur turun dan ladang ubi berhasil; ia juga dewa murka yang menghukum umatnya dengan merusak panen atau banjir.

Arwah orang yang baru meninggal melewati salah satu dari dua gua, Cibaciba atau Drakulu, sebelum dihakimi Degei. Beberapa arwah dikirim ke surga Burotu, dan sebagian besar lainnya dilemparkan ke danau tempat mereka akhirnya tenggelam ke dasar (Murimuria) untuk diganjar atau dihukum.

Sebuah catatan lain menggambarkan Ndengei sebagai wujud gagasan keberadaan abadi yang hidup monoton di gua suram dekat ujung timur laut Viti Levu, hanya makan, menjawab imamnya, dan berganti posisi. Walaupun tertinggi di antara para dewa, di luar sekitar Rakiraki ia nyaris tidak punya kuil; Tokairambe dan Tui Lakemba Randinandina disebut putra-putranya yang menjadi perantara doa. Ular adalah kuil pilihannya, dan sebagian tradisi menggambarkannya dengan kepala dan sebagian tubuh ular sedangkan sisanya batu. Adat merajah tubuh konon sesuai dengan ketetapan Ndengei.
long_description.en:
In Fijian mythology Degei (pronounced Ndengei) is enshrined as a serpent and known as the supreme god of Fiji. He is the creator of the world, fruits and men, and is specially connected to Rakiraki. One record says a bird laid two eggs that Ndengei, the great serpent, hatched, a boy and a girl coming from them.

Tradition says he first moved about freely, then in snake form grew into the earth and has since been the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons. When he shakes himself fertilising rain falls and the yam fields prosper; he is also a god of wrath who punishes his people by destroying the crops or by floods.

Newly dead souls pass through one of two caves, Cibaciba or Drakulu, before Degei judges them. He sends a few to the paradise Burotu; most others are cast into a lake and gradually sink to its bottom (Murimuria), where they are rewarded or punished as fits.

Another account describes Ndengei as an impersonation of the idea of eternal existence, living a monotonous life in a gloomy cavern near the north-east end of Viti Levu, eating, answering his priest and changing position. Although supreme among the gods, he has scarcely a temple except about Rakiraki; Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina are named as his sons and mediators. The serpent is his adopted shrine, some traditions show him with the head and part of the body of a snake and the rest stone, and the custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with his appointment.

statement.en: He is said to have first moved about freely, but then, in snake form, to have grown into the earth with his ringed tail; since then he has become the god of earthquakes, storms and seasons.

claims.quote: Whenever Degei shakes himself fertilising rain will fall, delicious fruits hang on the trees, and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.

statement.id: Setiap kali Degei mengguncang dirinya, hujan penyubur turun, buah-buahan lezat bergantung di pohon, dan ladang ubi memberi hasil yang sangat baik.
statement.en: Whenever Degei shakes himself, fertilising rain falls, delicious fruits hang on the trees and the yam fields yield an excellent crop.

claims.quote: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion. He punishes and chastens his people by destroying the crops or by floods; he could indeed easily wipe out mankind from the earth, for since he has lived in the bowels of the earth he has been tormented with so insatiable hunger that he would like to take in and swallow the whole world.

statement.id: Degei juga dewa murka yang menyatakan diri secara mengerikan; ia menghukum umatnya dengan merusak panen atau dengan banjir, dan karena tinggal di perut bumi ia disiksa lapar yang tak terpuaskan sehingga ingin menelan seluruh dunia.
statement.en: Degei is also a god of wrath who declares himself in terrible fashion; he punishes his people by destroying the crops or by floods, and having lived in the bowels of the earth he is tormented by so insatiable a hunger that he would like to swallow the whole world.

claims.quote: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.

statement.id: Rokola adalah nama putra Degei.
statement.en: Rokola is a name of the son of Degei.

claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake, living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda - the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.
claims.locator: In popular culture (quoting R. A. Derrick)

statement.id: Dalam tradisi-tradisi ini Degei tampil bukan hanya sebagai asal usul manusia, tetapi juga sebagai ular raksasa yang tinggal di gua dekat puncak gunung Uluda, puncak paling utara Pegunungan Nakauvandra.
statement.en: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people but also as a huge snake living in a cave near the summit of the mountain Uluda, the northernmost peak of the Nakauvandra Range.

claims.quote: In these traditions Degei figures not only as the origin of the people, but also as a huge snake ... He took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.
claims.locator: In popular culture (quoting R. A. Derrick)

statement.id: Menurut kutipan di halaman ini, ia tidak tertarik pada urusan umatnya; keberadaannya hanya berputar pada makan dan tidur.
statement.en: According to the passage quoted on this page, he took no interest in his people's affairs; his existence was no more than a round of eating and sleeping.

claims.quote: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.

statement.id: Dewa yang paling dikenal di Fiji adalah Ndengei, yang tampaknya merupakan personifikasi gagasan abstrak tentang keberadaan abadi.
statement.en: The god most generally known in Fiji is Ndengei, who seems to be an impersonation of the abstract idea of eternal existence.

claims.quote: The serpent - the world-wide symbol of eternity - is his adopted shrine. Some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone

statement.id: Ular, lambang keabadian di seluruh dunia, adalah kuil pilihannya; sebagian tradisi menggambarkannya dengan kepala dan sebagian tubuh ular sedangkan sisanya batu.
statement.en: The serpent, the world-wide symbol of eternity, is his adopted shrine; some traditions represent him with the head and part of the body of that reptile, the rest of his form being stone.

claims.quote: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern - the hollow of an inland rock near the N. E. end of Viti Levu - evincing no interest in any one but his attendant, Uto, and giving no signs of life beyond eating, answering his priest, and changing his position from one side to the other.

statement.id: Ia menjalani hidup monoton di gua suram, rongga batu pedalaman dekat ujung timur laut Viti Levu, tidak peduli pada siapa pun selain pelayannya Uto, dan hanya makan, menjawab imamnya, dan berganti posisi dari satu sisi ke sisi lain.
statement.en: He passes a monotonous existence in a gloomy cavern, the hollow of an inland rock near the north-east end of Viti Levu, showing no interest in anyone but his attendant Uto, and giving no sign of life beyond eating, answering his priest and changing his position from side to side.

claims.quote: All though Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods ... Except about Rakiraki, he has scarcely a temple

statement.id: Meski Ndengei dianggap tertinggi di antara para dewa, di luar sekitar Rakiraki ia nyaris tidak punya kuil.
statement.en: Although Ndengei ranks as supreme among the gods, he has scarcely a temple except about Rakiraki.

claims.quote: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and acting as mediators

statement.id: Tokairambe dan Tui Lakemba Randinandina tampaknya berkedudukan tepat di bawah Ndengei sebagai putra-putranya dan bertindak sebagai perantara.
statement.en: Tokairambe and Tui Lakemba Randinandina seem to stand next to Ndengei, being his sons, and act as mediators.

claims.quote: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.

statement.id: Pada hari persembahan, seorang imam masuk ke gua suci tempat Ndengei bersemayam sambil membawa apa yang dibutuhkan upacara.
statement.en: On the day of offering a priest entered the sacred cave where Ndengei dwelt, taking with him what the occasion required.

claims.quote: If rain was wanted, the bete would return dripping with rain from Ndengei, and with a promise that he would thus bestow showers on all the district after two or four days. If they asked success in war, a fire-brand was darted from the cave ; a token that they should burn up their enemies.

statement.id: Bila hujan diminta, bete (imam) kembali basah kuyup dari Ndengei dengan janji hujan dalam dua atau empat hari; bila diminta kemenangan perang, sebatang bara dilemparkan dari gua sebagai tanda musuh akan dibakar habis.
statement.en: If rain was wanted, the bete (priest) would return dripping from Ndengei with a promise of showers on the district after two or four days; if success in war was asked, a fire-brand was darted from the cave as a token that they should burn up their enemies.

claims.quote: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.

statement.id: Adat merajah tubuh konon sesuai dengan ketetapan Ndengei, dan pengabaiannya dihukum setelah mati.
statement.en: The custom of tattooing is said to be in conformity with the appointment of Ndengei, and its neglect punished after death.

claims.quote: At the other extremity of Melanesia, in Fiji, it is said that a bird laid two eggs which were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.

statement.id: Di Fiji dikatakan seekor burung bertelur dua yang dierami oleh Ndengei, sang ular agung; seorang anak laki-laki keluar dari satu telur dan seorang anak perempuan dari yang lain.
statement.en: In Fiji it is said that a bird laid two eggs that were hatched by Ndengei, the great serpent, a boy coming from one and a girl from the other.

claims.quote: A few he sends to paradise Burotu. Most others are thrown into a lake, where they will eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.

statement.id: Sebagian kecil arwah ia kirim ke surga Burotu; kebanyakan lainnya dilemparkan ke danau, tempat mereka akhirnya tenggelam ke dasar (Murimuria) untuk diganjar atau dihukum sepantasnya.
statement.en: He sends a few souls to the paradise Burotu; most others are thrown into a lake, where they eventually sink to the bottom (Murimuria) to be appropriately rewarded or punished.

summary.en: Wikipedia calls Degei a god of wrath who punishes his people by destroying crops or by floods.

summary.id: Kutipan di halaman yang sama menyatakan ia tidak tertarik pada urusan umatnya; catatan lain menggambarkannya pasif di guanya.
summary.en: A passage quoted on the same page says he took no interest in his people's affairs; another account describes him as passive in his cave.

short_description.id: Dōnotsura adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar dalam gulungan ilustrasi.
short_description.en: Dōnotsura is a Japanese yōkai depicted in illustrated scrolls.

long_description.id:
Dōnotsura adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambarkan dalam gulungan bergambar. Tubuhnya tidak berkepala di atas leher, dan wajahnya berada di batang tubuh. Gulungan lama hanya memuat nama dan gambar tanpa teks penjelasan.

Sumber lain menyebut tubuhnya mirip manusia kecuali bagian dari leher ke atas, dengan fitur wajah yang sangat besar di batang tubuh. Dalam gulungan lain, makhluk dengan rancangan serupa tercatat dengan nama Akahadaka.

Satu sumber mencatat bahwa makhluk berwajah di dada atau perut tersebar luas di Eurasia, dan menilai Xingtian dari gambar Shanhaijing tampaknya menjadi contoh bagi rupa ini. Sumber lain mengemukakan bahwa asal-usulnya kemungkinan besar adalah permainan kata.
long_description.en:
Dōnotsura is a Japanese yōkai depicted in illustrated scrolls. Its body lacks a head above the neck, and its face is on its torso. The old scrolls give only a name and a picture, without explanatory text.

Another source describes its body as much like a human's except for everything above the neck, with extremely large facial features on the torso. In another scroll, a yōkai of similar design is recorded under the name Akahadaka.

One source notes that beings with faces on the chest or belly are widely distributed across Eurasia, and considers that Xingtian from Shanhaijing illustrations appears to have served as the model for this form. Another source suggests that its most likely origin is a play on words.

summary.id: Sumber lain menyebut asal-usul yang paling mungkin adalah permainan kata dengan ungkapan "dono tsura sagete".
summary.en: Another source gives its most likely origin as a play on words with the expression "dono tsura sagete".

short_description.id: Doydu adalah ikan raksasa kematian penghuni samudera bawah tanah dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altay.
short_description.en: Doydu is a gigantic subterranean death fish in Turkic and Altay cosmogony.

long_description.id:
Doydu adalah Ikan Kematian raksasa dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altay, juga dikenal sebagai Toydu Balıq. Ia dipercaya hidup di lautan besar di bawah tanah dan digambarkan sebagai ikan legenda yang sangat besar.

Mulutnya berada di bawah tenggorokan dan matanya di tengkuk; tulang punggungnya terbalik dan ia dikatakan diikat dengan rantai. Bila ia menggerakkan kepala dan tubuhnya, terjadi gempa bumi dan badai. Namanya disebut bersama Abra dan Yutpa.

Karakurt mencatat bahwa dalam budaya rakyat Turki fungsi ikan sebagai penopang dunia kurang diminati, sedangkan ukurannya dan kehidupannya di bawah tanah lebih menarik. Ia juga disebut Ker Balık, dan nama Doydu ditafsirkan sebagai 'pemakan bumi'.
long_description.en:
Doydu is a giant Death Fish in Turkic and Altay mythologies, also known as Toydu Balıq. It is believed to live in the great sea underground and is described as a legendary giant fish.

Its mouth is under its throat and its eyes are on its nape; its spine is turned upside down and it is said to be kept bound with chains. When it moves its head and body, earthquakes occur and storms break out. Its name is mentioned together with Abra and Yutpa.

Karakurt notes that in Turkic folk culture the fish's role as world-bearer drew little interest, whereas its size and underground life were found more interesting. It is also called Ker Balık, and the name Doydu is interpreted as 'eater of the earth'.

era: Turkic and Altay mythology

literal_meaning.id: 'Pemakan bumi'; kata doydu juga berarti 'bumi' dalam beberapa dialek Turki.
literal_meaning.en: 'Eater of the earth'; the word doydu also means 'the earth' in some Turkic dialects.

who.en: A giant Death Fish living in the great sea underground.

short_description.id: Doydu adalah ikan raksasa kematian penghuni samudera bawah tanah dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altay.
short_description.en: Doydu is a gigantic subterranean death fish in Turkic and Altay cosmogony.

long_description.id: Doydu adalah Ikan Kematian raksasa dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altay, juga dikenal sebagai Toydu Balıq. Ia dipercaya hidup di lautan besar di bawah tanah dan digambarkan sebagai ikan legenda yang sangat besar.
long_description.en: Doydu is a giant Death Fish in Turkic and Altay mythologies, also known as Toydu Balıq. It is believed to live in the great sea underground and is described as a legendary giant fish.

long_description.id: Mulutnya berada di bawah tenggorokan dan matanya di tengkuk; tulang punggungnya terbalik dan ia dikatakan diikat dengan rantai. Bila ia menggerakkan kepala dan tubuhnya, terjadi gempa bumi dan badai. Namanya disebut bersama Abra dan Yutpa.
long_description.en: Its mouth is under its throat and its eyes are on its nape; its spine is turned upside down and it is said to be kept bound with chains. When it moves its head and body, earthquakes occur and storms break out. Its name is mentioned together with Abra and Yutpa.

long_description.id: Karakurt mencatat bahwa dalam budaya rakyat Turki fungsi ikan sebagai penopang dunia kurang diminati, sedangkan ukurannya dan kehidupannya di bawah tanah lebih menarik. Ia juga disebut Ker Balık, dan nama Doydu ditafsirkan sebagai 'pemakan bumi'.
long_description.en: Karakurt notes that in Turkic folk culture the fish's role as world-bearer drew little interest, whereas its size and underground life were found more interesting. It is also called Ker Balık, and the name Doydu is interpreted as 'eater of the earth'.

short_description.id: Dyrnwch Gawr adalah raksasa (cawr) dalam tradisi Welsh yang dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali ajaib, salah satu dari Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania; kuali itu tidak mau merebus daging untuk pengecut.
short_description.en: Dyrnwch Gawr is a giant (cawr) of Welsh tradition known as the owner of a magic cauldron, one of the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain; the cauldron will not boil meat for a coward.

long_description.id:
Dyrnwch Gawr, juga dieja Dyrnhwch Gawr, adalah raksasa Welsh (cawr Cymreig) yang dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd dan dengan Gwent. Naskah-naskah daftar pusaka juga memuat ejaan Dyrnog dan Tyrnog. Selain dalam daftar pusaka, namanya muncul dalam daftar raksasa Cymru yang disusun Siôn Dafydd Rhys pada akhir abad ke-16, dengan keterangan bahwa ia berada di negeri Ewias.

Ia terutama dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali istimewa dalam daftar Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania). Kuali itu membedakan pemberani dari pengecut: daging untuk orang pengecut tidak akan pernah mendidih di dalamnya, sedangkan daging untuk orang pemberani cepat matang. Pusaka-pusaka itu digambarkan sebagai benda ajaib tradisi Welsh yang disebut dalam naskah abad ke-15 dan ke-16, dan kebanyakan dikaitkan dengan 'Utara'.

Kisah kuali ini hampir pasti bersumber dari rujukan pada 'kuali Diwrnach Wyddel' dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen, dan karena nama Dyrnwch dan Diwrnach sangat mirip, nama pertama kemungkinan bentuk yang lebih muda dari yang kedua. Sifat serupa dikenakan pada kuali Pen Annwn dalam puisi 'Preiddiau Annwn' di Llyfr Taliesin, yang tidak merebus makanan pengecut. Walaupun pusaka-pusaka itu dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch tidak disebut dalam silsilah seperti Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.

Culhwch ac Olwen juga memuat tokoh lain bernama Wrnach Gawr, pemilik sebilah pedang istimewa. Mungkin ada hubungan antara Wrnach Gawr dan Diwrnach Wyddel, dan Dyrnwch Gawr mungkin perkembangan lebih kemudian dari tokoh-tokoh itu, tetapi hal ini tidak dapat dibuktikan secara pasti.
long_description.en:
Dyrnwch Gawr, also spelled Dyrnhwch Gawr, is a Welsh giant (cawr Cymreig) associated with the Hen Ogledd and with Gwent. The manuscripts of the treasure list also give the spellings Dyrnog and Tyrnog. Besides the treasure list, his name appears in the list of the giants of Cymru compiled by Siôn Dafydd Rhys at the end of the 16th century, which places him in the land of Ewias.

He is known chiefly as the owner of a special cauldron in the list Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain). The cauldron tells the brave from the cowardly: meat for a coward will never boil in it, while meat for a brave man cooks quickly. The treasures are described as magical items of Welsh tradition mentioned in 15th- and 16th-century manuscripts, most of them linked with 'The North'.

The story of the cauldron is almost certainly based on a reference to 'the cauldron of Diwrnach Wyddel' in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen, and because the names Dyrnwch and Diwrnach are so alike, the former is probably a later form of the latter. A similar virtue is given to the cauldron of Pen Annwn in the poem 'Preiddiau Annwn' in Llyfr Taliesin, which does not boil a coward's food. Although the treasures are linked with the Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch is not mentioned in genealogies such as Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.

Culhwch ac Olwen also contains another character called Wrnach Gawr, who owns a special sword. There may be a link between Wrnach Gawr and Diwrnach Wyddel, and Dyrnwch Gawr may be a later development based on those characters, but this cannot be proven conclusively.

short_description.id: Dyrnwch Gawr adalah raksasa (cawr) dalam tradisi Welsh yang dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali ajaib, salah satu dari Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania; kuali itu tidak mau merebus daging untuk pengecut.
short_description.en: Dyrnwch Gawr is a giant (cawr) of Welsh tradition known as the owner of a magic cauldron, one of the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain; the cauldron will not boil meat for a coward.

long_description.id: Dyrnwch Gawr, juga dieja Dyrnhwch Gawr, adalah raksasa Welsh (cawr Cymreig) yang dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd dan dengan Gwent. Naskah-naskah daftar pusaka juga memuat ejaan Dyrnog dan Tyrnog. Selain dalam daftar pusaka, namanya muncul dalam daftar raksasa Cymru yang disusun Siôn Dafydd Rhys pada akhir abad ke-16, dengan keterangan bahwa ia berada di negeri Ewias.
long_description.en: Dyrnwch Gawr, also spelled Dyrnhwch Gawr, is a Welsh giant (cawr Cymreig) associated with the Hen Ogledd and with Gwent. The manuscripts of the treasure list also give the spellings Dyrnog and Tyrnog. Besides the treasure list, his name appears in the list of the giants of Cymru compiled by Siôn Dafydd Rhys at the end of the 16th century, which places him in the land of Ewias.

long_description.id: Ia terutama dikenal sebagai pemilik kuali istimewa dalam daftar Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (Tiga Belas Pusaka Pulau Britania). Kuali itu membedakan pemberani dari pengecut: daging untuk orang pengecut tidak akan pernah mendidih di dalamnya, sedangkan daging untuk orang pemberani cepat matang. Pusaka-pusaka itu digambarkan sebagai benda ajaib tradisi Welsh yang disebut dalam naskah abad ke-15 dan ke-16, dan kebanyakan dikaitkan dengan 'Utara'.
long_description.en: He is known chiefly as the owner of a special cauldron in the list Tri Thlws ar Ddeg Ynys Prydain (the Thirteen Treasures of the Island of Britain). The cauldron tells the brave from the cowardly: meat for a coward will never boil in it, while meat for a brave man cooks quickly. The treasures are described as magical items of Welsh tradition mentioned in 15th- and 16th-century manuscripts, most of them linked with 'The North'.

long_description.id: Kisah kuali ini hampir pasti bersumber dari rujukan pada 'kuali Diwrnach Wyddel' dalam kisah Culhwch ac Olwen, dan karena nama Dyrnwch dan Diwrnach sangat mirip, nama pertama kemungkinan bentuk yang lebih muda dari yang kedua. Sifat serupa dikenakan pada kuali Pen Annwn dalam puisi 'Preiddiau Annwn' di Llyfr Taliesin, yang tidak merebus makanan pengecut. Walaupun pusaka-pusaka itu dikaitkan dengan Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch tidak disebut dalam silsilah seperti Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.
long_description.en: The story of the cauldron is almost certainly based on a reference to 'the cauldron of Diwrnach Wyddel' in the tale Culhwch ac Olwen, and because the names Dyrnwch and Diwrnach are so alike, the former is probably a later form of the latter. A similar virtue is given to the cauldron of Pen Annwn in the poem 'Preiddiau Annwn' in Llyfr Taliesin, which does not boil a coward's food. Although the treasures are linked with the Hen Ogledd, Dyrnwch is not mentioned in genealogies such as Bonedd Gwŷr y Gogledd.

long_description.id: Culhwch ac Olwen juga memuat tokoh lain bernama Wrnach Gawr, pemilik sebilah pedang istimewa. Mungkin ada hubungan antara Wrnach Gawr dan Diwrnach Wyddel, dan Dyrnwch Gawr mungkin perkembangan lebih kemudian dari tokoh-tokoh itu, tetapi hal ini tidak dapat dibuktikan secara pasti.
long_description.en: Culhwch ac Olwen also contains another character called Wrnach Gawr, who owns a special sword. There may be a link between Wrnach Gawr and Diwrnach Wyddel, and Dyrnwch Gawr may be a later development based on those characters, but this cannot be proven conclusively.

short_description.id: Emela-ntouka adalah makhluk legendaris dari wilayah Likouala di Afrika Tengah, berasal dari mitologi suku Pigmi di Kongo; ia digambarkan sebagai hewan bertanduk sebesar gajah yang menyerang hewan besar.
short_description.en: The emela-ntouka is a legendary creature of the Likouala region in Central Africa, rooted in the mythology of Pygmy tribes in Congo; it is pictured as a horned, elephant-sized animal that attacks big game.

long_description.id:
Emela-ntouka adalah makhluk legendaris dari wilayah Likouala di Afrika Tengah. Legendanya berasal dari mitologi suku-suku Pigmi yang tinggal di Kongo. Dalam bahasa Lingala namanya berarti pembunuh gajah, yang dikaitkan dengan sifatnya yang agresif.

Menurut orang Pigmi dan para saksi, makhluk ini sedikit lebih besar daripada gajah, berkulit keabu-abuan tanpa bulu, berkaki empat yang kokoh, dan berekor seperti buaya. Penduduk setempat juga menyebut satu tanduk besar di dahi atau hidungnya. Walaupun pemakan tumbuhan, ia sangat agresif dan konon sering menyerang gajah, badak, atau kuda nil, membunuhnya dengan tanduk tanpa memakannya.

Di dunia Barat, emela-ntouka pertama kali disebut pada 1954 dalam artikel jurnal Mammalia oleh Lucien Blancou, mantan inspektur wilayah Likouala, yang menyebut hewan itu lebih besar daripada bison. Pada 1980 dan 1981 kriptozoolog Roy Mackal mengadakan dua ekspedisi ke Kongo untuk mencari mokele-mbembe dan mendengar beberapa kesaksian orang yang mengaku pernah melihat emela-ntouka.

Kriptozoolog berbeda pendapat tentang hakikatnya. Sebagian menganggapnya dinosaurus yang bertahan hidup atau mamalia besar semi-akuatik yang belum dikenal, dan Roy Mackal membuka kemungkinan bahwa ia Centrosaurus. Zoolog Loren Coleman menolak gagasan dinosaurus dan lebih condong pada badak, entah badak raksasa prasejarah atau spesies badak baru yang belum dikenali.
long_description.en:
The emela-ntouka is a creature of legend from the Likouala region of Central Africa. Its story comes from the mythology of the Pygmy tribes who live in Congo. In Lingala its name means elephant killer, which is linked to its aggressive nature.

Pygmy informants and other witnesses make it a little bigger than an elephant, with greyish hairless skin, four strong legs and a crocodile-like tail. Local people also mention a single large horn on its forehead or nose. Though it feeds on plants, it is extremely aggressive and is said to attack elephants, rhinoceroses or hippopotamuses, killing them with its horn but not eating them.

Western writing first mentions the emela-ntouka in 1954, in a Mammalia article by Lucien Blancou, a former inspector of the Likouala region, who said the animal was bigger than a bison. In 1980 and 1981 the cryptozoologist Roy Mackal led two expeditions to Congo looking for the mokele-mbembe and heard several men say they had seen an emela-ntouka.

Cryptozoologists disagree about what it might be. Some suggest a surviving dinosaur or an unknown large semi-aquatic mammal, and Roy Mackal allowed that it could be a Centrosaurus. Zoologist Loren Coleman rejects the dinosaur idea and favours a rhinoceros, described either as a giant prehistoric one or as an unrecognised new species.

claim.id: Walaupun pemakan tumbuhan (erbivoro), ia konon sering menyerang hewan besar seperti gajah, badak, atau kuda nil (elefanti, rinoceronti, ippopotami) tanpa memakannya.

claim.id: Walaupun herbivora (植食性), hewan ini sangat agresif (极具攻击性) dan menyerang hewan besar lain lalu membunuhnya dengan tanduknya (角).
claim.en: Although herbivorous (植食性), the animal is extremely aggressive (极具攻击性) and attacks other large animals, killing them with its horn (角).

claims_provenance.quote: 并且这种动物虽然是植食性，但却极具攻击性，会攻击其它大型动物，利用牠的角将对方杀死。

claim.id: Menurut peneliti Loren Coleman (洛伦·科尔曼), emela-ntouka bukan dinosaurus (恐龙), melainkan spesies badak (犀牛) baru yang belum dikenali.
claim.en: According to researcher Loren Coleman (洛伦·科尔曼), the emela-ntouka is not a dinosaur (恐龙) but an unrecognised new species of rhinoceros (犀牛).

claims_provenance.quote: 动物学、人类学与神秘动物学研究者洛伦·科尔曼 ... 认为，埃米拉·恩图卡并非恐龙，而是一种未被确认的新种犀牛。

claim.id: Zoolog Loren Coleman lebih condong pada pandangan bahwa makhluk itu badak raksasa (rinoceronte gigante) dari zaman prasejarah.
claim.en: Zoologist Loren Coleman leans toward the view that the creature is a giant prehistoric rhinoceros (rinoceronte gigante).

claims_provenance.quote: Lo zoologo americano Loren Coleman è più propenso alla versione che vede nella creatura un rinoceronte gigante di epoca preistorica

claim.id: Dalam bahasa Lingala, namanya berarti pembunuh gajah (tueur d'éléphants), konon karena cara hidupnya yang agresif.

short_description.id: Emela-ntouka adalah makhluk legendaris dari wilayah Likouala di Afrika Tengah, berasal dari mitologi suku Pigmi di Kongo; ia digambarkan sebagai hewan bertanduk sebesar gajah yang menyerang hewan besar.
short_description.en: The emela-ntouka is a legendary creature of the Likouala region in Central Africa, rooted in the mythology of Pygmy tribes in Congo; it is pictured as a horned, elephant-sized animal that attacks big game.

long_description.id: Emela-ntouka adalah makhluk legendaris dari wilayah Likouala di Afrika Tengah. Legendanya berasal dari mitologi suku-suku Pigmi yang tinggal di Kongo. Dalam bahasa Lingala namanya berarti pembunuh gajah, yang dikaitkan dengan sifatnya yang agresif.
long_description.en: The emela-ntouka is a creature of legend from the Likouala region of Central Africa. Its story comes from the mythology of the Pygmy tribes who live in Congo. In Lingala its name means elephant killer, which is linked to its aggressive nature.

long_description.id: Menurut orang Pigmi dan para saksi, makhluk ini sedikit lebih besar daripada gajah, berkulit keabu-abuan tanpa bulu, berkaki empat yang kokoh, dan berekor seperti buaya. Penduduk setempat juga menyebut satu tanduk besar di dahi atau hidungnya. Walaupun pemakan tumbuhan, ia sangat agresif dan konon sering menyerang gajah, badak, atau kuda nil, membunuhnya dengan tanduk tanpa memakannya.
long_description.en: Pygmy informants and other witnesses make it a little bigger than an elephant, with greyish hairless skin, four strong legs and a crocodile-like tail. Local people also mention a single large horn on its forehead or nose. Though it feeds on plants, it is extremely aggressive and is said to attack elephants, rhinoceroses or hippopotamuses, killing them with its horn but not eating them.

long_description.id: Di dunia Barat, emela-ntouka pertama kali disebut pada 1954 dalam artikel jurnal Mammalia oleh Lucien Blancou, mantan inspektur wilayah Likouala, yang menyebut hewan itu lebih besar daripada bison. Pada 1980 dan 1981 kriptozoolog Roy Mackal mengadakan dua ekspedisi ke Kongo untuk mencari mokele-mbembe dan mendengar beberapa kesaksian orang yang mengaku pernah melihat emela-ntouka.
long_description.en: Western writing first mentions the emela-ntouka in 1954, in a Mammalia article by Lucien Blancou, a former inspector of the Likouala region, who said the animal was bigger than a bison. In 1980 and 1981 the cryptozoologist Roy Mackal led two expeditions to Congo looking for the mokele-mbembe and heard several men say they had seen an emela-ntouka.

long_description.id: Kriptozoolog berbeda pendapat tentang hakikatnya. Sebagian menganggapnya dinosaurus yang bertahan hidup atau mamalia besar semi-akuatik yang belum dikenal, dan Roy Mackal membuka kemungkinan bahwa ia Centrosaurus. Zoolog Loren Coleman menolak gagasan dinosaurus dan lebih condong pada badak, entah badak raksasa prasejarah atau spesies badak baru yang belum dikenali.
long_description.en: Cryptozoologists disagree about what it might be. Some suggest a surviving dinosaur or an unknown large semi-aquatic mammal, and Roy Mackal allowed that it could be a Centrosaurus. Zoologist Loren Coleman rejects the dinosaur idea and favours a rhinoceros, described either as a giant prehistoric one or as an unrecognised new species.

short_description.id: Enkō adalah makhluk terkait kappa dari Hiroshima, Chūgoku, dan Shikoku.
short_description.en: Enkō is a kappa-related creature of Hiroshima, Chūgoku and Shikoku.

long_description.id:
Enkō adalah makhluk terkait kappa dari Hiroshima, Chūgoku, dan Shikoku. Wujudnya berbulu dan menyerupai monyet. Ia konon tidak menyukai logam dan menghuni laut atau sungai.

Satu gambaran memberinya anggota tubuh yang lentur. Ia memiliki cakar tajam di jarinya. Cerita memberinya penyamaran sebagai perempuan dan boneka.

Nama 猿猴 pada asalnya berarti monyet. Menurut catatan yōkai dari Tosa, enkō seperti anak sekitar tiga tahun, berlengan panjang dengan cakar, dan bertubuh licin seperti ikan lele; enkō yang konon ditangkap di Tosa pada 1863 berwajah merah dengan kaki mirip manusia. Ia membenci logam dan sering menyerang sapi atau kuda yang masuk sungai.

Dalam satu kisah dari Tosa, seorang lelaki memelintir lengan enkō yang mengganggu kudanya, tetapi lengan itu tak habis-habis sehingga ia memelintirnya semalaman. Di Prefektur Yamaguchi, yōkai bernama takiwaro dikatakan menjadi enkō setelah tinggal tiga tahun di gunung dan tiga tahun di sungai. Enkō juga menjadi asal nama Sungai Enkō di Hiroshima, tempat festival kappa diadakan.
long_description.en:
Enkō is a kappa-related creature of Hiroshima, Chūgoku and Shikoku. Its hairy form resembles a monkey. It is said to dislike metal and inhabit sea or river water.

A description gives it elastic limbs. It has sharp claws on its fingers. Stories give it disguises as women and dolls.

The name 猿猴 originally meant monkey. According to Tosa yōkai records, the enkō is like a child of about three, with long clawed limbs and a body slimy like a catfish; one said to have been caught in Tosa in 1863 had a red face and human-like feet. It hates metal and often attacks cows or horses entering rivers.

In a Tosa tale, a man twisted the arm of an enkō pestering his horse, but the arm never ran out and he twisted it all night. In Yamaguchi Prefecture, a yōkai called takiwaro is said to become an enkō after three years in the mountains and three in the river. The enkō also gave its name to the Enkō River in Hiroshima, where a kappa festival is held.

long_description.id: Nama 猿猴 pada asalnya berarti monyet. Menurut catatan yōkai dari Tosa, enkō seperti anak sekitar tiga tahun, berlengan panjang dengan cakar, dan bertubuh licin seperti ikan lele; enkō yang konon ditangkap di Tosa pada 1863 berwajah merah dengan kaki mirip manusia. Ia membenci logam dan sering menyerang sapi atau kuda yang masuk sungai.
long_description.en: The name 猿猴 originally meant monkey. According to Tosa yōkai records, the enkō is like a child of about three, with long clawed limbs and a body slimy like a catfish; one said to have been caught in Tosa in 1863 had a red face and human-like feet. It hates metal and often attacks cows or horses entering rivers.

long_description.id: Dalam satu kisah dari Tosa, seorang lelaki memelintir lengan enkō yang mengganggu kudanya, tetapi lengan itu tak habis-habis sehingga ia memelintirnya semalaman. Di Prefektur Yamaguchi, yōkai bernama takiwaro dikatakan menjadi enkō setelah tinggal tiga tahun di gunung dan tiga tahun di sungai. Enkō juga menjadi asal nama Sungai Enkō di Hiroshima, tempat festival kappa diadakan.
long_description.en: In a Tosa tale, a man twisted the arm of an enkō pestering his horse, but the arm never ran out and he twisted it all night. In Yamaguchi Prefecture, a yōkai called takiwaro is said to become an enkō after three years in the mountains and three in the river. The enkō also gave its name to the Enkō River in Hiroshima, where a kappa festival is held.

short_description.id: Falhófnir adalah kuda dalam mitologi Nordik yang tercantum di antara tunggangan para dewa Æsir ketika mereka berkuda setiap hari untuk mengadili di Yggdrasil; tidak ada teks yang menyebut pemiliknya.
short_description.en: Falhófnir is a horse of Norse mythology, listed among the steeds the Æsir gods ride each day to judge at Yggdrasil; no text names its owner.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Nordik, Falhófnir adalah seekor kuda yang namanya tercantum dalam Grímnismál dan Gylfaginning di antara kuda-kuda yang ditunggangi para dewa setiap hari ketika mereka pergi mengadili di pohon abu Yggdrasil. Di kedua teks itu Falhófnir tidak dikaitkan dengan dewa tertentu, berbeda dengan Sleipnir dan Freyfaxi.

Dalam daftar kuda para Æsir di Gylfaginning, Falhófnir adalah kuda kesembilan, setelah Sleipnir milik Odin yang berkaki delapan. Namanya juga muncul dalam daftar nama kuda Þorgrímsþula di Skáldskaparmál, berdampingan dengan Gísl.

Arti nama Falhófnir berbeda-beda menurut sumber. Artikel bahasa Denmark dan artikel Horses of the Æsir memberi "kuku berbulu" atau "kuku tersembunyi" (artikel Inggris menambahkan "kuku pucat"), sedangkan Bellows menulis "Hollow-Hoofed" dan kamus Cleasby-Vigfusson "barrel-hoof, hollow-hoof".
long_description.en:
In Norse mythology Falhófnir is a horse whose name appears in both Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the steeds the gods ride each day when they go to judge at the ash Yggdrasil. In neither text is Falhófnir assigned to a particular god, unlike Sleipnir and Freyfaxi.

In the Gylfaginning list of the Æsir's steeds Falhófnir is the ninth, after Odin's eight-footed Sleipnir. Its name also appears in the horse-name list of Þorgrímsþula in Skáldskaparmál, next to Gísl.

The meaning of the name Falhófnir differs by source. The Danish article and the article on the Horses of the Æsir give "hairy hoof" or "hidden hoof" (the English article adds "pale hoof"), whereas Bellows writes "Hollow-Hoofed" and the Cleasby-Vigfusson dictionary "barrel-hoof, hollow-hoof".

claim.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Falhófnir adalah kuda yang tercantum dalam Grímnismál dan Gylfaginning di antara tunggangan para dewa yang setiap hari pergi memberi keputusan di Yggdrasil, tanpa dikaitkan dengan dewa tertentu.
claim.en: In Norse mythology Falhófnir is a horse listed in Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the mounts the gods ride daily to give judgements at Yggdrasil, not tied to any specific god.

claims_provenance.quote: In Norse mythology, Falhófnir (Old Norse: [ˈfɑlˌhoːvnez̠] ) is a horse listed in both Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the steeds ridden by the gods each day when they go to make judgements at Yggdrasil. However, in both stanzas Falhófnir is not assigned to any specific deity.

claim.id: Artikel bahasa Denmark mengartikan nama Falhófnir sebagai "kuku berbulu" atau "kuku tersembunyi"; ia salah satu kuda jantan yang ditunggangi para Æsir (aserne) ke Yggdrasil, dan tak satu bait pun menyebut pemiliknya, berbeda dengan Sleipnir (Sleipner) dan Freyfaxi (Frejfaxe).
claim.en: The Danish article glosses Falhófnir as 'hairy hoof' or 'hidden hoof'; it is one of the stallions the Æsir (aserne) ride to Yggdrasil, and no stanza names its owner, unlike Sleipnir (Sleipner) and Freyfaxi (Frejfaxe).

claims_provenance.quote: Falhófnir (norrønt for "behåret hov" eller "skjult hov") er en hest i nordisk mytologi, som bliver nævnt i både Grímnismál og Gylfaginning som en af de hingste, som aserne rider på hver dag, når drager til Yggdrasil for at dømme ting. I ingen af stanzaerne bliver ejerskabet af hesten tilskrevet til en bestemt gud, som det er tilfældet med bl.a. Sleipner og Frejfaxe.

claim.id: Gylfaginning (terjemahan Brodeur) mendaftar kuda para Æsir: Sleipnir yang terbaik milik Odin dan berkaki delapan, lalu Gladr, Gyllir, Glenr, Skeidbrimir, Silfrintoppr, Sinir, Gisl, Falhófnir, Gulltoppr, dan Léttfeti.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nordik, Falhófnir adalah seekor kuda yang namanya tercantum dalam Grímnismál dan Gylfaginning di antara kuda-kuda yang ditunggangi para dewa setiap hari ketika mereka pergi mengadili di pohon abu Yggdrasil. Di kedua teks itu Falhófnir tidak dikaitkan dengan dewa tertentu, berbeda dengan Sleipnir dan Freyfaxi.
long_description.en: In Norse mythology Falhófnir is a horse whose name appears in both Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the steeds the gods ride each day when they go to judge at the ash Yggdrasil. In neither text is Falhófnir assigned to a particular god, unlike Sleipnir and Freyfaxi.

long_description.id: Dalam daftar kuda para Æsir di Gylfaginning, Falhófnir adalah kuda kesembilan, setelah Sleipnir milik Odin yang berkaki delapan. Namanya juga muncul dalam daftar nama kuda Þorgrímsþula di Skáldskaparmál, berdampingan dengan Gísl.
long_description.en: In the Gylfaginning list of the Æsir's steeds Falhófnir is the ninth, after Odin's eight-footed Sleipnir. Its name also appears in the horse-name list of Þorgrímsþula in Skáldskaparmál, next to Gísl.

long_description.id: Arti nama Falhófnir berbeda-beda menurut sumber. Artikel bahasa Denmark dan artikel Horses of the Æsir memberi "kuku berbulu" atau "kuku tersembunyi" (artikel Inggris menambahkan "kuku pucat"), sedangkan Bellows menulis "Hollow-Hoofed" dan kamus Cleasby-Vigfusson "barrel-hoof, hollow-hoof".
long_description.en: The meaning of the name Falhófnir differs by source. The Danish article and the article on the Horses of the Æsir give "hairy hoof" or "hidden hoof" (the English article adds "pale hoof"), whereas Bellows writes "Hollow-Hoofed" and the Cleasby-Vigfusson dictionary "barrel-hoof, hollow-hoof".

short_description.id: Galeru (juga Galaru, Galoru, Kaleru) adalah Ular Pelangi dalam mitologi Aborigin Australia; menurut Kaberry di Kimberley timur laut ia penyelamat dan penopang hidup, pemberi hukum, dan sumber kerang mutiara.
short_description.en: Galeru (also Galaru, Galoru, Kaleru) is a Rainbow Serpent of Australian Aboriginal mythology; according to Kaberry in northeastern Kimberley he is a life saver and sustainer, a lawgiver and the source of pearl shells.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Aborigin Australia, Galeru atau Galaru dikenal sebagai ular pelangi, dan Wikipedia menyebutnya melambangkan keberlanjutan hidup di Bumi. Dalam daftar nama Ular Pelangi, Galeru (atau Galoru, Kaleru) dikaitkan dengan Wandjina di wilayah Kimberley.

Menurut Berndt yang merujuk Kaberry, di Kimberley timur laut Galeru (Kaleru) adalah penyelamat dan penopang hidup, perwujudan kesuburan. Ia pemberi hukum yang bertanggung jawab atas aturan perkawinan dan subseksi. Kerang mutiara berasal darinya, dan dalam keadaan tertentu berbahaya memimpikannya.

Daftar Wikipedia lain menempatkan Galeru dalam mitologi Arnhem Land sebagai ular yang menelan Djanggawul, sehingga wilayah asalnya berbeda menurut sumber. Ular Pelangi secara umum adalah dewa pencipta dengan banyak nama dalam bahasa Aborigin; ia menciptakan tanah dan keragaman, tetapi bila diganggu dapat membawa kekacauan besar.
long_description.en:
In Australian Aboriginal mythology Galeru or Galaru is known as a rainbow serpent, and Wikipedia says it symbolises the continuation of life on Earth. In a list of Rainbow Serpent names, Galeru (or Galoru, Kaleru) is attributed to the Wandjina of the Kimberley Region.

According to Berndt, citing Kaberry, in northeastern Kimberley Galeru (Kaleru) is a life saver and sustainer and an embodiment of fertility. He is a lawgiver responsible for marriage rules and subsections. Pearl shells come from him, and dreaming of them can be dangerous in some circumstances.

Another Wikipedia list places Galeru in Arnhem Land mythology as the snake that swallowed the Djanggawul, so sources differ on the home region. The Rainbow Serpent in general is a creator deity with many names in Aboriginal languages; it creates land and diversity but can bring great chaos when disturbed.

He is a lawgiver responsible for marriage rules and subsections. Pearl shells come from him, and dreaming of them can be dangerous in some circumstances.

long_description.en: Another Wikipedia list places Galeru in Arnhem Land mythology as the snake that swallowed the Djanggawul, so sources differ on the home region. The Rainbow Serpent in general is a creator deity with many names in Aboriginal languages; it creates land and diversity but can bring great chaos when disturbed.

short_description.id: Gazeka atau Papuan Devil-Pig adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan dari Papua Nugini.
short_description.en: Gazeka, or Papuan Devil-Pig, is a cryptid reported from Papua New Guinea.

long_description.id:
Gazeka, atau babi setan Papua, adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan dari Papua Nugini. Laporan menggambarkan moncong panjang dan penampilan mirip tapir atau kungkang raksasa. Makhluk ini dibedakan dari Gazeka karangan komedian George Graves di London pada 1905.

Menurut sebuah tulisan penulis kriptozoologi, pada 1906 dalam ekspedisi Kapten Monckton ke Gunung Albert Edward, seorang prajurit bernama Ogi menjumpai dua makhluk yang sedang merumput, berkulit gelap bercorak, berkuku belah, berhidung panjang, dan berekor seperti kuda. Ogi menyebutnya babi setan dan mencoba menembak satu tetapi meleset, dan Monckton menegaskan bahwa jejak berkuku belah yang sangat besar memang ditemukan.

Penulis itu mencatat gagasan bahwa palorchestid, marsupial besar yang telah punah, akan tampak seperti babi raksasa atau tapir dan cukup mengejutkan untuk memunculkan gagasan babi setan. Julukan "Monckton's gazeka" diberikan oleh orang tak dikenal dan berasal dari makhluk fiktif karangan George Graves, sehingga sering membingungkan.
long_description.en:
Gazeka, or Papuan Devil-Pig, is a cryptid reported from Papua New Guinea. Reports describe a long snout and a tapir- or giant-sloth-like appearance. This creature is distinguished from comedian George Graves's invented Gazeka in London in 1905.

According to a cryptozoology writer's post, in 1906 during Captain Monckton's expedition to Mount Albert Edward, a private named Ogi came upon two grazing creatures with dark patterned hides, cloven feet, long snouts, and horse-like tails. Ogi called them devil-pigs and tried to shoot one but missed, and Monckton affirmed that very large cloven-footed tracks had indeed been found.

The writer notes the idea that palorchestids, large extinct marsupials, would have looked like giant pigs or tapirs and been startling enough to conjure up notions of devil-pigs. The nickname "Monckton's gazeka" was applied by persons unknown and derives from the fictitious beast created by George Graves, which often causes confusion.

short_description.id: Huà-shé adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang dikaitkan dengan banjir.
short_description.en: Huà-shé is a Chinese supernatural creature associated with floods.

long_description.id:
Huà-shé adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang dikaitkan dengan banjir. Shan Hai Jing memberinya wajah manusia, tubuh mirip jakal, dan sayap burung di pertemuan sungai.

Ia bergerak seperti ular dan bersuara seperti teriakan. Ilustrasi belakangan berbeda antara ular bersayap dan binatang bersayap berwajah manusia.

Teks aslinya dalam bab Zhongshan Jing menempatkannya di Sungai Yang yang mengalir dari Gunung Yang ke Sungai Yi. Ia digambarkan berwajah manusia, bertubuh seperti serigala hutan, bersayap burung, bergerak seperti ular, dan bersuara seperti bentakan; bila ia terlihat, kotanya dilanda banjir besar. Huà-shé juga disebut mirip siluman ular lain, dansheng.
long_description.en:
Huà-shé is a Chinese supernatural creature associated with floods. The Shan Hai Jing gives it a human face, a jackal-like body and bird wings in a river confluence.

It moves like a snake and makes a cry like a shout. Later illustrations differ between a winged serpent and a winged human-faced beast.

The original text in the Zhongshan Jing chapter places it in the Yang River, which flows from Mount Yang into the Yi River. It is described with a human face, a dhole-like body, bird wings, a snake-like gait and a voice like a shout; when it is seen, its town suffers a great flood. The huà-shé is also said to resemble another snake monster, the dansheng.

claim.en: It moves like a snake and makes a cry like a shout.

claim.en: Later illustrations differ between a winged serpent and a winged human-faced beast.

claims_provenance.quote: 化蛇も、ほかの鳥獣と同様に『山海経』の本文や注に基づいて絵が描かれているのだが、大きく分けて二種類の図柄にわかれている。一つは蛇に翼の生えたもの（図参照）であるが、もう一方の明の時代の例には本文にさらに即した形状（人面の獣に翼が生え、長い尾がある）の絵もあり、そちらも後の時代まで化蛇の図として描き継がれている。

claim.id: Bab Zhongshan Jing (中山經) dalam Shanhaijing (山海經) menyebut Gunung Yang (陽山) yang berbatu dan tanpa tumbuhan; Sungai Yang (陽水) mengalir ke utara menuju Sungai Yi (伊水), dan di dalamnya banyak huà-shé (化蛇).
claim.en: The Zhongshan Jing (中山經) chapter of the Shanhaijing (山海經) mentions Mount Yang (陽山), rocky and bare of plants; the Yang River (陽水) flows north into the Yi River (伊水), and in it are many huà-shé (化蛇).

claims_provenance.quote: 又西三百里，曰陽山，多石，無草木。陽水出焉，而北流注于伊水。其中多化蛇
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (维基文库) — 山海經/中山經

claim.id: Teks aslinya: rupanya berwajah manusia dan bertubuh serigala hutan (豺身), bersayap burung dan bergerak seperti ular, suaranya seperti bentakan, dan bila ia terlihat, kotanya dilanda banjir besar (大水).
claim.en: The original text: it has a human face and a dhole-like body (豺身), bird wings and a snake-like gait, its voice is like a shout, and when it is seen its town suffers a great flood (大水).

claims_provenance.quote: 其中多化蛇，其狀如人面而豺身，鳥翼而蛇行，其音如叱呼，見則其邑大水。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (维基文库) — 山海經/中山經

claim.id: Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut huà-shé mirip dengan siluman ular lain, dansheng (擔生), dan kemunculannya menimbulkan banjir besar (大水災) di kota sekitarnya.
claim.en: Chinese Wikipedia says the huà-shé resembles another snake monster, the dansheng (擔生), and that its appearance brings a great flood (大水災) to nearby towns.

claims_provenance.quote: 而且，化蛇與另一種蛇怪擔生相似，當化蛇出現時，將會在附近城邑引起大水災。

short_description.id: Kisah Ainu menggambarkan Huri sebagai burung sangat besar.
short_description.en: Ainu stories describe Huri as an enormous bird.

long_description.id:
Kisah Ainu menggambarkan Huri sebagai burung sangat besar. Namanya mengarah pada burung merah, dan sebagian kisah menggambarkan sayap sangat besar. Satu asal-usul menyebut leluhurnya yang tinggal di gua mendatangkan badai angin merusak.

Sebagian kisah daerah menggambarkan burung tidak berbahaya yang memburu hewan besar dan paus. Kisah daerah lainnya menggambarkannya sebagai pembunuh yang perlu dibasmi. Tradisi Abashiri memakai dua pedang ipetam untuk mengalahkannya.

Namanya berbeda menurut daerah, misalnya hureu atau huri kamuy, dan dalam dialek Chikabumi hurin atau hurin tono. Nama tempat Kunnui konon berasal dari bayangannya yang membuat daerah itu gelap berhari-hari, meski nama itu lebih mungkin berasal dari batu atau air yang hitam. Dalam kisah lain, seorang dewi mengusir burung ini dan menyelamatkan dua anak yang ditindihnya.
long_description.en:
Ainu stories describe Huri as an enormous bird. Its name suggests a red bird, and some accounts describe an enormous wing. One origin makes its cave-dwelling ancestors bring destructive windstorms.

Some regional accounts describe a harmless bird hunting large game and whales. Other regional accounts portray it as a killer requiring extermination. An Abashiri tradition uses two ipetam swords to defeat it.

Its name varies by region, for example hureu or huri kamuy, and in the Chikabumi dialect hurin or hurin tono. The place name Kunnui is said to come from its shadow darkening the area for days, though the name more likely comes from black rocks or water. In another tale, a goddess drove the bird away and saved two children it was pinning down.

claim.id: Sebagian kisah daerah menggambarkan burung tidak berbahaya yang memburu hewan besar dan paus.
claim.en: Some regional accounts describe a harmless bird hunting large game and whales.

claims_provenance.quote: Some regions remember the huri as harmless to humans when it lived near them, though it hunted large game and even whales, but was offended by a girl's transgression in its drinking spot and moved away (§ Tokachi).

claim.id: Kisah daerah lainnya menggambarkannya sebagai pembunuh yang perlu dibasmi.
claim.en: Other regional accounts portray it as a killer requiring extermination.

claims_provenance.quote: Other regions characterize the huri as man-killers, requiring eradication.

claim.id: Tradisi Abashiri memakai dua pedang ipetam untuk mengalahkannya.
claim.en: An Abashiri tradition uses two ipetam swords to defeat it.

claims_provenance.quote: The eradication was done with the use of two special ipetam swords in the lore of § Abashiri (and Bihoro).

claim.id: Menurut daerahnya ia disebut hureu (フレウ), fūri (フウリ), atau huri kamuy (フリカムイ); dalam dialek Chikabumi (近文) disebut hurin atau hurin tono.
claim.en: Depending on the region it is called hureu (フレウ), fūri (フウリ) or huri kamuy (フリカムイ); in the Chikabumi (近文) dialect it is called hurin or hurin tono.

claims_provenance.quote: 地方によってフレウ、フウリ、フリカムイと称す。近文の方言ではフーリン(hurin)、フーリントノ(hurin tono)と呼ばれる。

claim.id: Konon nama tempat Kunnui (国縫, dari kunne, "gelap, hitam") berasal dari huri kamuy (フリカムイ), karena saat ia terbang di atas, bayangannya membuat daerah itu gelap berhari-hari.
claim.en: The place name Kunnui (国縫, from kunne, "dark, black") is said to come from the huri kamuy (フリカムイ), because when it flew overhead its shadow left the area dark for days.

claims_provenance.quote: そして、この国縫/訓縫（クンネ、「暗い、黒い」の意）の地名の由来になったためだとも伝わる。すなわち、フリカムイが上空にを飛んで影がさしかかり、被害地は何日も暗くなったためだ。

claim.id: Namun ini hanya legenda nama tempat (地名説話); nama itu lebih masuk akal berasal dari batu atau air yang "hitam".
claim.en: However, this is merely a place-name legend (地名説話); the name more plausibly comes from "black" rocks or water.

claims_provenance.quote: ただこれは俗説（地名説話）すぎなく、むしろ「黒い」岩・水などに由来する命名だと考えるのが道理であるという。

claim.id: Dalam kisah Sumunkur, dewi Kamuy Kakkemat mengusir burung yang tampak bergulat dengan nyala api, dan ternyata burung itu sedang menindih seorang anak laki-laki dan perempuan di bawah kakinya.
claim.en: In the Sumunkur tale, the goddess Kamuy Kakkemat shooed away the bird, which seemed to be struggling with flames, and found it had been pinning a boy and a girl underfoot.

claims_provenance.quote: The bird was struggling with what appeared to be flames, but when the goddess shooed the bird away, it turned out the bird had been pinning down a boy and a girl underfoot.
