short_description.id: Kijo adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang, umumnya perempuan yang berubah menjadi oni akibat karma dan dendam.
short_description.en: Kijo is a female oni in Japanese legends, usually a woman transformed into an oni by karma and resentment.

long_description.id:
Kijo (鬼女, harfiah 'perempuan iblis') adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang. Kamus mendefinisikannya sebagai oni berwujud perempuan, dan kata ini juga dipakai untuk perempuan yang hatinya sekejam oni. Biasanya dianggap perempuan yang berubah menjadi oni akibat karma dan dendam.

Menurut yokai.com, kijo mirip perempuan manusia tetapi sangat buruk rupa, dan sebagian bermata merah atau kuning, berkulit biru, bertanduk, atau berkuku panjang. Mereka terutama perempuan yang berubah akibat cemburu hebat, kejahatan, atau dendam, lalu menyingkir ke gua gunung, rumah terbengkalai, atau jalan pegunungan. Sumber yang sama menyebut mereka lebih kuat daripada kebanyakan manusia, ahli sihir, dan mampu mengutuk, meracik racun, serta merajut ilusi.

Kijo sering muncul dalam legenda, dongeng, dan seni pertunjukan Jepang; yang terkenal antara lain Momiji dari Togakushi dan Suzuka Gozen dari Pegunungan Suzuka. Onibaba dari Adachigahara juga dianggap kijo. Tosa Obake Zōshi menceritakan seorang kijo yang memakan janin dari perempuan hamil, dan Nihon Kokugo Daijiten mengutip lakon Noh bahwa Yamanba adalah kijo yang tinggal di gunung.

Menurut yokai.com, nama kijo hanya gabungan kanji oni dan perempuan, tetapi tidak ada dasar untuk menganggap kijo padanan perempuan oni; keduanya mungkin makhluk terpisah. Ensiklopedia lama Heibonsha mencatat bahwa perempuan tua dikatakan menjadi kijo.
long_description.en:
A kijo (鬼女, literally 'demon woman') is an oni woman from Japanese legends. Dictionaries define it as an oni in the form of a woman, and the word is also used for a woman whose heart is as cruel as an oni. They are usually thought to be women whom karma and resentment have transformed into oni.

According to yokai.com, kijo resemble human women but are hideously ugly, and some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, horns, or long claws. They are chiefly women transformed by intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a grudge, who retreat to mountain caves, abandoned houses, or mountain roads. The same source says they are stronger than most humans, excel in magic, and can bestow curses, brew poisons, and weave illusions.

Kijo often appear in Japanese legends, folktales, and performing arts; famous ones include Momiji of Togakushi and Suzuka Gozen of the Suzuka Mountains. The onibaba of Adachigahara is also considered a kijo. The Tosa Obake Zōshi tells of a kijo that ate a fetus from a pregnant woman, and the Nihon Kokugo Daijiten cites a Noh play saying Yamanba is a kijo who lives in the mountains.

According to yokai.com, the name kijo is just the kanji for oni and woman combined, but nothing supports treating kijo as the female counterparts of oni; the two may be separate creatures. The older Heibonsha encyclopedia notes that an old woman is said to become a kijo.

claim.en: Kijo are stronger than most humans (though weaker than oni), excel in magic, and can bestow hexes and curses, brew poisons and potions, and weave complex illusions.

claims_provenance.quote: Kijo are stronger than most humans, though their strength pales in comparison to oni. These demonesses excel in magic; they accumulate powerful spells over their long lives. claim.id: Kijo dapat ditemui tinggal di gua gunung terpencil, rumah terbengkalai, atau di jalan pegunungan tempat mereka mendapat korban.

claims_provenance.quote: Though their name might suggest that kijo are the female counterparts to the male oni, there is nothing to support this. ... It is likely that kijo are entirely separate creatures from oni, other than the fact that both are born from corrupted human souls.

claims.quote: ① 女の姿をした鬼。 [初出の実例]「山姥とは山に住む鬼女(キジョ)とこそ」(出典：謡曲・山姥（1430頃）)
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Kamus Nihon Kokugo Daijiten menjelaskan kijo sebagai oni berwujud perempuan dan mengutip lakon Noh Yamanba (sekitar 1430): "Yamanba adalah kijo yang tinggal di gunung."
statement.en: The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten defines kijo as an oni in the form of a woman and cites the Noh play Yamanba (c. 1430): "Yamanba is a kijo who lives in the mountains."

claims.quote: いま一つの契機は年を取り過ぎることである。年老いた女は鬼女になるといい(《今昔物語集》)
claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (旧版), entri Oni

statement.id: Ensiklopedia lama Heibonsha menyebut satu pemicu lain adalah usia yang terlalu tua, dan perempuan tua dikatakan menjadi kijo, merujuk Konjaku Monogatari-shū.
statement.en: The older Heibonsha encyclopedia names growing too old as another trigger and says an old woman is said to become a kijo, citing the Konjaku Monogatari-shū.

claims.quote: Kijo are female demons. They resemble human women in most ways, although they are hideously ugly to behold. Some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, long claws, or other supernatural features.

statement.id: Kijo adalah iblis perempuan yang mirip perempuan manusia tetapi sangat buruk rupa; sebagian bermata merah atau kuning, berkulit biru, bertanduk tajam, atau berkuku panjang.
statement.en: Kijo are female demons that resemble human women but are hideously ugly; some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, or long claws.

claims.quote: Kijo refers chiefly to women who have been transformed from humans into horrible monsters—either out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge that twists the soul into pure hatred. ... These transformed women retreat from common society into more secluded places where they continue to perpetrate their wicked deeds.

statement.id: Kijo terutama adalah perempuan yang berubah menjadi monster akibat cemburu hebat, kejahatan, atau dendam; mereka menyingkir dari masyarakat ke tempat terpencil dan terus melakukan perbuatan jahat.
statement.en: Kijo refers chiefly to women transformed into monsters out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge; they retreat from society to secluded places where they continue their wicked deeds.

claims.quote: Kijo are stronger than most humans, though their strength pales in comparison to oni. These demonesses excel in magic; they accumulate powerful spells over their long lives. Kijo are capable of bestowing hexes and curses, brewing poisons and potions, and weaving complex illusions.

statement.id: Kijo lebih kuat daripada kebanyakan manusia (tetapi kalah dari oni), ahli sihir, dan mampu mengutuk, meracik racun dan ramuan, serta merajut ilusi rumit.
statement.en: Kijo are stronger than most humans (though weaker than oni), excel in magic, and can bestow hexes and curses, brew poisons and potions, and weave complex illusions.

claims.quote: They can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

statement.id: Kijo dapat ditemui tinggal di gua gunung terpencil, rumah terbengkalai, atau di jalan pegunungan tempat mereka mendapat korban.
statement.en: Kijo can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

claims.quote: Though their name might suggest that kijo are the female counterparts to the male oni, there is nothing to support this. ... It is likely that kijo are entirely separate creatures from oni, other than the fact that both are born from corrupted human souls.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyatakan tidak ada dukungan bahwa kijo adalah padanan perempuan oni; kemungkinan keduanya makhluk terpisah, selain keduanya lahir dari jiwa manusia yang rusak.
statement.en: Yokai.com states nothing supports kijo being the female counterparts of oni; they are likely entirely separate creatures, apart from both being born from corrupted human souls.

claims.quote: Indeed, the name kijo is formed simply by combining the two kanji for oni and woman.

statement.id: Nama kijo terbentuk hanya dengan menggabungkan dua kanji untuk oni dan perempuan.
statement.en: The name kijo is formed simply by combining the two kanji for oni and woman.

claims.quote: Also, the Tosa Obake Zōshi (author unknown) that spelled out tales of yōkai in Tosa Province (now Kōchi Prefecture) had, under the title of "Kijo," stated that an oni woman (kijo) with hair of a length 4 shaku and 8 sun (about 150 centimeters) ate a fetus from a pregnant woman

statement.id: Tosa Obake Zōshi (pengarang tidak diketahui) mencatat di bawah judul "Kijo" bahwa seorang perempuan oni berambut sekitar 150 sentimeter memakan janin dari seorang perempuan hamil.
statement.en: The Tosa Obake Zōshi (author unknown) states, under the title "Kijo," that an oni woman with hair about 150 centimeters long ate a fetus from a pregnant woman.

summary.id: Kijo adalah oni perempuan (menurut artikel ensiklopedia dan kamus).
summary.en: A kijo is an oni woman (per the encyclopedia article and the dictionary).

summary.id: Yokai.com: tidak ada dukungan bahwa kijo padanan perempuan oni; kemungkinan makhluk terpisah.
summary.en: Yokai.com: nothing supports kijo being the female counterpart of oni; likely separate creatures.

short_description.id: Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan bergaun merah yang kisahnya melekat pada hotel, teater, dan tempat umum bersejarah [lady-in-red-c01, lady-in-red-c02, lady-in-red-c03].
short_description.en: The Lady in Red is a type of red-dressed female ghost tied to historic hotels, theatres and public places [lady-in-red-c01, lady-in-red-c02, lady-in-red-c03].

long_description.id:
Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan yang mirip White Lady, tetapi dikaitkan dengan kekasih yang dicampakkan atau perempuan sombong [lady-in-red-c01]. Ia selalu bergaun merah [lady-in-red-c02], biasanya ramah, dan kisahnya melekat pada hotel, teater, atau tempat umum bersejarah [lady-in-red-c03].

Lady in Red dilaporkan di gedung Weckesser, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], di Charleston sebagai hantu Nettie Dickerson yang tersambar petir [lady-in-red-c05], dan di Drake Hotel Chicago sebagai perempuan cemburu yang melompat [lady-in-red-c06]. Di Mizpah Hotel, Nevada, ia dikenal sebagai "Rose" yang tewas di tangan kekasih cemburu [lady-in-red-c07], meski satu sumber mencatat tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan identitas atau pembunuhan itu [lady-in-red-c08].

Laporan lain datang dari stasiun Lower Bay Toronto [lady-in-red-c09], di Pluckley Inggris sejak abad ke-12 [lady-in-red-c10], dan di Sungai Bang Pakong Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. Artikel Historic Hotels of America menyebut pria di Mizpah mendengar suara membisikkan rayuan [lady-in-red-c14] dan tamu menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal [lady-in-red-c15], serta bahwa ia dikatakan baik, ramah, dan murah hati [lady-in-red-c16].
long_description.en:
The Lady in Red is a female ghost type like the White Lady, but tied to jilted lovers or vain women [lady-in-red-c01]. She always wears red [lady-in-red-c02], is usually friendly, and haunts historic hotels, theatres and public places [lady-in-red-c03].

Lady in Red sightings are reported at the Weckesser building, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], in Charleston as the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, killed by lightning [lady-in-red-c05], and at Chicago's Drake Hotel as a jealous woman who jumped [lady-in-red-c06]. At the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada she is known as "Rose", who died at the hands of a jealous lover [lady-in-red-c07], though one source notes there are no records confirming her identity or the murder [lady-in-red-c08].

Other reports come from Toronto's Lower Bay station [lady-in-red-c09], at Pluckley in England since the 12th century [lady-in-red-c10], and at the Bang Pakong River in Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. The Historic Hotels of America article says men at the Mizpah hear a voice whispering sweet nothings [lady-in-red-c14] and guests find a pearl beneath their pillows [lady-in-red-c15], and that she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous [lady-in-red-c16].

claim.id: Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan yang mirip White Lady, tetapi menurut legenda lebih khusus dikaitkan dengan kekasih yang dicampakkan, korban pembunuhan karena emosi, atau perempuan yang sombong.
claim.en: The Lady in Red is a type of female ghost like the White Lady, attributed in legend to a jilted lover, a victim of passion, or a vain woman.

claims_provenance.quote: A Lady in Red or Red Lady is a type of female ghost, similar to the White Lady, but according to legend is more specifically attributed to a jilted lover, killed in a fit of passion, or a woman of vanity.

claim.id: Dalam semua versi, ia bergaun merah tua atau merah darah.
claim.en: In all cases she wears a scarlet or blood-red dress.

claims_provenance.quote: In all cases, the Lady in Red is wearing a scarlet or blood red dress.

claim.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan ramah, dan kisahnya melekat pada hotel bersejarah, teater, atau tempat umum lain.
claim.en: She is usually friendly, with stories tied to historic hotels, theatres and other public places.

claims_provenance.quote: She is said to typically be friendly in disposition, with a story attached to historic hotels, theatres or other public places

claim.id: Gedung Weckesser di Wilkes University, Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, konon dihantui Lady in Red yang menurut seorang saksi tampak nyata sampai menghilang.
claim.en: The Weckesser building at Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red who, according to one witness, appears real until vanishing.

claims_provenance.quote: At Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, the Weckesser building is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red that according to one witness appears real until vanishing.

claim.id: Di Charleston, South Carolina, dekat Dock Street Theatre, Lady in Red konon hantu Nettie Dickerson, pelacur yang sering mengunjungi Planter's Hotel; pada usia 25 tahun ia berdiri bergaun merah di balkon hotel saat badai dan tersambar petir hingga tewas.
claim.en: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel; at 25 she was standing in her red dress on the hotel balcony during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

claims_provenance.quote: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel (now the historic French Quarter building). ... At the age of 25 she was standing in her red dress on the balcony of the hotel during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

claim.id: Di Drake Hotel Chicago, seorang perempuan cemburu bergaun merah darah mengakhiri hidup dengan melompat dari lantai 10 (atau atap, tergantung versi); tamu mengaku melihat langkah terakhirnya dari Gold Coast Room, Palm Court, dan di lantai 10.
claim.en: At Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman in a blood-red dress took her life by jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary); guests claim to see her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court and on the 10th floor.

claims_provenance.quote: In Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman wearing a blood-red dress took her life after jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary). Guests claim to see her in her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court, and on the 10th floor.

claim.id: Lantai lima Mizpah Hotel di Nevada dikenal karena Lady in Red bernama "Rose" (nama pelacurnya) yang tewas di tangan kekasih yang cemburu.
claim.en: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red called "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

claims_provenance.quote: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red known as "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

claim.id: Menurut satu sumber, nama asli Rose adalah Evelyn May Johnston, tetapi tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan bahwa perempuan bernama itu ada pada masa itu, atau bahwa pembunuhan serupa kasus "Red Lady" pernah terjadi di hotel itu.
claim.en: According to one source, Rose's real name was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records confirming that a woman by that name existed at the time, or that a murder like the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

claims_provenance.quote: According to one source, Rose's real name, was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records to confirm that a woman by this name existed at that time, nor that a murder similar to the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

claim.id: Stasiun transit Lower Bay di Toronto ditutup sejak 1966 tetapi punya banyak laporan Lady in Red; menurut saksi, hantu itu tampak terpukul dan meluncur tanpa kaki atau mata.
claim.en: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red; according to witnesses the ghost appears distraught and glides without feet or eyes.

claims_provenance.quote: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red. According to witnesses, the ghost appears distraught as it glides without feet or eyes.

claim.id: Seorang Red Lady konon berjalan di sekitar Gereja St Nicholas di Pluckley, Inggris, sejak abad ke-12.
claim.en: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England, since the 12th century.

claims_provenance.quote: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England since the 12th century.

claim.id: Di Thailand ada kisah Lady in Red yang dipercaya roh perempuan yang tenggelam di Sungai Bang Pakong; saksi melaporkan melihatnya saat berkendara melintasi Jembatan Sungai Bang Pakong pada malam hari.
claim.en: In Thailand there is a story of a Lady in Red believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River; witnesses report seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

claims_provenance.quote: In Thailand, there is a story of a Lady in Red, believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River. Witnesses have reported seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

claim.id: Dalam film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall dihantui hantu Red Lady yang warna merahnya berasal dari dikubur dalam bak tanah liat merah.
claim.en: In the film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall is haunted by Red Lady ghosts whose red color comes from being buried in red clay vats.

claims_provenance.quote: In the film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall is haunted by Red Lady ghosts whose red color comes from being buried in red clay vats.

claim.id: Serial drama Korea The Ghost Detective dinamai menurut Lady in Red yang menemani tokoh utama memecahkan kejahatan.
claim.en: The Korean drama series The Ghost Detective is named for a Lady in Red who accompanies the main character in solving crimes.

claims_provenance.quote: Korean drama series The Ghost Detective is named for a Lady in Red that accompanies the main character in solving crimes.

claim.id: Menurut artikel Historic Hotels of America, banyak pria yang menginap di Mizpah Hotel melaporkan mendengar suara tanpa wujud membisikkan rayuan di telinga mereka, terutama di lift mewah yang dulu dipakai Lady in Red mengantar tamunya dari lobi ke kamarnya.
claim.en: According to the Historic Hotels of America article, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel report hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears, especially in the fancy elevator the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.

claims_provenance.quote: In spite of her brutal end, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel have reported hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears—especially in that fancy elevator, which the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Historic Hotels of America (National Trust for Historic Preservation) — Meet the Lady in Red: Nevada's Most Famous Ghost

claim.id: Menurut artikel itu, ratusan tamu terbangun dan menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal mereka, konon dari kalungnya yang putus dan berserakan di lantai saat pergumulan tragisnya.
claim.en: According to the article, hundreds of guests have awakened to find a pearl beneath their pillows, supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.

claims_provenance.quote: In addition, hundreds of guests have awakened to discover a pearl beneath their pillows—supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Historic Hotels of America (National Trust for Historic Preservation) — Meet the Lady in Red: Nevada's Most Famous Ghost

claim.id: Menurut artikel itu, asal-usul dan identitas aslinya hilang ditelan sejarah (banyak catatan menyebutnya hanya "Rose"), tetapi ia dikatakan baik, ramah, dan murah hati, dan tampaknya masih demikian.
claim.en: According to the article, her origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went by just "Rose"), but she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous, and evidently still is.

claims_provenance.quote: Although the Lady in Red’s origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went, appropriately, by just “Rose”), she was said to be kind, welcoming, and generous—and, evidently, still is.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Historic Hotels of America (National Trust for Historic Preservation) — Meet the Lady in Red: Nevada's Most Famous Ghost

claim.id: Menurut artikel itu, kisahnya berakhir ketika mantan kekasih, mungkin bekas pelanggan, menusuk dan mencekiknya dalam amarah cemburu.
claim.en: According to the article, her story ended when an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

claims_provenance.quote: At least until an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

long_description.en: The Lady in Red is a female ghost type like the White Lady, but tied to jilted lovers or vain women [lady-in-red-c01]. She always wears red [lady-in-red-c02], is usually friendly, and haunts historic hotels, theatres and public places [lady-in-red-c03].

long_description.id: Lady in Red dilaporkan di gedung Weckesser, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], di Charleston sebagai hantu Nettie Dickerson yang tersambar petir [lady-in-red-c05], dan di Drake Hotel Chicago sebagai perempuan cemburu yang melompat [lady-in-red-c06]. Di Mizpah Hotel, Nevada, ia dikenal sebagai "Rose" yang tewas di tangan kekasih cemburu [lady-in-red-c07], meski satu sumber mencatat tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan identitas atau pembunuhan itu [lady-in-red-c08].
long_description.en: Lady in Red sightings are reported at the Weckesser building, Wilkes University [lady-in-red-c04], in Charleston as the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, killed by lightning [lady-in-red-c05], and at Chicago's Drake Hotel as a jealous woman who jumped [lady-in-red-c06]. At the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada she is known as "Rose", who died at the hands of a jealous lover [lady-in-red-c07], though one source notes there are no records confirming her identity or the murder [lady-in-red-c08].

long_description.id: Laporan lain datang dari stasiun Lower Bay Toronto [lady-in-red-c09], di Pluckley Inggris sejak abad ke-12 [lady-in-red-c10], dan di Sungai Bang Pakong Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. Artikel Historic Hotels of America menyebut pria di Mizpah mendengar suara membisikkan rayuan [lady-in-red-c14] dan tamu menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal [lady-in-red-c15], serta bahwa ia dikatakan baik, ramah, dan murah hati [lady-in-red-c16].
long_description.en: Other reports come from Toronto's Lower Bay station [lady-in-red-c09], at Pluckley in England since the 12th century [lady-in-red-c10], and at the Bang Pakong River in Thailand [lady-in-red-c11]. The Historic Hotels of America article says men at the Mizpah hear a voice whispering sweet nothings [lady-in-red-c14] and guests find a pearl beneath their pillows [lady-in-red-c15], and that she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous [lady-in-red-c16].

claims.quote: A Lady in Red or Red Lady is a type of female ghost, similar to the White Lady, but according to legend is more specifically attributed to a jilted lover, killed in a fit of passion, or a woman of vanity.

statement.id: Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan yang mirip White Lady, tetapi menurut legenda lebih khusus dikaitkan dengan kekasih yang dicampakkan, korban pembunuhan karena emosi, atau perempuan yang sombong.
statement.en: The Lady in Red is a type of female ghost like the White Lady, attributed in legend to a jilted lover, a victim of passion, or a vain woman.

claims.quote: In all cases, the Lady in Red is wearing a scarlet or blood red dress.

statement.id: Dalam semua versi, ia bergaun merah tua atau merah darah.
statement.en: In all cases she wears a scarlet or blood-red dress.

claims.quote: She is said to typically be friendly in disposition, with a story attached to historic hotels, theatres or other public places

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan ramah, dan kisahnya melekat pada hotel bersejarah, teater, atau tempat umum lain.
statement.en: She is usually friendly, with stories tied to historic hotels, theatres and other public places.

claims.quote: At Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, the Weckesser building is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red that according to one witness appears real until vanishing.

statement.id: Gedung Weckesser di Wilkes University, Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, konon dihantui Lady in Red yang menurut seorang saksi tampak nyata sampai menghilang.
statement.en: The Weckesser building at Wilkes University in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, is reportedly haunted by a Lady in Red who, according to one witness, appears real until vanishing.

claims.quote: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel (now the historic French Quarter building). ... At the age of 25 she was standing in her red dress on the balcony of the hotel during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

statement.id: Di Charleston, South Carolina, dekat Dock Street Theatre, Lady in Red konon hantu Nettie Dickerson, pelacur yang sering mengunjungi Planter's Hotel; pada usia 25 tahun ia berdiri bergaun merah di balkon hotel saat badai dan tersambar petir hingga tewas.
statement.en: In Charleston, South Carolina, near Dock Street Theatre, a Lady in Red is said to be the ghost of Nettie Dickerson, a prostitute who frequented the Planter's Hotel; at 25 she was standing in her red dress on the hotel balcony during a storm when she was struck by lightning and killed.

claims.quote: In Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman wearing a blood-red dress took her life after jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary). Guests claim to see her in her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court, and on the 10th floor.

statement.id: Di Drake Hotel Chicago, seorang perempuan cemburu bergaun merah darah mengakhiri hidup dengan melompat dari lantai 10 (atau atap, tergantung versi); tamu mengaku melihat langkah terakhirnya dari Gold Coast Room, Palm Court, dan di lantai 10.
statement.en: At Chicago's Drake Hotel, a jealous woman in a blood-red dress took her life by jumping from the 10th floor (or the roof, as accounts vary); guests claim to see her last steps from the Gold Coast Room, the Palm Court and on the 10th floor.

claims.quote: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red known as "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

statement.id: Lantai lima Mizpah Hotel di Nevada dikenal karena Lady in Red bernama "Rose" (nama pelacurnya) yang tewas di tangan kekasih yang cemburu.
statement.en: The fifth floor of the Mizpah Hotel in Nevada is known for a Lady in Red called "Rose" (her prostitute name) who died at the hands of a jealous lover.

claims.quote: According to one source, Rose's real name, was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records to confirm that a woman by this name existed at that time, nor that a murder similar to the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

statement.id: Menurut satu sumber, nama asli Rose adalah Evelyn May Johnston, tetapi tidak ada catatan yang menegaskan bahwa perempuan bernama itu ada pada masa itu, atau bahwa pembunuhan serupa kasus "Red Lady" pernah terjadi di hotel itu.
statement.en: According to one source, Rose's real name was Evelyn May Johnston, though there are no records confirming that a woman by that name existed at the time, or that a murder like the "Red Lady" crime ever took place in the hotel.

claims.quote: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red. According to witnesses, the ghost appears distraught as it glides without feet or eyes.

statement.id: Stasiun transit Lower Bay di Toronto ditutup sejak 1966 tetapi punya banyak laporan Lady in Red; menurut saksi, hantu itu tampak terpukul dan meluncur tanpa kaki atau mata.
statement.en: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red; according to witnesses the ghost appears distraught and glides without feet or eyes.

claims.quote: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England since the 12th century.

statement.en: A Red Lady is said to walk around the Church of St Nicholas in Pluckley, England, since the 12th century.

claims.quote: In Thailand, there is a story of a Lady in Red, believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River. Witnesses have reported seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

statement.id: Di Thailand ada kisah Lady in Red yang dipercaya roh perempuan yang tenggelam di Sungai Bang Pakong; saksi melaporkan melihatnya saat berkendara melintasi Jembatan Sungai Bang Pakong pada malam hari.
statement.en: In Thailand there is a story of a Lady in Red believed to be the spirit of a woman who drowned in the Bang Pakong River; witnesses report seeing her while driving across the Bang Pakong River Bridge at night.

statement.en: In the film Crimson Peak, Allerdale Hall is haunted by Red Lady ghosts whose red color comes from being buried in red clay vats.

statement.en: The Korean drama series The Ghost Detective is named for a Lady in Red who accompanies the main character in solving crimes.

claims.quote: In spite of her brutal end, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel have reported hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears—especially in that fancy elevator, which the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.

statement.id: Menurut artikel Historic Hotels of America, banyak pria yang menginap di Mizpah Hotel melaporkan mendengar suara tanpa wujud membisikkan rayuan di telinga mereka, terutama di lift mewah yang dulu dipakai Lady in Red mengantar tamunya dari lobi ke kamarnya.
statement.en: According to the Historic Hotels of America article, many men visiting the Mizpah Hotel report hearing an incorporeal voice whispering sweet nothings in their ears, especially in the fancy elevator the Lady in Red used to escort her visitors from the lobby to her chambers.

claims.quote: In addition, hundreds of guests have awakened to discover a pearl beneath their pillows—supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, ratusan tamu terbangun dan menemukan mutiara di bawah bantal mereka, konon dari kalungnya yang putus dan berserakan di lantai saat pergumulan tragisnya.
statement.en: According to the article, hundreds of guests have awakened to find a pearl beneath their pillows, supposedly from her necklace, which broke and spilled onto the floor in her tragic scuffle.

claims.quote: Although the Lady in Red’s origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went, appropriately, by just “Rose”), she was said to be kind, welcoming, and generous—and, evidently, still is.

statement.en: According to the article, her origins and true identity are lost to history (many accounts suggest she went by just "Rose"), but she was said to be kind, welcoming and generous, and evidently still is.

claims.quote: At least until an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, kisahnya berakhir ketika mantan kekasih, mungkin bekas pelanggan, menusuk dan mencekiknya dalam amarah cemburu.
statement.en: According to the article, her story ended when an ex-lover, possibly a former patron, stabbed and strangled her in a fit of jealous rage.

short_description.id: Mami Wata adalah roh air, putri duyung, dan dewi dalam cerita rakyat berbagai wilayah Afrika, yang dikaitkan dengan kekayaan, kesuburan, dan kecantikan, serta dipuja hingga diaspora Atlantik.
short_description.en: Mami Wata is a water spirit, mermaid and goddess in the folklore of many parts of Africa, tied to wealth, fertility and beauty and honoured as far as the Atlantic diaspora.

long_description.id:
Mami Wata, juga disebut Mammy Water, adalah putri duyung, roh air, atau dewi dalam cerita rakyat Afrika Barat, Tengah, Timur, dan Selatan. Namanya berasal dari kata Inggris mother dan water dalam bahasa-bahasa kreol Afrika seperti Krio dan Naijá. Ia dipandang sebagai dewi kekayaan, kesuburan, penyembuhan, kebijaksanaan, dan kecantikan.

Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan berkulit terang dengan rambut panjang, yang menyukai benda-benda asing persembahan pemujanya. Ia dapat mengendalikan samudra dan sungai serta berubah wujud untuk memikat manusia. Kepercayaan di Liberia menyebut ia tinggal di istana bawah air dan kadang naik ke pantai untuk menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas; cermin menjadi lambangnya di tempat-tempat suci.

Wataknya ambivalen seperti air: ia bisa menyembuhkan dan memberi hidup, tetapi juga merusak. Ia dapat menganugerahkan kekayaan, penglihatan masa depan, atau perjalanan sangat cepat, tetapi lelaki yang tidak setia kepadanya dikatakan kehilangan kekayaan dan jatuh sakit atau gila. Di kalangan Kpelle ia kadang berwujud laki-laki, kadang perempuan, dan beberapa tradisi mengenal pasangan laki-laki bernama Papi Wata.

Para sarjana menelusuri asal-usulnya ke perjumpaan orang Eropa dan Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15, ketika gambaran putri duyung Eropa menjadi model awalnya; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 gambar pawang ular Nala Damajanti sangat memengaruhi ikonografinya. Barbara Paxson sebaliknya menempatkan asalnya di Amerika Latin. Di Afrika Tengah dikenal varian Mamba Muntu atau Mami Muntu, yang diidentifikasi sebagai putri duyung, buaya, atau ular.

Mami Wata dipuja di sebagian Afrika dan diaspora Atlantik, misalnya oleh orang Fon dan Ewe serta dalam Voodoo Haiti, tetapi dijadikan setan oleh sebagian komunitas Kristen dan Islam. Sebagian sarjana mengaitkannya dengan roh air di Karibia dan Amerika Selatan seperti Lasirèn, dan sumber kedua mencatat bahwa di Brasil ia diidentikkan dengan Yemanja.
long_description.en:
Mami Wata, also called Mammy Water, appears as a mermaid, water spirit or goddess in the folklore of Western, Central, Eastern and Southern Africa. Her name comes from the English words mother and water as used in African creoles such as Krio and Naijá. She is seen as a goddess of riches, fertility, healing, wisdom and beauty.

She is usually pictured as a light-skinned woman with long hair who delights in foreign objects her devotees offer. She commands seas and rivers and changes form to charm people. Liberian belief places her in an underwater mansion from which she now and then comes ashore to comb her hair with a golden comb, and mirrors serve as her emblem in shrines.

Her nature is two-sided like water itself, able to heal and give life yet also to destroy. She may bestow riches, foresight or unusually swift travel, but a man who breaks faith with her is said to lose his fortune and fall sick or go mad. Among the Kpelle she is sometimes male and sometimes female, and some traditions know a male counterpart called Papi Wata.

Scholars link her beginnings to contact between Europeans and West Africans in the 15th century, when European mermaid images served as an early model; in the mid-19th century a picture of the snake charmer Nala Damajanti reshaped her iconography. Barbara Paxson, by contrast, locates her homeland in Latin America. Central Africa knows a variant, Mamba Muntu or Mami Muntu, identified as a mermaid, crocodile or snake.

Mami Wata is venerated in parts of Africa and the Atlantic diaspora, for example by the Fon and Ewe and in Haitian Voodoo, but some Christian and Islamic communities have demonized her. Some scholars tie her to water spirits of the Caribbean and South America such as Lasirèn, and the second source notes that in Brazil she was identified with Yemanja.

text.id: Asal-usulnya ditelusuri ke perjumpaan Eropa-Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15; ikonografinya berubah pada pertengahan abad ke-19
text.en: Origins traced to European-West African encounters in the 15th century; iconography changed in the mid-19th century

short_description.id: Mami Wata adalah roh air, putri duyung, dan dewi dalam cerita rakyat berbagai wilayah Afrika, yang dikaitkan dengan kekayaan, kesuburan, dan kecantikan, serta dipuja hingga diaspora Atlantik.
short_description.en: Mami Wata is a water spirit, mermaid and goddess in the folklore of many parts of Africa, tied to wealth, fertility and beauty and honoured as far as the Atlantic diaspora.

long_description.id: Mami Wata, juga disebut Mammy Water, adalah putri duyung, roh air, atau dewi dalam cerita rakyat Afrika Barat, Tengah, Timur, dan Selatan. Namanya berasal dari kata Inggris mother dan water dalam bahasa-bahasa kreol Afrika seperti Krio dan Naijá. Ia dipandang sebagai dewi kekayaan, kesuburan, penyembuhan, kebijaksanaan, dan kecantikan.
long_description.en: Mami Wata, also called Mammy Water, appears as a mermaid, water spirit or goddess in the folklore of Western, Central, Eastern and Southern Africa. Her name comes from the English words mother and water as used in African creoles such as Krio and Naijá. She is seen as a goddess of riches, fertility, healing, wisdom and beauty.

long_description.id: Ia sering digambarkan sebagai perempuan berkulit terang dengan rambut panjang, yang menyukai benda-benda asing persembahan pemujanya. Ia dapat mengendalikan samudra dan sungai serta berubah wujud untuk memikat manusia. Kepercayaan di Liberia menyebut ia tinggal di istana bawah air dan kadang naik ke pantai untuk menyisir rambutnya dengan sisir emas; cermin menjadi lambangnya di tempat-tempat suci.
long_description.en: She is usually pictured as a light-skinned woman with long hair who delights in foreign objects her devotees offer. She commands seas and rivers and changes form to charm people. Liberian belief places her in an underwater mansion from which she now and then comes ashore to comb her hair with a golden comb, and mirrors serve as her emblem in shrines.

long_description.id: Wataknya ambivalen seperti air: ia bisa menyembuhkan dan memberi hidup, tetapi juga merusak. Ia dapat menganugerahkan kekayaan, penglihatan masa depan, atau perjalanan sangat cepat, tetapi lelaki yang tidak setia kepadanya dikatakan kehilangan kekayaan dan jatuh sakit atau gila. Di kalangan Kpelle ia kadang berwujud laki-laki, kadang perempuan, dan beberapa tradisi mengenal pasangan laki-laki bernama Papi Wata.
long_description.en: Her nature is two-sided like water itself, able to heal and give life yet also to destroy. She may bestow riches, foresight or unusually swift travel, but a man who breaks faith with her is said to lose his fortune and fall sick or go mad. Among the Kpelle she is sometimes male and sometimes female, and some traditions know a male counterpart called Papi Wata.

long_description.id: Para sarjana menelusuri asal-usulnya ke perjumpaan orang Eropa dan Afrika Barat pada abad ke-15, ketika gambaran putri duyung Eropa menjadi model awalnya; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 gambar pawang ular Nala Damajanti sangat memengaruhi ikonografinya. Barbara Paxson sebaliknya menempatkan asalnya di Amerika Latin. Di Afrika Tengah dikenal varian Mamba Muntu atau Mami Muntu, yang diidentifikasi sebagai putri duyung, buaya, atau ular.
long_description.en: Scholars link her beginnings to contact between Europeans and West Africans in the 15th century, when European mermaid images served as an early model; in the mid-19th century a picture of the snake charmer Nala Damajanti reshaped her iconography. Barbara Paxson, by contrast, locates her homeland in Latin America. Central Africa knows a variant, Mamba Muntu or Mami Muntu, identified as a mermaid, crocodile or snake.

long_description.id: Mami Wata dipuja di sebagian Afrika dan diaspora Atlantik, misalnya oleh orang Fon dan Ewe serta dalam Voodoo Haiti, tetapi dijadikan setan oleh sebagian komunitas Kristen dan Islam. Sebagian sarjana mengaitkannya dengan roh air di Karibia dan Amerika Selatan seperti Lasirèn, dan sumber kedua mencatat bahwa di Brasil ia diidentikkan dengan Yemanja.
long_description.en: Mami Wata is venerated in parts of Africa and the Atlantic diaspora, for example by the Fon and Ewe and in Haitian Voodoo, but some Christian and Islamic communities have demonized her. Some scholars tie her to water spirits of the Caribbean and South America such as Lasirèn, and the second source notes that in Brazil she was identified with Yemanja.

short_description.id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya dan tokoh penipu cerdik dalam mitologi Polinesia, yang dikenal lewat perbuatan seperti memancing pulau, mencuri api, dan memperlambat Matahari.
short_description.en: Māui is the great culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology, known for exploits such as fishing up islands, stealing fire and slowing the Sun.

long_description.id:
Māui adalah pahlawan budaya sekaligus tokoh penipu dalam mitologi Polinesia. Ia sangat jarang disembah; ia lebih dipandang sebagai pahlawan rakyat daripada dewa. Westervelt menyebutnya salah satu demigod Polinesia yang orang tuanya termasuk makhluk gaib, dengan kekuatan supernatural dan mantra.

Kisah petualangan Māui diceritakan di sebagian besar Polinesia dan dapat dilacak sampai ke pulau-pulau di dekat New Guinea. Perbuatan yang umum di kebanyakan tradisi adalah mencuri api dari dunia bawah, memancing pulau dengan kail sakti, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari. Meski dikatakan sangat nakal, banyak perbuatannya bertujuan memperbaiki hidup sesamanya.

Asal-usul Māui berbeda dari satu budaya ke budaya lain, termasuk orang tuanya, status ilahinya, dan bentuk beberapa mitos utama. Menurut Westervelt, ia kadang disebut Maui-Tiki-Tiki atau Maui-po-tiki. Dalam tradisi Hawaii ia dikreditkan dengan menarik gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra, sedangkan kisah Māori menjadikan ikan raksasa tangkapannya Pulau Utara Selandia Baru.

Dalam salah satu versi, tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
long_description.en:
Māui is the culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology. He was very rarely worshipped and is regarded more as a folk hero than a deity. Westervelt calls him one of the Polynesian demi-gods, whose parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings and who had supernatural powers and enchantments.

Tales of Māui's adventures are told throughout most of Polynesia and can be traced as far west as islands off New Guinea. Exploits common to most traditions are stealing fire from the underworld, fishing up islands with a magic hook and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days. Though said to be very rascally, many of his deeds improved the lives of others.

Māui's origins vary from culture to culture, including his parentage, divine status and the form of several major myths. According to Westervelt he is sometimes called Maui-Tiki-Tiki or Maui-po-tiki. In Hawaiian tradition he is credited with pulling island groups up from the ocean depths, while the Māori account makes the giant fish he caught the North Island of New Zealand.

In one version his final trick ended in his death and brought him into contact with Hine-nui-te-pō, goddess of death and the underworld.

role.id: Menurut Westervelt, ia adalah demigod yang memakai mantra dan kekuatan supernatural; dalam banyak kisah perbuatannya bermanfaat bagi manusia.
role.en: According to Westervelt, a demi-god who used enchantments and supernatural powers; in many tales his deeds benefit people.

famous_for.id: Dikenal karena memancing pulau, mencuri api, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari.
famous_for.en: Known for fishing up islands, stealing fire and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

did_you_know.id: Westervelt mencatat bahwa orang Samoa menceritakan kisah menjerat matahari tanpa menyebut nama Maui; mereka mengatakan jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
did_you_know.en: Westervelt records that the Samoans tell the story of snaring the sun without mentioning Maui; they say the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

cultural_context.id: Meski dikenal nakal, banyak perbuatan Māui bertujuan memperbaiki kehidupan sesama manusia.
cultural_context.en: Although known as rascally, many of Māui's deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

description.id: Menurut Westervelt, Maui memiliki kekuatan supernatural dan dianggap memakai segala macam mantra; dalam salah satu versi ia memberi kekuatan pada tali pancingnya dengan karakia.
description.en: According to Westervelt, Maui had supernatural powers and was supposed to use all manner of enchantments; in one version he gave his fishing line strength with a karakia.

description.id: Dalam kisah Hawaii, Māui dikreditkan menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra dengan kail ajaib.
description.en: In the Hawaiian account, Māui is credited with pulling various island groups up from the ocean depths with a magic hook.

description.id: Dalam salah satu versi, ikan raksasa yang ditarik Māui menjadi Pulau Utara Selandia Baru, Te Ika-a-Māui.
description.en: In one version, the giant fish Māui pulled up became the North Island of New Zealand, Te Ika-a-Māui.

description.id: Orang Samoa menceritakan kisah yang sama tanpa menyebut nama Maui; jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
description.en: The Samoans tell the same story without Maui's name; the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

role.en: Fishes up islands with a magic hook.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Māui menganyam tali pancing, memberinya kekuatan dengan karakia, dan memasang kail ajaib dari tulang rahang pemberian neneknya; ikan raksasa yang ia tarik menjadi Pulau Utara. Dalam kisah Hawaii, ia menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra.
summary.en: In one version Māui wove a fishing line, strengthened it with a karakia and attached a magic hook made from the jawbone his grandmother gave him; the giant fish he pulled up became the North Island. In the Hawaiian account he pulled various island groups up from the ocean depths.

summary.id: Māui, cucu Mahuika, pergi mencari Mahuika di gua dalam gunung yang menyala. Mahuika memberinya kuku jari yang menyala, tetapi Māui memadamkannya satu demi satu sampai Mahuika marah dan mengirim api mengejarnya. Māui kemudian membawa pulang ranting kering dan menunjukkan cara menggosokkannya untuk membuat api.
summary.en: Māui, a grandson of Mahuika, went to find Mahuika in a cave in a burning mountain. She gave him burning fingernails, but he put them out one by one until she became angry and sent fire to pursue him. Māui then brought dry sticks home and showed how to rub them together to make fire.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Tama-nui-te-rā terjerat dan Māui memukulnya dengan tulang rahang sampai ia menyerah dan setuju bergerak pelan melintasi langit.
summary.en: In one version Tama-nui-te-rā, trapped in the noose, was beaten with the jawbone by Māui until he yielded and promised to cross the sky slowly.

summary.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
summary.en: His final trick ended in his death and brought him into contact with Hine-nui-te-pō, goddess of death and the underworld.

description.id: Menurut Westervelt, Haleakala ("Rumah Matahari") adalah gunung tempat Maui menjerat matahari.
description.en: According to Westervelt, Haleakala ("the House of the Sun") is the mountain from which Maui snared the sun.

note.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Māui adalah cucu Mahuika, dewi api.
note.en: In one version Māui is a grandson of Mahuika, the fire goddess.

note.id: Māui menjerat dewa matahari Tama-nui-te-rā dan memukulnya sampai ia setuju bergerak lebih lambat.
note.en: Māui snares the sun-god Tama-nui-te-rā and strikes him until he agrees to move more slowly.

note.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō dan berujung pada kematiannya.
note.en: Māui's last trick involved Hine-nui-te-pō and led to his death.

long_description.en: Māui's origins vary from culture to culture, including his parentage, divine status and the form of several major myths. According to Westervelt he is sometimes called Maui-Tiki-Tiki or Maui-po-tiki. In Hawaiian tradition he is credited with pulling island groups up from the ocean depths, while the Māori account makes the giant fish he caught the North Island of New Zealand.

long_description.id: Dalam salah satu versi, tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
long_description.en: In one version his final trick ended in his death and brought him into contact with Hine-nui-te-pō, goddess of death and the underworld.

cultural_context.id: Meski dikenal nakal, banyak perbuatan Māui bertujuan memperbaiki kehidupan sesama manusia.
cultural_context.en: Although known as rascally, many of Māui's deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

who.id: Pahlawan budaya dan tokoh penipu dalam mitologi Polinesia.
who.en: A culture hero and trickster of Polynesian mythology.

origin.id: Tradisi Polinesia; kisahnya diceritakan di sebagian besar Polinesia dan dapat dilacak sampai pulau-pulau di dekat New Guinea.
origin.en: Polynesian tradition; his tales are told across most of Polynesia and can be traced as far as islands off New Guinea.

role.en: According to Westervelt, a demi-god who used enchantments and supernatural powers; in many tales his deeds benefit people.

description.en: According to Westervelt, Maui had supernatural powers and was supposed to use all manner of enchantments; in one version he gave his fishing line strength with a karakia.

description.id: Dalam kisah Hawaii, Māui dikreditkan menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra dengan kail ajaib.
description.en: In the Hawaiian account, Māui is credited with pulling various island groups up from the ocean depths with a magic hook.

description.id: Orang Samoa menceritakan kisah yang sama tanpa menyebut nama Maui; jerat itu dilemparkan oleh anak matahari sendiri.
description.en: The Samoans tell the same story without Maui's name; the snare was cast by a child of the sun itself.

role.en: Fishes up islands with a magic hook.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Māui menganyam tali pancing, memberinya kekuatan dengan karakia, dan memasang kail ajaib dari tulang rahang pemberian neneknya; ikan raksasa yang ia tarik menjadi Pulau Utara. Dalam kisah Hawaii, ia menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra.
summary.en: In one version Māui wove a fishing line, strengthened it with a karakia and attached a magic hook made from the jawbone his grandmother gave him; the giant fish he pulled up became the North Island. In the Hawaiian account he pulled various island groups up from the ocean depths.

summary.id: Māui, cucu Mahuika, pergi mencari Mahuika di gua dalam gunung yang menyala. Mahuika memberinya kuku jari yang menyala, tetapi Māui memadamkannya satu demi satu sampai Mahuika marah dan mengirim api mengejarnya. Māui kemudian membawa pulang ranting kering dan menunjukkan cara menggosokkannya untuk membuat api.
summary.en: Māui, a grandson of Mahuika, went to find Mahuika in a cave in a burning mountain. She gave him burning fingernails, but he put them out one by one until she became angry and sent fire to pursue him. Māui then brought dry sticks home and showed how to rub them together to make fire.

summary.id: Dalam salah satu versi, Tama-nui-te-rā terjerat dan Māui memukulnya dengan tulang rahang sampai ia menyerah dan setuju bergerak pelan melintasi langit.
summary.en: In one version Tama-nui-te-rā, trapped in the noose, was beaten with the jawbone by Māui until he yielded and promised to cross the sky slowly.

claims.quote: Māui or Maui is the great culture hero and trickster in Polynesian mythology.

statement.id: Māui adalah pahlawan budaya dan penipu ulung dalam mitologi Polinesia.
statement.en: Māui is the great culture hero and trickster in Polynesian mythology.

claims.quote: Tales of Māui's exploits and adventures are told throughout most of Polynesia; they can be traced back as far west as islands off New Guinea.

statement.id: Kisah petualangan Māui diceritakan di seantero Polinesia hingga pulau-pulau di lepas New Guinea.
statement.en: Tales of Māui's exploits are told across Polynesia and as far west as islands off New Guinea.

claims.quote: Very rarely was Māui actually worshipped, being less of a deity (demigod) and more of a folk hero.

statement.id: Māui sangat jarang disembah, lebih berposisi sebagai pahlawan rakyat daripada dewa.
statement.en: Māui was rarely worshipped, being viewed as a folk hero rather than a deity.

claims.quote: Some exploits common to most Polynesian traditions are stealing fire for humans from the underworld, fishing up islands with his magical hook, and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

statement.id: Beberapa perbuatan yang umum dalam kebanyakan tradisi Polinesia adalah mencuri api untuk manusia dari dunia bawah, memancing pulau-pulau dengan kail saktinya, dan menangkap Matahari untuk memperpanjang hari.
statement.en: Some exploits common to most Polynesian traditions are stealing fire for humans from the underworld, fishing up islands with his magical hook, and capturing the Sun to lengthen the days.

claims.quote: Although Māui was said to be very rascally or "kolohe", many of his deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

statement.id: Meskipun Māui dikatakan sangat nakal atau "kolohe", banyak perbuatannya bertujuan memperbaiki kehidupan sesama manusia.
statement.en: Although Māui was said to be very rascally, or "kolohe", many of his deeds were to better the lives of his fellow people.

claims.quote: His origins vary from culture to culture, with variation in his parentage, divine status, and the specific form of several major myths, but many of his main exploits remain relatively similar.

statement.id: Asal-usul Māui berbeda dari satu budaya ke budaya lain, termasuk orang tuanya, status ilahinya, dan bentuk beberapa mitos utama, tetapi banyak perbuatan pokoknya relatif serupa.
statement.en: Māui's origins vary from culture to culture, including his parentage, divine status and the specific form of several major myths, but many of his main exploits remain relatively similar.

claims.quote: The noted greenstone god of the Maoris of New Zealand, Potiki, may well be considered a representation of Maui-Tiki-Tiki, who was sometimes called Maui-po-tiki.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, dewa batu hijau (greenstone) Māori yang terkenal, Potiki, dapat dianggap sebagai perwujudan Maui-Tiki-Tiki, yang kadang disebut Maui-po-tiki.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the noted greenstone god of the Maoris, Potiki, may well be considered a representation of Maui-Tiki-Tiki, who was sometimes called Maui-po-tiki.

claims.quote: Māui's last trick led to his death and involved Hine-nui-te-pō, the goddess of death and the underworld.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — The death of Māui

statement.id: Tipu daya terakhir Māui berujung pada kematiannya dan melibatkan Hine-nui-te-pō, dewi kematian dan dunia bawah.
statement.en: Māui's last trick led to his death and involved Hine-nui-te-pō, the goddess of death and the underworld.

claims.quote: Māui also is credited with the creation of the Hawaiian islands, when he went on a fishing expedition with his friends, and, using a magic fish hook, pulled up various island groups from the oceanic depths.

statement.id: Māui juga dipercaya menciptakan kepulauan Hawaii: dalam ekspedisi memancing bersama teman-temannya ia memakai kail ajaib untuk menarik berbagai gugusan pulau dari dasar samudra.
statement.en: Māui is also credited with creating the Hawaiian islands: on a fishing expedition with his friends he used a magic fish hook to pull up various island groups from the ocean depths.

claims.quote: One night, he wove for himself a flax fishing line and enchanted it with a karakia to give it strength; to this he attached the magic fish-hook made from the jawbone that his grandmother Murirangawhenua had given him.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Islands of New Zealand

statement.id: Pada suatu malam ia menganyam tali pancing dari rami dan memberinya kekuatan dengan karakia (mantra); padanya ia mengikatkan kail ajaib dari tulang rahang yang diberikan neneknya, Murirangawhenua.
statement.en: One night he wove a flax fishing line and enchanted it with a karakia (incantation) to give it strength; to it he attached the magic fish-hook made from the jawbone his grandmother Murirangawhenua had given him.

claims.quote: He pulled up a giant fish which would become the North Island of New Zealand, known as Te Ika-a-Māui; the valleys and mountains of the island were made by his brothers chopping up the fish for themselves.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Islands of New Zealand

statement.id: Ia menarik seekor ikan raksasa yang kelak menjadi Pulau Utara Selandia Baru, yang dikenal sebagai Te Ika-a-Māui; lembah dan gunung di pulau itu terbentuk ketika saudara-saudaranya mencincang ikan itu untuk diri mereka sendiri.
statement.en: He pulled up a giant fish that would become the North Island of New Zealand, known as Te Ika-a-Māui; the island's valleys and mountains were made by his brothers chopping up the fish for themselves.

claims.quote: So Māui (a grandson of Mahuika) offered to go and find her. Mahuika lived in a cave in a burning mountain at the end of the earth. She gave Māui one of her burning fingernails to relight the fires, but Māui extinguished fingernail after fingernail until Mahuika became angry and sent fire to pursue Māui
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui brings fire to the world

statement.id: Māui (cucu Mahuika) menawarkan diri mencari Mahuika, yang tinggal di gua dalam gunung yang menyala di ujung bumi. Mahuika memberinya satu kuku jarinya yang menyala untuk menyalakan kembali api, tetapi Māui memadamkan kuku demi kuku sampai Mahuika marah dan mengirim api untuk mengejarnya.
statement.en: Māui (a grandson of Mahuika) offered to find her; Mahuika lived in a cave in a burning mountain at the end of the earth. She gave him one of her burning fingernails to relight the fires, but Māui put out fingernail after fingernail until Mahuika became angry and sent fire to pursue him.

claims.quote: Māui brought back dry sticks of these trees to his village and showed his people how to rub the sticks together and make fire.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui brings fire to the world

statement.id: Māui membawa pulang ranting kering dari pohon-pohon itu ke desanya dan menunjukkan kepada rakyatnya cara menggosokkan ranting untuk membuat api.
statement.en: Māui brought dry sticks of these trees back to his village and showed his people how to rub the sticks together to make fire.

claims.quote: Tama-nui-te-rā was caught in the noose and Māui struck him with the jawbone until he surrendered and agreed to travel slowly across the sky.
claims.locator: Māori mythology — Māui slows the sun

statement.id: Tama-nui-te-rā terjerat dalam jerat itu dan Māui memukulnya dengan tulang rahang sampai ia menyerah dan setuju bergerak pelan melintasi langit.
statement.en: Tama-nui-te-rā was caught in the noose and Māui struck him with the jawbone until he surrendered and agreed to travel slowly across the sky.

claims.quote: Maui was one of the Polynesian demi-gods. His parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings. He himself was possessed of supernatural powers and was supposed to make use of all manner of enchantments.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, Maui adalah salah satu demigod Polinesia; orang tuanya termasuk keluarga makhluk gaib, dan ia sendiri memiliki kekuatan supernatural serta dianggap memakai segala macam mantra.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, Maui was one of the Polynesian demi-gods; his parents belonged to the family of supernatural beings, and he himself possessed supernatural powers and was supposed to use all manner of enchantments.

claims.quote: The legends of Hawaii, Tonga, Tahiti, New Zealand and the Hervey group make this youngest Maui "the discoverer of fire" or "the ensnarer of the sun" or "the fisherman who pulls up islands" or "the man endowed with magic," or "Maui with spirit power."

statement.en: According to Westervelt, the legends of Hawaii, Tonga, Tahiti, New Zealand and the Hervey group make this youngest Maui "the discoverer of fire", "the ensnarer of the sun", "the fisherman who pulls up islands", "the man endowed with magic" or "Maui with spirit power".

claims.quote: The New Zealanders claim Maui as an ancestor of their most ancient tribes and sometimes class him among the most ancient of their gods, calling him "creator of land" and "creator of man."

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, orang Selandia Baru menganggap Maui sebagai leluhur suku-suku tertua mereka dan kadang menggolongkannya di antara dewa-dewa tertua mereka, menyebutnya "pencipta daratan" dan "pencipta manusia".
statement.en: According to Westervelt, the New Zealanders claim Maui as an ancestor of their most ancient tribes and sometimes class him among their most ancient gods, calling him "creator of land" and "creator of man".

claims.quote: Haleakala (the House of the Sun), the mountain from which Maui the demi-god snared the sun, looks down ten thousand feet upon the Kauiki headland.

statement.id: Menurut Westervelt, Haleakala ("Rumah Matahari") adalah gunung tempat Maui sang demigod menjerat matahari.
statement.en: According to Westervelt, Haleakala ("the House of the Sun") is the mountain from which Maui the demi-god snared the sun.

short_description.id: Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi adalah iblis berbulu dalam mitologi Georgian dan kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, penghuni gunung yang menyerang manusia dan mengejar Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan.
short_description.en: Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi is a hairy demon of Georgian mythology and Megrel folk belief, a mountain dweller that attacks people and pursues Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest.

long_description.id:
Oçokoçi, juga ditulis Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), adalah sosok dari mitologi Georgian, terutama di kalangan Mingrelian dan Colchian. Artikel pertama menempatkannya dalam mitologi Gürcü-Megrel-Laz sebagai penghuni gunung, sedangkan artikel kedua mengartikan namanya sebagai manusia-kambing.

Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, ia iblis berwujud manusia yang seluruh tubuhnya ditutupi bulu hitam pekat, bercakar panjang dan tajam. Pada musim dingin ia mendatangi desa dan memangsa anak laki-laki serta anak sapi di kandang. Ia tidak dapat berbicara, tetapi bunyi yang dikeluarkannya tak tertahankan bagi manusia.

Kedua artikel menggambarkan senjatanya secara berbeda. Artikel pertama menyebut ia membawa alat mirip kapak untuk membelah dua para penentangnya; artikel kedua menyebut dadanya bertonjolan berupa tulang runcing atau kapak batu dan ia membunuh orang lewat dengan memeluknya. Oçokoçi yang telah dibunuh pun dikatakan hidup lagi jika ditembak untuk kedua kalinya.

Ia tergila-gila pada Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan, dan terus mengejarnya, tetapi para pemburu yang datang ke hutan sering menggagalkannya. Kajian tentang panteon pagan Megrelian menyebut Ochokochi menempati tempat penting di dalamnya dan, bersama Tkashmapa, tampil di dekat manusia dalam legenda serta memberi keberuntungan berburu.
long_description.en:
Oçokoçi, also written Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), is a figure of Georgian mythology, especially among the Mingrelian and Colchian groups. The first article places it in Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mythology as a dweller of the mountains, while the second renders its name as goat-man.

In Megrel folk belief it is a demon in human form whose whole body is covered in jet-black hair, with long sharp claws. In winter it comes to the villages and preys on boys and on calves in the barn. It cannot talk, yet the noise it makes is unbearable to people.

The two articles describe its weapon differently. The first says it carries an axe-like tool with which it splits its opponents in two; the second says its chest bears a protuberance like a pointed bone or stone axe and that it kills passers-by by embracing them. An Oçokoçi that has been killed is even said to come back to life if shot a second time.

He is infatuated with Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest, and keeps chasing her, but hunters visiting the forest often foil him. A study of the Megrelian pagan pantheon says Ochokochi holds an important place in it and, together with Tkashmapa, appears near people in legends and grants luck in hunting.

short_description.id: Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi adalah iblis berbulu dalam mitologi Georgian dan kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, penghuni gunung yang menyerang manusia dan mengejar Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan.
short_description.en: Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi is a hairy demon of Georgian mythology and Megrel folk belief, a mountain dweller that attacks people and pursues Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest.

long_description.id: Oçokoçi, juga ditulis Oçi Koçi atau Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), adalah sosok dari mitologi Georgian, terutama di kalangan Mingrelian dan Colchian. Artikel pertama menempatkannya dalam mitologi Gürcü-Megrel-Laz sebagai penghuni gunung, sedangkan artikel kedua mengartikan namanya sebagai manusia-kambing.
long_description.en: Oçokoçi, also written Oçi Koçi or Ochokochi (ოჩოკოჩი), is a figure of Georgian mythology, especially among the Mingrelian and Colchian groups. The first article places it in Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mythology as a dweller of the mountains, while the second renders its name as goat-man.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, ia iblis berwujud manusia yang seluruh tubuhnya ditutupi bulu hitam pekat, bercakar panjang dan tajam. Pada musim dingin ia mendatangi desa dan memangsa anak laki-laki serta anak sapi di kandang. Ia tidak dapat berbicara, tetapi bunyi yang dikeluarkannya tak tertahankan bagi manusia.
long_description.en: In Megrel folk belief it is a demon in human form whose whole body is covered in jet-black hair, with long sharp claws. In winter it comes to the villages and preys on boys and on calves in the barn. It cannot talk, yet the noise it makes is unbearable to people.

long_description.id: Kedua artikel menggambarkan senjatanya secara berbeda. Artikel pertama menyebut ia membawa alat mirip kapak untuk membelah dua para penentangnya; artikel kedua menyebut dadanya bertonjolan berupa tulang runcing atau kapak batu dan ia membunuh orang lewat dengan memeluknya. Oçokoçi yang telah dibunuh pun dikatakan hidup lagi jika ditembak untuk kedua kalinya.
long_description.en: The two articles describe its weapon differently. The first says it carries an axe-like tool with which it splits its opponents in two; the second says its chest bears a protuberance like a pointed bone or stone axe and that it kills passers-by by embracing them. An Oçokoçi that has been killed is even said to come back to life if shot a second time.

long_description.id: Ia tergila-gila pada Tkashi-Mapa, Ratu Hutan, dan terus mengejarnya, tetapi para pemburu yang datang ke hutan sering menggagalkannya. Kajian tentang panteon pagan Megrelian menyebut Ochokochi menempati tempat penting di dalamnya dan, bersama Tkashmapa, tampil di dekat manusia dalam legenda serta memberi keberuntungan berburu.
long_description.en: He is infatuated with Tkashi-Mapa, the Queen of the Forest, and keeps chasing her, but hunters visiting the forest often foil him. A study of the Megrelian pagan pantheon says Ochokochi holds an important place in it and, together with Tkashmapa, appears near people in legends and grants luck in hunting.

short_description.id: Olanoiko zakurra adalah roh anjing abu-abu besar dalam mitologi Basque yang menjaga gua Olanoi di Beizama dan menyerang siapa pun yang mendekat.
short_description.en: Olanoiko zakurra is a big grey dog spirit of Basque mythology that guards the Olanoi cave at Beizama and attacks anyone who approaches.

long_description.id:
Olanoiko zakurra, "anjing Olanoi", adalah roh mitologi Basque berwujud anjing abu-abu besar yang menjaga gua Olanoi di Beizama dan menyerang siapa pun yang mendekat. Ia salah satu dari banyak roh berwujud hewan penghuni gua, seperti Aatxe dan Zezengorri, dan termasuk roh-roh berwujud anjing bersama Zuzidun Txakurra dan Mirokutana.

Artikel berbahasa Basque menyebutnya irelu yang, seperti banyak lainnya, terkait dengan gua. Artikel berbahasa Prancis mencatat bahwa roh-roh anjing ini berbeda kekuatannya menurut tempat dan legenda, dan bahwa anjing masuk ke dalam mitologi Basque terutama sejak datangnya agama Kristen.
long_description.en:
Olanoiko zakurra, 'the dog of Olanoi', is a Basque spirit in the form of a big grey dog that guards the Olanoi cave at Beizama and attacks anyone approaching. It is one of many animal-shaped cave spirits, like Aatxe and Zezengorri, and one of the dog-shaped spirits along with Zuzidun Txakurra and Mirokutana.

The Basque article calls it an irelu linked to caves like many others. The French article notes that these dog spirits differ in their powers by place and legend, and that dogs entered Basque mythology especially since the advent of Christianity.

short_description.id: Olokun adalah dewa Afrika Barat yang berkaitan dengan laut dan perairan, kekayaan, serta kesuburan, dan dipuja oleh orang Yoruba, Edo, dan bangsa-bangsa tetangga hingga ke diaspora.
short_description.en: Olokun is a West African deity of the sea and other waters, of riches and of fertility, honoured by the Yoruba, Edo and neighbouring peoples and in the diaspora.

long_description.id:
Olokun adalah dewa Afrika Barat yang berhubungan dengan laut serta perairan lain, kekayaan, dan kesuburan. Pemujaannya tercatat di kalangan Yoruba, Edo, Esan, dan Urhobo, juga di sebagian komunitas Igbo barat dan Ijaw pesisir, dengan nama lokal seperti Onoku atau Onokun. Tergantung tradisinya, Olokun bisa digambarkan sebagai perempuan, laki-laki, atau androgini.

Dalam satu kisah Yoruba dari Ile-Ife, Olokun adalah istri Oduduwa yang menjadi laut setelah meninggalkannya. Dalam tradisi Edo di Kerajaan Benin, Olokun adalah putra sulung Osanobua dan dewa laut, anak, serta kekayaan. Tradisi lisan Benin juga menceritakan pertempuran antara Olokun dan Oba yang berakhir dengan harta Olokun dilucuti.

Pemujaannya beragam menurut daerah. Perempuan Esan memujanya untuk kesuburan dan kekayaan, dengan upacara empat belas hari tarian dan kadang trans kerasukan. Di kalangan Itsekiri seekor ikan kecil bernama ogiden dianggap utusannya, dan di Ogulaha para pemuja mengadakan festival tahunan di tepi Samudra Atlantik untuk menangkal banjir.

Olokun juga dihormati dalam Santería dan Candomblé. Dalam Santería ia dikaitkan dengan kedalaman samudra dan kekayaan tersembunyinya, dan sebagian pemuja menganggap Olokun dan Yemayá aspek dari orisha yang sama. Artikel ketiga menyebut Obbatalá merantainya di dasar samudra setelah ia mencoba membinasakan manusia dengan air bah, dan kadang ia digambarkan setengah manusia, setengah ikan.

Asal-usul historis pemujaan Olokun belum pasti. Ben-Amos berpendapat bahwa nama Olokun mungkin berasal dari Yoruba, sedangkan sumber kedua menyebutnya dewi sungai yang memberi kekayaan dan anak, dengan pemujaan yang umum di Nigeria selatan.
long_description.en:
Olokun is a West African god of the sea and other waters, of wealth and of fertility. Worship of Olokun is recorded among the Yoruba, Edo, Esan and Urhobo, and in some western Igbo and coastal Ijaw communities, under local names such as Onoku or Onokun. Traditions differ on whether Olokun is female, male or androgynous.

One Yoruba account from Ile-Ife makes Olokun the wife of Oduduwa, who turned into the sea after leaving him. In Edo tradition of the Benin Kingdom, Olokun is the senior son of Osanobua and god of the sea, of children and of wealth. Benin oral tradition also tells of a battle between Olokun and the Oba that ended with Olokun stripped of possessions.

Its worship varies by region. Esan women sought fertility and wealth from the deity in ceremonies with fourteen days of dancing and occasional possession trances. The Itsekiri regarded a small fish called ogiden as its messenger, and at Ogulaha devotees hold a yearly festival on the Atlantic Ocean shore to keep floods away.

Olokun is honoured in Santería and Candomblé as well. Santería links the deity with the ocean depths and their hidden treasures, and some devotees treat Olokun and Yemayá as aspects of one orisha. The third article says Obbatalá chained Olokun to the sea floor after a failed attempt to drown humanity in a flood, and that Olokun is sometimes shown as half man, half fish.

The historical roots of Olokun worship are unclear. Ben-Amos proposes that the name Olokun may be Yoruba, while the second source describes a river goddess who grants riches and children, worshipped widely across southern Nigeria.
