short_description.id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan.
short_description.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.

long_description.id:
Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan. Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin. Ia juga disebut 水精將軍 dan, dalam arak-arakan, tampil sebagai salah satu dari dua jenderal pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu.

Shunfeng Er dan Shen Feng Er merupakan ejaan lain namanya. Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Shi Kuang. Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi telinga Kaisar Giok. Pendengarannya dipakai membantu pelaut membedakan angin baik dari badai, dan dalam sebagian kisah ia dipuja sebagai saksi sumpah dan kontrak.

Ia paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan oleh Mazu. Menurut satu kisah, selendang sakti Mazu meniupkan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; menurut kisah lain, ia dan Qianliyan adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming yang menghantui Gunung Peach Blossom; dan sebuah arsip budaya menyebut keduanya semula siluman di gunung itu yang ditaklukkan Mazu. Dalam seni ia biasanya digambarkan berkulit merah atau cokelat dengan tangan di telinga, dan 順風耳 di kuil Mazu memegang senjata di tangan yang lain.

Sebuah teks klasik menyebut kedua makhluk itu semula roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan yang meminjam daya gaib utusan tanah liat di kuil Xuanyuan; telinganya dapat mendengar seribu li tetapi tidak lebih jauh, dan daya itu dapat diputus dengan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liatnya serta akar persik dan willow.
long_description.en:
Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan. His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind. He is also called 水精將軍 and, in processions, appears as one of the two generals protecting Mazu on her left and right.

Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er are alternative spellings of his name. In the Ming period, he was also known as Shi Kuang. Journey to the West presents him as the personified ears of the Jade Emperor. His hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from storms, and in some accounts he is worshipped as a witness to oaths and contracts.

He is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed by Mazu. By one account, Mazu's magical scarf blew sand into their ears and eyes; by another, he and Qianliyan were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming who haunted Peach Blossom Mountain; and a cultural archive says the two were originally spirit-monsters on that mountain subdued by Mazu. In art he typically appears red- or brown-skinned with a hand at his ear, and in Mazu temples 順風耳 holds a weapon in his other hand.

A classical text says the two beings were originally the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan who borrowed the power of clay attendants in the Xuanyuan temple; the ears can hear a thousand li but no farther, and the power can be cut by destroying the clay bodies and the peach and willow roots.

claims_provenance.quote: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears. He also occasionally appears with three heads and six arms.

claim.id: Dalam mitos rakyat, dua dewa pengawal yang mengawasi dan mendengar urusan dunia bagi Mazu (媽祖) adalah 千里眼 (juga disebut 金精將軍) dan 順風耳 (juga disebut 水精將軍).
claim.en: In folk myth, the two guardian gods who observe and listen to the affairs of the world for Mazu (媽祖) are 千里眼 (also called 金精將軍) and 順風耳 (also called 水精將軍).

claims_provenance.quote: 在民間的神話傳說中，替媽祖察聽世情的兩大駕前護衛神分別為千里眼（又稱金精將軍）與順風耳（又稱水精將軍）。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 國家文化記憶庫 (National Cultural Memory Bank, Taiwan) — 千里眼、順風耳 - 國家文化記憶庫

claim.id: Di kuil Mazu (媽祖), 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berdiri di kiri dan kanan Mazu; 順風耳 mengangkat tangan ke samping telinga dalam sikap mendengar, memakai pendengarannya yang tak terbatas untuk menyelidiki segala hal di dunia bagi Mazu, dan tangan yang lain memegang senjata.
claim.en: In Mazu (媽祖) temples, 千里眼 and 順風耳 stand on Mazu's left and right; 順風耳 raises a hand to his ear in a listening pose, using his boundless hearing to scout everything in the world for Mazu, and the other hand holds a weapon.

claims_provenance.quote: 在媽祖廟裡，千里眼和順風耳分別站立於媽祖的左右兩側 ... 而順風耳則手舉至側耳做聽音狀的姿態，以其無遠弗屆的聽力，為媽祖偵聽世上的一切事物。祂們的另一手則持有兵器。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 國家文化記憶庫 (National Cultural Memory Bank, Taiwan) — 千里眼、順風耳 - 國家文化記憶庫

claim.id: Legenda tentang 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berbeda-beda, tetapi pada umumnya keduanya semula adalah siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom (桃花山) yang berwajah garang, menakuti penduduk, dan sering mengganggu daerah itu serta merugikan rakyat, hingga akhirnya ditaklukkan Mazu (媽祖) dan menjadi jenderal pengiringnya.
claim.en: Legends about 千里眼 and 順風耳 differ, but generally they were originally spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain (桃花山) with fierce faces who frightened residents and often disturbed the area and harmed the people, until Mazu (媽祖) subdued them and they became her attendant generals.

claims_provenance.quote: 關於千里眼和順風耳的傳說不一，總的來說，祂們原來是在桃花山上的妖精，不僅面貌猙獰，使居民恐懼外，更時常擾亂地方、為害百姓。最後為媽祖收伏，成為隨駕將軍。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 國家文化記憶庫 (National Cultural Memory Bank, Taiwan) — 千里眼、順風耳 - 國家文化記憶庫

claim.id: Dalam arak-arakan Mazu (媽祖), selain tandu Mazu selalu tampak dua jenderal besar, satu hijau dan satu merah, yaitu pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu: 千里眼 dan 順風耳.
claim.en: In Mazu (媽祖) processions, besides Mazu's palanquin one always sees two great generals, one green and one red, who are Mazu's left and right protectors, 千里眼 and 順風耳.

claims_provenance.quote: 在媽祖出巡的陣頭中，除了媽祖鑾轎外，我們總會看見一綠一紅的大將軍，這就是媽祖的左右護法──千里眼和順風耳。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 國家文化記憶庫 (National Cultural Memory Bank, Taiwan) — 千里眼、順風耳 - 國家文化記憶庫

claim.id: Dalam teks klasik ini disebut bahwa makhluk jahat itu adalah roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan (棋盤山), dan di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) di sana ada utusan hantu dari tanah liat bernama 千里眼 dan 順風耳; kedua siluman itu meminjam daya gaibnya sehingga mata dapat melihat seribu li dan telinga dapat mendengar seribu li, tetapi tidak dapat melihat atau mendengar melampaui seribu li.
claim.en: This classical text says the evil creature is the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan (棋盤山), and that in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) there are clay ghost attendants named 千里眼 and 順風耳; the two monsters borrow their spiritual power so that the eyes can see a thousand li and the ears can hear a thousand li, but they cannot see or hear beyond a thousand li.

claims_provenance.quote: 此業障是棋盤山桃精、柳鬼 ... 今棋盤山有軒轅廟，廟內有泥塑鬼使，名曰千里眼，順風耳；二怪托其靈氣，目能觀看千里，耳能詳聽千里；千里之外，不能視聽也。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (维基文库) — 封神演義/卷090

claim.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) disarankan mengirim orang ke Gunung Qipan (棋盤山) untuk menggali akar persik dan willow lalu membakarnya, dan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liat kedua hantu di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) guna memutus akar daya gaib mereka.
claim.en: In this classical text, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) is advised to send people to Mount Qipan (棋盤山) to dig up and burn the peach and willow roots and to smash the clay bodies of the two ghosts in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) in order to cut the root of their spiritual power.

claims_provenance.quote: 你可叫姜子牙著人往棋盤山去，將桃、柳根盤掘挖，用火焚盡；將軒轅廟二鬼泥身打碎，以絕其靈氣之根
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (维基文库) — 封神演義/卷090

His hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from storms, and in some accounts he is worshipped as a witness to oaths and contracts.

long_description.id: Ia paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan oleh Mazu. Menurut satu kisah, selendang sakti Mazu meniupkan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; menurut kisah lain, ia dan Qianliyan adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming yang menghantui Gunung Peach Blossom; dan sebuah arsip budaya menyebut keduanya semula siluman di gunung itu yang ditaklukkan Mazu. Dalam seni ia biasanya digambarkan berkulit merah atau cokelat dengan tangan di telinga, dan 順風耳 di kuil Mazu memegang senjata di tangan yang lain.
long_description.en: He is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed by Mazu. By one account, Mazu's magical scarf blew sand into their ears and eyes; by another, he and Qianliyan were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming who haunted Peach Blossom Mountain; and a cultural archive says the two were originally spirit-monsters on that mountain subdued by Mazu. In art he typically appears red- or brown-skinned with a hand at his ear, and in Mazu temples 順風耳 holds a weapon in his other hand.

long_description.id: Sebuah teks klasik menyebut kedua makhluk itu semula roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan yang meminjam daya gaib utusan tanah liat di kuil Xuanyuan; telinganya dapat mendengar seribu li tetapi tidak lebih jauh, dan daya itu dapat diputus dengan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liatnya serta akar persik dan willow.
long_description.en: A classical text says the two beings were originally the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan who borrowed the power of clay attendants in the Xuanyuan temple; the ears can hear a thousand li but no farther, and the power can be cut by destroying the clay bodies and the peach and willow roots.

description.id: Mampu mendengar suara yang dibawa angin dan, dalam sebagian kisah, segala sesuatu di dunia sepelan apa pun.
description.en: Able to hear any sound carried on the wind and, in some accounts, everything in the world however quietly spoken.

description.id: Pendengarannya dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai.
description.en: His hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from storms.

description.id: Menurut satu kisah, selendang sakti Mazu meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka sehingga mereka kalah.
description.en: By one account, Mazu's magical scarf blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes and defeated them.

name.id: Tubuh tanah liat dan akar persik-willow

description.id: Dalam teks klasik, daya gaib mereka dikatakan bergantung pada tubuh tanah liat di kuil dan akar persik serta willow, yang dapat dihancurkan untuk memutusnya.
description.en: In the classical text their spiritual power is said to rest on the clay bodies in the temple and on peach and willow roots, which can be destroyed to cut it.

summary.en: In one version the two are the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and haunted it as demons.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god. He usually appears with Qianliyan as a guardian of the temples of the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Qianliyan.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.

claims.quote: The name "Shunfeng'er" literally means "Wind Accompanying Ears" in reference to his ability to hear any sound carried upon the wind.

statement.id: Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin.
statement.en: His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind.

claims.quote: It also appears as Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er. His partner Qianliyan's name similarly means "Sharp-Eyed" or "All-Seeing".

statement.id: Shunfeng Er dan Shen Feng Er merupakan ejaan lain namanya.
statement.en: Shunfeng Er and Shen Feng Er are alternative spellings of his name.

claims.quote: Under the Ming, Shunfeng'er was also known as Shi Kuang. He is also sometimes known as Wanli'er, which has similar meaning, as the Chinese word wàn—like the English "myriad"—simultaneously means the number 10,000 and "innumerable" or "uncountably vast".

statement.id: Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Shi Kuang.
statement.en: In the Ming period, he was also known as Shi Kuang.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is first attested in the early-16th century novel Journey to the West, where he appears as the personified form of the Taoist Jade Emperor's ears and one of his lieutenants. There is, however, an earlier depiction of him in a Sichuan cave which has been dated to the Southern Song.

statement.id: Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi telinga Kaisar Giok.
statement.en: Journey to the West presents him as the personified ears of the Jade Emperor.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is employed to help sailors distinguish favorable winds from coming storms. In some accounts, he is capable of hearing everything in the world, no matter how quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

statement.id: Pendengaran Shunfeng'er yang tajam dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai yang akan datang; dalam sebagian kisah ia mampu mendengar segalanya di dunia, sepelan apa pun, sehingga juga dipuja sebagai saksi dan penjamin sumpah dan kontrak.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from coming storms; in some accounts he can hear everything in the world however quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan atau diajak berteman oleh dewi laut Mazu.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.quote: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes. After their submission, they pledged their loyalty when she kindly healed them of the damage she had caused them.

statement.id: Menurut satu kisah, ia dan Qianliyan muncul di lepas pantai Pulau Meizhou saat badai dan dikalahkan oleh selendang sutra sakti Mazu yang meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; setelah tunduk, mereka berjanji setia ketika Mazu menyembuhkan luka yang ditimbulkannya.
statement.en: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes; after submitting they pledged loyalty when she healed the damage she had caused.

claims.quote: In another, the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming. Ruthless generals, they fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.

statement.id: Dalam kisah lain, keduanya adalah saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming, jenderal kejam yang gugur di Gunung Peach Blossom dan kemudian menghantuinya sebagai iblis.
statement.en: In another account the two were the brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain and subsequently haunted it as demons.

claims.quote: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears. He also occasionally appears with three heads and six arms.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er biasanya digambarkan sebagai iblis berkulit merah atau cokelat yang menangkupkan tangan ke salah satu telinganya, dan kadang-kadang bertiga kepala dan berlengan enam.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears, and occasionally with three heads and six arms.

claims.quote: 在民間的神話傳說中，替媽祖察聽世情的兩大駕前護衛神分別為千里眼（又稱金精將軍）與順風耳（又稱水精將軍）。

statement.id: Dalam mitos rakyat, dua dewa pengawal yang mengawasi dan mendengar urusan dunia bagi Mazu (媽祖) adalah 千里眼 (juga disebut 金精將軍) dan 順風耳 (juga disebut 水精將軍).
statement.en: In folk myth, the two guardian gods who observe and listen to the affairs of the world for Mazu (媽祖) are 千里眼 (also called 金精將軍) and 順風耳 (also called 水精將軍).

claims.quote: 在媽祖廟裡，千里眼和順風耳分別站立於媽祖的左右兩側 ... 而順風耳則手舉至側耳做聽音狀的姿態，以其無遠弗屆的聽力，為媽祖偵聽世上的一切事物。祂們的另一手則持有兵器。

statement.id: Di kuil Mazu (媽祖), 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berdiri di kiri dan kanan Mazu; 順風耳 mengangkat tangan ke samping telinga dalam sikap mendengar, memakai pendengarannya yang tak terbatas untuk menyelidiki segala hal di dunia bagi Mazu, dan tangan yang lain memegang senjata.
statement.en: In Mazu (媽祖) temples, 千里眼 and 順風耳 stand on Mazu's left and right; 順風耳 raises a hand to his ear in a listening pose, using his boundless hearing to scout everything in the world for Mazu, and the other hand holds a weapon.

claims.quote: 關於千里眼和順風耳的傳說不一，總的來說，祂們原來是在桃花山上的妖精，不僅面貌猙獰，使居民恐懼外，更時常擾亂地方、為害百姓。最後為媽祖收伏，成為隨駕將軍。

statement.id: Legenda tentang 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berbeda-beda, tetapi pada umumnya keduanya semula adalah siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom (桃花山) yang berwajah garang, menakuti penduduk, dan sering mengganggu daerah itu serta merugikan rakyat, hingga akhirnya ditaklukkan Mazu (媽祖) dan menjadi jenderal pengiringnya.
statement.en: Legends about 千里眼 and 順風耳 differ, but generally they were originally spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain (桃花山) with fierce faces who frightened residents and often disturbed the area and harmed the people, until Mazu (媽祖) subdued them and they became her attendant generals.

claims.quote: 在媽祖出巡的陣頭中，除了媽祖鑾轎外，我們總會看見一綠一紅的大將軍，這就是媽祖的左右護法──千里眼和順風耳。

statement.id: Dalam arak-arakan Mazu (媽祖), selain tandu Mazu selalu tampak dua jenderal besar, satu hijau dan satu merah, yaitu pelindung kiri dan kanan Mazu: 千里眼 dan 順風耳.
statement.en: In Mazu (媽祖) processions, besides Mazu's palanquin one always sees two great generals, one green and one red, who are Mazu's left and right protectors, 千里眼 and 順風耳.

claims.quote: 此業障是棋盤山桃精、柳鬼 ... 今棋盤山有軒轅廟，廟內有泥塑鬼使，名曰千里眼，順風耳；二怪托其靈氣，目能觀看千里，耳能詳聽千里；千里之外，不能視聽也。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini disebut bahwa makhluk jahat itu adalah roh persik dan hantu willow dari Gunung Qipan (棋盤山), dan di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) di sana ada utusan hantu dari tanah liat bernama 千里眼 dan 順風耳; kedua siluman itu meminjam daya gaibnya sehingga mata dapat melihat seribu li dan telinga dapat mendengar seribu li, tetapi tidak dapat melihat atau mendengar melampaui seribu li.
statement.en: This classical text says the evil creature is the peach spirit and willow ghost of Mount Qipan (棋盤山), and that in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) there are clay ghost attendants named 千里眼 and 順風耳; the two monsters borrow their spiritual power so that the eyes can see a thousand li and the ears can hear a thousand li, but they cannot see or hear beyond a thousand li.

claims.quote: 你可叫姜子牙著人往棋盤山去，將桃、柳根盤掘挖，用火焚盡；將軒轅廟二鬼泥身打碎，以絕其靈氣之根

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) disarankan mengirim orang ke Gunung Qipan (棋盤山) untuk menggali akar persik dan willow lalu membakarnya, dan menghancurkan tubuh tanah liat kedua hantu di kuil Xuanyuan (軒轅廟) guna memutus akar daya gaib mereka.
statement.en: In this classical text, Jiang Ziya (姜子牙) is advised to send people to Mount Qipan (棋盤山) to dig up and burn the peach and willow roots and to smash the clay bodies of the two ghosts in the Xuanyuan temple (軒轅廟) in order to cut the root of their spiritual power.

summary.id: Saudara Gao Jue dan Gao Ming, jenderal kejam yang gugur di Gunung Peach Blossom.
summary.en: The brothers Gao Jue and Gao Ming, ruthless generals who fell at Peach Blossom Mountain.

summary.id: Siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom yang menakuti penduduk.
summary.en: Spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain who frightened residents.

short_description.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang bersarang di Gunung Ōe dan dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō setelah dibuat mabuk dengan sake pemberian dewa.
short_description.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend who dwelt on Mount Ōe and was killed by Minamoto no Raikō after being made drunk with sake given by a deity.

long_description.id:
Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō. Kamus Daijisen menyebutnya pemimpin oni legendaris yang tinggal di Ōeyama dan merampas perempuan serta harta di ibu kota sehingga diburu atas titah kaisar. Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang hilang di Kyoto, terutama perempuan muda.

Menurut versi Ōeyama Ekotoba, saat tidur ia kembali ke wujud aslinya yang setinggi 50 kaki, bertubuh merah, berkepala bertanduk lima, dan bermata lima belas. Dalam versi tertua itu, Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian salah satu dewa sehingga ia tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, sake dan helm diberikan oleh tiga dewa yang menjelma sebagai orang tua. Salah satu kisah menyebut kepalanya yang terpenggal masih menggigit Raikō.

Sarangnya ditempatkan di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi. Ensiklopedia Heibonsha mencatat bahwa Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka dekat ibu kota, dan menafsirkan gagasan oni yang bersembunyi di sana dengan latar tempat itu sebagai batas antara ibu kota dan dunia luar. Nama Shuten-dōji menurut Ōeyama Ekotoba berasal dari kegemarannya pada sake.

Teks tertua legenda ini, Ōeyama Ekotoba dari abad ke-14, adalah gulungan bergambar yang disimpan di Itsuō Art Museum.
long_description.en:
Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend, killed by Minamoto no Raikō. The Daijisen dictionary calls him a legendary oni leader living on Ōeyama who plundered women and treasure in the capital and was hunted under imperial command. In the oldest version, many people go missing in Kyoto, most of them young women.

According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, when asleep he returned to his true form, 50 feet tall, with a red body, a five-horned head and fifteen eyes. In that oldest version Raikō offers sake given by one of the deities, which leaves him incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version the sake and a helmet are given by three gods who appear as old men. One story says his severed head still bit at Raikō.

His lair is placed on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version. The Heibonsha encyclopedia notes that Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital, and interprets the idea of an oni holed up there against the background of that place being a boundary between the capital and the outside world. According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba his name comes from his love of sake.

The oldest text of the legend, the fourteenth-century Ōeyama Ekotoba, is a picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

literal_meaning.id: "anak laki-laki peminum sake"; dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, nama ini berarti orang yang sangat menyukai sake
literal_meaning.en: "sake-drinking lad"; in the Ōeyama Ekotoba the name refers to someone who deeply loves sake

description.id: Dalam versi tertua, sake pemberian salah satu dewa yang ditawarkan Raikō membuat Shuten-dōji tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, Raikō menerima sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang dari para dewa.
description.en: In the oldest version the sake given by a deity and offered by Raikō leaves Shuten-dōji incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version Raikō receives the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet from the gods.

role.id: Pemimpin oni yang menculik orang di ibu kota dan akhirnya dipenggal Raikō.
role.en: The oni leader behind the abductions in the capital, who is finally beheaded by Raikō.

summary.id: Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang, terutama perempuan muda, hilang di Kyoto. Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian dewa kepada Shuten-dōji hingga ia tak berdaya, lalu memenggalnya; kepala yang terpenggal masih menggigit, tetapi Raikō selamat karena memakai beberapa helm.
summary.en: In the oldest version many people, mostly young women, go missing in Kyoto. Raikō offers Shuten-dōji sake given by a deity until he is incapacitated, then beheads him; the severed head still bites, but Raikō survives by wearing several helmets.

role.id: Oni yang dihadapi Raikō dengan bantuan tiga dewa.
role.en: The oni whom Raikō confronts with the help of three gods.

summary.id: Raikō dibantu tiga dewa, yang memberinya sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang. Kepala Shuten-dōji yang terpenggal melayang ke langit dan mengincar Raikō, tetapi Raikō terlindung helm bintang.
summary.en: Raikō is helped by three gods who give him the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet. Shuten-dōji's severed head flies into the sky and aims at Raikō, who is protected by the star helmet.

description.id: Sarang Shuten-dōji di barat laut Kyoto, atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi.
description.en: Shuten-dōji's lair northwest of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

description.id: Menurut Heibonsha, Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka yang dekat ibu kota.
description.en: According to the Heibonsha encyclopedia, Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital.

description.id: Legenda tercatat dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, gulungan bergambar abad ke-14 yang disimpan di Itsuō Art Museum.
description.en: The legend is recorded in the Ōeyama Ekotoba, a fourteenth-century picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

note.id: Menurut legenda, Raikō membunuh Shuten-dōji.
note.en: According to legend, Raikō killed Shuten-dōji.

summary.id: Wikipedia: Gunung Ōe di barat laut Kyoto atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi.
summary.en: Wikipedia: Mount Ōe northwest of Kyoto or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

summary.id: Ensiklopedia Heibonsha: semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka; Ōeyama di Tanba/Tango dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, dan Gunung Ibuki di Ōmi dalam Shuten-dōji Emaki.
summary.en: Heibonsha encyclopedia: apparently originally Oi-no-saka; Ōeyama in Tanba/Tango in the Ōeyama Ekotoba and Mount Ibuki in Ōmi in the Shuten-dōji Emaki.

claim.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni yang dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō dalam legenda Jepang.
claim.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader killed by Minamoto no Raikō in Japanese legend.

claims_provenance.quote: Shuten-dōji (酒呑童子, also sometimes called 酒顛童子, 酒天童子, or 朱点童子) is a mythical oni or demon leader of Japan, who according to legend was killed by the hero Minamoto no Raikō.

claim.id: Salah satu kisah menyebut kepalanya yang terpenggal masih menggigit Raikō.
claim.en: One story says his severed head still bit at Raikō.

claims_provenance.quote: Although decapitated, the demon's detached head still took a bite at the hero, who avoided death by wearing multiple helmets stacked on his head.

claim.id: Berbagai versi menempatkan sarangnya di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki.
claim.en: Accounts place his dwelling on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki.

claims_provenance.quote: Shuten-dōji had his lair at Mount Ōe (大江山) northwest of the city of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

claim.id: Naskah Ōeyama Ekotoba dari abad ke-14 menyimpan versi awal legenda itu.

short_description.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang bersarang di Gunung Ōe dan dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō setelah dibuat mabuk dengan sake pemberian dewa.
short_description.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend who dwelt on Mount Ōe and was killed by Minamoto no Raikō after being made drunk with sake given by a deity.

long_description.id: Shuten-dōji adalah pemimpin oni dalam legenda Jepang yang dibunuh Minamoto no Raikō. Kamus Daijisen menyebutnya pemimpin oni legendaris yang tinggal di Ōeyama dan merampas perempuan serta harta di ibu kota sehingga diburu atas titah kaisar. Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang hilang di Kyoto, terutama perempuan muda.
long_description.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader in Japanese legend, killed by Minamoto no Raikō. The Daijisen dictionary calls him a legendary oni leader living on Ōeyama who plundered women and treasure in the capital and was hunted under imperial command. In the oldest version, many people go missing in Kyoto, most of them young women.

long_description.id: Menurut versi Ōeyama Ekotoba, saat tidur ia kembali ke wujud aslinya yang setinggi 50 kaki, bertubuh merah, berkepala bertanduk lima, dan bermata lima belas. Dalam versi tertua itu, Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian salah satu dewa sehingga ia tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, sake dan helm diberikan oleh tiga dewa yang menjelma sebagai orang tua. Salah satu kisah menyebut kepalanya yang terpenggal masih menggigit Raikō.
long_description.en: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, when asleep he returned to his true form, 50 feet tall, with a red body, a five-horned head and fifteen eyes. In that oldest version Raikō offers sake given by one of the deities, which leaves him incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version the sake and a helmet are given by three gods who appear as old men. One story says his severed head still bit at Raikō.

long_description.id: Sarangnya ditempatkan di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi. Ensiklopedia Heibonsha mencatat bahwa Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka dekat ibu kota, dan menafsirkan gagasan oni yang bersembunyi di sana dengan latar tempat itu sebagai batas antara ibu kota dan dunia luar. Nama Shuten-dōji menurut Ōeyama Ekotoba berasal dari kegemarannya pada sake.
long_description.en: His lair is placed on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version. The Heibonsha encyclopedia notes that Ōeyama was apparently originally Oi-no-saka near the capital, and interprets the idea of an oni holed up there against the background of that place being a boundary between the capital and the outside world. According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba his name comes from his love of sake.

long_description.id: Teks tertua legenda ini, Ōeyama Ekotoba dari abad ke-14, adalah gulungan bergambar yang disimpan di Itsuō Art Museum.
long_description.en: The oldest text of the legend, the fourteenth-century Ōeyama Ekotoba, is a picture scroll held by the Itsuō Art Museum.

literal_meaning.id: "anak laki-laki peminum sake"; dalam Ōeyama Ekotoba, nama ini berarti orang yang sangat menyukai sake
literal_meaning.en: "sake-drinking lad"; in the Ōeyama Ekotoba the name refers to someone who deeply loves sake

description.id: Dalam versi tertua, sake pemberian salah satu dewa yang ditawarkan Raikō membuat Shuten-dōji tak berdaya; dalam versi Otogi-zōshi, Raikō menerima sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang dari para dewa.
description.en: In the oldest version the sake given by a deity and offered by Raikō leaves Shuten-dōji incapacitated; in the Otogi-zōshi version Raikō receives the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet from the gods.

role.id: Pemimpin oni yang menculik orang di ibu kota dan akhirnya dipenggal Raikō.
role.en: The oni leader behind the abductions in the capital, who is finally beheaded by Raikō.

summary.id: Dalam versi tertua, banyak orang, terutama perempuan muda, hilang di Kyoto. Raikō menawarkan sake pemberian dewa kepada Shuten-dōji hingga ia tak berdaya, lalu memenggalnya; kepala yang terpenggal masih menggigit, tetapi Raikō selamat karena memakai beberapa helm.
summary.en: In the oldest version many people, mostly young women, go missing in Kyoto. Raikō offers Shuten-dōji sake given by a deity until he is incapacitated, then beheads him; the severed head still bites, but Raikō survives by wearing several helmets.

role.id: Oni yang dihadapi Raikō dengan bantuan tiga dewa.
role.en: The oni whom Raikō confronts with the help of three gods.

summary.id: Raikō dibantu tiga dewa, yang memberinya sake jinben kidoku dan helm bintang. Kepala Shuten-dōji yang terpenggal melayang ke langit dan mengincar Raikō, tetapi Raikō terlindung helm bintang.
summary.en: Raikō is helped by three gods who give him the Jinben kidoku sake and a star helmet. Shuten-dōji's severed head flies into the sky and aims at Raikō, who is protected by the star helmet.

description.id: Sarang Shuten-dōji di barat laut Kyoto, atau Gunung Ibuki, tergantung versi.
description.en: Shuten-dōji's lair northwest of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

description.id: Menurut Heibonsha, Ōeyama semula tampaknya Oi-no-saka yang dekat ibu kota.

short_description.id: Suijin atau Mizugami adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang, pelindung air tawar, nelayan, dan petani sawah, yang dipuja di kuil dan di tepi mata air.
short_description.en: Suijin, also called Mizugami, is the umbrella name for the Japanese water deity, a protector of fresh water, fishermen and rice farmers who is honoured at shrines and beside springs.

long_description.id:
Suijin atau Mizugami ("dewa air") adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang. Istilah ini merujuk pada perwujudan surgawi dan duniawi dewa air Shinto yang baik hati, terutama air tawar, serta beragam makhluk gaib di danau, kolam, mata air, dan sumur, termasuk ular, naga, belut, ikan, kura-kura, dan kappa pemakan daging. Ia sering dikacaukan dengan Ryūjin dan juga dikenal sebagai Suiten atau Suiō.

Dewa air Shinto dipercaya sebagai pelindung nelayan serta pelindung kesuburan, keibuan, dan persalinan tanpa rasa sakit. Orang memujanya dengan persembahan demi air yang bersih untuk minum, pertanian, dan sanitasi. Menurut ensiklopedia Jepang, bentuk yang paling khas adalah pelindung petani sawah yang membawa kesuburan dan dipuja di bendungan atau kuil batu di tepi sawah; di sumber air pegunungan ia disamakan dengan dewa gunung.

Lambang khas dewa air adalah kappa, dan dewa air dipercaya juga berwujud naga, ular, belut, monyet, atau laba-laba. Dewa air sering digambarkan sebagai dewi, yaitu ibu yang memiliki anak kecil. Suijin juga tampil sebagai lempeng batu atau batu kecil yang ditegakkan di dekat mata air, dan terus dimuliakan serta memengaruhi budaya Jepang.
long_description.en:
Suijin or Mizugami ("water god") serves as the umbrella name for the Japanese water deity in myth. It covers the heavenly and earthly forms of Shinto's kindly water divinity, chiefly of freshwater, as well as many legendary beings living in lakes, ponds, springs and wells, among them serpents, dragons, eels, fish, turtles and the flesh-eating kappa. It is often conflated with Ryūjin and is also known as Suiten or Suiō.

Believers hold that Shinto's water deity watches over fishermen and over fertility, motherhood and painless childbirth. People worship it with offerings for clean water for drinking, agriculture and sanitation. According to a Japanese encyclopedia, its most typical form is the guardian of rice-paddy farmers that brings fertility and is enshrined at irrigation weirs or stone shrines beside paddies; at mountain water sources it is identified with the mountain deity.

The typical emblem of the water deity is the kappa, and the water deity is believed also to take the form of a dragon, snake, eel, monkey or spider. The water deity is often represented as a goddess, a mother with a young child. Suijin also appears as a stone plaque or small upright stone near a spring, and continues to be revered and to influence Japanese culture.

short_description.id: Tezcatlipoca ('Cermin Berasap') adalah dewa penting bangsa Aztec dan Toltec: dewa pencipta dan pelindung prajurit yang membawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan, dikaitkan dengan langit malam, badai, obsidian, dan konflik.
short_description.en: Tezcatlipoca ('Smoking Mirror') is an important god of the Aztecs and Toltecs: a creator god and patron of warriors who brings both good and evil, associated with the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

long_description.id:
Tezcatlipoca adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik, terutama bagi bangsa Toltec dan Aztec. Ia dipandang sebagai dewa pencipta yang tak terlihat dan mahakuasa serta pelindung prajurit, dan sebagai pembawa kebaikan sekaligus kejahatan ia adalah perwujudan perubahan melalui konflik. Ia dikaitkan dengan langit malam, badai topan, obsidian, dan konflik.

Ia dianggap salah satu dari empat putra Ometecuhtli dan Omecihuatl, dewa ganda purba, dan dalam mitologi Aztec saudara Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli, dan Xipe Totec. Dalam mitos penciptaan ia menguasai dunia pertama Matahari lalu digulingkan Quetzalcóatl, dan keduanya kemudian bekerja sama menciptakan Matahari ke-5. Nagual atau roh hewannya adalah jaguar, dan ia dikaitkan dengan burung hantu bertanduk dalam kalender.

Ia dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan, dan dalam wujud yang lebih suram dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran. Sebagai pelindung prajurit ia tidak selalu melindungi mereka: kadang ia menunggu di persimpangan jalan tengah malam untuk menantang prajurit yang lengah.

Perayaan utamanya adalah Toxcatl yang, seperti kebanyakan perayaan keagamaan Aztec, melibatkan pengorbanan manusia. Seorang peniru sang dewa, paling sering tawanan perang yang paling tampan dan berani, menikahi empat dewi secara simbolis lalu dikorbankan dengan pisau obsidian. Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan ia memiliki cermin obsidian hitam sebagai pengganti kaki kirinya, merujuk pada luka dalam pertempurannya dengan Tlaltecuhtli.
long_description.en:
Tezcatlipoca was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture, particularly for the Toltecs and the Aztecs. He was regarded as an invisible and omnipotent creator god and patron of warriors, and because he brought both good and evil he embodied change through conflict. He is associated with the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

He was counted among the four sons of Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, the primordial dual deity, and in Aztec mythology was brother to Quetzalcoatl, Huizilopochtli and Xipe Totec. In the creation myth he ruled the first world of the Sun and was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl, and the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun. His nagual or animal counterpart was the jaguar, and he is associated with the horned owl in the calendar.

He could step directly into human affairs, bringing joy or grief, and in a darker guise was called lord of the shadows or night, a black-magic sorcerer who brought evil, death and destruction. As patron of warriors he was not always protective of them: sometimes he waited at crossroads at the dead of night to challenge unsuspecting warriors.

His chief festival was Toxcatl, which, like most Aztec religious festivals, included human sacrifice. An impersonator of the god, most often the best looking and most courageous prisoner of war, symbolically married four goddesses and was then sacrificed with an obsidian knife. In later depictions he has a black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, referring to a wound in his battle with Tlaltecuhtli.

claim.id: Dalam mitos penciptaan Mesoamerika dan Aztec, Tezcatlipoca menguasai dunia pertama Matahari tetapi digulingkan Quetzalcóatl. claim.en: In the Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was overthrown by Quetzalcóatl; the two later cooperated to create the 5th Sun and, transformed into giant snakes, attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli).

claims_provenance.quote: In the complex Mesoamerican and Aztec creation myth, Tezcatlipoca ruled the first world of the Sun but was then overthrown by Quetzalcóatl. The two later cooperated, however, to create the 5th Sun. Transformed into giant snakes, the two gods attacked and dismembered the female reptilian monster known as Tlaltecuhtli (or Cipactli)

claim.id: Pada bulan Tóxcatl, bulan keenam (atau kelima) tahun surya Aztec, Tezcatlipoca dipuja dalam upacara khusus; bagian penting upacara itu adalah peniruan sang dewa, paling sering oleh tawanan perang yang biasanya paling tampan dan paling berani.
claim.en: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth (or 5th) month of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies; an important part was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.

claims_provenance.quote: In the month of Tóxcatl, the sixth month (or 5th) of the Aztec solar year, Tezcatlipoca was worshipped in special ceremonies. As with other Aztec religious rites an important part of the ceremony was the impersonation of the god, most often by a prisoner of war, typically the best looking and most courageous one.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Tezcatlipoca: The Greatest of Aztec Gods

claim.id: Ketika bulan khusus itu tiba, sang peniru berpakaian prajurit dan dalam pesta pernikahan simbolis menikahi empat dewinya. Dihormati dengan bunga dan tarian, ia lalu dibawa ke kuil khusus tempat ia segera dikorbankan dan jantungnya diambil dengan pisau obsidian untuk menghormati Tezcatlipoca yang sejati.
claim.en: When the month came, the impersonator was dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival married his four goddesses; honoured with flowers and dances, the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was sacrificed and his heart removed with an obsidian knife to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

claims_provenance.quote: When the special month finally came around the impersonator was handsomely dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival he married his four goddesses. Honoured with flowers and dances the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was promptly sacrificed and his heart removed using an obsidian knife in order to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.
claims_provenance.source_citation: World History Encyclopedia — Tezcatlipoca: The Greatest of Aztec Gods

claim.id: Ia juga dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Biru, 'Penyihir Kolibri', dewa Tenochtitlán, tempat ia dikaitkan dengan matahari dan dewa perang Huitzilopochtli; ia bisa dikenal sebagai Tezcatlipoca Merah, 'Si Terkuliti', yang dikaitkan dengan dewa Camaxtli dan Xipe Totec (dewa bangsa Tlaxcaltec).
claim.en: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli; he could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One', associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans).

claims_provenance.quote: He is also known as Blue Tezcatlipoca, the 'Hummingbird Sorcerer', god of Tenochtitlán, where he was associated with the sun and the war god Huitzilopochtli. He could be known as Red Tezcatlipoca, the 'Flayed One' and associated with the gods Camaxtli and Xipe Totec (god of the Tlaxcaltecans)

claim.en: The ever-present god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow; Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction.

claim.id: Dikaitkan dengan konflik, ia dikenal sebagai Yaotl atau 'Musuh' dan menjadi pelindung prajurit serta kamp pelatihan mereka (telpochcalli); namun ia tidak selalu melindungi prajurit, sebab kadang ia dapat ditemui di persimpangan jalan pada tengah malam, siap menantang prajurit yang lengah.
claim.en: Associated with conflict, he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli); he was not always protective to soldiers, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

claim.en: In later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

claim.en: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake and sometimes carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

claims_provenance.quote: Then they decided to cook a fish but the smoke from their fire disturbed the stars, especially Citlallatonac and Citlalicue. These gods complained vociferously to Tezcatlipoca who, perhaps a little harshly, lopped off the heads of the couple and reattached them to their backsides, thus, the very first dogs were created.

claim.en: One of the most famous art objects of the god is the decorated skull now in the British Museum in London, covered in turquoise and black lignite mosaic with red thorny oyster shell in the nasal cavity.

long_description.id: Ia dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan, dan dalam wujud yang lebih suram dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran. Sebagai pelindung prajurit ia tidak selalu melindungi mereka: kadang ia menunggu di persimpangan jalan tengah malam untuk menantang prajurit yang lengah.
long_description.en: He could step directly into human affairs, bringing joy or grief, and in a darker guise was called lord of the shadows or night, a black-magic sorcerer who brought evil, death and destruction. As patron of warriors he was not always protective of them: sometimes he waited at crossroads at the dead of night to challenge unsuspecting warriors.

long_description.id: Perayaan utamanya adalah Toxcatl yang, seperti kebanyakan perayaan keagamaan Aztec, melibatkan pengorbanan manusia. Seorang peniru sang dewa, paling sering tawanan perang yang paling tampan dan berani, menikahi empat dewi secara simbolis lalu dikorbankan dengan pisau obsidian. Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan ia memiliki cermin obsidian hitam sebagai pengganti kaki kirinya, merujuk pada luka dalam pertempurannya dengan Tlaltecuhtli.
long_description.en: His chief festival was Toxcatl, which, like most Aztec religious festivals, included human sacrifice. An impersonator of the god, most often the best looking and most courageous prisoner of war, symbolically married four goddesses and was then sacrificed with an obsidian knife. In later depictions he has a black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, referring to a wound in his battle with Tlaltecuhtli.

short_description.id: Tinirau adalah dewa pelindung ikan dalam mitologi Polinesia, putra Tangaroa menurut Tregear, yang bertempat tinggal di Pulau Suci Motutapu dan dalam sebagian tradisi bersifat ganda.
short_description.en: Tinirau is a guardian deity of fish in Polynesian mythology, a son of Tangaroa according to Tregear, who dwelt on the Holy Island of Motutapu and in some traditions has a dual nature.

long_description.id:
Kisah tentang Tinirau ditemukan di seluruh kepulauan Polinesia, dan ia adalah penjaga ikan. Tregear menyebutnya dewa pelindung ikan dan putra Tangaroa, Penguasa Samudra. Nama lainnya dalam bahasa Polinesia antara lain Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau, dan Tinilau.

Menurut Tregear, Tinirau tinggal di Pulau Suci (Motutapu), yang disepakati semua orang Polinesia, dan rumahnya berupa cagar ikan yang dikelilingi kolam pembiakan. Dalam tradisi Mangaia ia setengah ikan, mewarisi Motu-tapu, dan menjadi penguasa semua ikan. Dalam sebagian tradisi lain ia memiliki dua sisi: yang merusak sebagai penjaga hiu dan yang ramah sebagai pemuda tampan, atau sisi kanan manusia dan sisi kiri ikan.

Tregear mencatat bahwa Tinirau meminjamkan seekor paus peliharaannya kepada penyihir Kae, yang membunuhnya. Tinirau murka dan mengirim Hina bersama sekelompok perempuan untuk menjebak Kae. Hina menjadi istri Tinirau. Di Samoa, kisah Tinilau (atau Tigilau) dan istrinya Sina sangat populer.
long_description.en:
Stories about Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia, and he is a guardian of fish. Tregear calls him the tutelary deity of fishes and a son of Tangaroa, the Lord of Ocean. His other names in Polynesian languages include Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau and Tinilau.

According to Tregear, Tinirau dwelt on the Holy Island (Motutapu), as all Polynesians agree, and his home was a fish preserve ringed by breeding pools. In the Mangaian tradition he is half a fish, inherits Motu-tapu and is lord of all fish. In some other traditions he has two sides: a destructive one as guardian of sharks and a kind one as a handsome youth, or a human right side and a fish left side.

Tregear records that Tinirau lent a pet whale to the magician Kae, who killed it. Furious, Tinirau sent Hina with a party of women to trap Kae. Hina became Tinirau's wife. In Samoa the stories of Tinilau (or Tigilau) and his wife Sina are very popular.

short_description.id: Tinirau adalah dewa pelindung ikan dalam mitologi Polinesia, putra Tangaroa menurut Tregear, yang bertempat tinggal di Pulau Suci Motutapu dan dalam sebagian tradisi bersifat ganda.
short_description.en: Tinirau is a guardian deity of fish in Polynesian mythology, a son of Tangaroa according to Tregear, who dwelt on the Holy Island of Motutapu and in some traditions has a dual nature.

long_description.id: Kisah tentang Tinirau ditemukan di seluruh kepulauan Polinesia, dan ia adalah penjaga ikan. Tregear menyebutnya dewa pelindung ikan dan putra Tangaroa, Penguasa Samudra. Nama lainnya dalam bahasa Polinesia antara lain Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau, dan Tinilau.
long_description.en: Stories about Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia, and he is a guardian of fish. Tregear calls him the tutelary deity of fishes and a son of Tangaroa, the Lord of Ocean. His other names in Polynesian languages include Kinilau, Sinilau, Tigilau and Tinilau.

long_description.id: Menurut Tregear, Tinirau tinggal di Pulau Suci (Motutapu), yang disepakati semua orang Polinesia, dan rumahnya berupa cagar ikan yang dikelilingi kolam pembiakan. Dalam tradisi Mangaia ia setengah ikan, mewarisi Motu-tapu, dan menjadi penguasa semua ikan. Dalam sebagian tradisi lain ia memiliki dua sisi: yang merusak sebagai penjaga hiu dan yang ramah sebagai pemuda tampan, atau sisi kanan manusia dan sisi kiri ikan.
long_description.en: According to Tregear, Tinirau dwelt on the Holy Island (Motutapu), as all Polynesians agree, and his home was a fish preserve ringed by breeding pools. In the Mangaian tradition he is half a fish, inherits Motu-tapu and is lord of all fish. In some other traditions he has two sides: a destructive one as guardian of sharks and a kind one as a handsome youth, or a human right side and a fish left side.

long_description.id: Tregear mencatat bahwa Tinirau meminjamkan seekor paus peliharaannya kepada penyihir Kae, yang membunuhnya. Tinirau murka dan mengirim Hina bersama sekelompok perempuan untuk menjebak Kae. Hina menjadi istri Tinirau. Di Samoa, kisah Tinilau (atau Tigilau) dan istrinya Sina sangat populer.
long_description.en: Tregear records that Tinirau lent a pet whale to the magician Kae, who killed it. Furious, Tinirau sent Hina with a party of women to trap Kae. Hina became Tinirau's wife. In Samoa the stories of Tinilau (or Tigilau) and his wife Sina are very popular.

short_description.id: Kaum Qizhong adalah bangsa utara legendaris dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Qizhong people are a legendary northern race in Chinese tradition.

long_description.id:
Kaum Qizhong adalah bangsa utara legendaris dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Kitab Gunung dan Laut menempatkan negeri mereka di timur kaum Juying dan menggambarkan kaki besar.

Komentar menyebut mereka berjalan tanpa menempatkan tumit di tanah. Novel Bunga dalam Cermin menggambarkan mereka berjalan dengan ujung jari kaki.

Teks Haiwai Beijing menempatkan negeri Qizhong di selatan atau timur Juying dan menyebut kaki penduduknya menopang, atau dalam versi lain bertubuh besar dengan kaki besar; negeri itu juga disebut Fanzhong atau Dazhong. Nama Qizhong juga dipakai untuk seekor burung dalam Shanhaijing, yang berbeda dari bangsa ini.
long_description.en:
Qizhong people are a legendary northern race in Chinese tradition. The Classic of Mountains and Seas places their land east of the Juying people and describes huge feet.

Commentary says they walk without placing heels on the ground. The novel Flowers in the Mirror portrays them walking on their toes.

The Haiwai Beijing text places the Qizhong country south or east of Juying and says its people’s feet are propped, or in another version that they are big with big feet; the country is also called Fanzhong or Dazhong. The name Qizhong is also used in the Shanhaijing for a bird, which is distinct from this people.

claim.id: Teks Haiwai Beijing (海外北經): negeri Qizhong (跂踵國) terletak di selatan (atau timur) Juying (拘癭); kedua kaki penduduknya menopang (兩足皆支), atau menurut versi lain mereka bertubuh besar dengan kaki yang juga besar; nama lainnya Fanzhong (反踵) atau Dazhong (大踵).
claim.en: The Haiwai Beijing (海外北經) text: the Qizhong country (跂踵國) lies south (or east) of Juying (拘癭); its people’s two feet are propped (兩足皆支), or in another version they are big with big feet; it is also called Fanzhong (反踵) or Dazhong (大踵).

claims_provenance.quote: 跂踵國在拘 癭一作「纓」 南一作「東」， 其為人兩足皆支一作「其為人大，兩足亦大」。一曰 反一作「大」踵。

claim.en: The name Qizhong (跂踵) can refer to a bird or to a country, the Qizhong country (跂踵国); both appear in the Shanhaijing (山海经).

claim.id: Negeri Qizhong terletak di timur negeri Juying (拘瘿国), dan penduduknya bertubuh tinggi besar dengan kaki yang sangat besar.
claim.en: The Qizhong country lies east of the Juying country (拘瘿国), and its people are tall and big with very large feet.

claims_provenance.quote: 跂踵国则是在拘瘿国的东面的一个国家，那里的人都身材高大，两只脚也非常大。

short_description.id: 顒 (Yú) adalah burung dalam Shan Hai Jing yang berbentuk seperti burung hantu, berwajah manusia, bermata empat, dan bertelinga; kemunculannya dianggap pertanda kekeringan besar.
short_description.en: 顒 (Yú) is a bird in the Shan Hai Jing shaped like an owl, with a human face, four eyes and ears; its appearance is taken as an omen of great drought.

long_description.id:
顒 adalah burung dalam kitab geografi kuno Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經). Bentuknya seperti burung hantu, tetapi ia berwajah manusia dengan empat mata dan telinga. Burung itu bersuara menyebut namanya sendiri, dan kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kekeringan.

Menurut teks itu, burung ini berada di lembah bernama 中谷 di sebelah selatan gunung 令丘, gunung yang tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya. Bila burung itu terlihat, seluruh negeri akan dilanda kekeringan besar.

Cara membaca aksara 顒 berbeda-beda. Dalam bahasa Jepang ia dibaca ぎょう atau ぐ, kamus Jepang memuat グ (ゴ), catatan pada teks asli (Guo Pu) memberi 娛, dan bacaan Tionghoa modernnya adalah yú.
long_description.en:
顒 is a bird in the ancient geographical text Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section). It is shaped like an owl, but has a human face with four eyes and ears. The bird cries out its own name, and its appearance is linked to drought.

According to the text, the bird lives in a valley called 中谷 south of Lingqiu mountain (令丘), a mountain without plants or trees and with much fire. When the bird is seen, the whole land will suffer a great drought.

How to read the character 顒 varies. In Japanese it is read ぎょう or ぐ, Japanese dictionaries give グ (ゴ), the note on the original text (Guo Pu) gives 娛, and its modern Chinese reading is yú.

claim.id: Shan Hai Jing menempatkannya di lembah selatan Gunung Lingqiu.

claim.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (南山經), 400 li lebih jauh ke timur terdapat gunung 令丘 yang tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya; di sebelah selatannya ada lembah bernama 中谷, tempat angin 條風 keluar.
claim.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (南山經), a further 400 li to the east lies Lingqiu mountain (令丘之山), without plants or trees and with much fire; to its south is a valley called Zhonggu (中谷), from which the tiao wind (條風) comes out.

short_description.id: 顒 (Yú) adalah burung dalam Shan Hai Jing yang berbentuk seperti burung hantu, berwajah manusia, bermata empat, dan bertelinga; kemunculannya dianggap pertanda kekeringan besar.
short_description.en: 顒 (Yú) is a bird in the Shan Hai Jing shaped like an owl, with a human face, four eyes and ears; its appearance is taken as an omen of great drought.

long_description.id: 顒 adalah burung dalam kitab geografi kuno Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經). Bentuknya seperti burung hantu, tetapi ia berwajah manusia dengan empat mata dan telinga. Burung itu bersuara menyebut namanya sendiri, dan kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan kekeringan.
long_description.en: 顒 is a bird in the ancient geographical text Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section). It is shaped like an owl, but has a human face with four eyes and ears. The bird cries out its own name, and its appearance is linked to drought.

long_description.id: Menurut teks itu, burung ini berada di lembah bernama 中谷 di sebelah selatan gunung 令丘, gunung yang tanpa tumbuhan dan banyak apinya. Bila burung itu terlihat, seluruh negeri akan dilanda kekeringan besar.
long_description.en: According to the text, the bird lives in a valley called 中谷 south of Lingqiu mountain (令丘), a mountain without plants or trees and with much fire. When the bird is seen, the whole land will suffer a great drought.

long_description.id: Cara membaca aksara 顒 berbeda-beda. Dalam bahasa Jepang ia dibaca ぎょう atau ぐ, kamus Jepang memuat グ (ゴ), catatan pada teks asli (Guo Pu) memberi 娛, dan bacaan Tionghoa modernnya adalah yú.
long_description.en: How to read the character 顒 varies. In Japanese it is read ぎょう or ぐ, Japanese dictionaries give グ (ゴ), the note on the original text (Guo Pu) gives 娛, and its modern Chinese reading is yú.

short_description.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa yang tinggi atau lehernya mencapai tujuh hiro.
short_description.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō is a giant female yōkai whose height or neck reaches seven hiro.

long_description.id:
Nanahiro-nyōbō adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa yang tinggi atau lehernya mencapai tujuh hiro. Tradisi Kepulauan Oki menempatkan pertemuannya pada jalan gunung.

Batu besar setempat dijelaskan sebagai tubuhnya yang membatu dan konon terus membesar. Versi Matsue memberinya rambut terurai dan gigi hitam ketika membentang pada gunung dan pesisir.

Ia juga disebut nanahiro-onna atau shichijō-onna dan diceritakan di Shimane timur serta Tottori tengah-barat. Dalam legenda zaman Oda Nobunaga, seorang lelaki menebas wajahnya dan ia berubah menjadi batu besar; keluarga Nakata setempat konon keturunan lelaki itu. Di Yasugi ia dikisahkan sebagai perempuan cantik yang mengemis dengan pakaian sepanjang tujuh hiro, sedangkan di Akasaki ia berambut biru dan berwajah putih, menumbuk padi sambil menyanyi sedih.
long_description.en:
Nanahiro-nyōbō is a giant female yōkai whose height or neck reaches seven hiro. An Oki Islands tradition places her encounters on mountain roads.

A large local rock is explained as her petrified body and is said to keep growing. A Matsue version gives her hanging hair and black teeth as she spans mountains and the coast.

She is also called nanahiro-onna or shichijō-onna and is told of in eastern Shimane and central-western Tottori. In a legend from Oda Nobunaga’s time, a man slashed her face and she became a huge rock; the local Nakata family is said to descend from him. In Yasugi she is a beautiful woman begging in clothes seven hiro long, while in Akasaki she has blue hair and a white face and pounds rice while singing sadly.

summary.en: The full body reaches seven hiro.

claim.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa yang tinggi atau lehernya mencapai tujuh hiro.
claim.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō is a giant female yōkai whose height or neck reaches seven hiro.

claims_provenance.quote: 名称の尋とは尺貫法における長さの単位であり、七尋女房はその名の通り身長または首が7尋（約12.6メートル）もある巨大な女性の妖怪といわれ、土地によって様々な伝承がある。

claim.id: Tradisi Kepulauan Oki menempatkan pertemuannya pada jalan gunung.
claim.en: An Oki Islands tradition places her encounters on mountain roads.

claims_provenance.quote: 隠岐諸島の中ノ島にある島根県隠岐郡海士町では、七尋女房が山道を行くものに様々な怪異をなしたといわれるが、織田信長の時代の以下のような伝説がある。

claim.id: Batu besar setempat dijelaskan sebagai tubuhnya yang membatu dan konon terus membesar.
claim.en: A large local rock is explained as her petrified body and is said to keep growing.

claims_provenance.quote: また、海士町日ノ津の山道にある奇石・女房ヶ石はこの七尋女房が石化したものといわれ、高さ6メートル、幅3メートルもあり、しかも少しずつ大きくなっているといわれる。

claim.id: Versi Matsue memberinya rambut terurai dan gigi hitam ketika membentang pada gunung dan pesisir.
claim.en: A Matsue version gives her hanging hair and black teeth as she spans mountains and the coast.

claims_provenance.quote: 島根町（現・松江市）では、浜地区の境の山から海岸の島にまたがって七尋女房が現れ、長い髪を垂らし、黒い歯をむき出し、道を行く人に笑いかけたという。

claim.id: Nanahiro-nyōbō, juga disebut nanahiro-onna (七尋女) atau shichijō-onna (七丈女), adalah yōkai perempuan raksasa dari Shimane timur dan Tottori tengah-barat (島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部).
claim.en: Nanahiro-nyōbō, also called nanahiro-onna (七尋女) or shichijō-onna (七丈女), is a giant female yōkai of eastern Shimane and central-western Tottori (島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部).

claims_provenance.quote: 七尋女房，又稱七尋女、七丈女，是流傳於島根縣東部與鳥取縣中西部，一種巨大的女性妖怪。

claim.id: Dalam legenda zaman Oda Nobunaga, seorang lelaki menebas wajah nanahiro-nyōbō, dan ia yang terluka berubah menjadi batu besar; keluarga Nakata (中田氏) setempat konon keturunan lelaki itu.
claim.en: In a legend from Oda Nobunaga’s time, a man slashed the nanahiro-nyōbō’s face, and, wounded, she turned into a huge rock; the local Nakata family (中田氏) is said to descend from that man.

claims_provenance.quote: 織田信長時代有一個著名的傳說，稱一名男子騎馬行於山道時，被不知從哪來的石頭砸中。 ... 男人一刀斬傷七尋女房的臉，負傷的七尋女房變為一塊巨石。據傳當地的中田氏便是那名男子的後代

claim.id: Di Yasugi (安來市), nanahiro-nyōbō dikisahkan sebagai perempuan cantik yang berkeliling mengemis dengan pakaian sepanjang tujuh hiro; gundukan tanah bernama Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) di sana dikaitkan dengannya.
claim.en: In Yasugi (安來市), the nanahiro-nyōbō is told of as a beautiful woman who went begging in clothes seven hiro long; a mound there called Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) is linked with her.

claims_provenance.quote: 在安來市，傳說七尋女房是個美人，身穿七尋長的衣服四處乞討。據說當地有一個名為「乙御前塚」的土丘，與七尋女房有關。

claim.id: Di Akasaki, Distrik Tōhaku (kini Kotoura, 琴浦町), ia dikisahkan sebagai yōkai perempuan berambut biru dan berwajah putih yang menumbuk padi sambil menyanyi dengan wajah sedih.
claim.en: In Akasaki, Tōhaku District (now Kotoura, 琴浦町), she is told of as a blue-haired, white-faced female yōkai who pounds rice while singing with a sorrowful look.

claims_provenance.quote: 在東伯郡赤碕町(今琴浦町)，傳說七尋女房是個青髮白臉的女妖怪，會一邊搗米一邊因吟唱歌謠，神色淒苦。

claims.quote: 織田信長時代有一個著名的傳說，稱一名男子騎馬行於山道時，被不知從哪來的石頭砸中。 ... 男人一刀斬傷七尋女房的臉，負傷的七尋女房變為一塊巨石。據傳當地的中田氏便是那名男子的後代

statement.id: Dalam legenda zaman Oda Nobunaga, seorang lelaki menebas wajah nanahiro-nyōbō, dan ia yang terluka berubah menjadi batu besar; keluarga Nakata (中田氏) setempat konon keturunan lelaki itu.
statement.en: In a legend from Oda Nobunaga’s time, a man slashed the nanahiro-nyōbō’s face, and, wounded, she turned into a huge rock; the local Nakata family (中田氏) is said to descend from that man.

claims.quote: 在安來市，傳說七尋女房是個美人，身穿七尋長的衣服四處乞討。據說當地有一個名為「乙御前塚」的土丘，與七尋女房有關。

statement.id: Di Yasugi (安來市), nanahiro-nyōbō dikisahkan sebagai perempuan cantik yang berkeliling mengemis dengan pakaian sepanjang tujuh hiro; gundukan tanah bernama Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) di sana dikaitkan dengannya.
statement.en: In Yasugi (安來市), the nanahiro-nyōbō is told of as a beautiful woman who went begging in clothes seven hiro long; a mound there called Otogozen-zuka (乙御前塚) is linked with her.

claims.quote: 在東伯郡赤碕町(今琴浦町)，傳說七尋女房是個青髮白臉的女妖怪，會一邊搗米一邊因吟唱歌謠，神色淒苦。

statement.id: Di Akasaki, Distrik Tōhaku (kini Kotoura, 琴浦町), ia dikisahkan sebagai yōkai perempuan berambut biru dan berwajah putih yang menumbuk padi sambil menyanyi dengan wajah sedih.
statement.en: In Akasaki, Tōhaku District (now Kotoura, 琴浦町), she is told of as a blue-haired, white-faced female yōkai who pounds rice while singing with a sorrowful look.

summary.en: The full body reaches seven hiro.

short_description.id: Ачбуудан adalah kuda perang dan tulpar milik Жолой dalam epos Манас; menurut legenda ia lahir dari kuda betina Кула secara gaib, dan dalam satu varian ia berbicara untuk memohon nyawa tuannya.
short_description.en: Ачбуудан is the war horse and tulpar of Жолой in the Манас epic; legend says it was born miraculously of the Кула mare, and in one variant it speaks to beg for its master's life.

long_description.id:
Ачбуудан adalah kuda perang Жолой dan tulpar, kuda unggul yang ia pacu dalam lomba, dalam epos Манас. Pada lomba kuda di pesta peringatan Көкөтөй, Ачбуудан tiba di belakang Аккула. Kuda ini dikenal selalu menyelamatkan tuannya dari maut.

Legenda Акас мерген menceritakan asal-usulnya. Pada masa perang, ketika sekelompok кыргыз terpencil di pegunungan, kuda betina Кула milik Акас мерген melahirkan anak kuda tanpa kuda jantan, dan para tetua berkata kelahiran itu datang dari alam gaib. Kuda betina yang sama melahirkan tiga tulpar termasyhur: Аккула, Ачбуудан, dan Мааникер.

Ачбуудан lahir sebagai anak kuda kelabu berekor pucat. Seorang pedagang membelinya, dan di pasar Жолой membelinya dari pedagang itu dan menamainya. Legenda itu juga menyebut bahwa suatu ketika seekor kuda jantan biru keluar dari danau dan mendekati kuda betina Кула.

Dalam satu varian epos, ketika Манас menawan Жолой dan hendak membunuhnya, Ачбуудан tiba-tiba dapat berbicara dan memohon nyawa tuannya. Setelah itu ia masuk ke dalam api yang berkobar dan lenyap. Kisah ini menjadi contoh hewan yang berbicara dan berpikir seperti manusia, citra yang sering muncul dalam epos.
long_description.en:
Ачбуудан is the war horse of Жолой and the tulpar, the champion steed, he raced in the Манас epic. In the horse race at Көкөтөй's memorial feast, Ачбуудан finished behind Аккула. The horse is known for always saving its master from death.

The legend of Акас мерген tells of its origin. In a time of war, when a group of кыргыз was cut off in the mountains, the Кула mare of Акас мерген foaled without a stallion, and the elders said the births came from the unseen world. The same mare bore three famous tulpars: Аккула, Ачбуудан and Мааникер.

Ачбуудан was born as a grey colt with a pale tail. A merchant bought it and led it away, and at the bazaar Жолой bought it from him and gave it its name. The legend also tells that at one point a blue stallion came out of a lake and approached the Кула mare.

In one variant of the epic, when Манас captured Жолой and was about to kill him, Ачбуудан suddenly gained speech and begged for its master's life. It then plunged into the blazing fire and vanished. The episode is an example of an animal that speaks and thinks like a human, an image that often appears in epics.

claims_provenance.quote: Жолойдун жоого минген аты, байгеге чапкан тулпары.

claim.id: Dalam lomba kuda pada pesta peringatan (ашындагы) Көкөтөй ia tiba setelah Аккула; ia selalu menyelamatkan Жолой dari maut (өлүмдөн).
claim.en: In the horse race at Көкөтөй's memorial feast (ашындагы) it finishes after Аккула; it always saved Жолой from death (өлүмдөн).

claims_provenance.quote: Көкөтөйдүн ашындагы ат чабышта Аккуладан кийин келет. Жолойду ар качан өлүмдөн куткарган.

claim.id: Dalam satu varian, ketika Манас hendak membunuh Жолой, Ачбуудан mendadak bisa berbicara (тил бүтүп) dan memohon darah (канын) Жолой, yakni nyawanya.
claim.en: In one variant, when Манас is about to kill Жолой, Ачбуудан gains the power of speech (тил бүтүп) and begs for Жолой's blood (канын), that is, his life.

claims_provenance.quote: Бир вариантта Манас Жолойду өлтүрөөрдө Ачбууданга тил бүтүп, Жолойдун канын сурап калат.

claim.id: Menurut legenda (уламыш), Акас мерген adalah pemilik kuda betina Кула yang melahirkan tulpar termasyhur Аккула, Ачбуудан, dan Мааникер.
claim.en: According to legend (уламыш), Акас мерген owned the Кула mare that foaled the famous tulpars Аккула, Ачбуудан and Мааникер.

claims_provenance.quote: Акас мерген — уламыш боюнча атактуу тулпарлар Аккула, Ачбуудан, Мааникерди тууган Кула бээнин ээси.

claim.id: Kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda tanpa ada kuda jantan (Айгыр жок), sehingga orang heran; para tetua bijak berkata ia melahirkan dari alam gaib (кайыптан).
claim.en: The Кула mare foaled with no stallion present (Айгыр жок), to people's wonder; the wise elders said she had foaled from the unseen world (кайыптан).

claims_provenance.quote: Айгыр жок туруп эле Кула бээнин Кула кулун тууп коюшу, элди кубандырат, бир чети таң калтырат. Айылдагы акылман аксакалдар Кула бээ кайыптан тууду деп айтышат.

claim.id: Musim semi berikutnya kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda kelabu (Сур кулун) berekor pucat (куйругу агыш).
claim.en: The following spring the Кула mare foaled a grey (Сур кулун) colt with a pale tail (куйругу агыш).

claims_provenance.quote: Кийинки жазда да Кула бээ куйругу агыш Сур кулун тууйт.

claim.id: Seorang pedagang (соодагер) membeli anak kuda ekor pucat (Ач куйрук, сур тай) itu seharga lima belas kuda betina beranak dan lima belas kuda; kemudian Жолой membelinya dari pedagang itu di pasar dan memberinya nama.
claim.en: A merchant (соодагер) bought the pale-tailed (Ач куйрук, сур тай) colt for fifteen mares with foals and fifteen horses; then Жолой bought it from the merchant at the bazaar and named it.

claims_provenance.quote: Ач куйрук тайды (сур тай) кулундуу он беш бээ, он беш атка бир соодагер сатып алып ... Базардан соодагер жетелеп турган ач куйрукту Жолой сатып алып, атын

claim.id: Suatu ketika seekor kuda jantan biru (көпкөк айгыр) keluar dari danau (көлдөн) dan mendekati kuda betina Кула.
claim.en: At one point a blue stallion (көпкөк айгыр) came out of the lake (көлдөн) and sniffed at the Кула mare.

claims_provenance.quote: Бир маалда көлдөн көпкөк айгыр чыгып келип Кула бээни жыттагылап калат.

claim.id: Legenda ini berlatar masa perang ketika калмактар menyerang кыргыз dan sepuluh keluarga (10 түтүн) кыргыз terpisah dan tinggal di pegunungan.
claim.en: The legend is set in a time of war when the калмактар attacked the кыргыз and ten households (10 түтүн) of кыргыз were cut off and stayed in the mountains.

claims_provenance.quote: Жоокерчилик заманда калмактар кыргызга кол салып, аларды туш тарапка таратканда 10 түтүн кыргыз бөлүнүп, тоо арасында калып калат.

claim.id: Ketika Манас menawan Жолой, Ачбуудан memohon kepada Манас nyawa (жанын) tuannya.
claim.en: When Манас captured Жолой, Ачбуудан begged Манас for its master's life (жанын).

claims_provenance.quote: Манас Жолойду колго түшүргөндө, Ачбуудан Манастан ээсинин жанын сурайт:

claim.id: Setelah berkata demikian, kuda itu masuk ke dalam api yang berkobar (алоолонгон отко) dan lenyap (кайып болуп); citra seperti ini banyak dijumpai dalam epos (эпосто).
claim.en: Having said this, the horse plunged into the blazing fire (алоолонгон отко) and vanished (кайып болуп); such images are common in the epic (эпосто).

claims_provenance.quote: деп алоолонгон отко түшүп кайып болуп кетет. Ошондой эле эпосто мындай образдар көп кездешет.

claim.id: Dalam epos (эпостордо), hewan dan benda mati dapat berbicara dan berpikir seperti manusia (адамча сүйлөп) serta memiliki sifat manusia; artikel ketiga membahas Ачбуудан sebagai contohnya.
claim.en: In epics (эпостордо), animals and inanimate things speak and think like humans (адамча сүйлөп) and gain human qualities; the third article discusses Ачбуудан as an example.

claims_provenance.quote: эпостордо жан-жаныбарлар (айбанат, канаттуу) жана жансыз нерселер (тооташ, суу, өсүмдүктөр) адамча сүйлөп, ойлоп кишидеги касиетке да ээ болушат.

claims.quote: Айгыр жок туруп эле Кула бээнин Кула кулун тууп коюшу, элди кубандырат, бир чети таң калтырат. Айылдагы акылман аксакалдар Кула бээ кайыптан тууду деп айтышат.

statement.id: Kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda tanpa ada kuda jantan (Айгыр жок), sehingga orang heran; para tetua bijak berkata ia melahirkan dari alam gaib (кайыптан).
statement.en: The Кула mare foaled with no stallion present (Айгыр жок), to people's wonder; the wise elders said she had foaled from the unseen world (кайыптан).

claims.quote: Кийинки жазда да Кула бээ куйругу агыш Сур кулун тууйт.

statement.id: Musim semi berikutnya kuda betina Кула melahirkan anak kuda kelabu (Сур кулун) berekor pucat (куйругу агыш).
statement.en: The following spring the Кула mare foaled a grey (Сур кулун) colt with a pale tail (куйругу агыш).

claims.quote: Ач куйрук тайды (сур тай) кулундуу он беш бээ, он беш атка бир соодагер сатып алып ... Базардан соодагер жетелеп турган ач куйрукту Жолой сатып алып, атын

statement.id: Seorang pedagang (соодагер) membeli anak kuda ekor pucat (Ач куйрук, сур тай) itu seharga lima belas kuda betina beranak dan lima belas kuda; kemudian Жолой membelinya dari pedagang itu di pasar dan memberinya nama.
statement.en: A merchant (соодагер) bought the pale-tailed (Ач куйрук, сур тай) colt for fifteen mares with foals and fifteen horses; then Жолой bought it from the merchant at the bazaar and named it.

claims.quote: Бир маалда көлдөн көпкөк айгыр чыгып келип Кула бээни жыттагылап калат.

statement.id: Suatu ketika seekor kuda jantan biru (көпкөк айгыр) keluar dari danau (көлдөн) dan mendekati kuda betina Кула.
statement.en: At one point a blue stallion (көпкөк айгыр) came out of the lake (көлдөн) and sniffed at the Кула mare.

claims.quote: Жоокерчилик заманда калмактар кыргызга кол салып, аларды туш тарапка таратканда 10 түтүн кыргыз бөлүнүп, тоо арасында калып калат.

statement.id: Legenda ini berlatar masa perang ketika калмактар menyerang кыргыз dan sepuluh keluarga (10 түтүн) кыргыз terpisah dan tinggal di pegunungan.
statement.en: The legend is set in a time of war when the калмактар attacked the кыргыз and ten households (10 түтүн) of кыргыз were cut off and stayed in the mountains.

claims.quote: Манас Жолойду колго түшүргөндө, Ачбуудан Манастан ээсинин жанын сурайт:

statement.id: Ketika Манас menawan Жолой, Ачбуудан memohon kepada Манас nyawa (жанын) tuannya.
statement.en: When Манас captured Жолой, Ачбуудан begged Манас for its master's life (жанын).

claims.quote: деп алоолонгон отко түшүп кайып болуп кетет. Ошондой эле эпосто мындай образдар көп кездешет.

statement.id: Setelah berkata demikian, kuda itu masuk ke dalam api yang berkobar (алоолонгон отко) dan lenyap (кайып болуп); citra seperti ini banyak dijumpai dalam epos (эпосто).
statement.en: Having said this, the horse plunged into the blazing fire (алоолонгон отко) and vanished (кайып болуп); such images are common in the epic (эпосто).

claims.quote: эпостордо жан-жаныбарлар (айбанат, канаттуу) жана жансыз нерселер (тооташ, суу, өсүмдүктөр) адамча сүйлөп, ойлоп кишидеги касиетке да ээ болушат.

statement.id: Dalam epos (эпостордо), hewan dan benda mati dapat berbicara dan berpikir seperti manusia (адамча сүйлөп) serta memiliki sifat manusia; artikel ketiga membahas Ачбуудан sebagai contohnya.
statement.en: In epics (эпостордо), animals and inanimate things speak and think like humans (адамча сүйлөп) and gain human qualities; the third article discusses Ачбуудан as an example.
