short_description.id: Jing adalah makhluk gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok: roh yang dipercaya muncul pada hewan, tumbuhan, bahkan benda mati yang sudah sangat tua, dan sebagian dapat berubah wujud.
short_description.en: Jing is a supernatural being in Chinese tradition: a spirit believed to arise in very old animals, plants and even objects, some of which can change form.

long_description.id:
Jing (精) adalah kategori makhluk gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok. Makhluk hidup dan benda dapat mengembangkan roh semacam itu seiring waktu: secara umum dipercaya bahwa benda yang hidup atau tersimpan seratus atau seribu tahun lebih menyerap sari alam dan menjadi jing, yang juga disebut jingguai. Contohnya meliputi roh rubah, ular, pohon, dan bunga.

Sebagian jing digambarkan dapat berubah wujud. Dalam Baopuzi, jing semua benda tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan dan menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di cermin; karena itu daoshi yang masuk gunung menggantungkan cermin di punggung mereka. Jika yang datang adalah makhluk burung atau hewan, wujudnya tampak di cermin, dan siluman tua yang pergi berjalan mundur dan tidak punya tumit.

Artikel Wikipedia menyebut bahwa Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu berjiwa dan lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman, bahwa jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah menurut Baize Jingguai Tu, dan bahwa Jepang memiliki konsep serupa seperti tsukumogami. Soushenji sendiri mengutip Baize Tu tentang jing anak kecil bernama Xinang di antara dua gunung.
long_description.en:
Jing (精) is a category of supernatural being in Chinese tradition. Living beings and objects may develop such spirits over time: it is widely believed that things that live or are kept for a hundred or a thousand years or more absorb the essence of nature and become jing, also called jingguai. Examples include fox, snake, tree and flower spirits.

Some jing are described as changing form. In the Baopuzi the jing of all aged things can take human form to dazzle and test people, but cannot change their true form in a mirror; so Daoists entering the mountains hung mirrors on their backs. If the visitor is a bird- or beast-spirit its form shows in the mirror, and an old spirit leaves walking backwards and has no heels.

The Wikipedia article says the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits and over time turn into monsters, that Chinese jing have a genealogy according to the Baize Jingguai Tu, and that Japan has a similar concept such as tsukumogami. The Soushenji itself quotes the Baize Tu about a child-like jing named Xinang between two mountains.

who.id: Roh gaib yang muncul pada makhluk atau benda yang sangat tua.
who.en: A supernatural spirit arising in very old creatures or objects.

origin.id: Tradisi Tiongkok, dengan konsep serupa di Jepang.
origin.en: Chinese tradition, with a similar concept in Japan.

role.id: Menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menguji orang, tetapi terbongkar oleh cermin.
role.en: Takes human form to test people but is exposed by a mirror.

famous_for.id: Rubah-jing dan jing yang wujudnya terbongkar di cermin.
famous_for.en: The fox spirit and jing whose true form is exposed in a mirror.

did_you_know.id: Artikel Wikipedia memberi contoh bahwa Sun Wukong dalam Xiyouji adalah batu yang menjadi jing lalu berubah menjadi monyet.
did_you_know.en: The Wikipedia article gives the example that Sun Wukong in the Xiyouji is a stone that became a jing and turned into a monkey.

cultural_context.id: Sebuah artikel ensiklopedia menyebut bahwa gagasan jing dipengaruhi pandangan bahwa segala sesuatu berjiwa.
cultural_context.en: An encyclopedia article says the idea of jing is influenced by the view that all things have spirits.

description.id: Sebagian jing digambarkan dapat berubah wujud; jing benda tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia.
description.en: Some jing are described as changing form; the jing of aged things can assume human form.

description.id: Legenda menyebut jingguai memiliki kemampuan seperti ilmu ilusi.
description.en: Legends say jingguai have abilities such as illusion arts.

description.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jing benda tua tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di cermin; wujud makhluk burung atau hewan tampak di cermin, sehingga daoshi menggantungkan cermin di punggung mereka.
description.en: According to the Baopuzi, the jing of aged things cannot change their true form in a mirror; the form of bird- or beast-spirits shows in the mirror, so Daoists hung mirrors on their backs.

variants.name: Fox, snake, tree and flower spirits

description.id: Jing yang dinamai menurut wujud asalnya: rubah, ular, pohon, bunga; umumnya disebut "[nama wujud asal] + jing".
description.en: Jing named for their original form: fox, snake, tree, flower; usually called "[original form] + jing".

description.id: Jing kayu disebut Youguang dan jing logam disebut Qingming dalam ucapan yang dikutip teks itu.
description.en: The jing of wood is called Youguang and the jing of metal Qingming in a saying quoted by the text.

title.id: Pengunjung yang tampak sebagai rusa di cermin
title.en: The visitor who appears as a deer in the mirror

role.id: Jing rusa tua menyamar sebagai manusia lalu terbongkar oleh cermin.
role.en: An old deer spirit disguises itself as a person and is exposed by the mirror.

summary.id: Dua orang di sebuah gua batu melihat seorang pengunjung berpakaian manusia tampak sebagai rusa di cermin; saat ditegur sebagai rusa tua, ia berubah menjadi rusa dan lari.
summary.en: Two men in a stone chamber see a visitor in human dress appear as a deer in the mirror; when addressed as an old deer he turns into a deer and runs off.

note.id: Konsep serupa di Jepang: perkakas tua menjadi tsukumogami.
note.en: A similar concept in Japan: old utensils becoming tsukumogami.

note.id: Rubah-jing disebut sebagai wakil jingguai.
note.en: The fox spirit is named as the representative jingguai.

note.id: Salah satu jing yang disebut dalam teks klasik.
note.en: One of the jing named in a classical text.

questions.en: Why was a mirror believed able to reveal a jing's true form?

questions.en: What distinguishes jing from other nature spirits in Chinese tradition?

sources.author: 干寶 (Gan Bao)

claim.id: Jing adalah kategori roh gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
claim.en: Jing is a category of supernatural spirit in Chinese tradition.

claims_provenance.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

claim.id: Makhluk hidup dan benda dapat mengembangkan roh semacam itu seiring waktu.
claim.en: Living beings and objects may develop such spirits over time.

claims_provenance.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

claim.id: Sebagian digambarkan dapat berubah menjadi berbagai wujud.
claim.en: Some are described as changing into different forms.

claims_provenance.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

claim.id: Contohnya meliputi roh rubah, ular, pohon, dan bunga.
claim.en: Examples include fox, snake, tree and flower spirits.

claims_provenance.quote: 精怪的代表可算狐狸精，其次還有蛇精、樹精和花精等等。稱呼時大多稱為「〔原形名〕+精」。

claim.id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Mandarin ini, Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu memiliki roh yang lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman; jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah lengkap menurut Baize Jingguai Tu dan sejenisnya, dan selain hewan serta tumbuhan juga mencakup benda mati seperti perkakas.
claim.en: According to this Chinese Wikipedia article, the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits which over time turn into monsters; Chinese jing have a complete genealogy according to works such as the Baize Jingguai Tu, and include non-living things such as utensils besides animals and plants.

claims_provenance.quote: 东晋干宝搜神记认为万物有灵，久了就会化作妖怪。中国的精，依《白泽精怪图》等书的记载有一个完整的谱系，其中印度的传入也汇进这个谱系。同时，中国的精除动植物之外，也有非生物包括器具，日本的精有较多受中国影响。

claim.id: Secara umum dipercaya bahwa segala hal, hidup maupun tidak, yang hidup atau tersimpan seratus atau seribu tahun lebih akan menyerap sari alam dan menjadi jing, yang juga disebut jingguai.
claim.en: It is widely believed that all things, living or not, that live or are kept for a hundred or a thousand years or more absorb the essence of nature and become jing, also called jingguai.

claims_provenance.quote: 普遍认为各种事物包括生物和非生物，只要活或保存百年、千年以上时间就会吸收自然界的精华成精，亦稱為精怪。

claim.id: Menurut legenda Tiongkok, sebagian kejadian ganjil yang berkaitan dengan manusia mungkin dipengaruhi jingguai; legenda menyebut jingguai memiliki kemampuan seperti berubah wujud dan ilmu ilusi, serta dapat bersemayam pada benda-benda tertentu.
claim.en: According to Chinese legend, some strange phenomena involving people may be influenced by jingguai; the legends say they have abilities such as transformation and illusion arts and may lodge in certain objects.

claims_provenance.quote: 中国传说认为包括与人有关的怪异现象可能有些是精怪影响的，传说精怪会包括变身、幻术等不同能力，还会寄宿在一些物体上。

claim.id: Selain Tiongkok, Jepang juga memiliki konsep serupa, misalnya legenda perkakas tua yang menjadi tsukumogami.
claim.en: Besides China, regions such as Japan have a similar concept, for example the legend of old utensils becoming tsukumogami.

claims_provenance.quote: 除了中国，其他一些地区如日本亦有类似成精的概念，如陈旧器具变「付喪神」的传说。

claim.id: Dalam budaya Timur, yaoguai kadang disebut yaojing, dan dalam percakapan huruf yao, jing, dan guai sering dipakai bersama atau saling menggantikan.
claim.en: In Eastern cultures a yaoguai is sometimes called a yaojing, and in speech the characters yao, jing and guai are often used together and sometimes interchangeably.

claims_provenance.quote: 在东方文化妖怪有时也叫妖精，在口語中，「妖」、「精」、「怪」幾個字經常連用，有時候還能相互替換。

claim.id: Contoh yang disebut: Sun Wukong dalam Xiyouji adalah batu yang menjadi jing lalu berubah menjadi monyet.
claim.en: The example given is Sun Wukong in the Xiyouji, a stone that became a jing and turned into a monkey.

claims_provenance.quote: 然后变成其他生物、非生物或人形态。（如西游记孙悟空就石头成精变猴子）

claim.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jing semua benda yang sudah tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan mata dan terus menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di dalam cermin.
claim.en: According to the Baopuzi, the jing of all aged things can all assume human form to dazzle people's eyes and constantly test them, but cannot change their true form in a mirror.

claims_provenance.quote: 又萬物之老者，其精悉能假讬人形，以眩惑人目而常試人，唯不能於鏡中易其真形耳。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Baopuzi (抱朴子), juan 17 (抱朴子/卷17)

claim.id: Menurut Baopuzi, para daoshi zaman dahulu yang masuk gunung menggantungkan cermin terang berdiameter sembilan cun atau lebih di punggung mereka, sehingga laomei (siluman tua) tidak berani mendekat.
claim.en: According to the Baopuzi, ancient Daoists entering the mountains hung a bright mirror nine cun or more in diameter behind their backs, so that the old spirits (laomei) dared not come near people.

claims_provenance.quote: 是以古之入山道士，皆以明鏡徑九寸已上，懸於背後，則老魅不敢近人。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Baopuzi (抱朴子), juan 17 (抱朴子/卷17)

claim.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jika yang datang adalah siluman burung atau hewan, wujudnya tampak di cermin; siluman tua yang datang juga pergi dengan berjalan mundur dan tidak punya tumit.
claim.en: According to the Baopuzi, if the visitor is a bird- or beast-spirit its form shows in the mirror; an old spirit that comes also leaves walking backwards and has no heels.

claims_provenance.quote: 若是鳥獸邪魅，則其形貌皆見鏡中矣。又老魅若來，其去必卻行，行可轉鏡對之，其後而視之，若是老魅者，必無踵也
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Baopuzi (抱朴子), juan 17 (抱朴子/卷17)

claim.id: Dalam kisah Baopuzi tentang dua orang di sebuah gua batu, seorang pengunjung berpakaian seperti manusia tampak sebagai rusa di cermin; ketika ditegur sebagai rusa tua, ia berubah menjadi rusa dan lari.
claim.en: In a Baopuzi tale of two men in a stone chamber, a visitor dressed as a person appears as a deer in the mirror; when addressed as an old deer he turns into a deer and runs off.

claims_provenance.quote: 於是二人顧視鏡中，乃是鹿也。因問之曰：汝是山中老鹿，何敢詐為人形。言未絕，而來人即成鹿而走去。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Baopuzi (抱朴子), juan 17 (抱朴子/卷17)

claim.id: Menurut ucapan yang dikutip dalam Soushenji dari Baize Tu, di antara dua gunung ada jing berupa anak kecil bernama Xinang yang mengulurkan tangan untuk menarik orang, dan ia mati bila ditarik dari tempat asalnya.
claim.en: According to a saying quoted in the Soushenji from the Baize Tu, between two mountains there is a jing like a small child named Xinang that stretches out a hand to pull people, and it dies if drawn away from its old place.

claims_provenance.quote: 此事在白澤圖內；曰：『兩山之間，其精如小兒，見人，則伸手欲引人，名曰「傒囊」，引去故地，則死。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Soushenji (搜神記), juan 12 (搜神記/第12卷)

claim.id: Soushenji mengutip ucapan bahwa jing kayu adalah "Youguang" dan jing logam adalah "Qingming".
claim.en: The Soushenji quotes a saying that the jing of wood is "Youguang" and the jing of metal is "Qingming".

claims_provenance.quote: 索縛，則可得食。」王子曰：「木精為『游光』，金精為『清明』也。」
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource (Chinese) — Soushenji (搜神記), juan 12 (搜神記/第12卷)

long_description.id: Artikel Wikipedia menyebut bahwa Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu berjiwa dan lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman, bahwa jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah menurut Baize Jingguai Tu, dan bahwa Jepang memiliki konsep serupa seperti tsukumogami. Soushenji sendiri mengutip Baize Tu tentang jing anak kecil bernama Xinang di antara dua gunung.
long_description.en: The Wikipedia article says the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits and over time turn into monsters, that Chinese jing have a genealogy according to the Baize Jingguai Tu, and that Japan has a similar concept such as tsukumogami. The Soushenji itself quotes the Baize Tu about a child-like jing named Xinang between two mountains.

claims.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

statement.id: Jing adalah kategori roh gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Jing is a category of supernatural spirit in Chinese tradition.

claims.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

statement.id: Makhluk hidup dan benda dapat mengembangkan roh semacam itu seiring waktu.
statement.en: Living beings and objects may develop such spirits over time.

claims.quote: 精，是一種超自然生命體，在世界各国皆有传说，天地万物皆可能寄宿精。有生物或非生物日积月累变成妖怪的成精，也有本来活在自然环境的自然精灵，有些能幻化成不同形态。

statement.id: Sebagian digambarkan dapat berubah menjadi berbagai wujud.
statement.en: Some are described as changing into different forms.

claims.quote: 精怪的代表可算狐狸精，其次還有蛇精、樹精和花精等等。稱呼時大多稱為「〔原形名〕+精」。

statement.id: Contohnya meliputi roh rubah, ular, pohon, dan bunga.
statement.en: Examples include fox, snake, tree and flower spirits.

claims.quote: 东晋干宝搜神记认为万物有灵，久了就会化作妖怪。中国的精，依《白泽精怪图》等书的记载有一个完整的谱系，其中印度的传入也汇进这个谱系。同时，中国的精除动植物之外，也有非生物包括器具，日本的精有较多受中国影响。

statement.id: Menurut artikel Wikipedia berbahasa Mandarin ini, Soushenji menganggap segala sesuatu memiliki roh yang lama-kelamaan menjadi siluman; jing dalam Tiongkok memiliki silsilah lengkap menurut Baize Jingguai Tu dan sejenisnya, dan selain hewan serta tumbuhan juga mencakup benda mati seperti perkakas.
statement.en: According to this Chinese Wikipedia article, the Soushenji holds that all things have spirits which over time turn into monsters; Chinese jing have a complete genealogy according to works such as the Baize Jingguai Tu, and include non-living things such as utensils besides animals and plants.

claims.quote: 普遍认为各种事物包括生物和非生物，只要活或保存百年、千年以上时间就会吸收自然界的精华成精，亦稱為精怪。

statement.id: Secara umum dipercaya bahwa segala hal, hidup maupun tidak, yang hidup atau tersimpan seratus atau seribu tahun lebih akan menyerap sari alam dan menjadi jing, yang juga disebut jingguai.
statement.en: It is widely believed that all things, living or not, that live or are kept for a hundred or a thousand years or more absorb the essence of nature and become jing, also called jingguai.

claims.quote: 中国传说认为包括与人有关的怪异现象可能有些是精怪影响的，传说精怪会包括变身、幻术等不同能力，还会寄宿在一些物体上。

statement.id: Menurut legenda Tiongkok, sebagian kejadian ganjil yang berkaitan dengan manusia mungkin dipengaruhi jingguai; legenda menyebut jingguai memiliki kemampuan seperti berubah wujud dan ilmu ilusi, serta dapat bersemayam pada benda-benda tertentu.
statement.en: According to Chinese legend, some strange phenomena involving people may be influenced by jingguai; the legends say they have abilities such as transformation and illusion arts and may lodge in certain objects.

claims.quote: 除了中国，其他一些地区如日本亦有类似成精的概念，如陈旧器具变「付喪神」的传说。

statement.id: Selain Tiongkok, Jepang juga memiliki konsep serupa, misalnya legenda perkakas tua yang menjadi tsukumogami.
statement.en: Besides China, regions such as Japan have a similar concept, for example the legend of old utensils becoming tsukumogami.

claims.quote: 在东方文化妖怪有时也叫妖精，在口語中，「妖」、「精」、「怪」幾個字經常連用，有時候還能相互替換。

statement.id: Dalam budaya Timur, yaoguai kadang disebut yaojing, dan dalam percakapan huruf yao, jing, dan guai sering dipakai bersama atau saling menggantikan.
statement.en: In Eastern cultures a yaoguai is sometimes called a yaojing, and in speech the characters yao, jing and guai are often used together and sometimes interchangeably.

claims.quote: 然后变成其他生物、非生物或人形态。（如西游记孙悟空就石头成精变猴子）

statement.id: Contoh yang disebut: Sun Wukong dalam Xiyouji adalah batu yang menjadi jing lalu berubah menjadi monyet.
statement.en: The example given is Sun Wukong in the Xiyouji, a stone that became a jing and turned into a monkey.

claims.quote: 又萬物之老者，其精悉能假讬人形，以眩惑人目而常試人，唯不能於鏡中易其真形耳。

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jing semua benda yang sudah tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan mata dan terus menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di dalam cermin.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, the jing of all aged things can all assume human form to dazzle people's eyes and constantly test them, but cannot change their true form in a mirror.

claims.quote: 是以古之入山道士，皆以明鏡徑九寸已上，懸於背後，則老魅不敢近人。

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, para daoshi zaman dahulu yang masuk gunung menggantungkan cermin terang berdiameter sembilan cun atau lebih di punggung mereka, sehingga laomei (siluman tua) tidak berani mendekat.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, ancient Daoists entering the mountains hung a bright mirror nine cun or more in diameter behind their backs, so that the old spirits (laomei) dared not come near people.

claims.quote: 若是鳥獸邪魅，則其形貌皆見鏡中矣。又老魅若來，其去必卻行，行可轉鏡對之，其後而視之，若是老魅者，必無踵也

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jika yang datang adalah siluman burung atau hewan, wujudnya tampak di cermin; siluman tua yang datang juga pergi dengan berjalan mundur dan tidak punya tumit.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, if the visitor is a bird- or beast-spirit its form shows in the mirror; an old spirit that comes also leaves walking backwards and has no heels.

claims.quote: 於是二人顧視鏡中，乃是鹿也。因問之曰：汝是山中老鹿，何敢詐為人形。言未絕，而來人即成鹿而走去。

statement.id: Dalam kisah Baopuzi tentang dua orang di sebuah gua batu, seorang pengunjung berpakaian seperti manusia tampak sebagai rusa di cermin; ketika ditegur sebagai rusa tua, ia berubah menjadi rusa dan lari.
statement.en: In a Baopuzi tale of two men in a stone chamber, a visitor dressed as a person appears as a deer in the mirror; when addressed as an old deer he turns into a deer and runs off.

claims.quote: 此事在白澤圖內；曰：『兩山之間，其精如小兒，見人，則伸手欲引人，名曰「傒囊」，引去故地，則死。

statement.id: Menurut ucapan yang dikutip dalam Soushenji dari Baize Tu, di antara dua gunung ada jing berupa anak kecil bernama Xinang yang mengulurkan tangan untuk menarik orang, dan ia mati bila ditarik dari tempat asalnya.
statement.en: According to a saying quoted in the Soushenji from the Baize Tu, between two mountains there is a jing like a small child named Xinang that stretches out a hand to pull people, and it dies if drawn away from its old place.

claims.quote: 索縛，則可得食。」王子曰：「木精為『游光』，金精為『清明』也。」

statement.en: The Soushenji quotes a saying that the jing of wood is "Youguang" and the jing of metal is "Qingming".

short_description.id: Chaofeng (嘲風) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang digambarkan menyerupai feniks; ia gemar bahaya, dan sosoknya diletakkan di sudut atap dan sudut istana.
short_description.en: Chaofeng (嘲風) is one of the dragon's nine sons, depicted as phoenix-like; it likes danger, and its likeness is placed at roof edges and palace corners.

long_description.id:
Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Chaofeng adalah salah satu putra naga dalam uraian Li Dongyang di 懐麓堂集. Wujudnya menyerupai feniks (鳳凰), penjelmaan burung. Ia konon menyukai tempat terjal dan memandang jauh, sehingga diletakkan di tepi atap bangunan.

Beberapa teks Ming mencatat daftar putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran". Dalam Shuo Lüe karya Gu Qiyuan, 嘲風 gemar bahaya dan berada di sudut istana; dalam Yangsheng fuyu karya Chen Jiru, ia gemar bahaya sepanjang hidupnya dan binatang-binatang yang berlari di sudut istana adalah sosoknya. Shuo Lüe menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi kaisar menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui.

Penulis Shuo Lüe sendiri meragukan daftar itu: setelah memeriksa catatan, ia menilai teori tersebut tidak berdasar dan menyisihkan 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 sebagai nama yang menunggu penelitian. Yŏrha ilgi membandingkan beberapa teks: Duilei zonggui menyebut 嘲風 berdiri di sudut istana, sedangkan Bowuzhi yipian menyebut 螭吻 (Chiwen) yang berdiri di sudut istana. Penulisnya bertanya bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
long_description.en:
According to Japanese Wikipedia, Chaofeng is one of the dragon's sons in Li Dongyang's account in the 懐麓堂集. It resembles a phoenix (鳳凰), an incarnation of a bird. It is said to like steep places and distant views, which is why it is placed on the eaves of roofs.

Several Ming texts record a list of dragon sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness". In Gu Qiyuan's Shuo Lüe, 嘲風 likes danger and is at palace corners; in Chen Jiru's Yangsheng fuyu, it liked danger all its life and the running beasts on palace corners are its likeness. The Shuo Lüe adds that in the Hongzhi period the emperor asked Li Dongyang for the names of the nine sons, and that Li obtained his information from an old register whose origin is unknown.

The author of the Shuo Lüe himself doubts the list: after examining records he judged the theory unfounded and set 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 aside as names awaiting investigation. The Yŏrha ilgi compares several texts: the Duilei zonggui has 嘲風 standing at the palace corner, while the Bowuzhi yipian has 螭吻 (Chiwen) standing at the palace corner. Its author asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and calls old theories of this kind mostly embellishment.

claim.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Chaofeng adalah salah satu putra naga menurut uraian Li Dongyang dalam Huailutang ji (懐麓堂集), digambarkan sebagai burung mirip feniks.
claim.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Chaofeng is a dragon offspring in Li Dongyang’s account in the Huailutang ji (懐麓堂集), depicted as a phoenix-like bird.

claims_provenance.quote: 嘲風（ちょうふう、Chaofeng）は、李東陽が著した『懐麓堂集』の説による竜生九子の一つ。姿は鳳凰に似て鳥の化身である。

claim.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, ia konon menyukai tempat terjal dan memandang jauh.
claim.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, it is said to favor steep places and distant views.

claims_provenance.quote: 険しいところを好み、遠くを眺める事を好むともされることから、建物の屋根の軒に置かれる。

claim.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, kegemaran itu menjelaskan penempatannya pada tepi atap bangunan.
claim.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, this preference explains its placement on the eaves of roofs.

claims_provenance.quote: 険しいところを好み、遠くを眺める事を好むともされることから、建物の屋根の軒に置かれる。

claim.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 嘲風 yang gemar bahaya (好險) dan berada di sudut istana (在殿角). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
claim.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 嘲風, which likes danger (好險) and is at palace corners (在殿角). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

claims_provenance.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。
claims_provenance.source_citation: Wikisource — 說略/卷三十 | 維基文庫

claim.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe mengingat pernah melihat teori itu dalam Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) ketika berusia sebelas atau dua belas tahun, tetapi setelah memeriksa catatan ia menyimpulkan teori itu tidak berdasar (不經). Dari nama-nama yang dibahasnya, tak satu pun ia temukan dalam catatan sebagai putra naga; 囚牛, 嘲風 (Chaofeng), dan 霸下 ia tinggalkan sebagai "menunggu penelitian" (俟考).
claim.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe recalls seeing the theory in the Duilei zonggui (對類總龜) when he was eleven or twelve, but after examining records he concluded that it was not canonical (不經). Of the names he discusses, he found none in records described as a dragon's son; 囚牛, 嘲風 (Chaofeng) and 霸下 he left as "to be examined" (俟考).

short_description.id: Chaofeng (嘲風) adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga yang digambarkan menyerupai feniks; ia gemar bahaya, dan sosoknya diletakkan di sudut atap dan sudut istana.
short_description.en: Chaofeng (嘲風) is one of the dragon's nine sons, depicted as phoenix-like; it likes danger, and its likeness is placed at roof edges and palace corners.

long_description.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, Chaofeng adalah salah satu putra naga dalam uraian Li Dongyang di 懐麓堂集. Wujudnya menyerupai feniks (鳳凰), penjelmaan burung. Ia konon menyukai tempat terjal dan memandang jauh, sehingga diletakkan di tepi atap bangunan.
long_description.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Chaofeng is one of the dragon's sons in Li Dongyang's account in the 懐麓堂集. It resembles a phoenix (鳳凰), an incarnation of a bird. It is said to like steep places and distant views, which is why it is placed on the eaves of roofs.

long_description.id: Beberapa teks Ming mencatat daftar putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran". Dalam Shuo Lüe karya Gu Qiyuan, 嘲風 gemar bahaya dan berada di sudut istana; dalam Yangsheng fuyu karya Chen Jiru, ia gemar bahaya sepanjang hidupnya dan binatang-binatang yang berlari di sudut istana adalah sosoknya. Shuo Lüe menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi kaisar menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui.
long_description.en: Several Ming texts record a list of dragon sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness". In Gu Qiyuan's Shuo Lüe, 嘲風 likes danger and is at palace corners; in Chen Jiru's Yangsheng fuyu, it liked danger all its life and the running beasts on palace corners are its likeness. The Shuo Lüe adds that in the Hongzhi period the emperor asked Li Dongyang for the names of the nine sons, and that Li obtained his information from an old register whose origin is unknown.

long_description.id: Penulis Shuo Lüe sendiri meragukan daftar itu: setelah memeriksa catatan, ia menilai teori tersebut tidak berdasar dan menyisihkan 囚牛, 嘲風, dan 霸下 sebagai nama yang menunggu penelitian. Yŏrha ilgi membandingkan beberapa teks: Duilei zonggui menyebut 嘲風 berdiri di sudut istana, sedangkan Bowuzhi yipian menyebut 螭吻 (Chiwen) yang berdiri di sudut istana. Penulisnya bertanya bagaimana nama dan sifat para putra naga dapat diketahui, dan menyebut teori kuno semacam itu banyak yang dibuat-buat.
long_description.en: The author of the Shuo Lüe himself doubts the list: after examining records he judged the theory unfounded and set 囚牛, 嘲風 and 霸下 aside as names awaiting investigation. The Yŏrha ilgi compares several texts: the Duilei zonggui has 嘲風 standing at the palace corner, while the Bowuzhi yipian has 螭吻 (Chiwen) standing at the palace corner. Its author asks how the dragon sons' names and natures can be known, and calls old theories of this kind mostly embellishment.

claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。

statement.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 嘲風, which likes danger (好險) and is at palace corners (在殿角). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

short_description.id: 䍺 (Huan) adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok. Shan Hai Jing menggambarkannya seperti domba tanpa mulut yang tidak dapat dibunuh, sedangkan Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebutnya lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana.
short_description.en: 䍺 (Huan) is a legendary Chinese animal. The Shan Hai Jing describes it as a sheep-like beast without a mouth that cannot be killed, while Japanese Wikipedia says it was born from the distress of imprisoned people.

long_description.id:
Dalam Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經), 䍺 adalah hewan di gunung 洵 yang bentuknya seperti domba tetapi tanpa mulut dan tidak dapat dibunuh. Catatan tafsir pada teks itu memberi bunyi namanya sebagai 還 atau 患. Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa juga menyebutnya 患 (羊患), makhluk legendaris Tiongkok kuno yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing.

Wikipedia bahasa Jepang memberi gambaran lain: 䍺 adalah hewan legendaris yang lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana yang dikurung di penjara. Tubuhnya digambarkan seperti kambing dengan mata biru, tingginya tujuh sampai delapan meter pada yang kecil dan lebih dari sepuluh meter pada yang besar, dan kakinya tertanam di tanah sehingga tidak dapat digerakkan oleh tenaga manusia.

Wikipedia bahasa Jepang mengaitkannya dengan kisah Kaisar Wu dari dinasti Han: makhluk raksasa menghalangi rombongan, dan Dongfang Shuo mengenalinya lalu menyiramnya dengan banyak arak hingga lenyap. Kisah serupa dalam Taiping guangji, yang dikutip dari Soushenji, menggambarkan sesuatu seperti sapi di Celah Hangu yang lenyap setelah disiram arak, karena menurut Dongfang Shuo ia terlahir dari kesusahan dan arak membuat orang melupakan kekhawatiran.
long_description.en:
In the Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section), 䍺 is a beast on Xun mountain (洵) shaped like a sheep but without a mouth, and it cannot be killed. The commentary on the text gives the sound of its name as 還 or 患. Chinese Wikipedia also calls it 患 (羊患), a legendary creature of ancient China recorded in the Shan Hai Jing.

Japanese Wikipedia gives a different picture: 䍺 is a legendary animal born from the distress of convicts shut up in prison. Its body is described as goat-like with blue eyes, seven to eight metres tall for the smaller ones and over ten metres for the larger, and its feet are sunk into the ground so that human strength cannot move it.

Japanese Wikipedia links it with a story of Emperor Wu of the Han dynasty: a giant creature blocked the party, and Dongfang Shuo recognised it and poured a great deal of wine over it until it vanished. A similar tale in the Taiping guangji, quoted from the Soushenji, describes an ox-shaped thing at Hangu Pass that vanished when wine was poured on it, because according to Dongfang Shuo it was born of affliction and wine makes people forget worry.

claim.en: In a tale quoted in the Taiping guangji from the Soushenji (搜神記): when Emperor Wu of Han travelled east and reached Hangu Pass (函谷關), something blocked the road; its body was several zhang long, it was shaped like an ox, with gleaming blue eyes, and its four feet were sunk into the earth; it moved but did not shift.

claim.id: Para pejabat ketakutan; Dongfang Shuo meminta arak untuk disiramkan ke makhluk itu, dan setelah beberapa puluh hu makhluk itu lenyap. Ia menjelaskan bahwa makhluk itu bernama 憂 (kekhawatiran), terlahir dari 患 (kesusahan); tempat itu pasti bekas penjara Qin, dan karena arak membuat orang melupakan kekhawatiran, arak dapat melenyapkannya.
claim.en: The officials were frightened; Dongfang Shuo asked for wine to be poured on it, and after several dozen hu it vanished. He explained that it is named 憂 (worry), something produced by 患 (affliction); the place must be a Qin prison site, and since wine makes one forget worry, wine could dispel it.

claims_provenance.quote: 百官驚懼，東方朔乃請酒灌之，灌之數十斛而消。帝問其故，答曰：「此名憂，患之所生也。此必是秦之獄地。不然，罪人徙作地聚。夫酒忘憂，故能消之也。」

short_description.id: 䍺 (Huan) adalah hewan legendaris Tiongkok. Shan Hai Jing menggambarkannya seperti domba tanpa mulut yang tidak dapat dibunuh, sedangkan Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebutnya lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana.
short_description.en: 䍺 (Huan) is a legendary Chinese animal. The Shan Hai Jing describes it as a sheep-like beast without a mouth that cannot be killed, while Japanese Wikipedia says it was born from the distress of imprisoned people.

long_description.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (bagian 南山經), 䍺 adalah hewan di gunung 洵 yang bentuknya seperti domba tetapi tanpa mulut dan tidak dapat dibunuh. Catatan tafsir pada teks itu memberi bunyi namanya sebagai 還 atau 患. Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa juga menyebutnya 患 (羊患), makhluk legendaris Tiongkok kuno yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing.
long_description.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (the 南山經 section), 䍺 is a beast on Xun mountain (洵) shaped like a sheep but without a mouth, and it cannot be killed. The commentary on the text gives the sound of its name as 還 or 患. Chinese Wikipedia also calls it 患 (羊患), a legendary creature of ancient China recorded in the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang memberi gambaran lain: 䍺 adalah hewan legendaris yang lahir dari kesusahan para narapidana yang dikurung di penjara. Tubuhnya digambarkan seperti kambing dengan mata biru, tingginya tujuh sampai delapan meter pada yang kecil dan lebih dari sepuluh meter pada yang besar, dan kakinya tertanam di tanah sehingga tidak dapat digerakkan oleh tenaga manusia.
long_description.en: Japanese Wikipedia gives a different picture: 䍺 is a legendary animal born from the distress of convicts shut up in prison. Its body is described as goat-like with blue eyes, seven to eight metres tall for the smaller ones and over ten metres for the larger, and its feet are sunk into the ground so that human strength cannot move it.

long_description.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang mengaitkannya dengan kisah Kaisar Wu dari dinasti Han: makhluk raksasa menghalangi rombongan, dan Dongfang Shuo mengenalinya lalu menyiramnya dengan banyak arak hingga lenyap. Kisah serupa dalam Taiping guangji, yang dikutip dari Soushenji, menggambarkan sesuatu seperti sapi di Celah Hangu yang lenyap setelah disiram arak, karena menurut Dongfang Shuo ia terlahir dari kesusahan dan arak membuat orang melupakan kekhawatiran.
long_description.en: Japanese Wikipedia links it with a story of Emperor Wu of the Han dynasty: a giant creature blocked the party, and Dongfang Shuo recognised it and poured a great deal of wine over it until it vanished. A similar tale in the Taiping guangji, quoted from the Soushenji, describes an ox-shaped thing at Hangu Pass that vanished when wine was poured on it, because according to Dongfang Shuo it was born of affliction and wine makes people forget worry.

short_description.id: White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok.
short_description.en: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.

long_description.id:
White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok. Harimau Putih berhubungan dengan arah barat dan musim gugur.

Nama lintas bahasanya meliputi Byakko di Jepang dan Baekho di Korea. Wilayah rasi Harimau Putih mencakup tujuh kedudukan bulan.

Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun mengaitkan barat dengan logam dan menyebut Harimau Putih sebagai binatang arah itu, sedangkan Liji bab Quli shang menempatkannya di sisi kanan dengan Naga Biru di sisi kiri. Dalam bacaan Werner, Naga Biru dan Harimau Putih menjalankan di kuil Tao tugas yang di kuil Buddha dijalankan Heng dan Ha di gerbang. Werner juga menceritakan Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, yang gugur ketika berusaha membalas ayahnya dan kemudian diangkat sebagai Roh Bintang Harimau Putih.
long_description.en:
White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations. The White Tiger corresponds to west and autumn.

Its names in neighboring traditions include Japanese Byakko and Korean Baekho. The White Tiger's constellation region contains seven lunar mansions.

The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun associates the west with metal and names the White Tiger as the beast of that direction, while the Liji chapter Quli shang places it on the right with the Azure Dragon on the left. In Werner's account, the Blue Dragon and White Tiger discharge in Taoist temples the functions that Heng and Ha discharge at Buddhist temple gates. Werner also tells of Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, who died trying to avenge his father and was later canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

claim.en: The White Tiger's constellation region contains seven lunar mansions.

claims_provenance.quote: As with the other three Symbols, there are seven astrological "Mansions" (positions of the Moon) within the White Tiger. The names and determinative stars are:

claim.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa arah barat adalah logam (金), kaisarnya Shaohao (少昊), pembantunya Rushou (蓐收) yang memegang penyiku dan mengatur musim gugur (治秋); rohnya adalah Taibai (太白) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Harimau Putih (白虎).
claim.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the west is metal (金), its emperor is Shaohao (少昊) and its assistant Rushou (蓐收), who holds the square and governs autumn (治秋); its spirit is Taibai (太白) and its beast (獸) is the White Tiger (白虎).

claims_provenance.quote: 西方，金也，其帝少昊，其佐蓐收，執矩而治秋。其神為太白，其獸白虎，其音商，其日庚辛。

claim.id: Liji bab Quli shang (曲禮上) menempatkan Naga Biru (青龍) di sisi kiri dan Harimau Putih (白虎) di sisi kanan, dengan 招摇 (Zhaoyao) di atas; gerak maju-mundur berpedoman pada aturan dan tiap bagian memegang tugas masing-masing.
claim.en: The Liji chapter Quli shang (曲禮上) puts the Azure Dragon (青龍) on the left and the White Tiger (白虎) on the right, with 招摇 (Zhaoyao) above; advance and retreat follow rules and each part keeps its own post.

claims_provenance.quote: 左青龍而右白虎，招摇在上，急繕其怒。進退有度，左右有局，各司其局。

short_description.en: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations.

long_description.id: White Tiger adalah Harimau Putih dalam Empat Lambang rasi Tiongkok. Harimau Putih berhubungan dengan arah barat dan musim gugur.
long_description.en: White Tiger belongs to the Four Symbols of Chinese constellations. The White Tiger corresponds to west and autumn.

long_description.id: Nama lintas bahasanya meliputi Byakko di Jepang dan Baekho di Korea. Wilayah rasi Harimau Putih mencakup tujuh kedudukan bulan.
long_description.en: Its names in neighboring traditions include Japanese Byakko and Korean Baekho. The White Tiger's constellation region contains seven lunar mansions.

long_description.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun mengaitkan barat dengan logam dan menyebut Harimau Putih sebagai binatang arah itu, sedangkan Liji bab Quli shang menempatkannya di sisi kanan dengan Naga Biru di sisi kiri. Dalam bacaan Werner, Naga Biru dan Harimau Putih menjalankan di kuil Tao tugas yang di kuil Buddha dijalankan Heng dan Ha di gerbang. Werner juga menceritakan Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, yang gugur ketika berusaha membalas ayahnya dan kemudian diangkat sebagai Roh Bintang Harimau Putih.
long_description.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun associates the west with metal and names the White Tiger as the beast of that direction, while the Liji chapter Quli shang places it on the right with the Azure Dragon on the left. In Werner's account, the Blue Dragon and White Tiger discharge in Taoist temples the functions that Heng and Ha discharge at Buddhist temple gates. Werner also tells of Yin Ch'eng-hsiu, who died trying to avenge his father and was later canonized as the Spirit of the White Tiger Star.

short_description.id: Yako atau nogitsune adalah jenis kitsune (roh rubah) liar berpangkat rendah yang dikisahkan di Kyūshū, dikenal merasuki orang dan menjelma manusia.
short_description.en: Yako, or nogitsune, is a type of low-ranking wild kitsune (fox spirit) told about in Kyūshū, known for possessing people and taking human form.

long_description.id:
Yako atau nogitsune (野狐) adalah jenis kitsune (roh rubah) yang dikisahkan di Kyūshū. Kerasukannya disebut yako-tsuki. Kata 野狐 juga dipakai bagi rubah liar secara umum. Menurut Yokai.com, istilah ini merujuk pada kitsune liar berpangkat rendah yang bukan utusan dewa.

Rupanya hampir selalu sama dalam semua legenda: hitam atau putih, sedikit lebih besar dari tikus dan lebih kecil dari kucing. Yako asli dikatakan tak terlihat mata. Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune dikenal menjelma manusia, memerlukan benda sihir seperti tulang sapi atau kuda untuk berubah wujud, dan sering merasuki orang.

Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune takut pada cahaya terang, benda tajam, dan anjing, serta menyelinap ke permukiman pada malam hari untuk mencuri lilin, minyak lampu, pernis, alkohol, dan tahu goreng. Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Kyūshū selatan garis keluarga dapat dirasuki yako dan di Pulau Iki yako yang menyerupai musang dikatakan bersembunyi di ketiak orang.
long_description.en:
Yako or nogitsune (野狐) is a type of kitsune (fox spirit) told about in Kyūshū. Possession by it is called yako-tsuki. The word 野狐 is also used for wild foxes in general. According to Yokai.com the term refers to low-ranking wild kitsune who are not messengers of the gods.

Its appearance is almost completely consistent among all legends: black or white, a little bigger than a mouse yet smaller than a cat. Legends also say the first yako cannot be seen by the eye. According to Yokai.com, nogitsune are known for transforming into humans, need a magical focus such as a cow or horse bone to change shape, and often possess people.

According to Yokai.com, nogitsune fear bright light, bladed objects and dogs, and sneak into inhabited areas at night to steal candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol and fried tofu. Wikipedia notes that in Southern Kyūshū family lines can be possessed by yako and on Iki Island weasel-like yako are said to hide under people's armpits.

statement.id: Yako adalah roh rubah dalam cerita dari Kyūshū.
statement.en: Yako is a fox spirit in stories from Kyūshū.

claims.quote: To be possessed by it is called "yako-tsuki" (野狐憑き).

statement.id: Kerasukan roh ini disebut yako-tsuki.
statement.en: Possession by this spirit is called yako-tsuki.

claims.quote: is also used for foxes in the wild in general.

statement.id: Bentuk tulis namanya juga dapat berarti rubah liar biasa.
statement.en: Its written name can also mean an ordinary wild fox.

claims.quote: The appearance of a yako is almost completely consistent among all legends; they are black or white, are slightly larger than a mouse, and smaller than a cat.

statement.id: Menurut kisah, tubuhnya kecil dan berwarna hitam atau putih.
statement.en: Accounts give it black or white coloring and a small body.

claims.quote: Nogitsune, also frequently called yako, are a type of kitsune-magical foxes found in East Asian folklore. Specifically the term refers to low ranking, wild kitsune that do not have a divine soul or serve as messengers of the gods.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune, yang sering juga disebut yako, adalah jenis kitsune; istilah ini merujuk pada kitsune liar berpangkat rendah yang tidak memiliki jiwa ilahi dan bukan utusan dewa.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune, also frequently called yako, are a type of kitsune; the term refers to low-ranking wild kitsune that have no divine soul and are not messengers of the gods.

claims.quote: They are particularly known for transforming into humans. In folktales where humans are tormented, tricked, or possessed by kitsune, the culprit is almost always a nogitsune.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune terutama dikenal karena menjelma manusia, dan dalam dongeng tentang manusia yang disiksa, ditipu, atau dirasuki kitsune, pelakunya hampir selalu nogitsune.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune are particularly known for transforming into humans, and in folktales where humans are tormented, tricked or possessed by kitsune, the culprit is almost always a nogitsune.

claims.quote: They dislike bright light, and hide from the sun during the daytime. They are also afraid of bladed objects, and will avoid swords and knives. They are frightened of dogs as well.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune tidak suka cahaya terang dan bersembunyi dari matahari di siang hari, takut pada benda tajam seperti pedang dan pisau, dan takut pada anjing.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune dislike bright light and hide from the sun by day, fear bladed objects such as swords and knives, and are frightened of dogs.

claims.quote: In order to change its shape, a nogitsune requires a magical focus of some kind; usually a bone from a cow or a horse. Kitsunetsuki-possession by a fox spirit-is also commonly performed by nogitsune.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, untuk berubah wujud nogitsune memerlukan benda sihir, biasanya tulang sapi atau kuda; kitsunetsuki (perasukan oleh roh rubah) juga sering dilakukan nogitsune.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, to change shape a nogitsune needs a magical focus, usually a bone from a cow or horse; kitsunetsuki, possession by a fox spirit, is also commonly performed by nogitsune.

claims.quote: they like to sneak into human-inhabited areas at night to steal some of their favorite foods: wax candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol, and fried tofu.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, nogitsune menyelinap ke permukiman manusia pada malam hari untuk mencuri makanan kesukaan mereka: lilin, minyak lampu, pernis, alkohol, dan tahu goreng.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, nogitsune sneak into human-inhabited areas at night to steal favourite foods: wax candles, lamp oil, lacquer, alcohol and fried tofu.

claims.quote: The most common one-yako-is simply another reading of the kanji in its name. The name yakan (野干) is more archaic, and has its origins in a different animal.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, yako hanyalah cara baca lain kanji nama nogitsune, sedangkan nama yakan (野干) lebih arkais dan berasal dari hewan yang berbeda.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, yako is simply another reading of the kanji of its name, while the name yakan (野干) is more archaic and originates from a different animal.

claims.quote: Nogitsune 野狐 のぎつね Translation: wild fox Alternate names: yako, yakan

statement.id: Yokai.com menulis 野狐 (のぎつね) dengan terjemahan "rubah liar" dan nama lain yako dan yakan.
statement.en: Yokai.com gives 野狐 (のぎつね) with the translation "wild fox" and the alternate names yako and yakan.

claims.quote: The original yako is said to be invisible to the eye. In Hirado, Nagasaki Prefecture, they normally bring along a great crowd that walks with them

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa yako asli dikatakan tak terlihat mata, dan di Hirado, Prefektur Nagasaki, mereka biasanya membawa serombongan besar yang berjalan bersama mereka.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that the original yako is said to be invisible to the eye, and that in Hirado, Nagasaki Prefecture, they normally bring along a great crowd that walks with them.

claims.quote: In Southern Kyūshū, family lines would get possessed by a yako, and family lines that raised yako (possessed by a yako) would have their progeny possessed, and if they were no longer able to support it, it would possess its cattle and horses.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Kyūshū selatan garis keluarga dapat dirasuki yako, keturunannya ikut dirasuki, dan bila tak sanggup lagi memeliharanya, yako merasuki ternak dan kuda mereka.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that in Southern Kyūshū family lines would get possessed by a yako, their progeny would be possessed, and if they could no longer support it, it would possess their cattle and horses.

claims.quote: On Iki Island, they are also called yako, and since they resemble weasels, it is said that when one of them conceals themselves under a person's armpits, that person would become possessed by a yako.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa di Pulau Iki mereka juga disebut yako dan menyerupai musang; bila salah satunya bersembunyi di ketiak seseorang, orang itu dikatakan dirasuki yako.
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that on Iki Island they are also called yako and resemble weasels; when one conceals itself under a person's armpits, that person is said to become possessed by a yako.

short_description.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir dalam mitologi, yang menurut Kojiki bersemayam di jasad Izanami di Yomi dan mengejar Izanagi.
short_description.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of the eight thunder kami in mythology, which in the Kojiki dwell in Izanami's corpse in Yomi and pursue Izanagi.

long_description.id:
Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir. Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai. Unsur ikazuchi (雷) berarti petir. Delapan kami ini mencakup, antara lain, Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi, dan Ō-ikazuchi.

Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, kedelapan kami petir membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami seperti dilihat Izanagi di Yomi. Kojiki menempatkan petir pada kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, kedua tangan, dan kedua kaki Izanami, sedangkan satu tulisan alternatif Nihongi memberi penempatan dan sebagian nama yang berbeda. Satu tafsir menyejajarkan kelahiran delapan petir ini dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi.

Menurut beberapa penuturan, para dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk. Setelah Izanagi melihat jasad Izanami dan melarikan diri ketakutan, Izanami mengirim Yomotsu-shikome, 150 pendekar, dan delapan kami petir mengejarnya. Menurut ensiklopedia, Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejar. Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami, sedangkan Nihon Shoki menempatkannya di dubur.
long_description.en:
Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami. The deities represent different forms of storm. The element ikazuchi (雷) means thunder. The eight include Fusu-ikazuchi, Hono-ikazuchi and Ō-ikazuchi, among others.

According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the eight thunder kami festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by Izanagi in Yomi. The Kojiki places thunders in Izanami's head, breast, belly, genitals, both hands and both legs, while an alternate writing in the Nihongi gives a different placement and some different names. One interpretation parallels the birth of these eight thunders with the eight kami from the body of Kagutsuchi.

Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse. After Izanagi saw Izanami's corpse and escaped in horror, Izanami dispatched the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, together with the eight thunder kami to pursue him. According to the encyclopedia, Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and dispersed his pursuers. The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami's belly, while the Nihon Shoki places it in her rectum.

claim.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami dalam Kojiki adalah "delapan jenis kami petir" yang membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami, seperti dilihat suaminya Izanagi di dunia bawah Yomi.
claim.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami of the Kojiki are the "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

claims_provenance.quote: [Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami] (Kojiki) The "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Menurut Kojiki, kedelapan petir itu berada di kepala (petir besar), dada (petir api), perut (petir hitam), kemaluan (petir belah), tangan kiri (petir muda), tangan kanan (petir tanah), kaki kiri (petir bergema), dan kaki kanan (petir beristirahat) Izanami.
claim.en: According to the Kojiki, the eight thunders were in the corpse's head (great thunder), breast (fire thunder), belly (black thunder), genitals (cleft thunder), left hand (young thunder), right hand (earth thunder), left leg (sounding thunder) and right leg (reposing thunder).

claims_provenance.quote: According to Kojiki, in her head was the "great thunder," in her breast was the "fire thunder," in her belly was the "black thunder," in her genitals was the "cleft thunder," in her left hand was the "young thunder," in the right hand was the "earth thunder," in her left leg was the "sounding thunder," and in her right leg was the "reposing thunder."
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Satu "tulisan alternatif" dalam Nihongi menyebut petir besar di kepala, petir api di dada, petir tanah di perut, petir muda di punggung, petir hitam di dubur, petir gunung di tangan, petir ladang di kaki, dan petir belah di kemaluan.
claim.en: An "alternate writing" transmitted by the Nihongi states that great thunder was in her head, fire thunder in her breast, earth thunder in her belly, young thunder in her back, black thunder in her rectum, mountain thunder in her hands, field thunder in her feet and cleft thunder in her genitals.

claims_provenance.quote: An "alternate writing" transmitted by Nihongi, however, states that "great thunder" was in her head, "fire thunder" was in her breast, "earth thunder" was in her belly, "young thunder" was in her back, "black thunder" was in her rectum, "mountain thunder" was in her hands, "field thunder" was in her feet, and "cleft thunder" was in her genitals.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Dari delapan petir itu, tiga memiliki nama dan tempat yang sama dalam dua catatan, tiga hanya sama namanya, dan dua sisanya berbeda.
claim.en: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

claims_provenance.quote: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Lahirnya delapan petir dari jasad Izanami disamakan dengan lahirnya delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi yang terpotong; delapan dianggap angka suci, tetapi di sini mungkin hanya berarti "sangat banyak".
claim.en: The eight thunders produced in Izanami's dead body parallel the eight kami produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi; eight is considered a sacred number but is here likely used merely to denote "a great many".

claims_provenance.quote: The fact that eight thunders were produced in Izanami's dead body parallels the fact that eight kami were produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi. While eight is considered a sacred number, it is here likely used merely to denote "a great many."
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Menurut berbagai catatan Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanami memerintahkan "nenek-nenek Yomi" dan delapan kami petir mengejar Izanagi; Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejarnya.
claim.en: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi; Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and thus dispersed his pursuers.

claims_provenance.quote: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts mentioned above, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi ... Izanagi, however, threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka (the "Even Pass of Yomi"), and thus dispersed his pursuers.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Kokugakuin University (Encyclopedia of Shinto) — Yakusanoikazuchi (Encyclopedia of Shinto)

claim.id: Daftar Wikipedia mencantumkan Fusu-ikazuchi (petir berbaring) dan Hono-ikazuchi (petir api); Kojiki menyebut Hono-ikazuchi berasal dari dada Izanami.
claim.en: The Wikipedia list gives Fusu-ikazuchi (couchant thunder) and Hono-ikazuchi (fire thunder); the Kojiki says Hono-ikazuchi came from Izanami's breasts.

claims_provenance.quote: Fusu-ikazuchi: (Couchant thunder) Hono-ikazuchi: (Fire thunder) the Kojiki says that this kami came from Izanami's breasts.

claim.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki sama-sama menyebut Ō-ikazuchi (petir besar) berasal dari kepala Izanami.
claim.en: Both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi (great thunder) came from Izanami's head.

claims_provenance.quote: Ō-ikazuchi: (Great thunder) both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi came from Izanami's head.

summary.en: After Izanagi sees Izanami's corpse and flees, Izanami sends pursuers including the eight thunder kami; Izanagi throws down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and disperses them.

description.id: Tempat Izanagi melihat jasad Izanami yang dihuni delapan kami petir.
description.en: Where Izanagi sees Izanami's corpse inhabited by the eight thunder kami.

description.id: "Even Pass of Yomi" (Yomotsuhirasaka), tempat Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib untuk mengusir para pengejar.
description.en: The "Even Pass of Yomi", where Izanagi throws magical peaches to disperse his pursuers.

note.id: Delapan petir membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami.
note.en: The eight thunders festered inside Izanami's corpse.

note.id: Dikirim Izanami untuk mengejar Izanagi, yang melarikan diri.
note.en: Sent by Izanami to chase Izanagi, who fled.

note.id: Ikut mengejar Izanagi bersama para pendekar Yomotsu-shikome.
note.en: Sent after Izanagi together with the Yomotsu-shikome.

note.id: Delapan petir dari jasad Izanami disejajarkan dengan delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi yang terpotong.
note.en: The eight thunders from Izanami's corpse are paralleled with the eight kami from the dismembered body of Kagutsuchi.

note.id: Salah satu dari delapan petir; menurut Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki berasal dari kepala Izanami.
note.en: One of the eight thunders; the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki say it came from Izanami's head.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa Kojiki dan Nihongi menempatkan petir pada bagian tubuh Izanami yang berbeda?
learning_questions.en: Why do the Kojiki and the Nihongi place the thunders on different parts of Izanami's body?

claims.quote: Yakusanoikazuchi or ikazuchi is a collective name for the eight kami of thunder in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Yakusanoikazuchi adalah nama kolektif delapan kami petir.
statement.en: Yakusanoikazuchi is the collective name of eight thunder kami.

claims.quote: Each one represents a different type of storm.

statement.id: Para dewa itu mewakili berbagai bentuk badai.
statement.en: The deities represent different forms of storm.

claims.quote: Ikazuchi (雷) literally means thunder in Japanese.

statement.id: Unsur ikazuchi berarti petir.
statement.en: The element ikazuchi means thunder.

claims.quote: Some tellings say that the eight deities were from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

statement.id: Beberapa penuturan menyebut kedelapan dewa itu berasal dari belatung jasad Izanami yang membusuk.
statement.en: Some tellings say the eight deities came from the maggots of Izanami's rotting corpse.

claims.quote: Many versions of the Nihon Shoki and the Kojiki state that after Izanagi saw his wife in such a state and fled in terror, Izanami sent the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, and the eight thunder kami after him.

statement.id: Mereka mengejar Izanagi ketika ia melarikan diri dari alam kematian.
statement.en: They pursue Izanagi when he flees the underworld.

claims.quote: Kuro-ikazuchi: (Black thunder) The Kojiki says that this deity came from Izanami's belly.

statement.id: Kojiki menempatkan Petir Hitam di perut Izanami.
statement.en: The Kojiki places Black Thunder in Izanami’s belly.

claims.quote: However, the Nihon Shoki says that Kuro-ikazuchi was in Izanami's rectum.

statement.id: Nihon Shoki justru menempatkan Petir Hitam di duburnya.
statement.en: The Nihon Shoki instead places Black Thunder in her rectum.

claims.quote: [Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami] (Kojiki) The "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

statement.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami dalam Kojiki adalah "delapan jenis kami petir" yang membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami, seperti dilihat suaminya Izanagi di dunia bawah Yomi.
statement.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami of the Kojiki are the "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

claims.quote: According to Kojiki, in her head was the "great thunder," in her breast was the "fire thunder," in her belly was the "black thunder," in her genitals was the "cleft thunder," in her left hand was the "young thunder," in the right hand was the "earth thunder," in her left leg was the "sounding thunder," and in her right leg was the "reposing thunder."

statement.id: Menurut Kojiki, kedelapan petir itu berada di kepala (petir besar), dada (petir api), perut (petir hitam), kemaluan (petir belah), tangan kiri (petir muda), tangan kanan (petir tanah), kaki kiri (petir bergema), dan kaki kanan (petir beristirahat) Izanami.
statement.en: According to the Kojiki, the eight thunders were in the corpse's head (great thunder), breast (fire thunder), belly (black thunder), genitals (cleft thunder), left hand (young thunder), right hand (earth thunder), left leg (sounding thunder) and right leg (reposing thunder).

claims.quote: An "alternate writing" transmitted by Nihongi, however, states that "great thunder" was in her head, "fire thunder" was in her breast, "earth thunder" was in her belly, "young thunder" was in her back, "black thunder" was in her rectum, "mountain thunder" was in her hands, "field thunder" was in her feet, and "cleft thunder" was in her genitals.

statement.id: Satu "tulisan alternatif" dalam Nihongi menyebut petir besar di kepala, petir api di dada, petir tanah di perut, petir muda di punggung, petir hitam di dubur, petir gunung di tangan, petir ladang di kaki, dan petir belah di kemaluan.
statement.en: An "alternate writing" transmitted by the Nihongi states that great thunder was in her head, fire thunder in her breast, earth thunder in her belly, young thunder in her back, black thunder in her rectum, mountain thunder in her hands, field thunder in her feet and cleft thunder in her genitals.

claims.quote: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

statement.id: Dari delapan petir itu, tiga memiliki nama dan tempat yang sama dalam dua catatan, tiga hanya sama namanya, dan dua sisanya berbeda.
statement.en: Of the eight thunders, three have the same name and place in the two accounts, three agree in name only, and the remaining two are different.

claims.quote: The fact that eight thunders were produced in Izanami's dead body parallels the fact that eight kami were produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi. While eight is considered a sacred number, it is here likely used merely to denote "a great many."

statement.id: Lahirnya delapan petir dari jasad Izanami disamakan dengan lahirnya delapan kami dari tubuh Kagutsuchi yang terpotong; delapan dianggap angka suci, tetapi di sini mungkin hanya berarti "sangat banyak".
statement.en: The eight thunders produced in Izanami's dead body parallel the eight kami produced from the dismembered body of the fire kami Kagutsuchi; eight is considered a sacred number but is here likely used merely to denote "a great many".

claims.quote: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts mentioned above, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi ... Izanagi, however, threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka (the "Even Pass of Yomi"), and thus dispersed his pursuers.

statement.id: Menurut berbagai catatan Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanami memerintahkan "nenek-nenek Yomi" dan delapan kami petir mengejar Izanagi; Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejarnya.
statement.en: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi; Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and thus dispersed his pursuers.

claims.quote: Fusu-ikazuchi: (Couchant thunder) Hono-ikazuchi: (Fire thunder) the Kojiki says that this kami came from Izanami's breasts.

statement.id: Daftar Wikipedia mencantumkan Fusu-ikazuchi (petir berbaring) dan Hono-ikazuchi (petir api); Kojiki menyebut Hono-ikazuchi berasal dari dada Izanami.
statement.en: The Wikipedia list gives Fusu-ikazuchi (couchant thunder) and Hono-ikazuchi (fire thunder); the Kojiki says Hono-ikazuchi came from Izanami's breasts.

claims.quote: Ō-ikazuchi: (Great thunder) both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi came from Izanami's head.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki sama-sama menyebut Ō-ikazuchi (petir besar) berasal dari kepala Izanami.
statement.en: Both the Kojiki and the Nihon Shoki state that Ō-ikazuchi (great thunder) came from Izanami's head.

summary.id: Kojiki menyebut perut.
summary.en: The Kojiki names the belly.

summary.id: Nihon Shoki menyebut dubur.
summary.en: The Nihon Shoki names the rectum.

topic.id: Letak delapan petir pada tubuh Izanami
topic.en: Placement of the eight thunders on Izanami's body

summary.id: Kojiki: kepala, dada, perut, kemaluan, tangan kiri, tangan kanan, kaki kiri, kaki kanan.
summary.en: Kojiki: head, breast, belly, genitals, left hand, right hand, left leg, right leg.

summary.id: Tulisan alternatif Nihongi: kepala, dada, perut, punggung, dubur, tangan, kaki, kemaluan, dengan sebagian nama berbeda; tiga cocok penuh, tiga hanya namanya, dua berbeda.
summary.en: Nihongi alternate writing: head, breast, belly, back, rectum, hands, feet, genitals, with some different names; three match fully, three in name only, two differ.

short_description.id: Areop-Enap, "laba-laba tua" dalam bahasa Nauru, berperan besar dalam penciptaan dunia menurut mitos masyarakat pribumi Nauru.
short_description.en: According to the indigenous myths of Nauru, Areop-Enap (Nauruan for "old spider") had a leading role in making the world.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitos masyarakat pribumi Nauru, Areop-Enap (bahasa Nauru: "laba-laba tua") berperan besar dalam penciptaan dunia. Pada awalnya hanya ada Areop-Enap, seekor laba-laba, dan laut. Dixon mencatat bahwa ia melayang di atas dalam ruang tanpa batas.

Dalam kisah penciptaan, Areop-Enap mencari makanan dalam kegelapan dan menemukan kerang raksasa yang menelannya. Setelah merapal mantra kekuatan pada cacing bernama Rigi, ia membujuk Rigi mencoba membuka kerang itu; asinnya air membunuh kerang dan membuka cangkangnya. Cangkang bawah menjadi Bumi dan cangkang atas menjadi langit, siput yang lebih kecil menjadi Bulan di barat, dan siput kedua menjadi Matahari di timur. Dalam versi Dixon, Rigi kelelahan karena kerja kerasnya dan mati setelah cangkang atas terangkat menjadi langit.

Areop-Enap membuat pulau-pulau dari daging kerang dan menyelimutinya dengan tumbuhan dari benang jaringnya, lalu membungkus Rigi yang tewas dalam kepompong sutra dan menggantungnya di langit menjadi Bima Sakti. Ia menciptakan manusia dari batu agar menopang langit. Setelah itu ia menemukan makhluk-makhluk lain di dunia baru dan menciptakan makhluk bersayap dari kotoran di bawah kukunya untuk mengetahui nama-nama penghuni dunia.
long_description.en:
In the indigenous myths of the people of Nauru, Areop-Enap (Nauruan: "old spider") plays a major part in the creation of the world. At the beginning only Areop-Enap, a spider, and the sea existed. Dixon records that he floated above in endless space.

In the creation tale Areop-Enap went looking for food in the dark and came upon an enormous clam, which swallowed him. After he cast a strength spell on a worm called Rigi and persuaded him to try to open the clam, the briny water killed the clam and its shell opened. The lower shell became the Earth and the upper shell the sky, the smaller snail became the Moon in the west, and the second snail became the Sun in the east. In Dixon's version Rigi, worn out by his labor, died after the upper shell was raised to become the sky.

Areop-Enap made islands from clam-flesh and clothed them with vegetation from his web-thread, then wrapped the dead Rigi in a silk cocoon and hung him in the sky as the Milky Way. He created humans from stones to support the sky. He then found other creatures in the new world and made a winged creature from the dirt under his nails to learn the names of the world's inhabitants.

who.id: Laba-laba pencipta dalam mitos Nauru.
who.en: The creator spider of Nauruan myth.

origin.en: The indigenous myths of the people of Nauru.

role.id: Berperan besar dalam penciptaan dunia: langit, bumi, matahari, bulan, pulau, dan manusia.
role.en: Plays a major part in creating the world: sky, earth, sun, moon, islands and humans.

famous_for.id: Dikenal lewat kisah ia dimakan kerang raksasa dan membuka cangkangnya untuk menjadi langit dan bumi.
famous_for.en: Known for the tale in which he is swallowed by a giant clam and opens its shell to form sky and earth.

did_you_know.id: Dalam kisah penciptaan, cacing Rigi yang tewas dibungkus kepompong sutra oleh Areop-Enap dan digantung di langit menjadi Bima Sakti.
did_you_know.en: In the creation tale, the dead worm Rigi is wrapped in a silk cocoon by Areop-Enap and hung in the sky to become the Milky Way.

description.id: Areop-Enap merapal mantra kekuatan pada Rigi agar mau mencoba membuka kerang.
description.en: Areop-Enap casts a strength spell on Rigi so that he will try to open the clam.

title.en: Creation of the world from a giant clam

role.id: Pencipta yang membuka kerang menjadi langit dan bumi.
role.en: The creator who opens the clam into sky and earth.

summary.id: Areop-Enap menemukan kerang raksasa yang menelannya, merapal mantra kekuatan pada cacing Rigi agar mencoba membuka kerang, lalu menjadikan cangkang bawah Bumi dan cangkang atas langit, serta dua siput sebagai Bulan dan Matahari. Ia membuat pulau dari daging kerang dan menggantung Rigi yang tewas di langit sebagai Bima Sakti.
summary.en: Areop-Enap found a giant clam that swallowed him, cast a strength spell on the worm Rigi to make him try to open the clam, then made the lower shell the Earth and the upper shell the sky, and two snails the Moon and the Sun. He made islands from clam-flesh and hung the dead Rigi in the sky as the Milky Way.

title.en: Learning the names of the world's inhabitants

role.id: Menciptakan makhluk bersayap untuk mengetahui nama-nama.
role.en: Creates a winged creature to learn names.

summary.id: Setelah menciptakan manusia dari batu dan menemukan makhluk-makhluk lain, Areop-Enap menciptakan makhluk bersayap dari kotoran di bawah kukunya dan menyuruhnya mengganggu mereka sehingga mereka saling memanggil untuk membunuhnya; dengan cara itu ia mengetahui nama-nama penghuni dunia.
summary.en: After creating humans from stones and discovering other creatures, Areop-Enap made a winged creature from the dirt under his nails and set it to pester them until they called out to one another to kill it; that is how he learned the names of the world's inhabitants.

description.id: Tempat asal mitos Areop-Enap, yaitu masyarakat pribumi Nauru.
description.en: The home of the Areop-Enap myth, the indigenous people of Nauru.

note.id: Cacing putih yang diberi mantra kekuatan oleh Areop-Enap untuk membuka kerang; ia tewas karena jerih payahnya.
note.en: The white worm on whom Areop-Enap casts a strength spell to open the clam; he dies of his exertions.

note.id: Dalam sebuah kisah yang dicatat Dixon, "Young Spider" lahir secara ajaib dari bisul pada seekor kura-kura.
note.en: In a tale recorded by Dixon, "Young Spider" is born miraculously from a boil on a tortoise.

claim.en: Areop-Enap is an ancient spider playing a central role in Nauruan creation myths.

claims_provenance.quote: Areop-Enap (Nauruan: old spider) played a major part in the creation of the world in the indigenous myths of the people of Nauru.

claim.id: Pada awal penciptaan hanya ada Areop-Enap dan laut.
claim.en: At creation's beginning only Areop-Enap and the sea existed.

claims_provenance.quote: At the beginning of creation, the only things in existence were Areop-Enap (a spider) and the sea.

claim.en: Areop-Enap fashioned humans from stones to uphold the sky.

claims_provenance.quote: Areop-Enap created humans from stones so they could support the sky, and then discovered there were other creatures in the newly created world.

claim.id: Areop-Enap mencari makanan dalam kegelapan dan menemukan kerang raksasa (dalam beberapa versi kerang Tridacna). Sebelum sempat membuatnya pingsan, kerang itu menelannya dan menutup lagi.
claim.en: Areop-Enap searched for food in the darkness and found an enormous clam (in some accounts a Tridacna clam). Before he could stun it, the clam swallowed him and snapped shut again.

claims_provenance.quote: Areop-Enap searched for food in the darkness and found an enormous clam (in some accounts a Tridacna clam). Before he could stun it, the clam swallowed him and snapped shut again.

claim.id: Mengabaikan siput itu, Areop-Enap merapal mantra kekuatan pada Rigi dan membujuknya mencoba membuka kerang.
claim.en: Ignoring the snail, Areop-Enap cast a strength spell on Rigi and persuaded him to try to open the clam.

claims_provenance.quote: Ignoring the snail, Areop-Enap cast a strength spell on Rigi and persuaded him to try to open the clam.

claim.id: Asinnya air membunuh kerang dan membuka cangkangnya. Areop-Enap menjadikan cangkang bawah sebagai Bumi dan cangkang atas sebagai langit, menempatkan siput yang lebih kecil di barat cangkang langit sehingga menjadi Bulan, dan siput kedua di timur sehingga menjadi Matahari.
claim.en: The saltiness of the water killed the clam and opened the shell. Areop-Enap made the lower shell into Earth and the upper shell into the sky, set the smaller snail west of the sky-shell where it became the Moon, and set the second snail to the east where it became the Sun.

claims_provenance.quote: The saltiness of the water killed the clam and opened the shell. Areop-Enap made the lower shell into Earth and the upper shell into the sky and set the smaller snail west of the sky-shell where it became the Moon. The second snail was set to the east and became the Sun.

claim.id: Areop-Enap membuat pulau-pulau dari daging kerang dan menyelimutinya dengan tumbuhan yang dibuat dari benang jaringnya sendiri.
claim.en: Areop-Enap made islands from clam-flesh and clothed them in vegetation made from his own web-thread.

claims_provenance.quote: Areop-Enap made islands from clam-flesh and clothed them in vegetation made from his own web-thread.

claim.id: Akhirnya ia menoleh kepada Rigi dan mendapati bahwa Rigi tenggelam dalam keringatnya sendiri, tewas karena jerih payahnya. Areop-Enap membungkusnya dalam kepompong sutra dan menggantungnya di langit menjadi Bima Sakti.
claim.en: Finally he turned to Rigi and found that he had drowned in his own sweat, killed by his own exertions. Areop-Enap wrapped him in a silk cocoon and hung him in the sky to become the Milky Way.

claims_provenance.quote: Finally he turned to Rigi and found that he had drowned in his own sweat, killed by his own exertions. Areop-Enap wrapped him in a cocoon of silk and hung him in the sky to become the Milky Way.

claim.id: Maka ia menciptakan makhluk bersayap atau burung terbang dari kotoran di bawah kukunya dan menyuruhnya mengganggu makhluk-makhluk itu sehingga mereka saling memanggil untuk membunuhnya. Dengan cara ini Areop-Enap mengetahui nama-nama penghuni dunia.
claim.en: So he created a winged creature or flying bird from the dirt under his nails and set it to annoy the creatures so that they called to each other to kill it. In this way Areop-Enap learned the names of the inhabitants of the world.

claims_provenance.quote: So he created a winged creature or flying bird from the dirt under his nails and set it to annoy the creatures so that they called to each other to kill it. In this way Areop-Enap learned the names of the inhabitants of the world.

claim.id: Dalam kisah yang dicatat Dixon, pada mulanya hanya ada laut dan Areop-Enap, "Laba-laba Purba", yang melayang di atas dalam ruang tanpa batas.
claim.en: In the tale recorded by Dixon, in the beginning there were only the sea and Areop-Enap, "Ancient Spider", who floated above in endless space.

claims_provenance.quote: in the beginning there were only the sea and Areop-Enap, ‘Ancient Spider,” who floated above in endless space.
