claims.quote: Gaoh, Ga-oh or Gǎ-oh is a wind spirit and giant of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat and Seneca people.

statement.id: Gaoh (juga Ga-oh) adalah roh angin dan raksasa orang Haudenosaunee, Wendat, dan Seneca.
statement.en: Gaoh (also Ga-oh) is a wind spirit and giant of the Haudenosaunee, Wendat and Seneca.

claims.quote: Gaoh was described as a cannibal and a giant who could uproot trees. He takes the form of a solitary old man.

statement.id: Gaoh digambarkan sebagai raksasa kanibal yang dapat mencabut pohon, berwujud lelaki tua yang menyendiri.
statement.en: Gaoh was described as a cannibal giant who could uproot trees, taking the form of a solitary old man.

claims.quote: Gaoh is subservient to the Great Spirit, and in Haudenosaunee mythology he is subservient to Adekagagwaa.

statement.id: Gaoh tunduk kepada Roh Agung, dan dalam mitologi Haudenosaunee ia tunduk kepada Adekagagwaa.
statement.en: Gaoh is subservient to the Great Spirit and, in Haudenosaunee mythology, to Adekagagwaa.

claims.quote: Gaoh is mostly a benevolent spirit, but can be restless and violent, and would create storms.

statement.id: Gaoh umumnya roh baik, tetapi bisa gelisah, ganas, dan menciptakan badai.
statement.en: Gaoh is mostly benevolent but can be restless and violent, creating storms.

claims.quote: From his home, he controls the seasons, and also winds of the four cardinal directions

statement.id: Dari rumahnya, ia mengendalikan musim dan angin dari empat penjuru mata angin.
statement.en: From his home he controls the seasons and the winds of the four directions.

claims.quote: Ya-o-gah ... or Bear of the north wind, Da-jo-ji ... or Panther of the west wind, O-yan-do-ne ... or Moose of the east wind and Ne-o-gah ... or Fawn of the south wind.

statement.id: Angin-anginnya adalah Ya-o-gah (beruang angin utara), Da-jo-ji (macan kumbang angin barat), O-yan-do-ne (rusa besar angin timur), dan Ne-o-gah (anak rusa angin selatan).
statement.en: His winds are Ya-o-gah (Bear, north), Da-jo-ji (Panther, west), O-yan-do-ne (Moose, east) and Ne-o-gah (Fawn, south).

claims.quote: In the Seneca version of the myth, Gaoh is chained to a rock, and winds would blow when he attempts to break free.

statement.id: Dalam versi Seneca, Gaoh dirantai ke batu, dan angin bertiup saat ia berusaha melepaskan diri.
statement.en: In the Seneca version, Gaoh is chained to a rock, and winds blow when he tries to break free.

claims.quote: Though of giant proportions, Ga-oh ... who governs the winds, is confined in the broad north sky.

statement.id: Meski bertubuh raksasa, Ga-oh, yang menguasai angin, dikurung di langit utara yang luas.
statement.en: Though of giant proportions, Ga-oh, who governs the winds, is confined in the broad north sky.

claims.quote: Were Ga-oh free, he would tear the heavens into fragments.

statement.id: Seandainya Ga-oh bebas, ia akan mencabik langit menjadi serpihan.
statement.en: Were Ga-oh free, he would tear the heavens into fragments.

claims.quote: Ga-oh is not an evil being, howsoever his four winds may rage, but on the contrary, solicitous for the welfare of men and ever obedient to the commands of the Creator.

statement.id: Ga-oh bukan makhluk jahat, seganas apa pun keempat anginnya; sebaliknya ia peduli pada kesejahteraan manusia dan selalu menaati perintah Sang Pencipta.
statement.en: Ga-oh is not an evil being, however his four winds may rage; on the contrary he is solicitous for the welfare of men and ever obedient to the commands of the Creator.

claims.quote: Ga-oh dwells in the west sky according to the researches of the writer, agreeing with Morgan who names the western sky as the abode of the wind spirit and calls his dwelling Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.
claims.locator: Ga-oh, Spirit of the Winds (catatan kaki)

statement.id: Dalam catatan kaki, penulis menyatakan berdasarkan penelitiannya bahwa Ga-oh tinggal di langit barat, sejalan dengan Morgan yang menyebut langit barat sebagai tempat tinggal roh angin dan menamai kediamannya Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.
statement.en: In a footnote the writer states, from her researches, that Ga-oh dwells in the west sky, agreeing with Morgan, who names the western sky as the abode of the wind spirit and calls his dwelling Da-yo-da-do-go-wa.

claims.quote: the Bear (north wind). Panther (west wind). Moose (east wind), and Fawn (south wind).

statement.id: Di pintu kediamannya ada empat penjaga: Beruang (angin utara), Macan Kumbang (angin barat), Rusa Besar (angin timur), dan Anak Rusa (angin selatan).
statement.en: At the entrance of his abode are four watchers: the Bear (north wind), Panther (west wind), Moose (east wind) and Fawn (south wind).

claims.quote: When Ga-oh is contented and happy, gentle and invigorating breezes fan Earth

statement.id: Ketika Ga-oh puas dan bahagia, angin sepoi-sepoi yang lembut dan menyegarkan berembus ke Bumi.
statement.en: When Ga-oh is contented and happy, gentle and invigorating breezes fan Earth.

claims.quote: Ga-oh is the name of the wind spirit according to Morgan.
claims.locator: Ga-oh, Spirit of the Winds (catatan kaki)

statement.id: Dalam catatan kaki disebutkan bahwa Ga-oh adalah nama roh angin menurut Morgan.
statement.en: A footnote says that Ga-oh is the name of the wind spirit according to Morgan.

claims.quote: Depending on the myths, he either lives in a house in the sky, or a mountain cave called "the House of Winds."

statement.id: Tergantung mitosnya, ia tinggal di rumah di langit atau di gua gunung bernama "Rumah Angin".
statement.en: Depending on the myths, he either lives in a house in the sky or in a mountain cave called "the House of Winds."

claims.quote: Some versions of the myths describe the winds as the guardians of Gaoh's home, while others describe the winds being locked up in his home, who were to be released once Gaoh receives the order from the Great Spirit.

statement.id: Sebagian versi mitos menggambarkan angin sebagai penjaga rumah Gaoh, sementara versi lain menggambarkan angin terkunci di rumahnya dan akan dilepaskan setelah Gaoh menerima perintah dari Roh Agung.
statement.en: Some versions of the myths describe the winds as the guardians of Gaoh's home, while others describe them as locked up in his home, to be released once Gaoh receives the order from the Great Spirit.

short_description.id: Giant anaconda adalah ular raksasa dalam kisah hutan Amazon yang dikatakan melebihi anaconda biasa, tanpa bukti spesimen.
short_description.en: Giant anaconda is a great serpent in Amazon forest tales, said to exceed ordinary anacondas, with no specimen evidence.

long_description.id:
Giant anaconda adalah ular raksasa dalam kisah hutan Amazon yang dikatakan melebihi anaconda biasa. Kisah yang dibaca menyebut panjang hingga sepuluh meter; angka itu merupakan laporan legenda. Penjelasan yang diajukan meliputi anaconda yang tumbuh sangat besar atau ular purba yang masih bertahan.

Pada 1907, Percy Fawcett mengaku melihat dan menembak anaconda raksasa sepanjang 62 kaki (19 m) dalam sebuah ekspedisi, klaim yang membuatnya ditertawakan para ilmuwan. Spesimen terpanjang dan terberat yang terverifikasi, yang ditemui Jesús Antonio Rivas, adalah seekor betina sepanjang 5,21 m dengan berat 97,5 kg.

Laporan anaconda sepanjang 11-12 m atau lebih harus disikapi hati-hati karena belum pernah ada spesimen sepanjang itu disimpan di museum. Dalam budaya populer, sebuah daftar di majalah TIME menggambarkannya sebagai ular secepat kilat sepanjang lebih dari 30 kaki yang mampu menggulingkan dan meremukkan perahu kayu di Amazon.
long_description.en:
Giant anaconda is a great serpent in Amazon forest tales, said to exceed ordinary anacondas. The account mentions a length up to ten meters as a legendary report. Proposed explanations include unusually large anacondas or surviving prehistoric serpents.

In 1907, during an expedition, Percy Fawcett claimed to have seen and shot a 62-foot (19 m) giant anaconda, and scientists ridiculed the claim. The longest and heaviest verified specimen, met by Jesús Antonio Rivas, was a female of 5.21 m weighing 97.5 kg.

Reports of anacondas of 11-12 m or longer must be regarded with caution because no specimens of such lengths have been deposited in a museum. In popular culture, a TIME list pictures it as a lightning-quick snake over 30 feet long that can capsize and crush wooden boats on the Amazon.

summary.id: Seorang penjelajah mengaku menembak anaconda raksasa sepanjang 62 kaki pada 1907.
summary.en: An explorer claimed to have shot a 62-foot giant anaconda in 1907.

summary.id: Menurut sumber lain, spesimen terverifikasi terpanjang adalah 5,21 m, dan laporan 11 m atau lebih harus disikapi hati-hati karena tidak ada spesimen di museum.
summary.en: According to another source, the longest verified specimen was 5.21 m, and reports of 11 m or more must be treated with caution since no museum specimens exist.

short_description.id: Glær adalah kuda dalam mitologi Nordik yang tercantum di antara tunggangan para dewa Æsir ketika mereka berkuda setiap hari untuk mengadili di Yggdrasil; tidak ada teks yang menyebut pemiliknya.
short_description.en: Glær is a horse of Norse mythology, listed among the steeds the Æsir gods ride each day to judge at Yggdrasil; no text names its owner.

long_description.id:
Dalam mitologi Nordik, Glær adalah seekor kuda yang namanya tercantum dalam Grímnismál maupun Gylfaginning di antara kuda-kuda yang ditunggangi para dewa setiap hari ketika mereka pergi mengadili di pohon abu Yggdrasil. Di kedua teks itu Glær tidak dikaitkan dengan dewa tertentu, berbeda dengan Sleipnir dan Freyfaxi.

Bentuk namanya tidak sama di semua teks. Grímnismál dan daftar Þorgrímsþula di Skáldskaparmál menulis Glær, sedangkan daftar kuda para Æsir di Gylfaginning menyebut kuda keempat sebagai Glenr, setelah Sleipnir milik Odin yang berkaki delapan.

Arti nama Glær diberikan berbeda oleh sumber: artikel bahasa Denmark mengartikannya "bening" atau "seperti kaca", artikel lain menyebut "transparent", dan Bellows, yang menulis nama itu Gler, memberi "Shining" (bersinar).
long_description.en:
In Norse mythology Glær is a horse whose name appears in both Grímnismál and Gylfaginning among the steeds the gods ride each day when they go to judge at the ash Yggdrasil. In neither text is Glær assigned to a particular god, unlike Sleipnir and Freyfaxi.

The form of the name is not the same in every text. Grímnismál and the Þorgrímsþula list in Skáldskaparmál write Glær, whereas the Gylfaginning list of the Æsir's steeds gives the fourth horse as Glenr, after Odin's eight-footed Sleipnir.

Sources give the meaning of the name Glær differently: the Danish article reads it as "clear" or "glassy", another article says "transparent", and Bellows, who writes the name Gler, gives "Shining".

short_description.id: Göl Boğaları (banteng danau) adalah makhluk dalam kepercayaan rakyat Artvin dan daerah Posof yang dipercaya menghuni danau-danau gunung, muncul saat fajar, lalu menghilang ke dalam air.
short_description.en: Göl Boğaları (lake bulls) are beings of folk belief in Artvin and the Posof area, thought to dwell in mountain lakes, to show themselves at dawn and then to disappear into the water.

long_description.id:
Göl Boğaları, disebut juga su boğaları (banteng air), adalah makhluk khayalan yang menurut kepercayaan setempat tinggal di danau-danau gunung Artvin, terutama di Ardanuç, Şavşat, dan Yusufeli, serta di sekitar Posof. Sumber kedua menyebut bahwa di beberapa daerah Anadolu, penghuni danau gunung semacam ini dikenal sebagai Göl Boğası atau Su Boğası. Mereka dipercaya dapat dilihat pada cahaya pertama pagi, sebelum menyelam dan lenyap ke dalam air.

Legenda yang paling dikenal bercerita tentang seorang pandai besi yang menggembalakan ternaknya di tepi Boğa Gölü. Banteng danau naik ke darat untuk bergulat dengan banteng milik pria itu dan menang. Untuk membalas, si pandai besi memasang tanduk baja pada bantengnya; pada pertarungan berikutnya banteng danau terluka parah, kabur ke danau, dan darahnya mewarnai air. Jalur kemerahan di danau, yang sebenarnya pantulan batu dan tanah merah, dipercaya sebagai bekas darah itu, dan banteng yang terluka konon mengutuk si pandai besi beserta keluarganya hingga jatuh sengsara.

Kumpulan legenda air dari Ardanuç memuat versi serupa. Di satu danau di pegunungan Karçal, banteng danau bergulat dengan banteng seorang gembala, lalu kalah setelah si gembala mengasah tanduk bantengnya. Dalam kisah Ağgöl, banteng danau bergulat dengan banteng desa Tütünlü, kembali ke danau setelah kalah, dan bekas darahnya dikatakan masih terlihat di sana.
long_description.en:
Göl Boğaları, also called su boğaları (water bulls), are imaginary beings that, according to local belief, live in the mountain lakes of Artvin, chiefly around Ardanuç, Şavşat and Yusufeli, and around Posof. The second source says that in some parts of Anadolu such dwellers of mountain lakes are known as Göl Boğası or Su Boğası. People hold that they can be glimpsed in the first light of morning, before they plunge into the water and vanish.

The best-known legend tells of a blacksmith grazing his animals by Boğa Gölü. The lake bull came ashore to wrestle the man's bull and won. In revenge the blacksmith fitted his bull with steel horns; in the next fight the lake bull was badly wounded, fled into the lake and stained the water with its blood. A reddish streak in the lake, actually a reflection of red stone and soil, is believed to be that blood, and the wounded bull is said to have cursed the blacksmith and his family into ruin.

A collection of water legends from Ardanuç contains similar versions. At a lake in the Karçal mountains a lake bull wrestled a shepherd's bull and was beaten after the shepherd sharpened his bull's horns. In the tale of Ağgöl the lake bull fought the bull of Tütünlü village, returned to the lake after losing, and the trace of its blood is said to be visible there still.

claim.id: Göl boğaları atau su boğaları (banteng danau/banteng air) adalah makhluk khayalan (düşsel varlıklar) yang dipercaya ada di danau-danau gunung (dağ göllerinde) di Artvin, terutama di distrik Ardanuç, Şavşat, dan Yusufeli, serta di daerah Posof.
claim.en: Göl boğaları or su boğaları (lake bulls/water bulls) are imaginary beings (düşsel varlıklar) believed to live in the mountain lakes (dağ göllerinde) of Artvin, especially the Ardanuç, Şavşat and Yusufeli districts, and of the Posof area.

claims_provenance.quote: Göl boğaları ya da su boğaları, Artvin (özellikle Ardanuç, Şavşat ve Yusufeli ilçeleri) ve Posof yöresinde dağ göllerinde bulunduğuna inanılan düşsel varlıklar.

claim.id: Dipercaya bahwa banteng danau dapat terlihat pada cahaya pertama pagi hari (sabahın ilk aydınlığında), lalu menyelam ke air dan lenyap.
claim.en: Lake bulls are believed to be visible at the first light of morning (sabahın ilk aydınlığında) and then to dive into the water and vanish.

claims_provenance.quote: Göl boğalarının sabahın ilk aydınlığında görülebildiğine ve daha sonrasında suya dalıp yittiklerine inanılır.

claim.id: Danau-danau Boğa Gölleri di Gunung Hargiver (Arı Dağı) mendapat namanya dari kepercayaan ini.
claim.en: The Boğa Gölleri (Bull Lakes) on Mount Hargiver (Arı Dağı) take their name from this belief.

claims_provenance.quote: Hargiver Dağında (Arı Dağı) yer alan Boğa Gölleri isimlerini bu inançtan almaktadır.

claim.id: Dalam legenda, banteng danau yang mendengar lenguhan dari dalam danau naik ke tepi dan mulai bergulat (güreşmeye) dengan banteng milik seorang pria.
claim.en: In the legend, the lake bull hears the bellowing from inside the lake, comes up to the shore and starts to wrestle (güreşmeye) with a man's bull.

claims_provenance.quote: Göl içerisinden bu sesi işiten göl boğası, gölün kıyısına çıkarak orada bulunan adamın boğasıyla güreşmeye başlar.

claim.id: Sampai kini, jalur kemerahan di danau yang berasal dari pantulan batu dan tanah merah dipercaya sebagai tempat banteng itu masuk ke air dan bekas noda darahnya (kan lekelerinin).
claim.en: To this day, a road-like red streak in the lake, reflected from red stone and soil, is believed to mark where the bull entered the water and the traces of its blood (kan lekelerinin).

claims_provenance.quote: Halen göl içerisinde kırmızı taş ve toprağın su yüzüne aksettirmiş olduğu yol şeklindeki bir kırmızılığı, boğanın suya girdiği yer ve ondan kalan kan lekelerinin izi olduğuna inanılmaktadır.

claim.id: Diriwayatkan bahwa banteng danau yang terluka mengutuk (beddua) si pandai besi (demirci) dan keluarganya, sehingga keluarga itu jatuh sengsara.
claim.en: It is related that the wounded lake bull cursed (beddua) the blacksmith (demirci) and his family, and that the family was ruined as a result.

claims_provenance.quote: Yaralı göl boğasının demirci ve ailesine beddua ettiği, ailenin bu nedenden dolayı perişan olduğu rivayet edilir.

claim.id: Di beberapa daerah Anadolu (Anatolia), makhluk yang dipercaya hidup di danau-danau gunung disebut Göl Boğası (Su Boğası).
claim.en: In some areas of Anadolu (Anatolia), beings believed to live in mountain lakes are called Göl Boğası (Su Boğası).

claims_provenance.quote: Anadolu'da kimi yörelerde dağ göllerinde yaşadığına inanılan varlıklara Göl Boğası (Su Boğası) denilmektedir.

claim.id: Untuk membalas dendam pada banteng danau, si pandai besi membuatkan tanduk baja (polat, çelik) bagi bantengnya sendiri.
claim.en: To take revenge on the lake bull, the blacksmith made steel (polat, çelik) horns for his own bull.

claims_provenance.quote: Göl boğasından öcünü almak için çare düşünmüş. Kendi boğasına polat (çelik) boynuzlar yapmış.

claims_provenance.quote: Van Gölü Canavarı söylentilerinde de pek çok kimse gördüğünü söylediği yaratığın boynuzlu ve hattâ mandaya benzediğini ifâde etmektedir.

claim.en: In the Boğa Gölü version collected in Ardanuç, a bull came out of a lake in the Karçal mountains, wrestled with a shepherd's (çobanın) bull and went back into the lake.

claims_provenance.quote: Karçal dağlarındaki gölden boğa çıkıp çobanın boğasıyla güreşip tekrar göle giriyormuş.

short_description.id: Göl Boğaları (banteng danau) adalah makhluk dalam kepercayaan rakyat Artvin dan daerah Posof yang dipercaya menghuni danau-danau gunung, muncul saat fajar, lalu menghilang ke dalam air.
short_description.en: Göl Boğaları (lake bulls) are beings of folk belief in Artvin and the Posof area, thought to dwell in mountain lakes, to show themselves at dawn and then to disappear into the water.

long_description.id: Göl Boğaları, disebut juga su boğaları (banteng air), adalah makhluk khayalan yang menurut kepercayaan setempat tinggal di danau-danau gunung Artvin, terutama di Ardanuç, Şavşat, dan Yusufeli, serta di sekitar Posof. Sumber kedua menyebut bahwa di beberapa daerah Anadolu, penghuni danau gunung semacam ini dikenal sebagai Göl Boğası atau Su Boğası. Mereka dipercaya dapat dilihat pada cahaya pertama pagi, sebelum menyelam dan lenyap ke dalam air.
long_description.en: Göl Boğaları, also called su boğaları (water bulls), are imaginary beings that, according to local belief, live in the mountain lakes of Artvin, chiefly around Ardanuç, Şavşat and Yusufeli, and around Posof. The second source says that in some parts of Anadolu such dwellers of mountain lakes are known as Göl Boğası or Su Boğası. People hold that they can be glimpsed in the first light of morning, before they plunge into the water and vanish.

long_description.id: Legenda yang paling dikenal bercerita tentang seorang pandai besi yang menggembalakan ternaknya di tepi Boğa Gölü. Banteng danau naik ke darat untuk bergulat dengan banteng milik pria itu dan menang. Untuk membalas, si pandai besi memasang tanduk baja pada bantengnya; pada pertarungan berikutnya banteng danau terluka parah, kabur ke danau, dan darahnya mewarnai air. Jalur kemerahan di danau, yang sebenarnya pantulan batu dan tanah merah, dipercaya sebagai bekas darah itu, dan banteng yang terluka konon mengutuk si pandai besi beserta keluarganya hingga jatuh sengsara.
long_description.en: The best-known legend tells of a blacksmith grazing his animals by Boğa Gölü. The lake bull came ashore to wrestle the man's bull and won. In revenge the blacksmith fitted his bull with steel horns; in the next fight the lake bull was badly wounded, fled into the lake and stained the water with its blood. A reddish streak in the lake, actually a reflection of red stone and soil, is believed to be that blood, and the wounded bull is said to have cursed the blacksmith and his family into ruin.

long_description.id: Kumpulan legenda air dari Ardanuç memuat versi serupa. Di satu danau di pegunungan Karçal, banteng danau bergulat dengan banteng seorang gembala, lalu kalah setelah si gembala mengasah tanduk bantengnya. Dalam kisah Ağgöl, banteng danau bergulat dengan banteng desa Tütünlü, kembali ke danau setelah kalah, dan bekas darahnya dikatakan masih terlihat di sana.
long_description.en: A collection of water legends from Ardanuç contains similar versions. At a lake in the Karçal mountains a lake bull wrestled a shepherd's bull and was beaten after the shepherd sharpened his bull's horns. In the tale of Ağgöl the lake bull fought the bull of Tütünlü village, returned to the lake after losing, and the trace of its blood is said to be visible there still.

cultural_context.id: Kepercayaan ini melekat pada bentang alam setempat: danau-danau Boğa Gölleri di Gunung Hargiver (Arı Dağı) mendapat namanya dari kepercayaan tentang banteng danau.
cultural_context.en: The belief is tied to the local landscape: the Boğa Gölleri lakes on Mount Hargiver (Arı Dağı) are named after the belief in lake bulls.

claims.quote: Boğa da göle geri dönmüş. Kanının izi hâlen daha gölde durmaktadır
claims.locator: Artvin Yöresinde Su ile İlgili Efsaneler: Ağgöl

statement.id: Banteng itu kembali ke danau, dan bekas darahnya (kanının izi) dikatakan masih tampak di danau sampai sekarang.
statement.en: The bull went back into the lake, and the trace of its blood (kanının izi) is said to remain in the lake to this day.

short_description.id: Golden Kite adalah burung emas suci dalam kisah Jinmu di Nihon Shoki.
short_description.en: The Golden Kite is a sacred golden bird in the Nihon Shoki’s Jinmu narrative.

long_description.id:
Golden Kite adalah burung emas suci dalam kisah Jinmu di Nihon Shoki. Ia bertengger pada busur Jinmu dan menyilaukan pasukan lawan dengan cahayanya.

Ia tidak muncul dalam Kojiki dan kerap tertukar dengan Yatagarasu. Tradisi kuil Kamo menganggap kedua burung itu perwujudan Kamo Taketsunumi.

Menurut kisahnya, langit tiba-tiba gelap dan turun hujan es ketika elang gaib itu hinggap di ujung busur Jinmu dan memancarkan cahaya keemasan seperti kilat, sehingga musuh silau dan pasukan kaisar menang. Burung itu disebut kinshi, dan medan perangnya dinamai Tobi no mura, yang kemudian menjadi Tomi.

Gambar kinshi dibordir pada panji brokat besar yang dipasang saat penobatan kaisar. Pada masa Perang Dunia II, merek rokok Golden Bat sempat berganti nama menjadi Kinshi dari 1940 sampai 1949.
long_description.en:
The Golden Kite is a sacred golden bird in the Nihon Shoki’s Jinmu narrative. It perches on Jinmu’s bow and dazzles the opposing army with its light.

It is absent from the Kojiki and is often confused with Yatagarasu. Kamo shrine tradition regards both birds as manifestations of Kamo Taketsunumi.

In the tale, the sky suddenly darkened and hail fell as the spirit kite perched on the tip of Jinmu’s bow and shone with a lightning-like golden light, dazzling the enemy so that the imperial army won. The bird was called kinshi, and the battlefield was named Tobi no mura, later Tomi.

The golden kite is embroidered on the great brocade banner set up at an emperor’s enthronement. During World War II, the Golden Bat cigarette brand was renamed Kinshi from 1940 to 1949.

claims_provenance.quote: 金鵄（きんし）は、『日本書紀』に登場し、神武天皇による日本建国を導いた金色の鵄。

claim.id: Ia bertengger pada busur Jinmu dan menyilaukan pasukan lawan dengan cahayanya.
claim.en: It perches on Jinmu’s bow and dazzles the opposing army with its light.

claims_provenance.quote: 『日本書紀』の記述では、東征を進める彦火火出見（後の神武天皇）が長髄彦と戦っている際に、金色の霊鵄が天皇の弓に止まると、その体から発する光で長髄彦の軍兵たちの目がくらみ、東征軍が勝利することができたとされる。

claim.id: Ia tidak muncul dalam Kojiki dan kerap tertukar dengan Yatagarasu.
claim.en: It is absent from the Kojiki and is often confused with Yatagarasu.

claims_provenance.quote: ただし、『古事記』に金鵄は登場せず、神武東征の際に熊野から大和へ東征軍を道案内した八咫烏と混同、あるいは同視されることが多い。

claim.id: Tradisi kuil Kamo menganggap kedua burung itu perwujudan Kamo Taketsunumi.
claim.en: Kamo shrine tradition regards both birds as manifestations of Kamo Taketsunumi.

claims_provenance.quote: また、平安時代から存続する賀茂神社においては、金鵄および八咫烏ともに、賀茂建角身命の化身とされており、この二つを合わせて「金鵄八咫烏」と呼び祀っている。

claim.id: Tiba-tiba cuaca menjadi gelap dan turun hujan es; seekor elang gaib (靈鵄) hinggap di ujung busur Kaisar Jinmu dan memancarkan cahaya keemasan seperti kilat (流電) yang menyilaukan musuh, sehingga pasukan kaisar menang.
claim.en: Suddenly the sky darkened and hail fell; a spirit kite (靈鵄) perched on the tip of Emperor Jinmu’s bow and shone with a golden light like lightning (流電) that dazzled the enemy, so the imperial army won.

claims_provenance.quote: 忽然天氣變得陰暗且下起冰雹，神武天皇的弓弭停了一隻靈鵄，發出的金色光輝狀如流電，使敵軍迷眩，故天皇軍獲得勝利。

claim.id: Elang gaib itu disebut "kinshi" (金鵄), dan medan kemenangan itu dinamai "Tobi no mura" (鵄邑), yang kemudian berubah menjadi "Tomi" (鳥見).
claim.en: The spirit kite was called "kinshi" (金鵄), and the battlefield of the victory was named "Tobi no mura" (鵄邑), later corrupted to "Tomi" (鳥見).

claims_provenance.quote: 此靈鵄被稱為「金鵄」，而獲勝戰場名為「鵄邑」，後訛傳成「鳥見」。

claim.id: Panji brokat besar (大錦旛) yang dipasang di halaman depan Shishinden saat penobatan kaisar dibordir dengan gambar kinshi.
claim.en: The great brocade banner (大錦旛) set up in the front court of the Shishinden at an emperor’s enthronement is embroidered with the golden kite.

claims_provenance.quote: 另外，大錦旛（一種靈鵄形大錦旛，天皇登基時豎立在紫宸殿前庭）上繡有金鵄圖案。

claim.id: Rokok Jepang "Golden Bat" (ゴールデンバット) sempat berganti nama menjadi "Kinshi" (金鵄) dari 1940 sampai 1949 karena gerakan menolak kata-kata bahasa musuh pada Perang Dunia II.
claim.en: The Japanese cigarette brand "Golden Bat" (ゴールデンバット) was renamed "Kinshi" (金鵄) from 1940 to 1949 because of the wartime movement against enemy-language words in World War II.

claims_provenance.quote: 此外，日本國產香菸「Golden Bat（日语：ゴールデンバット）」（ゴールデンバット）受到第二次世界大戰的反敌性语运动影響，曾於昭和15年（1940年）至昭和24年（1949年）間改名為「金鵄」。

short_description.id: Hıbılık adalah roh jahat dalam kepercayaan rakyat di beberapa daerah Turki yang menindih dada orang tidur hingga mereka tak bisa bergerak, bahkan dapat mencekik sampai mati.
short_description.en: Hıbılık is an evil spirit of folk belief in parts of Turkey that presses on the chests of sleepers so they cannot move, and may even throttle them to death.

long_description.id:
Menurut orang di beberapa daerah Turki, Hıbılık, yang juga disebut Gıbılık, adalah makhluk jahat yang rupanya menyerupai Alkarısı. Bedanya, Alkarısı hanya mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan, sedangkan Hıbılık mengusik siapa saja, perempuan maupun laki-laki. Dua kajian akademik tentang agama tradisional Turk mencatat perbedaan yang sama.

Biasanya ia berwujud perempuan, meski ada pula yang berwujud laki-laki. Ia datang kepada orang yang sedang tidur, menindih dadanya, dan mencekik lehernya; korbannya tak dapat bergerak, lidahnya kelu, dan ia bermandi keringat. Sebagian sumber menyebut serangan ini bisa berakhir dengan kematian, terutama bila korban tidak dibangunkan. Bagi orang yang didatanginya, ia tampak seperti kucing, lalu menghilang diam-diam dalam gelap.

Hıbılık juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan. Bila tertangkap, ia memberi banyak emas kepada penangkapnya agar dilepaskan. Di kepalanya ada börk, sejenis topi, yang ajaib, dan siapa pun yang berhasil merebut topi itu dipercaya akan menjadi kaya.
long_description.en:
According to people in some parts of Turkey, Hıbılık, also called Gıbılık, is a malevolent being that looks like the Alkarısı. The difference is that the Alkarısı troubles only women who have just given birth, whereas Hıbılık bothers anyone, woman or man. Two scholarly studies of traditional Turkic religion record the same contrast.

It usually takes a female form, though male ones exist as well. It comes to a sleeping person, sits on the chest and squeezes the throat; the victim cannot move, is tongue-tied and drenched in sweat. Some sources say such an attack can end in death, especially if the victim is not woken. To the person it visits it appears like a cat, and it then vanishes silently in the dark.

Hıbılık is also linked to wealth. If caught, it hands its captor plenty of gold to be let go. On its head it wears a magic börk, a kind of cap, and whoever manages to seize the cap is believed to become rich.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal karena topi ajaibnya yang dipercaya membuat kaya orang yang merebutnya.

did_you_know.id: Hıbılık yang tertangkap dipercaya akan menebus kebebasannya dengan banyak emas.
did_you_know.en: A captured hıbılık is believed to buy its freedom with plenty of gold.

cultural_context.id: Para peneliti menempatkan Hıbılık di antara roh maut atau roh rakus pada lapisan bawah di bawah Erlik, bersama Aldaçı dan Alkarısı, dan menyebutnya sebagai salah satu makhluk demonik yang diberi sifat feminin.
cultural_context.en: Scholars place Hıbılık among the death or gluttonous spirits of the lower layers below Erlik, together with Aldaçı and Alkarısı, and count it among the demonic beings to which femininity is attributed.

description.id: Menindih dada orang yang tidur sehingga mereka tak bisa bergerak atau berbicara, dan mencekik leher mereka.
description.en: Presses on the chests of sleepers so that they cannot move or speak, and squeezes their throats.

description.id: Bila tertangkap, ia memberi emas kepada penangkapnya, dan topi ajaibnya dapat direbut.
description.en: If caught, it gives gold to its captor, and its magic cap can be seized.

claim.id: Menurut orang di beberapa daerah Turki (Türkiye), Hıbılık adalah makhluk jahat (kötücül bir varlık) yang rupanya seperti Alkarısı; ia juga disebut Gıbılık.
claim.en: According to people in some parts of Turkey (Türkiye), Hıbılık is a malevolent being (kötücül bir varlık) that looks like the Alkarısı; it is also called Gıbılık.

claims_provenance.quote: Hıbılık, Türkiye'nin bazı yörelerinde yaşayan insanlara göre, görünüş olarak Alkarısı şeklinde olan kötücül bir varlık. Gıbılık da denir.

claim.id: Alkarısı hanya mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan, sedangkan hıbılık tidak memberi ketenangan kepada siapa pun, perempuan maupun laki-laki (kadın-erkek).
claim.en: The Alkarısı troubles only women who have just given birth, whereas the hıbılık gives no peace to anyone, woman or man (kadın-erkek).

claims_provenance.quote: Alkarısı sadece yeni doğum yapmış kadınları rahatsız eder. Oysa hıbılık kadın-erkek hiç kimseye rahat vermez.

claim.id: Hıbılık biasanya berwujud perempuan, tetapi ada juga yang berwujud laki-laki; ia menindih dada (göğsüne çöker) orang yang didatanginya dan mencekik lehernya hingga napasnya putus dan ia mati.
claim.en: The hıbılık usually has a woman's appearance, though there are male-looking ones too; it sits on the chest (göğsüne çöker) of the person it visits and squeezes their throat until their breath stops and they die.

claims_provenance.quote: Hıbılık genellikle yalnız kadın görünüşündedir ancak erkek görünüşlüsü de vardır. O, yanına gittiği kişinin göğsüne çöker ve nefesi kesilip ölene kadar boğazını sıkar.

claim.id: Menurut kepercayaan, hıbılık memberi banyak emas (altın) kepada orang yang menangkapnya; di beberapa daerah ia dianggap roh jahat (kötü ruh) yang menindih orang yang sedang tidur.
claim.en: According to belief, the hıbılık gives plenty of gold (altın) to whoever catches it; in some areas it is regarded as an evil spirit (kötü ruh) that presses down on people while they sleep.

claims_provenance.quote: İnanışa göre, hıbılık, onu yakalayan birine bol bol altın verir. Bazı yörelerdeki görüşlere göre, hıbılık uykudayken insanların üzerine çöken kötü ruhtur.

claim.id: Orang yang ditindih hıbılık tidak dapat bergerak (kıpırdayamaz), lidahnya kelu, dan ia bermandi keringat.
claim.en: A person pressed by the hıbılık cannot move (kıpırdayamaz), becomes tongue-tied and breaks into a sweat.

claims_provenance.quote: Hıbılık kimi basarsa, o insan yerinden kıpırdayamaz, dili tutulur ve ter basar.

claim.id: Nama padanan (eşdeğer) Hıbılık adalah Hıpılık, Hibilik, Hıbılıh, Gıbilik, dan Gıbılıh.
claim.en: Equivalent names (eşdeğer) for Hıbılık are Hıpılık, Hibilik, Hıbılıh, Gıbilik and Gıbılıh.

claims_provenance.quote: Eşdeğer: 1. HIPILIK, HİBİLİK, HIBILIH 2. GIBİLİK, GIBILIH

short_description.id: Hıbılık adalah roh jahat dalam kepercayaan rakyat di beberapa daerah Turki yang menindih dada orang tidur hingga mereka tak bisa bergerak, bahkan dapat mencekik sampai mati.
short_description.en: Hıbılık is an evil spirit of folk belief in parts of Turkey that presses on the chests of sleepers so they cannot move, and may even throttle them to death.

long_description.id: Menurut orang di beberapa daerah Turki, Hıbılık, yang juga disebut Gıbılık, adalah makhluk jahat yang rupanya menyerupai Alkarısı. Bedanya, Alkarısı hanya mengganggu perempuan yang baru melahirkan, sedangkan Hıbılık mengusik siapa saja, perempuan maupun laki-laki. Dua kajian akademik tentang agama tradisional Turk mencatat perbedaan yang sama.
long_description.en: According to people in some parts of Turkey, Hıbılık, also called Gıbılık, is a malevolent being that looks like the Alkarısı. The difference is that the Alkarısı troubles only women who have just given birth, whereas Hıbılık bothers anyone, woman or man. Two scholarly studies of traditional Turkic religion record the same contrast.

long_description.id: Biasanya ia berwujud perempuan, meski ada pula yang berwujud laki-laki. Ia datang kepada orang yang sedang tidur, menindih dadanya, dan mencekik lehernya; korbannya tak dapat bergerak, lidahnya kelu, dan ia bermandi keringat. Sebagian sumber menyebut serangan ini bisa berakhir dengan kematian, terutama bila korban tidak dibangunkan. Bagi orang yang didatanginya, ia tampak seperti kucing, lalu menghilang diam-diam dalam gelap.
long_description.en: It usually takes a female form, though male ones exist as well. It comes to a sleeping person, sits on the chest and squeezes the throat; the victim cannot move, is tongue-tied and drenched in sweat. Some sources say such an attack can end in death, especially if the victim is not woken. To the person it visits it appears like a cat, and it then vanishes silently in the dark.

long_description.id: Hıbılık juga dikaitkan dengan kekayaan. Bila tertangkap, ia memberi banyak emas kepada penangkapnya agar dilepaskan. Di kepalanya ada börk, sejenis topi, yang ajaib, dan siapa pun yang berhasil merebut topi itu dipercaya akan menjadi kaya.
long_description.en: Hıbılık is also linked to wealth. If caught, it hands its captor plenty of gold to be let go. On its head it wears a magic börk, a kind of cap, and whoever manages to seize the cap is believed to become rich.

cultural_context.id: Para peneliti menempatkan Hıbılık di antara roh maut atau roh rakus pada lapisan bawah di bawah Erlik, bersama Aldaçı dan Alkarısı, dan menyebutnya sebagai salah satu makhluk demonik yang diberi sifat feminin.
cultural_context.en: Scholars place Hıbılık among the death or gluttonous spirits of the lower layers below Erlik, together with Aldaçı and Alkarısı, and count it among the demonic beings to which femininity is attributed.

short_description.id: Halmasti adalah anjing langit jahat sebesar kuda dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan utara. Ia diyakini muncul di tempat kelahiran dan kematian, dan besi dipercaya dapat mengusirnya.
short_description.en: Halmasti is a malevolent, horse-sized sky hound of Chitrali mythology in northern Pakistan. It is believed to appear where births and deaths take place, and iron is said to keep it away.

long_description.id:
Halmasti, yang juga disebut Anjing Langit, adalah anjing jahat sebesar kuda dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan utara. Namanya, yang berarti guntur dalam bahasa Khowar, menunjukkan hubungannya dengan langit. Ia digambarkan mirip serigala besar berbulu merah gelap, berkaki panjang, dan bermoncong lebar; beberapa cerita bahkan menyebutnya mampu menyemburkan api.

Menurut kepercayaan setempat, Halmasti terutama datang ke tempat kelahiran bayi dan tempat jenazah dimandikan. Karena itu kedua tempat tersebut dijaga selama tujuh hari tujuh malam: bacaan Quran dilantunkan berkeliling di dekat jenazah, sementara bayi dinyanyikan lagu nina bobo. Melihat makhluk ini pun dianggap pertanda sial.

Bayi dianggap paling rentan, sehingga tidak pernah ditinggal sendirian. Bila keadaan memaksa, sebilah senjata besi diselipkan di bawah bantal bayi, sebab Halmasti diyakini membenci besi dan besi menjadi kelemahannya.

Penulis artikel kedua menelusuri asal-usulnya ke iblis perempuan Littu dari Sumer kuno, yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Lillith, dan ke penyihir Al atau Hal di kalangan suku Iran barat. Nama Halmasti diduga diwarisi dari roh perempuan Turkik Al-Basti, tetapi wujudnya sebagai anjing langit lebih menyerupai Tiangou dari mitologi Tiongkok kuno, yang memakan matahari dan bulan. Karena itu ia dipandang sebagai contoh perpaduan dunia Turkik, Iran, dan Sinitik di Chitral.
long_description.en:
Halmasti, also called the Celestial Hound, is a malevolent horse-sized dog of Chitrali mythology in northern Pakistan. Its name, meaning thunder in Khowar, reflects its tie to the sky. It is pictured as a big wolf-like beast with dark red fur, long limbs and a wide muzzle, and some tales even credit it with breathing fire.

In local belief, Halmasti mainly visits places where a baby has just been born or where a body is being washed. Both places were therefore watched for seven days and nights, with Quran recitation circling the dead and lullabies sung to the infant. Even catching sight of the creature was considered unlucky.

Infants were thought to be most at risk, so they were never left alone. When there was no choice, an iron weapon was slipped beneath the baby's pillow, because Halmasti was believed to loathe iron, which was its weak point.

The author of the second source traces it back to the Sumerian female demon Littu, later known as Lillith, and to the witch Al or Hal of western Iranic tribes. The name Halmasti is thought to come from the Turkic female spirit Al-Basti, but its form as a sky hound is closer to the Tiangou of ancient Chinese mythology, which devoured the sun and moon. It is therefore seen as an example of how Chitral blends Turkic, Iranic and Sinitic worlds.

short_description.id: Halmasti adalah anjing langit jahat sebesar kuda dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan utara. Ia diyakini muncul di tempat kelahiran dan kematian, dan besi dipercaya dapat mengusirnya.
short_description.en: Halmasti is a malevolent, horse-sized sky hound of Chitrali mythology in northern Pakistan. It is believed to appear where births and deaths take place, and iron is said to keep it away.

long_description.id: Halmasti, yang juga disebut Anjing Langit, adalah anjing jahat sebesar kuda dalam mitologi Chitrali di Pakistan utara. Namanya, yang berarti guntur dalam bahasa Khowar, menunjukkan hubungannya dengan langit. Ia digambarkan mirip serigala besar berbulu merah gelap, berkaki panjang, dan bermoncong lebar; beberapa cerita bahkan menyebutnya mampu menyemburkan api.
long_description.en: Halmasti, also called the Celestial Hound, is a malevolent horse-sized dog of Chitrali mythology in northern Pakistan. Its name, meaning thunder in Khowar, reflects its tie to the sky. It is pictured as a big wolf-like beast with dark red fur, long limbs and a wide muzzle, and some tales even credit it with breathing fire.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan setempat, Halmasti terutama datang ke tempat kelahiran bayi dan tempat jenazah dimandikan. Karena itu kedua tempat tersebut dijaga selama tujuh hari tujuh malam: bacaan Quran dilantunkan berkeliling di dekat jenazah, sementara bayi dinyanyikan lagu nina bobo. Melihat makhluk ini pun dianggap pertanda sial.
long_description.en: In local belief, Halmasti mainly visits places where a baby has just been born or where a body is being washed. Both places were therefore watched for seven days and nights, with Quran recitation circling the dead and lullabies sung to the infant. Even catching sight of the creature was considered unlucky.

long_description.id: Bayi dianggap paling rentan, sehingga tidak pernah ditinggal sendirian. Bila keadaan memaksa, sebilah senjata besi diselipkan di bawah bantal bayi, sebab Halmasti diyakini membenci besi dan besi menjadi kelemahannya.
long_description.en: Infants were thought to be most at risk, so they were never left alone. When there was no choice, an iron weapon was slipped beneath the baby's pillow, because Halmasti was believed to loathe iron, which was its weak point.

long_description.id: Penulis artikel kedua menelusuri asal-usulnya ke iblis perempuan Littu dari Sumer kuno, yang kemudian dikenal sebagai Lillith, dan ke penyihir Al atau Hal di kalangan suku Iran barat. Nama Halmasti diduga diwarisi dari roh perempuan Turkik Al-Basti, tetapi wujudnya sebagai anjing langit lebih menyerupai Tiangou dari mitologi Tiongkok kuno, yang memakan matahari dan bulan. Karena itu ia dipandang sebagai contoh perpaduan dunia Turkik, Iran, dan Sinitik di Chitral.
long_description.en: The author of the second source traces it back to the Sumerian female demon Littu, later known as Lillith, and to the witch Al or Hal of western Iranic tribes. The name Halmasti is thought to come from the Turkic female spirit Al-Basti, but its form as a sky hound is closer to the Tiangou of ancient Chinese mythology, which devoured the sun and moon. It is therefore seen as an example of how Chitral blends Turkic, Iranic and Sinitic worlds.

short_description.id: Hua Po adalah roh pohon dalam cerita Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Hua Po is a tree spirit in Chinese lore.

long_description.id:
Hua Po (花魄) adalah roh pohon dalam cerita Tiongkok. Kelahirannya dikaitkan dengan penyesalan orang yang meninggal setelah setidaknya tiga orang menggantung diri pada pohon itu.

Roh ini digambarkan sebagai perempuan cantik berkulit putih seukuran telapak tangan. Suaranya menyerupai parkit. Ia dikatakan mengering jika dibiarkan, lalu pulih ketika diperciki air.

Kisah tertulis tentangnya terdapat dalam kumpulan 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), bab 〈花魄〉. Di sana seorang terpelajar bermarga Xie menemukan makhluk perempuan setinggi sekitar lima cun yang berkicau seperti beo, membawanya pulang ke dalam sangkar, tetapi ia mengering dan mati setelah terkena sinar matahari. Orang yang mengenalinya menyebutnya Huapo dan berkata air masih dapat menghidupkannya. Xie lalu meletakkannya kembali di pohon, dan seekor burung besar membawanya pergi.
long_description.en:
Hua Po (花魄) is a tree spirit in Chinese lore. Its formation is linked to the regrets of the dead after at least three people hang themselves from the tree.

The spirit is described as a pale beautiful woman the size of a palm. Its voice resembles a parakeet. It is said to dry out if left alone and recover when sprinkled with water.

A written account appears in the collection 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), in the chapter "Huapo". There a scholar surnamed Xie finds a woman-shaped creature about five cun tall that chirps like a parrot and takes her home in a cage, but she dries up and dies after exposure to the sun. A man who recognised her called her Huapo and said water could still revive her. Xie then put her back in the tree, and a large bird carried her off.

description.id: Menurut sumber-sumber ini, ia mengering bila dibiarkan, dan dalam kisah Zibuyu ia mati setelah terkena matahari, sedangkan air dikatakan dapat memulihkannya.
description.en: According to these sources it dries up if left alone, and in the Zibuyu story it dies after being exposed to the sun, while water is said to be able to revive it.

role.id: Makhluk yang ditemukan seorang terpelajar di hutan.
role.en: The creature found by a scholar in the woods.

summary.id: Seorang terpelajar bermarga Xie menemukan makhluk perempuan mungil yang berkicau seperti beo dan membawanya pulang. Ia mati setelah terkena matahari; seorang yang mengenalinya menyebut namanya dan berkata air dapat menghidupkannya. Xie meletakkannya kembali di pohon dan seekor burung besar membawanya pergi.
summary.en: A scholar surnamed Xie finds a tiny woman-shaped creature that chirps like a parrot and takes her home. She dies after exposure to the sun; a man who recognised her named her and said water could revive her. Xie put her back in the tree and a large bird carried her off.

Saat mendekat, ia melihat seorang perempuan cantik setinggi sekitar lima cun, tanpa bulu di tubuhnya, putih mengilap seperti giok, dengan raut sedih di antara kedua matanya.

long_description.id: Kisah tertulis tentangnya terdapat dalam kumpulan 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), bab 〈花魄〉. Di sana seorang terpelajar bermarga Xie menemukan makhluk perempuan setinggi sekitar lima cun yang berkicau seperti beo, membawanya pulang ke dalam sangkar, tetapi ia mengering dan mati setelah terkena sinar matahari. Orang yang mengenalinya menyebutnya Huapo dan berkata air masih dapat menghidupkannya. Xie lalu meletakkannya kembali di pohon, dan seekor burung besar membawanya pergi.
long_description.en: A written account appears in the collection 《子不語》 (Zibuyu), in the chapter "Huapo". There a scholar surnamed Xie finds a woman-shaped creature about five cun tall that chirps like a parrot and takes her home in a cage, but she dries up and dies after exposure to the sun. A man who recognised her called her Huapo and said water could still revive her. Xie then put her back in the tree, and a large bird carried her off.

short_description.id: Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis.
short_description.en: Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being.

long_description.id:
Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis. Tradisi menyebut pengasingannya sebagai salah satu Empat Penjahat pada masa Shun. Sebuah teks klasik menyebut Huandou dibuang ke Gunung Chong bersama tiga hukuman lain, dan setelah itu seluruh negeri tunduk. Tidak ada bukti sezaman tentang keberadaannya karena ia hanya dikenal dari teks Tiongkok awal yang diwariskan.

Nama Huandou dan Huantou mempunyai beberapa varian aksara. Zhang Shoujie menyamakannya dengan Hundun, sedangkan Lüshi Chunqiu menggunakannya sebagai nama negeri. Kisah menyebut Huandou mengusulkan Gonggong untuk menangani banjir, tetapi Yao menolaknya karena menilainya pemimpin yang membangkang dan cacat. Teks klasik juga mencatat Huandou berbicara untuk Gonggong, dan sang kaisar menolak dengan menyebut Gonggong pandai bicara tetapi berbuat sebaliknya.

Serbuan Yu membuat Huandou mundur ke Gunung Chong, dan pada serbuan kedua Yu Agung ia akhirnya dikalahkan sehingga Sanmiao hancur. Classic of Mountains and Seas mencatat Huandou sebagai keturunan Zhuanxu, sedangkan catatan lain dari teks yang sama menyebutnya cucu Gun. Teks itu juga memitoskan Huandou sebagai lelaki berparuh burung dan bersayap yang memakan ikan dari laut, dan sebuah teks klasik melukiskan penduduk negeri Huantou berwajah manusia, bersayap, dan berparuh burung. Orang Miao masa kini mengakui Huandou bersama Chi You sebagai leluhur mereka.
long_description.en:
Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being. Tradition describes his exile as one of the Four Criminals under Shun. A classical text says Huandou was banished to Mount Chong together with three other punishments, after which the whole realm submitted. There is no contemporary evidence of his existence, since he is known only from transmitted early Chinese texts.

The names Huandou and Huantou have several written variants. Zhang Shoujie equates him with Hundun, while the Lüshi Chunqiu uses it as a state's name. The tale describes Huandou recommending Gonggong for flood control, but Yao rejected him, judging him a rebellious and flawed leader. A classical text also records Huandou speaking in favor of Gonggong, and the emperor refusing by saying Gonggong speaks smoothly but acts contrary.

The invasion by Yu led Huandou to retreat to Mount Chong, and in a second invasion by Yu the Great he was finally defeated, destroying the Sanmiao. In the Classic of Mountains and Seas, Huandou is traced to Zhuanxu in one line of descent and to Gun, Earl of Chong, as grandfather in another. The text also mythologises Huandou as a bird-beaked, winged man who eats fish from the sea, and a classical text depicts the people of the Huantou country as human-faced, winged, and bird-beaked. The modern Miao people claim Huandou, along with Chi You, as their progenitor.

short_description.id: Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis.
short_description.en: Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being.

long_description.id: Huān Dōu adalah penguasa Miao dalam tradisi Tiongkok kuno yang kemudian juga ditafsirkan sebagai makhluk mitologis. Tradisi menyebut pengasingannya sebagai salah satu Empat Penjahat pada masa Shun. Sebuah teks klasik menyebut Huandou dibuang ke Gunung Chong bersama tiga hukuman lain, dan setelah itu seluruh negeri tunduk. Tidak ada bukti sezaman tentang keberadaannya karena ia hanya dikenal dari teks Tiongkok awal yang diwariskan.
long_description.en: Huān Dōu is a Miao ruler in ancient Chinese tradition, later also interpreted as a mythical being. Tradition describes his exile as one of the Four Criminals under Shun. A classical text says Huandou was banished to Mount Chong together with three other punishments, after which the whole realm submitted. There is no contemporary evidence of his existence, since he is known only from transmitted early Chinese texts.

long_description.id: Nama Huandou dan Huantou mempunyai beberapa varian aksara. Zhang Shoujie menyamakannya dengan Hundun, sedangkan Lüshi Chunqiu menggunakannya sebagai nama negeri. Kisah menyebut Huandou mengusulkan Gonggong untuk menangani banjir, tetapi Yao menolaknya karena menilainya pemimpin yang membangkang dan cacat. Teks klasik juga mencatat Huandou berbicara untuk Gonggong, dan sang kaisar menolak dengan menyebut Gonggong pandai bicara tetapi berbuat sebaliknya.
long_description.en: The names Huandou and Huantou have several written variants. Zhang Shoujie equates him with Hundun, while the Lüshi Chunqiu uses it as a state's name. The tale describes Huandou recommending Gonggong for flood control, but Yao rejected him, judging him a rebellious and flawed leader. A classical text also records Huandou speaking in favor of Gonggong, and the emperor refusing by saying Gonggong speaks smoothly but acts contrary.

long_description.id: Serbuan Yu membuat Huandou mundur ke Gunung Chong, dan pada serbuan kedua Yu Agung ia akhirnya dikalahkan sehingga Sanmiao hancur. Classic of Mountains and Seas mencatat Huandou sebagai keturunan Zhuanxu, sedangkan catatan lain dari teks yang sama menyebutnya cucu Gun. Teks itu juga memitoskan Huandou sebagai lelaki berparuh burung dan bersayap yang memakan ikan dari laut, dan sebuah teks klasik melukiskan penduduk negeri Huantou berwajah manusia, bersayap, dan berparuh burung. Orang Miao masa kini mengakui Huandou bersama Chi You sebagai leluhur mereka.
long_description.en: The invasion by Yu led Huandou to retreat to Mount Chong, and in a second invasion by Yu the Great he was finally defeated, destroying the Sanmiao. In the Classic of Mountains and Seas, Huandou is traced to Zhuanxu in one line of descent and to Gun, Earl of Chong, as grandfather in another. The text also mythologises Huandou as a bird-beaked, winged man who eats fish from the sea, and a classical text depicts the people of the Huantou country as human-faced, winged, and bird-beaked. The modern Miao people claim Huandou, along with Chi You, as their progenitor.

short_description.id: Iemisch adalah kriptid dari Patagonia dekat Danau Colhué; digambarkan bersifat nokturnal dan sangat kuat sehingga dapat menyeret kuda ke dasar air, tetapi para peneliti menduganya berang-berang atau macan yang belum dikenali.
short_description.en: The Iemisch is a cryptid from Patagonia near Lake Colhué, described as nocturnal and so strong it can drag horses to the bottom of the water, though researchers suggested it was an unrecognised otter or jaguar.

long_description.id:
Iemisch (juga disebut Iemisch Listai) adalah kriptid dugaan dari Patagonia, khususnya di pegunungan dekat kawasan Danau Colhué. Pertama dicatat oleh Florentino Ameghino pada 1897, dan kajian lengkapnya terbit dalam buku On the Track of Unknown Animals tahun 1955. Ejaan lain dari para pencatat awal mencakup Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch, dan Hymché.

Hewan itu bersifat nokturnal dan konon begitu kuat sehingga dapat mencengkeram kuda dengan cakarnya dan menyeretnya ke dasar air. Menurut deskripsi dalam surat asli, kepalanya pendek, bertaring besar, tanpa telinga luar, berkaki pendek plantigrad dengan tiga jari depan dan empat belakang berselaput renang dan bercakar kuat, serta berekor panjang, pipih, dan dapat menggenggam. Ia konon bergerak secepat di darat seperti di air dan menjerit "soul-wrenching".

Robert Lehmann-Nitsche mengaku memiliki contoh kulit iemisch dari seorang peternak, dengan keping tulang kecil tertanam di kulit yang melindunginya dari mata panah. Dalam kajiannya, ia menulis bahwa kata Jemisch kemungkinan besar berarti berang-berang (Lutra felina) dan bahwa kisah hewan buas dalam mitos sebagian besar dapat merujuk pada macan. Ia dan Santiago Roth menyimpulkan bahwa iemisch tentulah sejenis berang-berang yang belum dikenal.

Paleontolog John Bell Hatcher mencatat bahwa walau lama bersama penduduk asli Patagonia ia tak pernah mendengar makhluk semacam itu, dan para sarjana kemudian meragukan penelitian Heuvelmans karena kata 'Iemisch' tidak dikaitkan dengan bahasa mana pun yang dituturkan di Patagonia. Tournouer, menurut Lehmann-Nitsche, mengaku melihat neomylodon yang misterius hidup di air, dan pemandunya menyebutnya Hymché.
long_description.en:
Reputed to dwell in the Patagonian mountains around Lake Colhué, the Iemisch (or Iemisch Listai) is a purported cryptid. Florentino Ameghino first recorded it in 1897, and the 1955 book On the Track of Unknown Animals gave it a complete study. Early recorders also wrote the name Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch and Hymché.

It keeps nocturnal habits and is reportedly strong enough to grab horses in its claws and haul them to the bottom of a lake or river. The original letter describes a short head, large canine teeth and no outer ears; short, flat-footed limbs with three toes in front and four behind, webbed for swimming and tipped with formidable claws; and a long, flat tail able to grip. Accounts say it is as fast on land as in water and gives a "soul-wrenching scream".

Robert Lehmann-Nitsche claimed to have a sample of iemisch skin from a rancher, with small bone plates embedded in it that protected the creature from arrowheads. In his study he wrote that the word Jemisch most probably means the otter (Lutra felina) and that tales of a fierce animal in the myths mostly may refer to the jaguar. He and Santiago Roth concluded it must be an unknown type of otter.

The paleontologist John Bell Hatcher observed that he had never encountered such a creature even after comparable time among Patagonian natives, and later scholars questioned Heuvelmans's work because 'Iemisch' belongs to no language spoken in Patagonia. Lehmann-Nitsche reports that Tournouer claimed to have seen the mysterious neomylodon alive in the water, with his guide naming it Hymché.

short_description.id: Iemisch adalah kriptid dari Patagonia dekat Danau Colhué; digambarkan bersifat nokturnal dan sangat kuat sehingga dapat menyeret kuda ke dasar air, tetapi para peneliti menduganya berang-berang atau macan yang belum dikenali.
short_description.en: The Iemisch is a cryptid from Patagonia near Lake Colhué, described as nocturnal and so strong it can drag horses to the bottom of the water, though researchers suggested it was an unrecognised otter or jaguar.

long_description.id: Iemisch (juga disebut Iemisch Listai) adalah kriptid dugaan dari Patagonia, khususnya di pegunungan dekat kawasan Danau Colhué. Pertama dicatat oleh Florentino Ameghino pada 1897, dan kajian lengkapnya terbit dalam buku On the Track of Unknown Animals tahun 1955. Ejaan lain dari para pencatat awal mencakup Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch, dan Hymché.
long_description.en: Reputed to dwell in the Patagonian mountains around Lake Colhué, the Iemisch (or Iemisch Listai) is a purported cryptid. Florentino Ameghino first recorded it in 1897, and the 1955 book On the Track of Unknown Animals gave it a complete study. Early recorders also wrote the name Chimchimen, Jémechim, Yem'chen, Jemisch and Hymché.

long_description.id: Hewan itu bersifat nokturnal dan konon begitu kuat sehingga dapat mencengkeram kuda dengan cakarnya dan menyeretnya ke dasar air. Menurut deskripsi dalam surat asli, kepalanya pendek, bertaring besar, tanpa telinga luar, berkaki pendek plantigrad dengan tiga jari depan dan empat belakang berselaput renang dan bercakar kuat, serta berekor panjang, pipih, dan dapat menggenggam. Ia konon bergerak secepat di darat seperti di air dan menjerit "soul-wrenching".
long_description.en: It keeps nocturnal habits and is reportedly strong enough to grab horses in its claws and haul them to the bottom of a lake or river. The original letter describes a short head, large canine teeth and no outer ears; short, flat-footed limbs with three toes in front and four behind, webbed for swimming and tipped with formidable claws; and a long, flat tail able to grip. Accounts say it is as fast on land as in water and gives a "soul-wrenching scream".

long_description.id: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche mengaku memiliki contoh kulit iemisch dari seorang peternak, dengan keping tulang kecil tertanam di kulit yang melindunginya dari mata panah. Dalam kajiannya, ia menulis bahwa kata Jemisch kemungkinan besar berarti berang-berang (Lutra felina) dan bahwa kisah hewan buas dalam mitos sebagian besar dapat merujuk pada macan. Ia dan Santiago Roth menyimpulkan bahwa iemisch tentulah sejenis berang-berang yang belum dikenal.
long_description.en: Robert Lehmann-Nitsche claimed to have a sample of iemisch skin from a rancher, with small bone plates embedded in it that protected the creature from arrowheads. In his study he wrote that the word Jemisch most probably means the otter (Lutra felina) and that tales of a fierce animal in the myths mostly may refer to the jaguar. He and Santiago Roth concluded it must be an unknown type of otter.

long_description.id: Paleontolog John Bell Hatcher mencatat bahwa walau lama bersama penduduk asli Patagonia ia tak pernah mendengar makhluk semacam itu, dan para sarjana kemudian meragukan penelitian Heuvelmans karena kata 'Iemisch' tidak dikaitkan dengan bahasa mana pun yang dituturkan di Patagonia. Tournouer, menurut Lehmann-Nitsche, mengaku melihat neomylodon yang misterius hidup di air, dan pemandunya menyebutnya Hymché.
long_description.en: The paleontologist John Bell Hatcher observed that he had never encountered such a creature even after comparable time among Patagonian natives, and later scholars questioned Heuvelmans's work because 'Iemisch' belongs to no language spoken in Patagonia. Lehmann-Nitsche reports that Tournouer claimed to have seen the mysterious neomylodon alive in the water, with his guide naming it Hymché.

short_description.id: Iliamna Lake Monster adalah makhluk air tak dikenal dalam cerita warga sekitar Iliamna Lake [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].
short_description.en: The Iliamna Lake Monster is an unknown aquatic creature in the stories of Iliamna Lake residents [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].

long_description.id:
Warga sekitar Iliamna Lake punya banyak cerita tentang Iliamna Lake Monster, makhluk air tak dikenal [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. Nama Iliamna sendiri konon nama ikan hitam besar mitos yang melubangi perahu penduduk yang jahat [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], dan berasal dari nama Dena'ina Nila Vena, "danau pulau" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. Danau itu terbesar di Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].

Menurut laporan berita, penampakan makhluk raksasa mirip ikan dilaporkan sejak jauh sebelum Alaska menjadi negara bagian; kebanyakan saksi menyebutnya gelap, mirip hiu, dan panjang 10 sampai 20 kaki [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], sering lebih dari satu dan sedang berburu [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. Dalam satu catatan, seekor makhluk sepanjang dan selebar perahu 18 kaki dengan mata sebesar bola sepak [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].

Ada dugaan penampakan itu sturgeon putih [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], hiu tidur Pasifik [iliamna-lake-monster-c07], atau pike utara raksasa [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; laporan berburu anjing laut dan memangsa salmon dinilai tidak cocok dengan sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. Sebuah surat kabar pernah menawarkan hadiah $100.000 untuk buktinya [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], tetapi belum ada bukti pasti diumumkan [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. Penampakan baru dilaporkan pada 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], dan seorang pria merasa yakin setelah jangkarnya terseret [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].
long_description.en:
Iliamna Lake residents tell many stories of the Iliamna Lake Monster, an unknown aquatic creature [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. The name Iliamna itself is said to be that of a mythical great blackfish that holes the boats of bad natives [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], and it derives from the Dena'ina name Nila Vena, "island's lake" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. The lake is the largest in Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].

According to a news report, sightings of giant fish-like creatures have been reported since well before Alaska became a state; most witnesses call them dark, shark-like and 10 to 20 feet long [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], often more than one and hunting [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. In one account, a creature was as long and wide as an 18-foot skiff with eyes the circumference of soccer balls [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].

Sightings have been suggested to be white sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], Pacific sleeper shark [iliamna-lake-monster-c07] or giant northern pike [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; reports of hunting seals and preying on salmon are said not to fit a sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. A newspaper once offered $100,000 for proof [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], but no definitive proof has been made public [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. New sightings were reported in 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], and one man became convinced after his anchor was dragged [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].

claim.id: Warga setempat punya sejumlah cerita tentang Iliamna Lake Monster, makhluk air yang tidak dikenal.
claim.en: Local residents tell stories of the Iliamna Lake Monster, an unknown aquatic creature.

claims_provenance.quote: Local residents have a number of stories about the alleged Iliamna Lake Monster, an unknown aquatic creature.

claim.id: Iliamna konon nama ikan hitam besar mitos yang menghuni danau ini dan melubangi perahu bidarka milik penduduk yang jahat.
claim.en: Iliamna is said to be the name of a mythical great blackfish of the lake that bites holes in the bidarkas of bad natives.

claims_provenance.quote: Iliamna is said to be "the name of a mythical great blackfish supposed to inhabit this lake, which bites holes in the bidarkas of bad natives."

claim.id: Ada dugaan bahwa penampakannya adalah populasi ikan sturgeon putih yang belum tercatat.
claim.en: Sightings may be of an undocumented white sturgeon population.

claims_provenance.quote: Speculation exists that reported sightings may be of an undocumented population of white sturgeon.

claim.id: Anchorage Daily News pernah menawarkan hadiah $100.000 untuk bukti nyata keberadaannya.
claim.en: The Anchorage Daily News once offered $100,000 for concrete proof of it.

claims_provenance.quote: The Anchorage Daily News once offered a prize of $100,000 for concrete proof of its existence.

claim.id: Nama Iliamna berasal dari nama Athabaskan Dena'ina pedalaman, Nila Vena, yang berarti "danau pulau".
claim.en: The name Iliamna is derived from the Inland Dena'ina Athabascan name Nila Vena, meaning "island's lake".

claims_provenance.quote: The name Iliamna is derived from the Inland Dena'ina Athabascan name Nila Vena, which means "island's lake".

claim.id: Iliamna Lake adalah danau terbesar di Alaska, terbesar ketujuh di Amerika Serikat, dan kedua puluh empat di Amerika Utara.
claim.en: Iliamna Lake is the largest lake in Alaska, the 7th largest in the United States and twenty-fourth in North America.

claims_provenance.quote: It is the largest lake in Alaska, 7th largest lake in the United States, and twenty-fourth in North America.

claim.id: Jeremy Wade, pembawa acara River Monsters di Animal Planet, termasuk yang menduga penampakan "monster" ini adalah sturgeon putih; yang lain meyakininya hiu tidur Pasifik.

claims_provenance.quote: Jeremy Wade, presenter of Animal Planet's River Monsters, is among those who speculate these sightings of a reputed "monster" are of a white sturgeon. Others believe that it is a Pacific sleeper shark.

claim.id: Ada beberapa dugaan penampakan baru pada 2017.
claim.en: There were several new supposed sightings in 2017.

claims_provenance.quote: There were several new supposed sightings in 2017.

claim.id: Menurut laporan berita, sejak jauh sebelum Alaska menjadi negara bagian telah banyak dilaporkan penampakan makhluk raksasa mirip ikan di danau itu; deskripsinya agak beragam, tetapi kebanyakan saksi menyebutnya berwarna gelap, mirip hiu, dan panjang 10 sampai 20 kaki.
claim.en: According to a news report, numerous sightings of giant fish-like creatures in the lake have been reported since well before Alaska became a state; descriptions vary somewhat, but most witnesses say the creatures are dark colored, shark-like in appearance and 10 to 20 feet long.

claims_provenance.quote: Since well before Alaska became a state, there have been numerous reported sightings of giant fish-like creatures in the lake. There’s some variation in descriptions, but most witnesses say the creatures are dark colored, shark-like in appearance and between 10 and 20-feet long.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Menurut laporan berita itu, sering ada lebih dari satu makhluk bersama-sama dan sering kali makhluk-makhluk itu sedang berburu.
claim.en: According to the news report, there is often more than one together and frequently the creatures are hunting.

claims_provenance.quote: Often there’s more than one together and frequently, the creatures are hunting.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Menurut laporan berita itu, laporan perilaku pemangsa makhluk tersebut, yakni menggiring anjing laut ke perairan dangkal untuk diburu dan memangsa kawanan salmon sockeye, tidak terdengar seperti sturgeon.
claim.en: According to the news report, reports of the creatures' predatory behavior, herding seals into shallows to hunt them and preying upon schools of sockeye salmon, do not sound like a sturgeon.

claims_provenance.quote: However, reports of the creatures’ predatory behavior — herding seals into shallows to hunt them and preying upon schools of sockeye salmon — don’t sound like a sturgeon.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Dalam satu catatan yang dimuat laporan berita itu, seekor makhluk sepanjang dan selebar perahu 18 kaki milik para pemburu dengan mata sebesar bola sepak, dan tampak seperti pike utara raksasa.
claim.en: In one account recorded in the news report, one creature was the length and width of the hunters' 18-foot skiff with eyes the circumference of soccer balls, and the creatures looked like giant northern pike.

claims_provenance.quote: One was the length and the width of their 18-foot skiff and had eyes the circumference of soccer balls. The creatures looked like giant northern pike.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Pada 1980 Anchorage Daily News menawarkan hadiah $100.000 selama lima bulan bagi siapa pun yang menunjukkan bukti jelas; belum ada bukti pasti diumumkan, meski penampakan dilaporkan hampir setiap tahun sejak itu.
claim.en: In 1980 the Anchorage Daily News offered a $100,000 reward over a five-month period for clear evidence of the monsters; no definitive proof has been made public, though sightings have been reported most years since.

claims_provenance.quote: In 1980, the Anchorage Daily News offered a $100,000 reward during a five-month period to anyone who presented clear evidence of the monsters. No definitive proof has been made public, though there have been sightings reported most years since.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Selama bertahun-tahun Wright menduga makhluk itu hiu tidur Pasifik yang beradaptasi di air tawar; kini ia bertanya-tanya apakah mereka populasi kecil pike utara raksasa; yang lain menduga sturgeon raksasa.
claim.en: For years Wright theorized the monsters might be Pacific sleeper sharks adapted to freshwater; now he wonders if they might be a tiny population of gargantuan northern pike; others have theorized giant sturgeon.

claims_provenance.quote: For years, Wright theorized that the monsters might be Pacific sleeper sharks that adapted to living in freshwater. Now, he’s wondering if they might be a tiny population of gargantuan northern pike. Others have theorized they’re giant sturgeon.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

claim.id: Pada 2017, setelah beberapa musim panas tanpa hasil, Stigar mengalami kejadian yang meyakinkannya bahwa monster itu nyata: jangkarnya seberat 38 pon terseret 50 yard dari tali pancing panjangnya.
claim.en: In 2017, after several summers with no action, Stigar had an experience that convinced him the monsters were real: his 38-pound anchor on his longline set had been dragged 50 yards.

claims_provenance.quote: In 2017, after several summers with no action, Stigar had an experience that convinced him the monsters were real. On that day he went to check his longline set and was surprised to see that his 38-pound anchor had been dragged 50 yards.
claims_provenance.source_citation: Juneau Empire — Pride of Bristol Bay: Catching the Iliamna Lake Monster

short_description.id: Iliamna Lake Monster adalah makhluk air tak dikenal dalam cerita warga sekitar Iliamna Lake [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].
short_description.en: The Iliamna Lake Monster is an unknown aquatic creature in the stories of Iliamna Lake residents [iliamna-lake-monster-c01].

long_description.id: Warga sekitar Iliamna Lake punya banyak cerita tentang Iliamna Lake Monster, makhluk air tak dikenal [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. Nama Iliamna sendiri konon nama ikan hitam besar mitos yang melubangi perahu penduduk yang jahat [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], dan berasal dari nama Dena'ina Nila Vena, "danau pulau" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. Danau itu terbesar di Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].
long_description.en: Iliamna Lake residents tell many stories of the Iliamna Lake Monster, an unknown aquatic creature [iliamna-lake-monster-c01]. The name Iliamna itself is said to be that of a mythical great blackfish that holes the boats of bad natives [iliamna-lake-monster-c02], and it derives from the Dena'ina name Nila Vena, "island's lake" [iliamna-lake-monster-c05]. The lake is the largest in Alaska [iliamna-lake-monster-c06].

long_description.id: Menurut laporan berita, penampakan makhluk raksasa mirip ikan dilaporkan sejak jauh sebelum Alaska menjadi negara bagian; kebanyakan saksi menyebutnya gelap, mirip hiu, dan panjang 10 sampai 20 kaki [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], sering lebih dari satu dan sedang berburu [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. Dalam satu catatan, seekor makhluk sepanjang dan selebar perahu 18 kaki dengan mata sebesar bola sepak [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].
long_description.en: According to a news report, sightings of giant fish-like creatures have been reported since well before Alaska became a state; most witnesses call them dark, shark-like and 10 to 20 feet long [iliamna-lake-monster-c09], often more than one and hunting [iliamna-lake-monster-c10]. In one account, a creature was as long and wide as an 18-foot skiff with eyes the circumference of soccer balls [iliamna-lake-monster-c12].

long_description.id: Ada dugaan penampakan itu sturgeon putih [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], hiu tidur Pasifik [iliamna-lake-monster-c07], atau pike utara raksasa [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; laporan berburu anjing laut dan memangsa salmon dinilai tidak cocok dengan sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. Sebuah surat kabar pernah menawarkan hadiah $100.000 untuk buktinya [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], tetapi belum ada bukti pasti diumumkan [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. Penampakan baru dilaporkan pada 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], dan seorang pria merasa yakin setelah jangkarnya terseret [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].
long_description.en: Sightings have been suggested to be white sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c03], Pacific sleeper shark [iliamna-lake-monster-c07] or giant northern pike [iliamna-lake-monster-c14]; reports of hunting seals and preying on salmon are said not to fit a sturgeon [iliamna-lake-monster-c11]. A newspaper once offered $100,000 for proof [iliamna-lake-monster-c04], but no definitive proof has been made public [iliamna-lake-monster-c13]. New sightings were reported in 2017 [iliamna-lake-monster-c08], and one man became convinced after his anchor was dragged [iliamna-lake-monster-c15].

short_description.id: İmrə adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat Turk dan Altai yang dipercaya membentuk Cemre, kehangatan yang jatuh berturut-turut ke udara, air, dan tanah pada awal musim semi.
short_description.en: İmrə is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture, believed to make up the Cemre, the warmth that falls in turn into the air, water and earth at the start of spring.

long_description.id:
İmrə, yang juga disebut İmere, Əmrə, Emire, atau Emre, adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat dan mitologi Turk dan Altai. Ia dipercaya membentuk Cemre, yaitu kenaikan panas pada awal musim semi yang muncul berselang tujuh hari: mula-mula di udara, lalu di air dan tanah. Menurut sumber, Cemre pertama jatuh ke udara pada 20 Februari.

Pada musim semi İmrə muncul dan naik ke langit sambil memancarkan cahaya yang bergetar. Setelah itu ia jatuh ke atas es dan mencairkannya, lalu masuk ke dalam tanah, sehingga uap naik dari tanah yang sudah hangat. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Anadolu, Cemre digambarkan sebagai bara api legendaris yang jatuh ke udara, air, dan tanah serta menghangatkannya; sebuah ensiklopedia daring menyebutnya tiga bara yang dikirim oleh jin pada akhir musim dingin.

İmrə melambangkan datangnya musim semi. Di kalangan orang Bulgar, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Zemire, dan sumber kedua menganggap jin Zemire itu sebagai bentuk tertua konsep ini.
long_description.en:
İmrə, also called İmere, Əmrə, Emire or Emre, is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture and mythology. It is believed to make up the Cemre, the rise in warmth at the start of spring that comes at seven-day intervals: first in the air, then in water and earth. According to the source, the first Cemre falls into the air on 20 February.

In spring İmrə appears and rises to the sky, giving off flickering lights. It then falls onto the ice and melts it, and enters the ground, so that steam rises from the warmed earth. In Anadolu folk belief the Cemre is pictured as a legendary ember that falls into the air, water and earth and warms them; an online encyclopedia calls them three embers sent by a genie at the end of winter.

İmrə represents the coming of spring. Among the Bulgars it is known as Zemire, and the second source regards that jinn Zemire as the oldest form of the concept.

short_description.id: İmrə adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat Turk dan Altai yang dipercaya membentuk Cemre, kehangatan yang jatuh berturut-turut ke udara, air, dan tanah pada awal musim semi.
short_description.en: İmrə is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture, believed to make up the Cemre, the warmth that falls in turn into the air, water and earth at the start of spring.

long_description.id: İmrə, yang juga disebut İmere, Əmrə, Emire, atau Emre, adalah jin musim semi dalam budaya rakyat dan mitologi Turk dan Altai. Ia dipercaya membentuk Cemre, yaitu kenaikan panas pada awal musim semi yang muncul berselang tujuh hari: mula-mula di udara, lalu di air dan tanah. Menurut sumber, Cemre pertama jatuh ke udara pada 20 Februari.
long_description.en: İmrə, also called İmere, Əmrə, Emire or Emre, is the spring jinn of Turkic and Altai folk culture and mythology. It is believed to make up the Cemre, the rise in warmth at the start of spring that comes at seven-day intervals: first in the air, then in water and earth. According to the source, the first Cemre falls into the air on 20 February.

long_description.id: Pada musim semi İmrə muncul dan naik ke langit sambil memancarkan cahaya yang bergetar. Setelah itu ia jatuh ke atas es dan mencairkannya, lalu masuk ke dalam tanah, sehingga uap naik dari tanah yang sudah hangat. Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Anadolu, Cemre digambarkan sebagai bara api legendaris yang jatuh ke udara, air, dan tanah serta menghangatkannya; sebuah ensiklopedia daring menyebutnya tiga bara yang dikirim oleh jin pada akhir musim dingin.
long_description.en: In spring İmrə appears and rises to the sky, giving off flickering lights. It then falls onto the ice and melts it, and enters the ground, so that steam rises from the warmed earth. In Anadolu folk belief the Cemre is pictured as a legendary ember that falls into the air, water and earth and warms them; an online encyclopedia calls them three embers sent by a genie at the end of winter.

long_description.id: İmrə melambangkan datangnya musim semi. Di kalangan orang Bulgar, makhluk ini dikenal sebagai Zemire, dan sumber kedua menganggap jin Zemire itu sebagai bentuk tertua konsep ini.
long_description.en: İmrə represents the coming of spring. Among the Bulgars it is known as Zemire, and the second source regards that jinn Zemire as the oldest form of the concept.
