claims.quote: Shibaemon-tanuki, or Shibaemon-danuki (芝右衛門狸 or 柴右衛門狸) is a bake-danuki told in the legends of Awaji island, Hyōgo Prefecture.

statement.id: Shibaemon-tanuki adalah tanuki gaib dari Pulau Awaji.
statement.en: Shibaemon-tanuki is a supernatural tanuki from Awaji Island.

claims.quote: Along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado island and the Yashima no Hage-tanuki of Kagawa Prefecture, he is counted among the "three famous tanuki of Japan." He is also written about in the colorful stories collection of the Edo period, the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari.

statement.id: Ia dihitung sebagai salah satu dari tiga tanuki terkenal Jepang.
statement.en: He is counted among Japan’s three famous tanuki.

claims.quote: Along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado island and the Yashima no Hage-tanuki of Kagawa Prefecture, he is counted among the "three famous tanuki of Japan." He is also written about in the colorful stories collection of the Edo period, the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari.

statement.id: Kumpulan cerita bergambar zaman Edo mencatat sosoknya.
statement.en: An Edo-period illustrated tale collection records him.

claims.quote: While disguised as a human and in the middle of performing an act, he was attacked by a dog and killed, but the details of the tale differ depending on region and literature.

statement.id: Satu cerita menggambarkan anjing membunuhnya ketika ia menyamar sebagai manusia.
statement.en: A tale describes a dog killing him while he is disguised as a human.

claims.quote: Mikuma (三熊山) behind the city of Sumoto, Awaji island, he lived with his wife Omasu (お増) and on moonlight nights with good weather, he drummed his belly.

statement.id: Satu kisah menyebut istrinya bernama Omasu.
statement.en: One account names his wife Omasu.

claims.quote: He performed mischief such as disguising himself as a human and making tree leaves seem like gold and sell them, but at the same time he did kind deeds such as guiding along humans who stumbled into the mountain while drunk, so nobody hated him.

statement.id: Cerita-ceritanya memadukan tipuan dengan bantuan bagi pelancong yang tersesat.
statement.en: His stories combine deceptive tricks with help for lost travelers.

claims.quote: While Shibaemon-tanuki was at the summit of Mt. Mikuma (三熊山) behind the city of Sumoto, Awaji island, he lived with his wife Omasu (お増) and on moonlight nights with good weather, he drummed his belly.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon-tanuki tinggal di puncak Gunung Mikuma di belakang Kota Sumoto, Pulau Awaji, bersama istrinya Omasu, dan pada malam berbulan yang cerah ia menabuh perutnya.
statement.en: Shibaemon-tanuki lived at the summit of Mt. Mikuma behind the city of Sumoto on Awaji island with his wife Omasu, and on fine moonlit nights he drummed his belly.

claims.quote: The people he has been kind to made offerings of 1 sho bottles of sake to where he dwelled.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Orang-orang yang pernah ditolongnya mempersembahkan botol sake satu sho ke tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: The people he had been kind to made offerings of one-shō bottles of sake at the place where he dwelled.

claims.quote: One time, Shibaemon heard that there was a very popular play called Nakaza that was being performed in Naniwa (now Osaka city) and disguised himself and Omasu both as humans to Osaka.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Suatu kali Shibaemon mendengar ada pertunjukan sangat populer bernama Nakaza di Naniwa (kini Kota Osaka), lalu ia dan Omasu menyamar sebagai manusia pergi ke Osaka.
statement.en: One time Shibaemon heard of a very popular play called Nakaza being performed in Naniwa (now Osaka city), and he and Omasu disguised themselves as humans and went to Osaka.

claims.quote: Shibaemon, who was stricken with grief, was about to return to Awaji, but decided to at least watch the play that Omasu wanted to see and used a technique to change tree leaves into gold and went to the theater.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon yang berduka hendak kembali ke Awaji, tetapi memutuskan menonton pertunjukan yang diinginkan Omasu dan memakai teknik mengubah daun pohon menjadi emas lalu pergi ke teater.
statement.en: Stricken with grief, Shibaemon was about to return to Awaji but decided to watch the play Omasu had wanted to see, and used a technique to change tree leaves into gold to go to the theater.

claims.quote: However, at the theater, there were tree leaves that were mixed in with the admission fees, so they suspected that a bake-danuki has slipped in among the guests and a guard dog was put on alert.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Namun di teater ditemukan daun pohon bercampur dalam uang karcis, sehingga orang curiga ada bake-danuki menyelinap di antara penonton dan seekor anjing penjaga disiagakan.
statement.en: At the theater, tree leaves were found mixed in with the admission fees, so people suspected a bake-danuki had slipped in among the guests and a guard dog was put on alert.

claims.quote: Shibaemon hid his fear and passed through the entrance, but within a gap of his confidence, the dog rushed to attack. Shibaemon immediately returned to his appearance as a tanuki, was chased around by the people who brought the dog and finally hit in the head and killed.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon menyembunyikan rasa takutnya dan melewati pintu masuk, tetapi saat kepercayaan dirinya lengah, anjing itu menerjang; ia segera kembali ke wujud tanuki, dikejar orang-orang yang membawa anjing, dan akhirnya dipukul di kepala hingga tewas.
statement.en: Shibaemon hid his fear and passed through the entrance, but when his confidence slipped the dog rushed to attack; he immediately returned to his tanuki form, was chased by the people with the dog and finally hit on the head and killed.

claims.quote: After Shibaemon's death, the people who came to see Nakaza decreased and there was a rumor that "it was a curse from having killed Shibaemon," so when the theater deified Shibaemon, the number of guests returned.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Setelah Shibaemon mati, penonton Nakaza berkurang dan beredar kabar bahwa itu kutukan karena membunuhnya; ketika teater itu mendewakan Shibaemon, jumlah penonton kembali.
statement.en: After Shibaemon's death, audiences at Nakaza fell and a rumor spread that it was a curse for having killed him; when the theater deified Shibaemon, the number of guests returned.

claims.quote: Afterwards, Shibaemon, as a popular god, was deeply worshipped by many actors such as Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon and Fujiyama Kanbi.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Kemudian Shibaemon, sebagai dewa yang populer, dipuja dengan sungguh-sungguh oleh banyak aktor seperti Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon, dan Fujiyama Kanbi.
statement.en: Afterwards Shibaemon, as a popular god, was deeply worshipped by many actors such as Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon and Fujiyama Kanbi.

claims.quote: Now, the Shrine of Shibaemon is near the castle ruins of Sumoto at the peak of Mt. Mikuma and due to the legend of Shibaemon, who liked theater, there are many performers who visit the shrine even now.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Kini kuil Shibaemon berada di dekat reruntuhan kastil Sumoto di puncak Gunung Mikuma, dan karena legenda Shibaemon yang menyukai teater, banyak pemain pertunjukan masih mengunjungi kuil itu.
statement.en: The Shrine of Shibaemon now stands near the castle ruins of Sumoto at the peak of Mt. Mikuma, and because of the legend of Shibaemon, who liked theater, many performers still visit it.

claims.quote: The Shibaemon Daimyoujin (柴右衛門大明神) that was deified in Nakaza also had a "return home" in the year 2000 and is now deified in the Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon Daimyoujin yang didewakan di Nakaza juga "pulang kampung" pada tahun 2000 dan kini dipuja di Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.
statement.en: The Shibaemon Daimyoujin deified in Nakaza also had a "return home" in the year 2000 and is now deified in the Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.

claims.quote: The next morning, when the government officials visited to inspect again, the soldier's appearance turned into a bloodstained tanuki. It was Shibaemon-tanuki.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Tokushima prefecture

statement.id: Dalam satu legenda, keesokan paginya wujud prajurit itu berubah menjadi tanuki berlumuran darah, dan itu adalah Shibaemon-tanuki.
statement.en: In one legend, the next morning the soldier turned into a bloodstained tanuki, and it was Shibaemon-tanuki.

claims.quote: In the past, in Awaji, there was a peasant called Shibaemon, and an old tanuki came to him and requested for food scraps, and feeling pity, he expressly left some food for the tanuki.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi, di Awaji dahulu ada seorang petani bernama Shibaemon, dan seekor tanuki tua datang meminta sisa makanan; karena kasihan, ia sengaja menyisakan makanan untuknya.
statement.en: In one version, there was once a peasant called Shibaemon on Awaji, and an old tanuki came to ask for food scraps; feeling pity, he deliberately left some food for the tanuki.

claims.quote: There are theories that reality of the legend of Shibaemon-tanuki is that it was an excuse for the Kougo Jihen, a struggle that broke out between Sumoto and Awa

statement.id: Ada teori bahwa kenyataan di balik legenda Shibaemon-tanuki adalah dalih bagi Kougo Jihen, pergolakan antara Sumoto dan Awa.
statement.en: There are theories that the reality behind the legend of Shibaemon-tanuki was an excuse for the Kougo Jihen, a struggle that broke out between Sumoto and Awa.

claims.quote: In the Edo period, at the base of Mount Seimi (勢見山) in Awa Province (now Tokushima prefecture), there was a theater business at the grounds of Kan'on-ji, and it earned great popularity.

claims.quote: The "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" is a sightseeing route featuring eight tanuki statues based on the legends of Shibaemon. Eight statues modeled on Shibaemon and his companions are located at various spots around the city. Each has its own name, blessing, and story.

statement.id: "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" adalah rute wisata dengan delapan patung tanuki berdasarkan legenda Shibaemon; tiap patung punya nama, berkat, dan kisahnya sendiri.

short_description.id: Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit.
short_description.en: Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics.

long_description.id:
Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit. Gulungan tersebut disimpan di Museum Nasional Nara. Ia digambarkan bertubuh seperti kumbang, berkaki delapan, dan menangkap sosok mirip oni.

Lukisan Hekija-e menghimpun dewa-dewa penolak kejahatan yang di Tiongkok dipercaya menghukum dan mengusir roh wabah; Shinchū muncul bersama Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki, dan Bishamonten. Polanya diduga berasal dari Tiongkok, tetapi wujud Shinchū hanya dikenal dari lukisan ini, dan warna tubuhnya yang berat dinilai khas. Karya itu diperkirakan dibuat antara akhir zaman Heian dan awal zaman Kamakura.
long_description.en:
Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics. The scroll is held by the Nara National Museum. It is depicted with a beetlelike body and eight limbs, grasping an onilike figure.

The Hekija-e brings together evil-repelling deities believed in China to punish and expel plague demons; Shinchū appears alongside Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki and Bishamonten. The designs are thought to derive from China, yet Shinchū's image is known only from this painting, and the heavy colouring of its body is considered distinctive. The work is dated to between the end of the Heian period and the start of the Kamakura period.

did_you_know.id: Shinchū dalam Hekija-e abad ke-12, sebuah Harta Nasional, disebut sebagai contoh paling jelas serangga yang diperbesar menjadi monster.
did_you_know.en: Shinchū in the 12th-century Hekija-e, a National Treasure, has been cited as the clearest example of an insect enlarged into a monster.

short_description.id: Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit.
short_description.en: Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics.

long_description.id: Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit. Gulungan tersebut disimpan di Museum Nasional Nara. Ia digambarkan bertubuh seperti kumbang, berkaki delapan, dan menangkap sosok mirip oni.
long_description.en: Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics. The scroll is held by the Nara National Museum. It is depicted with a beetlelike body and eight limbs, grasping an onilike figure.

long_description.id: Lukisan Hekija-e menghimpun dewa-dewa penolak kejahatan yang di Tiongkok dipercaya menghukum dan mengusir roh wabah; Shinchū muncul bersama Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki, dan Bishamonten. Polanya diduga berasal dari Tiongkok, tetapi wujud Shinchū hanya dikenal dari lukisan ini, dan warna tubuhnya yang berat dinilai khas. Karya itu diperkirakan dibuat antara akhir zaman Heian dan awal zaman Kamakura.
long_description.en: The Hekija-e brings together evil-repelling deities believed in China to punish and expel plague demons; Shinchū appears alongside Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki and Bishamonten. The designs are thought to derive from China, yet Shinchū's image is known only from this painting, and the heavy colouring of its body is considered distinctive. The work is dated to between the end of the Heian period and the start of the Kamakura period.

short_description.id: Sukunabikona adalah kami Shinto bertubuh kecil, dewa onsen, pertanian, penyembuhan, sihir, pembuatan sake, dan pengetahuan, yang membantu Ōkuninushi membangun negeri.
short_description.en: Sukunabikona is a small-bodied Shinto kami of hot springs, agriculture, healing, magic, brewing sake and knowledge, who helped Ōkuninushi build the land.

long_description.id:
Sukunabikona (少彦名神) adalah kami Shinto yang menguasai onsen, pertanian, penyembuhan, sihir, pembuatan sake, dan pengetahuan. Namanya berarti "tuan kecil yang termasyhur"; ia sering digambarkan sebagai kurcaci dan kerap dipasangkan dengan Ōkuninushi. Satu kisah bermula ketika Ōkuninushi melihat perahu kecil dari polong Metaplexis di Teluk Miho, dan di dalamnya ada kurcaci sebesar ibu jari.

Dalam usaha membantu Ōkuninushi menyelesaikan pembangunan negeri, ia menciptakan obat dan penawar penyakit serta mantra pelindung, dan ia disebut ahli sihir. Ketika ia jatuh sakit, Ōkuninushi merendamnya di mata air panas dan ia terbangun dalam keadaan sembuh dan menari di atas batu. Beberapa sumber juga menganggapnya penemu sake yang mengajari orang membuatnya dari beras.

Menurut tradisi, ia meninggalkan dunia ini di Pulau Awaji dengan memanjat sebutir jawawut yang melentingkannya ke Tokoyo no Kuni, sehingga ia dikenal sebagai dewa pendatang yang datang dari seberang laut lalu pergi. Kamus Jepang menyebutnya anak 神産巣日神 dalam Kojiki dan anak 高皇産霊尊 dalam Nihon Shoki, serta dewa obat-obatan.
long_description.en:
Sukunabikona (少彦名神) is a Shinto kami whose domains include onsen, farming, healing, magic, sake brewing and knowledge. The name is glossed "the small lord of renown"; he is often pictured as a dwarf and often appears alongside Ōkuninushi. One tale begins when Ōkuninushi sees a small boat made of a Metaplexis pod at Miho Bay, with a dwarf no bigger than a thumb inside.

In helping Ōkuninushi complete the building of the land, he invented medicines, cures and protective spells, and he is called a master of magic. When he fell ill, Ōkuninushi put him in a hot spring and he awoke cured and danced on a stone. Some sources also credit him with inventing sake, teaching people to brew it from rice.

According to tradition he departed from Awaji Island by climbing a grain of millet that flung him away to Tokoyo no Kuni, so he is known as an immigrant deity who arrived from overseas and later left. A Japanese dictionary calls him a deity of medicine, a child of 神産巣日神 in the Kojiki and of 高皇産霊尊 in the Nihon Shoki.

who.id: Sukunabikona adalah kami kecil, sering digambarkan sebagai kurcaci, yang menguasai penyembuhan, sihir, dan pembuatan sake.
who.en: Sukunabikona is a small kami, often described as a dwarf, who presides over healing, magic and brewing sake.

origin.id: Ia berasal dari mitologi Jepang dan dicatat sebagai putra dewa pencipta.
origin.en: He comes from Japanese mythology and is recorded as the child of a creator deity.

role.id: Ia membantu Ōkuninushi membangun negeri dan menciptakan obat serta mantra pelindung.
role.en: He helps Ōkuninushi build the land and invents medicines and protective spells.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal sebagai dewa kecil penemu obat dan, menurut beberapa sumber, sake.
famous_for.en: He is known as the small deity who invented medicines and, per some sources, sake.

description.id: Sukuna-biko-na menciptakan obat dan penawar penyakit; kamus Jepang menyebutnya dewa obat-obatan.
description.en: Sukuna-biko-na invented medicines and cures for illnesses; a Japanese dictionary calls him a deity of medicine.

description.id: Ia ahli sihir dan menciptakan mantra pelindung.
description.en: He is a master of magic and created protective spells.

role.en: The small dwarf inside the boat.

summary.id: Ōkuninushi melihat perahu kecil dari polong Metaplexis di Teluk Miho, dan di dalamnya ada kurcaci sebesar ibu jari.
summary.en: Ōkuninushi sees a small boat made of a Metaplexis pod at Miho Bay, with a dwarf no bigger than a thumb inside.

role.en: The ailing deity who is cured.

summary.id: Ōkuninushi merendam Sukuna-biko di mata air panas untuk menyadarkannya; setelah tidur sebentar ia sembuh dan menari di atas batu.
summary.en: Ōkuninushi put Sukuna-biko in the hot spring to revive him; after a nap he was cured and danced on a stone.

role.en: The deity who leaves the world.

summary.id: Ia memanjat sebutir jawawut di Pulau Awaji, yang melentingkannya ke Tokoyo no Kuni.
summary.en: He climbs a grain of millet at Awaji Island, which flings him into Tokoyo no Kuni.

description.en: Where Ōkuninushi saw Sukuna-biko-na's small boat.

description.id: Tempat ia meninggalkan dunia menurut tradisi.
description.en: Where he is said to have left this world.

note.en: Sukunabikona is frequently paired with Ōkuninushi and helped him build the land.

note.id: Dalam kisah Teluk Miho ia disebut anak Kami-Musubi.

claims.quote: Sukunabikona or Sukuna bikona (少彦名神, also known as Sukuna-biko, Sukuna-biko-na, Sukuna hikona) is the Shinto kami of the onsen (hot springs), agriculture, healing, magic, brewing sake and knowledge.

statement.id: Sukunabikona adalah kami Shinto yang menguasai onsen (mata air panas), pertanian, penyembuhan, sihir, pembuatan sake, dan pengetahuan.
statement.en: Sukunabikona is the Shinto kami of the onsen (hot springs), agriculture, healing, magic, brewing sake and knowledge.

claims.quote: His name means "the small lord of renown." He is often described as being a dwarf and is frequently paired with Ōkuninushi.

statement.id: Namanya berarti "tuan kecil yang termasyhur"; ia sering digambarkan sebagai kurcaci dan kerap dipasangkan dengan Ōkuninushi.
statement.en: His name means "the small lord of renown"; he is often described as a dwarf and is frequently paired with Ōkuninushi.

claims.quote: One day while Ōkuninushi was at Miho Bay, he saw a small boat on the whitecap waves.

statement.id: Pada suatu hari, ketika Ōkuninushi berada di Teluk Miho, ia melihat perahu kecil di ombak berbuih.
statement.en: One day while Ōkuninushi was at Miho Bay, he saw a small boat on the whitecap waves.

claims.quote: The boat was made of a Metaplexis pod.

statement.id: Perahu itu terbuat dari polong Metaplexis.
statement.en: The boat was made of a Metaplexis pod.

claims.quote: As part of his quest to help Ōkuninushi complete construction of the land, Sukuna-biko-na invented medicines and cures for illnesses and diseases, including magical spells for protection.

statement.id: Dalam usaha membantu Ōkuninushi menyelesaikan pembangunan negeri, Sukuna-biko-na menciptakan obat dan penawar penyakit, termasuk mantra pelindung.
statement.en: As part of his quest to help Ōkuninushi complete the building of the land, Sukuna-biko-na invented medicines and cures for illnesses and diseases, including magical protective spells.

claims.quote: In addition to his other domains, he is a master of magic and wizardry.

statement.id: Selain ranah-ranah lainnya, ia adalah ahli sihir dan ilmu gaib.
statement.en: In addition to his other domains, he is a master of magic and wizardry.

claims.quote: Ōkuninushi put Sukuna-biko in the hot spring water to revive him. Sukuna hikona then took a nap. When he awoke, he was cured, and Sukuna danced on a stone.

statement.id: Ōkuninushi merendam Sukuna-biko di air mata air panas untuk menyadarkannya; setelah tidur sebentar ia terbangun dalam keadaan sembuh dan menari di atas batu.
statement.en: Ōkuninushi put Sukuna-biko in the hot spring water to revive him; after a nap he awoke cured and danced on a stone.

claims.quote: Tradition holds that Sukuna-biko-na left this world at Awaji Island by climbing a grain of millet, which then dipped under his weight and rebounded, flinging him into Tokoyo no Kuni.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi, Sukuna-biko-na meninggalkan dunia ini di Pulau Awaji dengan memanjat sebutir jawawut yang melengkung karena beratnya lalu melenting dan melemparkannya ke Tokoyo no Kuni.
statement.en: Tradition holds that Sukuna-biko-na left this world at Awaji Island by climbing a grain of millet, which dipped under his weight and rebounded, flinging him into Tokoyo no Kuni.

claims.quote: Some sources credit him as well with the invention of Sake. He taught the people how to brew the beverage from rice.

statement.id: Beberapa sumber juga menganggapnya penemu sake; ia mengajari orang membuat minuman itu dari beras.
statement.en: Some sources also credit him with the invention of sake; he taught the people how to brew the beverage from rice.

claims.quote: Inside was a small dwarf, no bigger than a thumb.

statement.id: Di dalam perahu itu ada kurcaci kecil yang tidak lebih besar dari ibu jari.
statement.en: Inside the boat was a small dwarf, no bigger than a thumb.

claims.quote: 日本神話の神。古事記では 神産巣日神 かむむすひのかみ の子、日本書紀では 高皇産霊尊 たかひむすひのみこと の子。体の小さい神で、大国主神と協力して国づくりを行い、のち、 常世国 とこよのくに に帰った。医薬の神とされる。
claims.locator: Entri 少彦名神 (デジタル大辞泉)

statement.id: Kamus Jepang menyebutnya dewa mitologi Jepang yang bertubuh kecil, anak 神産巣日神 dalam Kojiki dan anak 高皇産霊尊 dalam Nihon Shoki, yang bersama 大国主神 membangun negeri lalu kembali ke 常世国, dan dianggap dewa obat-obatan.
statement.en: A Japanese dictionary calls him a small-bodied deity of Japanese mythology, a child of 神産巣日神 in the Kojiki and of 高皇産霊尊 in the Nihon Shoki, who built the land together with 大国主神 and later returned to 常世国, and is regarded as a deity of medicine.

claims.quote: He is known as an immigrant deity, in that he came from across the sea and then departed the land.

statement.id: Ia dikenal sebagai dewa pendatang, karena datang dari seberang laut lalu meninggalkan negeri itu.
statement.en: He is known as an immigrant deity, in that he came from across the sea and then departed the land.

claims.quote: When Kuebiko saw the dwarf, he said "That is Sukuna son of Kami-Musubi."

statement.id: Ketika Kuebiko melihat kurcaci itu, ia berkata bahwa itu Sukuna, putra Kami-Musubi.
statement.en: When Kuebiko saw the dwarf, he said that it was Sukuna, son of Kami-Musubi.

short_description.id: Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
short_description.en: Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils.

long_description.id:
Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya. Motif pada bejana perunggu menampilkan topeng hewan simetris dengan mata menonjol.

Nama yang dipakai masyarakat Shang dan Zhou untuk motif tersebut tidak diketahui. Zuo Zhuan mengaitkan taotie dengan kerakusan: seorang anak tak berbakat dari keluarga Jinyun yang rakus makanan dan minuman disebut orang 饕餮, dan Shun kemudian mengusir empat kaum jahat, termasuk Taotie, ke tepi-tepi dunia. Kutipan Lüshi Chunqiu menggambarkan kepala tanpa tubuh pada perunggu Zhou.

Li Zehou menafsirkan motif taotie sebagai komunikasi misterius antara manusia dan langit. Lüshi Chunqiu sendiri menyebut bahwa taotie pada tripod Zhou belum menelan manusia yang dimakannya tetapi sudah mencelakai tubuhnya sendiri.
long_description.en:
Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils. Bronze-vessel motifs depict a symmetrical animal mask with raised eyes.

The name used by Shang and Zhou people for the motif is unknown. The Zuo Zhuan associates taotie with gluttony: an untalented son of the Jinyun clan who was greedy for food and drink was called 饕餮 by the people, and Shun later banished four evil clans, Taotie among them, to the frontiers. A quoted Lüshi Chunqiu passage describes a head without a body on Zhou bronzes.

Li Zehou interprets taotie imagery as mysterious communication between people and heaven. The Lüshi Chunqiu itself says that the taotie on the Zhou tripod harms its own body before it has swallowed the people it eats.

note.en: Counted among the Four Perils together with Hundun, Qiongqi and Taowu.

note.en: Counted among the Four Perils together with Hundun, Qiongqi and Taowu.

claim.id: Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
claim.en: Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils.

claims_provenance.quote: The taotie is an ancient Chinese mythological creature that was commonly emblazoned on bronze and other artifacts during the 1st millennium BCE. Taotie are one of the Four Perils in Chinese classics like the Classic of Mountains and Seas, alongside the Hundun, Qiongqi, and Taowu.

claim.id: Motif pada bejana perunggu menampilkan topeng hewan simetris dengan mata menonjol.
claim.en: Bronze-vessel motifs depict a symmetrical animal mask with raised eyes.

claims_provenance.quote: The Taotie is often represented as a motif on dings, which are Chinese ritual bronze vessels from the Shang (c. 1600 – c. 1050 BCE) and Zhou dynasties (c. 1046 – 256 BCE). The design typically consists of a zoomorphic mask, described as being frontal, bilaterally symmetrical, with a pair of raised eyes and typically no lower jaw area.

claim.id: Nama yang dipakai masyarakat Shang dan Zhou untuk motif tersebut tidak diketahui.
claim.en: The name used by Shang and Zhou people for the motif is unknown.

claims_provenance.quote: Although modern scholars use the word taotie, it is actually not known what word the Shang and Zhou dynasties used to call the design on their bronze vessels; as American paleographer Sarah Allan notes, there is no particular reason to assume that the term taotie was known during the Shang period.

claim.id: Zuo Zhuan mengaitkan taotie dengan kerakusan.
claim.en: The Zuo Zhuan associates taotie with gluttony.

claims_provenance.quote: Within the Zuo Zhuan, taotie is used by the writer to imply gluttony.

claim.id: Kutipan Lüshi Chunqiu menggambarkan kepala tanpa tubuh pada perunggu Zhou.
claim.en: A quoted Lüshi Chunqiu passage describes a head without a body on Zhou bronzes.

claims_provenance.quote: The taotie on Zhou bronzes [ding] has a head but no body. When it eats people, it does not swallow them, but harms them.

claim.id: Li Zehou menafsirkan motif taotie sebagai komunikasi misterius antara manusia dan langit.
claim.en: Li Zehou interprets taotie imagery as mysterious communication between people and heaven.

claims_provenance.quote: Li Zehou, a Chinese scholar of philosophy and intellectual history, thinks the description of the taotie in the Lüshi Chunqiu has a much deeper meaning, and that "the meaning of taotie is not [about] 'eating people' but making a mysterious communication between people and Heaven (gods)."

claim.id: Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) menyebut seorang anak tak berbakat (不才子) dari keluarga Jinyun (縉雲氏) yang rakus makanan dan minuman (貪于飲食) serta tamak harta (冒于貨賄); orang-orang di dunia membandingkannya dengan tiga keburukan (三凶) dan menyebutnya 饕餮.
claim.en: The Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) tells of an untalented son (不才子) of the Jinyun clan (縉雲氏) who was greedy for food and drink (貪于飲食) and covetous of goods (冒于貨賄); the people of the world compared him with the three ills (三凶) and called him 饕餮 (taotie).

claims_provenance.quote: 縉雲氏有不才子，貪于飲食，冒于貨賄，侵欲崇侈，不可盈厭，聚斂積實，不知紀極，不分孤寡，不恤窮匱，天下之民，以比三凶，謂之饕餮
claims_provenance.locator: Zuo Zhuan, Wen 18 (bagian Jiu Fu Shu)

claim.id: Zuo Zhuan menyebut bahwa Shun (舜), sebagai menteri Yao (堯), mengusir empat kaum jahat (四凶族): Hundun (渾敦), Qiongqi (窮奇), Taowu (檮杌), dan Taotie (饕餮), melemparkan mereka ke empat penjuru tepi (四裔) untuk menangkal 螭魅.
claim.en: The Zuo Zhuan says that Shun (舜), as minister to Yao (堯), banished the four evil clans (四凶族): Hundun (渾敦), Qiongqi (窮奇), Taowu (檮杌) and Taotie (饕餮), casting them to the four frontiers (四裔) to ward off 螭魅.

claims_provenance.quote: 舜臣堯，賓于四門，流四凶族，渾敦，窮奇，檮杌，饕餮，投諸四裔，以禦螭魅

claim.id: Lüshi Chunqiu (呂氏春秋) menyebut bahwa pada tripod Zhou (周鼎) terukir (著) taotie (饕餮) yang berkepala tetapi tak bertubuh (有首無身); ia belum menelan manusia yang dimakannya (食人未咽) tetapi sudah mencelakai tubuhnya sendiri (害及其身). Kalimat berikutnya: berbuat tidak baik pun demikian (為不善亦然).
claim.en: The Lüshi Chunqiu (呂氏春秋) says that the Zhou tripod (周鼎) bears (著) a taotie (饕餮) with a head but no body (有首無身); before it has swallowed the people it eats (食人未咽) harm has reached its own body (害及其身). The next sentence says that doing wrong is likewise (為不善亦然).

claims_provenance.quote: 周鼎著饕餮，有首無身，食人未咽，害及其身，以言報更也。為不善亦然。

research_gaps.note: Ilustrasi dalam artikel tidak dipakai tanpa pemeriksaan berkas Commons, kecocokan subjek, dan lisensinya; belum ada gambar yang terverifikasi untuk entri ini.

Sumber kedua dicari di Wikisource Mandarin: Zuo Zhuan (Wen 18) dan Lüshi Chunqiu (卷十六) dipakai. Halaman Shanhaijing (Beishan jing, Paoxiao) dibuka tetapi tidak menyebut taotie, sehingga tidak dipakai.
Bagian lain (kemampuan, kelemahan, penggambaran modern) tidak diisi karena belum ada kutipan yang mendukungnya.

short_description.id: Tarkshya adalah makhluk Rigveda yang digambarkan sebagai kuda dengan sebutan arishta-nemi.
short_description.en: Tarkshya is a Rigvedic being described as a horse with the epithet arishta nemi.

long_description.id:
Tarkshya adalah makhluk Rigveda yang digambarkan sebagai kuda dengan sebutan arishta-nemi. Tafsir alternatif menganggapnya burung.

Mahabharata dan Harivamsha kemudian menyamakannya dengan Garuda. Bhagavata Purana juga mengaitkan nama itu dengan ayah Garuda. Mahabharata memasukkannya di antara keturunan Kashyapa. Sebutan arishta-nemi diterangkan berarti dengan pinggir roda yang utuh.

Dalam terjemahan himne Rigveda yang dikutip di sini, Tarkshya diseru demi kesejahteraan: ia disifati perkasa, ditugaskan para dewa, pemenang, pelampaui kereta, dan penakluk pasukan, serta cepat, dan di himne lain disebut bersenjata tanpa cela. Komentar yang menyertai himne-himne itu menyamakannya dengan suparna, putra Trksa, yang ditugaskan membawa Soma dari surga, dan dengan Garuda; komentar itu juga menafsirkan nama Aristanemi sebagai bersenjata tak rusak atau tak terkalahkan, tidak sama dengan penjelasan "pinggir roda yang utuh" dari sumber lain.
long_description.en:
Tarkshya is a Rigvedic being described as a horse with the epithet arishta nemi. An alternative interpretation regards him as a bird.

The Mahabharata and Harivamsha later identify him with Garuda. The Bhagavata Purana also associates the name with Garuda's father. The Mahabharata counts him among Kashyapa's offspring. The epithet arishta nemi is explained as with intact wheel rims.

In the translated Rigveda hymns quoted here, Tarkshya is invoked for welfare: he is described as mighty, commissioned by the gods, victorious, the outstripper of chariots, the overthrower of hosts and swift, and in another verse as having unblemished weapons. The commentary accompanying these hymns equates him with suparna, son of Trksa, commissioned to bring the Soma from heaven, and with Garuda; it also explains the name Aristanemi as having unharmed or irresistible weapons, unlike the "intact wheel-rims" explanation of another source.

short_description.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang.
short_description.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends.

long_description.id:
Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang. Mereka muncul sebagai satu raksasa, pasangan menikah, atau saudara dengan anggota tubuh luar biasa panjang.

Kisah Gunung Chōkai menggambarkan serangan terhadap pelancong dan kapal. Kisah berbeda antara hilangnya mereka setelah doa dan penyerahan diri disertai penghentian kanibalisme.

Kamus Digital Daijisen Plus mendefinisikannya sebagai yōkai raksasa bertangan atau berkaki luar biasa panjang dari wilayah Tōhoku dan Hokuriku. Dalam satu versi dari Yuza, raksasa ini menarik kapal dengan kakinya dari puncak Gunung Chōkai, sampai dewa langit meledakkan gunung itu dan puncaknya yang terlempar menjadi Pulau Tobishima.

Sebuah kamus biografi menyajikan tenaga-ashinaga sebagai sosok legenda Tiongkok yang tercatat dalam Shanhaijing sebagai orang berlengan panjang dan berpaha panjang. Menurut kamus itu, setelah masuk ke Jepang mereka dianggap makhluk abadi yang mendoakan umur panjang kaisar dan dilukis sebagai hiasan istana.
long_description.en:
Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends. They appear as one giant, a married pair or siblings with unusually long limbs.

Mount Chōkai accounts describe attacks on travelers and ships. Accounts differ between their disappearance after prayer and surrender with an end to cannibalism.

The Digital Daijisen Plus dictionary defines it as a giant yōkai with extraordinarily long arms or legs from the Tōhoku and Hokuriku regions. In one version from Yuza, the giant raked in ships with its feet from the summit of Mount Chōkai until the god of heaven blew the mountain apart, and the summit that flew off became Tobishima.

A biographical dictionary presents tenaga-ashinaga as legendary figures of China, recorded in the Shanhaijing as the long-armed and long-legged people. According to that dictionary, after entering Japan they were regarded as immortal beings invoked for the emperor's longevity and painted as palace decoration.

claim.en: After entering Japan (日本) under a new name, they were treated as immortal beings invoked for the emperor's (天皇) longevity and the permanence of the court, and were painted as decoration in the palace.

claims_provenance.quote: 日本にはいって名をかえ,天皇の長寿と朝廷の永久性をねがう不老長寿の神仙としてあつかわれ,宮中の装飾画にえがかれた。

claim.id: Dalam versi Yuza (Yamagata) yang dicatat basis data Nichibunken, makhluk raksasa ini duduk di puncak Gunung Chōkai (鳥海山), menarik kapal di lepas pantai dengan kakinya dan memakan awaknya; dewa langit marah dan meledakkan Gunung Chōkai, dan bagian puncak yang terlempar menjadi Pulau Tobishima (飛島).
claim.en: In a Yuza (Yamagata) version recorded in the Nichibunken database, this huge monster sat on the summit of Mount Chōkai (鳥海山), raking in ships offshore with its feet and eating their crews; the god of heaven grew angry and blew up Mount Chōkai, and the part of the summit that flew off became Tobishima (飛島).

claims_provenance.quote: この魔物はものすごく大きく、鳥海山の頂上にいながら沖合の船を足でかき寄せて乗員を喰っていた。天の神がこれを怒り、鳥海山を爆発させたとき飛んでいった頂上の一部が飛島である。

short_description.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang.
short_description.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends.

long_description.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang. Mereka muncul sebagai satu raksasa, pasangan menikah, atau saudara dengan anggota tubuh luar biasa panjang.
long_description.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends. They appear as one giant, a married pair or siblings with unusually long limbs.

long_description.id: Kisah Gunung Chōkai menggambarkan serangan terhadap pelancong dan kapal. Kisah berbeda antara hilangnya mereka setelah doa dan penyerahan diri disertai penghentian kanibalisme.
long_description.en: Mount Chōkai accounts describe attacks on travelers and ships. Accounts differ between their disappearance after prayer and surrender with an end to cannibalism.

long_description.id: Kamus Digital Daijisen Plus mendefinisikannya sebagai yōkai raksasa bertangan atau berkaki luar biasa panjang dari wilayah Tōhoku dan Hokuriku. Dalam satu versi dari Yuza, raksasa ini menarik kapal dengan kakinya dari puncak Gunung Chōkai, sampai dewa langit meledakkan gunung itu dan puncaknya yang terlempar menjadi Pulau Tobishima.
long_description.en: The Digital Daijisen Plus dictionary defines it as a giant yōkai with extraordinarily long arms or legs from the Tōhoku and Hokuriku regions. In one version from Yuza, the giant raked in ships with its feet from the summit of Mount Chōkai until the god of heaven blew the mountain apart, and the summit that flew off became Tobishima.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus biografi menyajikan tenaga-ashinaga sebagai sosok legenda Tiongkok yang tercatat dalam Shanhaijing sebagai orang berlengan panjang dan berpaha panjang. Menurut kamus itu, setelah masuk ke Jepang mereka dianggap makhluk abadi yang mendoakan umur panjang kaisar dan dilukis sebagai hiasan istana.
long_description.en: A biographical dictionary presents tenaga-ashinaga as legendary figures of China, recorded in the Shanhaijing as the long-armed and long-legged people. According to that dictionary, after entering Japan they were regarded as immortal beings invoked for the emperor's longevity and painted as palace decoration.

short_description.id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China.

long_description.id:
Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok. Erya memberi nama Fen untuk kura-kura bercangkang keras dan Nai untuk labi-labi.

Terjemahan Shan Hai Jing menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di River Mad pada Mount Bigbitter. Kisah lain menempatkan labi-labi berkaki tiga dengan ekor bercabang di River Trailer.

Teks-teks lama menambahkan beberapa rincian. Catatan pada Erya menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di 大苦山 dan labi-labi berkaki tiga di 從山, serta di kolam di 君山, tempat juga muncul kura-kura bermata enam. Komentar Erya menjelaskan bahwa hewan berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda karena kura-kura dan labi-labi biasanya berkaki empat. Kisah dalam 《庚巳編》 menyebut seorang pria yang lenyap setelah memakan labi-labi berkaki tiga, dan nelayan yang mencarinya lebih dulu menjaring gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia.
long_description.en:
Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China. The Erya names the hard shelled turtle Fen and the softshell turtle Nai.

A translation of the Shan Hai Jing places three-footed turtles in River Mad on Mount Bigbitter. Another passage places three-footed softshell turtles with branching tails in River Trailer.

Older texts add further details. The Erya annotation mentions three-legged turtles on Mount 大苦山, three-legged softshell turtles on Mount 從山, and a pond on Mount 君山 that also yields six-eyed turtles. The Erya commentary explains that the three-footed animals get distinct names because turtles and softshell turtles ordinarily have four feet. A tale in the 《庚巳編》 describes a man who vanished after eating a three-legged softshell turtle, and fishermen searching for one first netted a human-shaped lump of flesh.

claim.id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok.
claim.en: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China.

claims_provenance.quote: Three-legged turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足龟; traditional Chinese: 三足龜; pinyin: Sānzúguī) and Three-legged softshell turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足鳖; traditional Chinese: 三足鱉; pinyin: Sānzúbiē) are mythical turtles from China.

claim.id: Erya memberi nama Fen untuk kura-kura bercangkang keras dan Nai untuk labi-labi.
claim.en: The Erya names the hard shelled turtle Fen and the softshell turtle Nai.

claims_provenance.quote: According to the ancient dictionary Erya, the former (pertaining to hardshell turtles including tortoises) is properly called Fen (simplified Chinese: 贲; traditional Chinese: 賁; pinyin: Fén), and the latter, Nai (Chinese: 能; pinyin: Nái).

claim.id: Terjemahan Shan Hai Jing menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di River Mad pada Mount Bigbitter.
claim.en: A translation of the Shan Hai Jing places three-footed turtles in River Mad on Mount Bigbitter.

claims_provenance.quote: ...On the south face of Mount Bigbitter the River Mad rises and flows southwest to empty into the River Person. Three-footed turtles are numerous in the River Mad. Those who eat it won't have a serious illness, and it can be taken to cure a swelling.

claim.id: Kisah lain menempatkan labi-labi berkaki tiga dengan ekor bercabang di River Trailer.
claim.en: Another passage places three-footed softshell turtles with branching tails in River Trailer.

claims_provenance.quote: ...The River Trailer rises on its summit and runs a hidden course to its base. This river contains many three-footed [softshell] turtles with a branching tail. If you eat it, you won't succumb to the plague of the malign force.

claim.id: Catatan pada Erya mengutip 《山海經》: banyak labi-labi berkaki tiga di gunung 從山 dan kura-kura berkaki tiga di gunung 大苦山; catatan itu menambahkan bahwa di kolam di gunung 君山 di Kabupaten 陽羨 (Wuxing) muncul labi-labi berkaki tiga dan juga kura-kura bermata enam.
claim.en: The annotation to the Erya quotes the 《山海經》: three-legged softshell turtles are plentiful on Mount 從山 and three-legged turtles on Mount 大苦山; it adds that a pond on Mount 君山 in Yangxian County (吳興郡陽羨縣) yields three-legged softshell turtles and also six-eyed turtles.

claims_provenance.quote: 《山海經》曰：從山多三足鱉，大苦山多三足龜。今吳興郡陽羨縣君山上有池，池中出三足鱉，又有六眼龜。
claims_provenance.locator: 釋魚, 鱉三足，能。龜三足，賁 (annotation)

claim.id: Komentar pada Erya menjelaskan bahwa labi-labi dan kura-kura umumnya berkaki empat, sehingga yang berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda: 能 untuk labi-labi dan 賁 untuk kura-kura.
claim.en: The commentary to the Erya explains that softshell turtles and turtles ordinarily have four feet, so the three-footed ones are given different names: 能 for the softshell turtle and 賁 for the turtle.

claims_provenance.quote: 鱉、龜皆四足，三足者異，故異其名。鱉之三足者名能，龜之三足者名賁也。

claim.id: Dalam 《庚巳編》 diceritakan seorang warga 太倉州 membeli labi-labi berkaki tiga dari nelayan dan istrinya memasaknya; setelah ia memakannya sendiri, sang istri masuk dan hanya menemukan seuntai rambut serta pakaian suaminya di lantai, seolah ia telah meluruhkan wujudnya.
claim.en: The 《庚巳編》 tells of a commoner of 太倉州 who bought a three-legged softshell turtle from a fisherman and had his wife cook it; after he ate it, his wife found only a lock of hair and his clothes on the ground, as if he had shed his form.

claims_provenance.quote: 庚午夏，太倉州有百姓道見漁者，持一鱉而三足，買歸令婦炰之。既熟，呼婦共餐，婦不欲食，出坐門外。久之不聞其夫聲，入視已失所在，地上止存發一縷，衣服冠履，事事皆在，如蛻形者。

claim.id: Para nelayan dalam kisah itu mengatakan bahwa ketika diperintahkan menangkap labi-labi berkaki tiga, mereka lebih dulu menjaring benda yang sangat berat berupa gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia, berwajah lengkap tetapi tanpa tangan dan kaki, bergerak-gerak dengan mata terpejam, lalu melemparnya kembali ke air.
claim.en: The fishermen in the tale say that when ordered to catch a three-legged softshell turtle they first netted something very heavy, a lump of flesh shaped like a person with all facial features but no hands or feet, wriggling with closed eyes, and threw it back into the water.

claims_provenance.quote: 群漁云：初被命，網於川，舉網驚其太重，及岸視之，乃一肉塊如人形，五官俱具而無手足，閉目蠢動。漁大驚怕，擲之水中

statement.id: Komentar pada Erya menjelaskan bahwa labi-labi dan kura-kura umumnya berkaki empat, sehingga yang berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda: 能 untuk labi-labi dan 賁 untuk kura-kura.
statement.en: The commentary to the Erya explains that softshell turtles and turtles ordinarily have four feet, so the three-footed ones are given different names: 能 for the softshell turtle and 賁 for the turtle.

claims.quote: 庚午夏，太倉州有百姓道見漁者，持一鱉而三足，買歸令婦炰之。既熟，呼婦共餐，婦不欲食，出坐門外。久之不聞其夫聲，入視已失所在，地上止存發一縷，衣服冠履，事事皆在，如蛻形者。

statement.id: Dalam 《庚巳編》 diceritakan seorang warga 太倉州 membeli labi-labi berkaki tiga dari nelayan dan istrinya memasaknya; setelah ia memakannya sendiri, sang istri masuk dan hanya menemukan seuntai rambut serta pakaian suaminya di lantai, seolah ia telah meluruhkan wujudnya.
statement.en: The 《庚巳編》 tells of a commoner of 太倉州 who bought a three-legged softshell turtle from a fisherman and had his wife cook it; after he ate it, his wife found only a lock of hair and his clothes on the ground, as if he had shed his form.

claims.quote: 群漁云：初被命，網於川，舉網驚其太重，及岸視之，乃一肉塊如人形，五官俱具而無手足，閉目蠢動。漁大驚怕，擲之水中

statement.id: Para nelayan dalam kisah itu mengatakan bahwa ketika diperintahkan menangkap labi-labi berkaki tiga, mereka lebih dulu menjaring benda yang sangat berat berupa gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia, berwajah lengkap tetapi tanpa tangan dan kaki, bergerak-gerak dengan mata terpejam, lalu melemparnya kembali ke air.
statement.en: The fishermen in the tale say that when ordered to catch a three-legged softshell turtle they first netted something very heavy, a lump of flesh shaped like a person with all facial features but no hands or feet, wriggling with closed eyes, and threw it back into the water.

short_description.en: The Three Pioneer Kami (開拓三神) is the collective name for three kami, Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona, enshrined at Hokkaidō Jingū and at new shrines in territories of Japanese expansion.

long_description.id:
Tiga Kami Perintis (開拓三神, kaitaku-sanshin) adalah nama kolektif untuk tiga kami yang dipuja di kuil-kuil seperti Hokkaidō Jingū, yaitu kuil yang baru didirikan di wilayah yang dimasuki bangsa Yamato sejak zaman pramodern dan modern, bukan di daratan utama Jepang. Ketiganya adalah Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi, dan Sukunahikona.

Ōkunitama digambarkan sebagai roh negeri itu sendiri, Ōnamuchi sebagai dewa pembentuk negeri, dan Sukunahikona sebagai dewa yang membantunya. Menurut artikel jurnal Suga Kōji, ketiganya dipilih dari kelompok kunitsu-kami (地祇) dalam mitologi klasik Jepang dan dimohonkan sebagai penjaga pembukaan lahan (kaitaku, 開拓) di tiap wilayah.

Menurut Encyclopedia of Shinto, Sukunahikona adalah kami mungil yang jatuh dari sela jari induknya dan membantu Ōnamuchi membentuk negeri; di hampir semua versi kisah keduanya tampil berpasangan dan bekerja sama mengembangkan negeri serta menciptakan obat-obatan. Ōnamuchi biasanya dianggap nama lain Ōkuninushi, meski beberapa karya menggambarkannya sebagai kami pembentuk negeri.
long_description.en:
The Three Pioneer Kami (開拓三神, kaitaku-sanshin) is a collective name for three kami enshrined at shrines such as Hokkaidō Jingū, that is, shrines newly built in regions the Yamato people entered from the early modern and modern periods rather than on the Japanese mainland. The three are Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona.

Ōkunitama is described as the spirit of the land itself, Ōnamuchi as the land-making deity, and Sukunahikona as the deity who helped him. According to Suga Kōji's journal article, the three were chosen from the kunitsu-kami (地祇) of Japanese classical mythology and invoked as guardians of pioneering (kaitaku, 開拓) in each region.

According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, Sukunahikona is a tiny kami who fell from between his parent's fingers and helped Ōnamuchi form the land; in almost all versions of the story the two appear as a pair and cooperate in developing the land and inventing medicines. Ōnamuchi is usually considered another name of Ōkuninushi, although some works describe him as a land-forming kami.

short_description.en: Tōdaiki is a figure in a tale recorded in Heike Monogatari and other classical works.

long_description.id:
Tōdaiki adalah sosok dalam cerita yang dicatat Heike Monogatari dan sejumlah karya klasik lainnya. Dalam gambar Toriyama Sekien, ia berpakaian bergaya Tiongkok dan membawa lampu di atas kepala; wujud asalnya adalah manusia.

Kisahnya menceritakan Karu no Otodo yang hilang setelah pergi sebagai utusan ke Tiongkok. Anaknya, Hitsu no Saishō, pergi mencarinya dan menjumpai manusia yang dijadikan penyangga lilin. Anak tersebut kemudian mengenali sosok itu sebagai ayahnya. Folkloris Yoshiyuki Iikura menolak menganggap kemiripan dengan legenda urban modern sebagai bukti garis pewarisan cerita.

Kamus modern menggolongkannya sebagai yōkai dan meringkas kisahnya: seorang utusan ke Tiongkok dipakukan kandil di kepalanya lalu diubah menjadi oni. Contoh tertua nama itu yang dikutip kamus berasal dari Hōbutsushū sekitar tahun 1179, yang menyebut lampu dipasang di kepala dan tubuh yang dilukisi.
long_description.en:
Tōdaiki is a figure in a tale recorded in Heike Monogatari and other classical works. In Toriyama Sekien's depiction, the figure wears Chinese-style clothes and carries a lamp on the head; the underlying figure is human.

The tale tells of Karu no Otodo, who disappears after travelling as an envoy to China. His son Hitsu no Saishō searches for him and encounters a man turned into a candle stand. The son then recognizes the figure as his father. Folklorist Yoshiyuki Iikura rejects treating resemblance to a modern urban legend as proof of narrative transmission.

Modern dictionaries class it as a yōkai and summarise the tale: an envoy to China had a candlestand nailed to his head and was turned into an oni. The earliest example of the name cited by the dictionary is the Hōbutsushū of about 1179, which mentions a lamp fixed on the head and a painted body.

short_description.id: Trucafort adalah raksasa setinggi gunung dalam mitologi Katalan yang membawa dua batu dan menjatuhkan yang terberat kepada anak-anak nakal.
short_description.en: Trucafort is a mountain-tall giant of Catalan mythology who carries two stones and drops the heavier one on naughty children.

long_description.id:
Trucafort adalah tokoh mitologi Katalan: lelaki setinggi gunung dengan janggut begitu panjang hingga terinjak saat berjalan. Ia membawa dua batu, satu di atas kepala dan satu lagi sepuluh kali lebih berat yang dijatuhkannya kepada anak-anak nakal. Menurut Joan Amades, ia lazim dalam cerita anak di Castellar de n'Hug.

Antara 1970 dan 1990 ia tokoh umum dalam dongeng Katalan, bahkan di sekolah dasar. Sisinya sebagai bandit dikaitkan dengan bandit nyata Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, meski legenda menampilkannya jauh lebih romantis.

Ciri utamanya adalah batu besar yang dipakainya di atas kepala seperti topi. Lolongan kesakitannya, karena terus menginjak janggutnya sendiri, konon mengguncang gunung dan terdengar hingga tujuh jam jauhnya. Ia juga disebut membawa gada batu raksasa untuk meremukkan anak-anak nakal.

Banyak yang berpendapat tokoh ini mungkin berasal dari tokoh sejarah, atau setidaknya berbagi julukan dengannya.
long_description.en:
Trucafort is a figure of Catalan mythology: a man as tall as a mountain with a beard so long he treads on it. He carries two stones, one on his head and another ten times heavier that he drops on naughty children. According to Joan Amades he was common in children's stories at Castellar de n'Hug.

Between 1970 and 1990 he was a common figure in Catalan tales, even in primary schools. His bandit side is linked to the real bandit Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, though the legend paints him far more romantically.

His main feature was a huge rock worn on his head like a hat. His howls of pain from treading on his own beard were said to shake the mountains and be heard seven hours away. He was also said to carry a huge stone mace to crush bad children.

Many suggest the figure may stem from a historical person, or at least a shared nickname.

short_description.id: Trucafort adalah raksasa setinggi gunung dalam mitologi Katalan yang membawa dua batu dan menjatuhkan yang terberat kepada anak-anak nakal.
short_description.en: Trucafort is a mountain-tall giant of Catalan mythology who carries two stones and drops the heavier one on naughty children.

long_description.id: Trucafort adalah tokoh mitologi Katalan: lelaki setinggi gunung dengan janggut begitu panjang hingga terinjak saat berjalan. Ia membawa dua batu, satu di atas kepala dan satu lagi sepuluh kali lebih berat yang dijatuhkannya kepada anak-anak nakal. Menurut Joan Amades, ia lazim dalam cerita anak di Castellar de n'Hug.
long_description.en: Trucafort is a figure of Catalan mythology: a man as tall as a mountain with a beard so long he treads on it. He carries two stones, one on his head and another ten times heavier that he drops on naughty children. According to Joan Amades he was common in children's stories at Castellar de n'Hug.

long_description.id: Antara 1970 dan 1990 ia tokoh umum dalam dongeng Katalan, bahkan di sekolah dasar. Sisinya sebagai bandit dikaitkan dengan bandit nyata Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, meski legenda menampilkannya jauh lebih romantis.
long_description.en: Between 1970 and 1990 he was a common figure in Catalan tales, even in primary schools. His bandit side is linked to the real bandit Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, though the legend paints him far more romantically.

long_description.id: Ciri utamanya adalah batu besar yang dipakainya di atas kepala seperti topi. Lolongan kesakitannya, karena terus menginjak janggutnya sendiri, konon mengguncang gunung dan terdengar hingga tujuh jam jauhnya. Ia juga disebut membawa gada batu raksasa untuk meremukkan anak-anak nakal.
long_description.en: His main feature was a huge rock worn on his head like a hat. His howls of pain from treading on his own beard were said to shake the mountains and be heard seven hours away. He was also said to carry a huge stone mace to crush bad children.

short_description.id: Underwater panther atau Mishipeshu ("Lynx Besar") adalah makhluk air mitos terpenting bagi bangsa Anishinaabeg dan tetangganya di Great Lakes. Ia lebih sering dipandang jahat dan perlu ditenangkan, tetapi sebagian tradisi meyakininya juga melindungi.
short_description.en: The underwater panther or Mishipeshu ("the Great Lynx") is a key mythical water being of the Anishinaabeg and neighbours around the Great Lakes. It was more often seen as malevolent and in need of placating, though some traditions held it could also protect.

long_description.id:
Underwater panther adalah salah satu makhluk air mitos terpenting di wilayah Great Lakes, terutama bagi Anishinaabeg. Namanya, Mishipeshu, berarti "Lynx Besar"; ia berkepala dan bercakar kucing raksasa, bersisik, dan berduri di punggung serta ekornya. Ia tinggal di Pulau Michipicoten, Danau Superior, dan bagi orang Algonquin adalah makhluk dunia bawah yang paling kuat. Kamus Ojibwe mengartikan kata mishibizhii sebagai singa atau panter dan sebagai underwater panther.

Menurut kepercayaan itu, Mishipeshu hidup di bagian terdalam danau dan sungai, tempat ia dapat menimbulkan badai, jeram, dan arus, menenggelamkan kano, dan menewaskan orang, sering anak-anak. Ia juga dikenal sebagai penjaga tembaga di Danau Superior dan wilayah Great Lakes, dan manito air ini memberi hadiah tembaga. Ia dipandang berseberangan dengan thunderbird, penguasa kekuatan udara, dalam konflik abadi namun saling melengkapi.

Sebagian tradisi meyakini underwater panther dapat menjadi makhluk penolong dan pelindung: ia dipercaya melindungi dan memberi makan orang yang jatuh menembus es, dan memberi kekuatan penyembuhan kepada dukun yang menerima perlindungannya. Namun lebih sering ia dipandang sebagai binatang jahat yang membawa kematian dan kemalangan dan perlu ditenangkan. Mengambil tembaga sangat tabu, terlebih dari Pulau Michipicoten, dan hingga tahun 1950-an Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians masih menggelar upacara untuk menenangkannya.
long_description.en:
The underwater panther is a leading mythical water being of the Great Lakes region, especially for the Anishinaabeg. Its name, Mishipeshu, means "the Great Lynx"; it has a giant cat's head and paws, scales, and spikes down its back and tail. It lives on Michipicoten Island in Lake Superior, and for the Algonquins it ranked as the strongest underworld being. An Ojibwe dictionary glosses the word mishibizhii as a lion or panther and as an underwater panther.

In these beliefs, Mishipeshu lives in the deepest parts of lakes and rivers, where it can stir up storms, rapids and currents, sink canoes and drown people, often children. It is also known as the keeper of the copper of Lake Superior and the Great Lakes region, and this water manito made gifts of copper. It is seen as opposed to the thunderbirds, masters of the powers of the air, in an eternal yet complementary conflict.

Some traditions held the underwater panther to be a helpful, protective being: it was believed to shelter and feed those who fell through the ice, and to give medicinal power to shamans who accepted its guardianship. Yet more often it was viewed as a malevolent beast bringing death and misfortune, in need of placating. Taking copper was highly taboo, above all from Michipicoten Island, and as late as the 1950s the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians held a ceremony to calm it.

Kamus Ojibwe mengartikan kata mishibizhii sebagai singa atau panter dan sebagai underwater panther.
long_description.en: The underwater panther is a leading mythical water being of the Great Lakes region, especially for the Anishinaabeg. Its name, Mishipeshu, means "the Great Lynx"; it has a giant cat's head and paws, scales, and spikes down its back and tail. It lives on Michipicoten Island in Lake Superior, and for the Algonquins it ranked as the strongest underworld being. An Ojibwe dictionary glosses the word mishibizhii as a lion or panther and as an underwater panther.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan itu, Mishipeshu hidup di bagian terdalam danau dan sungai, tempat ia dapat menimbulkan badai, jeram, dan arus, menenggelamkan kano, dan menewaskan orang, sering anak-anak. Ia juga dikenal sebagai penjaga tembaga di Danau Superior dan wilayah Great Lakes, dan manito air ini memberi hadiah tembaga. Ia dipandang berseberangan dengan thunderbird, penguasa kekuatan udara, dalam konflik abadi namun saling melengkapi.
long_description.en: In these beliefs, Mishipeshu lives in the deepest parts of lakes and rivers, where it can stir up storms, rapids and currents, sink canoes and drown people, often children. It is also known as the keeper of the copper of Lake Superior and the Great Lakes region, and this water manito made gifts of copper. It is seen as opposed to the thunderbirds, masters of the powers of the air, in an eternal yet complementary conflict.

long_description.id: Sebagian tradisi meyakini underwater panther dapat menjadi makhluk penolong dan pelindung: ia dipercaya melindungi dan memberi makan orang yang jatuh menembus es, dan memberi kekuatan penyembuhan kepada dukun yang menerima perlindungannya. Namun lebih sering ia dipandang sebagai binatang jahat yang membawa kematian dan kemalangan dan perlu ditenangkan. Mengambil tembaga sangat tabu, terlebih dari Pulau Michipicoten, dan hingga tahun 1950-an Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians masih menggelar upacara untuk menenangkannya.
long_description.en: Some traditions held the underwater panther to be a helpful, protective being: it was believed to shelter and feed those who fell through the ice, and to give medicinal power to shamans who accepted its guardianship. Yet more often it was viewed as a malevolent beast bringing death and misfortune, in need of placating. Taking copper was highly taboo, above all from Michipicoten Island, and as late as the 1950s the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians held a ceremony to calm it.

cultural_context.id: Mengambil tembaga dari wilayah itu sangat tabu bagi bangsa Ojibwe, terlebih dari rumah Mishipeshu di Pulau Michipicoten.
cultural_context.en: Taking copper from the region was extremely taboo for the Ojibwe, above all from Mishipeshu's home on Michipicoten Island.

short_description.id: Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan.
short_description.en: Ura is an ancient oni of the Kibi region in southern Okayama.

long_description.id:
Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan. Tradisi menjadikannya penguasa Kibi yang dikalahkan Kibitsuhiko.

Kibitsuhiko melukai mata kirinya dengan menembakkan dua anak panah bersama. Pengejaran mereka berubah dari burung pegar dan elang menjadi ikan mas dan burung kormoran sebelum Ura menyerah.

Dalam versi yang diringkas basis data Nichibunken, Ura adalah roh jahat dari Baekje yang menjarah Kibi pada masa Kaisar Suinin. Setelah ditangkap dan dipenggal, kepalanya terus meraung selama bertahun-tahun sampai rohnya dipuja untuk menenangkannya.

Kepala itu dikatakan dikubur di bawah kuali di balai kuali Kibitsuhiko Jinja, dan bunyi kuali dalam ritual ramalan yang dipimpin miko dianggap sebagai teriakannya.
long_description.en:
Ura is an ancient oni of the Kibi region in southern Okayama. Tradition makes him a Kibi ruler defeated by Kibitsuhiko.

Kibitsuhiko wounds his left eye by shooting two arrows together. Their pursuit changes from pheasant and hawk to carp and cormorant before Ura surrenders.

In a version summarized in the Nichibunken database, Ura is a demon from Baekje who plundered Kibi in the reign of Emperor Suinin. After his capture and beheading, his head kept roaring for years until his spirit was enshrined to pacify it.

The head is said to be buried under the cauldron in the cauldron hall of Kibitsuhiko Shrine, and the sound of the cauldron in the divination led by a shrine maiden is regarded as its cry.

claim.id: Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan.
claim.en: Ura is an ancient oni of the Kibi region in southern Okayama.

claims_provenance.quote: 温羅（うら/おんら）は、岡山県南部の吉備地方に伝わる古代の鬼。

claim.id: Tradisi menjadikannya penguasa Kibi yang dikalahkan Kibitsuhiko.
claim.en: Tradition makes him a Kibi ruler defeated by Kibitsuhiko.

claims_provenance.quote: 温羅とは伝承上の鬼・人物で、古代吉備地方の統治者であったとされる。「鬼神」「吉備冠者（きびのかじゃ）」という異称があり、伝承によると吉備には吉備津彦命（きびつひこのみこと）が派遣され退治されたという。

claim.id: Kibitsuhiko melukai mata kirinya dengan menembakkan dua anak panah bersama.
claim.en: Kibitsuhiko wounds his left eye by shooting two arrows together.

claims_provenance.quote: 温羅に対して矢を1本ずつ射たが温羅はその都度石を投げて撃ち落とした。そこで命が2本同時に射たところ、1本は撃ち落とされたが、もう1本は温羅の左眼を射抜いた。

claim.id: Pengejaran mereka berubah dari burung pegar dan elang menjadi ikan mas dan burung kormoran sebelum Ura menyerah.
claim.en: Their pursuit changes from pheasant and hawk to carp and cormorant before Ura surrenders.

claims_provenance.quote: すると温羅は雉に化けて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鷹に化けて追った。さらに温羅は鯉に身を変えて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鵜に変化してついに捕らえたところ温羅は降参し「吉備冠者」の名を五十狭芹彦命に献上した。これにより五十狭芹彦命は吉備津彦命と呼ばれるようになった。

claim.id: Menurut ringkasan di basis data Nichibunken, pada masa Kaisar Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto dikirim untuk menumpas Ura, roh jahat (鬼神) dari Baekje (百済) yang terus menjarah negeri Kibi (吉備国).
claim.en: According to a summary in the Nichibunken database, in the reign of Emperor Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto was sent to subdue Ura, a demon (鬼神) from Baekje (百済) who repeatedly plundered the land of Kibi (吉備国).

claims_provenance.quote: 垂仁天皇の時代、吉備国で略奪を繰り返す百済の鬼神、温羅を退治するため、イサセリヒコノミコトが派遣された。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 国際日本文化研究センター — 鬼，温羅（末藤小百合「吉備「鬼、城」史跡と「温羅」伝承」）（怪異・妖怪伝承データベース 2600008）

claim.id: Setelah menangkap Ura yang melarikan diri dengan berubah menjadi burung pegar dan ikan mas, sang pangeran memenggal dan memajang kepalanya; karena kepala itu terus meraung keras selama bertahun-tahun, roh Ura dipuja untuk menenangkannya.
claim.en: After catching Ura, who fled by turning into a pheasant and a carp, the prince beheaded him and displayed the head; because the head kept roaring loudly for years, Ura's spirit was enshrined to pacify it.

claims_provenance.quote: 雉や鯉に姿を変えて逃れる温羅を捕らえたミコトは、首を刎ねて曝したが、その首が何年も大声でうなり続けたため、温羅の霊を祀って鎮めた。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 国際日本文化研究センター — 鬼，温羅（末藤小百合「吉備「鬼、城」史跡と「温羅」伝承」）（怪異・妖怪伝承データベース 2600008）

claim.id: Kibitsuhiko Jinja (吉備津彦神社) memiliki balai kuali (お釜殿); orang yang ingin meramal nasib meminta kepada miko bernama Asome (阿曾女), yang membakar ranting dan memegang beras persembahan dalam ayakan di atas uap kuali.
claim.en: Kibitsuhiko Shrine (吉備津彦神社) has a cauldron hall (お釜殿); those wishing to divine good or ill fortune ask a shrine maiden called Asome (阿曾女), who burns brushwood and holds offering rice in a sieve over the cauldron's steam.

claims_provenance.quote: 吉備津彦神社にはお釜殿があり、吉凶を占いたければ阿曾女という巫女に請えば、巫女は柴をたき、供米を篩に入れて釜の湯気にかざす。
claims_provenance.source_citation: 国際日本文化研究センター — 釜，温羅（保田素一郎「山陽の伝説玩具」）（怪異・妖怪伝承データベース 1232907）

claim.id: Bunyi kuali itu dikatakan sebagai teriakan Ura, karena ketika Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) memenggal kepalanya, kepala itu tampak masih hidup sehingga dikubur di bawah kuali.
claim.en: The cauldron's sound is said to be Ura's cry, because when Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) cut off his head it still seemed alive, so it was buried under the cauldron.

claims_provenance.quote: これは昔、吉備津彦命が温羅の首をはねたときに、まだ生きているようだったので命はこれを釜の下に生められたため、その叫び声であるといわれている。

claims.quote: 温羅（うら/おんら）は、岡山県南部の吉備地方に伝わる古代の鬼。

statement.id: Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan.
statement.en: Ura is an ancient oni of the Kibi region in southern Okayama.

claims.quote: 温羅とは伝承上の鬼・人物で、古代吉備地方の統治者であったとされる。「鬼神」「吉備冠者（きびのかじゃ）」という異称があり、伝承によると吉備には吉備津彦命（きびつひこのみこと）が派遣され退治されたという。

statement.id: Tradisi menjadikannya penguasa Kibi yang dikalahkan Kibitsuhiko.
statement.en: Tradition makes him a Kibi ruler defeated by Kibitsuhiko.

claims.quote: 温羅に対して矢を1本ずつ射たが温羅はその都度石を投げて撃ち落とした。そこで命が2本同時に射たところ、1本は撃ち落とされたが、もう1本は温羅の左眼を射抜いた。

statement.id: Kibitsuhiko melukai mata kirinya dengan menembakkan dua anak panah bersama.
statement.en: Kibitsuhiko wounds his left eye by shooting two arrows together.

claims.quote: すると温羅は雉に化けて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鷹に化けて追った。さらに温羅は鯉に身を変えて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鵜に変化してついに捕らえたところ温羅は降参し「吉備冠者」の名を五十狭芹彦命に献上した。これにより五十狭芹彦命は吉備津彦命と呼ばれるようになった。

statement.id: Pengejaran mereka berubah dari burung pegar dan elang menjadi ikan mas dan burung kormoran sebelum Ura menyerah.
statement.en: Their pursuit changes from pheasant and hawk to carp and cormorant before Ura surrenders.

claims.quote: 垂仁天皇の時代、吉備国で略奪を繰り返す百済の鬼神、温羅を退治するため、イサセリヒコノミコトが派遣された。

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan di basis data Nichibunken, pada masa Kaisar Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto dikirim untuk menumpas Ura, roh jahat (鬼神) dari Baekje (百済) yang terus menjarah negeri Kibi (吉備国).
statement.en: According to a summary in the Nichibunken database, in the reign of Emperor Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto was sent to subdue Ura, a demon (鬼神) from Baekje (百済) who repeatedly plundered the land of Kibi (吉備国).

claims.quote: 雉や鯉に姿を変えて逃れる温羅を捕らえたミコトは、首を刎ねて曝したが、その首が何年も大声でうなり続けたため、温羅の霊を祀って鎮めた。

statement.id: Setelah menangkap Ura yang melarikan diri dengan berubah menjadi burung pegar dan ikan mas, sang pangeran memenggal dan memajang kepalanya; karena kepala itu terus meraung keras selama bertahun-tahun, roh Ura dipuja untuk menenangkannya.
statement.en: After catching Ura, who fled by turning into a pheasant and a carp, the prince beheaded him and displayed the head; because the head kept roaring loudly for years, Ura's spirit was enshrined to pacify it.

claims.quote: 吉備津彦神社にはお釜殿があり、吉凶を占いたければ阿曾女という巫女に請えば、巫女は柴をたき、供米を篩に入れて釜の湯気にかざす。

statement.id: Kibitsuhiko Jinja (吉備津彦神社) memiliki balai kuali (お釜殿); orang yang ingin meramal nasib meminta kepada miko bernama Asome (阿曾女), yang membakar ranting dan memegang beras persembahan dalam ayakan di atas uap kuali.
statement.en: Kibitsuhiko Shrine (吉備津彦神社) has a cauldron hall (お釜殿); those wishing to divine good or ill fortune ask a shrine maiden called Asome (阿曾女), who burns brushwood and holds offering rice in a sieve over the cauldron's steam.

claims.quote: これは昔、吉備津彦命が温羅の首をはねたときに、まだ生きているようだったので命はこれを釜の下に生められたため、その叫び声であるといわれている。

statement.id: Bunyi kuali itu dikatakan sebagai teriakan Ura, karena ketika Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) memenggal kepalanya, kepala itu tampak masih hidup sehingga dikubur di bawah kuali.
statement.en: The cauldron's sound is said to be Ura's cry, because when Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) cut off his head it still seemed alive, so it was buried under the cauldron.

summary.id: Ura menyerah dan menyerahkan gelarnya (吉備冠者) kepada sang pangeran.
summary.en: Ura surrenders and gives his title (吉備冠者) to the prince.

summary.id: Ura dipenggal dan kepalanya terus meraung.
summary.en: Ura is beheaded and his head keeps roaring.

short_description.id: Vákner adalah makhluk mitologi Galisia berwujud manusia serigala raksasa yang ditemui uskup Armenia Mártir dalam ziarahnya ke Fisterra.
short_description.en: The Vákner is a Galician mythical creature shaped like a huge werewolf, met by the Armenian bishop Mártir on his pilgrimage to Fisterra.

long_description.id:
Vákner adalah tokoh mitologi Galisia, hewan ajaib yang biasanya berwujud manusia serigala raksasa. Kisahnya bermula dari Mártir, uskup Armenia dari Erzincan, yang memulai ziarah ke Roma pada Oktober 1485; ia tinggal 84 hari di Galisia pada 1492 dan menulis catatan singkat yang diterjemahkan ke bahasa Spanyol pada 1898.

Makhluk yang ditemui Mártir di jalan menuju Fisterra kini menjadi lambang ziarah Santiago ke Fisterra.

Dalam catatan perjalanan itu, Vákner disebut binatang buas besar yang sangat berbahaya; orang heran ia selamat, sebab rombongan dua puluh orang pun tidak bisa lewat. Para ahli menduga makhluk ini serigala atau serigala rabies, manusia serigala, naga, atau makhluk jahat lain yang sarat simbol. Sebuah instalasi patung manusia serigala karya Cándido Pazos kemudian direncanakan di Camino.
long_description.en:
The Vákner is a Galician mythological figure, a fantastic animal usually shaped like a huge werewolf. Its story starts with Mártir, an Armenian bishop from Erzincan, who set out for Rome in October 1485; he spent 84 days in Galicia in 1492 and wrote a brief account translated into Spanish in 1898.

The being Mártir met on the road to Fisterra has become a symbol of the Way of St James to Fisterra.

In the travel account the Vákner is a large and very harmful wild beast; people marvelled that he survived, since companies of twenty could not pass. Specialists have suggested a wolf or rabid wolf, a werewolf, a dragon or another symbolic evil being. A werewolf sculpture by Cándido Pazos was later planned for the Camino.

short_description.id: Veles, juga disebut Volos, adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia, dikenal dalam sumber lama sebagai dewa ternak.
short_description.en: Veles, also called Volos, is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology, known in early sources as the cattle god.

long_description.id:
Veles atau Volos adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia. Sumber sezaman menyebutnya dewa ternak, tetapi berbagai hipotesis memberinya wilayah kuasa yang lebih luas: kekayaan, alam orang mati yang dibayangkan sebagai padang rumput tempat jiwa-jiwa merumput, serta sihir, pengetahuan, ramalan, dan puisi. Sebagai penjaga batas antara dunia orang hidup dan orang mati, ia juga dewa alam liar, perburuan, dan hewan.

Ia menjamin sumpah dan menghukum pelanggarnya dengan membuat mereka "menguning". Dalam perjanjian dengan Bizantium, orang Rus bersumpah demi Perun dan demi Volos, dewa ternak, dan rela menjadi kuning seperti emas bila melanggar. Setelah dibaptis, Vladimir memerintahkan berhala Volos dilempar ke Sungai Pochaiv. Satu sumber menambahkan bahwa sesudah Kristenisasi Veles ditafsirkan ulang sebagai Iblis, dan peran pelindung ternaknya diambil alih Santo Blasius.

Ivanov dan Toporov merekonstruksi mitos tentang permusuhan Perun dan Veles: Veles sebagai ular merayap naik pohon dunia, diserang petir Perun, bersembunyi dengan berubah wujud, lalu dibunuh sehingga apa yang dicurinya jatuh sebagai hujan. Teori ini kemudian ditolak bahkan oleh Toporov sendiri, dan anggapan bahwa Veles adalah naga atau ular tidak lagi menjadi kesepakatan para ahli.
long_description.en:
Veles or Volos is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology. Contemporary sources call him the cattle god, but various hypotheses give him a wider domain: wealth, the realm of the dead imagined as a pasture where souls graze, and magic, knowledge, divination and poetry. Because he watched over the line separating living and dead, he also ruled the wild, the hunt and animals.

He guaranteed oaths and punished those who broke them by "turning them yellow". In treaties with Byzantium the Rus swore by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god, accepting to become yellow as gold if they failed. After his baptism Vladimir ordered the idol of Volos thrown into the Pochaiv River. One source adds that after Christianization Veles was reinterpreted as the Devil, and Saint Blasius took over his role as protector of cattle.

Ivanov and Toporov reconstructed a myth of enmity between Perun and Veles: Veles as a serpent climbs the world tree, is struck by Perun's lightning, hides by changing form, and is finally killed so that what he stole falls as rain. The theory was later rejected even by Toporov himself, and the view of Veles as a dragon or serpent is no longer scholarly consensus.

who.en: Veles is the Slavic god of the underworld and of cattle.

origin.id: Ia disebut dalam perjanjian Rus dengan Bizantium dan kronik lama.
origin.en: He is named in the treaties of the Rus with Byzantium and in old chronicles.

role.id: Ia menjamin sumpah dan menjaga batas dunia orang hidup dan orang mati.
role.en: He guaranteed oaths and guarded the border between the living and the dead.

famous_for.id: Ia dikenal sebagai lawan Perun dalam rekonstruksi mitos Slavia.
famous_for.en: He is known as Perun's adversary in reconstructions of Slavic myth.

did_you_know.id: Gugus bintang Pleiades dalam beberapa bahasa Slavia kemungkinan dinamai menurut Veles, misalnya Volosyni dalam bahasa Rusia Kuno.
did_you_know.en: In some Slavic languages the Pleiades are probably named after Veles, such as Old Russian Volosyni.

description.id: Dalam rekonstruksi mitos, ia lari dari Perun dengan bersembunyi atau berubah menjadi pohon, hewan, atau manusia.
description.en: In the reconstructed myth he flees Perun by hiding or turning into trees, animals or people.

description.id: Tempat berhala Volos dibuang atas perintah Vladimir.
description.en: Where the idol of Volos was thrown on Vladimir's orders.

note.id: Rekonstruksi Ivanov dan Toporov menjadikan Perun lawan Veles.
note.en: Ivanov and Toporov's reconstruction makes Perun his adversary.

note.id: Sifat dan kekuatannya mirip, meski tidak identik, dengan Varuna.
note.en: His nature and powers resemble, though not identically, those of Varuna.

note.id: Sifat dan kekuatannya mirip dengan Velnias.
note.en: His nature and powers resemble those of Velnias.

summary.id: Satu sumber: ia digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk berjanggut panjang.
summary.en: One source: he is depicted as a horned serpent with a long beard.

summary.id: Sumber lain: penyamaannya dengan naga atau ular keliru dan bukan lagi kesepakatan ilmiah.
summary.en: Another source: identifying him with a dragon or serpent is incorrect and no longer scholarly consensus.

short_description.id: Veles, juga disebut Volos, adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia, dikenal dalam sumber lama sebagai dewa ternak.
short_description.en: Veles, also called Volos, is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology, known in early sources as the cattle god.

long_description.id: Veles atau Volos adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia. Sumber sezaman menyebutnya dewa ternak, tetapi berbagai hipotesis memberinya wilayah kuasa yang lebih luas: kekayaan, alam orang mati yang dibayangkan sebagai padang rumput tempat jiwa-jiwa merumput, serta sihir, pengetahuan, ramalan, dan puisi. Sebagai penjaga batas antara dunia orang hidup dan orang mati, ia juga dewa alam liar, perburuan, dan hewan.
long_description.en: Veles or Volos is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology. Contemporary sources call him the cattle god, but various hypotheses give him a wider domain: wealth, the realm of the dead imagined as a pasture where souls graze, and magic, knowledge, divination and poetry. Because he watched over the line separating living and dead, he also ruled the wild, the hunt and animals.

long_description.id: Ia menjamin sumpah dan menghukum pelanggarnya dengan membuat mereka "menguning". Dalam perjanjian dengan Bizantium, orang Rus bersumpah demi Perun dan demi Volos, dewa ternak, dan rela menjadi kuning seperti emas bila melanggar. Setelah dibaptis, Vladimir memerintahkan berhala Volos dilempar ke Sungai Pochaiv. Satu sumber menambahkan bahwa sesudah Kristenisasi Veles ditafsirkan ulang sebagai Iblis, dan peran pelindung ternaknya diambil alih Santo Blasius.
long_description.en: He guaranteed oaths and punished those who broke them by "turning them yellow". In treaties with Byzantium the Rus swore by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god, accepting to become yellow as gold if they failed. After his baptism Vladimir ordered the idol of Volos thrown into the Pochaiv River. One source adds that after Christianization Veles was reinterpreted as the Devil, and Saint Blasius took over his role as protector of cattle.

long_description.id: Ivanov dan Toporov merekonstruksi mitos tentang permusuhan Perun dan Veles: Veles sebagai ular merayap naik pohon dunia, diserang petir Perun, bersembunyi dengan berubah wujud, lalu dibunuh sehingga apa yang dicurinya jatuh sebagai hujan. Teori ini kemudian ditolak bahkan oleh Toporov sendiri, dan anggapan bahwa Veles adalah naga atau ular tidak lagi menjadi kesepakatan para ahli.
long_description.en: Ivanov and Toporov reconstructed a myth of enmity between Perun and Veles: Veles as a serpent climbs the world tree, is struck by Perun's lightning, hides by changing form, and is finally killed so that what he stole falls as rain. The theory was later rejected even by Toporov himself, and the view of Veles as a dragon or serpent is no longer scholarly consensus.
